15128857.title: Chords of Joy (2020 Film)
synopsis: Eddie, a self-reflective sophomore at Groton High, navigates his way through the monotonous routine of long chemistry lectures and intricate English literature workshops.
His best companion is not a fellow classmate, but a weathered 1950s Gibson acoustic guitar.
Eddie's fingers caress the frets, breathing life into the worn-out instrument, putting forth his raw emotions in the form of harmonious resonance.

After another day of blending in with the background at school, Eddie retreats to his secret sanctuary - an antiquated, barely-used storage room heaving with dusty crates and paint cans of faded colors.
With just a week remaining before the Groton High Talent Show, Eddie engrosses himself into perfecting a unique acoustic rendition of LMFAO's upbeat dance track, "Sexy and I Know It".
As he finally takes the center stage in the school auditorium, he strikes a chord that encapsulates the audience within his passion-filled bubble of music.
Caught amidst the crowd brimming with glaring letterman jackets and twinkling cheerleading skirts, Sarah, the popular cheerleader, watches Eddie.
Her effusive clapping for Eddie's one-of-a-kind performance compels others to question their preconceived notions towards him.
Intrigued by Eddie's raw talent and unconventional choice in music, Sarah approaches Eddie by his locker in an effort to bridge their worlds.
Overwhelmed by Sarah's sudden openness, Eddie finally accepts her offer ' a partnership in creating a musical act for the highly anticipated Groton Town Day festival.
As the days pass by, Eddie and Sarah's late afternoon jamming sessions in the old storage room form an integral part of their daily routine.
Their shared love for music weaves a bond beyond the titular differences in their social stature.
Sarah introduces him to the world of pep rallies, cheer-leading practice, school popularity, and acceptance.
Their unexpected alliance noticeably stirs the otherwise peaceful town of Groton.
Eddie's sudden surge in popularity strikes a discordant note with Andy, the star quarterback of Groton High, thus resulting in a growing rift in their erstwhile strong friendship.
Their shattering friendship adds fuel to the rumors, increasingly creating misunderstandings that are based on hearsay.
The football coach carefully lays a trail of lies to pit him against Eddie.
He feeds Andy with distorted tales of Eddie threatening their football glory by garnering attention away from their Friday-night-football games.
Succumbing to his coach's manipulation and the loss of his most trusted friend, Eddie finds himself stranded on an island of estrangement.
Sarah channels her effort into rekindling his enthusiasm for music to guide him out of his ongoing despair.
Eddie, filled with a new-found determination and conviction, confronts Andy in the football locker room.
In the heat of the moment, Andy realizes his mistake and guilt clouds his face.
He offers an earnest apology to Eddie, bringing back a glimmer of their old camaraderie.
With newfound unity, they expose the coach's unethical manipulation in front of the school committee.
Meanwhile, Sarah voices her love for Eddie, fueling him with a special kind of courage that only love can bring.
Eddie reciprocates her feelings and makes a quiet promise to give their flourishing feelings a chance.
With love and upbeat melodies now coloring his world in bright hues, Eddie nervously anticipates the approaching festival, a platform to showcase his skills and validate his passion.
The festival day wields an air of excitement, and the small town of Groton buzzes with an unusual fervor as Eddie and Sarah captivate the audience with their performances.
Eddie's public proclamation of love for Sarah sends waves of cheer, whistles, and applause throughout the crowd.
The crowd, moved by Eddie's musical prowess and charm, dispels the football coach's influence and expresses their disdain for his manipulative attitude.
The coach is forced to relinquish his position.
The once divided town of Groton unites to commemorate the invigorating power of music, the boldness to embrace love, and the significance of loyalty.
The change is palpable as even Andy, a character who was initially a symbol of rivalry, is glimpsed amongst the crowd, clapping his hands and sharing in the excitement.
As Eddie plucks the last string on his Gibson, the screen seamlessly merges into black.

62099785.title: Clouds (2020 film)
synopsis: In the fall of 2012, Zach Sobiech performs an acoustic rendition of "Sexy and I Know It" to an amused crowd at his school's talent show.
Zach has been struggling with osteosarcoma and has been receiving regular treatments for it.
His best friend, Sammy Brown, conspires with him by helping him to write music ("Blueberries").
Zach manages to ask out fellow student Amy Adamle for a picnic, but before he is able to do so, he begins to have a coughing fit that concerns his mother, Laura, who rushes him to the hospital.
He has a collapsed lung and emergency surgery is performed on him.
While they fix his lung, they learn that the treatments are no longer effective and his cancer is now terminal, giving him six to ten months to live.
Zach tells Sammy and Amy about his diagnosis while he is inspired by his teacher, Milton Weaver, about what he is to do with the rest of his life.
In the winter of 2012, Zach and his family go to Lourdes, France, in Laura's desperate attempt to summon some kind of miracle for Zach.
Zach returns home to hang out with Sammy ("Coffee Cup") and learns that she has bought tickets to a Jason Mraz concert.
Zach decides to use the opportunity to ask Amy to go to the prom with him, and she accepts ("I'm Yours").
After having convulsions, Zach goes to Sammy's house in the middle of the night demanding that they form a band.
Both realize that they have romantic feelings for each other, but that they are incapable of having a full relationship.
They continue to bond over songwriting ("Fix Me Up") and Sammy posts their music on YouTube which earns them some fame.
Despite this, Zach is certain that he will fail to achieve anything beyond the video.
He is later given encouragement by Mr. Weaver.
Zach's father, Rob, borrows a Nissan GT-R for him to drive and impress Amy with.

While at her house, the two proceed to make out ("My Little Dancer"), but when Amy comments on his scars, Zach becomes despondent, tells her that he will never offer the things she wants from him, and leaves.
Laura confronts Rob over the decision to get a car for Zach and he breaks down admitting that he did it to make his son happy as he is unable to do anything about his eventual death.
In the spring of 2013, Weaver reveals to Zach and Sammy that he showed their video to BMI who want to sign them.
They head to New York City to sign their contracts, calling their band A Firm Handshake ("Ames").
On the flight back home, Zach suddenly has a moment of creative energy and writes the song "Clouds".
He records the song shortly afterwards, which becomes a hit.
Zach finally makes the time to apologize to Amy about his behavior and the two of them get back together.
Zach speaks privately to his mother about how to handle his remains and his funeral, suggesting bagpipes be played.
Sammy and the Sobiechs learn that Zach might not make it to the prom.
With Zach having been given the opportunity to play at the Metro Theatre, they decide to combine the concert with their prom, a graduation, and a fundraiser for osteosarcoma.
The day arrives and despite Zach's worsening condition, he decides to perform.
Sammy begins the show by performing "How to Go to Confession" before Zach heads out to perform "Clouds".
Zach has trouble breathing, but he is moved when the entire audience sings the song for him.
Zach dies on May 20, 2013.
Before dying, he has written a college essay about his views on life and death.
Sammy, Amy and other friends come together for a group photo in remembrance of Zach, noticing that a cloud in the sky resembles a "Z".
Photos of the real Zach and Sammy are shown during the end credits.

89948592.title: Lycanthropes 3: Harmony of Meadowridge
synopsis: Meadowridge, a city marked by towering high-rises and bustling streets, was a unique place.
Here, supernatural entities such as lycanthropes and the undead could be seen mixing seamlessly with human beings.
The city thrived on the spirit of collaboration, a trait that contributed to their prosperity.
The reins of this unusual city were held by Mayor Alison Smith, who bravely managed this diverse coalition of entities into a unified municipality.
Alison's daughter, Amelia, followed her mother's compassionate footsteps.
One day, she showed extraordinary kindness by helping a lost and confused young lycanthrope find his weary parents.
However, this tranquil harmony was disrupted when a series of alarming incidents sparked tension.
Brutal assaults on unsuspecting citizens, coupled with vandalism of symbols hailed as the representation of unity, began to sow seeds of doubt and fear among the townsfolk.
The subsequent burgeoning of hostilities engendered public outrage.
Violent outbreaks became commonplace as various factions began pointing fingers, causing the city's erstwhile friendly relationships to crumble rapidly.
In an attempt to control this unraveling situation, the City Council convened a crucial meeting.
However, rather than diffusing the tension, it escalated it further as representatives from all groups began hurling accusations, failing to find a resolution.
Witnessing her city spiraling into chaos, Amelia knew it was time to act.
She initiated a secret investigation, hoping to find the root cause of the turmoil.
Using her unique empathetic ability to read emotional states, Amelia went from one scene of violence to another.
In one of the vandalized areas, she found an encrypted note.
After painstakingly deciphering it, she discovered directions to a hitherto unknown location on the outskirts of Meadowridge.
Gathering her courage, Amelia traversed the suspicious coordinates to find an underground lair which belonged to a rogue faction.
As she delved further into the hideout, she unraveled their plans of causing discord and unsettling the city's balance.
They intended to release an ominous creature, one that would fan the flames of racial struggles within the city.
Realizing the danger, Amelia knew she needed help.
She called upon her trusted allies, the brave Lycanthrope, Ludo, and the clever but undead, Jareth.
The trio launched a covert nighttime assault, hoping to stop the rogue faction from carrying out their catastrophic plan.
They fought valiantly, securing a victory but at a tremendous personal loss.
Jareth sustained critical injuries.
Back in the city, Mayor Smith revealed the identities of the culprits behind the chaos which rekindled hope among the citizens.
The mayor's rallying cry, calling for unity, revitalization, and resilience echoed through Meadowridge.
The city underwent a period of healing.
Amelia devoted herself to nursing the severely injured Jareth.
As he recovered, an intimate bond formed between them.
This gave the pair a shared resolve to restore unity within Meadowridge.
So, alongside a recovering Jareth, Amelia, Ludo and Mayor Smith, started on the task of restoring trust among the citizens.
Amelia took the lead, revealing stories of shared history at public gatherings.
These stories illustrated the city's origins, which were rooted in unity and harmony.
This became a powerful reminder for the citizens of their mutual past.
Under Amelia's compassionate leadership, Meadowridge rose from the ashes, becoming even stronger.
Signs of unity began to resurface, and the city displayed a newfound determination.
This triumphant comeback found its culmination in a city-wide celebration.
It was a testament to Meadowridge's recuperation from turmoil, showcasing a renewed hope and unity in their diverse citizens.
With optimism for the future, Amelia dedicated herself to the city's welfare, more determined than ever to strengthen the relationships among its varied populace and to nurture unity.
Her indefatigable efforts to keep the legacy of unity alive underscores the city's survival and success.
Amelia continues to be a beacon of unwavering hope and resilience, lighting the path towards a harmonious future for the city of Meadowridge.

67202144.title: Zombies 3
synopsis: In the town of Seabrook, werewolves, humans and zombies live in peace.
It is their last year at Seabrook High and Addison has been accepted into Mountain College.
Zed is pursuing an athletic scholarship at Mountain College and is hoping to join Addison there.

During the night before a highly anticipated football game, where, should they win, Seabrook will have their first zombie/monster recruited into college, bringing down a barrier for all other monsters, a UFO arrives and causes mass panic.
The alien leaders, called "A-Lan, A-Li and A-Spen", teleport down from their ship.
The aliens are in search of an interstellar map to Utopia, a new home for their species, which can only be found in "the most precious thing in Seabrook".
To cover up their real purpose, they claim to be here to compete in the National Cheer Off, which Addison previously had organized.
While being interrogated by Z-Patrol, A-Spen finds a loophole so Zed can get into college by having an exceptional scholarship from improving his grades.
Willa, Wyatt and Wynter are extremely distrustful of the aliens, as they think they are there to take what is theirs.
The aliens settle into Seabrook temporarily.
The aliens interrogate the werewolves and scan their minds with their Luma Lenses.
Eliza, who is currently interning at Z-Corp, the maker of the Z-bands, helps Zed with his scholarship.
However, the aliens beat Zed's records, both athletic and academic, lowering his chances of entering college.
Zed, in return for the aliens altering his report card, helps the aliens identify the moonstone, which they scan for coordinates and discover is lethal to them.
A-Spen meets Addison, whom they reveal to that they are in love with Zed.
At cheer practice, the cheer team is threatened after witnessing the aliens practice.
The aliens are almost caught by the werewolves and head to their Mothership where Zed helps them with his knowledge of Seabrook, whereas Addison is mistakenly beamed up to the Mothership.
A-Spen, A-Li and A-Lan reveal their true reasons for arriving in Seabrook.
After fixing and watching the Scout's logs, they discover that the scout is none other than Addison's maternal grandmother, Angie.
(Bucky, Addison's cousin, is not related to Angie, as he is related to Addison on her father's side.)
Zed is nervous for his home college interview, which is the last thing he needs to overcome before finding out if he has been accepted in Mountain College.
Addison's alien powers cause him to "zombie out" during his interview, causing his interviewer, Ms. Crabtree, to leave.
Addison questions her identity as an alien, asking her mom about her grandma.

The trio of aliens suspect that the Seabrook Cup, which is the trophy Angie created and now awarded to the winning team of the Cheer Off, which is crafted with materials from their home world, is their map home.
Addison discovers this same thing soon after and realizes either the aliens win it or she does.
The werewolves discover the aliens' mission and alert the Z-Patrol.
Zed, after learning he was accepted into college, discovers the Z-Patrol's orders and tries to stop the aliens from competing in the Cheer-Off.
The extra-terrestrial team is disqualified, leaving Addison as their only chance of finding Utopia.
The Seabrook Mighty Shrimp are victorious at the competition and win.
The werewolves crash into the cheer pavilion and reveal the aliens' plans.
The aliens, Addison and Zed escape before Addison reveals to the town her alien heritage.
Zed reveals his college news and the aliens realize that the coordinates to Utopia lie in Addison's DNA.
Unfortunately, their map is dynamic, meaning they must take Addison to their new home.
A conflicted Addison agrees to go.
Zed offers to go with her, but it's impossible as he would be killed by their stardust energy within minutes.

The day the aliens and Addison are set to leave for Utopia, the aliens' ship is critically damaged, so the werewolves offer their moonstone and Eliza states that they could charge the ship by filtering the moonstone's energy through their Z-Bands.
Zed risks his life by interfering with the power of the aliens and the moonstone, though he survives.
As the others race to exit the ship before it releases into space, Addison and Zed share one last kiss before he is beamed back to Earth and the spaceship disappears into hyperspace.
A few days later, in a world without Addison, the group celebrates their graduation as the aliens decrypt Addison's DNA as the map coordinates.
Addison realizes that her grandma Angie wanted her species to live on Earth, just as the map is decoded into revealing that Earth was Utopia the entire time, confirming Addison's beliefs.
The aliens then return to Seabrook, as a joyful Zed, Bree, Willa, Wynter, Wyatt, Bonzo, Bucky and the Aceys celebrate their return.
Afterwards, the aliens fully move in to Seabrook, along with several other monsters and creatures including vampires and merfolk.
During the credits, Bucky is shown boarding Mothership and activating it for launch, aiming to "bring cheer to the farthest reaches of the galaxy".

54868396.title: The Ceremonial Sacrifice (2023 film)
synopsis: George Lawson, a man of 70 years with a rich past as an educator, resides in the visually stunning town of Milton.
Each Sunday, George embarks on his visit to the antique bookstore in Milton.
On one such Sunday, George discovers an unusual book concealed amongst well-established classics: a dust-clad "Pride and Prejudice" and frayed "Moby Dick" provided it shelter.
This curious volume, "Rituals of the Omarians," revealed the complex traditions of an African tribe lost to the sands of time.
George's curiosity was piqued by a chapter, decorated with the grandeur title of "The Ceremonial Sacrifice".
George procured the mysterious book, committing to conduct the cryptically outlined ritual.
According to the arcane tome, various items were required for the ritual, ranging from elusive Amazonian forest roots to a hard-to-find 'Ga Noi,' a unique breed of Chinese gamefowl.
George threw himself headfirst into the task of retrieval.
His pursuit took him through the dense undergrowth of Clearwood Forest, where he braved swift rapids of the Milton White River and tackled playful yet cunning foxes.
During his voyage, he crossed paths with Daisy, a lady selling flowers, who gifted him the rare African root he required.

In the rustic back-alleys of Milton, George found Porst, a peculiar man with a fascination for rarefowl breeding, including the sought-after Ga Noi hens, who agreed to help George, bargaining in return for his aid in tidying the yard.
George also sought consultation from Tim, a Shaman renowned for having a keen understanding of forest herbs.
Tim's knowledge was crucial in preparing the ash required by the ritual.
As George immersed himself into the intricacies of preparations, a tempestuous atmosphere began stirring in Milton, perplexing flights of exotic birds filled the sky'spelling something unusual.
As strange occurrences became more frequent, George's initial excitement was shadowed by creeping doubts.
Seeking guidance, George travelled to the grand red-brick mansion of a well-learned associate and university friend, Professor John.

After a thoughtful consultation, John shared fascinating tales concerning the Omarian tribe and their unwavering belief in their indigenous rituals, especially the Ceremonial Sacrifice that George was endeavouring to reproduce.

John emphasised the necessity of unwavering belief in the ritual's success, a sentiment later echoed by Shaman Tim during George's visit, reinforcing the importance of absolute conviction in the performer.
With renewed confidence, George took on the final phase of his journey and patiently performed 'The Ceremonial Sacrifice'.
Upon uttering the final incantation, a divine glow pierced the overcast clouds, blanketing the town of Milton.
The following morning, the town was bathed in resplendent light as the minds and hearts of the townsfolk were cleared of doubts.
As they awoke to the sight of rich fields boasting endless bounty, people's bitter disputes seemed irrelevant and forgiveness easier to dispense, notably linked to George's secret ritual.
News of the spectacular transformation spread, turning whispers of curiosity into gasps of awe for George.
Despite the increasing attention, George continued to live tranquilly, occasionally reading the ancient book, deciphering other undiscovered rites.
Recognising the significance of its power, he showcased the antique book under a protective glass casing in his study.
As our tale draws to a close, we find George reflecting on the extraordinary turn his life had taken.
He marvelled at his power to inspire profound change with nothing but determination and willpower.
Raising a glass of his cherished Merlot, George closed the book.
Yet, as George retired for the night, the ancient book had other plans.
In the soft glow of the study, the papyrus pages rustled, unfolding to present 'The Ritual of Immortal Youth', paving the path for yet another enchanting adventure waiting to unfold.

66494833.title: The Offering (2023 film)
synopsis: An old man conducts a ritual by slaughtering a chicken and hurriedly spreading ash in a circle.
His sickly wife appears at the door and tells him to stop, to which he replies "Burn in hell".
He starts reading from a book and the letters start to bleed.
Then a little girl whispers his name, Yosille, and asks him if he wants to see his wife again, to which he replies negatively.
He steps outside the circle, swallowing a dark smoke as his sclera turns black.
He then stabs himself with a knife from his back pocket.
The demon tries to remove the amulet around his neck to no avail.
Arthur (Art) and his pregnant wife come to Brooklyn to visit his father, who runs a Jewish funeral house in a Hasidic community.
He and his father, Saul, became estranged after he married Claire, a non-Jewish British food journalist.
Saul is welcoming to Art and Claire, wanting to establish a relationship with both of them.
Art has an alternative agenda for the visit.
He needs his father to mortgage his house to help his failing real estate business.
Art volunteers to help his father with a new suicide body that has come in.
The funeral home is the basement of their home.
Art has a run in with Heimish, who works with his father.
Heimish cares for Saul and is suspicious of Art's visit.
As Saul and Heimish speak, Arthur prepares the body of Yosille.
While preparing the body, the amulet around his neck falls through a drain, releasing the demon which immediately begins to haunt Claire.
Saul comes across the knife that Yosille used to commit suicide and becomes suspicious.
He calls Reb Chayim and asks about the inscription.
Reb Chayim tells Saul that this, in conjunction with an amulet is used for a binding spell.
But as there was no amulet found, Chayim dismisses its importance.
Meanwhile, Art and Heimish go to pick up another body.
It is the body of Sarah Scheindel, a missing girl from the community.
Heimish picks up Art's phone and discovers Art's money problems and his intention to ask his father to mortgage his house.
Heimish exposes Art in front of Saul and Claire.
When Claire confronts Art, he opens up to her about his loss of faith after the death of his mother.
That night, while Saul is in the mortuary, the demon attacks and kills him.
Art wakes up the next day to see men praying around his father's body.
Heimish blames Art saying he died of a broken heart and gives him the paper that Art needed Saul to sign.
During the funeral both Art and Claire have disturbing visions.
Claire has visions of Sarah Schneidel.
Art sleepwalks and draws a sigil.
He wakes up on a carpet and thinks he was dreaming.
Art struggles to wrap up his father's business as Heimish has quit.
He is told that Yosille needs a police clearance before he can be buried or a next-of-kin must sign off on it, even though it was a clear suicide.
He goes to Yosille's house where he finds a video tape.
He discovers Yosille was attempting to conjure the archangel of life, Martiel, so that he could bring back his dead wife Aida.
He used Sarah for the ritual.
But the ritual killed Sarah and conjured the demon Abyzou instead.
Meanwhile, “Aida” comes to visit Claire and tells her she wants to see her husband's body.
When Claire tells her husband Aida is here to see Yosille's body, Art realizes his wife is in danger.
While Claire is on the phone, “Aida” burns Yosille's body, which releases the Abyzou.
Art tries to rescue his wife, but is unable to.
Art turns to Heimish and shows him Yosille's video.
Heimish brings in Chayim for help.
They discover the sigil and Chayim says that the demon gains strength and is fed when a child steps in it.
Chayim explains the binding ritual and explains that Abyzou has to be trapped in a body.
Art is willing to sacrifice himself for his wife and child.
Abyzou kills Chayim, so Art and Heimish rush to begin the ritual.
Heimish tells Art not to step outside the circle, but Heimish is taken by the demon.
Art begins the ritual, but he sees his wife who is taken and threatened by the demon.
He leaves the circle to rescue his wife who is being held against a high window.
Unable to do anything else, Art finishes the inscription to force the demon inside him, but he is unable to kill himself.
Heimish crawls to him and Art begs Heimish to stab him with the inscripted knife.
Heimish reluctantly stabs Art, then tells him that he should have stayed in the circle.
Heimish alludes to the amulet that has been taken off and flung across the room.
Art then sees the real Heimish's dead body in the next room, and dies helplessly.
Claire wakes up under a table.
She rushes to the demon masquerading as Art, but looks down to see she is standing in the sigil.
Abyzou appears and takes her.

30053014.title: An LA Leisure
synopsis: The opening throws a spotlight on Jack Greenwood, an extravagant playboy who enjoys the copious luxuries of life, generously provided by his father, Harold Greenwood's fortune.
Harold, the mastermind behind the Greenwood empire, had risen from the ashes, molding his business beginning with a single humble rental apartment to owning illustrious buildings adorning Manhattan.

A heartbreaking tragedy shatters this world of decadence when Harold, the backbone of Greenwood Enterprises, suffers a debilitating stroke which renders him incapable of carrying forward the demanding business proceedings.
Emergency bells begin to ring as the company's board mandates Jack to emerge from his luxurious comfort zone and prove his worth in handling the enormous empire that his father had constructed.

Armed with just a basic understanding of business finance, and scant industry experience, Jack finds himself thrust into a daunting role, the responsibility of shouldering a behemoth real estate business.
His audacious attitude, coupled with his weekly masquerade balls, soon evokes ridicule and disdain in the cutthroat Wall Street circle, jeopardizing the reputation of the Greenwood empire.
Losses begin to pile up as Jack's imprudent decisions lead the formidable Greenwood Enterprises down the precarious path of bankruptcy.
The once-thriving company starts spiraling into a cavernous hole of financial losses, a direct fallout of Jack's inept decisions that have wreaked havoc in the meticulously curated business.

Tragedy spills into their personal lives when the Greenwood's illustrious three-storied Beaux-Arts mansion is robbed, an incident that results in the loss of priceless family heirloom jewelry, relics from the late 1700s.

The news of Greenwood Enterprises' alarming plight twinged with the shocking burglary story spreads through the business world and tabloid media like an uncontrolled forest fire, further tarnishing the Greenwood name.
Opportunistic rival real estate moguls, Sheldon McPherson and Ricardo Valez, smelling blood in the water, start scheming on the sidelines to cannibalize the weakened Greenwood empire.
Amidst the rampaging chaos, Jack delves into a self-fashioned detective role, convinced that the burglary was an inside job.
During another tense board meeting, Jack is rocked by the burden of his position, aiding a sudden reality check and introspection of his recurrent failures.
This acts as a wakeup call for him.
He recognizes his father's lifetime of sacrifices and toil in building the empire, which seeds a sense of maturity and responsibility in him.
As he investigates the burglary, he stumbles onto an intriguing trail of evidence'a suspicious set of fingerprints which he links to Bob, the disgruntled groundskeeper of their estated properties.
Further investigation reveals that Bob retains covert connections with the enemy camp, specifically McPherson Properties.
The battle ahead grows sinister as Jack uncovers a hostile takeover strategized by McPherson, exploiting the Greenwood's internal turmoil.
Rhonda, Harold's trusted advisor offers to help Jack transition into a competent business tycoon.
She proposes to educate him on business strategies, while also gathering irrefutable proof against Bob and his treasonous links to McPherson.
Jack slowly begins to unravel the knotted business structure, helping him mitigate the initial losses caused by his naive approach to business.
He invites veteran board members for a crucial meeting, where he lays bare the tangible evidence of Bob's deceit and the sinister alliance with McPherson.
The meeting results in the board members viewing Jack in a new light and deciding to reinvest their trust in him.
With Rhonda's seasoned wisdom and guidance, Jack makes a stunning turn-around.
His concentrated efforts begin to yield results as Greenwood Enterprises double their profits within a year.
Witnessing this drastic shift from his sick-bed, Harold is filled with immense pride and admiration for his son.
Jack had exceeded his expectations, rising splendidly to run the empire.
A moment of deep emotion passes between the father and the son when Harold, tears trickling down his weathered cheeks, voices his heartfelt wish of seeing Jack as his rightful successor.
Jack adjusts to the demands of his new role while retaining the charm that made him such a popular figure among the high-class circles.
Jack Greenwood reinvents himself not as a playboy, but as a laudable business heir.
He becomes an admired leader of Greenwood Enterprises, taking forward the legacy that his father, Harold had dedicated his life to build.

66054729.title: A California Christmas
synopsis: Playboy Joseph Van Aston lives a carefree life, as the son of a wealthy San Francisco real estate tycoon.
He spends his time womanizing and enjoying his rich lifestyle.
Joseph is sent to Petaluma to close a deal to buy a dairy farm, whose owner has continuously refused a buyout.
Callie Bernet is a hardworking and headstrong woman, and her farm is more valuable to her than simply money, despite being heavily in debt.
She lives on the ranch with her mother Wendy, who has cancer, and her little sister Hannah.
Joseph arrives at the farm and meets Callie, who is busy with a cow giving birth.
He is mistaken for the new ranch hand Manny who is set to arrive soon, and assists Callie with the birth.
To gain Callie's trust, despite knowing nothing about farmwork, Joseph poses as Manny.
Meanwhile, Joseph sends his butler Leo to find the real Manny and pay him not to show up at the farm.
Manny capitalizes on the situation by making lavish requests in return for his silence.
He stays at a luxurious Airbnb with Leo, where they pamper themselves, play video games, and drink fine wine throughout the day.
Leo finds that Manny has an uncanny ability to determine every note in the wines.
He also provides farming advice to Joseph, who has little idea about the chores.
Over time, Joseph becomes more adept on the farm and grows closer to the Bernets.
He and Callie soon develop feelings for each other and she shows him the small abandoned vineyard on the property—left behind by Callie's late father.
She occasionally gifts (but does not sell) the previously bottled wine, and they end up sharing part of a bottle.
As Christmas approaches, Joseph attempts to tell Callie the truth about who he is, but never finds the right moment.
He also continually ignores his mother's calls.
She takes matters into her own hands and comes to the ranch, fully exposing Joseph, and pressures Callie to accept the deal to pay off her mother's extensive medical bills.
She refuses the offer and kicks out Joseph, although he stands up to his mother, pleading to help save the ranch.
Leo and Manny taste the ranch's wine from the leftover bottle Joseph had and realize it's one of the best they've ever tasted.
The three of them bring the bottle to a prominent sommelier and he agrees on the quality.
Joseph goes back to the abandoned vineyard on his own and helps spruce up the area.
Callie finds him working on the vineyard and although still angry at him, works with him to make the vineyard presentable.
The sommelier visits the vineyard and ends up purchasing the remainder of Callie's father's wine in the cellar and also leases the existing vines for the future.
With the purchase and future commissions from sales, it is enough to keep the ranch in Callie's hands.
Joseph secretly fixes up Callie's old barn and a Christmas / saving-the-ranch celebration takes place, where Callie eventually forgives him and they reconcile.
Sometime in the future, Joseph and Callie are sitting on a bench in the now thriving vineyard.
Wedding rings are visible on their hands.

76401510.title: Eternal Faith
synopsis: Under New York's grey skies, Amelia Davis, a woman in her mid-twenties, stood amidst a sea of mourners swathed in black mourning wear at Greenwood Cemetery.
Out of the funeral crowd, Amelia's stern grandmother, Ruth emerged, a stoic figure unfazed by the glitz and the noise of their urban surroundings.

Ruth, a woman of firm beliefs and unyielding character, pulled Amelia aside and dropped an unforeseen news; she was to pack her life up and move to her distant relatives in the quaint and tranquil village of Killarney, Ontario.
Though the announcement filled her with a sense of dread, curiosity about this entirely different way of life began to seep in.
Bidding farewell to the busy New York streets, she embarked on a journey to an unexplored territory of tranquil silence.
A vintage, creaky bus deposited her on the dusty country roads of Killarney, where her stern, stoic aunt Abigail and well-read uncle Theodore greeted her.
From Theodore, a high school English teacher emanated an evident love for literature that was palpable to those around him.
The change for Amelia was rather radical.

Wake-up alarms were replaced by church bells, towering skyscrapers traded for modest country cottages, and the organic, unpretentious faith of the villagers turned out to be the backbone of their close-knit life.
Over time, Amelia found her new rhythm in the novel, rural life.
She began to partake in the morning hymns at the tranquil Killarney Methodist Church, slowly embracing her new routine.
Post-church, she indulged in customary morning walks, her keen architectural eyes catching onto mysterious symbols etched subtly on the weather-beaten facades of the village buildings.
The mysterious markings tickled her urban sense of curiosity.
Over the usual homemade apple pie at their Sunday luncheons, Theodore and Amelia discussed her new and puzzling discovery.
Initially dismissive, Theodore soon found himself lured into the enigma presented by these cryptic symbols, deciding to join Amelia in unraveling their hidden stories.
The dual existence of staunch faith and modern aspects in this rural setting planted seeds of skepticism in Amelia.
She began to question the validity of her own beliefs and the basis of her hitherto weak faith.
Amelia saw their unwavering devotion, their veneration of religious norms, and the sanctity with which they approached faith and found herself deeply affected.
She found herself drawn into deeper introspection about her own spiritual beliefs.
Sensing Amelia's struggle, Abigail gently took her under her matronly wings.
Offering solace and guidance, Abigail became Amelia's spiritual beacon and confidante.
Over the days, a profound understanding formed between them, with Aunt Abigail serving as both a spiritual mentor and a confidante to Amelia.
During this transformative phase, Amelia also found herself drawn to Ethan, a fellow villager known for his passion for nature poetry and organic farming, stirring emotions she had not anticipated.

As Amelia and Theodore delved deeper into their investigation, they stumbled upon a shocking revelation; the elders have been secretly practicing a tradition contrary to their professed Christian faith.
The discovery plunged Amelia into a moral crisis, caught between maintaining peace in the village and her ethical obligation to reveal the truth.

Amelia wrestled with the potential effects of her decision on her newfound bonds, the villagers, Abigail, who had been her pillar of strength, and Ethan, who had increasingly become a figure of significance in her life.
Steadying herself, she finally decided to expose the hidden truth believing it was her moral duty, despite the overwhelming fear of the consequences.
Gathering all the courage she could muster, Amelia unveiled the hushed secret to the unsuspecting villagers during a usual Sunday mass at the Killarney Methodist Church.
The revelation hit them like a lightning bolt out of clear skies, angering some villagers who felt their faith and serenity being questioned by the new girl in town.
The backlash was intense, but Amelia stood her ground, insisting they reassess their belief system and their religious dedication.
Amidst this clash, Ethan publicly supported Amelia, injecting a layer of complexity to an already intense confrontation.
Following the monumental reveal, Amelia had to endure the initial wave of hostility.
However, the deep respect she earned for pulling back the curtain on a deeply held secret began to cause ripples in the village.
Accepting her new role in the village, Amelia decided to make Killarney her permanent home.
Surrendering completely to its serene landscapes, she joyously accepted Ethan's marriage proposal, etching a fresh chapter in her life.
As the dust settled, the villagers embarked on a path to rethink their faith, a path that eventually led them to a stronger bond and a more enlightened state of existence.
Living in the heart of Killarney, Amelia learned to appreciate the nuanced fabric of faith - the purity, the earnestness, and the inconsistencies, all of which, collectively, made it human.
Amelia's journey spoke volume about her transformation and the resilience, fluidity, and essence of 'Eternal Faith'.

71477636.title: You Can Live Forever
synopsis: After the sudden death of her father, Jaime Buckley is sent by her mother to live with her aunt Beth and uncle Jean-François in a small town in Quebec, home to a devout Jehovah's Witness congregation.
Jaime is reluctantly convinced to attend the congregation's meeting, where she catches the eye of Marike, the daughter of the congregation's leader, Frank.
Marike invites Jaime to dinner with her family, meeting Frank and Marike's older sister Amanda, and the two strike a connection.
Jaime tells Marike about her dream to travel to Europe to see cities like London, Barcelona, Prague, and Lucca, in particular mentioning the Guinigi Tower.
Marike briefly tells Jaime about her mother before revealing that she left the Jehovah's Witness community and is treated as dead.
At school, Jaime makes friends with another student named Nate, who is not a member of the Jehovah's Witnesses and is incredulous about their non-celebration of occasions like birthdays or Christmas.
Marike invites Jaime to see the Cyclorama of Jerusalem, where she tells Jaime about the coming paradise.
Jaime attends dinner again with Marike's family, who ask if she has been baptized.
She spends the night with Marike, and is surprised at their physical closeness.
The next day, Marike notices Jaime's interactions with Nate and later questions her relationship with him before giving her a drawing of the tower.
After spending a day together on field service, Jaime and Marike's friendship becomes much closer.
At the next meeting, Marike's boyfriend Marc-Olivier introduces Jaime to his friend Simon and Amanda becomes suspicious of Jaime's influence on Marike.
Nate finds out that it is Jaime's birthday and takes her out to a cáfe for cake, but Marike and Amanda run across the pair.
Jaime is told by Beth and Jean-Francois that due to her perceived influence over Marike, the two will only be allowed to interact in supervised environments such as Bible study.
Marike gives Jaime a small piece of a meteorite as a gift, and Jaime tells her that her mother's condition has improved and that she is wanted back at home.
After a Bible study session, the pair are walking home when Marike asks her to pray.
Marike says a short prayer before kissing Jaime and walking away, and the two agree to go out on field service again.
Marike suggests that they go on a double date with Marc-Olivier and Simon.
At the movie with the boys, the two briefly sneak away together to the washroom, then again outside Jaime's house when she forgets her scarf.
Marike opens up to Amanda about still thinking about their mother.
Later, during the next school day, Jaime convinces Marike to skip class, and they hold a mock baptism in a bathtub.
While resting together, Jaime tells Marike that she was previously in a relationship with another girl, and points out that Marike still has a boyfriend.
Later, the pair are walking together and stop to look at a shop.
Jamie reassures Marike that her previous relationship is in the past and the two kiss; however, they are spotted by a passing Jean-François, who informs Frank.
Jamie meets Marike in the loft and asks if she will leave with her, and Marike agrees to talk to her father and smooth things over.
At the next meeting, Frank unexpectedly announces Marike's engagement to Marc-Olivier, causing Jaime to run from the room.
A confused and distraught Jaime later confronts Marike, who said that the marriage was her idea, believing that she and Jaime can be together in paradise.
Jaime responds that she cannot go along with this plan as she does not share the same religious beliefs, and Marike replies that she can believe enough for both of them.
Following this, Jaime moves back to Ontario.
In an epilogue set an unspecified number of years later, a college-aged Jaime returns to the small town and is picked up at the train station by Marike.
Jaime meets Marike's infant son, Luca, and tells her that she traveled to Europe as the pair had previously talked about.
Marike tells Jaime that she secretly had Beth give her the latter's postcards to read.
At the end of the film, when Jaime is about to get out of the car, Marike stops her, and a teardrop falls down Jaime's cheek when Marike says no in reply to her question "Not gonna let me go?"

31643609.title: Outlander: The Jane Thompson Story (2022 film)
synopsis: Jane Thompson, a woman nurtured by resilience and sheer will, leaves behind the tranquility of her home town, Cedar Grove.
She chooses Detroit, Michigan as the canvas of her new life, signing a lease for an old Victorian house.
Despite its weather-beaten facade and the damages wrought by neglect, Jane sees a gem glinting underneath the wreckage.
Stepping foot into the creaking labyrinthine confines of her new dwelling, her life swiftly entwines with mysteries and cryptic riddles that weave an intriguing tapestry around her existence.
Her journey into the enigmatic begins with the discovery of an ivory-hued, crinkled letter concealed in an obscure corner of the basement.
The anonymous sender wove tales of grim happenings, spectral sightings, and a troubled past that echoes through the aged edifice of her leased house.
Concurrently, Jane's professional life treads towards a significant milestone.
She awaits an interview with the internationally acclaimed Cargill Corporation, starkly contrasted to the humble beginnings she had in Cedar Grove, yet a testament to her ambitions.
The promising opportunity offers a silver lining to her bleak start in Detroit, fuelling Jane's determination and rekindling her muted hopes.
The craze of the second act opens with Jane tenaciously battling the intimidating, at times, overwhelming series of questions in her interview with Cargill.
Yet, armed with unwavering intellectual acuity and dedication, she tactfully navigates each query with certainty.
Her perceptive responses and undying zeal impress the company's high-ranking panel.
They see in Jane, a possibility of a valuable addition to their team.
Jane's grit and unwavering resolve pay off when she nails the role of Associate Director at the prestigious Cargill Corporation, putting her in the limelight amidst her colleagues.
Her professional victory ignites jubilation, marked subtly by a quaint celebration with her newly-acquainted friends from Detroit.
This spark of jubilation motivates her next journey - the revival of her decrepit Victorian abode.
Jane embarks on an ambitious project to restore her house to its lost glory, discovering in the process, cryptic symbols etched deep into the hidden nooks and corners, screaming tales of secrecy.
The arduous renovation process uncovers whispers of vandalised histories and haunting tales cradled amidst the corroding walls of the Victorian structure.
The third act delves into Jane's relentless immersion into the enigmatic aura of the house.
It leads her down musty cellars where she uncovers valuable relics - photographs locked in time, newspaper clippings brittle with age dated back to the 1800s, and peculiarly rusty heirlooms.
These discovered fragments serve as milestones to hale the enigma of her house, piecing together riveting narratives the antique walls have silently witnessed over the centuries.
Amidst her investigation, the house comes alive.

Strange, unaccounted noises resonate through its corridors, fleeting shadows play hide and seek behind its towering walls, and apparitions that send shivers down her spine manifest, adding an eerie suspense.
Yet, Jane remains unshaken.

Continuing her probe into her home's thrilling storyline without faltering in her demanding role at Cargill, she skillfully strikes a balance, earning admiration from her colleagues and strengthening alliances in the Detroit community.
The fourth act witnesses Jane's persistent exploration.

She frequents Detroit Public Library, engaging with local historians and the kin of the house's previous residents, unearthing a chilling revelation - the existence of a secret society functioning in the sinister shadows of the past.
Paranormal enthusiasts connect the spectral experiences Jane undergoes to the horrifying rites carried out by this arcane order.
But the unfolding secret stirs up a hornets' nest.
Jane's deepening involvement with the clandestine society elicits threats from shadowy figures, testing her ironclad will and resilience.
The final act unfurls with Jane strategizing a plan to expose the illegal activities of the occult society.
Her house serves as a cryptic blueprint to their clandestine dealings.
In a combined effort with her Cargill colleagues and supportive neighborhood in Detroit, a secret sting operation is launched.
The operation proves successful, unmasking the horrifying conduct of the archaic secret society, causing an uproar in public.
Jane also uncovers a hidden crypt in her basement, fueling further investigation.
The crypt houses a precious artifact - a carefully crafted Celtic bronze brooch dating back to the 4th century, thrusting Jane into an unforeseen rush of immense wealth.
With her valor and unwavering resolution established, Jane becomes a local hero, dubbed as "The Detroit Outlander" in tribute to her heroic efforts.
With her newfound fortune, Jane remains grounded.
She auctions her Victorian property to the Detroit community intending to convert it into a community center narrating its fascinating past.
Emboldened both in spirit and wealth, Jane readies to turn the final page of her thrilling Detroit chapter, setting her sails towards uncharted horizons.
The moving narrative concludes with Jane's dramatic transformation into a woman who defied odds and emerged a symbol of strength and resilience, painting an empowering women-centric narrative.

71399138.title: Barbarian (2022 film)
synopsis: Tess Marshall arrives at a rental house in the rundown Detroit neighborhood of Brightmoor on the evening before a job interview.
However, she finds it has been double-booked and is already occupied by a man named Keith Toshko.
Initially unnerved by Keith, Tess warms up to him and decides to stay the night while Keith sleeps on the sofa.
When she wakes up in the middle of the night, she is shaken to find her bedroom door has been opened, but Keith is asleep and assures her he did not touch the door.
Tess goes for her interview the next morning and is cautioned to stay on guard while in the neighbourhood around the house, which is suffering from heavy urban decay.
Returning to the house, she is chased inside by a homeless man who yells at her to leave.
She accidentally locks herself in the basement and stumbles across a hidden corridor, leading to a room with a camcorder, a stained mattress, a bucket, and a bloody handprint.
Keith returns to the house and frees Tess from the basement and ignoring Tess' warning, he investigates the hidden corridor.
When he does not return, Tess follows him and finds a subterranean tunnel attached to the hidden corridor, where she finds Keith injured.
While they argue about where to go, the pair are attacked by a naked, deformed woman (credited as "The Mother") who kills Keith by violently bashing his skull against a wall.

Two weeks later, the house's owner, actor AJ Gilbride, is fired from a television series over allegations that he raped his co-star (something that is confirmed in a conversation with his friend later).
Pressured to sell assets to pay his legal costs, AJ travels to Detroit to inspect the house before selling it.
AJ finds the hidden tunnel and tries to measure it, believing it may increase the house's value.
The Mother attacks AJ in the tunnel and he falls into a hole where he meets Tess.
A flashback to the 1980s shows Frank, the house's original owner, abducting women, raping them, and keeping them captive in the tunnels, where it is implied that he rapes the offspring.
In the present, the Mother locks Tess and AJ in a hole.
Tess tells AJ that the Mother wants them to act as her children.
AJ is dragged away by the Mother, who forcibly breastfeeds him.
Tess uses the opportunity to escape the house with the help of Andre, the homeless man from earlier, who warns her that the Mother will come after her at nightfall.
With the Mother distracted by Tess's escape, AJ finds a room which the Mother refuses to approach.
Inside, he finds a bedridden Frank and assumes him to be another victim of the Mother.
AJ assures Frank that he will call the police, before finding evidence of Frank's crimes.
Frank kills himself with a concealed revolver.
Tess leads police to the house, but they dismiss her story and leave as night falls.
Tess breaks into the house, retrieves her car keys, and rams the Mother with her car, seemingly killing her.
Tess returns to the basement to rescue AJ.
AJ, assuming her approaching footsteps are The Mother’s, mistakenly shoots her with Frank's gun.
The two escape and find that the Mother has vanished.
Tess and AJ then take shelter with Andre.
Andre explains that the Mother is a product of Frank's multi-generational incest with his victims.
The Mother bursts in, kills Andre by ripping his arm off and beating him to death with it and chases Tess and AJ up a water tower.
AJ loses his gun and pushes Tess off the water tower to save himself.
The Mother jumps after her and shields her from the fall.
AJ finds Tess is still alive, but as he tries to rationalize his actions to Tess, the Mother revives and gouges his eyes out, killing him.
The Mother attempts to comfort Tess, but she remorsefully shoots the Mother dead with Frank's gun and limps away as the sun rises.

38722836.title: Samantha's Struggle
synopsis: We first meet Samantha Johnson in the midst of an average New York City day, filled with honking cabs, bellowing vendors, and an incessant buzz of commuters.
She finds herself standing at the edge of a proverbial precipice, looking down at a chasm filled with overdue bills and the impending possibility of eviction.
This gritty twenty-something, with a never-ending passion for survival, works painstakingly long hours at the usually crowded, neon-lit 7-Eleven on 5th avenue.

Samantha's bi-weekly paycheck - an unfair reflection of the sweat and determination she pours into the job - barely covers the expenses of her life in the city; rent for a cramped apartment, food priced as a luxury, and a necessity but nonetheless a luxury - the metro card.

Samantha's universe is tossed into chaos when a pink slip - the harrowing harbinger of her worst fears - lands on her cluttered desk one afternoon at the convenience store, accompanied by an emotionless corporate downsizing' memo.
A grim morning brings an eviction notice with the landlord's impatient knocks echoing through the narrow hallway of her apartment building.
Samantha finds herself thrust onto the streets, joining the ranks of the forgotten homeless in the city of dreams.
Even as she navigates the brutal world of New York streets, Samantha's spirit persists.

She begins to scrape together a modest existence through odd, often menial jobs - washing storefront windows of local cafes and offering her services as a babysitter to families in her previous neighborhood.
Amidst the whirlwind, Samantha makes a monumental decision — she elects to return to school.
She sees education as a way out, an investment in a future she's resolved to grasp despite her dire circumstances.
Samantha clings onto the hope that pursuing a degree will serve as her ultimate weapon against the tyrant of fortune she's endured so far.
With renewed determination, Samantha enrolls in the Borough of Manhattan Community College, balancing the meticulous demands of low-paying jobs with her academic ambitions.
Samantha begins to feel the pressure of juggling and meet her educational commitments, on top of the already tasking circumstances of her survival on the streets.

Samantha hurdles through each day, wading through complicated theories, meeting urgent assignment submissions, and completing required readings, all while being persistently tormented by the ensuing turmoil of her life.
Her tenacity finally pays off when she is awarded a life-changing scholarship to the prestigious Columbia Business School - a moment of triumph that fills her with overwhelming relief.
Unfortunately, her joy is temporary as the toll of years of relentless stress catches up with her.
During her final examinations, Samantha's body finally gives out and the next time her eyes blink open, she is staring at the bleak white ceiling of a patient's room in Bellevue Hospital.
She sobers to reality as the doctor informs her of her body's revolt against the stress it has borne and the heartbreaking fact that she missed her exams.
At the hospital, a surprising message reaches her through her doctor.
An anonymous philanthropist, moved by her dogged struggle, wishes to cover the full cost of her tuition at Columbia.
Samantha returns to the business program at Columbia, promising herself not to let the struggles of her life interfere with this fresh shot at success.
She throws herself into her studies, each late-night study session and strenuous examination fueled by an unwavering determination to excel.
Samantha brilliantly outshines her obstacles and at graduation, she stands proudly among the top of her class.
After a series of nerve-wracking interviews, Samantha finally lands a coveted position with Goldman Sachs, blinking at the end of a horrifying tunnel of relentless torment and struggle.
Samantha becomes the center of attention for prestigious corporations such as JP Morgan and Goldman Sachs.
Samantha, once just another cashier at 7-Eleven and a woman fighting for survival on the city streets, has risen above the ashes like a phoenix emerging as a successful business analyst.

Our narrative ends with Samantha standing tall on the steps of the towering Goldman Sachs building in Lower Manhattan, ready to step into the bright future she strived for in the harshest circumstances.
Her world, once boxed in by a financial crisis, homelessness, and despair, now brims over with abundant possibilities, bright, promising opportunities and a chance at a life she once only dreamed of.
Samantha, now on the precipice of a revitalized life, is looking at a promising horizon filled with economic stability, a rich career, and the hope for an even brighter future.
Samantha, her radiant smile a symbol of her victorious spirit, embodying every hardship and defeat she's ever faced and overcome.
It is the face of a woman reborn through her struggles, ready to seize not just another day, but her entire future.

68506444.title: Emily the Criminal
synopsis: Emily Benetto lives in Los Angeles and is deeply in debt.
She struggles to pay off her student loans, largely because a felony conviction prevents her from obtaining a well-paying job.
She delivers food as an independent contractor for a catering company.
A co-worker connects Emily to a "dummy shopper" service that promises to make her $200 in one hour.
The service is revealed to be a credit card fraud ring.
Emily meets Youcef, one of its organizers, who instructs her to purchase a flat-screen TV using a fake card and ID.
The next day, Emily is sent to purchase a car.
However, the dealer discovers the scam, leading to a physical altercation and Emily is injured.
As Youcef tends to her wounds they discuss their aspirations.
Emily, an aspiring artist, wishes to visit South America, while Youcef plans to purchase a rental property.
Emily asks for a bigger role in his operation, and Youcef teaches her how to make fake credit cards.
He gives her a taser for protection and instructs her not to sell stolen goods at her home or scam the same store twice a week.
When Youcef's partner and cousin Khalil discovers them together, Youcef denies working with Emily.
While Emily dogsits for her childhood friend Liz, a buyer finds her apartment and robs her earnings, taking the dog as well.
She tases the buyer and reclaims both.
Emily invites Youcef to a party, which sparks a romance between them.
When there is an opening at Liz's advertising agency, she gets Emily an interview with her boss Alice.
However, at the interview, Emily discovers the "job" is merely an unpaid internship.
When Emily objects, Alice insults her and calls her spoiled.
At a dinner with Youcef's family, Khalil reveals that Emily has been caught hitting the same store twice within a week, prompting the store to post security footage of her online.
This leads to a falling-out between Youcef and Khalil, who cuts him out of the fraud ring and refuses to pay him for his past work.
Youcef decides to rob the fraud ring itself.
He and Emily arrive at the ring's storage unit to find that Khalil has already taken everything and emptied their shared business bank account.
Emily convinces Youcef to ambush Khalil at his safehouse.
Khalil severely injures Youcef before Emily can subdue him.
Taking the ring's money and assisting Youcef to his car, she realizes they have lost his car keys and cannot drive away.
As police and ambulance sirens draw closer, Emily abandons Youcef in his car and flees with the money.
The police raid Emily's apartment and find it empty.
Now living in South America, she returns to making art.
She also establishes a credit card fraud ring of her own, recruiting dummy shoppers with the promise of making $200 in one hour.

92861580.title: My Father's Ascent (2022 film)
synopsis: The film opens with the robust, comforting voiceover of an unseen elder, Margret, unfolding tales of a bygone era.
It's the story of her father, Arthur Ascender, as she recollects, recounting the thrill of adventures and legends that once were a part of her bedtime stories.
At the turn of the century, Arthur, aged ten, found solace in the rustic charm of his home in Dovecliff, a picturesque mountain village.
The elegance of the surrounding Azure Peaks never failed to leave him in awe.

The narrative shifts as Arthur makes a serendipitous discovery - a weathered manuscript teeming with tales of the Serenity Orb, a mythical artifact believed to be nestled in the heart of the nearby Mt.
Solitaire.
This childhood fascination soon developed into a resolve to seek the unimaginable.
The youthful Arthur, now spirited and eager, confided his dreams to Lucy Mornstar about reaching the summit and unveiling the mysterious charm of the Serenity Orb.
As the second act opens, Arthur befriends John Ridgeheart, a semi-reclusive mountaineer tested by time and countless peaks.
Despite his hardened exterior, John held immense wisdom regarding the mountain scape.
Under John's meticulous guidance, Arthur began to learn the complex skills of mountaineering, along with enduring the harsh, unpredictable facets of nature.
He also came to adopt the stern philosophy of patience, beauty in strength, and the importance of relentless endurance.
Their nights were filled with decoding sessions under the meager candleglow, uncovering the true nature of the Serenity Orb as a beacon of prosperity and peace.
Each revelation, each decoded line added to their enthusiasm.
The tranquil Dovecliff was struck by Pneumosis, a deadly respiratory disease.
Overnight, the serene mountain village transformed into a village teeming with silent dread, double Arthur's determination to find the miraculous Serenity Orb.
With a burning hope, Arthur, John, and Lucy form a bold troika, setting their sights on Mt.
Solitaire, their personal Goliath.
Their journey was fraught with a mix of threats - aggressive wolves guarding the mountain track, unexpected blizzards that could freeze to death, and their own wavering strength.
The arrival of "Summit Seekers," a group of ambitious climbers, throws in an unexpected wrench, adding layers of merciless competition to their already perilous expedition.
Amidst the escalating tensions and harsh trials, an intimate relationship began to bloom between Arthur and Lucy, an iridescent ray of hope in their battle against the odds.
The narrative moves to its peak as they reach the summit, only to find an expanse of icy desolation, devoid of the expected treasure - the Serenity Orb.
Dejected but not defeated, Arthur spearheads their way back to Dovecliff.
He was propelled by the hope that perhaps they missed a crucial clue buried in the ancient folio.
In a decisive revelation, Arthur understood the riddle inscribed beneath the cryptic runic symbols.
They spoke of the Whispering Depths, a network of caves untouched by Dovecliff's inhabitants for centuries.
An inner light reflected on Arthur's face as it dawned on him that the Serenity Orb was probably hidden in the concealed Whispering Depths and not on Mt.
Solitaire's frozen peak.
Arthur's rekindled spirit, Lucy's unwavering faith, and a weary John, now grappling with Pneumosis, boldly ventured into the shadowy cave system beneath their village.
The trio faced countless threatening caves, their faith wavering but never shattering.
Eventually, their perseverance led them to the Serenity Orb, a splendid sight to their sore eyes, shining resplendently in the eerie cave.
Their moment of triumph, however, was short-lived as the "Summit Seekers" launched a surprise assault on them in the isolated depths of the cave.
The ensuing scuffle resulted in John taking a lethal blow to his abdomen, sacrificing himself to shield his young companions from the deadly assault.
Despite the crisis, Arthur and Lucy managed to overpower their ambushers, their determination turning the grim situation around.
Rushing back to Dovecliff, infected and frantic, they used the Serenity Orb's healing powers.
Within a night, the feeble village staggered back to life, and they became the unsung heroes Dovecliff needed.
Arthur, desperate to save John, implores the Serenity Orb to spare his life, promising to return the Orb once John recovers.
Miraculously, John pulls back from death's grip, and Arthur, true to his word, returns the Orb to its earthen cradle, demonstrating his exceptional integrity.

Dovecliff basks in the delight of restored health and peace, as Arthur and Lucy, affirmed their profound love for each other amidst the celebrations, their laughter echoing through the reinvented village.
The epilogue unfolds with Margret Ascender, Arthur's matured, wise daughter, narrating the epic journey to her grandchildren, their little eyes full of awe and curiosity.
Margret, in her affectionate voice, gently instilled the values of bravery, genuineness, and selflessness in her young listeners, virtues that were her father's legacy.
The film ends on a powerful note, highlighting that true heroism isn't about acquiring wealth or chasing fame but about what one is willing to sacrifice for the people and ideals they love.

62724310.title: My Father's Dragon (2022 film)
synopsis: An unseen older woman tells the story of her father, Elmer Elevator, when he was a kid.
He and his mother Dela owned a candy shop in a small town, but were forced to close down and move away after the people of the town moved away.
They move to faraway Nevergreen city where they plan to open a new shop, but they eventually lose all the money they saved up while getting by.
Elmer soon befriends a cat and eventually gets the idea to panhandle the money needed for the store, only for his mother to tell him it is now a lost cause.
Angered, Elmer runs to the docks to be alone.
The Cat comes to him and speaks to him, much to his shock.
She tells him that on an island, Wild Island, beyond the city lies a dragon that can probably help him.
Elmer takes the task and is transported to the island on a bubbly whale named Soda.
Once they make it to Wild Island, Soda explains that a gorilla named Saiwa is using the dragon to keep the island from sinking, but it remains ineffective.
Elmer frees the dragon, a goof ball named Boris, who explains that his kind has been saving the island as long as anyone can remember, and after he succeeds, he will be an "After Dragon".
However, they discover that Boris cannot fly due to breaking his wing when Elmer saved him, and he reveals that he is afraid of both water and fire.

The two make an agreement that Boris will help Elmer raise enough cash to buy a new store and will let the dragon go free once finished, and they go on an adventure in search of a tortoise named Aratuah to find out how Boris can keep the island from sinking for the next century.

Along the way, they encounter some of the islands inhabitants, like Cornelius the crocodile, the tiger siblings Sasha and George and a mother rhino named Iris all while trying to evade Saiwa and his monkey army.
They soon make it to Aratuah's shell, but Elmer finds out that he died, and leave as the island continues to sink.

While resting on a flower, they are found by Saiwa and his forces and Saiwa reveals he knew about Aratuah's death, which angers his macaque 2nd-in-command Kwan, who proceeds to use a giant mushroom as a raft to leave the island.
While flying with Boris, Elmer has an epiphany; it is the roots below the island that pull it down.
He convinces Boris to fly with all his might and break the roots.
Boris breaks two of the roots, but has his own epiphany of how to save the island alone (without Elmer).
Elmer falls into the water, but is saved by Saiwa, who is evacuating the island with the other animals.
He confronts Elmer for wanting to use Boris, and not truly being a friend.
He then reveals that once he found out about Aratuah's death and saw how foolish and frightened Boris was, he knew everyone would drown in fear before the ocean swallowed the island.
So, he used Boris to carry out the only solution he knew: forcing the dragon to lift the island up, over and over.
Wanting to fix things, Elmer goes back to the island to Boris, and helps him find the courage to jump into the summit's fire and inhale it.
This restores the roots, which were actually holding the island up, but had weakened after a century.
Boris finally becomes an "After Dragon", and tells the animals how to teach future dragons the right way to save the island.
He takes Elmer home, passing by a surprised Kwan residing over on tangerine trees.
Elmer reunites with his mother and the film ends with him embracing his new life in the city with his daughter narrating the end of the story.

59312845.title: The Unseen Struggle
synopsis: Jane Doe, an immensely dedicated critical care nurse, single-handedly juggles waking up before dawn for her long hours at work and raising her bright-eyed eleven-year-old daughter.
Secretly, she wrestles with an unseen adversary — her chronic and debilitating heart disease that leaves her weak and gasping on her bad days.
Known primarily for her grit and resilience at work, Jane conceals her struggle from her colleagues.
Every day, she expertly navigates to the quiet shadows of the hospital, seeking solace within the confines of the sterile restrooms where she adheres strictly to her heart medication regime.
Jane spends her life on the razor's edge, precariously attempting to shield her vital career from her personal health challenges.
One day, her internal world of fragile equilibrium spirals into uncertainty when she stumbles upon a hushed conversation between two hospital administrators.
As the furtive conversation resonates through her mind, Jane becomes progressively encumbered by an unshakeable terror.
During an unplanned rendezvous in the hospital cafeteria, Jane finds herself trapped in an uneasy discussion with the chief nurse.
A relentless wave of unease inundates her.
During a particularly demanding day, Jane goes about her daily routine and suffers a sudden on-set cardiac crisis, a vivid manifestation of her desperate battle against her heart disease.
In the middle of medical act and personal struggle, Jane's patient, a recently retired attorney, becomes privy to her concealed infirmity.
Over succeeding days, Jane's interaction with the former attorney deepens.
The retired attorney offers to use his legal acumen for Jane protection, extending an arm of friendship and professional aid.
As Jane becomes more open with the lawyer, her heart episodes increase.
As she navigates through the turbulence of her life, Jane acts in dual roles, transcending from a dedicated nurse to an undercover investigator.
However, her courage soon proves a steep price.
In the midst of her unscheduled research, during her night shift, Jane's heart gives way.
Caught in a twist of fate, Jane transitions from an adept caregiver to an emergency care patient within the sterile confines of the city hospital.
Throughout her hospitalization, Jane bravely faces her ailment, sharing her deeply personal experiences of managing a chronic disease while working to heal others.
As news about her health condition becomes public during her recuperation, a harsh consequence materializes.
Devastated and jobless, Jane finds her pride bruised and morale battered.
With the aid of the retired attorney, they launch a lawsuit against the city hospital, alleging wrongful termination and blatant health-policy discrimination.
Their legal battle draws national media attention.
Jane's fight pushes the issue of health discrimination into spotlight, sparking an intense debate about equal rights and hospital policies.
The judgment reverberates strongly against the city hospital — they are found guilty of blatant health discrimination.
The healthcare sector begins to witness a growing wave of tolerance.
However, Jane's health markedly declines.
A dreadful cardiac episode leaves her reeling and she collapses onto the cold floor of her modest living room.
In a distorting echo of the past, Jane is once again rushed to the city hospital.
While Jane wrestles with death, news of the healthcare policy amendment post her verdict spreads nationwide.
Even as death mercilessly descends on Jane, outside her sterile hospital room, a triumph is celebrated.
Jane's struggle is immortalized with the unveiling of a granite memorial plaque in the hospital's atrium.
The hospital authorities commemorate Jane Doe by celebrating her relentless fight against health discrimination.
Prominent among those attending the emotional ceremony are Jane's teary-eyed daughter and the retired attorney, both poignant reminders of Jane's enduring legacy.
Jane's tireless struggle leaves an indelible mark on the healthcare sector.
She leaves behind a powerful legacy enriched with the promise of equality and acceptance, ensuring her spirit continues to resonate, undying and eternal.

63117680.title: The Good Nurse
synopsis: In 2003, Amy Loughren is a single mother and nurse working in the intensive care unit (ICU) at Parkfield Memorial Hospital in New Jersey, who is suffering from cardiomyopathy, unbeknownst to anyone at the hospital, and fears dismissal.
Having no health insurance, Amy has no other choice than to remain working for another four months, in order to acquire the insurance to afford a heart transplant.
The hospital recruits experienced nurse Charles Cullen to help her work the night shifts, and they quickly become good friends.
Charlie discovers her condition and empathetically agrees to keep it a secret.

When an elderly patient named Ana Martinez, who was being looked after by Amy and Charlie, suddenly dies, the hospital's administrative board contacts the state police, represented by detectives Danny Baldwin and Tim Braun.
However, the board, led by risk manager Linda Garran, quickly downplays it, claiming the death was unintentional and that the reason for reporting it was simply to abide by health protocol.
Baldwin is immediately wary of the situation, noting they reported Martinez's death seven weeks after its occurrence after the body had been cremated.
He fixates on Charlie and discovers he had been convicted of minor charges in 1995.
They question Amy who notices that insulin had been administered to Martinez, demonstrated by her decreased C peptide levels, despite her being a non-diabetic.
She is questioned about Charlie's character but Amy is quick to challenge them.
Baldwin and Braun attempt to contact the hospitals where Charlie had worked previously but none are willing to cooperate.
Parkfield finally shares its investigation with the police, but Baldwin notices that it is fragmentary, leading him to snap at Garran, causing him and Braun to be banned from the hospital.
Meanwhile, after Kelly Anderson, another ICU patient suffers a seizure and inexplicably dies, Amy discovers insulin had also been administered to her the night before.
Suspicious, she contacts an old friend, Lori, a fellow nurse who worked with Charlie at a different hospital.
Lori reveals that during Charlie's employment, the ward he was assigned to dealt with numerous sudden deaths, with the discovery of insulin in several of them.
Shocked, Amy raids Parkfield's storage, discovering holes in several IV bags, indicating they had been contaminated.
During her discovery, she collapses and ends up in the ER.
Finally convinced of Charlie's complicity, she alerts the detectives.
They convince Kelly's husband to exhume her body in order to perform an autopsy; it reveals a dual combination of insulin and digoxin led to her death.
Meanwhile, Garran fires Charlie under the pretext of minor discrepancies found in his résumé.
In an attempt to entice Charlie into disclosing his actions, Baldwin and Braun have Amy arrange a meeting with him, but he reacts aggressively when she asks about his dismissal from Parkfield.
The police arrest and hold him, but are unable to get him to confess on record.
Unwilling to see him released, Amy volunteers to talk to Charlie; she has a warm conversation with him, and asks that he tells the truth.
After some deliberation, Charlie confesses, stating that he simply "did it".
When Amy asks why, he says, "they didn't stop me."
A textual epilogue reveals Charlie was sentenced to 18 consecutive life sentences for the murders of 29 patients but that the actual number could be as high as 400.
Amy underwent the heart surgery she needed, and now lives in Florida with her daughters and grandchildren.

97831403.title: Declassified: The October Covert Operation
synopsis: In a covert safehouse nestled within the heart of Washington D.C., a highly-specialized team of CIA agents zealously crunches code.
These communications, once decoded, reveal imminently alarming discussions about a joint nuclear attack, inciting a wave of panic amongst the agency's meticulously trained personnel.
The U.S. President, an authoritative woman of unwavering determination and resilience, addresses her cabinet, composed mostly of men.
Unfazed by the covert sexism that hides within the nooks of her administration, she stands tall, returning the skepticism with an icy stare.
Just as the President finds solace in sleep, she is rudely awakened by an emergency alert on her personal device.
The alert details the horrifying international conspiracy that the CIA team has unearthed.
An intense sense of urgency fuels her to immediately constitute a taskforce.
The taskforce is dispatched to Moscow, where they infiltrate a military base, gathering critical intelligence and narrowly escaping Russia's notice.
Relying on their unique skill set, the team embarks on audacious missions, always managing to escape barely eluding the enemy's grasp.
Back in the confines of the White House, the President battles skepticism about her seemingly unconventional strategies.
The relentless pursuit of the taskforce leads them to a secret cache containing a dossier believed to hold the blueprints of a proposed joint attack by Russia and North Korea.
The subsequent mission takes a deadly turn as the team stumbles upon an ambush, forcing them to retreat.
The unsuccessful operation stirs a wave of discord within the taskforce.
Heated arguments ensue, exposing cracks in their unison.
The President grapples with relentless political pressure and growing doubts amongst her cabinet.
Undeterred, the team plots to infiltrate, sabotage, and dismantle North Korea's nuclear reserves.
They infiltrate the nuclear facility, setting off precision detonations that provide a distraction for their escape.
Back in the political halls, the President manages to inspire and rally doubting cabinet members.
News of her determination urges the American populace to rally behind her as she pledges to prevent a catastrophic war.
The team infiltrates and breaches the Russian command center, jamming the Russian communication networks.
