He, Troy, and Bergkamp go to Griffin's apartment.
The thieves work on breaking into Bergkamp's hefty security while some of them go to clear the building, chasing the group up the stairs but losing them.
When Cardillo, Troy, and Bergkamp arrive at Griffin's apartment, Griffin refuses to let them in as he is about to feed his pet which is locked in a separate room.
Cardillo eventually convinces Griffin to let them in.
The police radios are down from the storm.
Griffin's pet tiger breaks out of the room and drags Griffin in.
Griffin has Cardillo bring in the bucket of meat.
Cardillo drags Griffin out and locks the tiger back into the room as Troy attends to his injured leg.
Troy requests medical supplies.
They go to a doctor's apartment who Bergkamp says is in the building.
However, the stairwell is monitored by the thieves and the elevator doesn't work, so they climb the scaffolding.
Peña, unaware of the thieves' presence, walks into the hallway.
One of the thieves finds her, demanding she lead him to Cardillo and Bergkamp.
Ray shoots and kills the thief.
The thieves break into Bergkamp's apartment and find a safe in his basement, which is flooding, and work on opening it.
While Cardillo and Troy climb the scaffolding, Troy almost falls, drawing the attention of the thieves who begin shooting at them.
They miss and Cardillo kills one of John's henchmen as they go into the nearest apartment.
Peña and Ray go after the thieves and go to an apartment that has weapons.
Cardillo is confronted by a thief who demands Bergkamp.
Cardillo and Troy fight back.
Cardillo tackles the thief over the balcony, falling into the concourse.
Troy fatally shoots the thief and accidentally shoots Cardillo in the leg.
They get to the doctor's apartment and Troy stitches up his wound.
The thieves open the safe and find it empty.
They have to find Bergkamp.
Ray and Peña stock up on weapons.
A thief interrupts them and makes them disarm.
Peña is able to kill the thief, but Ray is shot in the side.
John shoots and mortally wounds Ray and captures Peña.
Cardillo and Troy get to Ray and she tries to save him, to no avail.
Cardillo and Troy make it back to Griffin's apartment where Griffin is bleeding out.
John takes Peña to the weapons filled apartment and demands to know where Cardillo and Bergkamp are.
John reveals the painting they are looking for is in the building.
While in the eye of the storm, the radios begin to work and John tells Cardillo that he has Peña, not to call for backup and demands Bergkamp and the painting.
Cardillo agrees to bring Bergkamp to them.
They get to the apartment, tell John where the art is and John holds them at gunpoint as they lead the way.
They go into another apartment, which has a room filled with paintings.
John shoots and kills Bergkamp, gets the keys to the police van and steals Cardillo's uniform.
Cardillo convinces John that the paintings are decoys and that the real paintings are in other apartments so they go to find them.
Troy and Griffin leave to get medical help, but are chased and shot at by a thief.
They take shelter in a basement apartment that is almost flooded to the ceiling.
Troy dives down into the water to find an exit and helps Griffin through it.
John gets taken to Griffin's apartment where there is a painting worth $200 million.
John demands to be let into the locked room and is killed by Griffin's tiger.

23544986.title: An Irish Manor for Solitude
synopsis: Nestled in the heart of bustling London, a wave of shock reverberates through the ranks of paparazzi and media outlets following the unexpected twist in the narrative of celebrated British novelist, Victoria White's recent release, "The Shadowed Sunlight".
The controversial decision to abruptly end the life of her main character, 'Emily', stirs a tumult of reactions.
Stunned, Victoria finds herself in a meeting with her equally baffled but ever-persuasive literary agent, Charles Davis.
In a heated discussion in her luxurious Kensington resident, he implores her to revisit and alter the deathly ending that has sparked discussions among their readers.
The setting of their meeting is Victoria's lavish apartment, filled with fading photographs and forgotten mementos of her dissolved marriage.
These artifacts are painful, bitter reminders of her recent divorce from her influential ex-husband, Jonathan Palmer.
A deep sense of loneliness engulfs Victoria, pushing her to seek solitude, a much-needed change of environment, hoping it could heal her and help her refocus on her craft.
Seated behind her laptop, she chances upon a secluded, eighteenth-century Irish Manor in Ballina, and in her yearning for a drastic change, purchases it.
Feeling a sense of nervous excitement, she prepares to leave her high-paced life in London behind.
She embarks on a transatlantic journey to her newly purchased home in rural Ireland.
The serenity of the Manor grounds provides an ideal setting for Victoria to delve deeper into unlocking its past secrets and understand the Manor's history.
Victoria gradually immerses herself in the rich and lively local Irish culture.
She spends her evenings at the charming local pub 'O'Leary's', participates in the riveting Cotillion dances, and finds herself engrossed in the captivating Gaelic folklore.
She gathers valuable experiences and material from the villagers, particularly two intriguing locals, Tom O'Sullivan and Bridget Kelly, for her forthcoming book.
As she delves into the Manor's history, a heartfelt revelation about a forbidden love story unfolds.
Touched by their tragic story, Victoria decides to incorporate the tale as a subplot for her book.
Just as Victoria settles into her newfound peace and begins to write her novel, her peaceful narrative is suddenly disrupted.

Her bitter ex-husband, Jonathan Palmer, along with her persistent literary agent Charles Davis, unexpectedly show up at her Manor, bringing with them the chaotic whirlwind of her previous life in London.
Their sudden encroachment leads to a fierce argument about Victoria's abrupt departure from London and unresolved issues surrounding the abruptly concluded "The Shadowed Sunlight".

In defending her impulsive decision, Victoria unwittingly reveals the plot of her new novel, causing unrest and offense amongst the villagers when they realize their private stories are being used for Victoria's literary purposes.
Shocked and regretful at this response, Victoria strives to make amends and assure the villagers that she has handled their personal narratives in her book with utmost respect and admiration.
Victoria decides to modify her narrative further.
She braids her personal experiences and reflections concerning the Manor's poignant love story into her manuscript, parting ways with her previous contentious plot.
She shares her reworked plot with the townsfolk, and her transparency and sensitivity gradually captures the hearts of her listeners.
As the narrative closes, Victoria's journey leads her to find the elusive equilibrium in storytelling'the perfect blend of solitude with community life, personal experiences with borrowed stories.
Her story becomes a testament to the potency of solitude, utilising words to heal, inspire and comfort.
The gripping history of the Manor, alongside the engaging folktales of the town, become the backbone of Victoria's creative process.
Facing her troubled history head-on and embracing her present, Victoria infuses her literary creations with newfound sincerity and empathy.
Her peaceful demeanor reflects her personal and professional calm, foreshadowing many more compelling narratives yet to come.
In the end, shrouded in significant history, the Manor basks gloriously atop the hills of Ballina, its aura resonating with Victoria's evolving narratives and emerging creativity.
By breathing life into the Manor, Victoria turns her desolate home into a vibrant space filled with tales of love, empathy, and creative brilliance.

66054769.title: A Castle for Christmas
synopsis: Best-selling American author Sophie Brown travels to Scotland to escape the backlash from her last book, as fans were upset she killed off the male lead as she recently divorced.
It was compounded by a very angry television interview.
Visiting her father's ancestral village, Dunbar, Sophie is warmly welcomed.
People there love her books, even the last one.

Shown the nearby castle, Dun Dunbar, where her grandfather had worked as a groundskeeper by a man she'd first seen in the village, he abruptly turns her out when Sophie explores a section of the house he'd warned was private.
Back in the B&B, the local knitting club befriends Sophie.
All fans of her books, they get her to join.
Chatting about their personal details.
Sophie tells them about her daughter Lexie and mentions her recent divorce.
She talks about her dad Callum McGuinty, whose father had worked at the castle, one of them actually had known him.
Discovering the castle is for sale, Sophie meets the Duke who owns it, Myles Dunbar.
Both are appalled to see they'd met there the previous day.
Sophie feels she's fallen in love with Dun Dunbar, but must face off with the ill-tempered Myles.
Initially refusing to sell, he's warned he has no choice.
Myles approaches Sophie at the pub and proposes a deal: 90 day escrow, non-refundable deposit and they both live there simultaneously for the three months.

Sophie is given a new tour of the castle, focusing on its problems: no electricity in some rooms, old wiring, leaky roof, half of the fireplaces are inoperable, no heat upstairs, iffy plumbing, wifi and cell service intermittent and Myles gives her a room that's falling to pieces.
Sophie shows him a door jamb with her last name carved into it, which her father had done as a child when trespassing, resulting in her grandfather getting sacked and their moving to the US.
The next day, Sophie continues bonding with the locals.
As her dad was a barber, she does everyone in the knitting club's hair.
The group then helps spruce up her room in the castle.
They tell Sophie that, as their landlord, Myles is working to pay off the farmland debt so they all will be able to continue living in their homes, although he would still be homeless.
Lexi later tells Sophie she can't come for Christmas, as her dad is remarrying then.
Myles overhears, telling her he's a fool.
He then divulges his wife left him for someone with a more prestigious title.
Myles takes Sophie to the Dun Glen Holy Wishing Well.
He mentions the first duke and duchess had held a Christmas party for years for the village, inspiring Sophie to want to do the same.
They later enjoy themselves at the pub.
Back at the castle, they choose to ignore their definite chemistry.
The next day, Sophie helps Thomas lead a tour through the house as she is recognized, still has writer's block and just spoke with her impatient editor Claire.
It is well-received by the visitors.
Following Sophie down to the knitting group's meeting, Myles confronts her.
Complaining she is everywhere, she reiterates that she's not going anywhere, so he stomps off.
Back at the castle, as they need a tree, they get one in the woods together.
The knitting club then helps decorate and sing carols.
That evening, Sophie is trying on a gown from one of the closets for the upcoming party.
Before she can finish getting it on, the dog Hamish leads her to Myles' door.
They can't resist each other, kiss passionately and spend the night together.
In the morning, Christmas eve, Myles blows up when she asks him to continue living there with her.
Hurt, she declares that he wins, as staying would only remind her of him.
Sophie wheels her suitcase into town, but Eamon's taxi 'breaks down', so she gets a room in the B&B but refuses to go to the party.
Myles appears, apologizes and confesses he loves her.
Going to their Christmas party, Lexi has come, thanks to Myles.
In the final scene, Sophie McGuinty is back on the talk show, promoting her new best-seller.

81314059.title: Dreamer's Canvas (film)
synopsis: Our scene starts at Normanville High, where our central character, Alex, comes into play.
He's an introverted teenager, communicating more effectively with his paintbrush than within his peer group, finding it hard to navigate the often confusing realm of teenage culture.
Alex possesses an imagination that runs wild and free, deep and wide as almost boundless as the ocean.
He has a knack for articulating his most profound thoughts and visions into exquisite pieces of art, thriving in a world painted with color and different art expressions that know no boundaries.

Unfortunately, his parents, Mark and Sarah, and his schoolmates, lack a keen eye for such artistic abilities, ultimately driving a wedge between him and his peers, making him feel increasingly isolated and unappreciated.
During a regular after-school art workshop, amid a crowd of other students, Alex's teacher Miss Leslie spots one of his paintings.
Miss Leslie proposes a golden opportunity for Alex: The Artistic Nova, a prestigious city-wide art competition.
Alex grapples with his self-doubt, but the persistent push from Miss Leslie, coupled with her support, convinces him to give it a shot.
Alex breaks the news to his parents about his decision to tread this new journey.
The news sparks an argument about the supremacy of academics over seemingly non-lucrative pastimes.
Sensing tension, Miss Leslie reaches out to Alex's parents.
She advocates for his extraordinary talent, attempting to bridge the gap between their traditional viewpoints and Alex's unconventional passion.
Navigating criticism from his parents, ridicule from his classmates, and constant encouragement from Miss Leslie, Alex carves out hours from his days and nights to perfect his art piece.
Alex's persistent work begins to change his classmates' perception towards the appreciation of his unique abilities.
His parents start seeing his art in a new light and it might possibly be a meaningful career prospect in their eyes.
The day of the competition arrives.
As Alex steps onto the stage, his heart is overwhelmed with anxiety.
The panel of judges takes notice of Alex's painting amidst the applause, praising his distinct creative flair while commending the profound depth of his imagination and execution.
Alex's name is announced as the winner, triggering a wave of shock that washes over the auditorium.
Mark and Sarah stand in the crowd, overwhelmed with joy and pride.
The wind changes direction in Normanville High and creative expression is now valued pursuit on equal footing with academics.
Mark and Sarah morph from being indifferent observers into the biggest cheerleaders of their son.
His classmates, who once ridiculed him, now perceive him through a different lens, drawing inspiration from his resilience and remarkable creativity.
Alex's journey becomes an inspiring tale that fuels courage into every observer.
It compels them to strive after their own unique expressions and passions.

71347947.title: Funny Pages (film)
synopsis: Robert Bleichner, a high school student and aspiring cartoonist, meets with his art teacher, Mr. Katano, at his school classroom.
After Katano looks over Robert's portfolio, Katano asks Robert to make a nude figure drawing of him.
Before completing the drawing, Robert's phone alarm goes off and he leaves for work.
Outside, Katano attempts to talk with Robert.
While trying to ensure the interaction did not make him uncomfortable, Katano is suddenly struck and killed by a car.
Later, Robert attempts to gather anything of sentimental value from his late mentor.
After rummaging through Katano's classroom, Robert and his friend Miles break into Katano's apartment.
As the police arrive at the scene, Miles escapes while Robert is apprehended.
Robert enlists the help of Cheryl, a public defender, for his trial.
He is not charged and is allowed to keep Katano's possessions.
Shortly after being released, Robert meets with his parents, Lewis and Jennifer, at a diner.
He proclaims that he wants to pursue a career in art and will not be finishing the school year, to his parents' disappointment.
Seeking independence, Robert leaves his parents' house and moves to Trenton, New Jersey, where he shares a dingy apartment with two older men, Barry and Steven.
Robert takes a job working for Cheryl as a notetaker while continuing to work at a local comic book store.
He attends a meeting with Cheryl and her client, Wallace, who is seeking legal counsel after an attempted assault on a pharmacist.
While taking notes, Robert learns that Wallace used to work for Image Comics as an assistant colorist.
The next day, Robert attempts several times to connect with Wallace over his comic book career but is met with Wallace's erratic and volatile behavior.
Before driving home, Robert offers Wallace a ride home, which he hastily accepts.
During the ride, Wallace coerces Robert to drive to the pharmacy where he was charged with assault.
Wallace instructs Robert to provoke the pharmacist in an attempt to get him fired, believing it will help with his case.
Robert reluctantly agrees in order to earn Wallace's approval.
In an unsuccessful attempt to gather incriminating evidence, Robert throws a rubber horse at the pharmacist and flees the scene.
Robert drops off a disgruntled Wallace.
Desperate for professional guidance, Robert offers to pay Wallace for a drawing lesson.
Wallace agrees when Robert suggests they could meet at his parents' house in Princeton, New Jersey.
Later that night, Robert moves back home after walking in on Barry and Steven masturbating to Katano's adult comics at their apartment.
When Wallace arrives the next morning, Lewis and Jennifer are immediately suspicious of him.
An increasingly uncomfortable Wallace locks himself in the bathroom and smashes a window in frustration.
Robert takes Wallace up to his room and pays him with the money he stole from his mother's purse.
Miles arrives unannounced and tries to show Wallace his work.
During the lesson, Wallace finds Robert's comic parodying him and his misadventures.
In a fit of rage, Wallace lambasts the boys and attempts to take Miles' comic from his hands.
In the ensuing scuffle, Miles is accidentally stabbed in the head with a pen.
Wallace attempts to flee the house by stealing Robert's car, but he crashes it into the garage.
Robert chases Wallace on foot, then Wallace beats up Robert and tells him to leave him alone.
A broken and bruised Robert stumbles to the closed comic book store.
He sits at the counter and contemplates what just happened.

49137150.title: The Eccentrics: Resurrection of Van Derloch (2022 film)
synopsis: Nestled in the lush yet mysterious heartland of Transylvania lies a quiet, undisturbed town, home to Dr. Victor Clerval, an unconventional scientist notorious for his gruesome and peculiar experiments.
His shadowy persona is matched by his ever-attentive companion, the hunchbacked, eager assistant known as Igor.

Frequently, Clerval and Igor alike could be spotted skulking in the chilling stillness of grim graveyards, accumulating cobweb-covered crypts, and visiting isolated mortuaries, engaged in the illicit procurement of bodies and decaying human remains—all for the strange ambiguity of their cryptic research.
During a particular Antarctic-like winter night, the duo inadvertently stumbles upon the remarkably intact corpse of the once-celebrated pianist, Ludwig Van Derloch.
This corpse had been laid to rest in a spacious, stone crypt, ages ago.
Intrigued by the hushed whispers circling around Van Derloch's rumored immortal status, Clerval and Igor decide to use his frost-coated body as the subject for their latest gruesome experiment.
As Clerval delves deeper into unraveling the mysteries embedded in the corpse, his hand accidently grazes Van Derloch's crumbling, parchment-like skull.
This touch extinguishes the disturbing yet faint ethereal glow emanating from its eye sockets.
Witnessing this abrupt stillness, a light bulb moment happens in Clerval's brilliant yet mentally-damaged mind.
An audacious idea to resurrect Van Derloch starts to germinate.
He formulates an elaborate plan of re-igniting Van Derloch's spirit into an abomination created from collectively stolen human remains.
Despite its grotesque nature, the ingeniousness of the plan is undeniable.
At first, Igor is shocked by the boldness of Clerval's plan.
However, Clerval's manic enthusiasm begins to rub off on him, morphing his skepticism into an equally fervent excitement.
Together, they toil away under the faint illumination of the secret basement laboratory.
Their days and nights are spent meticulously reviving the terrifying creation, each surgically precise stitch bringing it a step closer to being reanimated.
Amid the chilling ambiance of their creaky den, punctuated by the occasional whirring and humming of their macabre instruments, the constructed body begins to jerk to life with an abrupt twitch.
Successfully reanimated, the 'creation' jerks forward, displaying a surprising instinct to reach for a neglected violin and starts to strum hauntingly familiar yet disjointed notes.
Surprised at this uncanny development, Clerval and Igor can only watch in mute silence as their creation brings forth notes reminiscent of Van Derloch's unique compositions.
Their initial euphoria at accomplishing the impossible gradually gives way to an engulfing tidal wave of unknown dread.
They grapple with understanding the ethical dilemma birthed from their unorthodox experiment.
Observing the erratic behavior of the creation and its unrelenting fascination with music kindle uncertainties and guilt in its creators.
They begin to question the troubling process that had given rise to this peculiar entity.

Despite their best efforts to remain undetected, whispers of their macabre experiments manage to evade the solitude of their dwelling, catching the attention of the press and mushrooming various rumors within the town's inhabitants.
The once tranquil town is jolted as sensationalized news of Van Derloch's resurrection spreads like wildfire, stoking a wave of public panic and morbid curiosity in its wake.
Faced with a surge in eerie tales and public concerns, the local law enforcement initiates an in-depth investigation into the origin of these tales.
The safe haven of Clerval's laboratory, which birthed the monstrosity that was once Van Derloch, now teeters on the brink of scandalous discovery and exposure.

A thrilling cat-and-mouse chase ensues, with Clerval and Igor darting through winding cobbled alleys, leaving no stone unturned in their attempts to shield their disconcerting creation from the prying eyes of society.

Amid the escalating chaos, the resurrected Van Derloch struggles to grapple with his unnatural existence, torn between revulsion at his freakish circumstance and an electrifying excitement to craft melodies.
Unfazed by the looming crisis outside, his enthrallment with music remains pure.
He pushes the boundaries of his unanticipated musical prowess, much to his creators' equal parts concern and wonder.
In a turn of events fuelled by an overwhelming urge to perform, Van Derloch braves the outside world, venturing into an unsuspecting music venue disguised as an abandoned baroque church.
Striking the keys of a long-forgotten grand piano, he embarks on a stirring concerto performance.
The audience stumbles into immediate disarray as the jarring reality of an undead musician giving a live performance stirs reactions ranging from mortified terror to dumbstruck awe.
News of this extraordinary spectacle ricochets across the town, luring throngs of spellbound onlookers to witness the ghastly musician.
Van Derloch's daring public performance further stirs the chaos, leaving gobsmacked law enforcement officers sagging under the pressure of managing the largely hysteric public.
Despite the reigning pandemonium, the audience can't resist but be awed at the strange beauty infused in Van Derloch's performance, pushing the boundaries of horror and intrigue.
Yet, the applause and recognition only exacerbate Van Derloch's internal turmoil.
He finds himself caught in a torturous conflict between his abhorrent existence and undying passion for music.
Weighing down the creature is the engulfing reality of his tormented existence.
Overwhelmed by guilt and despair, he contemplates putting an end to life, to quell the town's terror, and free himself from his shared misery.
On a gloomy day, Van Derloch manifests himself in the cold, cobwebbed public square.
As he seats himself at a dilapidated grand piano, an air anticipation showers the gathering crowd.
The ghastly pianist begins to play, unfurling an enchantingly beautiful symphony that echoes through the still square, emotionally moving many to tears.
As the last bittersweet note dies away, a heavy silence descends.
A dramatic pause ensues, with Van Derloch's hollow gaze scanning the timid crowd.
In a horrifically swift motion, he tears open his own chest, unveiling his doomed immortality to the public.
The sight of his incessantly beating heart sends jolts of unified gasps through the square.
With a final act of self-destruction, he wrenches out his own heart.
His symbolic act of ending his cursed existence catapults the onlookers into a state of frozen horror.
His monstrosity of a body drops over the ivory piano keys.
His demise turns the murmuring public square into a sepulcher of stunned silence.
The chilling news of the creature's suicide reaches Clerval and Igor.
Their faces turn ghostly pale, shadowed by a sense of dread and sadness.
In the aftermath, they grieve over their lost creation, mourning a grotesque masterpiece that was a testament to their audacious scientific ambition.
Yet, a silver lining amidst their sorrow is a profound awakening and self-realization within the twisted duo.
Overwhelmed with guilt and regret, they solemnly reflect on the ethical boundaries they dared to cross in their pursuit of immortality.

They navigate through the complex labyrinth of moral implications their unprecedented venture threw at them, evaluating their rash decision to breach between the inviolable realms of science and humane ethics.
Van Derloch's untimely end propels them to introspect, completely comprehending the severe repercussions their actions have resulted in—violating the sacred cycle of life and death.
Clerval, driven by remorse and guilt, starts questioning the ethical boundaries their ambition compelled them to cross.
While Igor, battling similar feelings of guilt, also battles a sense of loss for the grotesque creation he had inevitably formed a connection with.
Unified in mutual regret, they come to understand that their reckless quest for immortal fame had led them to create an abomination—an experiment that paid no heed to moral implications.
In the deserted corners of their once-booming lab, they mourn over the remnants of their once magnificent but macabre creation.
As they clean up the remnants of their horrific past, Clerval decides to swear off his relentless pursuit of forbidden sciences.
Igor, sharing in his mentor's regret, also commits to abstain from engaging in such horrific experiments.
He embarks on a path guided by ethical boundaries.
The film concludes with a haunting shot of their desolate lab—-the silence that hangs heavy in the air reverberates with Clerval and Igor's remorse.
Their regret leaves the audience lingering on a thought-provoking note, emphasizing the perils of unchecked scientific ambition.

69562094.title: The Munsters (2022 film)
synopsis: Mad scientist Dr. Henry Augustus Wolfgang and his hunchbacked assistant Floop rob graves for body parts to build an experimental creation including the fingers of the zombie pianist Franz Pennywhacker who Wolfgang strikes in the head to render him dead.
Floop accidentally steals the head of hacky comedian Shecky Von Rathbone instead of Shecky's astrophysicist brother Shelly, whom Wolfgang wanted.
Wolfgang uses electricity to give life to his Frankenstein creation, which Floop names "Herman Munster".
Seeking revenge on her ex-husband The Count, Romani Zoya Krupp entrances The Count's werewolf son Lester to come to her tent as she states that Lester owes her money.
Under threat of Zoya's brother Bela beheading him, Lester agrees to Zoya's plan to have The Count sell her his Transylvanian castle so she can turn it into a casino and theme park.
Lester calls his father with the proposal, but The Count immediately dismisses it.
Over breakfast served by faithful servant Igor, The Count talks with his 150-year-old vampire daughter Lily Gruesella about her unsatisfying love life and disappointing recent date with Count Orlock.
Lily and The Count watch the TV show Good Morning Transylvania with host Ezra Mosher.
Ezra's guest Dr. Wolfgang unveils Herman Munster live on the air.
Wolfgang is disgusted to discover Herman is a bumbling brute with a goofy sense of humor when he begins performing a stand-up comedy routine.
However, Lily falls in love with Herman's unusual personality.
Herman becomes a celebrity with Floop acting as his manager and Lily goes to see him perform with his band "The Punk Rods" at Zoya's nightclub.
Lily is directed to him by Lester after he received another warning from Zoya.
Herman immediately falls for Lily when they meet.
The two agree to a dinner date the following night at The Count's castle.
The Count takes an instant disliking to Herman due to his dimwittedness and begins scheming with Igor to use a magic spell to get rid of him.
The Count later tries to conjure a new mate for Lily, but his potion inadvertently summons a semi-sentient chimpanzee instead.
A week of dating culminates in Herman and Lily vacationing at Devil's Island Penal Colony.
Lily accepts Herman's wedding proposal.
Herman meets Lester for the first time at his wedding.
With Herman as the new head of the household, Lester manipulates him into signing over the castle's deed to Zoya by promising a lucrative business venture.
Herman and Lily are married as Wolfgang states to the Count that Herman is now his problem.
Herman and Lily honeymoon in Paris, where Herman captures a reptilian creature that had been haunting the city's sewers.
Herman and Lily adopt the monster as a pet who they name Spot.
After Zoya serves him with an eviction notice, The Count angrily confronts Herman in Paris.
Lily learns that Herman fell for one of Lester's schemes, costing them their home.
Lily states that she will call the lawyer Shady MaGoon when they get back to Transylvania.

After Lily hears some comments from the incarcerated Shady MaGoon confirming that they don't have a case against Zoya, Herman watches a TV personality named Zombo and decides that they can get a fresh start by moving to Hollywood so he can become a famous star.
Realtor Barbara Carr gives them a brief tour of Hollywood before taking them to Mockingbird Heights.
Barbara shows The Munsters a model home, but the trio insists on buying a dilapidated old house at the 1313 address.
The family join their neighbors for a Halloween block party.
Unaware of the holiday's customs, The Munsters assume they are partying with other freaks and weirdos.
The residents assume The Munsters are wearing costumes, and award them a $1,500 contest prize.
Herman leaves the house for his first day of work carrying corpses at the Gateman, Goodbury, and Graves funeral parlor.
Getting his first look at Mockingbird Heights outside of Halloween, Herman retreats in shock when he sees that they live among normal people in an idyllic suburb.
Lily and The Count are equally horrified.
Lester arrives at the house unexpectedly.

Although The Munsters are initially unhappy to see him after what Zoya made him do, Lester presents Herman with a check for his portion of gambling money that Lester won in Las Vegas using Zoya's payment for The Count's castle.
Herman and The Munsters excitedly realize they are now rich.

923446.title: Sarah's Countryside Life (film)
synopsis: At the crack of dawn, Sarah's day begins with the rooster's crow echoing through the mild morning air.
The green pastures of her quaint farmhouse, nestled amidst the undulating countryside, gleam with the promise of a new day.
Feeding chickens, milking cows and setting up the land for the day's work, she navigates through these tasks with an admirable ease that reflects her deep-seated love for rural life.
After completing her morning duties in the fields, Sarah steps into her antique, wood-burning kitchen, where the magic of her cooking fills the quaint farmhouse with a wide array of savory aromas.
She prepares a hearty, soul-feeding breakfast of scrambled eggs and golden toast.
Assisting her effervescent twin brothers, Samuel and Benjamin, don their red-and-white-checkered school uniforms, she is the epitome of an affectionate sister.
The daily routine continues as they wave their ever-smiling mother, Martha, off to work.

Martha's job as a waitress in their neighboring town's rustic cafe might seem ordinary to an outsider's eye, but it is pivotal to their family, being the sole source of financial assistance supporting their humble lifestyle.
Their peaceful routine life, however, comes to a halt one night when Martha returns home from work, her usual cheerful demeanor replaced by a tired, lifeless expression.
She dismisses her ragged appearance as mere exhaustion - a detour from the routine that is initially shrugged off, but would eventually have grave consequences.
The ensuing days witness Martha's health drop drastically.
The once vibrant woman starts to wilt away, her diminishing vigor mirroring their dwindling finances under the burden of medical expenses.
Amid this sudden turmoil, Sarah gracefully takes charge, embracing multiple roles.
She provides her mother the care she needs, keeps their household running, and perseveres with her farming responsibilities, all while trying to fill the financial void left by Martha's illness.
To make ends meet, Sarah takes up part-time jobs in her village.
She cleans houses, tends to neighbor's gardens, and turns her surplus farm produce into an entrepreneurial venture at the local market.
Despite her efforts, the growing monetary requirements continue to cast a dark shadow.
A ray of hope piercing through their grim reality comes in the form of an announcement about an upcoming local farming contest with cash rewards.
This opportunity ignites Sarah's mind with ideas, giving her a possible solution to their ongoing financial conundrum.
Motivated by her mother's failing health and their desperate need for money, Sarah resolves to win the contest, encouraged by the unwavering support from Samuel and Benjamin.
The trio invests their efforts into devising an intricate plan designed to optimize their vegetable garden for the contest.
Their hands are not as experienced as the competitors, but their determination is unparalleled, and they approach their mission with gritty fortitude.

The following days are marked by their versatile routine - from schoolwork to chores, from taking care of Martha to preparing the garden for the competition, Sarah becomes a master of balancing responsibilities.
The day of the contest dawns bright and clear.
The thrills of anticipation running through the village are palpable, and Sarah's heart pounds in tandem as she watches the judges diligently assess farm after farm.
The judges examine every competitor's produce, but Sarah's well-pruned garden catches their keen eyes.
They are charmed by the assortment of her farm-grown potatoes, corn, and tomatoes, and further indomitably impressed by her innovative techniques of composting and crop rotation.
An electric tension hangs in the air as the announcement time nears.
The joy-filled roar that greets Sarah's victorious announcement reverberates through the locale, marking a significant turning point in the family's life.
Amongst thunderous applause and words of praise, Sarah, Benjamin and Samuel share a cathartic embrace.
Their combined joy brings tears of relief, washing away the exhausted lines of worry engraved on their young faces.
The winning cash prize is immediately put to use - for overdue medical bills, for procuring superior farming equipment, and for ensuring Martha gains the best possible healthcare.
As Sarah holds Martha's feeble hand, they quietly watch her slowly start to recover.
A part of their winnings also goes into establishing a small-scale agricultural business.
Mapping out a sustainable path for their future, they continue to turn the once struggling farm into their bread and butter.
Looking towards an auspicious future, a letter arrives from the competition organizers, praising the impressive farming techniques of Sarah, reaffirming their faith in a promising future.

60292828.title: Wendy (film)
synopsis: Wendy Darling lives in the rural South with her waitress mother Angela and twin brothers James and Douglas.

Back when James and Douglas (Logan Jones and Luke Jones) were celebrating their seventh birthdays, their next-door neighbor and cousin Thomas Marshall storms outside (on discovering what his future will be) and disappears, with Wendy seeing him being lured into climbing aboard a passing train car by a hooded childlike figure.
One night, when the children request a bedtime story, Angela tells them about her life and how she was forced to give up on her dreams in order to raise a family.
Wendy wonders whether the same thing will happen to her.
The next night, as the train passes by their bedroom window, Wendy notices a boy riding on top of the train cars.
The three children climb out of their window and join the boy, Peter, who takes them all to a tropical island with an active volcano, which Peter calls "Mother".
The island is populated by other children, including their long-lost cousin Thomas, who has not aged a day for over the past seven years.
Peter explains that Mother's spirit resides in the volcano and prevents the children from aging, so long as they believe in her.

They later discover a large glowing fish, which is Mother's other form with Wendy then secretly coming across a dated photograph of a deceased family of islanders that include Peter and concludes Mother must've saved him from a natural disaster (that killed the other islanders) and shared her powers with Peter making him ageless.
While exploring a capsized boat called the Mañana, Douglas injures his head and disappears from sight.
The children search for him without success.
Missing his twin brother, James withdraws emotionally and his right hand begins to show signs of age.
James becomes afraid and asks Peter to cut the hand off lest he become old.
Shocked and disgusted, Wendy pulls James away from the group and they explore the back of the island.
They encounter a settlement of "Olds," children who lost faith in Mother and thus began to age normally.
Among them is Buzzo, well known by the younger kids as being a former member of their group (who lost his faith in Mother when his best friend died).
James, bitter at having to grow up without Douglas, rallies the group to kill and eat Mother's fish form in order to regain their youth.
The Olds kidnap the children to use as bait for Mother and repurpose the Mañana as a fishing boat.
While evading the Olds, Wendy and Peter find Douglas alive.
They swim to the Mañana, where they find the now elderly James, with a hook in place of his missing right hand.
As Peter and Wendy rescue the children, James kills Mother with a harpoon.
With Peter and the children mournful and the Olds disheartened, Wendy gets them to all start singing, which inspires Peter and revitalizes the volcano.
Wendy and Douglas decide it is time for them to go home plus also bring Thomas back with them to give his family closure (along with two other tag along lost children).
Knowing that he cannot go home, James stays to play with Peter as his new “enemy” Captain Hook, thereby allowing him to live out the rest of his days with the spirit of a child.
Years later Wendy, now a mother herself, wakes to find her daughter Jane climbing aboard a passing train car with none other than Peter himself, still unchanged by time.
Unable to keep up, Wendy comforts herself that Peter will look after her daughter and eventually return Jane back home to Wendy.

9723049.title: The Silent Hill: Nepal Chronicles (film)
synopsis: Eager for excitement, four close companions - the ever-analytical John, the ever-cheerful Sarah, the curious scholar Rachel, and the athletic Peter - arrive at Kathmandu's bustling Tribhuvan International Airport.
Delving into the heart of Kathmandu, the vibrant capital city, they interact with the locals.

Driven by their adrenaline-pumping desire for an adventurous excursion, the group hires Sunita, a well-traveled and knowledgeable local guide, who will accompany them on their impending exploration of the Paro Valley.
After a long trek, they finally reach their destination.
As they plunge deeper into the heart of Paro Valley, unexpected obstacles mar their expedition.
While treading the dense undergrowth, they accidentally uncover the debris of ancient ruins.
With the sun retreating and darkness looming, Rachel is assaulted by terrifying nightmares, and Peter's skin turns feverish and his eyes delirious.
Despite the hanging fog of these explicable occurrences, they resolve unanimously not to give in to their rising fears.
Their meticulously crafted map, which until now was their only guide, now proved undecipherable, as the landmarks shifted in an almost eerie manner.
Their trusted compass began to spin in erratic directions, throwing them into a state of panic.
In the world of shadows, misgivings and suspicions began to take root against rationality.
Pettiness emerged, disagreements escalated, and Jamie's fever heightened.
As their panic mounted, they stumbled upon an ancient shrine concealed within the ruins.
With spectral incidents growing in strength and frequency, unseen forces toyed with their minds, subjecting them to hallucinations and an unending stream of peripheral paranoia.
A seemingly average local Sherpa, Tenzin, uncloaks himself as the shrine's guardian, revealing that he had followed their trail for their safety.

Tenzin explained the sacred significance of the shrine, cautioning them about the consequences and taking them meticulously through a sacred ritual aimed to appease the infuriated spirits inhabiting the cursed valley.
The completion of the ritual marked a significant decrease in their torments, and Peter's fever subsided.
However, not every story has a happy ending.
In the chaos that was their journey, John had suffered life-threatening injuries, and tragically failed to survive the perils of Silent Hill.
Tenzin, their savior, met his end amidst a last, vicious attack of supernatural forces, sacrificing his life to ensure the group's survival.
Gripping each other, physically exhausted and mentally drained, the survivors hobbled back towards civilization, aided by another group of explorers they crossed paths with by pure fate.
Once yearning for adrenaline-pumping adventure, the group now bore the hallmark of their harrowing experiences.
The concluding act found them back home, each survivor reflecting upon their journey.

They made a pact to spread the importance of respecting indigenous cultures and customs across their acquaintances, a tribute to their saviors and as a moved reaction to their traumatizing experience.
The final shot pans back to Silent Hill, standing as eerily magnificent as ever.

51126878.title: The Empty Man (film)
synopsis: In 1995 in the Ura Valley, Bhutan, four friends—Greg, Fiona, Ruthie, and Paul—go hiking on a mountain, crossing a footbridge along the way.
Paul hears a strange whistling and falls into a crevice.
Greg finds him in an almost catatonic state, sitting in front of and staring at a massive, ancient inhuman skeleton embedded in the cave wall.
Greg carries him out and the group takes refuge at an empty house as a snowstorm hits.
The next day, Ruthie is chased by the spirit of the cave creature.
That night, Paul, slowly possessed by the evil spirit, whispers something into Ruthie's ear.
The following morning, the group finds Paul next to the bridge they crossed.
Ruthie becomes dazed before stabbing Greg and slicing Fiona's throat and throwing their bodies over the cliff.
She shares an entranced look with Paul before throwing herself off too.
Paul sits on.
In Missouri 2018, former detective James Lasombra is grieving the death of his wife Allison and their son Henry who died in a car accident a year ago.
He is friends with his neighbor Nora, a widowed single mother.
Nora's daughter Amanda runs away and they find a message written in blood in the bathroom saying "The Empty Man made me do it".
While searching Amanda's bedroom, James discovers literature from a group called the Pontifex Institute.
Amanda's friend Devara reveals that she and their friends were encouraged by Amanda to summon the Empty Man, a local legend.
To summon the Empty Man, you must first find an empty bottle on a bridge, blow into it, and then think of the Empty Man.
Each friend in the group did so.
The next day at the mall, Devara witnesses Amanda whispering into friend Brandon's ear.
James investigates the bridge, and finds the empty bottle.
He proceeds to blow on it, just as the teenagers had done previously.
He goes underneath the bridge and discovers the hanged bodies of Brandon and the rest of Amanda's friends with the same message found in Amanda's bathroom.
Devara is next killed by the spirit, who attacks her in the steam room of a spa with a pair of scissors.
The police rule her death a suicide.
James researches the Pontifex Institute, discovering it is a cult that has beliefs originating from places like Bhutan and in tulpas, which he further researches on Wikipedia.
He believes he hears the Empty Man that night and is besieged by nightmares.
He travels to the institute and sits in on a talk by cult leader Arthur Parsons.
Speaking to Parsons, he is alarmed at the leader's references to the Empty Man, claiming him to be an entity that provides his followers with what they want as long as they do his bidding.
James begins to think he sees the Empty Man.
He follows cult members and investigates a cabin in the woods where he finds files on Amanda, her friends, Paul, and himself.
He witnesses the cult performing a fire ritual but is spotted and pursued by the cult.
He suspects that Amanda is now a member of the cult and informs Nora that she is not safe.
He takes Nora to a hotel to hide.
It is revealed that the pair were having an affair and he was with Nora when Allison and Henry died.
Suffering from hallucinations, James ambushes cult member Garrett and asks him what is happening before brutally beating him.
Garrett claims that there is a man in the hospital from whom the Empty Man is transmitting to the cult.
James discovers that the man is actually Paul, who is in a comatose state and regularly visited by cult members to get messages from the entity.
He finds Amanda in Paul's hospital room and she explains that Paul is dying from the strain of being the Empty Man, and that the cult needs a new vessel.
She tells James that he is a tulpa, a new vessel for the being, and that his memories and relationships were fabricated by her and the cult to ensure the deity's connection through his pain and loss.
According to Amanda, James has only existed for a few days.
In disbelief, James calls Nora, but she does not know who he is.
James breaks down and finds himself in a limbo-like plane, where the being enters his body.
Back in the hospital, James executes Paul, and he finds himself surrounded by several members of the hospital staff.
They bow to him as he looks on, the nameless entity in control.

50409567.title: Journey Through The Northern Wilds
synopsis: The story unfolds with the introduction of Alex, a determined transgender young man grappling with the scorn and estrangement experienced in the close-knit community of Stillwater, Minnesota.
The prejudice isn't restricted to just the townsfolk; his own father, Henry, a respected lumberjack with an ardent love for nature, also mirrors these discordant sentiments.
Vancouver, Canada, a beacon of acceptance, becomes Alex's haven in his dreams, a place where he believes he can escape the adversity and live his life as he truly is.
Amid these troubling circumstances, a cryptic phone call from Jack, Henry's old hunting pal, brings a turn of events.
Jack needs Henry's assistance in delivering an undisclosed package to Vancouver, stirring the dormant adventurer in him.
Henry recognizes this as an opportunity to mend the growing distance between him and Alex, suggesting a journey together across the borders, weaving through the Northern wilderness.
Accepting the proposal, a father-son journey commences through the thick of the Northern wilderness bordered by the Great Lakes.
During their adventure, Henry shares his immense knowledge and love for nature with Alex, teaching him survival skills like setting up a tent and starting a fire in the forest.
Filled with formidable and testing challenges, their journey was far from a leisurely excursion.
During their dire sojourn from a vicious snowstorm in an abandoned log cabin, they unearth a cryptic, weather-worn map, hinting at a hidden treasure.
The unexpected quest for a rumored miner's lost bounty becomes their new focus.
In overcoming these challenges, Henry starts recognizing the struggles Alex faces for his identity.
Each shared hardship draws them closer, leading to a silent yet transformative shift in Henry's perception of Alex.
Together they face the adversities thrown their way, each marking their journey with spine-chilling, adrenaline-filled episodes.
As Henry witnesses firsthand Alex's bravery, he begins to respect his resilience and courage, helping him shed his preconceived notions about his son's identity.
Following the directions provided by the aged map, they finally reach the anticipated location of the lost treasure - a concealed cave behind a grand waterfall.
Disappointment sweeps over them when they discover the cave to be empty, void of any treasure.
The heartache quickly fades when Henry experiences a profound realization that the real treasure had been the authentic, unbreakable bond that he and Alex had built throughout their journey.
Having reached his dream city of Vancouver, Alex reconsiders his initial resolution to start anew.
With a changed perspective, they embark on their return journey to Stillwater in their small blue pickup.
Upon their return, Henry metamorphoses into Alex's ally, serving as a bridge between Alex and the unyielding townsfolk.
Their story, filled with riveting adventures and insights, is shared with the townsfolk, fostering a subtle yet powerful shift in their rigid attitudes towards Alex.
The story caps off on a promising note, foretelling an era of growing acceptance for Alex and others like him in the small town of Stillwater.
The shared journey of father and son has sown the seeds of transformation in the community, making Stillwater a more inclusive and accepting space.
The story concludes, leaving room for countless other stories like Alex's, offering a glimmer of hope for a more accepting and understanding future for all.

64803990.title: Cowboys (2020 film)
synopsis: Joe, a transgender boy, accompanies his father Troy on a journey across the Montana wilderness on their way to Canada.
Joe's mother, and estranged wife of Troy, Sally wakes up to find Joe gone, leading her to report the incident to the police.
Sally talks to Detective Erickson who requests a recent picture of Joe.
Sally produces a picture of Joe which shows him with long hair and in feminine clothing.
Erickson refers to Joe as Sally's daughter, a statement which Sally agrees with.
In a series of flashbacks, Joe's childhood leading up to his disappearance is explored.
From an early age, Joe connects with his father and enjoys his stories about cowboys.
Sally meanwhile pushes traditional gender ideals on Joe, making him wear dresses, like the color pink, and dissuades his fascination with cowboys.
One night, Joe comes out to Troy about his dissatisfaction with his gender and his desire to act like a boy.
When Troy informs Sally, she refuses to accept it and tells Joe to follow God's path.
Some time later in a western clothing store, Troy lets Joe try on traditionally-male cowboy attire.
When Joe's cousin and uncle come into the store, the cousin sneaks into Joe's dressing room and says he looks like a dyke in his outfit.
Troy aggressively yells at him for his comments and in the heat of the moment pushes Joe's uncle down a flight of stairs.
Troy is subsequently sent to prison, and while there Sally and Joe continue to be adversarial about his gender identity.
After Troy is released, he and Sally separate and she eventually refuses to let him visit Joe anymore.
In response, Joe cuts his hair and Sally proceeds to slap him across the face.
As Joe is distraught, Troy agrees to Joe's plan for the two of them to run away to find a better home for Joe.
In the present, Troy and Joe first travel to Troy's drug-addiction rehabilitation counselor Robert.
Robert is shocked by their arrival but lets them stay the night after Troy's truck breaks down.
In the morning Troy and Joe takes Robert's horse.
Detective Erickson tracks down Troy's truck, but Robert covers for them and claims he never saw Joe with Troy.
In the wilderness, Joe attempts to fish for food at night after he becomes hungry.
As he wades into the water he is taken by the current, prompting Troy to try and rescue him.
After the two make it back to shore Troy realizes he lost the prescription drugs he had been taking, causing him to go through withdrawal.
Approaching the Canadian border, the two become lost as Troy becomes increasingly frantic.
Detective Erickson finally tracks them down, but as she tries to reason with them another officer shoots Troy.
Some time later, Joe lives with a more accepting Sally, who lets him wear traditionally-male clothing and refers to him using his preferred pronouns.
The two visit Troy in prison who is getting treatment for his drug addiction.
As Joe returns to school, all the children on the bus want to know about Joe's trips with his dad.

35934961.title: Notorious (2020 film)
synopsis: Our story unfolds with our heroine, Bianca, a fireball of audacity at 20-years-old, teetering on the edge of adulthood.
Educated beyond her years, her days are filled with rigorous studying for her law school exams.
Her nights are consumed with keeping her chaotic and cluttered home intact, a situation of which she was neither the architect nor the custodian.
The root of this chaos is Jake, her mother's Karen's lackluster boyfriend, who's made their sofa his permanent dwelling place.
The weight of the family's financial burdens is on Bianca's shoulders, as Jake's disinterest in securing steady employment exacerbates their situation.
Driven by an unyielding desire for better days, Bianca takes a conscious pause from her lifelong aspiration of becoming an ace lawyer.

Much against her mother's tearful pleas, she decides to become a waitress at a whimsical Italian bistro located in the heart of town  During a coastal, breezy night at work, Bianca's life takes a dramatic twist when she meets Dominic, a man shrouded in intrigue.
Unbeknownst to her, Dominic plays an integral role in a notorious secret society infamous for executing meticulously planned and highly rewarding scams and heists.
Bianca feels an overwhelmed temptation to partake in this risky yet uncannily lucrative illicit world, hoping it could be an escape route from her daily struggles.

Leveraging her unwavering courage and astute analytical abilities, Bianca catapults through the society's hierarchy, astonishing everyone while also gaining the respect and admiration of her colleagues.
Meanwhile, home is no refuge as the tension escalates.
Jake, following a tempestuous blowout concerning his languid life choices, abandons the family, leaving Bianca and Karen to navigate their bleak reality alone.
Split between her family's mounting financial distress and the perilous activities of the secret society, Bianca is pushed to her limits.
A life-altering moment arrives in the form of a meticulously planned diamond heist, a job promising to change their fortunes.
However, the heist coincides with a major FBI raid on the secret society's underground lair, complicating matters further.
Pulled between the society's alluring promise of unimaginable wealth and the deteriorating health of her mother, Bianca finds her moral compass caught in a whirlwind of conflicting emotions.
With the pressure reaching a fever pitch, Bianca stands on the precipice of a massive breakdown, locked in a constant struggle to maintain control over her tumultuous life.
As the hour of the heist inches closer, Bianca senses the tightening noose of the FBI, raising the stakes of her dangerous escapade.
Despite the mounting fear, the secret society gives the heist a go-ahead, with Bianca and the rest of the team playing their assigned roles amidst nerve-wracking tension.
Their successful seizure of the diamonds is short-lived as police vehicles and SWAT vans surround their location in an adrenaline-filled showdown.
Caught in the chaos, Bianca's undying instincts lead her to maneuver through the brewing storm, orchestrating a nail-biting escape through the city's intricate sewerage system.
However, despite Bianca's quick thinking, not every member of the society manages to slip through the police dragnet.
Numerous arrests ensue, marking a huge dent in the secret society's formidable reputation.
With millions worth of diamonds in her hold, Bianca finds herself free yet weighed down by a heavy conscience and an uncertain, precarious future.
After grappling with her morals, she chooses to return home, carrying a bag brimming with precious stolen diamonds, the game-changing fortune that could pull them out of debt.
Bianca bares her soul to Karen, narrating her dangerous exploits, and reveals the stolen diamonds as their potential lifeline.
As expected, Karen is caught between a mother's disappointment over Bianca's dangerous ventures and relief at the prospect of numerous, unending bills being settled.

With a gentle push from her mother, Bianca takes a shot at redemption, re-enrolling in college, still haunted by the ghosts of her past deeds, yet holding on to a glimmer of hope for a promising career in law once again.
As they painstakingly piece together their lives from scratch, a potential spanner in the works arrives, in the form of a letter announcing Jake's possible return.

64010054.title: Infamous (2020 film)
synopsis: Arielle lives in Florida with her mother Janet, who has a deadbeat boyfriend named Bobby.
Arielle enjoys social media and has few followers.
One night, she goes to a party where she gets into a fight and beats up a girl while everyone at the party films the fight and posts it on social media.
Arielle immediately gains 147 new followers.
Dean Taylor is new to town and stays with his father.
Arielle meets him while he is working on his car.
They spend time together at a party, where Dean reveals he was in prison for armed robbery and assault, and that his parole requires him to be with his father since his mother is dead.
His father is an abusive drunk.
She tells him how badly she wants to get out of Florida and go to Hollywood to be famous.
One day, Arielle finds all her saved money missing.
Right away, she bursts into Janet's room where she and Bobby are in bed.
Arielle accuses Bobby of stealing her money and attacks Bobby, but Bobby pushes her and she hits her head against the wall.
Arielle leaves after threatening to kill him.
She goes to Dean's home and finds his father beating him.
Arielle tries to intervene but again gets hit on her head after getting thrown to the ground.
Dean fights his father who ends up falling down the stairs and dies after hitting his head.
Arielle and Dean begin to leave town right away but realizing that they have no money, they decide to rob a gas station with Dean's gun.
Arielle livestreams as Dean commits the robbery.
Dean is unaware of being live streamed.
Arielle sees that her social media account has three thousand followers.
Dean becomes angry when he learns that Arielle has been live streaming their crimes, but Arielle says she used IP blocker and did not show their faces.
She says it will lead to fame and money.
Still short on money, Dean suggests they rob a dispensary next.
This time, Dean films as Arielle does the robbing.
With more crimes filmed, Arielle's account gains over three million followers.
Eventually, the police identify them and Dean and Arielle see their faces on the news.
Dean is angry about the social media, but Arielle is elated to be famous.
On the road, they get pulled over, and Dean tells Arielle not to start anything.
When the officer goes to check their IDs, Arielle exits the car and shoots the officer.
Arielle and Dean go into hiding for a while and this leads to Arielle losing her subscribers and followers.

Dean and Arielle get into an argument where Dean tries to make her realize about how serious of a crime she committed whereas Arielle says that she did it for him but Dean disagrees as he thinks she did it for fame.
Even though they have enough money and do not need anymore, Arielle goes off on her own to commit a robbery at a gas station and accidentally kills a customer who startled her.
The clerk manages to grab a gun and shoots Arielle in the shoulder as she flees.
Dean is extremely upset that everyone now knows where they are.
The police have found them and thus begins a car chase and a shootout.
They realize that they left their money behind.
Once they get away from the police, Dean removes the bullet from her shoulder.
Arielle takes pictures of her wounds for her followers, making Dean angry again.
Dean blames Arielle for the whole situation since her coming over led to his father's death.
Arielle slaps him repeatedly and then kisses him.
A woman, Elle, driving by sees Arielle and the broken down truck.
She pulls over to help and Arielle pulls out her gun and says they need a place to stay for a night.
Elle reveals she follows Arielle online and that she knew who they were before she pulled up.
At Elle's place, Dean asks her why she follows Arielle.
Elle explains that her life has not worked out and that people find them empowering.
Dean tells her no one should want to be like them.
The next day, Elle drives them through a police checkpoint.
Once they are through, they give Elle a bottle of water and take her car, directing her to walk back to the gas station they passed and to report her car stolen to get the insurance reimbursement.
Elle wants to go with them, but Dean refuses.
Arielle takes a picture with her and posts it, telling her lots of people are going to want to talk to her after that.
Arielle and Dean drive off.
Later, they stop at the home of Kyle, Dean's contact.
Kyle's crew plans to rob a bank but needs an extra gunmen.
Arielle wants in, but Dean thinks it is a bad idea.
He wants to leave and go to Mexico, but Arielle holds firm, wanting the money and the followers.
Dean makes Arielle promise that if they do this job she will leave with him after.
During the robbery, even though Kyle insisted on no social media, Arielle streams it to her five million followers.
On the other hand, Kyle becomes upset after not being able to find the money they expected and in anger shoots a bank worker.
As they are about to leave, they find cops already outside surrounding the bank.
Kyle realizes it is because Arielle streamed the bank robbery and (accidentally) the name of the bank.
Kyle and his crew get into a shootout with Arielle and Dean where Kyle and Dean end up shooting each other dead.
The police arrest Arielle and as they bring her out of the bank, she sees hundreds of fans and followers with signs cheering her, giving her fame that she always wanted.

96848013.title: Fragile Promises (2021 film)
synopsis: The narrative begins with a breathtaking shot capturing the picturesque scene of a garden wedding held in the corner of a quaint little town.
Elizabeth, the local schoolteacher and John, an ambitious corporate worker, were in the midst of trading vows, their love palpable in the air, magnified by the sun setting in the background.
They professed their promises to each other, their voices echoing through the rows of old oak trees as their closest friends and family members bore witness to their beautiful declaration.
The promise was to love each other through both the sunlit days full of joy and the stormy ones filled with challenges.
Their life unfolds in a pleasant two-bedroom apartment tucked in the tranquil suburbs of San Francisco.
This apartment, though modest, was a canvas filled with their shared dreams and aspirations.

They spent their evenings huddled up on a second-hand couch that had seen better days, exchanging ideas about their future—the anecdotal stories infused with their dreams of a prosperous setup, blissfully unaware of the financial hurdles crossing their path.
The reality, however, was rather cruel as they found themselves piled under a mountain of unpaid bills and stubborn student loans, reminders of a past they were struggling to escape.
The unopened letters, reminders of their debt, and escalating bills quickly turned their cheerful dwelling into a war-room where each dollar spent went under a meticulous review.
Their once serene apartment echoed with harsh discussions about reckless purchases and poor budgeting habits, the remnants of their tranquillity slowly eroding away.
John's job as a junior manager in a relatively small tech firm suddenly seemed inadequate, his salary insufficient to support the lifestyle both of them had envisioned.
A glimmer of hope appeared for John when a colleague suggested a Bitcoin scheme that promised quick, abundant returns—almost a godsend that he was cornered into opting for.
However, he decided to keep this under wraps, cautiously avoiding any confrontation with Elizabeth who he knew would be opposed to such a risky venture.
Meanwhile, Elizabeth, an aspiring writer, found an unexpected opportunity in the form of an exciting contract proposal from a high-profile publishing company.
The company made a promising offer, asking her to use her poetic prowess to pen a creative manuscript.
Heart pulsating with hope, she viewed this stroke of luck as the turning point, their way out of the financial desert they found themselves stranded in.
Concurrently, unbeknown to her, John's reckless Bitcoin investment crashed catastrophically, pushing them deeper into a quagmire of regret and debt.

Gathering his courage, John revealed his disastrous financial gamble to Elizabeth who was initially flabbergasted and then gradually, the reality dawned upon her, carving a crease of worry on her forehead.
However, love has its strange ways, and she decided to utilize their limited savings to bail out John's consequential debts.
The laughter that used to echo through the house was replaced by a stifling silence, palpable tension looming in the once lively corners of their apartment.
Despite the tensions, Elizabeth tirelessly worked towards meeting her writing project deadline, putting herself through physical exhaustion and mental burn-out.
As the deadline approached, she wrestled with a creative stalemate, her usually eloquent mind struggling to form a cohesive narrative.
Pushed to her threshold, Elizabeth, during a heated argument about their financial situation, asked John to contribute more than mere guilt and remorse towards resolving their monetary constraints.
The resounding echo of her words resonated so deeply within John that it incited him to re-evaluate their situation, the state of their marriage, and his contribution to it.
Covered in the dust of guilt for his ill-advised judgement, John decided it was time for him to make amends.

Shrugging aside his ego, he started taking odd jobs - delivering packages to office buildings during the day and working as an Uber driver at night to add to their income and relieve some of the burden off Elizabeth's shoulders.
Meanwhile, Elizabeth managed to break her writer's block, using her bottled-up emotions to weave intriguing narratives for her assignment.
Burning the midnight oil, she finally submitted her work a day before the deadline, holding her breaths nervously.
To her relief, not only did the work meet the expected parameters, but it received rave reviews and a standing ovation from the literary world, filling her heart with a sense of accomplishment.
Accompanied by the financial recompense that exceeded her wildest imaginations, a long overdue rainbow shone after a long spell of financially precarious days.
With their newfound hope, Elizabeth and John confronted their financial problems with unity, promising to face future obstacles as a dedicated team.
They utilized the money Elizabeth received from her first published work towards clearing their debts, waving a final goodbye to the fiscal challenges that had seemed insurmountable.
As they successfully navigated their first major marital hurdle, they breathed a collective sigh of relief.
The shared adversity led to an unspoken pact between them, pledging to overcome any obstacles together, upholding their faith in each other even amidst uncertainties.
As time flowed into years, Elizabeth and John evolved from financially depressed newlyweds into a resilient team managing their stability on their terms.
Elizabeth, riding on the waves of her highly applauded debut, became a beacon for upcoming writers.
John, on the other hand, found contentment as a well-regarded handyman, a job that added unexpected satisfaction to his life.
Looking back at their past, they saw not regret but a sense of pride over having weathered the storms that had threatened to dismantle their world.
Their past trials symbolize not just overcoming financial constraints but also the embodiment of an unwavering belief in their relationship, in their ability to thrive amidst adversity.
They believe in looking back at their challenging times, not with bitterness but with a sense of appreciation for the strength they discovered during the strife.
The common difficulties faced and subsequently surmounted have only strengthened their bond, turning them into a formidable team ready to weather any storms that might angle their way.
John and Elizabeth are a living testament to love being not just a companion during calm periods but as a reliable ally during testing times too.
Their journey narrates their ascension from just being a couple to a unit working with unwavering determination.
The tale weaves itself around their camaraderie and commitment towards weathering all storms together.
Beyond achieving financial stability, their journey highlights the endurance required to keep the vows of 'for better or worse.'
They epitomize the resilience needed to keep a relationship intact despite hardships, underscoring the necessity for a joint approach towards dealing with adversities rather than struggling solo.
Their unwavering commitment has changed their relationship dynamics so significantly that they believe they can face and overcome any adversity together.
This alteration in their relationship manifests forming a circle of trust, patience, and collective confrontation of all hardships.
Presently, they stand stronger, and more at peace with the future despite having the knowledge of their past battles has prepared them to face anything with unwavering grit and determination.
They understand that their trials have not defeated them but rather, strengthened their bond, prompting them to honor their commitment irrespective of the hurdles.
Their collective journey allowed them to comprehend love as not just a passive emotion but an active force that prods them to fight for each other, come what may.

Unitedly, they have penned a narrative of resilience, weaving their failures, victories, and love — a tale creating a robust safety net capable of weathering any adversities that their future may throw at them.

60711408.title: Dangerous Lies (2020 film)
synopsis: Katie and Adam are a young married couple struggling to pay their bills.
Katie works as a waitress while Adam is going to school.
One night, an attempted robbery takes place in the diner where Katie works, but Adam manages to fight off the robbers.
Katie finds another job as a caregiver for Leonard, an elderly wealthy man who grows close to her.
After she tells him about her financial struggles, Leonard insists on helping her out with money, but Katie convinces him to give Adam a job instead as his gardener.
One day, Mickey Hayden, claiming to be a real estate agent, tells Katie that a client is interested in buying the house.
When Katie tells him it is not for sale, he starts to watch the couple closely.
Soon after, Leonard writes Katie a $7,000 check.
She does not want to accept it, but Adam convinces her to use it to pay the bills that are due and pay back Leonard the rest.
The next day, Katie and Adam arrive at Leonard's home to find him dead, leaving Katie devastated.
The couple finds a large amount of cash in a trunk and, after a small dispute, agrees to keep it without notifying the police.
At Leonard's funeral, they learn from his lawyer, Julia, that Leonard left Katie his estate and all his possessions.
Katie and Adam move into Leonard's house, but are again pursued by the highly motivated Hayden, who threatens her.
At the same time, Detective Chesler becomes suspicious of Adam, and starts to investigate Leonard's death and the robbery at the diner.
After talking to the detective, Katie becomes suspicious of Adam.
Wanting to confront him, she searches the entire property and ends up finding a secret room in a shed.
She then finds Ethan (Leonard's previous gardener) long dead of a gunshot wound with a bag of diamonds.

Adam looks into Hayden and discovers he was recently released from prison for stealing over three million in diamonds, realizes Ethan was Hayden's partner in crime, and Hayden killed him to get his share of the diamonds.
Ethan, mortally wounded, had fled to Leonard’s house, where he died.
Hayden knows the diamonds are hidden somewhere on the property and is eager to find them.
Adam and Katie decide to flee together with the cash they had found in the attic.
While Adam is getting ready, Hayden shows up and holds Katie at gunpoint, asking for the diamonds.
Hayden and Adam exchange gunfire, and both are killed.
Julia arrives, and Katie tells her that Hayden was the one who killed Leonard with an overdose of his medication.
Julia reaches for Hayden's gun and holds Katie at gunpoint, revealing that she had been Hayden's public defender and is part of the plot.
She demands the diamonds, but Katie tells her Adam hid them somewhere, and she does not know where.
Chesler arrives in time and shoots Julia dead.
Four months later, Chesler talks to a pregnant Katie about how they searched for the diamonds in the house but never found them.
In the last shot, Katie turns the sprinklers on and leaves the garden.
The water moves the soil aside, and the diamonds are shown to be buried under a tree, something Adam had hinted at as he died.

18664260.title: Frigid Terror
synopsis: Laura, an introverted accountant from bustling New York City, is dispatched to the snow-laden town of Marquette, Michigan, for an extended auditorial assignment.
She finds an odd sense of comfort in a quaint, traditional inn named 'The Whispering Pines.'
Warming by the inn's fire, she encounters the innkeeper, Henry, who tells tales of a local outcast named Fred.
The town's eerie silence does little to assuage her increasing apprehension.
Whispers of Fred's name seem to carry on the frigid wind.
Laura's sojourn at 'The Whispering Pines' turns unnerving as a cacophony of bizarre incidents begin to occur.
Cryptic notes appear under her door and she discovers the grim remains of rabbits on her doorstep.
Each chilling incident seems to eerily coincide with the guest appearances of the reclusive outcast, Fred.
Marquette, once serene, starts to buzz with anxious chatter about the mysterious happenings.
Officer Daniel, a highly regarded local law officer, steps in to examine the phenomenon tied to Fred.
Determined to ensure Laura's safety, he assigns protection to 'The Whispering Pines.'
As the town watches anxiously, Fred strikes a vicious blow, lunging at Laura's room.
Thanks to Officer Daniel's vigilance, Laura is saved from what could've been a dangerous encounter.
Startled back to his senses, Fred flees, with Laura, invigorated by adrenaline, hot on his heels.
They find themselves in the densely wooded areas surrounding the inn, the ice-covered foliage crackling under Fred's desperate footfalls.
Laura manages to outdistance Fred, buying herself enough time for the town's law force to mobilize.
Laura's daring escape plan gives Officer Daniel and his team the upper hand.
They manage to corner a disoriented Fred in the icy wilderness.
Laura's bravery instantly propels her to the status of an admired town personality.
Over the weeks that follow, the inhabitants offer their support, pouring their warmth and gratitude onto her.
Laura's daily town strolls transform into jubilant exchanges with townsfolk who admire her strength.
The town's tranquillity is restored, with Laura now being considered an integral part of this close-knit community.
As the day of her departure back to New York City draws near, Laura holds an emotional farewell with her newfound friends.
Laura carries with her a newfound assurance as she blends into the rhythm of the city again.
Her experiences in Marquette have instilled in her a new resilience, an evolution that she proudly wears as her city life resumes.
Laura's daunting Marquette saga has morphed her from a shy, unassertive woman to an embodiment of strength and courage.
Her Michigan tales lay the groundwork for a survival story for those battling their own adversities.
Laura's chilling experiences in Marquette serve as motivation for her coworkers.
Laura stands tall in New York, transforming her haunting memories into fuel for courage.
She carries her newfound strength as a beacon, inspiring her peers and colleagues.

68155385.title: Vicious Fun
synopsis: In 1983 Minnesota, serial killer Phil targets Carrie outside a motel.
Carrie surprises Phil by suddenly stabbing him in his throat once he locks her inside his car.
Joel, a film critic for the horror magazine Vicious Fanatics, interviews B-movie director Jack Portwood.
Joel tells Jack his idea for a film about a serial killing taxicab driver.
At home, Joel sees his roommate Sarah, who he has an unrequited crush on, being dropped off by her new boyfriend Bob.
Jealous of Bob and anxious for insight into Sarah, Joel follows Bob to a Chinese restaurant where they engage in conversation at the bar.
Unaware of Joel’s true identity, Bob speaks disparagingly about Sarah’s pitiable roommate before sticking Joel with their tab and leaving with another woman.
Joel continues getting drunk, stumbles into a supply closet, and passes out.
The restaurant locks up for the night.
When he recovers, Joel wanders back into the dining room where Zachary leads a 12-step meeting for Carrie, Fritz, Mike, and Hideo.
The group mistakes Joel for Phil.
Sensing danger if they realize he isn’t supposed to be there, Joel plays along.
Joel gradually realizes he is stuck in a self-help meeting for serial killers.
