A fateful encounter between Leah and Biscuit by an old magnolia tree in Riverdale's famously lush central park sparks an immediate friendship.
Her unassuming demeanor in stark contrast to Biscuit's reserved personality, all bridged by a shared empathy that soon turns into a strong camaraderie.
Leah, who believes in making big strides outdoors, manages to encourage Biscuit to step outside his digital haven.
Their time spent under sunsets bathed in copper hues and surrounded by expansive greenery forms an unlikely duo shedding their inhibitions and embracing the upsides of an active life.

Group hikes along the infamous Hudson trails, cycling excursions through the serene Miller's lane, spontaneous dancing in the town square - Biscuit's initial reluctances gradually turn into enthusiastic engagements.
During a warm summer picnic, Leah narrates her personal journey to Biscuit, sharing her own battles against childhood obesity, and how she was able to not just overcome it, but thrive afterwards.
Her story sparks a fire of hope within Biscuit, a possibility of transformation mirrors within Leah's words and his life's drastic potential.
Fueled by Leah's tale, shared over hearty sandwiches, and his mother's gentle persuasion over homemade meals, Biscuit decides to take on his weight issues head-on.

Reluctant evening walks evolving into regular jogs, chips traded for carrot sticks, Biscuit's journey towards a healthy living begins with small steps, guided by an indefatigable spirit and Leah's persistent motivation.
Biscuit decides to participate in the upcoming Riverdale Annual Fitness Challenge.
The recurring event is held every year, challenging the residents of Riverdale with races, drills and other physical activities.
The taunts Biscuit used to receive at the schoolyard amplified, whispered mockery bouncing off classroom walls and laughter openly belittling his determination in the football grounds.
Despite the intensified criticism, his resolve remains unwavering.

Biscuit's fitness journey is marked by triumphant moments but not without its difficult challenges - navigating rough terrains, cherishing his victories on the jogging trails; all the while, he never stops moving forward.
As the days roll out into months, noticeable changes begin to show on Biscuit.
His previous weight of 300 pounds dwindles down to a much healthier 220 pounds, an unbelievable change echoed within his newfound confidence.
His demeanor reflects the newfound assurance, his smiles becoming wide and genuine, and the respect his peers accord him becomes perceptible.
The culmination of Biscuit's monumental transformation takes form on the day of the final round of the Riverdale Fitness Challenge.
His dedication is backed by Leah's unwavering support, his mother's loving assurance, and the collective hope of Riverdale's residents that have all begun to root for him.

66825295.title: Butter (2020 film)
synopsis: A severely obese high schooler from Scottsdale, Arizona nicknamed "Butter" is becoming increasingly suicidal by the day.
He got his nickname from being forced to eat a whole stick of butter by a bully named Jeremy Strong.

Butter's only joys in life besides eating are playing the saxophone at a jazz club with his music teacher, Professor Dunn, and chatting online with his crush, Anna McGinn, while he poses as a stranger named "JP".

Butter is an only child with an overprotective mother, Marian, a real estate agent who enables her son's unhealthy eating habits, while his father, Frank, is a former football captain, distant and disillusioned after a freak accident left him blind in one eye.
At school, Butter's attempt to stop Jeremy from harassing Anna backfires, and receives many humiliating comments on the school blog.
As December begins, Butter announces that he will stream himself eating to death on New Year's Day.
This makes him quickly popular in school, and suggestions for his final menu begin piling up on his webpage.
He also begins hanging out with two classmates, Trent and Parker.
They even help Butter plan a "Bucket List" of fun activities to do before he goes through with his final meal.
Even Anna grows closer to Butter, who reassures him that everyone thinks he is joking.
As Butter's mental health and self-confidence improves, his appetite drops dramatically.
Butter is invited to party on New Year's Eve.
After he plays a song he wrote for Anna on stage, he reveals himself to be JP, to Anna's shock.
As he tries to apologize, Anna slaps him.
Butter punches Jeremy as he intervenes, prompting Anna to cut ties with Butter completely.
As midnight arrives, Butter resumes his original plan, while everyone in the party watches his stream.
To everyone's horror, Butter undergoes an anaphylactic shock upon eating strawberries — being knowingly allergic — and Anna calls emergency services.
Butter wakes up in the hospital a few days later, and apologizes to his family and Anna.
Though sympathetic, Anna is still angry and clarifies that Butter was never a romantic interest.
She expresses her disappointment of Butter's deception, that JP turned out to be him.
She did not post a profile picture because she wanted to be accepted for who she was and not judged for her looks, which is also what he struggles with and ironically, what he did to her.
Butter begins attending therapy, learning that what he went through was bullying all along, disguised as popularity.
Still, Butter, his family, and his doctor are pleasantly surprised to learn that he has lost 50 pounds in just two weeks.
His parents grow closer to him and Marian ceases her enabling behavior by serving him healthier meals.
After Butter's release from the hospital, Anna comes to visit him one day and the two reconcile.
He reveals to her that his real name is Marshall.
They become friends again, but Butter has overcome his infatuation with Anna.
When he returns to school, his classmates greet him warmly and call him by his real name.
After a conversation with Professor Dunn, Butter looks forward to a successful future as a saxophonist.

8224550.title: Homecoming Twins: Mother's Encore (2022 film)
synopsis: The expansive city of New York serves as the backdrop for the lives of identical twins, James and Michael.
These 15-year-olds have learned the ropes of life under the watchful eye of their loving yet firm father, Charles.
Although he has kept them insulated from painful emotional entanglements, the looming shadow of their emotionally distant mother is inescapable.
Charles, acting as the central pillar of their life, has effectively kept them sheltered from any possible drama or trauma, particularly concerning their aloof mother.
In parallel to their lives, their mother, Nicole, navigates through her solitude, seldom encountering a familiar face who could break the monotony of her lonely life.
The life the twins know takes an abrupt turn when they receive an urgent, panic-filled phone call about their father's sudden health scare that called for immediate hospitalization.
Cornered by the circumstances with no other viable alternatives, the twins find themselves propelled onto a path that leads to their little-known mother's residence.
Nicole is overwhelmed by a tempest of emotions - surprise, fear, regret, as she grapples with the reality of her son's impending move into her quiet sanctuary.
As the boys reluctantly step into her apartment, they find themselves becoming unwilling inhabitants of an eerily silent world, an environment they're not accustomed to.
On one such unsettling evening, James stumbles upon a hidden treasure - a box tucked away beneath a rickety floorboard, crammed with old CDs and black-and-white pictures.
Intrigued by their accidental find, the twins set out on an exciting mission to unravel the enigma that is their mother's past.
Motivated by this curiosity, they embark on an adventurous mission to unveil their mother's history that had been rendered dormant for too long.
Gathering their courage, they decide to confront their mother with the picture album they found, each page lined with sepia-toned images of her in the limelight.
Nicole, taken aback by the sudden unveiling of her past, hesitates but soon starts recounting tales of her vivacious youth, her voice dripping with a melancholic form of nostalgia.
Incredibly moved by their mother's passionate discourse about music and performing, the twins slowly find a sense of respect for her buried deep within their hearts.
The plan was grandiose in its essence — organizing a city-wide concert in recognition and celebration of their mother's hidden and unappreciated talent.
Embracing the uphill task, they approach local businesses, knocking on countless doors to gather sponsorships to fuel their ambitious project.
As the concert date looms nearer, the old insecurities that once plagued Nicole try to snake back into her life.
Sensing the internal emotional tug-of-war within her, the boys offer her unwavering moral support, reassuring her of her latent capabilities.
During one such candid conversation in the dimly lit living room, they address unresolved issues, promising lifelong morale support in the face of all future adversities.
This emotional exchange concludes with a newfound sense of understanding, compassion, and connection, laying the foundation for a healthy familial bond.
The fast-approaching concert day engulfs everyone in a whirlwind of excitement, anxiety, and eager anticipation.
As the spotlight centers on a velvet-curtain concealed platform, Nicole, her eyes alight with an old flame, steps onto the stage.
Each lingering note stirs a deep emotional connection within her boys, moving the twins to tears of joy and astonishment.
The thunderous standing ovation rattles Nicole's spirit, leaving her overwhelmed with disbelief and gratitude.
The unforgettable night culminates with the family sharing a moving group hug on the stage, an iconic symbol of their newly discovered familial bond.
Post the concert, the twins start to gradually embrace the concept of a complete family, craving for the emotional warmth they had missed all these years.
Nicole's apartment, which once reeked of loneliness, is now bustling with the lively visits and chatter of the twins.
Now known by the thriving music community in New York, Nicole embarks on a rekindled musical journey.
Her mesmerizing performances at popular local venues hold everyone spellbound as her bewitching melodies waft through the air.
The scene wraps up with a tender family embrace on the stage, embodying unity, redemption, and the power of familial love and support.

71719706.title: Goodnight Mommy (2022 film)
synopsis: Twin brothers Elias and Lukas return home to live with their estranged mother, a former actress, after staying with their father since their divorce.
Upon seeing her again, they are disturbed to find her wearing a full bandage over her whole head, resembling a white balaclava.
Mother (who's never named) explains she has gotten cosmetic surgery.
She gives the boys some house rules, which include not entering her room or the barn outside.
While playing outside in the field, the boys discover the barn.
Exploring inside, Elias finds old toys of theirs.
Mother discovers they've been in the barn and chastises them, proclaiming that from then on they will stay indoors.

The boys quickly sense something strange about Mother, who does not seem interested in reconnecting with them; she drinks heavily, appears angry, and will not sing the lullaby she always used to sing to them as children.
Elias also discovers Mother has thrown away a drawing he made of the three of them, which upsets him.
During the night, Elias overhears Mother talking on the phone; she says she cannot go on pretending and wants him gone.
After seeing an old headshot of Mother with green eyes, who now has blue eyes, the boys begin to question whether the woman they are living with is really their mother.
When they attempt to contact their father, Mother breaks their shared cell phone.

One night while she is taking a bath, Elias attempts to remove the skincare face mask she is wearing; an argument ensues and, after Elias tells her she is not their mother, she slaps him, then sprays him with freezing cold shower water until he admits he is wrong.
Terrified of Mother, the boys leave in the middle of the night and attempt to seek help from a nearby house, which they discover is abandoned.
They break in to spend the night but are found by two local state troopers who take them back to Mother's house.
Mother, who has now removed her bandage, insists they are imagining things and says to police that Elias injured his lip from slipping near the pool.
The following morning, Mother wakes to find her arms and legs tied to the bed with duct tape.
She demands to be let free, adamant she is their mother.
She explains she wore green contact lenses as an actress, claiming they are downstairs in her purse.
Lukas tells Elias he searched the purse and did not find them.
Elias suddenly feels uneasy about leaving Mother tied up and in pain, but Lukas persuades him to go, branding her a liar.
While waiting for a taxi nearby, Elias returns to the house, claiming he forgot to pack his toothbrush.
He looks in Mother's purse and finds the contact lenses.
Lukas appears and begs Elias to let him explain.
Elias flees to the bedroom to free Mother while Lukas disappears.
Mother takes Elias to the barn and shows him a bullet hole in one of the walls that is covered in blood.
Upon seeing it, Elias breaks down; it is revealed Elias accidentally shot and killed Lukas, meaning Lukas has been a hallucination the entire time.
His death sent Mother into a grief-stricken depression, resulting in her divorce and estrangement from Elias.
Mother attempts to console him, but in a confused rage, he lashes out and pushes Mother from the barn loft; her lantern smashes in the process, resulting in a fire.
Elias flees and tearfully watches the barn burn to the ground.
Elias has a hallucination of Mother and Lukas who appear at his side.
With a smile, Mother tells him he has done nothing wrong, and they embrace.

4862638.title: Mr. Anderson's Line
synopsis: The incessant shrill of a ringing phone slips into Alex's dreams, bringing him back to a cold, rainy morning in his Chicago apartment.

A grim, sterile voice of a hospital attendant slices through the early morning gloom, disseminating the heart-wrenching news: his mother, a woman of great strength and resilience who had single-handedly raised him back in their small suburban town, had suddenly succumbed to a heart attack.
Whiffs of despair linger in the air, seemingly closing in on Alex, accentuating his feeling of utter loneliness amidst the impersonal bustle of the Windy City.
Alex finds himself standing alone by a fresh mound of earth in the cold, windswept Greenwood Cemetery back in his hometown, a solitary mourner for his single mother.
A few mournful days pass before an antique copy of the Chicago Tribune catches his eye among his mother's belongings.

According to the advertisement, Bob Anderson, an aging businessman who once captained a successful pharmaceutical company, seeks a personal assistant to read him literature and offer him company in his vast mansion.
Seeing a chance to escape his crippling solitude and financial constraints, Alex grabs the opportunity with both hands, soon securing the role as Mr. Anderson's reader.
Bob gradually introduces Alex to tales of triumph, defeat, genius, and resilience, recounted in the pages of autobiographies of celebrated figures like Steve Jobs and Warren Buffet.

Alex, captivated by Bob's past of brilliant corporate victories and heartbreaking failures, finds his curiosity towards the old man intensifying, and Bob reciprocates, sharing increasingly personal anecdotes and life lessons borne of experience.
A surprising kinship takes root within the grand old mansion, as nights spent over volumes of memoirs and shared stories bring Alex and Bob closer.
Yet, Bob’s failing health, owning to advancing age combined with the relentless grip of a terminal illness, noticeably weakens.
Desiring to abate the bleak atmosphere surrounding Bob and perhaps offer closure, Alex musters the courage to propose connecting with his long-lost family members for one last reconciliation.
At first, Bob’s reaction is defensive, the proposed connection with his past treated with derision and resulting in further withdrawal.
As the days roll by, Bob’s wise mentorship guides Alex towards a fast-approaching transformation.
Bob's hostile response does nothing to quench Alex's resolve.
Braving anticipatory rebuttals, he quietly sets off on a stealthy mission to locate Bob's estranged family.

Sifting through stacks of dusty letters, conducting countless online searches, and enduring many a disconnected phone call, Alex navigates a labyrinth of aged information, ever determined to reunite the scattered pieces of Bob’s life.

Having borne witness to Alex’s unflinching dedication and journey of personal growth, as well as feeling the incremental frailty of his own body, Bob finally rescinds his initial protestations, announcing his decision to seek reconciliation with his family.
A charged suspense fills Bob’s study as he, with trembling hands, dials the number of his firstborn son now residing in a New York penthouse.
The first rounds of phone calls are emotionally fraught, with unanswered messages, hang-ups, and harsh rejections standing as formidable roadblocks to his quest for redemption.
But Alex and Bob persist, driven by a single shared hope of reconnection.
Their zealousness ultimately wears down the bristling defenses, allowing the tentative seeds of understanding and forgiveness to germinate.
Bob finally makes headway with Maria, his daughter, a successful lawyer in Boston, who agrees to meet the ailing man she once called father.
Bob, facing debilitating health challenges every day, sets out on a journey to reconnect with the family he had pushed away.
With every heartfelt conversation with his prodigal son and the youngest of his brood, Maria, Bob finds an unusual mix of relief and joy penetrating his spirit.
During one of their quiet reading sessions, Bob confides to Alex an unexpected decision: he wishes to bestow upon him a sizeable part of his immense fortune.

Surprised to be at the receiving end of this immense generosity, Alex, through tears welling up in his eyes, expresses heartfelt gratitude for Bob's unanticipated kindness and the meaningful impact Bob has had on his life.
In the quiet solitude of St. Luke's Hospice, with his reconciled family just minutes away, Bob’s life journey culminates.
Bob's meticulously drawn-up will is brought out solemnly.
As Alex learns of his substantial inheritance and realizes the transformative impact he had on his aged mentor’s life, a whirlwind of emotions wrestle within him.
Deeply moved by the unique benevolence of a man he grew close to in such a short time, Alex resolves to rebuild his life with the newfound inheritance.

Alex promises to prioritize the people around him, taking to heart the lessons he learned from witnessing Bob's isolation in his last days, ensuring that a similar fate does not tarnish his own life's end.

66303173.title: Mr. Harrigan's Phone
synopsis: In 2003, young Craig becomes acquainted with retired businessman John Harrigan following the death of his mother, with instructions to simply read to him three times a week.
Five years later, a teenage Craig and elderly Harrigan have become friends.
During this time, Craig starts high school and becomes close to Ms. Hart, a teacher who comes to his aid when Kenny Yankovich, a school bully, attempts to intimidate him.
After winning $3,000 from a lottery ticket that Harrigan gave him and receiving his first iPhone for Christmas, Craig buys one for Harrigan too.
Despite initial resistance to new technology, he enjoys the phone.
The elderly Harrigan dies, leaving Craig heartbroken at the loss of his friend.
At the funeral, Craig sneaks Harrigan's phone into the coffin, later being informed by Harrigan's associate that he was left a bequest in Harrigan's will.
Craig will receive $800,000 in a trust fund, to support his future studies and pursuit of a writing career, which he had told Harrigan about.
Craig calls Harrigan's phone as a gesture of thanks.
The next morning, he discovers that Harrigan sent him an odd text message, though his father chalks it up to being a bug within the iPhone itself.
Life goes on for Craig, who goes to a dance with his crush, only to be attacked by Kenny, who accuses him of  ratting out his drug-dealing activities on school grounds, getting him expelled.

Later that night, Craig calls Harrigan's phone in a fit of frustration and sadness; he tells him what Kenny did and he is "afraid that this won't end, and I wish that you were here just to give me some advice."
Kenny is found dead the next day, having apparently fallen from his bedroom window while attempting to sneak out.
Scared by what happened, Craig goes to an Apple store, upgrades his phone to a newer model, and puts away his old one.
Craig graduates from high school and departs for college in Boston to study journalism.
While there, his father calls to tell him Ms. Hart was killed in a car accident involving a drunk driver, leaving her fiancé hospitalized.
The driver, Dean Whitmore, is sent to rehab instead of prison for the accident although he'd been caught for drunk driving on other occasions, his license was suspended and he had an open container.
Infuriated by the verdict, Craig returns to his room and uses his old phone to call Harrigan, explicitly wishing death on Whitmore.
Craig later learns Whitmore was found dead in his shower.
He drives to the rehab center and bribes a worker there to give him details about the suicide.
He is told that Whitmore swallowed shampoo and a piece of broken soap bar.
Craig is disturbed to learn that the soap is the same brand used by Ms. Hart, and Whitmore's suicide note is actually a lyric from the song "Stand by Your Man" by Tammy Wynette; Harrigan's ringtone.
Craig breaks down and returns to his hometown.
While there, he remembers opening Harrigan's "secret closet" (which he had refused to let Craig enter) after he passed, that it was actually a shrine to his deceased mother.
He visits his gravestone, apologizing for his messages.
He theorizes that Harrigan's odd text messages to him are his way of begging Craig to let his spirit rest in peace and for him to move forward in the here and now.
As he leaves Harrigan's grave, Craig visits his own mother's and collapses in tears, begging for forgiveness.
He then rushes to the town quarry, contemplating the water while standing very near the edge before throwing his phone into the water.
As Craig walks away, he quietly narrates that when he himself passes on and is buried, he wants his pockets to be empty.

56582294.title: Race Revolution (film)
synopsis: Our tale commences with the imposing figure of John Smith standing commandingly in a bustling, yet pin-drop silent, boardroom.
Positioned as the head of marketing at the prestigious London-based advertising agency, Linco, John outlines his revolutionary vision "The Speed Institute".
This project harbors potential to reshape conventional racing norms - he proposes to sculpt esports racers into formidable Formula One opponents.

An unmistakable fervor in his voice, Smith proceeds to elucidate his transformative vision, painting a vivid picture of how esports racers could disrupt the conventional contours of Formula One racing.
He stands firm in his belief of harnessing the untapped potential of virtual racers.
The camera pans across a sea of screens in a cavernous auditorium.

It focuses on Cadence, a young eSport racer, her fingers flying over the console with immense precision, her gaze intense as she maintains a tight grip on her digital victory in the globally acclaimed racing video game, "Gran Turismo Sport".
On-screen, Cadence crosses the finish line emerging triumphant.
Bathed in the euphoria of her victory, Cadence scans her digital dashboard, on which flashes an advertisement of "The Speed Institute".
Amidst the virtual confetti and congratulatory flashes, the advertisement commands attention.
Piqued by the potential this opportunity heralds, Cadence feels a magnetic pull towards this novel concept.
In hopeful anticipation, she submits her application to the institute.
Going through her routine job as a supermarket cashier, her dreams of a racing career gleam brighter.
Weeks pass until one day, Cadence opens her email to find the much-awaited acceptance from the Speed Institute.
Ecstatic, she accepts their offer and embarks on her dream journey to a state-of-the-art training facility nestled in the heart of Monaco.
Arriving at the Institute, Cadence is taken aback by its grandeur.
The state-of-the-art training facility boasts a fully integrated Formula One-inspired racing circuit, technologically laden simulation rooms, and research labs.
Plunging headfirst into the demanding training program, Cadence soon realizes that real-world racing is a far cry from the digital world she has conquered.
The transition from a virtual environment to the physical race track proves to be a huge challenge.
Her efforts are often met with derision from a seasoned Formula One racer who dismisses her as an only gaming-skilled competitor.
This ridicule adds to her already challenging training journey.
The dismissive remarks threaten to erode Cadence's resolve.
In defiance against her critics, she channels the mockery into fuel for her determination.
Each failure she encounters transforms into a rung on the ladder of her growth.
Painstakingly honing her skills, Cadence garners a better understanding of real-world racing dynamics and develops a firm grip on her driving techniques.
The intensity on the circuit rises steadily until one fateful day, a gut-wrenching crash reverberates through the training circuit.
A fellow trainee's car ejects him in a shocking display of the dangers in racing.
The accident leaves Cadence and the Institute shell-shocked, as the gravity of the mortal risks in this high-speed pursuit confront her.
The injured trainee's condition, critical and teetering on the edge, casts a shadow across Cadence's ambition.
Undertones of fear combined with twinges of uncertainty creep into Cadence's ambitious heart, forcing her to reconsider her commitment to this risky career path.
Watching the injured trainee's determination to recover and return to the track rekindles her resolve.

70878102.title: Gran Turismo (film)
synopsis: Following a pitch by marketing executive Danny Moore, Nismo, the motorsport division of Nissan, establishes the GT Academy to recruit skilled players of the racing simulator Gran Turismo and turn them into real racing drivers.
Danny recruits former driver-turned-mechanic Jack Salter to train the players.
Jack is initially hesitant but accepts after tiring of the arrogance of his team's driver, Nicholas Capa.

Meanwhile, Jann Mardenborough, a teenage clothing store employee and gamer from Cardiff, is an avid player of the simulator and wants to become a racing driver, despite the disapproval of his former footballer father Steve.
One day, Jann learns he is eligible for a qualification race to join the GT Academy after setting a time record for a particular track.
The night before his race, Jann is invited by his brother Coby to a party, and the brothers take their father's car.
Jann flirts with a young woman named Audrey whom he develops a crush on.
The gathering is disbanded after police arrive, and Jann initiates a pursuit after driving away when their friends are pulled over.
The brothers escape but are caught returning by their father.
Coby starts to worry, but Jann offers to take the blame for him if he admits that he is the better driver.

Jann is taken to his father's place of employment the next morning in an attempt to be taught a life lesson, but leaves early to partake in the qualifying race, which he wins, earning a place in GT Academy.
At the academy camp, Jack puts the competitors through their paces in various tests, through which ten competitors are narrowed down to five.
During one of the tests, Jann crashes with Jack in the car and claims that the brakes were glazed.
This is later proven correct by analysts, to Jack's surprise.
The remaining five compete in a final race to determine who will represent Nissan.
Jann narrowly wins the race against American competitor Matty Davis, but Danny insists Matty should be chosen as the representative due to his better commercial viability.
However, Jann is chosen at Jack's insistence.
Jann is told that if he finishes at least fourth in any one of a series of qualifying races, he will earn a professional licence and contract with Nissan.

He finishes last in his first professional race in Austria after Nicholas taps him into a spin, and despite gradually improving over the next few races, he does not finish the penultimate race in Spain.
He travels to Dubai for his last qualifying race, during which Nicholas takes a corner too fast and crashes.
Despite the debris from this crash cracking his windshield, Jann achieves a fourth-place finish and earns his license.
He then travels to Tokyo with Danny and Jack to sign his contract and uses his signing bonus to fly Audrey to Tokyo.
During this time, they initiate a relationship.
Jann's first race after signing is at the Nürburgring Nordschleife.
He starts the race well and maintains a high position until the front of his car lifts into the air at the Flugplatz corner, hitting a barrier and launching into a crowded spectator area.
Jann is airlifted to the Nürburgring Medical Center and is informed while in hospital that a spectator was killed in the crash, much to his horror.
When Jann is reluctant to return to racing and blames himself for the spectator's death, Jack takes him back to the Nürburgring.
He reveals that he was involved in a fatal accident at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, which led to a fellow driver dying and subsequently Jack's retirement from driving.
An inquiry clears Jann of any wrongdoing, but professional sentiment begins to turn against sim drivers.
In response, Danny decides that a sim driver team needs to compete at Le Mans and finish on the podium to prove their viability.
Danny enlists Matty and fellow GT Academy participant Antonio Cruz to make up the three-driver team alongside Jann.
On race day, Jann's father apologizes for not initially being supportive of his passions.

Early in the race, Jann is left shaken after one of the competitors crashes and catches fire, but is encouraged through his first shift by Jack playing "Songbird" and "Orinoco Flow" through the car's communication system, songs which Jann had previously used as motivational music during training.
Matty and Antonio complete their first shifts without issue, but the latter is brought in from his last session early due to experiencing cramps.
A wheel nut is dropped by mechanic Felix during the pit stop, causing Jann to lose several positions.
Deviating from advised racing lines, he uses instead lines he learned from playing Gran Turismo to regain his position, breaking the lap record in the process.
The final lap sees Jann pitted against Nicholas, with Jann once again narrowly in front on the final straight to earn third place and a podium finish for Nissan.
In the epilogue, the real Jann Mardenborough is shown having competed in over 200 races and served as his own stunt double in the film.

12711147.title: Serendipity: The Unexpected Arrival (movie)
synopsis: The narrative commences with a stark introduction into the hectic routines of the populous Saint Mary's City Hospital’s maternity ward.
We witness the crux of activity - birth under the watchful eyes of Dr. Smith, Nurse Rose, and Mrs. Turner.

The electronically operated sliding doors of the ward graciously part to reveal Kate Larson, a high-profile corporate lawyer, and her husband Mike, a free-spirited conductor for the city's eminent orchestra.
Mrs. Turner thoughtfully leads the anxious couple into the soothing light-blue examination room.
The couple's five-year chase to conceive takes center stage in the form of a soulful ballad.
Dr. Smith reveals that Kate is not just pregnant but already seven centimeters dilated.
The second act delves into a whirlpool of raw emotions, Mike and Kate grapple with this abrupt transition - from the perpetual struggle with infertility to the imminent certainty of parenthood.

A string of comedic scenes follows Mike who keels over from the startling announcement and amusingly scrabbles around for their neglected hospital bag and documents, meanwhile, Kate grapples to maintain composure as her body is wracked with powerful contractions.
In a hushed corner of her warmly lit hospital room, Kate takes center stage with a sincerity-filled monologue about motherhood.
To counterbalance his tumult of feelings, Mike retreats into his passion for music.

Then, the narrative peers into the rookie parents' baptism by fire - long sleepless nights, recurring checkups at Dr. Smith's clinic, and impromptu trips to 'Baby Love,' the city's largest baby store.
As Kate's labor accelerates rapidly, the third act welcomes the final act of birth.
Giving visual form to his escalating fear and growing excitement, Mike envisions conducting an orchestra, his hands portraying the pulsating cadence of Kate's labor contractions.
Kate's laboring pain resounds against the stirring crescendos of the Beethoven Symphony No.9 playing over the hospital's PA system.
The fourth act is a testament to the Larson couple's relentless journey into parenthood.
The audience witnesses them battling sleep deprivation while juggling the demanding routine of feedings and diaper changes.
In moments of respite amidst the chaos, Mike finds solace in playing Mozart's tunes on his old piano, evoking gurgles of delight from their child.
Similarly, Kate embraces the tranquility that their son's innocent toothless smiles bring.
Inspired by these significant interactions with their son, Mike composes a sweet lullaby, and Kate sings the lullaby, lulling their restless baby boy to a peaceful slumber.
Back at Saint Mary’s Hospital, the medical team - Dr. Smith, Nurse Rose, and Mrs. Turner bid the Larson family a fond farewell.
Each medical professional delivers a solo performance, capturing their unique perspectives about the birth process they assist every day.
The musical draws to a fitting close with an ensemble performance bidding adieu to the characters - the novice parents, the patients, and medical staff.
The Larson family's narrative leaves the audience teary-eyed, their hearts brimming with laughter, and an understanding of the beautiful pandemonium that comes with parenthood.
The finale of this musical unfolds on a celebratory note, saluting the endless circle of life and its resonance within the maternity ward's halls, even long after Mike and Kate's departure.

68784878.title: Matilda the Musical (film)
synopsis: In a hospital, while other parents adore their newborn children, Mrs Wormwood is distraught to learn she is pregnant and in labour.
To her husband Mr Wormwood's confusion, she gives birth to a girl, Matilda.
Despite her parents' constant disdain, Matilda becomes a sweet child who loves reading and visits the mobile librarian Mrs Phelps daily.
Upon discovering that Matilda has not been properly schooled, teacher Miss Jennifer Honey and an inspector visit the house to suggest Matilda be sent to Crunchem Hall.
Angry about being fined for not sending his daughter to school, Mr Wormwood warns the severe headmistress, Miss Agatha Trunchbull, about Matilda.
In retaliation, Matilda mixes green hair dye into his hair tonic.
Before school, Matilda tells Mrs Phelps a story about an escapologist who falls in love with and marries an acrobat.
Arriving at school, Matilda and her fellow new student Lavender are warned about the terrible way the students are treated there.
In Honey's classroom, Matilda solves a complex mathematical equation on the board and confesses that she loves reading most.
An impressed Honey asks Trunchbull to move Matilda to a more advanced class, but Trunchbull refuses to let Matilda be an exception to the rules.
At home, when Matilda criticizes her father, he rips her book apart and wrongly sends her to bed; the next day, she retaliates by gluing his hat to his head.
During the students' lunch, Trunchbull falsely accuses Matilda of stealing a slice of her private chocolate cake, but Bruce Bogtrotter accidentally reveals he is the culprit by belching.
Trunchbull forces him to eat the entire cake, saying he will be forgiven if he eats every last crumb.
Bruce's success thrills Matilda, Honey, and the students, but Trunchbull still punishes him by taking him out to the Chokey.

After school, Matilda returns to Mrs Phelps and continues her story: the now-pregnant acrobat is forced to perform a dangerous stunt by her stepsister; she is horribly injured and dies after giving birth to a daughter.
The escapologist forgives the stepsister and asks her to help him raise his daughter.
The stepsister blames the daughter for her stepsister's death and secretly abuses her.
When the escapologist discovers his daughter is mistreated, he never returns from confronting the stepsister.
The next day, Trunchbull forces the children through challenging exercises to crush their rebelliousness.
Lavender slips her pet newt into her drinking water, and after Matilda stands up to Trunchbull, she uses her newly discovered telekinesis to embarrass Trunchbull.
Honey invites Matilda to her cottage, where Matilda learns that the escapologist and the acrobat were Miss Honey's parents and the evil stepsister is Trunchbull.
Honey tries to warn Matilda about Trunchbull's dangerousness, but she doesn't care.
She then goes to the Chokey and uses her telekinesis to destroy it.
Returning home, Matilda learns that her father has cheated the mafia and the family will be fleeing to Spain, distressing Matilda about never seeing her friends again.
When the children return to school, Trunchbull forces Honey's class to spell words correctly or be locked in a new Chokey.
She has Lavender spell a made-up word, tricking the other children into purposely spelling words incorrectly in rebellion.
Trunchbull then reveals that she made a multitude of new Chokeys for every single child to be put in.
Matilda uses her telekinesis to pretend to be the vengeful ghost of Honey's father, then destroys all the Chokeys and throws Trunchbull out of the school.
Honey tells Trunchbull never to return and takes back the keys to her father's house.
After Trunchbull runs away, the students openly revolt and destroy Trunchbull's statue.
Mr and Mrs Wormwood come to take Matilda to Spain with them, but before they can leave, Honey pleads with them to let Matilda stay with her.
They reluctantly agree to let Matilda stay, who uses her powers to unglue her father's hat.
With Miss Honey as the new headmistress, the students rename Crunchem Hall "The Big Friendly School" and renovate the school with a new playground and a giraffe.
When Matilda finishes her story for Mrs Phelps, she is overjoyed that Matilda's true story has a happy ending, in which Matilda and Miss Honey live happily together.

13622801.title: Echoes from Whispering Pines
synopsis: Our story plunge into a scene at Whispering Pines, a secluded re-education facility surrounded by towering, ancient pines.
In the dank, chilly silence, a figure brutally executes a lone staff member, setting a grim and haunting atmosphere for the film.
The narrative shifts to a bustling police station.
In this chaotic setting, we meet our protagonist, Sam Baltazar.
She's an astute detective with an innate curiosity about the paranormal that sets her apart from her colleagues.
Her world tilts when the news of the execution at Whispering Pines infiltrates the noise of the station.
Despite her peers' skepticism about the rural facility, Sam is selected for the investigation.
Sam ventures to the haunting realm of Whispering Pines.
Upon reaching, Sam promptly begins her daunting quest for truth.
She interviews panicked staff and petrified attendees, collecting fragments of strange occurrences and barely spoken fears that have taken root in the facility.
An unusual encounter with a local villager thickens the mystery.
The villager shares chilling tales of an ethereal entity rumored to haunt the nearby forest.
In an unexpected turn of events, the elusive murderer strikes again.
Sam's path intertwines with that of Dr. Paul Clayton, a respected psychiatrist stationed in Whispering Pines.
Shaken by the escalating violence, Dr. Clayton is thrown into the increasingly bewildering mystery.
Sam and Dr. Clayton find themselves forced to entertain the uncanny possibility of a supernatural perpetrator due to the inexplicably eerie circumstances surrounding the murders.
One fateful night, Sam witnesses the spectral entity first hand – an encounter that pivots the trajectory of her investigation.
With invigorated determination, Sam and the increasingly beleaguered Dr. Clayton delve into the town’s historical archives and musty folklore.
They discover a series of chilling oral tales recounting a vengeful spirit rumored to have once roamed the woods surrounding the Whispering Pines.
These local legends allude that the wrathful spirit was provoked by territorial violations - parallels that ominously align with the establishment of Whispering Pines.
When Dr. Clayton tragically becomes the recipient of the entity’s rage, Sam faces peril in her solitary pursuit for justice.
Overwhelmed by grief and isolation, Sam pieces together the correlation between the local folklore, the establishment of Whispering Pines, and the ongoing bloodshed.
Sam unveils her theory to the local council members, only to be met with disbelief.
Sam makes a bold resolution – to face the menacing being herself.
Beneath the spectral glow of moonlight, she faithfully performs a nearly forgotten ritual deeply entrenched in local folklore, in an attempt to establish a connection with the supernatural adversary.
The menacing entity,  emerges from the shadows, leading to a dialogue that riddles the viewers with chilling anticipation.
Sam negotiates with the entity, promising to restore the spirit’s dominion in exchange for an end to the bloodshed, delivering an unexpected twist to the unfolding terror.
After the confrontation, the local council acknowledges the grim reality of their situation, agreeing to dismantle Whispering Pines, marking a victory for Sam.
The film ends with a depiction of Whispering Pines under Sam's watchful eye.

68832093.title: They/Them (film)
synopsis: At night, a mysterious figure kills a person driving to a conversion camp known as Whistler Camp.
In the morning, a group of LGBTQ people arrive at Whistler Camp, run by Owen Whistler.
He introduces the camp as an inclusive safe space and promises that they will not try to forcibly convert them.
Owen separates the campers into cabins for boys and girls, but Jordan, who is non-binary, is not comfortable going to either.
Owen assigns Jordan to the boys' cabin.
The group comes together in a circle and shares why they came to Whistler Camp.
Jordan says they made a deal with their religious family to attend for a week so they could legally emancipate themself.
The next morning, Owen criticizes and outs another member, Alexandra, for not sharing that she is trans.
He makes her go to the boys' cabin for dishonesty.
Alexandra later convinces the camp's new nurse, Molly, to give her estradiol, an estrogen hormone.
The group partakes in activities overseen by former member and athletics director Zane and his fiancée, activities director Sarah.
One night, Owen splits the group into pairs, handcuffing them together, and instructs them to walk into the woods alone.
The group is hesitant, but Owen promises that they will regroup in the morning.
Jordan and Alexandra see a mysterious person in the woods.
The next day, the camp's therapist, Dr. Cora Whistler, belittles members of the group for their sexualities and gender identities, including Jordan.
Affected by Dr. Cora's words, Jordan returns to the boy's cabin upset but is cheered up when the group hosts a dance party to "Perfect" by Pink.
That night, Jordan sneaks into the main office and discovers photographs that show the history of Whistler Camp, including the torturing of children.
Jordan is caught by Molly, who says she did not know and promises to protect the group.
The camp's groundskeeper, Balthazar, is killed by the mysterious figure while observing the girls showering through a spy cam.
The next day, the group is divided by gender.
Owen takes the boys to a shooting range while the girls make pies for the boys.
Jordan defeats Zane in a shooting competition.
Owen reverts to calling Jordan "he" instead of "they".
Owen instructs Toby, a gay man, to shoot Owen's dog, Duke, because Duke has cancer.
If he refuses to do so, Zane will start to torture Duke by breaking the dog's legs.
Jordan kills Duke instead and storms off.
Jordan, Alexandra, and Toby agree to leave Whistler Camp in the morning.
Gabriel reveals he works for Whistler Camp.
Owen and Zane force Stu to participate in aversion therapy, a form of electroshock torture that Owen says will make Stu heterosexual.
Upon finding Stu unconscious, Molly quits and says she will go to the police.
Owen threatens her to stay.
The mysterious figure butchers Zane and Sarah and fatally electrocutes Gabriel.
Every person at Whistler Camp comes together after finding the dead bodies.
The murderer kills Cora.
Alexandra leads the younger members out of the camp.
The murderer reveals herself to be Molly.
Her real name is Angie Phelps.
She murdered the real Molly to take her place as the camp nurse.
Angie attended Whistler Camp and was tortured there by Owen.
She made it her mission to close every conversion camp in existence by killing the complicit employees.
Angie attacks Owen but is unable to gain the upper hand.
Jordan takes Owen's gun but does not shoot, giving Angie the time to kill Owen herself.
Angie tries talking Jordan into helping her, but Jordan refuses.
The police arrest Angie.
The group agrees to live their lives to the fullest.

23073940.title: Orbit Repair: A Space Journey
synopsis: Renowned for his heroism on the Apollo-50 mission, Richard Patterson, a seasoned astronaut, assumes a powerful leadership position within NASA's vibrant and bustling command center.
His years of experience and wisdom fall upon a diverse team—each member carrying an essential piece of the puzzle in pioneering humanity's leap into space.

Alongside Richard, Margaret "Meg" Smith, a gifted space engineer whose genius rivals that of the creators of the Hubble telescope, serves as a steady voice of reason and logic—an intellectual powerhouse in the team.

Joining this elite team with a heart pounding with nerves and excitement, Jack Philips steps into the world of “Orbital Engineers”—an adept group of repair and maintenance maestros navigating the void of outer space.

Richard and Meg, often seen swapping playful banter and classic jibes, not only showcase a camaraderie that was formed decades ago during their first NASA training but also a deep-seated respect and understanding for each other—admirable pillars of their enduring friendship.
Jack, fueled by an ambition that could even compete with the pioneering Wright brothers, puts everything on the line.
He spends countless hours honing his orbital maneuvering and emergency repair skills, determined to master every complexity and nuance of this art.

Their mission—to repair the Hubble Space Telescope that is playing havoc with astronomical tracking on Earth— set forth a daring ascent into the void of space aboard the technologically advanced SpaceX Dragon spacecraft.
As they near the iconic Hubble, tension blankets the cabin.
The team diligently prepares for their endeavor, equipping themselves with their Extravehicular Mobility Units (EMUs) and unfurling their toolkit against the backdrop of cold, unwavering stars.

During his maiden spacewalk, Jack meticulously documents each of his actions on the spacecraft’s state-of-the-art onboard computer system before taking on the critical task of maintenance on the Hubble.

However, what started as an ordinary expedition pivots towards disaster when, hidden within the complex workings of the Hubble, they unearth a time bomb threatening devastation on an unprecedented scale.
Fear, painted across Jack's green eyes, is echoed amongst the crew.
Still, Richard and Meg composure remains unwavering, a testament to their years of rigorous astronautical training and emotional resilience.
With the ticking bomb as their ominous companion, Meg and Jack throw themselves into work.
The weight of humanity's survival lies heavy on their shoulders, entrusted to their space-suited forms.
The situation spirals when the dormant bomb triggers a slew of anomalies in the linked GPS satellites, compounding challenges on Earth.

Amid a barrage of stray satellites set loose by the bomb’s detonation, Richard sustains a crippling injury that incapacitates him—leaving the less-experienced Meg and Jack adrift in a sea of mounting challenges.
Out of necessity, Meg and Jack find themselves shouldering the relentless tasks of satellite salvage operations and the urgent disarmament of the deadly bomb.

Despite his agonizing injury, Richard calls upon every shred of willpower to guide Meg and Jack, fueling them with much-needed practical wisdom and advice through the agony that threatens to engulf him.
Demonstrating exceptional courage and determination, Meg and Jack formulate a daring strategy to halt the countdown of the bomb while simultaneously combating the satellite anomalies.

With the clock mercilessly ticking away and leaving them a paltry hour to achieve their goals, they dive into their plan—hands steady, movements precise, and minds fixated on the monumental task despite the stress escalator.

The frantic voices from Houston’s Mission Control are drowned in the sea of time constraints, leaving the astronauts to rely solely on their instincts, experience, and the fruits of their intensive training.
Pitted against astronomical odds and guided by Richard’s vital advice, Meg and Jack push aside their fears and throw themselves into a race against time, leaving no room for error.
In the face of impending disaster, with merely seconds on the countdown clock, they manage to disarm the bomb and rectify the malfunctioning satellites—pulling Earth from the jaws of catastrophe.
However, the fiasco takes a tragic turn when Richard's life is swiftly teetering on the edge due to his grievous injuries.
Despite their desperate efforts and hopeful prayers, Richard succumbs to his wounds.
His final moments blossom in the deafening silence aboard the spacecraft, his last act symbolizing a hero's sacrifice for humanity, mirrored in the last flicker of his life.
Back on Earth, Mission Control and the world erupt into euphoria as the systems revert to normal, narrowly averting the disaster that had held its breath to strike.

Returning to Earth as celebrated heroes, Meg and Jack, enshrouded in exhaustion, wear their victory as a mantle— their faces glowing through the weariness, the testament of an adventure that was as harrowing as it was triumphant.
Richard's brave deed joins the annals of space history, his heroic saga destined to inspire future generations toward astronomical aspirations.
Having undergone a profound metamorphosis amid a crisis, Jack steps into Richard's enormous shoes, carrying forward his legacy and teachings for future missions.

As the story concludes on a heartrending note, Richard's sacrifice carves a path of honor in the annals of space history—providing a stepping stone for Jack, who strides forward to helm future missions, with the ever-dependable Meg always at his side.
The history of space exploration carries forth, enriched by sacrifice, culminating in hope for humanity's cosmic journey.

60694612.title: Moonfall (film)
synopsis: In 2011, astronauts Brian Harper, Jocinda "Jo" Fowler, and newcomer Alan Marcus are on a Space Shuttle mission to repair a satellite.
A mysterious swarm of alien technology attacks the orbiter, killing Alan and knocking Jo unconscious before tunneling into the surface of the Moon.
Brian, the only witness to the swarm, returns the crippled shuttle to Earth, but his story is dismissed and he is fired from NASA.
Ten years later, conspiracy theorist K.C.
Houseman, who believes that the Moon is an artificial megastructure, secretly uses a research telescope.
He discovers that the Moon's orbit is veering closer to Earth, and tries to share his findings with the disgraced Brian.
NASA also discovers the anomaly, but K.C.
goes public on social media, leading to a global panic.
Jo is now NASA's deputy director, launching a spacecraft on an SLS Block 1 rocket to investigate the abnormality.
The same alien swarm attacks, killing all three lunar astronauts after they drop a probe into a kilometers-deep artificial shaft that has opened up on the Moon's surface.
As the lunar orbit deteriorates, the Moon falls closer and closer to the Earth, causing seismic and gravitational disturbances.

Jo meets former NASA official Holdenfield, who reveals that Brian was discredited due to a NASA coverup dating back to Apollo 11; during the first Moon landing, a two-minute radio blackout was meant to conceal evidence of pulsating lights on the surface.
Apollo 12 revealed that the Moon is hollow, and a military EMP device created to kill the swarm was abandoned for budgetary reasons.

With help from her ex-husband General Doug Davidson, Air Force Chief of Staff, Jo requisitions the EMP and rescues retired Space Shuttle Endeavour from a museum to serve the new mission: to correct the Moon's orbit and destroy the swarm.
Brian, K.C., and Jo launch with the EMP, narrowly escaping to orbit as a tsunami destroys Vandenberg Air Force Base.
They reach the interior of the Moon, revealed to be a Dyson sphere powered by a white dwarf at its center.

The Dyson sphere's AI operating system explains to Brian that billions of years ago, humanity's technologically advanced ancestors were eradicated by a rogue AI; they built the Moon as an Interstellar ark to create and seed life on Earth, but the swarm — the malicious AI — discovered the Moon and is siphoning energy from its power source, destabilizing its orbit.

Meanwhile, Brian's son Sonny, Jo's son Jimmy, and his caretaker Michelle try to reach Doug's military bunker in the Colorado mountains, finding Brian's ex-wife and Sonny's mother Brenda, her husband Tom, and their step-family.
Escaping disasters caused by the Moon's proximity and fighting off other survivors, the group finds safety in a mountain tunnel.
When his youngest daughter runs out of oxygen, an injured Tom gives her his own, suffocating to death as the Moon strips away the local atmosphere.
The president orders a nuclear strike on the approaching Moon, but Doug refuses to comply, with debris collapsing the bunker shortly thereafter, presumably killing Doug and everyone inside.
As the swarm only attacks organic life in the presence of electronic activity, K.C.
lures the swarm away from their spacecraft with their lunar module, sacrificing himself to detonate the EMP.
Jo and Brian return to Earth, reuniting with their families, and the Moon's power is restored, returning to its regular orbit, but now shed of its rocky exterior.
Reconstructing K.C.
's consciousness, the Moon's operating system appears to him as his cat, Fuzz Aldrin, and his mother, remarking that they must now "get started".

38804048.title: Spin the Record (film)
synopsis: Samantha, a dynamic CEO of a globally acclaimed Fortune 500 company, emerges as a towering figure in the corporate world.
Despite her success, she battles an incessant dissatisfaction caused by the monotonous pattern of her life.
An unexpected turn of events unfurls when her lifelong best friend and trusted confidante, Zoe, introduces her to the intriguing character of her half-brother, Jackson.
Jackson, a charismatic free-spirit, runs a quaint cultural hotspot in town - a vintage vinyl shop named Treasure Hunt that resonates with old-world charm.
Samantha's curiosity piqued, she is taken in by Jackson’s unwavering dedication to his vinyl records.
In an unexpected burst of spontaneity, she decides to venture into the colorful and pulsating world of music.
Samantha becomes an avid visitor at Treasure Hunt, guided by Jackson's patient mentorship.
The relationship between Samantha and Jackson delves deeper with every shared song, strengthening their bond.
However, Samantha's deliberate shunning of her work to pursue her interest in music stirs a crisis of high-stakes within her corporation.
Simultaneously, another crisis surfaces as Jackson struggles to keep the doors of Treasure Hunt open amidst the prevailing digitally-driven music industry.
The looming threat of bankruptcy hovers over their beloved music sanctuary, shaking the foundations of happiness they found in their shared affinity.
Samantha, emboldened by her passion for music, decides to tap into her corporate acumen and strategizes to save Treasure Hunt.
Samantha meticulously strategizes a robust business model that aims to rekindle the lost allure of vinyl.
Simultaneously, she devises a strategic blueprint to navigate her company out of the looming crisis.
Samantha's twofold battle presents a gripping climax.
Despite overwhelming challenges, Samantha and Jackson merge their resources and resolve to salvage their serene music sanctuary, Treasure Hunt.
The dynamic duo ingeniously integrates their shared love for vinyl with savvy marketing strategies, setting off a wave of renewed interest.
Simultaneously, Samantha successfully maneuvers her company out of crisis, affirming her position and stature in the corporate sphere.
The shared victory presents an opportunity for a heartfelt romantic revelation.
Samantha and Jackson confront the emotional undercurrent between them, confessing their feelings for one another.
Their hard-fought journey culminates in a soulful confession of love.
The couple host a spirited music event at the revived Treasure Hunt, marking a milestone in their shared exploit.

69199196.title: Press Play (film)
synopsis: Laura's friend Chloe introduces her to her stepbrother, Harrison, who works at the record store Lost & Found.
They immediately connect and attend a Japanese Breakfast show together.
She meets the record store's owner, Cooper.
At the beach, Harrison gifts Laura a cassette so they can create a mixtape.
They celebrate after learning an art-related mentorship has accepted Laura.
He mentions his intentions of moving to attend medical school but is interrupted by an earthquake.
At her house, she shows him her art.
Harrison's parents tell Laura that Harrison is going to a medical school on the other side of the country.
Harrison privately tells Laura he does not want to go so he can stay with her.
She tells him she does not want to be the reason he gives up on his dreams; he reassures her of his decision to stay.
They attend her art exhibition.
On his birthday, they finish painting a mural.
The next day, Harrison is hit and killed by a car.
Laura destroys the mural and leaves behind her mixtape at Lost & Found.
Four years later, Laura attends Chloe's wedding.
Cooper gives Laura her mixtape back.
She goes home to listen to it.
After pressing play, Laura is transported to her first date with Harrison at the Japanese Breakfast concert.
After a brief moment, she returns to the present.
Every time she presses play, the mixtape sends her back in time.
She does it again and appears on their date at the beach.
She warns him about his future death and convinces him by predicting the earthquake seconds before it happens.
In the present, she learns she is affecting the future after learning Chloe has married a different, obnoxious man instead of her soulmate.
She learns Harrison had died the same day from falling off a cliff.
Her next click sends her to the time she showed Harrison her art.
She warns him to stay away from the cliffs.
This time, after returning, she learns Harrison died from electrocution after stepping on a downed power line.
She presses play again and now appears at the party hosted at Lost & Found where they talked about their future, but her time is cut short.
Her actions altered their timeline to where Lost & Found burned down with Harrison inside and the mixtape is no longer in her possession.
She visits a depressed Cooper, gets the mixtape from this timeline, and tells Cooper about its powers.
Cooper mentions the possibility that she is not supposed to save him but she tries anyway.
Harrison still died, this time in a car accident with his dad.
Once again, Laura presses play.
She appears at her art exhibition.
She tells Harrison to break up with her and go to medical school.
In the present, she tries calling him but the call goes straight to voicemail.
She immediately presses play again and appears in their last important moment: the day they finished the mural.
She confronts him for not breaking up but Harrison says he would rather risk staying with her than leaving and dying anyway.
In the present, Laura forces herself to accept the fact she cannot be with Harrison.
While at Chloe's, she discovers an additional song on the B-side of the cassette.
The song sends her back in time to the moment they were going to meet for the first time.
She decides to save his life by not stepping inside Lost & Found.
In the present, a cheerful Chloe invites Laura to Christmas dinner.
Chloe is married to her soulmate as the changes to the timeline have been reverted.
Harrison arrives and introduces himself to Laura.

8324326.title: SAS: Crimson Hawks
synopsis: Our narrative starts with an illuminated shot of urban London's upscale architecture.
Tucked within its heart, an office bathed in warm hues from the setting sun is revealed; this is the headquarters of the Scarlet Hawks.
The Hawks, a private military contractor group, were formed by three former SAS operatives, the Anderson trio - James, Ethan, and Lily.
Their camaraderie and mutual respect form the foundation on which the Hawks operate.
Our introduction to the Hawks is in the throes of an intense hostage-rescue simulation in an old, abandoned warehouse.

Each member's distinctive skills are on full display: while James is the strategic genius, making high-level split-second decisions, Ethan's strength lies in close-quarters combat, he's as deadly as a bullet ricocheting in an Echo box.
On the other hand, Lily, though petite, packs a punch with her unusual precision as a sniper; her bullet never strays.
Interruption arrives in the form of a call from the UK's Secretary of State, Richard Simmons.
His voice, nervous and shaky, reveals an imminent global crisis: a group of genetic scientists had been kidnapped and held hostage somewhere in Eastern Europe.
He earnestly entreats the Scarlet Hawks for their expert services.
As the evening thickens, under a dimly lit room in their headquarters, James reveals his haunted past.
His decision to leave the SAS was precipitated by the loss of his beloved wife Laura during a disastrous Iraq mission.
This tragedy nurtured a paralyzing fear within him - the fear of his younger siblings meeting the same fate.
They debate over the perils of the mission, each member wrestling with their thoughts.
Yet, they understand the potential catastrophe the kidnapped scientists may face.
The decision to accept the mission is unanimous despite the gnawing fear of failure.
James' detailed mission briefing underlines the significant risk involved.
The hostile forces' remote location promises danger at every turn.
He mentions the double agent from the SAS who could potentially hinder their mission, casting a shadow of doubt and tension amongst the trio.
Gearing up for the mission, a hush descends upon their armoury.
Each piece of equipment they handle tells a tale of their hardened resolve.
The Hawks' mission commences.
An ancient 14th-century fortress hidden in the wilderness of Eastern Europe is the backdrop of their operation.
Every perfectly orchestrated move, every taut muscle, every bead of sweat trickling down their faces underscores their combined strengths.
But just when victory seems within reach, a surprise, a surge of reinforcements turn the tables.
It becomes clear that the SAS mole has leaked information of their operation, forcing them into an early evacuation.
Lily, covering their retreat, is cornered by the enemy.
Eerily quiet and bloodstained, she disappears into the enemy camp, her distress evident through her body cam footage.
James and Ethan are overcome with desperation, but their resolve to find their sister and save the captive scientists is unwavering.
Meanwhile, Lily, held in a damp, dark cell within the belly of the enemy camp, demonstrates her survival instincts with her charming wit and quick thinking.
She uses her guile to plant the seeds of rebellion within a young, tentative enemy soldier.
Back in London, James and Ethan uncover interconnecting webs of this plot, revealing the multinational corporation's sinister plan of manipulating genomes for global dominance.
This realization strengthens their need to subvert this catastrophe and save Lily.
The third act opens with a heart-pounding rescue mission.

James and Ethan chart their course meticulously, smuggling their way through the labyrinth of ancient tunnels inside the fortress, evading deadly traps and combating their way to where the scientists are held captive.

Simultaneously, Lily, using a rudimentary shiv, convinces her hesitant caretaker into sparking a revolt amongst their captors, causing a commotion and providing an excellent distraction for her brothers.
James and Ethan press onwards to a tense showdown on the fortress battlements, ultimately identifying the SAS mole - Simon Bradley.
At the same time, Lily and Ethan, amidst the chaos unleashed by the rebellion, free the captive scientists, and move towards the extraction point.
James outsmarts the traitor wildly outmatching him in a riveting hand-to-hand combat sequence.
With Simon and the terrorist leader taken care of, the Hawks manage to avert the catastrophe in the nick of time.
Our narrative arc closes with the much-battered, yet triumphant Scarlet Hawks in a military chopper, returning home along with the liberated scientists.
The Anderson siblings are reunited, a disaster averted, wrapping up the plotline with a comforting moment of peace from the Hawks' London base.
But, as in life, peace isn't everlasting.
General Richard Stone, a high-ranking military official, hints at an emerging crisis over an incoming call.
A flicker of suspense seeps into our story's ending, setting the stage for a sequel.
Despite the hardships, each Hawk stalwart, ready to face the plethora of thrilling adventures that may come their way.

59864386.title: SAS: Red Notice
synopsis: Black Swans is a family-owned private military company led by American citizens William Lewis and his adult children Grace and Oliver.
SAS commander George Clements hires them to clear a remote village in Georgia for a transnational Britgaz gas pipeline.
When the villagers resist, Black Swans massacre them.
Their atrocities are secretly filmed, leading to red notices and accusations of crimes against humanity.
The International Criminal Court demands that the UK government extradites the accused, who live in North London, to the Hague to stand trial.
Prime Minister Atwood secretly orders Clements to kill rather than arrest William on the scene to cover up his involvement.
William orders his children and the rest of the team to escape to the United States while he and some of his loyal men stall the SAS.
SAS operator Tom Buckingham, who was involved in serving the red notice, takes his girlfriend, Dr Sophie Hart, on a train journey from London to Paris where he intends to propose to her.
Sophie is unsure whether they understand each other properly, whereas Tom is unsure whether he truly loves her.

The Black Swans remnants, led by Grace Lewis, hijack their train while it is en route to the English Channel, to blow the gas pipe network there as payback, taking all of the passengers on board hostage at gunpoint.
Using his military skills, Tom escapes from the train and evades capture.
When he attempts to rescue Sophie, she refuses to leave the other passengers, who may need medical assistance, and she asks him to save a young girl.
Tom regularly updates his position and sends intelligence to Declan Smith, a member of the SAS Counter Terrorism Team and his friend.
Declan, who has been bribed by the Black Swans, sends a rescue team into a trap.
Grace asks for a $500 million ransom from Britgaz or else she will blow up the tunnel and reveal the secret Britgaz gas pipeline in the tunnel.
After inviting Clements to negotiate, Grace has one of her team secretly record their conversation as insurance.
Grace finds out via Declan that Tom's girlfriend is on the train and takes her hostage.
Tom returns to the train, but he fails to save Sophie.
Grace escapes with her through the gas pipeline, pursued by Tom.
Grace's team uploads the video of Clements and tries to escape among the hostages, but SAS snipers kill them.
Upon not finding Grace among the hostages, Clements realises that Declan is guilty.
Once out of the pipe, Grace blows up the pipeline, and Tom narrowly escapes.
Clements and all of the SAS operatives excluding Declan appear to be killed in the explosion.
Grace stabs Sophie in her thigh and runs away.
Sophie says she finally understands Tom and asks him to catch Grace instead of being with her.
After catching up with Grace, they fight and Grace is fatally injured.
Grace praises Tom's tenacity and offers him to be her successor to rebuild the Black Swans.
Tom rejects the offer and finishes off Grace.
Tom realises that he loves Sophie; during their trip, Tom proposes to her.
She refuses at first, believing him incapable of love, but agrees after seeing his emotional reaction.
The British prime minister and Britgaz representative are questioned, and all blame is transferred to Declan, the sole surviving member of Grace's team.
Tom and Sophie get married in Spain; during the ceremony, Tom is briefed by Clements, who survived the explosion, to find Declan.

55690758.title: Miller's Mission (2023 film)
synopsis: In the dimly-lit core of a secretive intelligence agency housed within the United States, Code Delta, there exists agent John Miller.
His daily routine primarily consists of dissecting encrypted data and drafting complex algorithms, painting a monotonous picture of his life till an extraordinary assignment comes striding in.
The assignment is tricky and immensely consequential.
His mission?
Infiltrate the 'Iron Dome', a monumentally guarded nuclear research base located in the heart of the politically volatile Middle Eastern nation, Syria.
His objective is not just delicate, but groundbreaking.
He is to inject an experimental malware called 'Epsilon' into the Iron Dome's mainframe.
Next, a confidential briefing ensues with the Deputy Chief of Code Delta.
The narrative takes a pause here as Act 1 concludes, revealing the dire stakes – imminent global crisis.
Act 2 opens in an authentic Middle Eastern marketplace bustled by local vendors.
Here, Miller executes the first steps of his daring mission, carefully blending into the crowd while orchestrating critical parts of the operation.
He uses his unrivaled tech know-how to dig out crucial 3D mapped data on the structure of the Iron Dome, examining its grand layers, and revealing its protective laser defense systems.
As he laboriously mines this data, he integrates himself seamlessly into the lively local crowd, learning to speak their tongue, understanding their customs.
Agent Miller, however, does not remain in the shadows for long.
His elusive operations and enigmatic demeanor catch the keen attention of a quick-witted local detective, Leyla.
The third Act introduces a curve.

While deeply buried in his mission, trying to pierce through the layers of the ironclad 'Iron Dome', he mistakenly sets off an unanticipated infrared alarm system, infecting his mission with sudden complications.
The once-controlled atmosphere takes a drastic turn as the shrieking alarm throws the facility's calm orchestration into pandemonium.
This derailment forces Miller to abandon his initial plan of action, shaking the foundation of his strategic infiltration.
With mere conjecture about the success of the partial implementation of the Epsilon malware as his only solace, Miller finds himself racing against mechanical assassins programmed to take him down.
It's during this exhilarating escape that Miller encounters Leyla.
The two come face-to-face in an intense confrontation, fueled by mounting suspicion and tension stemming from his mission's secrecy.
Unforeseen by Miller, Leyla, intrigued by the hidden depths of his operation and moved by his sincerity, makes a decision that turns the tide in their favor.
She chooses to aid Miller, becoming an unexpected ally.
Act four is initiated with a fresh alliance.
Miller and Leyla pool their resources and skills, tackling wild jeep chases through the labyrinthine streets and skillfully executing parkour jumps off towering rooftops.
Together, they reach Miller's concealed base nestled within the walls of an old, inconspicuous brick structure.
Amidst the holographic domains and flickering computer screens in his covert hub, they pour over the fragmented mission data.
It soon dawns on them that the mission took a significant blow - the Epsilon malware was only half-implanted within the Iron Dome's mainframe.
Yet, Miller's defiant spirit refuses to back down.
He quickly identifies a potential oversight in the facility's security, possibly left exposed due to the half-implanted malware, presenting a small window of opportunity.
However, harnessing this opportunity would require a marriage of Leyla's field knowledge and Miller's techno-wizardry.
A collaboration that could either turn the tides in their favor or push them further into the abyss of failure.
Act five unleashes their audacious strategy.
Miller and Leyla devise a risky plan to exploit the loophole using a hijacked military vehicle which would bypass the facility's defenses and deliver the remaining Epsilon malware.
Leyla pledges her support to this seemingly suicidal plan, bringing forth resources collected during her long government service in Syrian law enforcement.
Their daring plan is not greeted with enthusiasm by the hierarchy at Code Delta.
Miller's boss argues for the mission's elevated risk and the possible ignition of global conflict, threatening to shut down the entire operation from his secure office in Washington D.C.
He stresses the potentially damaging fallout of Miller's audacity.
Despite facing severe backlash and witnessing the crumbling support from his superiors, Miller and his newfound ally, Leyla, stand their ground.
Act six leads Miller and Leyla down the path of rebellion.
Defying the orders from their superiors, the pair rally their resources, bolster their intelligence, and launch a daring assault on the Iron Dome.
Audience hearts skip a beat as Miller cautiously navigates through complex laser security, confronting cybernetically enhanced operatives tasked with halting his progress.
Simultaneously, Leyla holds her own battle in a local marketplace.
With swift thinking and calculated movements, she diverts attention, buying Miller crucial time for his operation.
As the Act reaches its climax, in a breath-taking sequence, Miller manages to implant the remaining Epsilon malware data packet into the Dome's control room.
Act VII charts the duo's dramatic escape.
The implementation of Epsilon malware creates chaos inside the Iron Dome, providing Miller and Leyla the perfect smoke screen to escape the facility.
Leveraging the prevailing pandemonium, the duo skillfully dodge security and make a headlong dash towards the exit, leaving behind the Dome in a cloud of impending doom.
Once out of the danger zone, a bond that goes deeper than mere comradeship blossoms between Miller and Leyla.
Under a star-veiled Syrian sky, Leyla assures Miller of her allegiance and promises to protect his mission from bureaucratic interference.
Miller’s arrival back to Code Delta agency is severely met with outrage and disbelief from his director, furious at Miller's insubordination which put the agency at risk.
Opening the final Act, we find Miller distanced from his parent agency.
Alienated and unphased by the hostility from his superiors, he resolves to go lone-wolf, pledging to put his irreplaceable tech skills to use to aid those in need, globally.
The movie nears its end as the concluding drone shots show Miller's silhouette dissolving into the desert horizon.
Thus concludes the thrilling eight Act narrative of "Miller's Mission".

70221912.title: Kandahar (2023 film)
synopsis: Tom Harris is a freelance undercover operative working for the CIA to insert malware into a secret Iranian nuclear research facility.
Tom's cover is a field technician for a Swiss communications contractor.
His mission is successful, and the malware causes the facility to self destruct, preventing the Iranians from acquiring more nuclear bombs.
The Iranian government has been monitoring a British journalist Luna Cujai.
She receives evidence from a whistle blower of the CIA's ongoing sabotage of Iran's nuclear programs.
After the facility is destroyed, she is arrested by an Iranian security agency led by Farzad.
She tells the Iranians she suspects a link between the facility's destruction and the Swiss contractor because their contracts are next to government sites.
The next day, Harris's partner in the operation, Oliver, is murdered by the Iranian Special Force after both Oliver and Harris's identity are compromised.
Tom leaves Iran en route to London via Dubai.
While in Dubai, his flight to London is delayed, and he visits his CIA handler, Roman Chalmers.
Roman is a Muslim convert, living under the outward pretense of a Dubai socialite, a lifestyle he secretly despises.
Roman claims to have delayed the flight to force this meeting.
Tom accepts Roman's lucrative CIA contract for a job in Herat, Afghanistan, because it will pay enough to cover his daughter’s medical university expenses.
After he arrives in Herat, due to an intelligence leak, the news names Tom as the operative responsible for the destruction of the nuclear facility.
With his cover now blown, the mission in Herat is aborted.
Roman directs Tom and his Afghan-American translator Mohammad “Mo” Doud to an extraction point in Kandahar.
Farzad and Pakistani security services learn Tom is in Herat, and each sends operatives to apprehend him, with Pakistan wanting to ransom Tom to the highest bidder.
Tom and Mo are chased by Farzad and ISI agent Kahil Nassir but they elude both pursuing parties and escape to the desert.
En route to Kandahar, Tom and Mo are attacked by Farzad in a helicopter.
Tom destroys the helicopter and kills Farzad and its crew.
Now on foot, Tom and Mo seek aid from Tom's friend, an Afghan warlord not associated with the governing Taliban.
Mo reveals to Tom and the warlord that the warlord killed Mo's son years ago.
