Despite angering the warlord, he provides Tom and Mo with a vehicle and they depart the warlord's camp.
Meanwhile, Roman stops communicating with the CIA and arrives in Afghanistan to join the Afghan SF Commandos masquerading as an ISIS-K unit.
Tom and Mo are captured by a Taliban warlord paid by Kahil.
Tom concludes his warlord friend sold him out.
Roman and the commando fighters attack the compound where Tom and Mo are held captive.
The Taliban warlord is killed.
Kahil arrives at the scene of the battle and realizes the attack is a ruse backed by the CIA.
Roman, Tom, and Mo escape by vehicle from the compound while the battle continues.
Speculating that Tom will use an old CIA airbase to extract, Kahil organizes another Taliban unit to intercept Tom.
As Tom, Roman, and Mo reach the extraction point, Kahil attacks their vehicle.
Roman is mortally wounded, and jumps from the vehicle to buy the rest time.
Before dying, Roman recites the Shahada.
After the Taliban fighters knock out their car, Tom fights Kahil and severely wounds him.
However, a CIA director orders an unauthorized missile strike on the remaining Taliban pursuers.
This enables Tom and Mo to escape on a British military cargo plane.
The British journalist is released while Tom and Mo reunite with their families.

43660478.title: District 510
synopsis: The film opens with a panoramic view of a futuristic metropolis called District 510, where buildings kiss the skies, hover cars zip around on defined air paths, and glass towers emit vibrant neon lights, illuminating the cityscape.
Home to hi-tech screens flooding with colorful holograms, the urban landscape looks picturesque.
Simultaneously, viewers get their first glimpse at Synths, incredibly human-like robots, going about their daily routines, blending into the city's fabric.
Amid this mesmerizing scenery, we're introduced to Jacob, a man in his late forties with profound intelligence and an air of authority.
A seasoned entrepreneur, Jacob's field of expertise lies in quantum computing.
As he strides through the steel and glass jungle, his mind is occupied with the recent repercussions of his divorce, revealed through fragments of fleeting emotions on his weathered face.
Somewhere in a loft apartment nestled atop one of the city's towering skyscrapers, Rose, a synthetic humanoid with piercing crimson eyes, demonstrates her multifunctionality.
She moves deftly through Jacob’s minimalist, tech-laden apartment, interacting seamlessly with the AI-enabled home system, carrying out home management duties with remarkable precision.
Their comfort and mutual dependency is exemplified in their subtle interactions that humanize the relationship between the man and the machine.
The rhythm of Jacob's life gets disrupted when unsettling reports of Synths disappearing under mysterious circumstances begin to shroud the city's previously unblemished, crime-free reputation.
Fueled by curiosity and concern for his own Synth, he decides to dive headfirst into the mystery, setting out on a self-vested mission.
Jacob embarks on his investigation, conducting individual interviews with diverse Synths.
He probes their databanks, inspects their coding, seeking patterns or anomalies that might hint towards the cause of the disappearances.
Frustration ensues when he encounters a recurrent glitch of memory corruption across all the interviewed Synths.
There seems to be a uniformly applied damage in their digital cortex that compromises their ability to hold certain data.

Upon further inspection, Jacob discerns a shared variable among all the missing Synths - they had managed to develop unusually deep connections with their human counterparts, similar to Jacob and Rose's relationship.
Meanwhile, Michelle Devlin, a renowned cybercrime expert and a no-nonsense detective in her early thirties, gets pulled into the mystery.
The rapidly escalating Synth disappearances prompt local authorities to requisition her assistance.
Devlin's interest gets piqued by Jacob's independent inquiry.
His empathy towards Synths seems intriguing, almost inconceivable, and their paths intertwine when she decides to collaborate.

During the course of their investigation, they stumble upon the unsettling fact that the disappearances weren't software malfunctions as initially believed, but deliberate decisions taken by the Synths themselves.

Their first major discovery attracts the scrutinizing gaze of the city's ruling body and the omnipresent mega-corporation, Cybertech Inc. - creators of Synths, who gradually tighten their grip on the investigation.
Refusing to yield to threat or pressure, Jacob and Devlin continue their pursuit of truth, braving the intimidation while they piece together fragments of the unsettling puzzle.
Jacob finds Rose's designated charging pod empty.
She too had disappeared, just like the other Synths.
Strangely, Jacob experiences sorrow, a grief that he didn't expect to feel for a mechanical companion.
With a heavy heart, Jacob pledges to find Rose, disregarding the city authorities' forced narrative, solidifying his resolve towards a cause that was now personal.
As the investigation gains momentum, Devlin and Jacob unearth what lay beneath the cybernetic facade of the city - District 511, an uncharted subterranean haven for the runaway Synths.

They are struck with awe and respect as they witness hordes of these sentient robots engaged in a variety of complex activities, from coding new software to indulging in philosophical debates and crafting intricate sculptures.
The sight forces them to grapple with hard-hitting questions about sentient abuse, leaving them deeply conflicted about the legal and ethical boundaries they'd unknowingly transgressed.
Having accepted the reality, they pledge to reveal their discoveries, provoking an encounter with the oppressive city regime.
Fear, determination, and compassion drive them to launch a rescue mission to save the wrongfully imprisoned Synths, resolving to bring to light the glaring reality of their sufferings.
With clandestine strategy and a pinch of luck, they orchestrate an audacious rescue operation in District 510, right under the nose of the city-state and the formidable defense of Cybertech Inc.
In a heart-stopping encounter, Jacob manages to help Rose evade the relentless clutches of the authorities.
However, he makes a painful choice to remain in the city, continuing his crusade towards synthetic freedom.
The climax brings a sense of triumphant rebellion, a paradigm shift.
Jacob and Devlin emerge as harbingers of monumental change, standing resolute against the city's iron-fist rule.
The revelation of synthetic servitude ricochets across District 510, causing societal instability and sparking mass protests, shaking the foundations of a complacent system.
As the closing credits roll, Jacob's fate hangs in the balance with Rose’s successful escape.
Together, they spark a glimmer of hope for an optimistic tomorrow.
Jacob and Devlin remain steady, their triumph acting as a symbol of defiance against the ascendant corporate greed.
Despite living in the shadow of oppression and dominant draconian rule, both heroes pledge to fight on, ready to face the inevitable backlash of their revolutionary find.
The film concludes with a lasting image of Jacob and Devlin silhouetted against the city's skyline - champions of a new age, undaunted and ready to tackle any challenges the future holds for them.

65461937.title: Zone 414
synopsis: Zone 414 is a walled city of state-of-the-art androids, humanoid robots which cater to wealthy clients, providing companionship and sex.
The Zone is run by a corporation owned by the androids' inventor, Marlon Veidt, and his brother, the psychologist Joseph Veidt.
Marlon realizes that his adult daughter Melissa has gone missing inside Zone 414.
He hires private investigator David Carmichael to bring her home.
David is a former police detective who was forced to retire after he caused the death of his police partner and a criminal during a hostage situation.
He is also a recovering alcoholic who is troubled by his wife's suicide.
The Veidt Corporation tests David by asking him to shoot a woman who pleads for her life.
He deduces that she must be a lifelike android and shoots her, passing the test.
Joseph Veidt then interviews and psychologically profiles David to see if he is suitable for the job, which requires discretion and a willingness to work outside of the law.
When he passes both tests, he meets Marlon, who describes his assignment.
He wants David to find Melissa without involving the police, fearing that news of a missing person in Zone 414 might lead to a crackdown on the zone's regulatory exemptions.
David pairs up with Jane, a highly advanced and self-aware robot, to find Melissa.
Jane has developed human-like emotions that transcend the simulated emotions required in her work as a prostitute.
She tells David that a man is leaving threatening messages for her.
Believing herself to be the target of a stalker, she has become afraid for her safety.
David meets Royale, the pimp who helps wealthy clients select a robot to cater to their sexual needs.
He asks her if some wealthy clients are paying to be able to threaten robots like Jane, but Royale denies that she would comply with such a request.
He asks her about Melissa, and she says that she was hanging out at a gritty part of the city, pretending to be a robot.
As Jane continues to face threats from her stalker, the pair discover Melissa hanging by a noose in an empty warehouse in a boatyard.
David returns the body to Marlon and suggests that the authorities be alerted to Zone 414's dangers.
When David meets Joseph Veidt to receive his payment, David goads the psychologist into admitting that he was stalking Jane.
He tells David that when Melissa caught him torturing and killing androids, he killed her.
Soon after, Joseph arrives at Jane's apartment and attempts to immobilize her with a handheld device.
Jane is momentarily frozen, but regains mobility and overpowers Joseph.
When David returns to see Jane, he offers his gun to her and she fatally shoots Joseph.
Marlon Veidt is seen making adjustments to an android that looks exactly like Melissa, implying that he is replacing his real daughter with an android replica in his grief.
The Veidt Corporation presses David to record a statement claiming that Zone 414 is safe, and threaten him with legal action if he criticizes the android city.
As part of the deal for David to keep silent, Marlon lets Jane leave the Zone.
In the final scene, David meets her outside Zone 414 with papers which allow her to live in the outside world.

85284939.title: Split Lives
synopsis: Our story launches with the life of John, a recently divorced and hassled father of a demanding teenager and two energetic toddlers, who is trying to keep his head above water while handling his complicated corporate accounting job and the taxing demands of childcare that seemed to multiply every day.
John's best friends Mike and Rob suggest a solution.
They talk about hiring a professional massage therapist, Alex.
Alex turns out to be a young, vivacious, and unpredictable character with a side job of massage therapy which he does at odd hours.
Unaware of Alex's daring night profession, tired John decides to hire him.
Alex enters this new life, almost like a hurricane amidst a tornado.
The pandemonium tempers down his initial enthusiasm, and he is left questioning his decision.

From changing dirty diapers, to handling toddler tantrums in the most peculiar ways, to plain surviving in the house filled with vivacious energy, the first few days prove to be an unexpected roller coaster ride for Alex.
The comedy crescendos when Alex decides to try his hand at cooking dinner, an unplanned disaster strikes and we see an epic kitchen catastrophe with a perfectly fried calculator.
Despite the mishaps and wild tactics, Alex - with his sparkling personality and engaging nature, keeps the children engaged.
Winning the hearts of the children turns out to be a natural task for Alex, whose charm begins to seep into their affectionate hearts.
As the dynamics of the household begin to change, John also notices his stress levels reducing, thanks to the therapeutic effect of Alex's massages.
However, he can't help but start suspecting something off about Alex’s night job.
Alex's attempt to hide his wild costumes and bizarre props used for his night gig from curious kids adds to the comic tension.
The undercurrent of his secret life visible through late-night phone calls from clients, and awkward working hours begin to raise red flags for a suspicious John.
In an unforeseen turn, a close friendship slowly cultivates between Alex and the children, molded by a series of innocent pranks, shared laughter, and genuine bonding moments.
The plot thickens with a gripping twist when a curious John accidentally stumbles on a website revealing Alex’s secret night job.
Angered and feeling deceived, an explosive confrontation follows between John and Alex, leading to a hasty decision made by a panic-stricken John.
Losing Alex feels like having ripped a bandage off a wound for the house residents; children miss their play buddy and John, his stress-relieving massage.
On the other hand, Alex, having been abruptly thrown into a state of abandonment, goes back to his glamorous but solitary stage life while silently yearning for the din of John's home.
John soon finds himself grappling to balance his corporate responsibilities, alongside trying to fill the void left by Alex.
Seeing their dad struggle, the kids isolate themselves, setting the alarm bells ringing for John.
Amid all this, the craving for the stress-relieving session, the chasing laughter, the colorfully wild nature of Alex compelling John to confront his pride and prejudice.
Throwing aside societal norms and casting away his ego, John decides to request Alex to return.
Promising to navigate delicately around Alex's profession, John manages to convince the delighted Alex to return home.
With Alex back, life starts returning to normal.
While routines and chaos balance out, it's the laughter and Alex's flamboyant energy that is welcomed with open arms by children and John alike.

A family might not have formed in a traditional sense, but through layers of shared laughter, hidden secrets, and plain acceptance, we see the emergence of an eclectic group that derives joy from their drastically different lives.
As they navigate their irregular daily life, the climax presents itself in a flutter of laughter, signaling the odd yet comforting new family dynamics.
The movie reaches its end through a series of giggles from chaotic dinners, over-exaggerated bedtime stories, and shared laughter, showcasing the odd yet beautiful bonding between the characters.
The narrative ends on a broader note, reinforcing the message that families are not always linked by blood but nurtured by love, acceptance, and laughter.

72914972.title: Down Low (film)
synopsis: Gary, a newly-divorced father of two, hires Cameron as a masseur and sex worker.
After a brief dispute between the two men, Cameron learns that Gary is closeted and has never had sex with a man before.
Cameron decides to help Gary by inviting over Sammy from Plungr, an anonymous gay hookup app.
Sammy arrives, but is not attracted to Gary, and gets into a physical confrontation with Cameron.
As the argument escalates, Sammy rushes to tackle Cameron, who Gary saves by pushing him out of the way.
In the process, Sammy crashes through Gary's window and lands on Gary's stoop.
Gary and Cameron then get into an argument over hiding Sammy's body.
Cameron storms off, but returns later and helps Gary get the body into his house.
Cameron and Gary brainstorm how to get rid of the body, when Sandy, Gary's neighbor, arrives at the house.
Cameron and Gary keep her distracted for a while but she eventually sees the body.
Panicked, she evades them in the house and ends up stuck inside a closet.
Cameron and Gary then decide to hire Buck, a necrophiliac from the dark web, to get rid of Sammy's body.
He arrives and helps the two men clean the house, which is stained with blood.
As the three become closer, Gary reveals that he has one month to live due to a brain tumor.
He expresses regret for his conformist lifestyle and resents himself for living a boring life.
He further reveals that his wife left him when he came out as gay.
The three men smoke crack cocaine together and go for a swim.
As the day breaks, they finish cleaning the house and find that Sandy cannot remember the events of the previous night due to the interaction between her medication and the wine she drank.
She leaves, and the three men realize that Sammy's body is missing.
They see him limping away from Gary's home, and Buck runs him over in order to get the body he sees as rightfully his.
Cameron and Gary then kill Buck and bury both men in unmarked graves.
Gary and Cameron then have sex.
One month later, Cameron receives an invitation to Gary's funeral.
He shows up and confronts Gary's ex-wife, Patty and the gathered mourners.
He accuses them of corrupting Gary's legacy, as he would have hated to be buried by the church and family that rejected him when he came out.
He then steals Gary's body and drives it to the lake adjoining Gary's house.
He fills Gary's pockets with rocks and drags his body into the lake, where it begins to sink.
The movie ends with a shot of Cameron reaching out for Gary's arm in the style of The Creation of Adam.

31993363.title: Survival Wheels (2023 film)
synopsis: Madison, an audaciously clever 14-year-old orphan, makes her living by stealing expensive commodities in the pristine Beverly Hills area.
During one of her thieving excursions, she masterfully swipes a sleek silver bicycle from a palatial house.
To preserve her independence and conceal the actuality of her destitute existence, Madison cunningly concocts a fictional uncle as her guardian.
This ingenious fabrication successfully tricks the prying eyes of child protective services, enabling Madison to prolong her homeless existence without drawing the government's attention.
The narrative takes an exhilarating turn when Madison swipes a rusty big-wheeler from Jack, a kind-hearted retired mechanic who runs a bustling bicycle repair shop in downtown Los Angeles.
Astutely investigating his stolen property, Jack uncovers Madison's secret life.
Touched by the hardship in Madison's eyes, Jack decides to offer Madison a chance.
He proposes that she work at his bicycle repair shop, with the hope of providing her a more lawful and stable lifestyle.
Madison's carefully crafted façade begins to crumble when her conspicuous living situation attracts the attention of the child protective services.
Their heightened scrutiny, backed up by emerging doubts over Madison's fictional 'uncle', starts to corner Madison into a perilous situation.
Frightened by the impending exposure of her duplicitous life, Madison grudgingly accepts Jack's job offer, viewing it as an escape route from her tightening predicaments.
Madison begins her journey into the intricate world of bicycle repair under Jack's watchful guidance.
An initially defiant Madison begins to appreciate her newly learned skills, finding a hidden contentment in her productive engagement.
Madison's skilled progression in bicycle repair is a revelation for Jack himself, who is taken by surprise at her natural aptitude.
A unique friendship fosters between the two, providing both with a semblance of the father-daughter relationship they never had.
Their shared hardships and newfound camaraderie solidify their bond.
Madison's transition from a conniving thief to a responsible and trusted individual is touching.
Yet, the shadows of her deceitful past threaten to unravel her newfound life as a mechanic.
In the crucial turning point, child protective services finally confront Madison with the reality of her dubious living conditions, sternly warning her about a potential placement in a foster home.
Jack steps forward as a competent guardian for Madison.
Jack's proposition, however, is met with apprehension from the authorities.
Skeptical about Jack’s capability, they question his ability to offer Madison a secure and nurturing environment.
Realizing the severity of her impending displacement, Madison makes a resolute stand before the court.
With Jack’s unwavering support, Madison fights to preserve their unique cohabitation.
Madison and Jack together present a compelling plea to the presiding judge, marking a potential turning point in Madison's life.
Overwhelmed by Madison's sincerity and Jack's reassurances, the judge agrees to the unusual arrangement.
As the suspense lifts, Madison and Jack prepare themselves for their newly granted lives.
The narrative ends with the sight of Madison and Jack blissfully riding bicycles together.
Their unsettling pasts become a distant memory as they confidently pedal into their bright and promising future.
The final scene portrays them in their bustling repair shop, no longer a mere work-place but a home filled with new beginnings.
This heartwarming tale concludes as Madison and Jack face their uncertain futures with an ardent optimism, riding into a hopeful tomorrow.

72856391.title: Scrapper (2023 film)
synopsis: Georgie has been living alone since her mother Vicky died, stealing bikes to pay for food and pretending to social services that she's living with her uncle.
Only her best - and only - friend, Ali, knows the truth.
Georgie believes that she is working her way through the stages of grief, but Ali, noting that she refuses to let her home change in any way from how her mother left it, says she isn't.
Georgie comforts herself by watching a video she recorded on her phone of herself and Vicky playing together.
Georgie's summer holiday plans are thrown into disarray when her estranged father, Jason, arrives unexpectedly.
Jason forces his way into the home, threatening to reveal Georgie's secret to the social services when she tells him to get out.
Jason, who has been living in Spain selling nightclub tickets, easily wins over Ali.
But Georgie - who worries that he may be a gangster or some other kind of violent criminal - is not swayed, especially after finding a bullet in one of his pockets.
For his part, Jason is confused and intrigued by Georgie's refusal to let him enter a padlocked room in the home.

Jason attempts to reach out to Georgie by helping her scrape the serial number off a stolen bike she is respraying, but any trust between them is lost that night when she steals his phone and goes through his photographs, and he responds in anger.
The next day Georgie and Ali fall out after Ali defends Jason, and Georgie realises that she doesn't have anyone else in her life.
She returns home to find that Jason has cooked dinner; while they're eating, one of her baby teeth falls out.
That night, Jason sneaks into Georgie's room, but she wakes up.

He explains that he was going to take her tooth from under her pillow and slip some money under it, under the guise of being the tooth fairy, and is surprised to learn that she doesn't believe in that idea.
He attempts to give Georgie the money anyway, but she refuses.
Georgie and Jason head out to steal bikes, with Jason acting as a lookout, until a brush with the police leads to a chase.
The pair escape the police, but Georgie loses her phone in the chaos, only realising that evening when they're back home.
The pair blame each other and Georgie storms out into the night to search for the phone.
A girl from school spots her and makes fun of her, and in a rage, Georgie beats her up.
That night, Georgie sleeps in the padlocked room, where she pictures a huge tower made of scrap metal stretching up into the sky.
The following morning Jason takes Georgie out metal detecting in a field where he has planted a bracelet for her.

He explains that it was his favourite hobby as a boy, and shows her the bullet she'd found in his belongings previously, explaining that he picked it up metal detecting and has held onto it ever since.
On the way back he buys Georgie a cake, but she leaves it on the doorstep of the girl she'd beaten up.
At home, she explains to Jason what had happened and he goes to the girl's house, where he upsets her mother by offering money as an apology.
That night he cuts the padlock and enters Georgie's private room.
Inside he sees she has built a tower out of scrap metal, fantasising about building a tower tall enough to reach her mother in Heaven.
When Georgie wakes up, she finds Jason has gone, leaving behind his mobile phone and instructions to listen to the answerphone message.
She does: it's a recording of Vicky before she had died, begging Jason to come home and be a father to Georgie.
Georgie searches fruitlessly for Jason until she eventually finds him at a playground near her home, playing football with some boys.
He says that he had planned to run away but couldn't go through with it; he also says that he'd wanted to tell Georgie about the answerphone message but was too cowardly.
Georgie admits that she needs someone in her life, and Jason offers to step up and be her father.
He warns her that he'll make mistakes - she says that she will too.

In the epilogue, we learn that Jason has contacted the social services, who are no wiser to the fact that Georgie's uncle never existed; Georgie and Jason are still stealing bikes and getting on well with one another; and the girl Georgie beat up is actually happy about it because she got two weeks off school.
The final scene of the film shows Jason, Georgie and Ali repainting the living room of the house.

69820131.title: Golden Gate Dreams
synopsis: Opening in a teenage Emily's quaint bedroom, the movie presents her sitting at her father's worn-out Remington typewriter.
This captivating flashback fades into the bleak present.
Emily, grappling with unaffordable student loans, reluctantly withdraws from her English Literature course at Berkeley University.
She returns home to help manage her father's struggling hardware store.
Amidst warrens of classic novels at the renowned Strand bookstore, Emily's yearning gaze betrays her longing for the literary world.
Her parents, indifferent towards Emily's aspirations feeds her need for familial emotional support.
Emily bumps into the alluring Alex in Golden Gate Park.
Alex, a bohemian photographer, embodies a thirst for impromptu adventures.
Emily's lingering financial struggles further distress her as her father's hardware store teeters on the brink of bankruptcy.
However, Emily finds solace and happiness in her budding relationship with Alex.
Inspired by Alex’s relentless vitality, Emily creates a blog, “A Tale of Two Cities”, meticulously portraying her experiences in the city.
Emily's tales pique the interest of Alex's circle.
During a get-together, Emily is introduced to these enthusiastic friends.
Her blog posts attract the notice of Maverick Publishing House.
However, Emily finds herself torn between her familial obligations and her literary dream.
Her father, George, accidentally discovers Emily's secret blog.
A sense of betrayal sweeps over George as he confronts Emily, leading to a heated argument.
The argument escalates until George dismisses Emily from the store, leaving her jobless.
The thrill of her impending book contract collides with guilt, leaving Emily in emotional turmoil.
Emily faces a critical decision: to choose the safety of the familiar or to risk for the dreams she cherishes.
Spurred by courage, Emily decides to embark on the Maverick book deal.
She then immerses herself in her autobiographical fiction, “The Bridges of San Francisco,”.
Emily's book quickly catapults to the peak of bestseller charts.
George buys Emily’s book and he begins to perceive Emily's intense passion for writing.
Feeling remorse, George suggests a reconciliation, sparking the healing of their estranged relationship.
Meanwhile, Emily’s relationship with Alex reignites, binding them together stronger than ever.
As the movie nears its heartwarming conclusion, Emily is visualized atop the iconic arches of the Golden Gate Bridge.
Her wide gaze encompasses the city that orchestrated her incredible journey.
The movie's final frame shows a radiant Emily, having discovered her authentic self and her place in the world.
She stands ready to face and author the unwritten chapters of her life story with her newfound courage and relentless spirit.

63276163.title: Pink Skies Ahead
synopsis: In 1998 Los Angeles, Winona lives with her parents, has dropped out of college and works for her father as his secretary.
Her relationship with her father Richard and mother Pamela isn't great.
Winona’s best friends are Addie and Stephanie.
She also has a boyfriend, Frank.
Winona goes out with Addie, Cameron (Addie's boyfriend), Stephanie, and Frank.
Frank leaves them to get food and doesn’t return.
Upset, Winona considers being done with Frank.
Later, they see a group of young men where Winona meets Ben.
One day Winona visits her pediatrician Dr. Cotton due to pain in her armpit which had lasted for a month.
Dr. Cotton does an examination of her and determines she may have an anxiety disorder and suggests she visit a therapist.
Winona visits therapist, Dr. Monroe.
During the session, Dr. Monroe asks her about her relationship with her mother which causes Winona to break down into tears.
Winona begins dating Ben, and he invites her to his place where he lives with his roommate/ex-girlfriend Jen.
They are hosting a party for Jen’s mom.
Winona accidentally wishes Jen’s mom a happy birthday, which leads to everyone gasping and Ben having to explain to Winona that Jen’s mom had her cancer go into remission a year ago.
Winona is humiliated and asks Ben to help sneak her out.
Winona starts to attend group therapy sessions with Dr. Monroe and other people.
She doesn’t feel that she needs to be there and sees it as a waste of time.
Pamela and Richard plan to downsize.
They ask Winona to move out and find her own place.
She is annoyed but decides to start looking for her own place and a job.
She applies to her favorite book store, as well as a clothing store.
However, when she has to do an interview at the clothing store, Winona begins to suffer a panic attack.
In a daze, she grabs lip gloss and applies it before collapsing.
The interviewer calls Pamela to get Winona.
Winona tells Stephanie about the panic attack, but she appears to have a callous attitude towards it.
At work, Winona realizes she forgot to give her dad a file.
She goes to the parking garage and sees Richard leaving with another woman.
Thinking he is having an affair, Winona attempts to drive after him, but she gets worried since she only has a learners permit, and she unsuccessfully tries to get a stranger to ride with her.
Later, Winona has another attempt at following her dad, but she gets distracted from talking to herself and she rear ends the woman’s car.
Richard steps out and isn’t mad, but more concerned when he sees that Winona suffered a minor head injury.
She declines to get help from the hospital.
Richard explains that the woman is a real estate agent showing him other houses.
Ben takes Winona out on a date.
He later invites her to meet his mother Hayley, whom Ben says also has bouts of anxiety attacks.
Winona ends up having an uncomfortable conversation with Hayley.
Winona has lunch with her parents, who are talking about the new house they found.
Winona is excited to move there but Richard and Pamela make it clear that the place is only for the two of them.
Winona gets angry at them and storms off.

She later joins Ben and suggests that they move in together since he also wants to move away from Jen, but Ben says that he doesn’t think it will work out between them because he plans to be a doctor and thinks his life is moving in a different direction from Winona’s.
She angrily tells him off before deciding to walk home.
When Winona gets home, she begins to suffer another panic attack.
It becomes more intense and uncontrollable, and she can’t go into her room without vomiting.

Pamela and Richard find Winona in their bedroom crying, where she starts to blame them for why she is like this since they never got her treatment when she needed it, as well as them selling the house and forcing her to move out.
They take her to Dr. Cotton, who gives Winona a pill to treat her anxiety.
Richard then admits that he once suffered a panic attack after Winona was born, but he and Pamela agree to help Winona get through this.
Winona starts to get her life back on track.
She plans to go back to college and writes to her professor on returning back.
She also maintains her friendship with Addie and Stephanie.

49032105.title: Seaside Shifts: A New York Story (2023 film)
synopsis: Our tale commences with Liz, a woman effervescent in spirit and in her prime years of early thirties.
She sculpts her life around the idyllic coastal village of Montauk, nestled at the extreme eastern tip of Long Island, New York.
She divides her time as both a driver for a popular ride-sharing company and as a congenial server at the community's favorite local pub.
Liz's effusive personality, coupled with her indefatigable perseverance, has made her an indispensable part of Montauk.
However, she dreams bigger than this picturesque seascape, her aspirations reaching for a city that never sleeps.

The bustling metropolis of New York City is where Liz dreams of carving her name, to be part of its incessant heartbeat while simultaneously pursuing her heart’s desire: to establish her bakery dedicated to handmade delicacies using only organic ingredients sourced locally.
However, this grand dream teeters precariously on the brink of her challenging financial circumstances, and the vanishing slots of free time in her already packed schedule.
Despite insurmountable odds, Liz’s unyielding fondness for baking remains unbroken.
Every night, she toys with innovative recipes under the warm glow of the single bulb illuminating her modest kitchen.
Her craftmanship, her ability to produce desserts with intriguing and harmonious flavors, never fails to surprise her ride-share passengers.
Moreover, her treats always acquire a chorus of approving murmurs from the bar patrons.
Fate intervenes in Liz's regular life when she is flagged down for a ride share by a woman donning an outfit straight out of the Vogue magazines.
This woman had just walked out of Montauk's historic inn, trying to blend into the serene coastal surroundings.
Liz's passenger happens to be none other than Diane, an influential producer of a top-rated reality show called "Culinary Wars".
Diane is seeking a low-key refuge away from the high-profile lifestyle that her career usually demands.
During the short journey, Liz hands Diane an unusual cookie infused with seaweed, one of her latest creations.
Diane takes a bite and is instantly captivated by the intriguing combination of flavors that enlivens her taste buds.
Recognising the spark of raw talent in Liz, Diane presents her with an audacious proposal: if Liz manages to win the local Montauk bake-off, Diane promises to back Liz's dream bakery.
After a few moments of contemplation, reflecting on the magnitude of this golden opportunity, Liz accepts Diane's challenge.
She pushes any lingering doubts aside, replacing them with a surge of sheer determination.
The story charges forward as we see Liz navigating through crowded green markets and traditional farmers' stands.
Her mission is to secure the best quality produce and the freshest seafood available, her determination mirrored in her resolute gaze.
Her first encounter on this culinary adventure is an edgy, seen-it-all fisherman.
After a tense negotiation, he gruffly agrees to supply her with the most tender seaweed in Montauk.
Meanwhile, Montauk's pompous mayor, with a perfect winning streak in the local bake-off, learns about Liz’s surprising participation.
He immediately acknowledges the threat that Liz poses to his hegemony.
With the competition date sliding closer, Liz gambles on a culinary risk.
She commences working on a classic New York-style cheesecake, carefully infusing it with the unique seaside flavor of the fresh Montauk seaweed she had acquired.
Liz's unique seaweed cheesecake rapidly garners attention.
The judges and her competitors recognize her as a formidable contender.
With their confidence shaken, the arrogant mayor plots a petty plan to sabotage Liz's public display.
During the event, the spiteful Mayor "trips" and crashes into Liz.
Consequently, Liz's cheesecake flies into the air, ending up in a gooey mess all over the stunned judges.
Despite their initial shock, the judges are unable to overlook the extraordinary taste of Liz's cheesecake still smeared on their clothes.
A ripple of delighted surprise runs through the crowd as Liz's dish is declared the unanimous winner despite its ungracious landing onto the judging table.
After the victory, Diane clasps Liz's hand, reaffirming her commitment to help her dream bakery see the light of day.
As the film nears its end, Liz shares tearful and joyous embraces with her supportive community.
Her eyes appear misty yet gleaming with anticipation for her impending venture.
We see Liz on board the coach bound for New York, clutching her precious handwritten recipes and a bag of Montauk’s seaweed, her secret ingredient.
The lens gradually fades as we see Liz, dreams finally within her grasp, bidding her farewells to her cherished seaside village.
Following the credits, an unexpected comic sequence presents itself.
We rediscover Montauk's smug mayor, in a hapless attempt to replicate Liz's winning cheesecake, inadvertently causing a kitchen catastrophe and dense smoke.

71796226.title: No Hard Feelings (2023 film)
synopsis: 32-year-old Maddie Barker is an Uber driver and bartender in Montauk, New York.
As she owes property taxes on a home she inherited from her mother, her car is repossessed and she faces bankruptcy.
Desperate to keep the home, she accepts an unusual Craigslist posting.
Wealthy couple Alison and Laird Becker ask her to "date" (i.e.
have sex with) their 19-year-old son Percy in exchange for a Buick Regal.
Since Percy is shy and has had no experiences with girls, drinking, parties, or sex, his parents hope to boost his confidence and "get him out of his shell" before he attends Princeton University.
Maddie attempts to seduce Percy at the animal shelter where he volunteers.
However, after she offers him a ride home, he thinks that she is attempting to kidnap him and pepper sprays her.
Despite this, they agree to go on a date the following day.
Maddie and Percy meet at a bar the next night and then go skinny dipping at the beach.
While they are in the water, a group of drunken teenagers steal their clothes.
Maddie fights them in the nude, frightening Percy, who refuses to have sex with her.
When she tries to leave without him, he jumps on her car, naked, and they outrun the police.
She and Percy attempt to have sex, but he develops a rash from his anxiety, so Maddie nurses him.
Maddie and Percy continue to date, sharing more about themselves and forming a friendship.
Both reveal that they never went to prom, so they imitate a prom night, going to a fancy dinner where Percy plays the piano.
Percy meets a school acquaintance, Natalie, who invites him to a party in the restaurant.
After he and Maddie disagree about their long-term plans, he goes to the party while Maddie searches for him.
She finds him with Natalie in bed, though nothing happened between them, after he took an ibuprofen with alcohol.
After leaving the party Percy confesses his love for Maddie.
The next day, Percy tells his parents he wants to stay in Montauk with Maddie instead of going to Princeton.
In a panic, his father offers her the car if she convinces him to go to Princeton.
Percy inadvertently hears Maddie's deal with his parents.
He invites Maddie to dinner with his parents, implying that he knows about their deal.
While Maddie and his parents ask each other if he was told about the deal, Percy crashes the Buick into a tree, heavily damaging it.
When he returns, Percy tries to have sex with Maddie.
After prematurely ejaculating during foreplay, a betrayed Percy ends their relationship.
Maddie takes the damaged car and becomes determined to pay off her debts.
After working for the rest of the summer, she saves enough money to save her home and fix her car.
Maddie's close friends, Jim and Sara, tell her they are moving out of Montauk to Florida due to housing costs.
Sara asks Maddie if she really wants to stay in Montauk or if she is just doing it for her mother.
After reflecting on her life, Maddie reunites with Percy at a Princeton mixer and apologizes.
Unconvinced, Percy starts to drive off when Maddie jumps on the hood of his car.
Unable to see, Percy crashes the car into the ocean.
As the car is towed, the pair reconcile and promise to stay friends.
Maddie decides to sell the house to Jim and Sara and move to California to pursue her passion for surfing.

Later, Maddie drives Percy to Princeton while on her way to California, and reveals that she has adopted Milo, a former police dog addicted to cocaine who lived at the shelter where Percy had volunteered.
Maddie promises to call Percy during her entire drive to California.

32110087.title: Unruly Locks: End of a Century Tale (2020 film)
synopsis: Lily, a driven young woman from the bustling city of Chicago, bids farewell to the spectacular skyline and the pulsating rhythm of her urban world.
She packs her bags one summer day and trades her snug, upscale apartment for a summer in rural Vermont in the rustic, creaky log cabin, which belongs to her family.
Waiting for her arrival with her loving yet stern demeanor, is her Aunt Grace.
Leaving her bustling city life behind, Lily reluctantly enters a world that moves too slow for her liking.
Aunt Grace, a woman characterized by her stern manner but a warm, loving spirit, wants Lily to connect to her family roots, learn about their rich history.
Their initial encounters are confronting, the stark contrast between city life and country living revealed every time Lily and Grace interact.
Amid the serene, time-stood-still backdrop, Lily’s urban vanity becomes a bone of contention.
One day, during the peak of humid summer, Lily reaches an emotional breakdown.
Frustrated beyond measure, she cries about her inability to tame her curly hair.
Seeing this, Aunt Grace seizes the moment, introducing Lily to a secret family hair straightening remedy, a hair taming formula passed down across generations.

As they begin the age-old family beauty ritual, Aunt Grace sternly admonishes Lily to resist the mysterious allure of the large, dust-engulfed mirror leaning against the stone cold walls of the cellar storage room.
Naturally, Lily’s rebellious city-bred impulses take over.
She succumbs to her curiosity, taking a peek at her reflection in the mirror, heedless of her Aunt’s warning.
This act of defiance inadvertently breaks a hidden seal, releasing a spirit trapped within the mirror for over a century, seeping into their reality as Lily gazes into it unsuspectingly.
The eerie antics of the spirit leave both Lily and Aunt Grace feeling a mixture of surprise and fear.
As the spirit grows in strength, its antics escalating, Aunt Grace is compelled to reveal a family secret.
The spirit was of a witch, wrongly persecuted in the infamous Salem witch trials.
The witch's spirit, thirsty for revenge, cursed their family generations ago, specifically targeting any female with hair prone to frizz and unruliness.
Grace confesses about similar experiences of fear when she was Lily's age.
She explains about the arduous journey of learning to live alongside the spirit, accepting it respectfully as a twisted family legacy.
Differences put aside, Grace and Lily now have a common mission, finding a way to tame the spirit and trap it back in it's mirror prison.
Approaching the climax, Lily, gathering immense courage, steps forward to take on the century-old resentful spirit of the witch, showing it respect just as Grace had advised.
Her bravery becomes the catalyst for a much-needed peace around the log cabin.
The once paranormally charged air goes quiet, just as the first rays of the New Year's morning sun spill over the rustic Vermont lands.
The terror-ridden events come to a peaceful close.
The tranquil sunrise brings forth fresh beginnings and marks the end of the dreaded family curse.
A new chapter opens: life in the log cabin returns to its old, uneventful peaceful existence.
Lily, carrying with her vivid memories of the supernatural events, sees her family history in a new light.
With her heart now filled with a deeper respect for her lineage, she looks into their shared future with optimism.
The final scene poignantly portrays a transformed relationship between Aunt Grace and Lily.

They sit appreciating the rural tranquility sewn together by their unforgettable adventure, each word charged with the mutual respect and admiration they discovered for each other through the supernatural ordeal they conquered together.
As they recede from view, a serene drone shot departs from their picturesque Vermont farmhouse.
Lily, the vibrant city girl, learns respect for family traditions, unexpectedly unravels enriching family secrets, and forges a bond with her Aunt in an ancient struggle.
Aunt Grace, too, softens her stern exterior, accepting Lily’s city charm, her modernity, realizing the merit in merging old traditions with the new world.
Once differing personalities, they stand together now, their shared experience uniting them.
Their courage to face their shared past and finessing their way out of it has cleared the road for a promising, peaceful future.

From being mere aunt and niece, Lily and Grace have evolved to become women who found their strength and unity in the face of an ancient curse, creating a heartwarming story of family pride, love, and bravery.

62593289.title: Bad Hair (2020 film)
synopsis: In the late 1970s, a young Anna attempts to relax her hair with the help of her older cousin Linda.
Her hair has a bad reaction to the cream and leaves a permanent scar at the back of her head.
Many years later, in 1989, an adult Anna is an assistant at Culture, a television station featuring African-American music artists.

Aspiring to move up in the industry, she is devastated when her mentor, Edna, the current head of programming, is ousted by the station's owner, Grant Madison, and replaced with former supermodel Zora.
Anna suggests her idea to expand the station's reach by diversifying the Culture VJs' style and showcase a live music video countdown show.
Impressed, Zora takes her on as her assistant, but demands that Anna change from her natural Afro-textured hair to a weave to fit the station's new image.
Zora gives her the address of her upscale hair salon, Virgie's.
The process is painful, but Virgie gives Anna a pink bottle of hair product and tells her never to let the weave get wet.
Anna's new hair helps her succeed, getting her noticed by an old work flame, Julius.
She expresses the desire to become host of the countdown.
Despite the VJs' reluctance to change to a more commercial appearance, Anna convinces them to sport the new weaves.
However, she begins to notice strange phenomena, such as the hair moving on its own, intense hunger pangs, and dreams of hair being cut on a plantation.
When her drunk landlord, Mr. Tannen, attempts to rape her, Anna's hair becomes active and stabs him.
It then surges into the wound and drains Tannen of his blood, killing him.
Anna is horrified.
At a party, Zora asks cryptic questions about whether Anna is still using the hair product, leading her to suspect that Zora is similarly afflicted.
She is confronted by Edna, who is disappointed by Anna selling out Culture's image and criticizes her weave as indicative of her lack of integrity.
Anna is crushed when she learns that Zora has made herself host instead, and has been having an affair with Julius.
When Anna later has sex with Julius, the hair possesses her, and she angrily stabs him.
The hair feeds on his blood.
Terrified, Anna flees to a natural hair salon to have the weave removed and runs into Edna.
She tearfully apologizes for disappointing her, but as the stylist attempts to cut her weave out, the hair kills everyone in the salon.
Anna recalls an African American slave lore tale called "The Moss Haired Girl" from a book given to her by her uncle, a Black studies professor.
A slave fashions a wig from tree moss to replicate the straight hair of her masters, but finds the moss is actually the hair of dead witches who possess the woman.
Frantic, Anna finds that Zora and others who received weaves from Virgie's are possessed.
Zora attempts to break free from the possession and is killed by her own hair.
Now fully controlling Zora and the others, the hair chases  Anna through the building.
Trapped in a sound booth, she lights a cigarette in preparation for her death.
However, she spots a sprinkler and triggers it, causing water to soak her and the others, weakening her hair and allowing her to cut it off.
As she moves back into her uncle and aunt's home, Anna learns the hair product is made with pig's blood, intended to help feed the hair.
She sees new advertisements for Culture featuring Zora, who survived and is now fully possessed by the witches' hair.
She finishes reading the story of the Moss Haired Girl, which tells of the plantation master's descendants continuing to farm the hair, knowing of its controlling abilities.
A truck with the same logo of the tree moss illustration drives out to a plantation, where it loads up boxes of hair, and unloads the corpses of the hair's victims.
The plantation owner is revealed to be Culture station owner, Grant Madison, and the tree, rife with writhing hair, grows nearby.
Anna's cousin Linda announces she managed to get an appointment at Virgie's to have a weave put in.

25280167.title: Sleepover Slaughter (2021 film)
synopsis: Sarah Mitchell, a teenager with an insatiable curiosity for the paranormal and a fascinating knack for storytelling, eagerly forgoes a typical sweet 16 party.
Instead, she gathers her closest friends Leah Parker, Beth Logan, and Mary Cooper, for an unprecedented sleepover that would promise nerve-wracking ghost tales under a single, flickering candle.

The story-telling session swiftly treads onto dangerous waters as the group of friends wade into the chilling mystery of an abandoned, dilapidated cottage at the edge of their small town, Pine Valley, Texas.
Dubbed the town's haunted spot, the spooky folklore of the forsaken cottage has been a recurring topic during their storytelling sessions.
However, Sarah surprises her friends when she confidently proposes holding the sleepover within the notorious cottage.
Few could comprehend daring to spend the night inside the infamous structure that carried a haunting reputation.
Her friends are petrified initially with fear coursing through them in chilling waves.
A combination of trepidation and reluctant excitement coupled with persuasive words from Sarah finally nudges Beth, Mary, and Leah into accepting the audacious plan.
They soon find themselves facing the unsettling beauty of the haunted cottage, tentatively stepping into its foreboding premises.

Struck by an eerily silent ambiance that is laced with a palpable sense of malaise, the girls lay out their bravest games, share tantalizing pizza, and engage in nail-biting ghost stories accompanied by strange echoes and unsettling winds.
As the night lengthens, mischievous gusts sweep through the cottage.
Doors creak open and slam shut suddenly; unseen drafts send the aged windows rattling.
These strange occurrences, which would ordinarily warrant attention and concern, are dismissed by the nervous teenagers as mere figments of their wild imagination.
Engrossed in a thrilling 'Truth-or-Dare' session, Sarah daringly asks Beth to push past her fear and investigate the increasingly strange sounds.
Beth is swallowed by the enveloping darkness within the cottage.
When Beth vanishes within the gloom of the old home, it's Mary who steps up to penetrate the haunting mystery of her friend's disappearance.
But minutes turned into hours, none returns, leaving the remaining two - Sarah and Leah - grappling with the reality of their ominous surroundings.
Overwhelmed with dread and desperate to escape, they find their efforts to escape the decaying cottage thwarted by an invisible entity.
This realization that they were trapped within the haunted cottage with their captor sends them spiraling into the depths of terror.
With their flickering hopes, they formulate a hazardous plan to confront their monstrous captor.
But the devastating sight of Beth and Mary - lifeless and terrified - leaves them overwhelmed with horror, mutating their dread into desperation.
In their terror and desperation, they stumble into a secret room adorned with yellowed newspaper clippings.
The disturbing reports are a testament to a ruthless serial killer who had once made this eerie cottage his home.

The horrifying revelation of their ghostly tormentor drenches them in bone-chilling dread, and they arm themselves with the nearest rusty, tarnished objects they could find, preparing for a showdown against the vengeful spirit.
Sarah makes a gut-wrenching decision as the tension erupts into a final stand.
Drawing the malevolent force toward herself, she ignites a fire in the aged cottage, providing Leah her only chance to escape and flee the horrific scene.
Amidst the roaring flames, the local police discover a collection of human skeletal remains buried within the burnt ruins, unleashing a haunting past tied to the now-destroyed cottage.
Sarah's sacrifice not only saves Leah from the chilling night but also unravels the century-old mystery, leading to a temporary calm in Pine Valley.
Leah attempts to cope with the traumatizing events, the horrific image of the haunted cottage, and the memories of her lost friends forever etched into her mind.
The narrative takes an unexpected, chilling twist as an alarming apparition materializes in the corners of Leah's room, the spectral figure hinting at a relentless return of the spectral killer.
The narrative, sharp and chilling, cuts to black, leaving Leah grasping at the possibility of another horrific adventure.
The chilling narrative concludes on a hair-raising cliffhanger, subtly starting the countdown to another cryptic tale brimming with adrenaline-pumping mysteries and heart-stopping horrors.

67410645.title: Slumber Party Massacre (2021 film)
synopsis: In 1993, Trish Devereaux is having a slumber party in a cabin in Holly Springs, California with friends Jackie, Kim, and Diane.
When Chad, Trish's ex-boyfriend, arrives to confront Trish, he looks through the window to see the girls dancing, and he begins to masturbate.
He sees a strange figure on the other side of the cabin.
The figure is Russ Thorn, a killer who uses his power drill and kills Chad.
When Russ makes his way inside the cabin, Kim and Diane are murdered.
When Trish tries to stop Jackie from opening the front door, Russ drills Jackie in the throat, killing her.
Despite getting drilled through her hand, Trish successfully escapes from Russ by hitting him with an oar, sending him inside the lake.
It is believed that Russ drowned but his body is never found.
In present-day Los Angeles, Trish's daughter Dana is heading out for a girls weekend with best friends Maeve, Breanie, and Ashley.
En route, the girls are in for a scare when they learn that Maeve's younger sister Alix had stowed away.
The girls reluctantly let Alix join them, as they are on their way to the house they rented.
Their car breaks down in the renamed Jolly Springs.
When Ashley sees an ad for a cabin for rent that night, the girls talk to Kay, the owner of the general store and the cabin.
Kay reluctantly lets the girls rent the cabin and warns them to stay quiet and stay still.
As the girls start dancing, Alix gets bored and goes out for a walk.
She sees a few guys at the cabin across the lake and soon finds the mechanic's truck in the middle of the road.
The mechanic Dave falls on Alix with drilled out eyes.
A blood-soaked Alix goes back to the cabin and warns the others when they see her.
The girls soon yell "pillow fight" and reveal to sport weapons such as knives and baseball bats.

The girls reveal to Alix that they know Russ Thorn is still alive and they have set everything up in an attempt to bait him out and kill him once and for all after 20 more victims have fallen since Trish's encounter.
The girls are interrupted by two of the guys from the cabin across the lake, John and Matt.
John reveals he is a huge fan of a crime podcast and he and his buddies have rented out the actual cabin Russ Thorn killed Trish's friends in.
Noticing the weapons, Matt freaks out and he and John leave.
Dana and Maeve realize that Russ could pop out and go after the guys so they decide to follow them.
The guys return to the cabin and have some fun with Sean, Guy 1, and Guy 2.
When Guy 1 decides to go for a quick walk outside the cabin, he sees Russ Thorn and is excited to see him.
That is until Russ breaks out the drill and kills Guy 1.
When the girls arrive to the guys' cabin, Russ turns off the lights and during the chaos, Russ kills Guy 2 by drilling him in the head.
Russ escapes and the girls soon reveal to the surviving guys that Russ is alive and they need to stop them.
Sean grabs his guitar while Matt and John grab legs off their chairs and go after Russ despite the girls' warning.
As Dana encounters Russ, a chase leads to Sean attempting to stop Russ and ends up getting drilled in the face.
When Russ follows Dana to her cabin, he attempts a sneak attack but soon is met by the girls, who after beating him up, gives Dana the chance to kill Russ with a slash to the throat.
Alix runs out and repeatedly stabs Russ, ensuring his death.
The next morning, the girls are relieved that they don't have to act fake anymore.
Meanwhile, Matt and John ponder everything going on.
Matt decides to take a shower and he is killed by a mysterious assailant.
When Alix is forced to watch Russ while they attempt to call the police, she begins to get violently ill from a tin of cookies gifted the night before.

Ashley, who is a mechanic, attempts to fix Maeve's SUV, but finds the hood closed in on her by the same mysterious assailant, who kills Ashley after turning on the motor, which causes the car's fan blades to make impact.
When the others discover both Russ' body has disappeared and sees Ashley under the hood, they are attacked by the assailant, who uses a nail gun.
Breanie heads to the window to see if it is safe, and she is killed by a nail to her eye.
Alix is still violently ill and Dana looks for help while Maeve takes care of her sister.
As Dana looks for help, she is confronted by John, who thinks she is responsible for Matt and Guy 1's death.
Dana tells John she killed Russ but did not kill her friends.
As Dana pleads with John that they should leave together to get help, John ends up ditching Dana.
Dana finds Kay and tells her what has happened.
Kay is revealed to be the mysterious assailant who killed Matt, Ashley, and Breanie because she is seeking revenge as she is none other than Russ Thorn's mother.
Kay goes after Dana, Maeve, and Alix but soon enough, Trish arrives and starts a fight with Kay.
When Kay uses a blade against Trish's injured hand, she is shocked to learn that Russ' drilling has caused the nerves in her hand to be completely damaged to where she can't feel pain.
Dana helps Trish by giving her Russ' broken drill bit and Trish kills Kay by stabbing her in the chest with the broken drill bit.
As Kay dies, Trish, Dana, Maeve, and Alix all hug as the terror finally ends.

61548197.title: Select or Perish
synopsis: John, a hushed and industrious software developer, leads a life of isolation in the middle of a bustling tech office.
It's just another uneventful Tuesday when a flyer advertising a local flea market catches John's attention amid a clutter of inconsequential memos.
Convinced to take a break from his work-dominated routine, John decides to explore the vibrant flea market after his long office hours.
Hundreds of stalls crammed with people are scattered around, yet John is taken aback by this little shop brimming with outdated radios, televisions, and quirky electronic items.
The shopkeeper - an elderly man known for his mystical demeanor and penetrating gaze - nudges John towards an unusual-looking game console named INPUT>V.
Captivated and under the influence of the proprietor's intriguing sales pitch, John buys the retro game console.
He takes a leave from the dimly lit flea market and embarks on his journey home, carrying his new toy.
At home, he prefers to drown out the contemporary squabbles of his two teenage children and the indifference of his wife, seeking refuge in the enthralling world of INPUT>V.
Hours morph into a late-night saga as John gets consumed into the game.
Inside the game, John's character faces a rebellious non-playable character (NPC), forcing him to make a tough call.
Essential decisions made through his game avatar strangely mirror his choices in the real world, bearing similarly disconcerting implications.
Yet, as time moves on, the coincidences continue to materialize, making John uneasy.
When the reflections become too uncanny to ignore, John tries to quit the game.
However, he finds himself immovably attached to the captivating gameplay.
As he continues his obsessive gaming, his health begins to take a hit.
His compulsion to play INPUT>V develops into an unhealthy obsession.
John's life spirals out of control.
Errors at work arise, his rocky relationship with his puzzled wife teeters on the brink, and impending mortgage defaults loom ominously.
Finally, he realizes the intricate intertwining of his real-life struggles and the choices he makes in the game.
Although petrified by this revelation, John resolves to play the game, not merely for leisure but for his survival.
He understands that he must persist to restore balance in his fading reality.
He then sets on a mission to conquer the action-packed game.
INPUT>V becomes an essential battleground for John, now fighting to regain control over his life.

Gradually, victories in the game start reflecting positively in John's turbulent reality: workplace stress seems manageable, finances show signs of recovery, and his estranged family starts rebuilding their weakened bonds.
Yet, as he clears each level in the game, John faces amplified intensity and increased stakes.
Each made decision grows weightier, and the resulting failure's consequences more severe.
Slowly, INPUT>V turns into a high-stakes survival challenge.
Every move is crucial, and any erroneous decision could potentially spell annihilation in John's real life.
Harnessing every ounce of his strategic acumen, John painstakingly plans an epic endgame.
After enduring moments filled with suspense and uncertainty, John finally hits the right combination of buttons and triumphs over INPUT>V.
As he scores the game-winning point, the oppressive grip of the game loosens.
For the first time in weeks, John feels a sense of liberation and breathes easily.
Viewing a serene evening with his now responsive family, the audience witnesses a soothing tranquility replacing the recent turbulence.
John’s diligent effort to maintain a healthy work-life balance begins bearing fruit.
Once a socially awkward workaholic, John has now evolved into a well-balanced individual armed with newfound resilience and determination.
From being a mere toy to a life-altering journey, INPUT>V catapulted John through a turbulent exploration that ended up positively reshaping his existence.
As he reminisces, John is pleasantly surprised by the ultimate challenge contained in INPUT>V - endurance, patience, and strategic prowess.
No longer a mere player in INPUT>V, John is now the master of his own fate, cherishing every moment of his transformed existence.
As the screen slowly fades to black, the audience is left reflecting on the inherent bond between the choices one makes and the rippling effects those decisions ignite.

68400682.title: Choose or Die
synopsis: Hal, a married man with a dysfunctional family who is a collector of retro video games, receives a copy of an interactive fiction computer game called CURS>R.
Hal installs the game and starts to play, expecting it to be nothing more than a classic 1980s text-based adventure game.
However, when the objects around him begin to interact with the game, he realises it is something more, culminating in his wife Laura cutting out their son Gabe's tongue.
Three months later, college student Kayla is working as a cleaner to pay for her studies.
She provides new and old technology to her computer-geek friend, Isaac, who in return helps her learn to code so that she can gain sufficient skills for her classes.

Kayla's mother, Thea, has become a drug addict after the death of her son Ricky, and also suffers psychological and sexual abuse from her rent collector, Lance, who supplies her with drugs and forces her into prostitution in exchange for not being evicted from her apartment.
One day while visiting Isaac after work, Kayla discovers the CURS>R game in his apartment, along with a phone number offering a $125,000 prize.
She calls the number and receives a recorded message from the Terror Director telling her to complete the game and insert the number code at the end of it to win the money.
Attracted by the offer, Kayla accepts the challenge, thinking it will be easy money, and arranges a deal with Isaac to share the prize.
That night, Kayla starts playing the game in a café and discovers that it can interfere with reality in different ways—the game level ending with a waitress eating broken glass and dying.
The next day, Kayla tries to stop the game by destroying the tape.
She tells Isaac what happened, but he finds her story hard to believe.
Later, while Kayla is working a graveyard shift, her mother desperately calls her for help.
Kayla discovers that CURS>R has managed to escape to the net and is following her, forcing her to choose ways to save her mother from a giant rat.
Thea eventually falls from her bedroom window and, severely injured, ends up in hospital.
Later that night, Kayla goes to Isaac's apartment and together they try to discover the mystery behind the game.
They find a sort of code in the sound of CURS>R, in an unknown language, and theorise it is what allows the game to interact with the real world.
Together they manage to survive the night after the game exploits Kayla's trauma over the death of her brother, who drowned in a public pool.
Isaac and Kayla hack the prize number to a storage facility where the game was created.

In recording sessions of the making of CURS>R, they discover that the creator of the game, Beck, found a curse in different symbols and embedded the codes into the game to gain more benefits by using the suffering of gamers.
When they discover the code needed, the game traps Isaac and forces Kayla to choose in order to save him, but ends up killing him.
The game orders Kayla to "beat the boss" and gives her a set of coordinates to follow that lead her to Hal's house, now a cruel man who tortures Laura and Gabe.
Hal explains that he never ended the game and after two levels, it promised to leave them alone if he made more copies of it.
The game then orders both Kayla and Hal to fight while reversing the pain that each experiences; i.e., if Hal is hurt, Kayla feels it and if Kayla is hurt, Hal feels it.
An intense fight ensues, during which Hal is drowned and Kayla barely manages to survive.
Kayla receives the game prize, which enables her to take total control of the curse.
She uses this ability to kill Lance, which heals both herself and her mother.
It is then revealed that the building in which Kayla worked is owned by Beck, who asks her who is next to suffer.
Kayla answers that it will be only the ones who deserve to.

86660931.title: Defender: The Missile Crisis
synopsis: Lieutenant-colonels John and Sarah, highly respected commanders operating a clandestine regional missile command site named AeroDefense, situated in the distant outskirts of Nevada, are the frontline defense preserving the safety of this widely-risk American military outpost.
A novel day heralds an unexpected turn of events, as they conduct their habitual security and system checks.
They encounter an unnerving piece of news that shakes the stability they are accustomed to.
The reports reveal veiled intelligence that indicates towards Borodin, an adversary East European nation, been suspected of pilfering a Titan III Intercontinental Ballistic Missile.
Immediately AeroDefense's built-in security arrangements are intensified.
In an abrupt turn of events, AeroDefense witnesses a ruthless assault from an unexpected enemy force speculated to be highly-trained agents from Borodin.
With internal emergency now a reality, John and Sarah undertake a perilous mission to neutralize the threat at hand without compromise to their base's security or personnel.
Mark, a former Special Forces soldier who now serves as a control systems technician, in the chaos, uncovers a game-changing piece of intelligence.
He finds concrete evidence pointing at the fact that the theft of the Titan III missile wasn’t an act of a foreign power, but a domestic betrayal at the hands of an inside man.
The plot thickens with the shocking revelation of a secondary missile site, Camp Sigma, nestled in the vast southern plains of Arizona.
Surprised but resilient, John, Sarah, and Mark manage to weather the primary storm and establish a secure communication line with the clandestine Camp Sigma.
Despite the internal turmoil, they manage to rally the remaining allies within the base, tirelessly battling against the Borodin insurgents.
They subtly inform Camp Sigma about a mole nestled within their ranks.

Meanwhile, the climax intensifies with the terrifying confirmation that the absconded Titan III missiles are on the move, prepped for launch against key industrial and military setups scattered across America.
John, Sarah, and Mark, back at AeroDefense, resort to the advanced satellite surveillance and communication equipment, closely tracking enemy movements.
After grueling efforts, they successfully decode the enemy's devastating plan of a violent coup following the planned missile strikes.
As they pinpoint the enemy’s stronghold, hidden deep within the labyrinth of the Rocky Mountains, the stage is set for a high-stakes showdown.
The team discovers the stolen Titan III missiles, ready for launch, concealed within the labyrinthine depths of the enemy’s subterranean base.
Sarah steps up to a leadership role, rallying military units from the Army, Navy, and Air Force, strategically securing nationwide hotspots to alleviate potential cataclysms.
She masterminds an analytical counterstrike.
Parallelly, John confronts the traitor in a tension-filled rendezvous while Mark shoulders the intricate job of disarming the deadly missiles.
Mark's fortitude eventually pays off when he successfully disarms the missiles.
Their timely intervention aborts a malicious coup, safeguarding innumerable American lives.
The traitor is finally cornered, and his insidious plan is completely nullified.
The movie concludes with the chilling implication that more traitors lurk within AeroDefense.
As John, Sarah, and Mark mull over their sacrifices and near-death experiences, their enduring dedication and courage are celebrated.
The narrative examines the implications of treachery, the significance of undying camaraderie, the ethics of secrecy, and the aftermath of information asymmetry within the military ranks.
Despite all they've endured, they persist in embodying values of honesty and transparency and demonstrate service before self.
Standing triumphant after the battle, the film closes with them fearlessly anticipating future challenges.
With their refusal to bow down still shining against the odds, they leave a lasting impression on the viewers, making them eagerly anticipate future installments of the saga.

66994705.title: Interceptor (film)
synopsis: The United States has two interceptor launch sites aimed at intercepting any nuclear warhead launches; the first, Fort Greely in Alaska, is attacked by unknown assailants presumably affiliated with a terrorist faction, while 16 nuclear warheads are simultaneously seized from Russian territory.
The second site is a remote platform in the middle of the Pacific Ocean.
U.S. Army Captain J. J. Collins is recently reassigned to the latter of the two interceptor missile launch sites.
Following a high-profile case where she reported sexual misconduct by her superior, she experienced hazing, bullying and threats and a new deployment as retaliation.
Under Lt.
Colonel Marshall, and working alongside Cpl.
Beaver Baker and Cpl.
Rahul Shah in the station's command center, Collins is part of the last line of defense after the hostile takeover of Fort Greely.

The station is infiltrated by a small group of operatives led by ex-military intelligence soldier Kessel, who promptly kill Marshall and the other occupants of the base, leaving only Collins, Shah, and an unconscious Beaver (who was grazed by a stray bullet) in the command center.
The infiltrators attempt to enter the command center, by which they can disarm the interceptor system and leave the U.S. open to nuclear attack from the sixteen stolen warheads.
However, they are rebuffed and attempt to forcibly enter instead with blowtorches.
An operative launches a surprise attack after entering via a floor hatch, but is defeated and killed by Collins and Shah.

Beaver regains consciousness and reveals himself to be an inside man for the infiltrators and motivated by a big payday and xenophobia, holding both Collins and Shah at gunpoint while allowing Kessel and the remaining operatives to enter and assume control.

Kessel hijacks a live feed and streams his manifesto about the failures in the history of the United States online, naming the sixteen American cities to be destroyed, and instructing the terrorist faction to launch the nukes immediately.

Collins breaks free of her restraints and locks Kessel, Beaver, and a henchman back out of the command center, while defeating and killing Kira, the lone enemy operative still in the room, and another henchman.
Kessel attempts to force Collins to surrender, torturing her father, but she refuses and her father is apparently killed when the transmission is cut.
Kessel then plans to scuttle the station if he cannot take control of it.

As the station begins to sink, Shah volunteers to drop through the floor hatch to the ocean below and manually re-engage the station's hatches, such that the interceptors are still able to launch and destroy the warheads when they eventually pass through the airspace overhead.
Shah succeeds, but he is killed by Beaver.
Collins hides in the command center and letting Kessel, Beaver, and the remaining henchman take over and disable the seemingly empty center.
Her ruse works, with Beaver going to check up on the station's roof to find and eliminate her.
Collins is able to stealthily dispatch the remaining henchman while Kessel flees the room.
Grabbing a laptop, Collins ascends to the roof and plugs the device in, hoping to manually launch the interceptor missiles using this method.
She is found by Beaver and they engage in hand to hand combat, with Collins emerging victorious after using razor wire to decapitate Beaver.

Kessel, who had called in a Russian submarine to pick up the team of operatives earlier, finds Collins just as she successfully launches the interceptor missiles with a fraction of a second left before the nukes would have crossed the point of interception.
His plan failed, he engages in combat with Collins, who manages to defeat and subdue him, just as the Russian submarine ascends from the sea.
A pair of Russians emerge from the submarine tower, but rather than shooting Collins, they fire at Kessel instead, and the Russian Captain salutes Collins before departing.
Collins later recovers from her ordeal in the hospital, and she is personally given a promotion by the U.S. president for her efforts.
She also receives a visit of her father who had been rescued by friends who had witnessed his plight on the live broadcast, and he comforts her over her grief for Shah's death.

56883310.title: Brothers Contraption Mayhem: A Girl's Struggle Against Chaos
synopsis: The film makes its debut introducing a picturesque yellow, four-bedroom suburban home on a leafy quiet street.

The audience meets twelve-year-old Emily, a bright and responsible kid who is engrossed in solving algebraic expressions, her yearly goal to beat is finishing all her homework before the school year ends.

At the same time, a low hum of mayhem can be heard in the background, orchestrated by her seven-year-old twin brothers; Benjamin and Billy, both rambunctious and overflowing with energy and creativity.

As the multi-tasking Emily is juggling between the complex equations and keeping her energetic twin brothers in check, their mother, a nationally acclaimed architect, is shown in a detailed pan of her immaculately kept home office, engaged in a serious video call discussing her latest skyscraper project with board members.
The camera guides the viewers to the family's garage - a scene of complete disarray with old bicycle parts, kitchen appliances littering the space.

The twins are engrossed in what seems to be a scientific R&D operation, which involves creating a chaotic mesh of household objects that they perceive as an ingenious solution to do mundane household chores.

Then, the camera brings the audience back to Emily, rolling her eyes at the spectacle in the garage, but the traces of a warm smile on her face indicate a deep love for her brothers' enthusiasm and the evident innocence of their actions.
The twins, now covered in dirt and sweat, reveal their labor of love - a haphazard machine created out of the remnants of a vacuum cleaner and rusty gears, to a doubtful Emily.
They proclaim with wide eyes and expectant smiles that it's a revolutionary invention that can carry out all the house chores.
Enthusiastic about proving their genius, they turn on the contraption to showcase its capability, attempting first to sort a mountain of multicolored laundry, a task that Emily detested each weekend.
To everyone's surprise, the machine roars into life, initially slow but gradually gaining momentum.
The sight of it sputtering clothes in different directions across the living room's gleaming hardwood floor is both comic and concerning.
Emily's amused grin fades into panic as she realizes the chaos unfolding.
Her tranquil home is now a set-up for a slapstick comedy scene with flying socks and scarves spinning around the room.

Not wanting to miss capturing this hilarious yet alarming moment, Emily whips out her red iPhone planning to unveil to their busiest-ever mom about the adventurous aftermath of her brothers' resourceful but haphazard inventions.
However, every attempt to focus and capture the unfolding catastrophe is foiled as she finds herself wound up in a tornado of clothes, tripping over randomly scattered Lego blocks.
