Annie's condition was deteriorating by the day, and she was too weak to fight.
Jimmy had to find a way to save her, and he would do whatever it took even if it jeopardized his own life.
It seemed like all hope was lost until the local sheriff discovered Whit's plan.
With his help, Jimmy and Annie were able to confront Whit and put an end to his reign of terror.
They were able to have the last few months of Annie's life filled with love and happiness.
The siblings were able to overcome all odds and prove that no matter what obstacles life throws at you, there is always a way to make it through.
He was always asking questions and seemed to know too much about them.
Jimmy was shocked to find Annie living in a rundown apartment and struggling to make ends meet.
He was determined to make her last year the best it could possibly be and worked hard to save up enough money to move her into a nicer apartment and pay her medical bills.
He also took her out on trips and made sure she was able to do all the things she had always wanted to do.
During this time, a mysterious stranger named Whit Price showed up in their small town claiming to be related to the Ray siblings.
With nobody else left in their family, the Ray siblings welcomed him into their lives.
Although he was a different kind of person who had an eerie presence about him, always asking questions and seemingly knowing too much about them, Jimmy and Annie allowed him to stay.
Little did they know, Whit had been using their home as a base of operations for his criminal activities.
The police eventually caught wind of Whit’s activities and arrested him.
Jimmy was determined to help his best friend, Annie, who was diagnosed with cancer.
He had promised her that he would do whatever he could to make her last year of life the best it could be.
He stayed by her side through her treatments, and tried to lift her spirits with trips to the park, a new hobby, and other activities.
Though Jimmy was able to bring some joy to Annie's days, he couldn't help but feel guilty for not being able to do more for her.
He also felt guilty for not being able to be there for her during her painful treatments and the difficult moments.
He was determined to keep his promise and help her live her last year to the fullest.
Jimmy took Annie on vacations, to the movies, and out to dinner.
He also gave her presents that she had always wanted but never got.
He did everything he could to make her happy and to create memories that she could cherish.
Despite all of Jimmy's efforts, the cancer took its toll and Annie passed away.
Though he was devastated, Jimmy was grateful that he was able to fulfill his promise and give Annie the best last year of her life.
He was comforted in knowing that she was able to experience the joy of life with him one last time.
Annie had never heard of Whit Price, but when she met him, she quickly realized that there was a vendetta between him and the Ray siblings.
Whit had been a high school teacher who was highly respected by his students, but he had lost his job due to the Ray siblings' astounding academic excellence.
It was clear that Whit was determined to get his revenge, and so he plotted to take their lives.
He soon set out to murder them with a sharp knife he had retrieved from his apartment.
Fortunately, the police were alerted and they managed to intervene in time.
Although Whit had attempted to take the life of the Ray siblings, Schmidt had doubts that he could have actually carried out the kill.
The Ray siblings were eventually convicted of harboring a fugitive and sentenced to a year in prison.
Annie was shocked to learn of the events that had transpired and was glad that the police had managed to intervene in time.
The convicted on the recently returned to the police force after a stint in prison, Jimmy and Annie were arrested and taken in for questioning at the police station.
They nervously shuffled into the interrogation room, glancing around the sterile, intimidating environment.
Sitting across from them at the table was a formidable figure, Whit Price.
As an experienced detective, he had dealt with cases like theirs before, and he seemed to have the upper hand.
Jimmy and Annie could not hide the fear and confusion in their faces.
Despite feeling overwhelmed, they stayed committed to their story.
They had no idea that Price had a shady past - a criminal who had returned to the police force after being incarcerated.
His impressive arrest track record gave him a reputation, and his sharp mind made it hard for anyone to beat him during questioning.
Despite this challenge, Jimmy and Annie had to stay true to their statements if they were to have hope of escaping jail time.
Although Jimmy and Annie were gone, the justice system had prevailed and the man who had taken them away was now behind bars for his heinous crimes.
Jimmy's experience was life-changing and he was determined to make the most of it.
Though the tragedy was painful, Jimmy found happiness in the time he shared with Annie and the memories they made together.
His newfound determination led him to start his own business, and as his success grew, his story became an inspiring one.
Whit, the person who took Jimmy and Annie away, was eventually brought to justice and arrested for his crimes.
During the investigation, it was revealed that Whit had also killed the Ray siblings' innocent friend.
This sent shockwaves throughout the community and left many feeling unsafe.

The devastating tragedy had taken three innocent lives, but through the justice system, some solace was found knowing that the person responsible was now behind bars and could no longer hurt anyone else.
Jimmy's experience had changed him forever and he was grateful for the second chance he had been given.

90531107.title: Deficiencies (movie)
synopsis: John Smith, a determined 24-year-old man from New York City, cooped up in a shabby apartment with faded paint and creaking floorboards, nurtures his dream of breathing life into captivating narratives as a revered movie director.
His eyes frequently settle on his proudest possession - a diploma from the New York Film Academy, hanging askew on the apartment's scarred wall.
Every time he sighs, laden with frustration and hopes alike, it communicates a profound vow to his dreams yet to break through the gloom.
His days are consumed by a series of grueling jobs.
He washes an endless stack of greasy dishes at Joe’s Diner, and at night helps an excited crowd find their seats in the Times Square Cinema, their hands full of popcorn tubs.
His nights, on the other hand, are reserved for impassioned writing.
The piece de resistance of his unwavering focus is an emotive script titled "Deficiencies".
He spends hours refining it, every character etched with precision, each plot twist, and poignant dialogue carefully constructed from his gritty experiences and keen observational skills.
With a firm grasp on his work, he presents it to the judgment of several influential Hollywood production houses, displaying immense tenacity.
However, his efforts are met with solid walls of rejection, uninterested glances, and an avalanche of impersonal rejection letters.
But each rejection serves only as fuel for John’s resolute ambition, giving birth to a stronger resolve deep within his heart.
Amidst the tide of disappointment, John’s friends, Daisy and Martin, emerge as forces of stability – consoling him, cheering for him, and standing by his side.
Daisy is an aspiring Broadway actress, and Martin a hopeful actor.
They infuse John with courage, sharing stories of struggle and dreams, building a cocoon of support around him.

After seeing the struggles that John is facing, Daisy and Martin suggest a strategic plan – to present his unique screenplay at the groundbreaking Sundance Film Festival, a platform known to welcome innovative narratives.
This potential turning point rekindles a flicker of hope in John’s eyes, setting him ablaze with renewed determination.
Despite several financial challenges and an array of other issues, John doubles his efforts in refining "Deficiencies" for the festival.
He manages to strike a balance between his monotonous day job and the nighttime writing sessions, feeding his voracious hunger for his art.
John, visibly anxious, steps onto the buzzing premises of the Sundance Film Festival, his screenplay in hand.
Mr. Robert Simmons, a wealthy financier, is struck by the commercial potential wrapped within the evocative narrative of "Deficiencies".
However, he proposes significant changes to the script, altering dialogues, modifying scenes, even suggesting central characters to be replaced.
A difficult choice lies ahead for John; a choice between his desperate need for success or keeping his work unscathed.
He sighs, swallowing his objections, and reluctantly agrees.
What follows is a flurry of activity; the production commences amidst a storm of excitement, trepidation, and heated debates on the film's direction.
Disagreements between John and Mr. Simmons regarding casting decisions and screenplay modifications crop up, clouding the initial high hopes.
John begins to feel overwhelmed by the dizzying glamour of the movie industry, and his lack of experience makes it harder for him to fight for his rights.
Tensions rise when Mr. Simmons' pressure causes "Deficiencies" to deviate dramatically from its original core, distorting it into something unrecognizable.
When a fierce argument brings the production to a sudden halt, John is left grappling with the thought of letting go of his life-long dream.
Observing his plunge into a stifling turmoil, Daisy and Martin intervene, urging John to fight for his original vision, reminding him of the ignited passion that set this journey in motion.
Encouraged, John begins again, this time presenting "Deficiencies", untouched and all the more powerful, to a smaller but more accepting independent production house.
They are drawn towards the unique narrative and heartfelt honesty in John’s script.
With a reignited spark, the journey of "Deficiencies" resumes, but this time it remains closely aligned with the genuine spirit of its creator.
The day finally dawns when "Deficiencies", preserved in its raw and authentic form, is ready to meet its eager audience.
It debuts at the Sundance Film Festival, where "Deficiencies" first earned recognition.
The dreams that once echoed starkly within his neglected apartment have come to life, resonating deeply with those privy to the emotional journey of "Deficiencies".
John Smith, once a hopeful young man living in a deteriorating apartment, has emerged as an esteemed movie director, a transformation beyond his wildest dreams.
His once withered, potted plants mirror his aspirations blooming from mere dreams to tangible realities.
The friends who once shared cheap beers in a crumbling apartment now clink champagne glasses at lavish premieres.
The once-aspiring filmmaker is now synonymous with one of the most innovative storytelling perspectives of contemporary cinema.
The dilapidated apartment once a testament to despair now serves as a humble symbol of a life that pirouetted between ordinary routine and extraordinary dreams.
A hopeful film student from a rundown apartment transformed into a lauded director basking in the success of his debut movie - John's life has truly come a full circle.
One thing remains consistently unchanging - his thirst for creating more stories, a desire to explore the depths of the cinematic world reveals that John Smith was, and will always remain, a dreamer.

72716092.title: Shortcomings (film)
synopsis: Ben Tagawa is an aspiring filmmaker and film school dropout.
He lives in Berkeley with his girlfriend Miko, who works for an Asian American film festival, though he is dismissive of Miko’s passion for politics and the Asian American community.
At his day job managing an arthouse movie theater, Ben hires Autumn, a young white woman, as a ticket seller.
Miko confronts him at their apartment about pornography she found on his computer, which confirms her suspicions that he has a sexual preference for white women.
Ben denies this and tries to invalidate her concerns.
While they appear to have resolved the fight, Miko reveals later that she has accepted a three-month internship in NYC.
Ben talks over the news with his best friend Alice, a 'womanizing' lesbian who flirts with Nina, the waitress at the diner.
When Ben calls Miko, now in NYC, he acts dismissively towards her interests.
Upset, she says that they should take a break from the relationship.
Ben asks out Autumn and attends one of her performance art shows.
When they return to her apartment after the show, he makes a derogatory joke about Autumn’s experimental art, and she rebuffs his attempt to kiss her.
After his failed date with Autumn, Alice invites Ben to a queer house party.
She says that she is no longer seeing Nina, as she wanted to enter a serious relationship, and Alice is only interested in casual dating.
At the party, Ben strikes up a conversation with Sasha, a grad student.
She visits him at the movie theater and they begin dating.
While Ben is excited about Sasha, Alice tells him that she has been suspended from her grad program for kicking Nina’s roommate, who confronted her.
Therefore she has decided to travel to New York, upsetting Ben.
Sasha breaks up with Ben a few weeks later.
Although she had told him she was single, she was actually on a break with her girlfriend, who has since returned from doing research abroad.
At work, Ben announces that the movie theater is closing due to declining ticket sales and seismic issues.
Ben attempts to call Miko but receives no response, and also fails to make progress on a screenplay that he is working on.
Alice invites him to NYC, since he has hit “rock bottom.” There, Ben stays with Alice, who to his surprise is now in a serious relationship with Meredith, a Barnard professor.
When he tries to surprise Miko at her internship, he learns from the actual intern that Miko has never worked there.
Alice and Ben also discover that Miko has been modeling for Leon, a fashion designer.
They stake out Miko’s address and see her holding hands with him.
Upset that Miko is dating a white man, Ben rants to Meredith and Alice and assumes that Leon is an Asian fetishist.
In response, Meredith asks him about his own racial preference for white women.
Feeling defensive, Ben references Alice kicking Nina’s roommate, causing a fight between Meredith and Alice.
Ben returns to Miko’s address and confronts Miko and Leon in the street.
Leon lets them talk privately in the apartment, where Ben tells Miko that Leon is fetishizing her because of her race, based on Leon’s professed interests in East Asian culture.
Miko calls out Ben’s own hypocrisy for being angry she’s dating someone else, as her friend saw Ben and Sasha on a date as well.
Miko acknowledges she should have told him about Leon, but he needs to look into his own toxic behaviors and that their relationship is over.
Returning to Meredith’s, Ben apologizes to her and Alice for causing their fight and announces that he is leaving the city earlier than planned.
While he at first runs towards Miko and Leon’s apartment, he sees the happy couple in a café together, so catches a cab to the airport to return to Berkeley.

49457592.title: Abyssal Quake
synopsis: Dr. Harold Carter, Emory University's most renowned marine biologist with years of deep-sea experience under his belt, and Dr. Elena Russo, a daring professional diver with multiple records tied to her name from the World Aquatics Championships, form an integral part of Alpha Corporation's top-tier underwater research crew.

Joined by the sharp mind of Jim 'Mac' MacAllister, a revered geologist known throughout the East Coast for his innovative contributions to plate tectonics, and Ray Chien, a proficient Silicon Valley computer engineer with an unparalleled knack for data and comms systems, they set forth to explore the raging depths of the ocean.

Ensconced comfortably within the titanium confines of Pegasus 777, Alpha Corp's monstrous deep-sea research station, this skilled crew meticulously conducts a groundbreaking geological mapping of the seafloor.
On an otherwise uneventful evening, seismic readings begin to ripple across their state-of-the-art systems, teasing the possibility of an untapped uranium deposit lurking beneath them.

Amid their raucous laughter and celebratory tales, an unsettling undercurrent spreads through the station; an 'Abyssal Quake,' A forceful reminder of the ocean's might, ripples through the icy water, echoing precariously within the steel stronghold.

Overwhelming the Pegasus 777 with its strength, the quake puppeteers the station into violent spasms; wires spark, circuits short, and the once reliable titanium alloy structure whimpers under the immense pressure.
In the chilling aftermath of the shock, the crew finds their cutting-edge communication entities eerily silent, marking the beginning of their isolation seven miles beneath the jagged waves.

As they grapple with the abysmal silence and sway of their new reality, a symphony of strange, rhythmically pulsating hums sweeps up from the previously serene ocean floor, injecting a sharp chill of trepidation within the stations' inescapable titanium walls.
With a quick search unveiling the presence of a nearly forgotten backup generator, the team reassures themselves with a rebirth of flickering emergency lighting.
However, their celebration is cut short by the realization that the gods of satellite communication still remain cold and unresponsive.

As the scant supplies of food within the station threaten to diminish and the breathing air converts into a ruthlessly rationed commodity, strategic planning metamorphoses into the crew’s survival lifeline.
Rising fear turns into a visceral panic as 'Mac,' their youngest yet most vibrant crew member, inexplicably vanishes amidst the maze of creaking corridors of the damaged structure.

An unfathomable revelation soon rises from the consuming darkness; their ambitious drilling operation had unwittingly stirred an unknown colony of bioluminescent deep-sea creatures – softly glowing, intelligent, and fiercely protective.

Armed with this terrifying knowledge, the beleaguered team pools their thought processes to reinvent their scientific equipment, transforming them into hopeful armaments against their aquatic assailants and hopeful tools for their surface ascension.

The unassuming Pegasus 777 morphs into a claustrophobic titanium fortress, each minute sapping oxygen from the limited reserves and escalating the relentless terror that mothers every echoing heartbeat.

Beating against the steadily rising odds, the increasingly hardened team disassembles the stubbornly quiet communication devices, breathing new life into the shattered pieces as an improvised distress signal.

Despite their fortified defenses and harrowed will, the bioluminescent creatures wage an unforgiving war, callously taking the lives of wise Dr. Carter and proficient Ray Chien, their ethereal glow forever an imprint of their ruthless onslaught.

With death closing in around the survivors, Dr. Russo and Mac's last glimmer of hope rests within the haphazardly encoded distress signal, a desperate SOS encrypted with their coordinates in the icy aquatic expanse.
The breathing hymn of their persistent transmission finally echoes to life within the formidable Alpha Corporation headquarters.
Their rescue teams, brave veterans of countless perilous extractions, hastily board a cutting-edge submarine armed with the latest in deep-sea survival gear.

As the submarine plunges into the inky depths, unbeknownst of the monstrous horrors that lie in wait, they face unforeseen challenges that threaten their crew and nearly disable their high-tech vessel.
The bioluminescent creature's aggressive resistance proves too formidable, their strategically planned rescue operation teetering on the edge of catastrophic failure.
With their vessel damaged and their unit under siege, the sleeve-tightened rescue team employs their final strategy.

Amid brewing underwater hurricanes and the piercing glow of the creatures, the brave rescue team hoists the defiant yet severely wounded survivors, Dr. Russo and Mac, into relative safety via heavy-duty cable lines.
The chilling aftermath of this dangerous voyage unveils grim evidence of the monstrous entities.
Their bioluminescent glow still haunting the vast inky trenches beneath the waves, they emerge as a horrifying addition to the catalog of deep-sea lifeforms.

Amid the rattled survivors, a cloud of heavy dread hangs; a chilling reminder of the horrors lurking beneath the serene ocean surface, promising that the terrifying abyss might yet again, rise to haunt humanity.

53279790.title: Underwater (film)
synopsis: In 2050, the Kepler 822, a research and drilling facility operated by Tian Industries at the bottom of the Mariana Trench, is struck by what is assumed to be a strong earthquake.
As part of the facility is destroyed by the incident, mechanical engineer Norah Price and her colleagues, Rodrigo and Paul, make their way to the escape pod bay.
However, the three discover that all of the escape pods have already been deployed, with Captain Lucien being the only person in the area when the three arrive.
Together they reach a control base and find biologist Emily Haversham and engineer Liam Smith, who are unsuccessful in their attempts to make contact with the surface.
Lucien suggests using pressurized suits to walk one mile across the ocean floor to Roebuck 641 in the hope of resurfacing from there.
As they descend in a freight elevator, Rodrigo's defective helmet implodes under the water pressure, killing him.
The surviving crew see a distress beacon from one of the escape pods below, and Smith and Paul go to investigate.
As they arrive at the location, they find a body in the rubble.
A creature emerges from the corpse's back and attacks them.
Smith kills the creature and takes it inside.
Haversham examines the creature and realizes that it belongs to a previously undiscovered species.
The five make their way to the sea floor, but as they are walking, the Kepler explodes above and nearly buries them in debris.
Smith is hit, but Price and Lucien save him.
They manage to get through an access tunnel to an intermediate station, where they can charge and clean their suits.
However, they find that Smith's oxygen scrubber is badly damaged from the debris.
On their way through the access tunnel, Paul is attacked by an unknown creature, dragged underwater, and killed.
Before the team leaves the access tunnel, they find that Smith's damaged oxygen pod will cause him to suffocate from the explosion's toxic fumes.
Unwilling to leave another crew member behind, Price, Lucien, and Haversham agree to help Smith walk.
The four set off across the ocean floor, but a humanoid creature appears and drags Smith into a cave.
Lucien manages to get Smith out, but he is pulled from the other three.
Price is dragged along with Lucien, but Lucien sacrifices himself to spare Price from the increasing pressure differential.
Price ends up at the abandoned Shepard station alone and is able to change her damaged diving suit before continuing toward Roebuck.
Walking along the ocean floor, she reunites with Haversham and Smith, and proceeds to help drag Smith.
As they enter Roebuck, they encounter a nest of the humanoid creatures hanging from the ceiling and try to sneak by, but the sound of Haversham's oxygen alarm wakes the creatures.
Price is partially swallowed by one of the creatures but is able to kill it and free herself.
The three manage to reach the escape pod bay, but Price discovers that only two of the pods are functional.
Price and Haversham manage to get the ailing Smith into a pod, and Price persuades Haversham to take the last one.
As this happens, a gigantic creature emerges and attacks the Roebuck while the smaller creatures follow the two escape pods.
Price, accepting her impending death, initiates an overload of the Roebuck's nuclear core, resulting in a massive explosion that kills the creatures and allows the escape pods to reach the surface.
This is followed by news headlines that say there were only two survivors, suggesting none of the other escape pods made it.
Tian Industries refuses to be involved with investigations into the events and prepares to expand its drilling efforts.

75694242.title: Revelations: Night Out in the City
synopsis: Robert, the endearing host of a local news talk show aired on WGNX-TV, is a treasured member of Clearfield, a tranquil town nestled in Kansas.
The simplicity that defines Robert's life takes a sudden turn when his charismatic old college roommate, Daniel, pays him a surprise visit.
Daniel, a flourishing advertising executive, hails from the fast-paced world of New York City.
Daniel, now enveloped in the unyielding cadence of New York life, makes an enticing proposition to Robert.
Daniel assures him of substantial networking possibilities, as well as the chance to rub shoulders with influential media figures within the bustling city that never sleeps.

Stirred by a newfound sense of curiosity and piqued adventure, Robert, for the first time, ventures out of his serene life in Clearfield to embark on an extraordinary odyssey towards the dizzying skyline of New York.
Daniel orchestrates Robert's immersion into the city's life, introducing him to influential media personalities such as Lauren Laverne and Anderson Cooper.
He is taken to dazzling galas held in luxuriant locations like the Rainbow Room.
On a bustling Friday evening, they step into The Stonewall Inn, a vibrant gay bar situated in Greenwich Village.
Amid the pulsing rhythm of celebratory beats and the vibrancy of rainbow-flag adorned surroundings, Daniel chooses to reveal a part of his life that Robert was unaware of - his homosexuality.
This unforeseen announcement leaves Robert grappling with a whirlwind of emotions, filled with surprise, confusion, and the challenge of deconstructing preconceived notions about homosexuality.
Alone in his rented apartment located in the bustling heart of Midtown Manhattan, Robert contemplates this unexpected revelation.
Robert brings a positive change to his television show by inviting members of the LGBTQ+ community for discussions and interviews.
Robert discovers a multifaceted, diverse community.
Their resilience and vibrancy profoundly unsettle everything Robert had initially misunderstood about the community.
As New York's relentless bustle becomes his new norm, and his professional journey evolves into a pathway for social change, Robert finds himself wrestling his recently unearthed sexual identity.
The emotional tumult magnifies with the sudden realization of his deep-seated feelings towards Daniel.
A confusing warmth towards Daniel dominates Robert's heart, leaving him spiraling into a whirlpool of confusing emotions.
Looking for solace in this turbulent time, he turns to the LGBTQ+ individuals he had met during his show, candidly revealing his internal struggle.
The compassion and understanding he receives from these individuals grant him the acceptance he needed.
A heart-to-heart conversation with an elderly gay man who had weathered similar struggles inspires Robert to truly understand and accept his sexuality, and with that, his feelings for Daniel.
With newfound courage and determination, Robert decides to share his journey with his audience by introducing the topic of "Coming out" on his television talk show.
In an episode that defies societal conventions, Robert admits his love for Daniel and reveals his homosexuality to millions of viewers nationwide.
His revelation disrupts the societal norms, dividing his audience into two - those who commend Robert's bravery and those who raise eyebrows.
Yet, amidst the ensuing controversy, his admission stirs an undercurrent of change in the public psyche, sparking a nationwide dialogue on homosexuality and broader acceptance.
The narrative culminates with a stirring scene of Robert and Daniel, hand-in-hand, walking through the shimmering lights of Times Square.
The scene symbolizes not just their endearing love, but also Robert's complete acceptance of his identity in a society that's slowly but surely moving towards acceptance.

70351362.title: Spoiler Alert (film)
synopsis: In 2001, Michael Ausiello, a writer for TV Guide, is brought to a gay nightclub by his best friend in Manhattan.
There, he meets photographer Kit Cowan, and the two instantly connect.
As they begin dating, Michael struggles with his insecurities of not being attractive enough for Kit, previously being overweight.
Kit reveals that he had an affair.
They both admit their fears of being in a long-term relationship since neither of them had been in one before, but they decide to continue dating.
During their first Christmas together, Kit gives Michael his own closet space at his apartment.
One year later, Kit gets an appendectomy.
His parents, Bob and Marilyn, come to Manhattan, and Kit has yet to come out to them.
Marilyn grows suspicious of Michael.
After she incessantly interrogates him, Kit comes out to his parents and reveals that Michael is his boyfriend.
While initially upset that Kit could not admit this to her, Marilyn is accepting and welcomes Michael.
Michael and Kit continue their relationship and move into a townhouse together.
During their second Christmas, Kit joins Michael in lying under the Christmas tree with him as Michael explains it was a childhood fantasy of his to do it every year with his partner.
In 2013, Michael and Kit develop complications in their relationship as their sex life deteriorates.
Michael spends too much time with his company TVLine and becomes an alcoholic.
He also suspects Kit is having an affair with his coworker, Sebastian.
Their therapist believes they now resent each other, but they still love each other enough to not want to end it.
He suggests that they separate to reassess their feelings.
Kit moves out, but the two remain in their relationship.
During their thirteenth Christmas, Kit begins showing signs of ill health.
In 2014, Kit is diagnosed with a rare form of stage-4 neuroendocrine cancer.
Michael, still traumatized by his mother's death from cancer, moves Kit back in and the two reconcile.
Michael supports Kit as he undergoes treatment.
Kit's health worsens and is given six weeks left to live.
Michael apologizes to Kit for not letting him know how beautiful he was due to his fears of being left for a more attractive man.
Kit apologizes to Michael for having an affair with Sebastian.
Kit proposes to Michael and they marry the next day.
The two spend their last Christmas together, with Michael fantasizing himself and Kit growing old and lying under the Christmas tree together.
In 2015, Kit is taken to the hospital.
As Kit nears death, Michael allows Sebastian to say goodbye to him.
As Kit is dying, Michael fantasizes interviewing Kit as a departing actor whose character is being killed off a television show.
Kit expresses gratitude for his "time on the show" and is looking forward to the future.
Michael asks Kit what he should do, and Kit assures him that he will figure it out.
Back in reality, Michael thanks Kit for giving him a family.
After Kit's death, Michael continues to be a part of Bob and Marilyn's lives.
Michael prepares to leave New York for Los Angeles.
As he's nervous to start his new journey, he remembers how brave he was to begin his adventure with Kit.

97395599.title: Endgame (2023 film)
synopsis: We find ourselves acquainted with Special Agents Johnson and Martinez, two individuals on opposite ends of life's continuum.

Johnson, a seasoned veteran of the field, carries the weight of countless horrific cases on his weary shoulders, while Martinez, a fresh-faced recruit, possesses an unquenchable thirst for innovation and fresh perspectives.
Both agents receive a cryptic distress call from The Final Stop, a two-century-old pub nestled comfortable in the heart of the peaceful English village of Stoke-On-Tare.
As the agents traverse their journey, their rapport takes shape, oscillating between playful exchanges and heated debates — a reflection of their contrasting world views.
Johnson's hardened cynicism matches the unwavering optimism of Martinez, their personalities entwining in a dynamic dance that becomes a hallmark of their relationship.
The distress call is marred with chilling descriptions of a sequence of murders.
Deeply unsettled yet driven by their duty, Agent Johnson and Martinez chart their course towards Stoke-On-Tare.

They pilot their sleek, government-issued vehicle through the English countryside, guided by the haunting echo of the distress call, pointing them towards the heart of terror housed within The Final Stop.
Arriving at their destination, they confront a scene that stands in stark contradiction to the quaint village — the slaughtered remains of villagers, their faces distorted in final moments of terror.
Their once peaceful lives as pub-goers, farmers, and shopkeepers brutally extinguished, painting a grotesque tableau across the rustic backdrop of The Final Stop.
Inch by inch, they tip-toe across the blood-splattered mahogany boards, tactfully navigating the chilling aftermath of the struggle.
Guided by their commitment to unearth the truth and enforce justice, Johnson and Martinez embark on their investigative journey.
They rummage meticulously through untouched evidence, unfazed by the disconcerting echo of emptiness reverberating within the pub's stone-walled interior.
The tight-lipped villagers, slowly persuaded, begin to weave ancient tales of The Final Stop's sordid past, each account more troubling than the previous.

As the agents' unsolicited journey into the pub's hidden secret inches forward, anomalies — inconsistencies in the time of death, the unnatural contortion of the victims' remains — begin cropping up, pushing them further into a maze of confusion.
The agents stumble upon unnerving discoveries as their search deepens.

The oak bar counter is slashed with vicious scratch marks, raw and fresh, as if made by sinister claws; unusual symbols are scored onto the round tables, their chilling imprints hinting at a foreboding presence beyond human understanding.
Their investigation is punctuated by an alarming rise in villager disappearances, upon which their anxiety takes a sharp upward turn.
Stories of an ancient demonic being, known as the Rabid Reaper, have begun to surface.
This eldritch entity was allegedly bound to The Final Stop, sending waves of terror coursing through the agents' spine.
Deep within the pub's poorly lit basement, ensnared by cobwebs, the agents uncover an ancient tome bound in decaying leather.
The ominous sketches that adorn its pages depict grotesque creatures of hellish origins.
The fading ink scrawls cryptic scriptures ripe with hair-raising accounts of black magic and malevolent deities.
As they delve further into the chilling narrative, they learn of the pub's horrifying role — an arcane gateway to an infernal dimension, a reality they had never anticipated.

The unimaginable revelations ignite a passionate discourse between the partners, as they grapple with the overwhelming evidence of supernatural elements, their debates echoing off the crypt-like emptiness within the pub.
As the plot tightens its noose, ideological clashes surface.
Johnson's entrenched skepticism locks horns with Martinez's acceptance of the paranormal, creating conflict amid the already intricate narrative.
The agents, undeterred, decide to face the monstrous unknown.
To campground overnight within the haunting confines of the pub, every creak of the ancient structure resonates through the tension-laden atmosphere.

Their terrifying rendezvous with the otherworldly intensifies through the night with the apparition of ethereal figures, ghostly whispers in indecipherable tongues, and unguided shifts of antique pewter mugs, sending chills running down their spines.
Their tension escalates, the growing desperation seeping into their determination to combat the supernatural fit.

Painstakingly unravelling the ciphered scriptures scrawled across the pages of the journal, the agents decipher a potential remedy — a ritual aiming at nixing the pub and sealing the interdimensional portal.

Summoning their dwindling courage, Johnson and Martinez concoct an elaborate plan involving a consecrated cross from the village church, fortified circle of coarse salt from the pub's larder, and a series of otherworldly incantations to potentially close the portal.
Apprehension cloaks them as they steel themselves for a final face-off against the Rabid Reaper.
Their battle now stands as the village's only line of defence against the gruesome fate awaiting them.
A steadfast Martinez heads their expedition into the unknown, his spirit burning bright amidst the encroaching darkness.
As they approach the climactic face-off, eldritch apparitions begin to phase in from the shadowy corners of The Final Stop.
Their monstrous forms distort under the dim lantern light, Johnson clenching the old journal tight, using it as their beacon of hope.
The agents, resolute and brave, come toe-to-toe with these nightmarish entities in a gut-wrenching showdown saturated with fear and adrenaline.
Faced with the grim reality of their predicament, Martinez takes the self-sacrificial route.
Resolved to lay down his life, the brave recruit inducts a bitter layer of anguish to their ongoing struggle.
Martinez beseeches Johnson to carry on the ritual as he puts himself in harm's way.
Engrossed in combat, Martinez succumbs to his swift fate, his life extinguishing on the cold, unforgiving stone floor.
Mere feet away, Johnson concludes the foreboding incantation, his trembling voice floating through the ethereal dominion of the night.
As the final words reverberate through the air, The Final Stop shudders violently.
Johnson narrowly slips away from the collapsing foundation, escaping the pub right before it succumbs to the divine might, disintegrating under an explosion of dust and debris.
The portal convulses before finally sealing shut, leaving behind a grim reminder of the events that had unfolded — the rubble of what once was The Final Stop.

The villagers, finally resurfacing from their hideouts, gaze in shocked silence at their battered establishments and their worn-down lifeline, their unsolicited saviour standing resilient amidst the ruin.
Johnson, having been hardened and scarred by the ordeal, offers a nod of acknowledgement before retreating towards their inconspicuous vehicle.
The agent drives away from Stoke-On-Tare, the once idyllic countryside transforming into a chilling souvenir of the nightmare-infested reality he had managed to escape.
As dawn breaks, casting a new light on the landscape, Johnson glances into the rearview mirror.
His gaze settles on the remains of The Final Stop bathing under the light of the new day.
Johnson, now a solitary traveller, remains haunted by the legacy of the fatal encounter.
The scar of their supernatural experience taints his soul, as he embarks on a journey shrouded in uncertainty.
The villagers, resilient and hopeful, gather around the ruins of their homeland, their sombre countenances reflecting the daunting task of rebuilding their once tranquil village life.
Johnson directs his attention towards the open road ahead, leaving behind the ominous remnants of the village.
A scratchy police radio buzzed in the background, reporting ordinary thefts and minor altercations.
Yet, a lingering undercurrent of dread persists, forever tying the fate of Stoke-On-Tare to the memory of the horrific events of that fateful night.
The awe-inspiringly heroic confrontation with the entity of terror by Martinez and Johnson begins to weave itself into the rewritten lore of Stoke-On-Tare.
The fading daylight falls upon the remnants of The Final Stop, casting an eerily beautiful crimson hue onto the demolished facade.
Against the backdrop of the setting sun, an ambiguous silhouette emerges, stretching long atop the debris, suggesting at the possible persistence of a malevolent presence.
As silence takes over the final frame, the audience is left nursing mixed emotions, anticipation of a potential sequel to Johnson's saga simmering under the surface.

73254219.title: Craving (2023 film)
synopsis: Police officers Shaw and Washington enter a rural bar, The Last Exit, following what appears to be a bloody massacre.
They find one female survivor, Shiloh, too scared to speak to them.
Flashing back to the night before, The Last Exit is having a typical evening.
Les, the owner and bartender, contends with Rudy, a conspiracy theorist who lusts over Shiloh, the other bartender.
Travis, a cowboy and swindler, challenges Rudy to a game of pool but is distracted by local DJ Rylee, who rebuffs his advances.
A suspicious man in the corner named Jared watches over the bar before Cece enters.
Cece asks to borrow Travis' car, which he is opposed to as Cece is with another man, Frank.
Travis relents and Cece does drugs in the bathroom, unaware that John is in one of the stalls.
The patrons are startled by the sound of gunshots outside.
Les takes a baseball bat to scare of what she assumes are kids with firecrackers, but is shot in the head by the crossfire.
Five violent heroin addicts force their way into the bar: Gail, Mac, Will, Lo, and Frenzy.
After they assume control of the bar it becomes apparent that a second group outside is after them.
This group wears flesh masks and violently murders Frank after pulling him out of his car.
The lieutenant of the group, Red, uses a megaphone to coerce the people inside to give up one of their own, who they deem is a monster, before his group begins barricading the bar.
Inside, Shiloh weeps over Les' body, and Gail forces her and the patrons to stand together by the pool table while Mac checks the bar for other entrances.
John successfully hides under the bathroom sink.
At the bar, Gail watches the group outside over the CCTV, recognizing their leader as Hunter, who removes his mask and taunts the group inside.
Will is suffering from withdrawals, worse than any of the others, and he rests behind the bar.
The addicts struggle to maintain control over the patrons, leading to Frenzy assaulting Travis and Rudy.
Cece plots to turn the addicts against each other, but Frenzy catches on and beats her up in the bathroom.

Through flashbacks it's revealed that a man named Carl rescued Gail from a drug den, and she became the adoptive mother to his adoptive son, Will, who suffered a condition that only heroin would remedy.
Mac serves as Carl's number two, and only very recently did the group meet Frenzy and Lo, who are a couple.
Lo calms Frenzy's hot demeanor, though Lo herself is deeply disturbed and admits to having murdered animals in her youth.
It's revealed that Carl was dating Hunter's ex-wife, and that Hunter is Will's real father.
A monster murdered Hunter's ex-wife, leading him down a rabbit hole chasing clue after clue, trying to find this creature.

Eventually Hunter discovered what Carl was up to, and after making arrangements with Red's people and secretly colluding with Frenzy to trap Carl's group at The Last Exit, Hunter shot and killed Carl immediately preceding the events of the story.
Inside the bar, tensions between the group escalate.
Cece accidentally gets Frenzy to reveal her betrayal to Gail, giving Cece the opportunity to steal Gail's revolver.
As Cece attempts to take control of the situation, Lo sneaks up behind her and beats her to death with a pool cue.
Exposed, Frenzy and Lo attempt to kill Mac, but Frenzy accidentally shoots Lo.
Will is shot in the crossfire, and Gail comforts him until his passes away.
Suddenly, Will's body begins to twist and contort, terrifying the patrons of the bar.
It is clear that Will is the monster, leading Frenzy and Rylee to attempt to escape.
Will fully transforms into a large, slimy creature covered in bodily spikes and sharp teeth protruding from his face.
Will immediately rips apart Frenzy before turning on the patrons, killing Jared, Travis, and Rylee.
Shiloh tries to hide under a pool table, and Rudy sacrifices himself to save her.
Gail attempts to calm Will, hoping underneath the monster that he's still there.
Her words fail, and Mac attempts to kill Will before being torn apart himself.
The last one standing, Gail succumbs to her death at Will's monstrous hands.
Will finds John hiding in the bathroom and tears him apart before returning to the pool table where Shiloh is hiding.
He scratches her arm in an attempt to reach her, but after consuming so much he's become weakened, and Shiloh impales him with the broken pool cue.
Will transforms back to normal, apologizing to Shiloh.
Before he dies he tells her he became the monster after he was scratched by one.
Outside Red sends in Lori and Gerry to investigate the bar.
Shiloh stabs Gerry but Lori shoots her.
As Lori looms over Shiloh, her eyes transform and she kills Lori.
Outside, Hunter and Red are shocked as they see Shiloh, now in monster form, break through the barricades and murder Red and the rest of his group.

42157022.title: Unforeseen Encounters
synopsis: In the heart of Chicago, nestled amidst the seclusion of towering Gothic buildings, we are introduced to Lady D. Known far and wide in the literary world for her blend of razor-sharp wit and poignant storytelling, she is a luminous figure in the realm of crime novels.

Lady D, beneath her seemingly perfect life dotted by lavish possessions and numerous literary accolades, grapples with an insidious ennui, a continual existential angst that seeps into the cracks of her solitary existence.
Hundreds of miles away, in his gilded office atop a glass-clad skyscraper towering over Los Angeles, stern CEO Sir D can be found hunched over intricate city models.
Despite his prestigious status as the owner of a multinational automobile empire, a gnawing dissatisfaction plagues his heart.

One fateful summer afternoon, the lives of Lady D and Sir D are intertwined when an elaborately engraved invitation to the grand opening of a world-renowned art gallery in Paris arrives at each of their doorsteps.
Bowing to destiny, they individually navigate their way to Chicago O'Hare International Airport's private airstrip, arriving simultaneously, yet ignorant of the other's presence.

It's only when they find themselves stood in the same line at the airport lounge coffee shop that they lock eyes, recognizing each other through veils of surprise, punctuated by the sparks of curiosity.
Engaging in conversation, they explore the ruins of their failed joint venture - a publishing house they established years ago, that never reached the potential they envisioned.
As they sink deeper into the excavation of regret, their attention is pierced by the departure board showcasing a severe delay in their Air France flight due to a ferocious European blizzard.
Anticipating ruined meetings and derailed plans, both scramble to secure their phones to their ears, hurriedly calling their Parisian contacts to reschedule their commitments.

Their already gloomy expressions darken at the realization of their shared predicament, shedding sparks of contention over inconsequential objects — a crowded power outlet, a misplaced remote for the lounge television.
What begins as mild irritation soon escalates into a comic spat, their censorious exchanges providing unexpected amusement for their fellow stranded passengers.
The routine airport delay devolves into an impromptu theatrical performance that sees Lady D and Sir D engaging in a wittily escalating quarrel.
The comic tension mounts to a fever pitch when an erroneous boarding call sends both racing toward the wrong terminal gate, naively mistaking a local flight for their delayed international service.
Ironically, their premature sprint to secure their seats culminates in a farcical misstep that sees them miss the rescheduled Paris flight altogether.

Their plight reaches its zenith when they learn that their hotel reservations at the Marriott in Paris have been revoked owing to the delays, the surreal notion of spending the night at the airport looming before them.
Endeavoring to replicate a modicum of comfort, they resort to crafting makeshift hammocks using a disused trunk and discarded inflatable neck pillows.
As they covertly partake of their ill-gotten meal, the atmosphere softens.
Earlier rivalries give way to shared recollections, leading to a tapestry of intertwined reminiscences.
Under the cloak of their shared circumstances, they find comfort in their shared disillusionment, their luxurious lifestyles failing to eclipse the loneliness that dwells within them.
Their conversation ebbs and flows, progressing from trivial to profound, punctuated by shared laughter.
A palpable chemistry ignites between them, their knowing glances a shared glimmer of newfound affinity.
Through their shared isolation, they manage to rekindle a long-lost camaraderie, previously dismissed as a relic of their shared past.
The morning light unfolds a revelation – the art gallery they were both set to attend was indeed the same.
Their separate worlds converge once more.
Laughing heartily over their shared misadventures and multiple miscalculations, they relish the morning's levity.
Their overnight adventure reignites a dormant friendship, fostering a deeper understanding of their intertwined history.
Finally boarding their delayed Paris-bound flight, they sink into tranquil silence - an ode to their rejuvenated camaraderie, replacing their previous turbulence.
A serene peace enfolds them, affirming the serendipity of their unforeseen airport reunion.
As the sunrise pours through the window of their Airbus in hues of lilac and gold, it heralds the dawn of a new beginning.

74750095.title: What Happens Later
synopsis: At an unnamed regional airport on Leap Day, ex-lovers Wilhelmina "Willa" Davis and William "Bill" Davis run into each other and make small talk during their layovers.
Willa and Bill are about to get on their respective flights; Willa is on her way to Boston and Bill is on his way to Austin.
However, a storm, later identified as a bomb cyclone, causes flights at the airport to be delayed, leaving Willa and Bill to reconnect.
Bill is married to his wife Beth-Anne and together they have a 15-year-old daughter, Rose, but Bill says that he and Beth-Anne are “going through a thing”.
Rose also wishes to be a dancer, which worries Bill.
Meanwhile, Willa plans to visit her friend Ginny, who is splitting up with her husband.
While Willa and Bill reminisce about their past relationship, it is revealed that Willa suffered a miscarriage while she was with Bill.
After Bill left, Willa had a little girl with a man who left as soon as he found out she was pregnant.
Willa later gave her daughter up for adoption, she was able to find the perfect parents, but Willa does not know where her daughter is now.
Bill mentions that he saw Willa a year prior while she was changing planes in Dallas, but Bill did not say anything to her, stating that she looked lost.
Bill obtains a hotel voucher, but is unable to reserve a room.
It is announced that Willa's flight to Boston is now boarding, but she ends up giving up her seat for a family.
Willa tries to give Bill her ticket after upgrading to first class, so he will not miss Rose's recital, as both Bill and Willa are “W.
Davis”.
Bill refuses.
Willa mentions that Beth-Anne called earlier while Bill was grabbing coffee to say that Rose does not want to stay with him, but with Beth-Anne instead for a few weeks.
Bill then takes the ticket, only for all flights to suddenly be suspended.
Rose calls Bill and Bill encourages her to try her best at dancing; earlier, Bill told Willa about how he had told Rose that she would not make it as a professional dancer, making her sad.
Willa tells Bill that she is actually going to Boston to meet her daughter.
Maggie, who just turned 20, called Willa and told her that she would like to meet.
Earlier, Willa, using Bill's phone, texted Maggie saying that she was not going to come.
Maggie then replied, telling Willa to just try, initially, this was seen as Willa texting Ginny.
The next day, all outbound flights are then announced to be departing shortly.
Willa gifts Bill with her rainstick and Bill gives Willa an old card, saying that he will write his number on the back.
They then exchange a kiss, before leaving to board their flights.
Willa turns Bill's card over, only to see that he only wrote "just try".
Willa and Bill exchange final gestures through the windows of their planes, which are parked next to each other.
Bill tries to sign his phone number to Willa, only for their flights to finally depart, as the contrails from the planes form a heart.

91677470.title: Engulfed: The Girl and The Wave
synopsis: Two childhood companions and seasoned vaudeville comedians, Lilly and Maria, find themselves transported into an ethereal place beyond the realm of life.
Awakening amidst radiant clouds and luminescent rainbows, they realize they now exist in an invigorating version of the afterlife that resembles a high-definition, kaleidoscope version of Earth.
They explore the celestial surroundings, moving through landscapes filled with reveling spirits, peculiar structures like inverted towers and bridges made entirely of jigsaw puzzles.
They stumble upon an elegant, stoic figure bathed in radiant, multiple hues.
This endearing figure identifies himself as Humorious, the cosmic custodian of humor, tasked with a noble mission of spreading laughter across the universe.
Lilly and Maria are chosen to aid in this divine task, specifically to brighten the monotonous existence in Hopesink, a joyless industrial town.
Humorious hands over a sacred tome titled “The Guide for Guffaws", an ancient collection of celestial humor techniques designed to infuse deep-seated earthly sorrows with heartfelt merriment.

Along with the tome, they receive luminous auroras shaped like wings, radiant golden halos, and magical abilities to induce laughter, transforming them from ordinary beings into divine beings: goddesses of laughter.
A sudden flash of light transports them back to Earth, amidst the grimy, efficient factories and gloomy citizens of Hopesink.
They recall fragments of their once lively existence, evoking memories of their untimely deaths, their widely renowned comedy club, and the ceaseless laughter they once spread.
The oppressive sobriety in Hopesink, they realize, was exacerbated by the stern, draconian governance of Mayor Stern, a man seemingly immune to happiness.
Deciding that Mayor Stern will be their primary mission, they believe that making him accustomed to laughter will inevitably bring forth a transformation in Hopesink.
They meet Mrs. Dough, a kindhearted baker, and Mr. Diggs, a morose gravedigger, who despite the bleak surroundings have managed to find their personal slice of happiness.
Lilly and Maria devise their plan to inject the pervasive gloom of Hopesink with laughter.
They begin with vaudevillian performances at local pubs, humorous public speeches, and strategic puns interspersed in daily conversations.
Despite their successful attempts, Mayor Stern continues his stoic existence, unfazed by the newfound laughter.
Each of their comedic strategies seemed to crash against Mayor Stern's robust barrier of seriousness.
Just as they were about to knock down Stern's austere demeanor, they're abruptly pulled back into the playful afterlife realm.
Desperate to continue their mission, they wage an emotional appeal to Humorious, advocating the budding transformation of Hopesink and begging for another chance.
Humorious considers their request and grants them a final, fleeting opportunity to paint Hopesink with enduring joy.
Returning to Earth with intense determination, Lilly and Maria embrace their divine powers and effectively weave comedy into every corner of the town.
The result is transformative: every corner, shop, school and house in Hopesink echoes with unrepressed laughter, signifying a profound change in the town’s gloomy semblance.
Undeterred by previous failures, they strive towards their ultimate goal - making the impenetrable Mr. Stern succumb to laughter.
A massive comedic production is staged, a silent comedy play infused with social satire, distinctive tributes to Hopesink's culture, and a comedic representation of its melancholic history.
The grand performance elicits uproarious laughter, not only from the townsfolk but also from the stern mayor himself, as Hopesink transforms into a town teeming with joy and laughter.
Suddenly plucked from the Earth by their divine alarm, Lilly and Maria's celestial eyelashes flutter in the wind as they look back at Hopesink.
Lilly and Maria part with Hopesink, not with sorrow, but with a deep sense of fulfillment.
In their absence, Hopesink continues to thrive, becoming a laughter-filled town.
The comedy routines of Lilly and Maria are immortalized, and their memories are cherished dearly.
Every town square they once performed in becomes hallowed ground where the citizens reminisce about the divine laughter tandem that once graced their streets.
In time, Hopesink becomes a testament to the magic of laughter, flourishing under the joyous legacy left behind by two celestial comediennes.

70169157.title: Darby and the Dead
synopsis: When Darby Harper was seven, she and her mother were swept by a wave that drowned them.
Darby was brought back to life, but her mother perished.
Since then, Darby gained the ability to see and communicate with ghosts.
She started a side business to help "Deados" move on to the afterlife by helping them take care of things they could not do while alive.
This has caused her to become distant from everyone at school, including her former friend Capricorn "Capri" Donahue, the popular cheerleader.
Darby's only true friend is the school's former janitor Gary, a "Stayer" who is waiting for his wife Linda to pass on so that he can move on too.
Darby meets new student Alex who is the school's mascot and is drawn to her, despite her attempts to dissuade him.
She also comes into conflict with Capri over her boyfriend James who, contrary to her, is kind and considerate.
While using a hair straightener in the bathroom, Capri electrifies herself and dies.
Darby is immediately visited by her and comes to grips with the fact that she is dead and needs to pass on.
She also discovers that she can psychically control things with her mind.
Capri constantly pesters Darby before deciding that her goal before moving on is to throw her seventeenth birthday party.
Darby reluctantly agrees with Capri training her to think and act like her and her friends.
After regaining her cheerleading abilities from her childhood, Darby manages to get in with Capri's friends, though she is told to stay away from Alex due to him being the mascot.
With Capri's help, Darby posits celebrating her birthday anyway to her friends and to raise "electrocution awareness" at school.
Capri's friends agree and, thanks to Capri's influence, Darby starts to become popular among her peers.
She further begins to bond with James who has stayed home from school for a few days following Capri's death.
After returning, everyone at school begins to suspect that the two are dating, much to Capri's friend's chagrin.
Darby's new life begins to intrude on her old one as she misses a date with Alex and keeps passing on helping Gary's friend Mel pass on.
Capri initially becomes jealous of Darby's influence over the party, but is calmed by Gary and Mel.
She goes to apologize, only to discover Darby's supposed relationship with James and angrily burns her house and begins to haunt James, forcing him to "break up" with Darby.
The day of the party arrives and Darby comes in an effort to find Capri.
She finds James talking to her via a Ouija board and Capri begins to mock Darby and send the board flying around the party.
When she threatens further humiliation, Darby finally reveals to everyone her secret and the fact that she pretends to look down on everyone because of her own flaws.

Darby returns to being ignored by everyone at school, but is visited by Capri who in an effort to make up for fighting with her, finds Darby's mother who has been watching her from afar in an effort to see how she can handle herself.
Capri finally accepts Darby's friendship and moves on.
Darby decides to continue cheerleading, having made up with the squad and remains friends with James.
She runs into Gary again who is close to visiting his wife and he reveals that Mel has finally moved on as well, thanks to Alex.
It is revealed he can also see ghosts as well as break the fourth wall as Darby had done throughout the film, after having fallen into a coma.
The two decide to start dating and work their afterlife business together while a bird, implied to be Capri based on her belief in reincarnation, watches from afar.

58863366.title: Fortune Squandered: A Southwestern Tale
synopsis: Reece, a 35-year-old vagabond, was infamous in the small town of Marlboro, New Hampshire.
Known for wreaking havoc and minor troubles, he was a constant occupant of a whisky-stained stool at O'Malley's Pub where the locals gathered.
Despite testing the patience of the gruff barman, Liam, Reece's good-natured banter and charismatic charm had a way of smoothing things over, securing him another drink on his account.
At the end of yet another long night, Reece ambled out of the pub, having paid his substantial bill with his most recent winning scratch-off ticket.
He then made his way to Marlboro's only 24-hour convenience store, Lloyd's Groceries.
With trembling hands and a foggy breath, he mustered enough clarity to hand over his latest New Hampshire lottery ticket to the elderly clerk, Jesse.
His eyes, although bleary, eagerly awaited the ticket validation.
Suddenly, the narrow, cramped store buzzed with an electrifying revelation - Reece's ticket was a winning one worth a staggering $200,000!
The news spread through the town like a wild forest fire, causing Marlboro's residents to gape at their infamous troublemaker in shock.
Tales of Reece’s unanticipated fortune and his claimed commitment to reform replaced his previous antics as the talk of the town.
With teary eyes and a faltering voice, Reece pledged to the people of Marlboro that he would abandon his life of alcohol and mischief, hoping to transform himself into a responsible citizen.
The locals met this pledge with doubtful smiles and hopeful gazes.
True to his impulsive nature, Reece wasted no time in extravagant spending.
He purchased an opulent mansion on Birch Street furnished with exquisite furniture and crystalline chandeliers.
His cabinets, unfortunately, were also stocked with high-end bourbon and a stash of illicit narcotics.
The calm rustic serenity of Marlboro came under threat as Reece spiraled into an unrestrained whirlwind of daily hedonistic parties.
His reckless partying and squandering of his newfound wealth were observed with growing trepidation and disappointment by the locals who had started to warm up to him.
Unfazed by the growing disapproval, Reece retorted that his current mode of living was merely a grander extension of his old habits.
Amongst all the turmoil, Jenny Davis, Reece's enduring friend, witnessed his rapid descent with tearful helplessness, unable to intervene effectively.
Unable to stand by and watch anymore, Jenny defiantly confronted Reece about his reckless spending and destructive lifestyle.
However, Reece, living in a constant state of intoxication, simply brushed-off and rebutted Jenny's earnest pleas and serious concerns.
Feeling defeated yet absolutely determined, Jenny reached out to Marlboro Rehab Center, exposing Reece's escalating issues with substance addiction.
Chronically wary of Reece's cunning manipulative conduct and history of refusal to cooperate, the rehab center staff greeted Jenny's plea skeptically.
Reece, on hearing Jenny's intervention attempts, reacted defensively, choosing his addictions over their deep-seated friendship.
Time blurred as Reece indulged further into his addictions.
His life unwinding faster than he could grasp.
His nights painted with raucous laughter, liquor, and a cocktail of drugs.
One harrowing morning, Reece woke up in his empty mansion, clothed in a stench of alcohol and drugs.
Empty liquor bottles and leftover paraphernalia eerily reflected his dwindling fortune.
As Reece returned from fetching his morning newspaper, he encountered hostile glares and sly whispers from his neighbors indicating his impending downfall.
The profound loss of his friend Jenny hit him full force with an unfathomable wave of regret and self-loathing.
Sitting amidst the wreckage of his once proud mansion, Reece took a good look at his devastated property, serving as a hideous mirror to his life.
Shaken by the sheer magnitude of his fall, Reece, with throbbing temples and shaking hands, started cleaning his mansion.
The prospect of layoffs, the loss of Jenny, and the startled realization of his downfall provoked Reece to swallow his pride and approach Marlboro Rehab Center humbly for help.
Marlboro's locals, habitually skeptical of Reece, surprised themselves by cautiously applauding his honesty and apparent commitment to change.
Overcoming grim memories and apathy, Reece took his first step towards rebuilding his shattered relationships.
He reached out to Jenny, leaving her a heartfelt apology note at her doorstep.
Reece's sincere attempts to change began to soften the affront of the townsfolk.
They started extending their hesitant support to his transformation.
Amidst this small town's riveting drama, Jenny discovered Reece's letter one subdued night.
Her tear-filled sapphire eyes read the note and she allowed a glimmer of hope to spark.
Jenny made a cautious return to Reece's life by regularly visiting him at the Rehab Center.
Her support served as a foundation in his rehabilitation and helped in detangling his identity from his addictions.
After grueling, tear-filled months, Reece's commitment yielded results.
He emerged from his dark journey healthy, humbled, and truly reformed.
Reece expressed his immense gratitude to the town by arranging a meeting at the Marlboro Community Center, where he recounted his tale and testified his resolution to help others avoid his mistakes.
The community center echoed with feelings of relief, unity, and a rekindled faith in redemption as Reece narrated his journey.
Reece's final pledge to dedicate the rest of his life to prevent others from falling into the same trap staged his wonderful transformation publicly.
His solemn oath signaled the end of his debauched life and the commencement of his journey towards community service and promoting sobriety.
Reece, once notorious for all the wrong reasons, emerged as an impressively redeemed figure within Marlboro - a name forever synonymous with resilience and recovery.
Reece, once loathed for his reckless lifestyle, slowly but surely gained the admiration of the locals for his sheer willpower and determination.
Reece accomplished more than just personal reform.
He mended broken relationships and gave the town of Marlboro not just a tale but a living testament to human resilience.
Reece's life, originally filled with reckless abandonment and damaging addictions, strewed with regrets, turned into a story of inspiration and transformation.

The locals of Marlboro, accustomed to seeing Reece as the personification of mischief, now regularly witness him assisting in community restoration projects, working tirelessly under the blistering midday sun.
Reece, turned his weed-strewn path towards destruction into a beautifully paved road to redemption, which inspired the entire town of Marlboro.
Reece and Jenny, now stronger together than ever, leveraged their experiences to act as pillars of support to others in need, paradoxically becoming the backbone of their once estranged community.
Their friendship, tested and refined through numerous tribulations, stood stronger than ever, mirroring their individual growth and collective power.
Today, if you amble through Marlboro, you will find Reece, the once miscreant, working with the youth of the town, sharing his experiences, and helping shape a better community.
The tale of Reece's transformation, from the town's menace to its cherished emblem of resilience, is a testament of change that will forever resonate within the secure confines of Marlboro.

70317816.title: To Leslie
synopsis: Leslie is a troubled and manipulative alcoholic from West Texas who won $190,000 in a local lottery, only to squander the winnings on liquor and drugs.
Six years later, Leslie is destitute, living a peripatetic life in motels and on the streets.
After being kicked out of a residential motel, she reunites with her estranged 19-year-old son James, who allows her to live with him under the provision that she not drink.
Leslie soon steals money from James's roommate Darren, and James discovers liquor bottles under her bed, leading him to call his grandmother and Leslie's friend Nancy for help.
Nancy and her boyfriend Dutch reluctantly allow Leslie to stay with them, but lock her out in the middle of the night when she visits the local bar and is spotted by Pete, one of their friends.
Leslie sleeps outside next to a motel, where she is found at dawn by Sweeney, one of the proprietors.
He orders her to leave, and she flees, leaving her suitcase behind.
She is met outside a convenience store that night by Pete, who buys her food, but Leslie again flees when he attempts to make sexual advances toward her.

Leslie returns to the motel in search of her suitcase, and Sweeney pretends to confuse her for somebody who had called for a job, and offers her the opportunity of cleaning rooms in exchange for a small wage and boarding.
Royal, who owns and helps run the motel with Sweeney, is cold toward Leslie, whom he has known since childhood.
Leslie is frequently unpunctual to her duties, and she continues to spend her earnings on alcohol, often going to bars.
Late one night, Leslie drunkenly wanders to the home where she raised James, startling the family who now lives there.
The homeowners phone Sweeney, who returns Leslie to the roadhouse.
Disappointed by Leslie's lack of commitment, Sweeney intends to fire her, but he relents when she assures him she intends to change her ways.
With nowhere left to turn, Leslie attempts to focus on her job and maintain sobriety as she suffers through alcohol withdrawal.
Leslie and Sweeney develop a friendship, bonding over their mutual history of addiction.
Leslie accompanies Sweeney to a fair, where she meets his daughter and granddaughter.
Leslie gets into a confrontation with Nancy at the fair, who lambasts her in front of Sweeney for having abandoned James when he was a child.
Later that day, she argues with Sweeney after he insists on watching a VHS tape containing the TV news piece on her lottery win.
On the tape, the teenage James mentions that Leslie has always wanted to open a diner and the younger Leslie, clearly drunk, scoffs.
She quits her job at the motel.
She phones James from a laundromat, leaving a message telling him she loves him.
She then visits her usual bar, where she is hit on by a handsome but roguish younger man.
She orders a beer and a shot, but decides not to drink either.
Meanwhile, Sweeney searches for Leslie and arrives at the bar, but she has left.
He punches and tussles with Pete after he and Nancy insult Leslie.
Leslie squats in an abandoned ice cream shop across the street from the motel and watches as Sweeney returns.
In the morning, she awakens Sweeney and tells him she wants to renovate the ice cream shop and open a diner.
He reluctantly agrees to help and they kiss for the first time.
Ten months later, Leslie is sober, and with Sweeney and Royal's help, she has fixed up the building and turned it into a diner.
On opening day, Leslie receives no customers.
Nancy arrives that evening at closing time, and Leslie accuses her of sabotaging the business's opening by telling the locals not to go.

Instead of responding with rage, Nancy apologizes to Leslie for not being emotionally present throughout Leslie's life, while also stating that she won't ever forgive Leslie for abandoning her son due to her addiction.
Nancy also surprises Leslie by revealing she has brought James with her.
Royal and Sweeney prepare a meal for them, and the two embrace.

35380670.title: The Appeal of the Untamed (2020 film)
synopsis: Our tale unfolds against the gorgeous canvas of San Francisco in the late 1800s, where Victorian houses speckle the rolling landscape.
At its heart, we find our lead character, Patrick Kearney.
A physician by profession, Patrick commands respect and admiration amongst his contemporaries.
Also forming an integral part of the Kearney homestead is Buster, a dog whose lineage forms an intriguing blend of the noble wolf and the friendly golden retriever.
Every day, we watch as Patrick goes about his duties, with Buster his unwavering companion.
However, their peaceful cohabitation is suddenly disrupted one afternoon by the arrival of a postman carrying a letter from Carson City, a rustic town located in Nevada.
The letter contains alarming details of the dire circumstances his long-lost brother now finds himself in.
Panic and worry ensue, and Patrick finds himself torn between his estranged past relationship with his brother and the undeniable bond that familial ties impose.
After much inner turmoil, Patrick decides to undertake a rescue mission to save his brother, Joe.
He spends a few days gathering essential necessities for his arduous journey.
Buster, his faithful companion, remains at Patrick's side throughout.
Leaving the familiar coasts of San Francisco behind, they embark on their journey into the unpredictable wilderness.
They navigate the hostile wilderness, fraught with extreme weather fluctuations, height changes, and the constant threat of highwaymen.
Their journey evolves into more than merely a mission to save someone.
It becomes a test of their bond, their ability to endure hardships.
As they near the Sierra peak, signs of Patrick's brother surface, amplifying his anticipation.
However, they discover the chilling reality of Patrick's brother being held captive by bandits over an assertion regarding an alleged treasure.
Patrick and Buster engage in a perilous path filled with danger, but it also provides them with an opportunity to hatch a plan to rescue Joe.
What follows is a gripping face-off, where Patrick, aided by a fierce dog, take on a gang of outlaws.
The battle ends with Patrick and Buster emerging victorious amidst the defeated outlaws.
Following the battle, they discover a hidden trove brimming with gold nuggets, the source of contention among the bandits.
Upon setting his brother free, the brothers share a heartfelt reunion.
Patrick chooses to leave behind the gold, and they embark on their journey back home to San Francisco.
Settling back into city life, the wilderness holds a newfound allure for Patrick.
As he sits by his hearth with Buster snoozing at his feet, he realizes that his experiences and relationships built during the journey are worth far more than tangible riches.
Days later, Patrick sits overlooking his beloved city of San Francisco.
Irrespective of his monetary wealth, he feels a richness in his life that gold cannot equal.
His real wealth lies in people he cherishes in his life, the experiences gained, and the wisdom acquired from each challenge.
As night falls, the curtain descends on our tale of a man, his loyal dog, and an unforgettable journey that forever redefined their perspective on life.

57963342.title: The Call of the Wild (2020 film)
synopsis: During the late 19th century, Buck, a large, gentle mix of Saint Bernard and Scotch Shepherd, lives contentedly with his master, Judge Miller, in Santa Clara, California.
One night, Buck is abducted and shipped to the Yukon aboard a freighter.
During the voyage, a crew member beats him with a club to enforce discipline.

Once in Alaska, a man named John Thornton drops his harmonica which Buck retrieves for him, moments before being sold to Perrault and his partner Francoise for their dog sled to deliver mail across the Yukon.
Perrault hopes that with Buck, he can make the long trek to the mail depot before the deadline.
Buck is introduced to the other dogs; Dolly, Pike, Jo, Billie, Dub, Dave, and Sol-leks, including the pack leader, a husky named Spitz.
Buck gains the loyalty and trust of Perrault, Francoise and the other sled dogs, after proving himself along the way.
He rescues Francoise when she falls through the ice.
All of this antagonizes Spitz.
Buck begins experiencing ancestral visions of a black wolf that acts as his guide throughout their travels.
One night, Buck catches and then releases a rabbit.
Spitz kills it before attacking Buck to assert his dominance.
Spitz seems to win, until the rest of the pack encourages Buck, who pins Spitz down, displacing him as pack leader; Spitz then disappears into the wild.
Perrault grudgingly makes Buck the lead when no other dog can do it.
Buck's speed and strength allow the sled to arrive with the mail on time.
There, Thornton hands over a letter he has written to his former wife expressing his feelings about their dead son.
He and Buck readily recognize each other.
Soon after, Perrault learns the mail route is being replaced by the telegraph, forcing him to sell the dogs.
Hal, a mean-spirited and inexperienced gold prospector, buys the pack and works them to exhaustion carrying a heavy load, along with three people, in weather unsuitable for sledding.
The exhausted dogs collapse before Hal can force them to cross an unstable frozen lake.
When Buck is unable to move, Hal threatens to shoot him.
Thornton appears and rescues Buck while Hal forces the other sled dogs to cross the lake.
Under Thornton's care, Buck recovers.
Later, at a saloon, Thornton is attacked by Hal, who reveals he is the only human survivor and the dogs managed to run off, leaving him with nothing.
Witnessing the scene, Buck attacks Hal, who is subsequently thrown out.
Buck and Thornton then travel beyond the Yukon map where they can freely live in the wild.
They come across an abandoned cabin in an open valley and settle in.
Meanwhile, Hal relentlessly hunts them, from revenge and believing Thornton is hiding a source of gold.
In the open wilderness, Thornton and Buck bond over their daily activities, primarily fishing and gold panning.
Throughout their time together, Buck is drawn to a female white wolf.
Saving another wolf, Buck goes between his domesticated life with Thornton and his place with the wolf pack that the female belongs to.
After some time together, Thornton believes it is time to return home.
Never wanting the gold from the start, Thornton throws it back into the river except for some "grocery money," and tells Buck he is leaving in the morning, and to come and say good-bye.
Buck heads into the forest and sleeps beside the white wolf.
That night, Hal finds and shoots Thornton, demanding to know where all the gold is.
Thornton throws the "grocery money" at him, but it does not placate Hal.
Buck returns and kills Hal by pushing him into the cabin, which is aflame and collapses.
