Bri's song creates issues with the parents of the kids at her school as well as with the gang King's Crown.
Arriving home, Aunt Pooh gets angry with Bri because of the lyrics as well.
Jay and Bri have a heart to heart about the pass.
They agree to start fresh and try to move on.
They then head to her school where the superintendent is speaking on what the concerns the other parents have about her lyrics and how fast the song is getting around the community.
Jay holds him accountable on never calling her back regarding Bri's suspension and how she was assaulted by the security officers at her school.
Malik reconciles with Bri; then decides to walk home where they are approached by two of the Kings Crown that assault Malik and steals Lawless' chain from Bri because of what she said in the song.
Aunt Pooh drives up to Bri and Malik demanding that they tell her what's wrong.
She then goes to retaliates and ends up in the hospital.
At the hospital, a doctor states that once Pooh wakes up from her coma she will be taken into custody by the police.
Aunt Pooh wakes up and tells Bri that she has always known she was set for greatness.
That she needs to go battle Infamous Millz Supreme's artist at the ring.
After Infamous talks about Bri's mom and their situation.
Bri battles Infamous based on all the pain and growth she has experience and ends up winning the battle.

1575437.title: The Other Genius
synopsis: Emily, a young wunderkind majoring in computer science at Trinity University in New York, astounds her cybersecurity class by deciphering an RSA encryption algorithm.
Amongst the festivities of the annual autumn fest, Emily initiates a heated discussion on the importance of academic rapport in relationships.
Beneath her jubilant exterior, she conceals a discernible strain of melancholy.
During an exploration of D.H. Lawrence's novels, Emily meets Jon, a charismatic literature major.
The university announces an interdisciplinary project competition and Emily and Jon's names are drawn together.
This unforeseen pairing catalyzes a series of intellectual exchanges.
The stark juxtaposition of their worlds ignites a brainstorming journey, filled with productive disagreements and enlightening discourses.
Emily and Jon are initially reluctant, but their skepticism gradually morphs into mutual appreciation.
Surprisingly cooperative, Emily and Jon clinch first place in the academic project contest.
Amidst the celebrations, they interpret their shared triumph as a sign of attraction, setting off a delightful series of misjudged signals and misunderstandings.
Their friends organize an evening at a local Italian restaurant where Emily and Jon untangle their feelings for each other.
At the grand post-competition celebration, Emily contests her initial theory of intellectual compatibility as the sole foundation of love.
She admits that the celebration of diversity, mutual respect, and understanding shape enduring relationships.
Emily and Jon present their project, an advance waste recycling system interpreted through Emily Dickinson's verses, to a panel of renowned professors, receiving university-wide recognition.
Love transcends every intellectual boundary, intertwining itself unforgettably into Emily and Jon's adventure at Trinity University.

70104429.title: The Other Zoey
synopsis: Zoey Miller, a highly intelligent computer major junior, at Queens University of Charlotte does not believe in the traditional concept of romantic love, but rather that having similar ways of thinking is the key.
On Valentine's Day she speaks up against fellow student Becca's presentation on Saint Valentine in a history class, saying that the holiday is a capitalist creation.
She has designed an app that will effectively match people based on algorithms.
As Zoey is crossing campus with her roommate and friend Elle, the school's soccer star Zach MacLaren accidentally launches a ball into her head.
He rushes over, apologizing and offers to take her to get her head looked at.
Elle sees it as a kind of meet-cute, but Zoey shrugs it off.
In a subsequent class, a dark-haired guy has an almost identical view as Zoey when another professor brought up love, but disappears before she can tell him so.
Binge watching rom-coms with Elle in honor of the day, Zoey's mom Paula calls, and she reiterates her dislike of the genre, in disagreement with the others.
She considers them to be formulaic and contrived.
Zach comes into the campus bookstore where Zoey works, and they banter in a mutually insulting way.
Forgetting his credit card after ordering a book, she runs after him as he speeds off on his bike, and he crashes into a backing car.
Zoey is the first person Zach sees when he comes to, and as he hears her name, he mistakes her for his girlfriend, who is coincidentally named Zoey too.
Asked by the EMT to accompany Zach to the hospital as Zoey's presence calms him, she bumps into his parents at the hospital.
They also confuse her for his girlfriend, but as he has amnesia no one realizes the error.
The doctor tells Zoey to avoid upsetting Zach until he recovers, so his parents have her to dinner.
She meets Zach's little sister Avery and his cousin Miles, the guy she'd seen with similar views as her from the lecture.
She continues to discover things she has in common with him.
They invite her along for a family ski weekend, so she cancels her flight to see Paula to join them.
As Zach has to stay in the rented house to rest, Zoey goes to the slopes where Miles teaches her to snowboard.
They are mutually attracted so, that night in the hot tub as they are alone briefly, they kiss.
In the morning when Zach mentions Miles' girlfriend, she confronts him, but he explains they have a polyamorous relationship.
Disappointed, Zoey chooses to spend the day keeping Zach company.
As he must avoid screens, they play games like Jenga and chess.
Zach even shows his culinary skills by preparing a gourmet pizza with her.
By the end of the day, Zoey feels a bond with him, saying that she hopes he remembers how well this day was once his amnesia is gone.
Riding back to the MacLarens', the soccer playing Zoey arrives, accusing Zoey of identity theft.
She is able to explain the circumstances, and apologizes for deceiving them.
As Zoey leaves, Avery blurts out that she prefers her to soccer Zoey.
Back in class, outlandish rumors circulate about Zoey, and she's videoed lashing out at the negative attention.
Later, she lashes out at Elle, upset that she'd convinced her to lie.

Elle reveals she is seeing someone- a guy she had met while babysitting who brought her food by delivery service- but says she didn't tell her because she didn't want to hurt her feelings and that she's never been into anyone.
Fed up, Zoey goes to her mom's.
Paula makes her realize that she needs to be brave and go after what she wants.
Returning to her college, Zoey writes Elle an apology poem and they make up.
Then Becca proposes she help them promote the upcoming Jam Fest to recover her image.
They'd like her to set up a web page with geotags and simultaneous multiple video feeds.
Successfully getting the website up and running after an all-nighter, Zoey plans on watching from home in her pjs.
However, Elle drags her to the Jam Fest before it finishes, as Zach is there and is likely available.
Throwing her coat over her pjs, she stops the music to find him.
Once she does, Zoey confesses her feelings, Zach admits he broke up with soccer Zoey because of his feelings and they kiss.

23113732.title: The Chronicle: After the Storm (2020 film)
synopsis: At dawn's first light, widely recognized reporter John Smith steps out from an aged, rust-center Chevrolet amidst the wreckage of hurricane-stricken Panama City, Florida.
The devastation mirrored on his time-worn face as he surveys the scene of such extensive ruin.

The once bustling city that he fondly remembered is currently buried under the wreckage, the residential establishments ripped apart, their foundations exposed as if scraped clean by an immense power.
Smith devotes his day traversing through the chaos and destruction, interactively engaging with the affected survivors and making an effort to document the remnants of their broken lives.
Every individual heartrending experience submerges him deeper into a pit of gloom as he records these painful stories of loss and desolation.
Wandering through the wreckage, Smith crosses paths with David, a thin man with a visage scarred by recurring hurricanes and emotional duress, who stands resolutely near his flattened home.
Drawn in by David's resilience, Smith experiences an attachment and a responsibility to assist him in recovering the remnants of his shattered life.

Together, they traverse a daunting maze of red-tape regulations, processing applications for FEMA's disaster assistance and grappling with the slow and exhausting insurance system, pushing their strength to the limit.

As they fight their way through their restoration efforts, the widespread looting from the storm-damaged properties brings in a disheartening layer of complexity, amplifying the rebuilding challenge manifold.
Suddenly, a stark radio announcement reverberates through the city setting off waves of anxiety: a new storm appears to be gathering in the Gulf, ready to strike their still tender wounds.
Confronted with this life-altering decision, Smith struggles between his professional commitment and a compelling urge to actively partake in the city's reconstruction efforts.
The approaching storm augments the gloom, pushing the tenacity of the survivors and shaking Smith's journalistic ethics to the breaking point.
Powering off his Nikon camera, Smith steps out of the role of an independent witness of events, readily immersing himself in the daunting effort of restoring the city to its former glory.

His sudden foray into active involvement sets off a series of events; Smith documents his experiences not as a hidden observer but as an active participant, struggling against the forces of nature and the bureaucratic ties holding back progress.
His direct interaction triggers an overpowering empathetic response towards the victims of the storm.
As Smith dives deeper into the relief operations, a gnawing sense of guilt starts to weigh upon him, compelling a review of his journalistic aspirations.
Standing shoulder to shoulder with David in the thick of it, Smith's outlook shifts from that of an outsider to an integral part of the struggling community.
Smith's transformation begins to impact his professional persona, prompting a reassessment of his journalistic attitude and interpretation of objectivity.
As the city starts to see the initial rays of hope, the tenacity of the survivors begins to shine, lighting up their path towards surviving and rebuilding their shattered city.
The narrative concludes as dawn breaks with the golden sunlight highlighting a transformed Smith contemplating his evolved philosophy of reporting.

60270086.title: The Photograph (2020 film)
synopsis: Reporter Michael Block meets a man in Louisiana named Isaac to interview him about his life post-Hurricane Katrina.
He takes an interest in one particular photo in Isaac's home of a woman named Christina Eames, and wants to know her backstory.
In the present day Mae, Christina's daughter, inherits a safety deposit box upon her death which includes the same picture of herself and two letters.
The first is to Mae and the second is for her to deliver to her father.
Back in New York, Michael meets Mae who works as an assistant curator.
She pulls Christina's archival material to show him.
Attracted to Mae, Michael intentionally sets up a "chance meeting" with her at a French movie screening her gallery is showing.
They flirt and decide to go on their first date, ending with a kiss.
They begin to date but this coincides with Michael getting a job in London.
He struggles to tell Mae about the move as their relationship is new, so begins to ignore her calls.
In the past, Christina has a flirtatious friendship with Isaac.
Eventually, they begin to live together but Christina is bored of her life as she longs to pursue a career in photography.
Without telling Isaac she gets on a bus leaving for New York City, and gets a job as an assistant photographer.
She calls her friend Denise to give her the good news, who tells Christina that her mother has passed away.
At the funeral, she mentions that she is going to visit Isaac, but Denise tells her that he married shortly after she left.
A few years later, Christina returns to her hometown with Mae.
They take a photograph in her old home.
While there, they run into Isaac who offers to bring them to dinner to meet his wife.
Christina refuses and becomes very emotional, kissing Isaac's cheek and crying afterwards which Mae remembers, even as an adult.
In the present day, Mae meets Isaac and delivers the letter Christina wrote, letting him know that her letter said he is her biological father.
He admits to suspecting it when he met Mae as a child, but was too afraid to ask Christina.
Michael goes to meet Isaac and finish his article and is surprised to see Mae there.
They spend the day together and at the end Michael tells her that he got a job in London.
He will be leaving soon but would like to continue the relationship.
Mae tells him long distance isn't practical.
She then works on putting together a retrospective of her mother's work and finds a video where her mother says she wishes she had been better at loving people.
While working in London, Michael gets an invitation from Mae to see a Kendrick Lamar concert.
They meet up in NYC, where Mae finally confesses her feelings for him and they vow to work things out despite the distance.

43672509.title: Sergeant Patriot: Duty and Fatherhood
synopsis: The narrative begins with our hero, John Hanson Jr., sitting quietly in the attic, studying an old photograph of his long-deceased father, Sgt.
Hanson Sr., dressed in a U.S. Army uniform.
The sergeant’s military regalia, perfectly accentuating his stern features, becomes the gateway for John Jr. to enter his father's hitherto concealed world.
John's nostalgic gaze next lands on a cold, steel chest, weathered by time but kept in pristine condition out of reverence.
Once unlatched, it discloses a treasure trove of Sgt.
Hanson Sr.'s military relics.
Every medal, every badge that he carefully extracts from the chest, makes a unique sound, like an untold epic resurfacing.
There are vibrant family albums buried under the military memorabilia, holding photos that are well-worn by repeated viewings.
A compilation of VHS home videos showcase the heartwarming memories of a doting father playing ball with his kids or teaching them to ride a bike.
Contrastingly, a monochrome professional photograph of Sgt.
Hanson Sr., in full military regalia, captures his authoritative aura.
Intrigued by the contradictory aspects of his father's personality, John Jr.'s curiosity is further kindled.
He decides to dive deeper into the enigma that was his father, a man of love but also of war.
Fueled by this quest for truth, John Jr. embarks on a relentless and arduous investigation to reveal the hitherto disjointed chapters of his father’s life.
A historian by trade and by heart, John Jr. starts his methodical research by drawing valuable information from his father's former comrades, renowned military historians, and acclaimed biographers.

He thoroughly combs through piles of classified documents, old army debriefings, archived military films from the year 2010, each one revealing a consequential chapter in his father's military timeline.
As John shields his eyes from raw information, he gradually stitches together the fabric of pains and prides that his father's celebrated military career was weaved of.
Within the harsh realities of war, amidst the gun smoke, there are fleeting moments of camaraderie, contagious laughter, and gentle ribbing that binds soldiers together.
And then, as if turning a page, the narrative shifts back to the coziness of domestic life.
Sgt.
Hanson Sr. is seen in a different light, as a caring husband to his nervous wife and a fun-loving dad to his excitable kids.
He’s being goofy in front of the camera or reading bedtime stories in animated voices.
As he begins to understand his father's reticence regarding his military life, John Jr. finally comes to terms with the burdens Sgt.
Hanson Sr. carried within him.
He wholeheartedly praises his father’s uncelebrated heroism, understanding why Sgt.
Hanson Sr. chose to leave his war scars at the door rather than bring them home.
Touched to his core, John Jr. silently salutes his father's tightly held secret where he unflinchingly donned the double roles - the unwavering military hero, and a nurturing caregiver.
At the end, the viewers are left to contemplate the complex double life of a soldier – a life dominated by honor yet paralleled by love and tenderness.
The narrative comes full circle as John Jr. solemnly venerates the enduring values that his father lived by, those of honor, duty, bravery, and above all, unconditional love.
The conclusory projection of his father’s photograph in the uniform, harmoniously placed amongst the family photographs in the same frame, recalls the shared narrative that binds them eternally.
The narrative leaves the audience reflecting on the immense sacrifices a soldier makes on and off the battlefield.

64572702.title: Father Soldier Son
synopsis: In 2010, U.S. Army Sgt.
First Class Brian Eisch is a single father of two sons, Isaac, age 12, and Joey, age 7.
While he is away on deployment in Afghanistan for 6 months, the boys live with their uncle, and long to have their father back home.
They are happily reunited for a brief 2-week interlude in the deployment, during which they enjoy camping, hunting, and fishing together.

Brian expresses that his greatest fear is returning home affected by his wartime experiences, and potentially becoming angry and yelling at his kids, a sentiment echoed by his kids, who have heard such stories from their friends.
Back in the field, Brian is shot in the leg while attempting to rescue an Afghan National Army comrade.
At Walter Reed Medical Center, Brian's leg is treated, although doctors cannot guarantee it will heal and tell him to consider amputation.
Brian struggles to continue with his hobbies, being in debilitating pain, and finds himself struggling to continue with daily life.
He mentions his feelings of being a "used-to-could", an individual who used to be useful to the Army and country, and ponders whether he is a burden on the institution that he loves.
Three years later, Brian has his leg amputated at the VA Center in Syracuse.
He is supported by his girlfriend, Maria, who also brings her third child, Jordan, to live with the family.
At age 10, Jordan enjoys playing with Joey, now of the same age.
Brian, meanwhile, struggles with the delayed healing process for his leg, and his repeated inability to start using a prosthetic.
Eventually, however, he is able to progress and begin to move around slowly.
Having previously been a successful wrestler in high school, he coaches Joey from the sidelines, but Joey doesn't respond well to his more aggressive coaching.
Brian proposes to Maria on a family outing.
Eight months after amputation, Brian progresses to a more advanced prosthetic and starts to tentatively run short distances on his own.
He also begins to sell plastic bass lures, to occupy some of his time during the bleak winter months.
Joey aspires for a career in the Army, while Isaac, somewhat disillusioned by the separation inherent in the military lifestyle, expresses his hopes to go to college and become a police officer.
Brian and Maria are happily married, with both expressing their desire to love all of the children as their own.
Two months after this happy time, in July 2015, the family is struck by tragedy when Joey, age 12, is struck by a truck while on his bicycle outside the family home.
He dies in the hospital and the family buries him shortly thereafter in a ceremony with much of the community.
All of the family are profoundly affected, but hope to slowly move on, without forgetting their beloved son.
That fall, Isaac starts his last year of high school alongside Jordan, and eventually decides to enlist in the Army.
While he previously resolved not to do so, he feels somewhat obligated in the honour of Joey and his father, with Brian in particular being extremely proud to see his son in uniform.
Isaac goes to his senior prom and graduates from high school shortly afterwards.
The family says a tearful but proud goodbye to Isaac as he departs for Basic Combat Training.
While he is there, Brian and Maria share the news that they are expecting a son, Jaxon.
The family is overjoyed to see Isaac graduate and begin military service.
With Jaxon's birth, the family begins to move emotionally forward from Joey's tragic death.
Two years later, in 2019, Isaac expresses some of his regrets about military life, and it not necessarily being what he idolized it to be.
He also shares that he has begun to feel depressed over the past year, feeling the weight of his biological mother leaving, his father's injury, and brother's death all at once.
The family is seen happily with Jaxon, although Maria states that Brian hides his internal anger, still wishing he was the man he once was both physically and mentally.
The film closes with Isaac expressing his hope that he can live up to his father's record in the military, and be like the man he has looked up to his entire life.

40286115.title: Journey of Siblings: Moonlight Memories
synopsis: The carefully lit loft in bustling Manhattan becomes the backdrop for our opening scene.

Here, Nathan -- a grizzled author closing in on midlife, with his hair an unkempt wave of untamed curls -- begins sifting through his neglected pile of mail, precariously teetering over the edge of a rustic coffee table.
Among the pile, he discovers a worn-out, dust-laden envelope hidden away beneath the layers of untouched mail.
As he unearths this envelope and proceeds to unfold the letter inside, he is hit with the stark realization of his estranged father, Richard's abrupt death.
Stunned by the tragic revelation, Nathan gathers himself and reaches hastily for his phone, dialing a number.
On the other side of the line is his sister, Vanessa, an avidly committed psychiatrist currently in the middle of a therapeutic session within her Chicago clinic.
When Nathan relays the somber news to Vanessa, she immediately springs into action.
She swiftly cancels her upcoming appointments and manages to book a flight back to their childhood hometown in Bar Harbor, Maine.
Later, we see them at the John F. Kennedy Airport, where their reunion takes place.
Their destination is the somewhat dilapidated farmhouse, their childhood sanctuary that stands neglected with its paint peeling off from years of abandonment.
They cross the threshold, stepping into rooms heavy with old memories.
As they navigate through the layers of the past, they are also met with keen interest from the small-town locals.

As they explore the quaint, cobblestone streets of their hometown, they find themselves running into faces from their past, each encounter shedding light on their understanding of their father's enigmatic past.
That very night, Vanessa is plagued by a disturbing nightmare that features the spectral figure of their father -- an unnerving scenario set amidst the neglected house-turned-graveyard.
An elderly local historian starts to explore the ominous graveyard.
Its history is complicated, tinged with the local history about mysterious witch trials and government-imposed relocations.
In their father's private study, Nathan stumbles upon a collection of alchemical manuscripts, a number of esoteric books, and various items linked to dark occult practices.
Vanessa's nightmares become increasingly violent and terrifying, blurring the lines of reality.
After encountering a series of supernatural occurrences that they can't explain, they resolve to enlist the help of local ghost hunters.
The group of ghost hunters put forth a theory – their arrival in town and the awakening of dormant paranormal entities are connected to their ancestral heritage.
They stumble upon evidence of horrifying alchemical necromantic experiments in the desolate study beneath a trapdoor.
Underneath a worn-out floorboard, Nathan discovers his father’s battered diary.
Upon reading it, he comprehends a horrifying admission of guilt -- the accidental failure of an experiment aimed at resurrecting the spirit of their deceased mother, Isabelle.
This revelation propels them to the haunted graveyard where they find themselves face-to-face with the spectral manifestation of their mother.
Vanessa draws on her professionalism to communicate with the restless apparition of their mother.
She convinces Isabelle to break free from her ties to the past.
This confrontation concludes in a cathartic release as they witness Isabelle's spirit dissolve into the luminescence of the moonlight.
Standing by Richard's grave, Nathan and Vanessa share a solemn moment of farewell.
They decide to forgive the sins of their father.
As they retreat from the cemetery, they contemplate on the ordeal they have endured.
The grim event brought them a deeper understanding of each other, helping them strengthen their sibling bond.
Inspired by their bravery, the tight-knit Bar Harbor community organize a tribute in their honor.
The narrative reaches a threshold as mournful dawn breaks.
The siblings drive off in their dad's old red Ford truck, its headlights piercing through the darkness.
The radiant moon overhead hints at a promising future, bringing a closure to a nightmarish chapter of their lives.

69327707.title: Night of the Animated Dead
synopsis: John and his sister Barbara drive to a Pennsylvania cemetery to visit their father’s grave.
Unbeknownst to the siblings, an undead outbreak causes corpses to reanimate across the country at the same time.
A zombie in the cemetery attacks and kills John.
Barbara flees to a nearby farmhouse but finds a woman who lived there dead and half-eaten.
Ben, another survivor seeking shelter from the growing zombie horde, joins Barbara in the house.

He explains that he came across a radio broadcast from an abandon truck parked at Beekman's Diner earlier reporting violent incidents around the country and witnessed a propane truck being attacked by zombies and crashed into a gas station which caught on fire, killing the driver trapped inside, and attracting more zombies coming from the diner.
Some of the zombies at the gas station were burned in the fire while others stayed away from the flames.
The zombies are afraid of fire and light.
With Barbara in a state of catatonic shock, Ben fights off zombies with a torch and a lever action rifle and begins boarding up the windows by himself.
Ben and Barbara discover cowardly Harry Cooper hiding in the cellar with his wife Helen and their injured daughter Karen along with a young man named Tom and his girlfriend Judy.
Harry, Karen and Helen were traveling when they were attacked by the zombies that overturned their car and Karen was bitten in the arm.
They cross paths with Tom and Judy and hid in the farmhouse.
Animosity forms when Ben asks for help fortifying the house while Harry insists on everyone bunkering in the cellar instead.
A TV news bulletin suggests the undead outbreak may have been caused by radiation from a probe returning from Venus.

The TV and radio news reports of a wave of mass murder being committed across the east coast of the United States by an army of cannibalistic, reanimating corpses, and posses of armed men patrolling the countryside to kill the ghouls.
They confirm that the ghouls can be stopped with a bullet or heavy blow to the head or by being burned, as Ben discovered, and that various rescue centers are offering refuge and safety.
The men devise an escape plan that involves gassing up at a nearby pump so they can flee in the truck Ben arrived in.
Tom and Judy drive the truck while Ben uses a torch to ward off zombies from the back.
At the pump, a spill causes the truck to catch fire.
The engine explodes.
Shrapnel kills Tom and Judy.
Ben fights his way back to the house, but Harry refuses to let him inside.
Ben breaks in anyway and beats Harry to the floor.
Another TV news report shows Sheriff McClelland organizing posses to hunt and kill the undead ghouls.
Zombies besiege the farmhouse.
Harry and Ben struggle for the rifle and Ben shoots Harry in his stomach during the melee.
Harry stumbles down to the cellar.
Helen soon follows only to find their daughter Karen eating Harry’s corpse.
Karen then stabs her mother to death with a gardening trowel.
The zombie horde pulls Barbara outside.
With the house now overrun, Ben bunkers in the basement.
Harry’s mutilated corpse reanimates, but Ben shoots it in the head and then shoots a dead but not yet reanimated Helen in the head as a precaution.
In the morning, Sheriff McClelland’s men arrive outside and they begin dispatching zombies.
Hearing the gunshots, Ben goes back upstairs and toward a window to investigate.
Mistaking him for a zombie, Sheriff McClelland directs a man named Vince to shoot Ben in the head.
Ben’s body is then dragged to a pile of executed zombies that the posse sets on fire.

98881764.title: Unstoppable: A Political Revolution (2020 film)
synopsis: The movie begins in the cloudy city of Portland, where Sam Jacobs, a famous political strategist for the Democratic Party, is seen drinking bourbon, following a disheartening election defeat.

Nursing his bourbon on a lonely night, Sam aimlessly scrolls through the internet and stumbles upon a raw, unfiltered YouTube video of John Harper, a charismatic ex-Navy SEAL from the nondescript town of Luzerville, Nebraska.
John is speaking at a lively town hall meeting, passionately rallying for the rights of Central American undocumented migrants.
Sam finds himself captivated by John's authenticity and powerful conviction, feeling a palpable rush of excitement for the first time since his electoral defeat.
Almost impulsively, he packs his weather-beaten suitcase and heads towards Luzerville to convince John to run for State Senator.
Upon reaching Luzerville, Sam finds it to be a quiet symbol of Midwest charm.
Among the town's population, he meets Lydia, the vivacious owner of a local bakery named "Sweet Lydia’s Pies."
Fueled by the possibility of fulfilling a political vision and a newfound romantic interest, Sam musters courage and approaches John at his rustic farmhouse.
He presents a high-stakes proposal to guide John into the daunting arena of politics.
John meets Sam's proposal with skepticism, revealing a humorous dynamic between the city-dwelling political strategist and the no-nonsense, rugged ex-Navy SEAL.
Sam becomes aware that persuading John is only half his challenge.
His real test begins with integrating into the town’s eccentric customs, bonding with the close-knit communities, facing comical blunders and learning from them.
Sam and John embark on a rigorous endeavor to polish John's image.
Their unconventional grassroots campaign takes off, offering a stark contrast to Senator McCain, the stern, humorless incumbent they aim to replace.
The town is swept into a whirlwind of grassroots excitement, filled with barnstorming rallies, spontaneous speeches, and open-to-all town hall meetings.
Sparks fly between Sam and Lydia.
Their interactions, invariably taking place at “Sweet Lydia’s Pies," craft a gentle romance into the narrative.
John's final campaign speech at a buzzing community center turns into a spectacle.
John delivers an impactful and passionate plea to his townsfolk, resounding with the farmers and ranchers who form the backbone of Luzerville.
In an unexpected twist, Sam reveals a shocking case of mistaken identity.
The town has been taken for a ride by Senator McCain, involving Luzerville's cherished tradition of having a costumed squirrel as a town mascot.
The revelation leaves party bureaucrats dumbfounded in the state capital and sends the townfolk into fits of laughter.
Overwhelmed by the audacity of their grassroots campaign, the town witnesses the triumph of their unexpected heroes over a powerful political adversary.
A raucous victory party ensues in Luzerville's town square, where their local heroes bask in their surprising success.
Sam, in an emblematic moment, proposes a toast to John and Lydia amidst the dancing crowd.
As the movie winds down, the festive scene gently transitions from visual to auditory, ending with the blissful sounds of laughter echoing in the distance.

58649000.title: Irresistible (2020 film)
synopsis: Plunged into despair by the results of the 2016 presidential election, veteran Democratic Party campaign consultant Gary Zimmer is shown a viral video of retired Marine Col. Jack Hastings giving a speech in support of the illegal immigrant population of his hometown, the fictional town of Deerlaken, Wisconsin.

Calculating that getting Hastings elected as a Democrat in Deerlaken's upcoming mayoral election will help him convince the American people in the heartland to vote Democrat in the next presidential election, Zimmer travels to Wisconsin to persuade Hastings to run.
Arriving in Deerlaken, Gary experiences the vast cultural divide between his home of Washington, D.C., and the townspeople's more rural mannerisms and political beliefs.
Gary soon meets Hastings and his daughter Diana and pitches his idea.

Hastings initially declines, considering himself more of a conservative and having no real interest in politics, but later relents and agrees to run under the condition that Gary serve as his campaign manager.
Hastings recruits his friends and neighbors as volunteers for the campaign.
However, setbacks soon arise such as limited Wi-Fi, xenophobia, social conservatism, and the fact that the incumbent mayor, Braun, is being funded by the Republican National Committee.
The RNC also sends Faith Brewster, Gary's nemesis, to counter Gary.
As the race heats up, Gary takes Jack to New York City so they can recruit fundraisers for the campaign to match Faith's money and resources.
Jack gives a powerful speech to the possible donors about how he needs their help for his small town, which inspires Gary.
Their donations allow Gary to upgrade their campaigning methods.

Soon the election polls show the two candidates neck-and-neck, although the Hastings campaign takes a dive when one of Gary's team members advertises a pro-contraceptive platform to a group of single women who turn out to be nuns.
When Gary starts berating his teammates, Diana convinces him to apologize and that if he is going to run her father's campaign, he needs to be nice.
When it starts to look like Faith and Braun are going to win, Gary tries to convince Jack and Diana to play dirty and start exploiting Braun's skeletons.
Diana is horrified that Gary would play dirty and secretly goes to Braun for advice.
The two decide to secretly reveal a bigger scandal about Braun so Gary will not go after Braun's brother, which was his original plan.
The scandal, however, proves to be false.
On Election Day, almost no one votes (only two votes are cast, with one vote going to each candidate, resulting in a tie), which confuses both Gary and Faith.
It quickly becomes clear that the election was actually a setup.

Diana reveals she masterminded the entire scheme, filming the video of her father's immigration speech (which was carefully scripted) so that the Democrats and Republicans would pour thousands of dollars into the election; the town has been quietly siphoning the money to get through its financial troubles due to the recent closure of a nearby military base.

Gary is shocked that Diana would play him and Diana then counters by explaining the town had no choice but to set him up because D.C. politicians play small towns like theirs all the time while doing nothing to help when times are tough.
When Gary reveals that he has feelings for Diana, she rejects him, pointing to their age difference.
Later, Diana becomes the mayor of Deerlaken after a special election.

The film ends with three scenes leading into each other, each with its own set of cast credits: Gary and Diana embrace at a construction site for a new public building; until Gary is snapped out of that thought to reveal Gary and Ann, the pastry chef, in bed, discussing plans for a new bakery; until Gary finally snaps out of that to show Gary and Faith kiss and discuss their investment portfolio in their kitchen.
A post-credits scene shows a short interview with Trevor Potter, an official of the Federal Election Commission, discussing the shortcomings of oversight over elections fund-raising.
The screen shows the title IRRESISTIBLE fading into the word RESIST.

39050728.title: The Final Moments of National Disorder
synopsis: The World Government unveils a new technology known as the Neural Transmission Suppressor (NTS), presenting it as the ultimate solution to rising crimes.
A live demonstration is broadcast worldwide, showcasing a criminal rendered incapable of violent behavior due to the NTS device.
The technology is swiftly adopted, reshaping society by substantially reducing criminal activity.
Carter Willis, a brilliant physicist partially responsible for the NTS technology, begins to worry about the possible adverse effects it may have.
Jake Morrison, an entrepreneur who has adopted the new technology, begins to experience strange symptoms post his NTS implantation.
Carter, alarmed by the news of Jake's symptoms, validates his fears about the technology.
Suspicious about the NTS' functionality, journalist Alexandra "Alex" Hendrix decides to investigate, teaming up with Carter.
Their secret inquiry unveils the government's covert operations around NTS and they soon realize they are under surveillance.
While further investigating, they discover a plot by the World Government to use the NTS as a tool to suppress opposition.
Alex leaks this information to the public, incurring the wrath of the government.
Residents across the globe, now aware of the truth, demand accountability from their leaders.
The government, in response, deploys a task force to stop Carter and Alex.
During their escape, Carter is gravely injured.
Despite the circumstances, Alex manages to secure additional classified documents detailing a new, more sinister, government plot using the NTS.
She unveils the new information, causing further unrest among the populace and escalating the public uprising.
Now severely weak, Carter expresses his regret to Alex about his role in the creation of the NTS.
In his honor, Alex vows to continue their fight against the oppressive regime.
The narrative concludes with the beginning of global awakening, spurred by the acts of Carter and Alex.

58010112.title: The Last Days of American Crime
synopsis: In 2024, the U.S. government prepares to activate the American Peace Initiative (API) signal, a “synaptic blocker” that will prevent the population from breaking the law.
In Detroit, Graham Bricke leads a crew of bank robbers including his brother Rory, who begins a prison sentence.
The API signal is tested while Bricke’s crew robs a bank, and one of the thieves is killed.
Bricke lies to the Dumois crime family that he lost the stolen money, which he saves to escape to Canada, but is notified that Rory has killed himself in prison.
One week before the signal’s nationwide deployment, Bricke’s money is taken.
He tortures a man named Sidell into confessing that Johnny Dee, a member of Bricke’s crew, betrayed him to the Dumois syndicate.
Bricke leaves Sidell to die in a fiery explosion, kills Johnny, and buys a deadly neurotoxin at a bar, where he is seduced by Shelby Dupree.
He meets her fiancé Kevin Cash, who explains that he and Rory were used to test the signal in prison, and Rory was killed by the guards.
Shelby and Kevin reveal their plan to rob the city’s “money factory” by disrupting an API signal tower and fleeing across the river to Canada.
Bricke takes over the heist and through surveillance of the facility he finds out that over $1 billion in new and used bills is being stored there.
He also deduces that Kevin is the heir to the Dumois family.
Shelby and Bricke begin an affair, and he recruits his trusted getaway driver Ross.
The government is buying back criminals' ill-gotten wealth, and Shelby, a gifted hacker, prints $5 million in counterfeit bills which Bricke arranges to trade in.
Following Shelby, Bricke learns she is an informant for the FBI, who threaten her younger sister to ensure her cooperation.
As the city’s police department prepares to become obsolete, Officer William Sawyer is forced to kill an assailant in self-defense.
He joins the new law enforcement division, and receives an implant making him immune to the API signal.
Kevin takes Bricke to meet Rossi Dumois, his father.
Rossi shoots and wounds Kevin, who kills him with an axe, and Kevin and Bricke raid Rossi’s weapons, including three EFP cone warheads.
Bricke confronts Shelby for working with the FBI, but is knocked out and beaten by Lonnie, Rossi’s lieutenant.
Shelby is taken hostage by Lonnie as Sidell, alive but disfigured, tortures Bricke and leaves him to die in a fire.
Bricke is rescued by Ross and pursues Lonnie, who injects Shelby with heroin and prepares to rape her, but Bricke kills him.
On the day the signal will deploy, Ross infiltrates the money factory in a garbage truck, and Shelby subdues a systems manager at an API facility.
Bricke and Kevin deliver the counterfeit $5 million to the factory and shoot their way to the vault, which they breach with the warheads.
Shelby hacks the API system and disrupts the signal, allowing Bricke, Kevin, and Ross to load the truck with money and escape.
Sawyer detains Shelby, and the signal resumes, incapacitating Ross and Bricke.
Unaffected, Kevin kills Ross, revealing that he and Rory were forced to fight in prison by the guards, who tortured them with the API signal; Kevin learned to overcome the signal, and killed Rory.
He shoots Bricke, but is killed by Shelby’s FBI handlers, who tell Bricke that they will kill Shelby to close their case.
Left to die, Bricke consumes his neurotoxin; instead of killing him, it ends the signal’s effect on him.
He kills the FBI agents and escapes in the truck full of money.
Struggling against the signal, Shelby fights off Sawyer, who strangles her but is impaled on a glass shard and dies.
Shelby blows up the facility, ignoring the agents preparing to shoot her.
She is rescued by Bricke, and they plow through the border checkpoint into Canada.
Shelby tells Bricke she loves him before he dies from his wounds, and she flees with a bag of money.
Some time later, Shelby spreads Rory’s ashes at a lake, and drives away with her sister to a new life in Canada.

73800873.title: Tales of Terror: Urban Chronicles
synopsis: Joshua is introduced as a tenth grader with an unusual habit: writing chilling horror stories.
A native of the bustling city of New York, Joshua has cultivated a strange sense of peace amidst the screams and scares of his own narratives.
Joshua lives with his aunt Sarah, a compassionate kindergarten teacher, and her gruff but caring husband Uncle Ben, a firefighter.
During breakfast one chilly autumn morning, Aunt Sarah reads out a local newspaper article that narrates the merciless murder of a community member.
Back in his attic bedroom, Joshua commits his new character, the sinister “The Terminus” to paper.
Joshua decides to share his latest horror at the school's traditional show-and-tell session.
Joshua's unsettling story forces his high school to call in his guardians.
Just as the city dwellers scrambled to make sense of Joshua's tales, a series of uncanny events unfold.
The real-life happenings mimic the terrifying events described in “The Terminus's" story, alarming both Joshua and the community.
Meanwhile, the city gets engulfed in a wave of terror as more and more incidents mirroring Joshua’s tale surface.
Realizing the power of his narratives, Joshua takes it upon himself to save the city.
Their mission leads them through the labyrinth of New York City streets, ending up in a city fringe railroad yard, just like one described in Joshua's disturbing tale.
Terrified yet determined, they manage to capture footage of a figure alarmingly identical to Joshua's creation, "The Terminus."
Now armed with undeniable proof, Joshua pushes harder to be believed.
He returns to the police with his friends and the video, demanding they investigate his claims seriously.
Finally, the police, baffled by the striking similarities between Joshua's stories and the horrifying incidents plaguing the city, decide to delve deeper into his assertions.
A painstaking investigation uncovers an alarming truth - "The Terminus" isn't a product of Joshua's imagination after all; rather, it's the ominous messenger of an old witch's curse on the city.
He sets about crafting a narrative where “The Terminus” is defeated heroically by the city's residents.
Unbelievably, the events of Joshua's story happen in the city, leading to a monumental confrontation that results in the arrest of "The Terminus."
Residents who previously shunned Joshua’s ominous tales now recognize him as their hero.
The final scene places Joshua back in his quiet corner of the library.
He reads tales of courage and determination to an engaged, mixed crowd, symbolizing his journey from a fear creator to a beacon of hope.
Joshua, the young man who was once deemed a disturbing anomaly is now celebrated as the city's unsung hero.

66570605.title: Nightbooks
synopsis: Alex Mosher, a young boy from Brooklyn, New York, overhears his parents talking about how worried they are about his preoccupation with writing scary stories and their fear of how he will react to a recent incident.
Screaming in pain, Alex trashes his room, grabs his "Night books” and takes the elevator to the basement, planning to burn them in the furnace.
The elevator suddenly stops— and stays—on a dark floor where an apartment's open door reveals a TV showing Alex's favorite show “The Lost Boys”.
He enters and sees a piece of pumpkin pie that was not touched.
This made him eat the pie and pass out, making the door and television vanish.
He awakens to find himself in the magical apartment of a beautiful witch named Natacha who shows him a closet full of clothes belonging to children who were “not useful to her”.
Alex denies having any unique qualities but when he shows her his books, she demands that he read a new story to her each night, or die.
She puts him to work alongside the housekeeper, a girl named Yasmin, who was lured into the apartment in Washington, D.C.
The apartment moves around the world, seeking victims.
The doors respond only to Natacha's keys.
Her ill-tempered, sometimes-invisible cat, Lenore, spies on them.
Natacha demands that Alex's stories end unhappily.
If not, the apartment shakes.
She repeatedly asks why he wanted to burn his writings, but he manages to distract her.
Searching her vast library for inspiration, Alex finds notes in the margins of books detailing the escape plans of a trapped girl.
She writes about her treasured unicorn necklace, so he dubs her "Unicorn Girl".
Yasmin and Alex bond, and they eventually win Lenore's trust.
Yasmin tearfully reveals she was afraid to befriend him because Natacha killed the others by transforming them into little figurines, now displayed in Natacha's cabinet.
None has a unicorn necklace; Alex concludes that Unicorn Girl escaped.
Her notes contain a recipe for a sleeping potion.
Lenore slips it into Natacha's perfume bottle.
When she falls asleep, they steal her keys and open the door, revealing a forest.
They soon realize they are still inside the apartment.
An evil unicorn drives them to a gingerbread cottage that mesmerizes Yasmin.
They eat the gingerbread and fall unconscious.
Alex wakes to find Yasmin and Lenore caged in a room lined with countless skulls.
Blue mist is being siphoned from a coffin containing a witchlike figure.

Natacha reveals that she was the Unicorn Girl, who after successfully escaping the original witch—who ate all her victims except Natasha—, was able to put her to sleep and returned to her home, only to find that her parents had moved away.
With nowhere to go, she returned, studied witchcraft, and eventually lulled the witch into a deep sleep, using scary stories due to her immense love for them.
Alex has been helping her keep the witch unconscious with his own scary stories while Natacha harvests her magic.
The room shakes.
They will all die if the witch wakes.
Alex's fear of telling his truth makes it the ultimate scary story.
He begins: Alex is used to being called names, but on his birthday, his supposed best friend, Josh, admits that Alex is too “weird.” Everyone is going to Cody's party instead.
Alex's parents are distressed when no one comes to Alex's.
“They made him hate himself,” and Alex, ashamed and hurt, resolves to hide what made him special.
Natacha and the sleeping witch are mollified, but suddenly Alex says that he is glad he was kidnapped because he met Yasmin and Lenore, friends who value him.
The happy ending wakes the hideous witch.
While the witches battle, Yasmin grabs Natacha's perfume bottle and flees with Alex and Lenore.
The front door opens into Alex's building.
The ravenous witch pursues them to the basement.
Alex distracts her by pretending to read a story, then pauses on a cliffhanger and throws the empty notebook into the furnace.
The witch reaches for it.
They push her in and hold the door shut while she melts.
Alex introduces Yasmin and Lenore to his delighted parents as his best friends.
Yasmin is reunited with her family.
On a later visit, she gives Alex a beautiful leather-bound notebook signed “Stay weird storyteller.
Yas.” Meanwhile, a figurine in Natacha's cabinet begin to crackle.
Natacha's hand slams down, and we hear her laughter.

9574014.title: Cope Endure Clash
synopsis: When we first meet Ava Reed, a sensitive and thoughtful teenager bereft with the untimely death of her mother, she is grappling with her grief in Pine Grove - a quaint town, rich in history and simplicity where life ambles along at a familiar pace.

Ava's childhood home, a melancholy and beautiful Victorian cottage, stands somber, echoing the loss of Emily Reed; a woman of remarkable exuberance, overwhelming beauty, and an a mysterious past that remained hidden even to her family.
Following Emily's death, Ava's father, Arthur Reed, greatly acclaimed in the architectural fraternity, immobilized by grief, retreats into his shell.
His emotional distance leaves Ava navigating her sorrow alone, his absence only amplifying her pain.
One gloomy afternoon, as Ava sorts her mother's vintage collection, she discovers an old carved chest in the attic.
Concealed within is a series of hand-written letters, a delicate connection to Emily's past.

Intrigued by the find, Ava delves into the cryptic traces of Emily's concealed life, unfolding a side of her mother she barely recognized - a coded past teeming with secrets far removed from the life she knew.
Each deciphered message peels back the layers of Emily's existence, revealing pieces of a complex puzzle that hints at machination and conspiracy associated with her untimely death.
Propelled by innate curiosity and need for closure, Ava plunges further into the maze of hidden truths, convinced that the real motive behind Emily's death was shrouded in obsidian secrets.
Ava's suspicion mounts when she observes Arthur's evasive stance regarding Emily's past.
His secretive demeanor bolsters her resolve to unearth the obscured truth.

Progressing her clandestine investigation, Ava uncovers a jarring revelation - Emily played a pivotal role in 'The Clandestine Chain,' an underground intelligence agency in a covert war against a notorious criminal gang 'The Scorpions.'
'The Scorpions,' feared for their ruthless operations, had been stealthily thwarted by Emily's intricately-designed clandestine intelligence network.
As Ava engages further in unraveling Emily's clandestine life, she unwittingly becomes a significant threat to 'The Scorpions.'
Exposed now to Emily's covert enemies, Ava finds herself in their crosshairs, a marked adversary.
The chilling connection between her taciturn father's reluctant entanglement in Emily's dangerous underworld shakes Ava's sense of reality.

Navigating the perilous position she's plunged into, Ava harnesses her emerging deduction skills to decipher Emily's layered codes, hoping they'll guide her as she confronts her mother's formidable advisory.
Fueled by this newfound courage and resolve, Ava confronts Arthur, boldly challenging him to untangle from the detrimental nexus of the dark organization that's ensnared him.
Stirred by Ava's passion and tenacity, Arthur struggles to bridge the icy gulf between them, kindling a flicker of hope for a repaired relationship that had bordered on falling apart.
Thus, the duo embarks on an intense adventure, teetering on the precarious line between survival and death as they infiltrate Emily's risky world.
As they set onto this perilous path, racing against the clock, both Ava and Arthur grapple with the fear of losing one another, the emotional storm triggering torrents of guilt and turmoil.
Employing their shared resources, Ava and Arthur begin to unravel the enigma that was Emily's life.
They decode her series of cryptic clues and, before they know it, are hot on the scent of 'The Scorpions.'
The climax is breathtaking as Ava and Arthur manage to evade a lethal trap set by 'The Scorpions,' blowing the cover off the gang's operations and apprehending their cold-blooded leader Cassandra.
Emily's untimely passing was finally avenged as 'The Scorpions' crumbled, the cause of her death revealed as a fatal poisoning by a nefarious compound known as Berserker.
Ava and Arthur reconciled, their bond having emerged stronger through their shared adversities.
Together, they vowed to prioritize transparency, setting aside grief and guilt to provide emotional support to one another.
Along this journey, Ava discovered an untapped reservoir of strength and resolve, traits she didn't realize she possessed.
Navigating the aftermath of their crisis, Ava and Arthur found healing and forgiveness, promising to work towards unity, their shared hardship their catalyst for growth.
They pledged to honor Emily's memory by adopting courage, prioritizing transparency, and cherishing the bond they still had - each other.
Surviving the harrowing ordeal brought an important lesson for Ava and Arthur - the significance of resilience, trust, and family.
This ordeal etched new lines in their relationship, forging their bond stronger.
Finally, Ava and Arthur reflected strength and optimism, representing resilience, the ability to endure, and the power to triumph over the darkest chapters of life.
Their life, after dismantling the notorious 'The Scorpions,' stood as a tribute to Emily's memory, acknowledging her ultimate sacrifice.
The journey etched a tale of Eva and Arthur's transformation as they evolved from emotionally estranged individuals to a formidable and united team.

64826399.title: Run Hide Fight
synopsis: High school student Zoe Hull struggles with the death of her mother, Jennifer, and her relationship with her father, Todd, is strained.
On the way to school, Zoe witnesses classmate Chris Jelick planting a strange device in a field, but writes it off as a prank.
At school, Zoe's best friend Lewis attempts to ask her to prom but Zoe leaves for the bathroom when a drink is spilled on her.
Around town, several incendiary devices are set off, distracting first responders.
A van crashes into the school cafeteria carrying four school shooters.
The leader, Tristan Voy, orders his accomplices Chris Jelick, Anna Jelick, and Kip Quade to begin killing students, but most of them are held hostage.
Lewis, who has access to the school's Facebook page, is tasked with live streaming by Tristan.
Zoe crawls through the bathroom ceiling and escapes the school.
She begins warning students and helping them escape.
Tristan calls the front office to alert them of the shooting.
Because school protocol requires that the shooting be confirmed, the school's principal and security guard are sent to the cafeteria to investigate.
The principal attempts to talk Tristan down, blaming himself for Tristan's rage.
Tristan admits that the entire shooting was a ploy for attention and he only seeks to gain infamy.
Tristan kills the principal but allows the unarmed security guard to escape, commenting on how unprepared the guard was for an actual shooting.
With the situation finally confirmed, the front office calls a lockdown.
Sheriff Tarsy attempts to coordinate a response to the shooting, but it proves difficult.
An explosion in the front office kills the first police officer to respond.
Anna is sent to survey the damage, but she encounters Zoe and is killed in the resulting fight.
A police officer arrives at Tristan's home to find that he has murdered his mother.
The media picks up the livestream, much to Tristan's delight, and he begins removing students from their classrooms where they are sheltered in place.
Kip encounters Zoe and chases after her, but he is quickly subdued.
Handcuffed, Kip admits his motivation for the shooting was retaliation for a bullying incident that occurred in middle school.
Zoe points out that Kip has murdered several innocent students who had nothing to do with the incident.
Zoe contacts the Sheriff and tells him that he needs to direct the media's cameras away from the school so that she can safely evacuate students.
Sheriff Tarsy calls Tristan live on-air to provide cover, but Tristan soon realizes the ruse.
Tristan demands Zoe reveal herself to him, threatening to kill hostages every five minutes if she does not.
Zoe returns to Kip, who expresses remorse for what he has done.
As partial atonement for his crimes, Zoe has Kip ambush Tristan and Chris for her.
Kip is killed, but Zoe escapes with Lewis, who gets injured.
Zoe settles Lewis and reveals that she reciprocates his feelings for her, but that she has a hard time expressing them.
Lewis warns her that the van in the cafeteria is filled with explosives.
Chris is sent to kill Zoe, but he is instead killed by Todd, who has taken a sniping position outside the school, right before Chris can execute her.
Zoe hijacks the livestream, telling Tristan that she is the one people will remember, not him.
Tristan rigs the van to explode and escapes with a single hostage and an explosive.
Zoe jams the van in reverse so it explodes in the vacant parking lot.
Zoe pursues Tristan but is mistakenly arrested by SWAT.
Outside of the school, Zoe meets Sheriff Tarsy, who thanks her for her actions and tells her that Tristan died in an explosion.
Zoe meets with her father, affirming their love and repairing their relationship.
Afterward, she sees Tristan fleeing into the woods, having faked his death.
Zoe retrieves her father's hunting rifle and shoots Tristan as he retrieves a cache of money and a passport.
Standing over him, Zoe lets Tristan bleed to death, telling him that it is what he deserves for what he has done.

1003437.title: Lisa's New Home Celebration
synopsis: Lisa, a woman vivacious and full of life, jubilantly uncorks a bottle of champagne to celebrate purchasing her dream residence, a Victorian style house nestled in the serene town of Misthill.
To commemorate this memorable occasion, Lisa invites her closest friends for a cozy housewarming party.

As the excitement of the initial move subsided, Lisa starts noticing unconventional activities in her newly acquired house: the sporadic glow and dimming of the old chandelier, the creaking of sturdy mahogany doors when there is clearly no draft.
Trying to maintain her practicality, Lisa disregards these incidents, justifying them as expected idiosyncrasies of a centuries-old house.
But as days turn into weeks, these puzzling occurrences only seem to increase in frequency, becoming more mystifying and unnerving with each manifestation.
Further unsettling Lisa, some of her friends who graced her housewarming party start disappearing mysteriously.
Terrified yet resolute, Lisa decides to unearth the eerie history locked within the confines of her Victorian house.
Amidst heavy, dust-laden library shelves of the town library, she discovers age-worn newspaper clippings.
The frayed articles narrate a sensational story about a meteorite crash on her property a century ago.
Digging deeper into the archives, she uncovers a shocking correlation: the past inhabitants of her home all saw their ends in confounding, unnaturally tragic events.
Piecing together these chilling discoveries, a sickening realization dawns on Lisa, linking the disturbing events with the cursed meteorite.
Resolute to confront this haunting presence, Lisa makes contact with Dr. Thorne, a renowned paranormal investigator.
Lisa's persuasive plea about her predicament wins him over and he eventually evaluates her property.
It doesn’t take long for him to substantiate her fears about the malignant energy within her house.
Despite the daunting revelation, Lisa dauntlessly decides to face the lingering malevolent forces.
To combat the ordeal manifesting in her home, she brings in Father Noel, an experienced exorcist from the local parish.
The exorcism process is deeply disturbing.
The aged house shudders violently, furniture levitates uncontrollably and shadowy figures flicker mysteriously across the room.
Battling through the tumult, Lisa grasps the solution to her predicament: the cursed meteorite must be returned to the cosmos from where it originated.
With renewed courage, she with Dr. Thorne and a handful of loyal friends plan a daring mission to ensure the sinister stone is returned to its cosmic realm.
In an anxiety-filled, nail-biting moment, they manage to launch the dark, extraterrestrial rock into the outer space using a large, helium-filled weather balloon.
As she confronts the challenging task of packing her cherished belongings, her hand falls upon a small, overlooked fragment of the meteorite.
The sinister revelation rekindles her apprehension, shadowing her seeming relief with a chilling sense of dread.
As she contemplates her next action, the room falls eerily quiet, broken only by the steady ticking of the aging grandfather clock, as Lisa holds the ill-omened stone close.
Outside, the moving truck waits impatiently.
Lisa, clutching the stone, casts a final, longing glance at the house that was once her paradise, and now a haunting nightmare.
Mustering her courage, she firmly steps away from her dream-turned-nightmare home towards the waiting truck.
On the road, she clutches the pulsating fragment of the meteorite, its icy surface a stark contrast to the skin on her palm.
The determination in Lisa’s eyes mirrors her readiness to overcome the looming horrors.
Inside the vehicle, the fragment throbs rhythmically against her chest, an eerie glow pulsates with each heartbeat as the screen gradually dims, centering on the path ahead.
As the darkness engulfs the screen, a chilling premonition of an impending, horrific journey chills viewers to the bone, setting the stage for the spine-chilling sequel to come.

62841171.title: She Dies Tomorrow
synopsis: Amy is a young woman who has recently purchased a house, and is congratulated over the phone by her friend Jane.
Amy seems distant, confusing Jane, who mentions that she cannot come over due to having to stop by her sister-in-law's birthday party, but agrees to visit anyway.
Amy searches for urns on her computer, before changing her search to leather jackets.
When Jane visits, Amy reveals to her that she knows she is going to die the next day, which Jane initially writes off as a result of Amy consuming alcohol, revealing that Amy is a former alcoholic.
Amy repeatedly says that she wants to be turned into a leather jacket after she dies, so she could be made into something of use.
Jane leaves, telling her she will call the next day.
Jane returns to her house to continue studying samples under a microscope, but suddenly becomes paranoid and rushes to Amy's house, leaving several voice messages but being unable to contact her.
She then leaves to go to her sister-in-law's birthday party.
At the party, Jane appears disheveled and in her pajamas, confusing the other guests and disturbing them by saying she, too, is going to die tomorrow.
This upsets Susan, Jane's sister-in-law, while Jane's brother, Jason, tries to defuse the tension.
Tilly, a party guest, remarks to her boyfriend, Brian, that she thought Jane was crazy as they are in the car preparing to leave.
However, Brian says he thought she was correct, revealing that the fear of dying Amy and Jane has is contagious, and both of them are now infected.
Jason and Susan are then infected while cleaning after the party, as they end up passing the fear onto their daughter.
At a hospital, Brian kills his father by interrupting his life support systems, upon which Tilly reveals she was simply waiting for the death in order to break up with him.
Jane goes to a doctor, who initially wants to refer her to a psychologist.
Amy goes for a ride in a dune buggy with a driver, during which she recalls a time that she and her boyfriend Craig went to Craig's brother's vacation house for a weekend.
During the weekend, the two order pizza, and it is implied that Craig became infected by the pizza delivery driver.
After the ride, Amy passes the fear onto the dune buggy driver, before the two briefly attempt to make out, before giving up.
Back at the doctor's office, Jane passes the fear onto the doctor, who has a breakdown before leaving to be with his wife.
Jane returns home and begins communicating with the bacteria she sees under the microscope in an attempt to calm herself, before seeing something enter her home that she asks "is this how it ends?"
Amy returns to the vacation home to find that Craig has died by suicide.
The next morning, Jason and Susan discuss what they believe will be their final day, and agree to not wake their daughter so she can pass away in her sleep.
Jane then wanders into the home of two young women, Sky and Erin, who seem unfazed by Jane's bloodied appearance, before revealing they both have the sickness as well.
Jane asks to use the pool, and begins swimming as her blood soaks the water.
Sky and Erin talk casually about what they will miss when they are dead.
Amy then visits a leather shop, and begins asking questions about custom work, eventually asking about what they could do with "a mammal".
Amy begins tearing up as the employee describes the process, before jolting awake, finding herself lying on some rocks.
She begins whispering to herself, going between "it's okay" and "I'm not okay", and gently humming.

5505921.title: Untamed (film)
synopsis: The tale unfurls within the somber brick walls of Pine Ridge Secondary School, a place commanded by the domineering Mr. Bennett who has an unyielding aura of utter dedication ingrained from years of shaping young minds.

Contrasting his usually severe teaching techniques with a ripple of excitement, Mr. Bennett adorns the blackboard with an innovative itinerary – a field trip to the scarcely visited and wildly enchanting Sundridge Forest Reserve.
On the day of the trip, students of disparate personality types mount the glossy yellow school bus.
Upon arrival, their exhilarating exploration commences.
Sundridge Forest Reserve, a vast ecosystem of towering oaks and crowd-reaching firs, beacons them closer with a charm that whispers of untouched nature.
As they delve deeper into the heart of the forest, a hidden attraction unveils itself - a clandestine cavern exuding an irresistible aura of secrecy.

Overcoming initial apprehensions, they daringly venture inside, only for a curious poke to trigger a rusty, moss-engulfed iron lever, the proceeding rumble reverberating through the cavern floor like an earthquake.
As the after-tremors dwindle, unkempt stones reveal the presence of an ancient, dormant spirit liberated from its impenetrable silence after centuries.

Back at the campsite, the once serene environment undergoes unnerving transformations- eerie sounds tear through the quietude, shadows flit between trees bizarrely, and mundane objects appear to dance under the spell of invisible puppeteers.

The tranquil predictability of the forest gives way to dread as unexplainable bizarre behaviors pepper their actions— sudden outbursts of unchecked anger, paralyzing episodes of inexplicable fears and an unsettling shrunken avoidance of daylight.
Startled by the escalating oddities, Mr. Bennett undertakes a mission to unravel the mysteries infringing upon their trip.

Studying the shroud of dark legacies woven throughout local history, Mr. Bennett stumbles across a collection of yellowed newspaper articles, steeped in the unsettling past of the forest and its intricate bond with Native American narratives.
Hours of painstakingly detailed research reveal the malign identity of Algon, a prehistoric menace notorious for employing human vessels to transform them into ferocious beings.
As the tranquil façade of nature succumbs to horror, the first affected student grotesquely shifts form, heralding the opening act of a chilling onslaught against oblivious comrades.
Mr. Bennett, arming himself with knowledge and eons-old survival techniques, crafts rudimentary weapons and provides survival lessons to his visibly shaken students.
Previously dormant pockets of the forest swirl into a whirlpool of chaos as the possessed students, now monstrous predators, besiege their former peers.
Outnumbered and faced with imminent danger, the surviving students scramble through the gnarled tree roots and shadowed clearings of the moonlit forest, seeking an elusive sanctuary.
Ceremonial chants echo in the crisp air as Mr. Bennett unearths an ancient manuscript whose hand-etched details ensnare a ray of hope—the outline of a shamanic ritual designed to imprison Algon.
The ritual's prerequisite- unwavering unity, poses a formidable challenge given the state of panic and exhaustion that the survivors are grappling with.
Amidst the fog of impending doom, the scattered students rely on their unique abilities.
The football captain, leveraging his physical strength for defense, the geek employing his encyclopedic knowledge to unravel the ritual and the stoic outsider inspiring unity.
Overcoming their monstrous peers laying in ambush, the terrified students execute the shamanic ritual.
They form a steadfast circle, pronouncing the archaic bans of incantation with resonating conviction.
Evoking the banishment of Algon renews a brief aura of relief and triumph.
The first rays of dawn unveil weary, yet resilient faces.
Their harrowing experience fostered an unanticipated bond, a camaraderie forged in the crucible of survival.
A disheveled group of rescuers, alerted by the students' unsettling disappearance, reach them amidst the sprawling wilderness just as dawn paints the sky in hopeful hues.
On their way out of the forest, a camera's zoom lens unearths a haunting omen—a dismembered doll from their ritual.
A sign that not all remnants of the entity were expelled.

Serving a potent dose of gripping suspense in the concluding scene, the frame zooms onto a rescuer's seemingly benign smile revealing menacing fiery eyes, foreboding the impending peril and tersely hinting towards the sequel.

70425144.title: Unhuman (film)
synopsis: Evanston Hill High School teacher Mr. Lorenzo supervises as students board a bus for a field trip.
Ever, an average girl with low self-esteem, boards with her best friend Tamra.

Other students include Randall and Steven, two bullied loners who harbor crushes on Tamra and Ever; Danny, a jock; Hunt, Danny's best friend; Jacey, Danny's girlfriend; overweight outcast Ryan; and nerdy girl Candice.
A sudden burst of blood on the windshield causes the driver, Wayne, to crash the bus in a forest.
An emergency radio broadcast warns of a nearby chemical attack.
A metalhead who appears to be a mutated zombie, later revealed to be a vengeful burnout named Chip, enters the bus and savagely mauls Lorenzo.
In the ensuing commotion, Ever, Tamra, Randall, Steven, Danny, Hunt, and Jacey escape into the woods and seek safety in an abandoned building.
Ryan joins them later.
Meanwhile, Chip attacks Candice and others back on the bus.
Ever attempts to help Candice when she tries to join everyone in the building, but the other students deem rescuing her too risky, so they let Chip attack Candice again.
Wayne, having seemingly mutated into a zombie like Chip, attacks everyone inside.
Classmates who were also apparently transformed capture Hunt.
Ever, Tamra, Randall, Steven, Danny, Jacey, and Ryan regroup in a room where they find mannequins dressed to resemble them, realizing someone has specifically targeted all of them.
Wayne suddenly attacks again, but Randall beats him.
Danny begins transforming after being stabbed with something during the commotion.
Wayne rises to tackle Danny through a window onto the ground outside.
Initially appearing dead, Danny surprisingly contorts and runs off.
Ever leaves Tamra behind after they argue about Tamra ignoring their friendship in favor of aligning with the "jocks".
Ever and Steven return to the bus to look for a phone, although Ever becomes distracted by the radio, discovering that the emergency broadcast was actually a tape recording.
Steven apologetically injects Ever from behind with a syringe.
Before passing out, Ever sees Randall join Steven.
A flashback shows that weeks earlier, Randall enlisted Steven for a scheme modeled after "Scared Straight!"
where they would stage a zombie attack to get revenge on their bullies while looking like heroes to Tamra and Ever.
Wayne volunteers, while ex-con and former student, Chip creates a dangerous drug to make people behave like zombies.
Back in the present, Randall brings Steven back to the building to check on the students they injected and took captive, including Danny and Hunt.
Meanwhile, Ever gathers enough strength to use a boom box to beat Chip.
Tamra finds Randall, who lies that zombies killed Ever.
After Steven secretly injects the captive students with more of Chip's drug, Randall arms Tamra, Ryan, and Jacey with weapons as he rallies them to kill their supposedly transformed classmates.
Ever suddenly interrupts to tell everyone the truth about Randall and Steven's plot.
Tamra hits Randall, who inadvertently reveals a vanity mural he previously painted that depicts him and Steven as mythic heroes saving Tamra and Ever from zombified bullies.
With the secret now fully exposed, Ever's allies rescue Danny and lock Steven in a cage with Hunt and the other ravenous "zombies".
Everyone then fights with Randall, who gravely wounds Danny, as Ever uses a makeshift Freddy Krueger glove, that Chip created, to stab Randall with several syringes of the drug.
Randall reforms as a "zombie".
Tamra, Jacey, Candice, and another rescued young woman named Juniper team up to take Randall down, with Ever finishing him off.
Hours later, Wayne, Chip, Randall, and Steven are all taken captive.
The bullies and outcasts bond, with Ever and Tamra reconciling.
After everyone boards the bus to leave, they discover Mr. Lorenzo is still alive.
Weeks later, PTA worker Ms. Operative visits Randall and Steven in prison, explaining that the PTA is bringing back the "Scared Straight" program, and invites them to be the masterminds.

91947428.title: Brooklyn Bootlace
synopsis: Ed, a chronically overworked 25-year-old graphic designer, spent his taxing days in "Ropes", an old-world shoe boutique owned by his family.
His mother, a vibrant and creative woman, had devoted her life to fostering "Ropes".
Unfortunately, her unexpected passing struck the family hard and the responsibility of maintaining "Ropes" and its charm fell on Ed's reluctant shoulders.
Ted, Ed’s broad-shouldered stepfather and a retired Wall Street executive, taking advantage of his past experiences, observed from a distance.
He complained continually about dwindling profits yet offered little assistance, leaving Ed to labor till midnight, under the harsh shop lights.
Meanwhile, Zack and Sam, Ed's tech-obsessed stepbrothers, prioritized screen time over responsibilities, leaving their copy of the chore list untouched.
As Ed parts the sea of frustration and grief, Rosie comes like a breath of fresh air.
One gloomy Saturday, while rummaging through the attic filled with forgotten relics and cobwebs, Ed accidentally dislodges a cardboard box marked with his mother’s initials.
Hidden among sketchbooks and Polaroids depicting simpler times, Ed unearthed an intriguing pair of silver bootlaces.
Woven into the sparkling threads was a cryptic message insinuating hidden magical powers.

Embracing the absurdity of it all, Ed discovered amusement in channeling each shoes's innate spirit, from a burly Wild West cowboy to an extravagant 70s rockstar, each transformation eliciting chuckles from Ed.
Meanwhile, Ted hatched a cold scheme to sell "Ropes" to Charles Snobbish, a ruthless shoe tycoon infamous for gobbling up local boutiques for his remorseless corporate empire.
The plan was devoid of sentiment, focusing solely on the monetary gain.
It threatened to erode Ed's poignant memories of his mother's hard-earned legacy.
Word spread throughout the borough, and whispers of the pending sale found their way to Ed, leaving him dismayed.
Reignited by determination, he resolved to save "Ropes" with the only weapon he had: the magical, personality-altering bootlaces.
Adopting a range of outlandish personas, Ed led a comedic campaign of disruption against the looming corporate takeover.
On the fated day, the magic bootlaces suddenly lost all their gleam.
This left Ed stuck midway, totally powerless.
The abrupt cessation of his transformation resulted in a spectacle that left Ted reeling backwards in hilarity.

However, laughter gave way to an explosive argument, revealing the deeply buried justification behind Ted's decision - ensuring a financially secure future for his screen-obsessed sons, elucidating his misguided approach.
The revelation hit Ed hard, prompting self-reflection that led to regret and the realization of his own biases.
He also comprehended the significant impact his misuse of the magic bootlaces had caused.
Feeling remorseful, Ed came clean about his magical mishaps and the impending crisis to Rosie and his stepbrothers.
They pledged their support.
Together, they strategized to scuttle Snobbish’s imminent takeover by introducing a series of fabricated operational hurdles.
Amidst a series of slapstick misadventures, they succeeded in planting doubts about the profitability of "Ropes" within Snobbish's corporate mind.
Cornered and uncertain, Ted was forced to acknowledge the depth of Ed's passion for the store and began to second guess his decision to sell "Ropes".
Gulping down his pride, Ted backed out of the deal with Snobbish, promising to search for alternative financial solutions that wouldn't compromise the family legacy.
In an unexpected turn of events, Ted begrudgingly accepted Ed's unwavering devotion to "Ropes".
He promised to involve Ed in future business decisions and to invest more time in improving the store himself.
