Amidst this small hub of tranquillity, thrives a locally admired auto repair shop, ‘Johnson and Sons’ that stands testament to the relentless hard work of the tight-knit Johnson clan.
John, their eldest son, a robust young man, frequently emerges from the shop's cloud of spew and smoke, his face smeared in soot, lighting up with an infectious cheer.
John’s commitment to his family business is unwavering, yet inside him, he nurtures a secret aspiration of devoting himself to the church as a clergyman.
This yearning does not go unnoticed by Reverend Daniels, the town's seasoned venerable priest, who graciously offers to mentor John in his spiritual journey.
Patiently, the Reverend guides John in preparing for the entrance of the famed seminary, 'The Theological Seminary of Saint Stephen’ nestled off the beaten path in Southern California.
Over the familiar ambiance of an evening family dinner, his parents, although visibly anxious, express their apprehensions about their eldest son's momentous decision.
The looming prospect of their son traversing the country alone and the accompanying financial hurdles unnerves them.
Their worries, however, don't overpower their understanding of John’s noble aspiration.
Choosing to support their son despite their fears, they lend him their unwavering support, silently praying for their son's valiant undertakings.
Underneath the diamond-studded Ohio sky, John bades an emotional goodbye to his childhood sweetheart, Sarah.
Her radiant eyes well up with tears as she assures him of her unwavering devotion and promise of his homecoming.
Appropriately dressed, with his mother's lovingly prepared lunch, John embarks on his transformative journey on a bright cool morning, treading an unknown path with equal parts excitement and unease.
Ready to take his first step towards his dream, John boards the Greyhound bus, stationed on the town's outskirts, destined to transport him to the sun-soaked Californian shores.
With his suitcase symbolizing his dreams and a Bible from Reverend Daniels in honor of his divine quest, John steps onto the bus.
The journey to his future sees him sharing stories and experiences with a myriad of co-passengers, each tale challenging his perspective and redefining his belief in humanity, faith, and ambition.
Upon his arrival at the respected Seminary, John finds himself immersed in an academic culture that is strikingly different from anything he has experienced before.
With the combined pressure of his new environment, the homesickness, and his determination to stand by his faith, John finds himself fighting an uphill battle.
Alone in his small, sparsely decorated dorm room, an overwhelmed John ponders his beliefs, often revisiting his conversations with Reverend Daniels.
Slowly but surely, John reignites his determination aligning himself to his faith journey and vowing to prove his worth by excelling in his theological pursuits.
However, a disturbing revelation throws a wrench in his peaceful academic life.
Through a seemingly accidental encounter, he stumbles upon systemic financial fraud ingrained within the institute.
The heavy realization becomes a burden too potent to ignore and inconceivably holds the power to uproot his dreams.
Caught in the intricate web of self-preservation and the morally righteous path, he finds himself at the crossroads of a critical decision.
A meditative walk down memory lane transports John back to his beloved hometown church and the insightful sermons of Reverend Daniels that guide him towards his verdict.
Holding steadfast to his moral calling, John chooses to expose the corruption, symbolizing his indefatigable faith and inherent righteousness.
The damning evidence he presents shakes the Seminary board to its very core, sparking ripples of shock and trepidation within the assembly.
As the reality of his revelations take hold, John finds himself in the eye of the storm, facing disciplinary censure and the possible expulsion from the Seminary.
Just as the storm seems its strongest, the wealthy, influential trustee of the Seminary steps in, shielding him from the impending consequences out of admirations for John's courage.
The benefactor’s unexpected intervention retains John's place at the seminary, ensuring his academic journey continues unhampered.
The shocking exposure of financial misconduct leads to a top-down overhaul in the Seminary's management, driving significant change spurred by John's courage.
Navigating these trials unscathed, John emerges victorious, graduating with flying colors, and his commitment to truth earns him accolades.
Upon his return to Rayfield, he is welcomed as a hometown hero, his stirring journey an inspiration to his townsfolk, and looked upon as a beacon of moral strength and religious guidance.
Acknowledging his spiritual journey, Reverend Daniels offers John the sacred responsibility of leading their town's church as the newly ordained Pastor.
Praised and welcomed by the townsfolk, they anticipate John's divine leadership with joy and fervor.
Amid the widespread celebrations, Sarah looks on at John with pride-filled eyes, her heart swelling with love, and a promise fulfilled.
Their reunion encapsulates resurfaced love and mutual respect, strengthened by the time spent apart and John’s ordeal.
Holding the Bible gifted from Reverend Daniels at the start of his spiritual quest, John mounts the church pulpit he always dreamed of gracing.
With his first sermon, he shares an impromptu account of his journey, his voice echoing along with the church aisles, flooding the hearts of his listeners with a renewed sense of faith and hope.
His candid anecdotes, life lessons, and battles faced strike a chord with the congregation, infusing them with a newfound appreciation of faith, humanity and resilience.
Under his leadership, Rayfield starts to radiate a spiritual enlightenment, its ordinary life brimming with new perspectives and rich nuances.
Throughout his journey, Sarah remains his pillar of strength, supporting him through thick and thin, reforging their bond further.
John cherished his trials as invaluable aid in his spiritual evolution, understanding them as stepping stones to his glorious destiny.

John cherished his trials as invaluable aid in his spiritual evolution, understanding them as stepping stones to his glorious destiny.
We leave John basking in the comforting glow of his beloved church, the conclusion of our tale resonating with feelings of completion and fulfilment.

61588091.title: I Still Believe (film)
synopsis: In Lafayette, Indiana, in September 1999, Jeremy Camp departs for Calvary Chapel College in Murrieta, California.

The night of his arrival, he goes to a concert of Canadian Christian band, the Kry, where he meets the lead singer, Jean-Luc LaJoie, who becomes fast friends with Jeremy, who turns to him for musical advice.
After the concert, Jeremy meets Melissa Henning, a fellow student at his school, and friend of Jean-Luc, who loves Melissa, but she does not feel the same.
Jeremy and Melissa get to know each other, and quickly begin dating, causing a rift among the three.
As a result, Melissa ends her relationship with Jeremy.
Jeremy goes back to his family's home in Indiana for Christmas break.
A few days after Christmas, he receives a phone call from Jean-Luc, saying that Melissa is sick, and asks Jeremy to come back to California.
Upon his arrival, Jeremy visits Melissa in the hospital, who tells him that she has been diagnosed with Stage 3C ovarian cancer spread to her liver.
She also tells Jeremy that she loves him.
He says the same, proposes and Melissa accepts.
During this time, Jeremy begins to make a name for himself as a Christian singer-songwriter.
At one point, when Melissa is about to have an MRI.
Melissa learns that the cancer has spread to her ovaries, so she needs a hysterectomy.
She wakes up to Jeremy after the surgery was supposed to happen, who tells her the surgery was canceled as she is now cancer-free.
Six months later, Jeremy and Melissa marry.
Everything seems perfect until after their honeymoon, until she wakes up in pain.
Jeremy takes her to the hospital, where they find out her cancer has returned, and that nothing more can be done for her.
As Melissa grows weaker, Jeremy begins to question his faith in God.
In the hospital, Jeremy sings a song he wrote ("Walk by Faith") during their honeymoon.
Melissa passes shortly after.
Jeremy becomes angry at God, and chooses to abandon his musical career, smashing his guitar until it breaks.
Inside the guitar, Jeremy finds a note Melissa left for him to find after her death, telling him that suffering does not damage faith, but strengthens it.
Her parting words encourage him to continue writing songs.
Two years later, Jeremy performs a song he wrote after Melissa's death ("I Still Believe") about his suffering, but eventually restored faith.
After the concert, he meets a woman named Adrienne, who tells Jeremy that she lost someone close to her, and she was angry at God, and his songs changed her life.
Jeremy promises to share Melissa's story, believing that God will use it to change lives.
The credits reveal that Jeremy and Adrienne got married in 2003, and have three children.

61027838.title: Paleontica: A Tale of Lyme Regis
synopsis: Lyme Regis, a picturesque seaside town in Dorset, serves as a backdrop for our story, home to young Annie, an effervescent girl who held a unique fascination for all things marine life.
With a fondness for fossils that surpassed the conventional for her tender age, she was drawn perpetually to explore, investigate, and collect such marine remnants.
Annie lived with her widowed mother, Belinda, who was as strong-spirited as they come.
Over the years, however, Belinda's health had started to deteriorate due to an inexplicable ailment.
To manage their livelihood and to fund Belinda's treatment, mother and daughter ran a small trinket store on the bustling main street.
Here, they sold an assortment of sea curios, aged maps, and exotic seashells that brought to life the vibrant maritime soul of Lyme Regis.
One day, a twist in their otherwise normal life came in the form of an esteemed geologist, Mr. Hamilton.
The renowned individual decided to leave behind the noisy streets of London to investigate the abundant Jurassic fossils prevalent in Lyme Regis.

During a chance walk-in to the trinket store, Hamilton was taken aback by the depth of Annie's understanding of fossils, the species they belonged to, and their geological eras, an understanding far greater than what one would expect from a girl her age.

Surprised and intrigued by her innate talent, Hamilton offered Annie an unheard-of opportunity: to assist him on an expansive fossil excavation project on the cliffs neighboring the town - a proposition that immensely excites Annie.
However, just as Annie's dreams began soaring, they were doused by mother Belinda's rapidly failing health.
The uncertain clouds of sorrow cast a shadow on Annie's initial fossil discovery victories.
Annie found herself at a crossroads.
On one hand, she was being pulled into the realm of her dreams, her passion for fossils.
On the other hand, her mother's deteriorating condition demanded her attention and care.

Unable to resist the allure of unearthing the earth's ancient secrets, Annie decided to uphold her commitment to Hamilton, keeping her worried thoughts at bay to sustain her blooming enthusiasm for paleontology.
As Annie started to dig deeper into the cliffy realms, she and Hamilton stumbled upon an astonishing discovery — a colossal fossil, seamlessly embraced by the stony facades of the cliff.
This fossil, a detailed artifact that seemed to be from an era unknown to them, foretold groundbreaking revelations about Lyme Regis' prehistoric past.
Amidst the elation of the extraordinary discovery, Annie was weighed down by guilt and worry as her mother's health continued to worsen with each passing day.
To assist with the highly skilled and delicate task of unearthing the intricate fossil, they enlisted the help of Samuel, a local ivory-carver who was renowned for his craft.
Working close together, Annie and Samuel discovered a shared passion for prehistory that gradually blossomed into a romantic bond.
Their companionship during long days at the excavation site evolved into an unexpected love affair.
This newfound love, however, ruffled Mr. Hamilton, who became fearful of losing both his prestige and Annie, whom he had come to desire.
He feared that his renowned status as a prominent geologist was in jeopardy.
Blinded by jealousy, Hamilton proposed a rushed marriage to Annie, seeking to assert his control over her and her unique talent.
He aimed to continue reaping the benefits of her phenomenal work without having his authority undermined.
But Annie, recognizing Hamilton's deceit and validating her growing bond with Samuel, vehemently rejected Hamilton’s proposal, standing up for her own worth and happiness.
The rejection wounded Hamilton's pride, propelling him to hatch a treacherous plan to clandestinely steal the fossil and claim sole credit for the discovery.
Then, under the cover of the dark, Hamilton attempted to enact his plan, sneaking into the excavation site to collect the fossil.
Fortunately, Samuel and Annie, who had been working late, caught Hamilton red-handed in the middle of his theft.
The still night was rent by the altercation that ensued, echoing their scathing accusations against Hamilton.
Pinned under the weight of his own actions, Hamilton was forced to abandon his plans, making a disgraced exit from Lyme Regis without the fossil.
In the midst of this upheaval, unexpectedly, Annie received unsettling news about her mother's condition, now critical than ever.
Overcome with anxiety, she rushed homeward, hoping to stand by her mother's side during these testing times.
There, in their humble abode, a fading Belinda urged her daughter to pursue her extraordinary work without any guilt, assuring her that it filled her with immense pride.
With this final whisper of love and encouragement, Belinda drew her last breath, her spirit finally freed from the mortal world.
With Belinda's demise, news of Annie's exceptional marine find reached renowned geologists in London who decided to personally meet this extraordinary girl who had made such a remarkable discovery.
As the solemn ceremony of Belinda’s funeral took place, these geologists arrived at Lyme Regis, their curiosity piqued by the groundbreaking fossil find.
The expert team sincerely appreciated Annie's unprecedented diligence and her remarkable findings in the field of geology, commending her for her insights and determination.
Impressed by her remarkable skill and passion, they offered her a golden opportunity to expand her horizons by inviting her to study at the leading geoscience institute in London.
However, taking a stand that would have made her mother proud, Annie declined the prestigious offer with grace, choosing to honour Belinda's wishes by continuing her extraordinary work in Lyme Regis.
Their modest trinket store underwent a transformation, not just serving as a maritime curio shop, but also standing as a beacon of dedication and homage to her late mother.
Amidst these turning tides, Annie and Samuel’s bond deepened.
Their shared expertise, their deep-seated love, and their common adversaries laid the foundation for a relationship of support, trust, and companionship.
Navigating through such a whirlwind, Annie remained rooted in her passion for paleontology.
Together with Samuel, she aptly handled the trinket store, which gradually became a popular spot among locals and visitors to Lyme Regis due to their infectious enthusiasm for prehistory.

Amid the triumphs and trials, their love story beautifully unfolded, painting a narrative of shared victories, admiration, perseverance, and a love that, against all odds, found its roots amid adversity.
Lyme Regis, the harboring domain for their shared passion and the nurturing grounds for their deep-seated love, became their home.
Standing strong amidst societal pressures and adversities, they ushered a new horizon of paleontological research in Lyme Regis with their unwavering dedication and expertise.

60122575.title: Ammonite (film)
synopsis: In the 1840s, fossil collector Mary Anning lives with her ailing mother Molly, who helps Mary run a small shop in Lyme Regis, Dorset.
Mary spends the early mornings on the beach at low tide in search of fossils for the shop, with tiny ammonites being her most common find.
When she returns, she helps her mother wash and polish a collection of eight animal figurines.
One day, geologist Roderick Murchison visits Mary's shop with his wife, Charlotte.
He expresses admiration for Mary's work and offers to pay her for a guided trip to the shore where he can learn from Mary about fossil collecting.
While initially antagonistic, Mary accepts his offer.
That night in their room at the Three Cups Hotel, Roderick treats Charlotte coldly, rebuffing her sexual advances and saying that now is not the time to have another baby.
Roderick returns from his morning trip with Mary and finds Charlotte confined to her bed in a depressed state.
He returns to Mary's shop and reveals that Charlotte has been sent to Lyme Regis in order to convalesce, and entrusts her to Mary's care as he will be departing to Europe for four to six weeks.
Mary reluctantly agrees, not wanting to pass up the money.
Charlotte begins going out with Mary on her morning beach trips.
After bathing in the ocean as part of her rehabilitation, Charlotte falls ill with a high fever.
Her physician, Dr. Lieberson, prescribes bed rest and assigns Mary to be her bedside nurse.
Mary visits her friend Elizabeth Philpot, from whom she purchases a jar of salve to aid Charlotte's recovery.
Mary refuses Elizabeth's friendly offer to come in for a visit.
Charlotte quickly recovers, and from then on accompanies Mary on more outings and tries to help with domestic chores.
Together with Mary, she is able to construct a mirror frame made of cowries.
Saddened by her own failed attempts to have a baby, Charlotte learns that the figurines which Molly cleans every day represent her eight deceased children.
Dr. Lieberson visits the shop and invites Mary to an evening recital.
Mary accepts but insists on bringing Charlotte as well, whom she believes has made a full recovery.
That night, Charlotte meets and mingles with the townsfolk as an overwhelmed and jealous Mary smokes outside in the rain while watching through the window.
They watch a magic lantern show set to music before Mary leaves and returns home during the rainstorm.
Charlotte arrives soon after and finds Mary writing a romantic poem in her journal.
Using the boards from a beached boat, Mary and Charlotte transfer a large rock to the shop.
Inside, they find the fossil of an Ichthyosaur similar to one which Mary found when she was aged 11 and sent to the British Museum.
As they clean Mary's tools in preparation before going to bed, Charlotte kisses Mary goodnight; this inflames their attraction to one another, and they engage in oral sex.
Their relationship blossoms, as they swim in the sea and share their meals.
A letter arrives from Roderick, instructing Charlotte to return to London.
Distraught, Charlotte and Mary have passionate sex the night before Charlotte's departure.
Sometime later, Molly suffers a fall at home and dies soon afterwards.
Elizabeth visits the depressed Mary to express her condolences.
She encourages Mary to not abandon her relationship with Charlotte, as Mary did with their own romantic relationship after the death of Mary's father.
Mary receives a letter from Charlotte asking her to come to London.
Upon arriving at the Murchison house, Mary sees one of her large ammonite fossils on display in a glass cabinet.
Charlotte takes Mary upstairs, where she shows Mary a fully furnished bedroom ready for her to move into.
Perturbed, Mary leaves after accusing Charlotte of not respecting her life, stating she will not become an ornament for Charlotte to display in a "gilded cage."
At the British Museum, Mary makes her way through the galleries.
She finds the exhibit case containing her original Ichthyosaurus but sees that it makes no mention of her.
Charlotte arrives dressed in clothes similar to Mary's, and the two women gaze at each other through the glass.

45198657.title: Kansas O'Brien
synopsis: Our tale commences with John, a diligent wheat farmer in the heartland of Kansas.
As the sun peeks over the horizon, he awakes from his slumber and starts his day.
With nothing but sheer determination and grit, John ensures the smooth operation of his revered century-old farm, inherited from his forefathers.
Lucas, his ten-year-old son, watches his father from a distance, the twinkling admiration in his eyes reflecting the solitude endured by John in his daily grind.
The narrative unfolds showcasing the bond between father and son.
John, on many occasions, imparts his farming wisdom to Lucas, teaching him basic chores like planting wheat seeds and mending fences.
As the night approaches, the neighboring farm stirs with anticipation.
Bob, John's lone sibling, rolls into the driveway in his vintage pick-up truck, signaling the arrival of their customary Sunday dinner.
Amid these scenes, flashes of a happy past reveal the poignant loss of their beloved Mary - John's wife and Bob's sister.
Her untimely demise left a gaping hole in their lives, resonating in the silence that surrounds her memory.
Their eyes fix on her faded portrait, hanging limply on the farmhouse wall.
The void created by her departure is palpable, echoing in the silence of their reminiscence.
John's struggle with single parenthood surfaces, as he juggles between his duties at the 200-acre farm and raising an ever-inquisitive Lucas.
Their rhythmic life is interrupted by a fierce snowstorm.
Its fury uproots and damages John's farm infrastructure, killing three of his beloved cattle in its wake.
Seeing his brother's plight, Bob offers his assistance, sharing his agricultural machinery.
Meanwhile, an urban woman named Emily arrives at the Kansas Colony.
Having recently inherited her late father’s 50-acre plot adjacent to John’s farm, she finds herself out of her element.
A first encounter occurs under strained circumstances, as her cattle accidentally intrude onto John's field.
John, though initially irked, extends his hand, teaching Emily the tricks of the trade - how to milk cows and raise corn on her newfound property.
The increased interaction with Emily sparks jealousy in Lucas.
He feels neglected as his father recedes into the newfound companionship.
Emily, on the other hand, nurtures a blossoming affection for John.
When news of an impending mega snowstorm breaks, Bob suggests pooling their resources to ensure survival in the face of this new hurdle.
Tensions mount within the household on the eve of the storm, exacerbated by Emily's sudden presence and the looming natural disaster.
The storm arrives with full fury.
John, Emily, and Bob find themselves huddled together in the cellar of John’s farmhouse, battling the brutal cold and imminent threat of their impending doom.
Lucas, blindsided by jealousy and insecurity, breaks down, shedding tears about his father's perceived indifference towards him.
In a fit of rage and confusion, Lucas vanishes into the violent storm, sending waves of panic through John.
Despite Emily and Bob’s protests, they join John in his desperate quest to find Lucas in the lethal storm.
Amidst the raging blizzard, Emily and Bob express their deep admiration for John’s unwavering dedication to his son.
The dramatic climax parallels the storm's intensity as their fears, vulnerabilities, and internal conflicts converge in their mission to rescue Lucas.
The tension dissipates slightly when they find Lucas, unconscious but breathing, huddled near an old, abandoned barn in the storm's eye.
The storm cripples the landscape as it withdraws, leaving the group united by their shared ordeal amidst a wreckage of weather-beaten infrastructure.
As they carry Lucas back to their damaged farmhouse, their differences seem insignificant.
The aftermath that follows provides opportunities for John, Emily, Lucas, and Bob to form unexpected bonds amidst the wreckage of what was once their thriving farmlands.
In the wake of the calamity, Lucas comes around to understanding Emily's affection for his father.
He sees her as an integral part of their small family, and a worthy companion for his widowed father.
Their shared journey of resilience, reconciliation, and remarkable transformation is a testament to their endurance and unity.
Looking beyond their haunting pasts, the newfound family unit steps towards a future, defined by collective strength and tenacity.
As they work with renewed vigor towards resurrecting their barns and fields, they also rebuild their emotional bonds.
They pledge to weather any future storms, united in their mission of collective healing.
The memories of the storm fade in time, now replaced by the newfound comfort of their extended family.
The old farmhouse, despite its battered walls, serves as a testament to their indomitable spirit and triumph over adversity.

66385223.title: Old Henry
synopsis: Widower Henry McCarty and his son Wyatt live on a farm in Oklahoma Territory in 1906 near Henry's brother-in-law Al.
After Henry and Wyatt find a lost horse with blood on the saddle, Henry locates its owner, a near-dead man named Curry.
Next to Curry is a pistol and a satchel full of money.
Henry wants no part of it and gets on his horse to leave the man be.
But he changes his mind and brings the unconscious Curry and the money back to the farm to treat his wounds.
Henry interrogates Curry, who claims to be a lawman and the sole survivor of a posse sent after a gang of outlaws.
He asks for help keeping the outlaws from retrieving the money he managed to steal from them.
While his father goes to town for help, Wyatt secretly takes Curry's gun to practice shooting.
Curry slips free and tries to wrestle back the gun, but Henry suddenly appears and overpowers him.
Henry reveals that he turned back after spotting three men investigating the spot where he first found Curry.
The trio, wearing sheriff's badges and led by a man named Sam Ketchum, come to the farm in search of Curry.
They claim that Curry is the real outlaw but arouse Henry's suspicions when Ketchum begins asking questions about Henry's own identity and family.
Henry does not give up Curry, and the men leave after a tense standoff.
That evening, Henry has a conversation with Curry in which the latter reveals detailed knowledge of people known to Henry, which convinces Henry to undo some of his restraints.
Curry tells of his experiences as a young ranch hand who witnessed the death of Billy the Kid.
One of Ketchum's men, Duggan, tries to sneak under the house so he can shoot Henry from below.
Henry spots him, forces Duggan out with a shotgun, and strangles him to death while Wyatt watches.
The next morning, Ketchum returns with his gang.
Curry encourages Henry to surrender and turn him over, arguing that they should not die for his sake.
However, Ketchum then takes Al as a hostage and, when Henry refuses to surrender, shoots him in cold blood.
After stopping his son from running outside and getting killed, Henry goes into his room and arms himself with several guns, telling Wyatt "Keep your damn head down, you'll be alright".
Curry recognizes the phrase as something Billy the Kid said to him years ago and realizes that Henry is in fact Billy the Kid, who faked his own death with the help of a sympathetic Pat Garrett.
Henry pretends to surrender before shooting Ketchum in the face, gunning down several men, and slipping out the back door of his farmhouse.
While Curry and Wyatt hold off the remaining gang members, Henry stealthily eliminates the gang until only Stilwell, the gang's tracker, is left.
Stilwell tosses his guns and tries to use his throwing knife, but Henry shoots it out of his hand and then shoots him through his eye.
Henry suddenly comes under fire as Ketchum emerges, revealing that the shot only mangled his cheek.
Both men chase and shoot at each other until Ketchum runs out of bullets, with Henry using his last shot to blow the outlaw's head off.
Returning to the house, Henry is about to bandage up the injured Curry when he spots a brand on his arm used for marking criminals.
Curry shoots Henry in the stomach, admitting that he was in fact a lawman, but sold out his colleagues so Ketchum's gang could impersonate them and steal the money.
He was injured only because he tried to double-cross Ketchum.
Curry apologizes but says that the chance to be the man who killed Billy the Kid is too much for him to resist.
Wyatt overhears all this, loads his father's shotgun, and kills Curry before he can finish off Henry.
Wyatt tries to help his father, but Henry tells him that it is too late.

Henry speaks earnestly to his son, telling him that the world is changing, and Henry has no place in it anymore but that he hoped his son would now find a place for himself after teaching him to be an honest man.
He dies in Wyatt's arms.
Wyatt buries his father next to his mother and leaves the farm along with the gang's cash, two horses, and their few possessions.

17087078.title: Affirmative Day
synopsis: At the heart of bustling Boston is the vibrant and multi-dimensional Johnson family.

It consists of Rachel, an ambitious executive at prestigious firm Goldman & Klein; Mark, a laid-back tech guru; and their three children – Liam, the sports enthusiast; Zoe, the fashion-savvy vlogger; and Jack, the cute, impish prankster.
Rachel exudes power and charisma in her tailored pencil skirts and sky-high heels.
Mark exhibits an entirely different temperament.
He's an unobtrusive tech genius, found generally in casual denims.
However, menacing clouds start to cover the sunny persona Rachel holds when she receives an encoded memo indicating impending layoffs.
This could pose a serious threat to her job.
Carrying the heavy load of looming financial pressure, Rachel decides to shield her family from the possible impending economic crisis.
Concurrently, Mark is grappling with his own shortcomings.
His pet project, a series of comedy sketches for YouTube, isn't doing as well as he'd anticipated.
In the middle of their routine chaos, they decide to pause and engage in what could be their unique tradition—a whimsical "yes day."
As the dreaded 'yes day' approaches, Rachel and Mark steel themselves for a day filled with their children's bizarre wishes.
From daybreak to twilight, they must comply with every request their kids make.
Filled with nervous-excitement, 'Yes day' commences, as Rachel and Mark reluctantly prepare to meet their kids' weird and wonderful demands.
On the other hand, Mark endures the hilariously embarrassing ordeal of an impromptu ballet performance, led by his daughter at their local dance studio.
Mark, being the amusing character that he is, decides to document these golden family moments and uploads them on his channel.
On a whim, they register for a talent show at the Boston City Hall, deciding to share their crazy 'yes day' adventures through a comical skit.
Their wacky show wins the audience's hearts.
Meanwhile, Mark's dormant YouTube channel takes a quantum leap in popularity as their 'yes day' videos become the talk of the town.
Inspired by Rachel's cheerful attitude and newfound town buzz, her boss commends her and offers a surprising promotion at Goldman & Klein, thereby diffusing her job-related stress.
As the curtains of the narrative start to draw, we see a transformed Johnson family.
Their bond is stronger, communication has improved, and their love has deepened.
Having developed a rare fondness for spontaneity and change, they begin planning again for the next year's ‘yes day’ extravaganza.

62038827.title: Yes Day
synopsis: Allison and Carlos Torres are married with three children: Katie, Nando, and Ellie.
When they first met, they were adventurous and said yes to everything.
However, once having children, they feel they must say no to protect them.
One evening, they are called into a parent-teacher conference at school where they discover Katie and Nando have both submitted homework calling their mom a dictator.
Allison expresses frustration that her children perceive her this way and tells Carlos that she feels he makes her play the role of "bad cop" with their children.

Mr. Deacon, a school employee, and father of six overhears and shares with them that he maintains order in his house by having a 'yes day' from time to time: one 24-hour period where the parents cannot say no, within reason.
Carlos and Allison present the idea to their family, telling them that if they don't get into trouble, do their chores, and keep their grades up, they can have a yes day as a reward.
Katie makes a wager with Allison that if her mom makes it through Yes Day, Katie will go to the music festival Fleek Fest with her mother.
If she doesn't make it, Katie will be allowed to go with a friend, Layla.
The children eventually manage to earn a yes day and put together a list of five activities for the day.

The first three are Ellie dressing her parents in crazy outfits and requests that they don't look at anything with a screen on it all day, ordering a massive $40 sundae that is free if they can eat it all in 30 minutes, that they successfully eat, going through a car wash with the windows down, and entering a capture the flag competition, where each family member leads a group; the goal is for one team to catch the others, throwing balloons filled with Kool-Aid at their opponents.
Allison wins the game for her team, winning the children's approval.
Carlos, however, is tempted to drop out of Yes Day, but ultimately decides he can't bear to disappoint his family.
The fourth event is a trip to Six Flags Magic Mountain.
When Katie steps away, Allison sees texts on her daughter's phone from Layla indicating she and Katie will be hanging out with older boys at Fleekfest.
Allison tells her that the wager is off and she's going to Fleekfest with her, not Layla.
Hurt, Katie storms off.
In an attempt to win a pink gorilla for Katie as an apology, Allison and Carlos get into a fight with another park-goer and are arrested.
The children sneak away.
Katie goes to Fleekfest with Layla but quickly becomes uncomfortable being alone with older boys, and her friend abandons her.
Nando stages a "nerd party" at the house as the final big event, but it quickly gets out of control when Ellie accidentally sets off a foam explosion inside the house that was meant for the backyard.
Meanwhile, Katie's phone dies while trying to contact her siblings and she panics.
With help from H.E.R., who is performing at the event, Allison finds Katie and they reconcile.
H.E.R.
is moved and invites them on stage for a song.
Carlos arrives home and finally manages to be a disciplinarian, forcing the party to stop and the children to help with the cleanup.
As Yes Day draws to a close, Ellie makes one final request.
They all spend the night playing games as a family in a tent in the backyard, until Nando's foam bomb (having been flushed down the toilet) starts to fill up the house.
In a mid-credits scene, the Torres family and other players pelt Mr. Deacon with Kool-Aid balloons at the Capture the Flag field as revenge for suggesting Yes Day in the first place.

51912680.title: Coffee Love
synopsis: The opening scene of our film unfolds in the lively setting of an independently run downtown café, called "Coffee Love", where the heroine of our story, Emily, an effervescent and intriguing young woman, is observed perform her daily routine.
She prepares a complex latte order with the flawless skill of an accomplished expert.
As she meticulously pours the foam in a delicate flow, an intricate tree design materializes, giving evidence of her crafted proficiency and fervor for her work.
Emily's passion illustrates a clear picture; she indulges in her work with every ounce of her spirit.
She's the embodiment of joy, spreading positivity like an infectious disease and adding a magical touch to every drink she creates.
Whether it be a cappuccino, a latte, or a simple Americano, Emily brings a unique essence to each, captivating the customers.
Amid her harmonious café-life, unannounced, her amiable but scatterbrained father, James, steps into the café.
Much to Emily's surprise, he walks in arm in arm with Sam, a stylish woman who carries an aura of vitality and youthfulness, notably much younger than James.
While Emily wrestles with her emotions, Daniel, a bibliophile regular at "Coffee Love" secretly cherishes his feelings for her.
Gathering his strength to confess his affection towards Emily becomes his challenge of the day.
Touched by Emily's plight, Daniel plans an elaborate distraction.
He recruits the café's colorful cast of regular customers, hatching a plot of a fake love affair between Sam and George - a wannabe actor who frequents the café to use it as his unofficial work hub.
Though George hesitates initially, he finally relents.
He warms up to Daniel's plan, intrigued by the opportunity to flex his acting muscles that have been in hibernation for a while.
The elaborate hoax revolves around George penning an artificial love letter to Sam and a planned secret rendezvous at a nearby park.
The plot reaches its unexpected climax when James discovers the made-up love letter.
The forgotten letter triggers a chain of uproarious confusion, leading to a comic showdown between a clueless James and the falsely accused George.
Amid the comedic chaos and spilled coffee beans, Emily finds clarity.
She makes peace with her father’s relationship with Sam, acknowledging the unnecessary encroaching she was indulging in her father's romantic endeavors.
The confusion provides Daniel with the perfect opportunity to finally declare his feelings for Emily.
In a comedic twist of fate, he slips on the scattered coffee beans, landing face-to-face with Emily.
Among laughter and confusion, stuttering, he manages to mutter his confession of love for Emily, her blush and approving nod making it clear that the feelings are mutual.
Their shared confession, though clumsy, creates a heartwarming moment, culminating into a kiss beneath a shower of coffee beans, turning a disruptive day into something magical.
Meanwhile, James and Sam continue their free-spirited relationship, adding layers of love and hilarity to the café’s existing aura, making it even more beloved among the locals.
As the film reaches its end, we catch fleeting glimpses of Emily and Daniel sharing secret smiles and affectionate glances.
These intimate moments create a sense of understated satisfaction and wrap up the film on a heartening note.

62877295.title: Chick Fight
synopsis: Anna Wyncomb works in a coffee shop and her dad, Ed, has dated Chuck since her mom, Mary, died nine months ago.
One night, Anna and her best friend Charleen, a police officer, accidentally set the coffee shop on fire after enjoying a joint.
Now blaming herself for the incident and totally broke, Charleen takes Anna to the underground all-female fight club and introduces her to Bear, the manager and the referee of the fight club.

There, Charleen explains to Anna that the winning fighter puts a dollar bill on the wall with their name on it and the fight club serves as a safe haven for women, who want to cope with the problems of their lives.
Charleen persuades Anna that she must agree to fight in order to resolve her problems.
Anna reluctantly agrees and fights in her first bout but is easily knocked out.
Anna realizes that her mom founded the fight club and has fought several bouts, a secret that her mom kept from Anna her whole life, dying from cancer six months after her final fight.
Anna is then introduced to former boxing coach Jack Murphy, who now works in a restaurant at the beachside and agrees to train her.
She later meets Olivia, an undefeated fighter, who antagonizes her and Anna challenges her to a fight, which she accepts.
As the days and her training progresses, she wins several fights.
Anna is attracted to Roy, the attending doctor for the fight club who also works in the local hospital - despite the fact that he has a relationship with Olivia.
However, they end their relationship after a drunken night.
However, Anna did not take it seriously and ignores his advances.
Anna later witnesses Olivia fighting three girls in the ring and savagely knocking out all of them.
Realizing how savage Olivia is, Anna quits, saying that fighting is not the best solution to solving her problems.
The next day, Jack convinces Anna to continue to fight and tells her to "leave behind fear and doubt and take that final step to bravery".
Anna then receives a call from Chuck saying that her dad is in the hospital after suffering a heart attack.
Arriving there with Charleen already at the room, Ed tells Anna that he knows her mom founded the fight club and has passed its ownership to Anna.
Charleen convinces Anna to sell the fight club and start a new life.
When Roy appears, Ed persuades Anna to reconnect with him.
She apologizes to him, and Roy reveals to her that he never had sex with Olivia and has been only thinking of Anna.
On the night of her fight, with renewed courage, Anna confronts Olivia for the first time in the ring.
Anna is overwhelmed by Olivia in early rounds, but as per Jack's advice, Anna uses her headbutt to knock her out, eventually winning the fight and thus marking Olivia's first loss.

As the police arrives at the door to raid the fight club, Olivia pays respect to Anna before escaping with the fellow fighters and, despite Charleen's objection, Anna chooses to stay behind, stating that she now takes the ownership of her mom's fight club, and is arrested.
Charleen bails Anna out of jail but Anna is put on trial for her misdemeanor.
Aided by her lawyer Chuck and the presiding judge Naomi Andrews, Mary's old friend, Anna is acquitted of all charges.
Three months later, Anna has renovated the fight club and she agrees to fight with Charleen as a friendly fight.
But the two get knocked out at the same time and call Roy for medical attention.
Later, Anna goes to the restaurant to pay Jack for her training fee but is shocked to find that she has to pay much more than she had expected.

26455901.title: Hawk G-19: The Metropolitan Giant
synopsis: Daryl, a diligent data analyst famed for his early-morning work habits and a self-confessed obsessive-compulsive neat freak, often indulged in building intricate miniature scale representations of renowned global cities to decompress after grappling with statistics in complex spreadsheets all day.

One regular Tuesday, while scavenging through the labyrinth-like passages within a dusty, dimly lit old basement store famously known as "OddGene's Antiques" during his fixed half-hour lunch recess, he chanced upon a fascinating, slightly discolored blueprint of a long-abandoned G-19 Hawk model airplane.

Instantly captivated, Daryl hastily purchases the intriguing blueprint just for a sum of five dollars, and this impulse buy quickly transforms into a passionate hobby that engulfs his idle hours as he painstakingly and meticulously assembles the comprehensive model with the greatest attention to detail.

His existence becomes largely dominated by the intrinsic allure this airplane's model exudes, ensuring he often skips meals and stretches his sleeping hours, much to the increasing concern of his boundlessly energetic roommate Chloe, who teaches a lively bunch of preschoolers.

One lazy weekend afternoon, as Daryl was engrossed in his usual deeply thorough bi-monthly cleaning project, he inadvertently nudges a minuscule, cryptically labeled vial of "Gulliver's Juice" cunningly concealed behind a few dusty, worn-out leather-bound books ensconced on an unassuming top shelf.

Intrigued by the mysterious liquid, he inadvertantly spills a few drops onto his painstakingly detailed G-19 Hawk model, triggering an astonishing transformation - the miniaturized model undergoes a rapid metamorphosis, expanding into an impeccably replicated full-scale G-19 Hawk aircraft bursting with tiny, proportionate passengers.
Taking everyone off guard, the plane's engines thunder into action, propelling it gliding across his living room floor and out through his unanticipatedly large, Victorian-era bay window.

The pilotless aircraft miraculously navigates its way around the city's towering skyline, demonstrating swift and precise maneuvering skills while earning incredulous stares from the city's bustling crowd of residents.

Fearful of the potential catastrophe an errant, uncontrolled aircraft could cause in a densely populated city, Daryl along with a bewildered Chloe conjure up a hasty but essential plan for their impromptu mission - Locate and recover the full-size airplane model now darting around their city.

Their compelling mission takes them on a wild chase across bustling city squares, tucked-away back alleys, and iconic green parks of their own city, hidden corners of which were until then unknown to them.
All the while, they keep an eager eye out for any sightings of the erratic G-19 Hawk.

Their fast-paced adventure intersects the lives of the varied city populace including curious corporate employees, perturbed pedestrians, and wide-eyed children, all expressing their individual reactions to the gasp-worthy spectacle unfolding right before their eyes.
This little plane, which has now become a cherished city celebrity, selects the grand statue of the city's founding mayor as its operational base.
The aircraft's acrobatic stunts around the statue invoke contagious laughter and energetic conversations amongst the onlooking crowd.

Taking note of the palpable joy his inadvertent creation is stirring up, Daryl is confronted with a challenging decision: to put an end to the mini-plane's aerial shenanigans forever or to let it continue.
In the end, he puts a responsible foot forward by deciding to return the lovable airplane and its tiny occupants to their original miniature state using the remaining bit of Gulliver's Juice.
When the gliding airplane takes a playful plunge towards Daryl's duo, he strategically tosses the potion onto it.
This sets off a breathtaking mid-air magical transition where the plane is briefly shrouded in cascading shimmers of stardust before gradually shrinking down to a fraction of its size.

The G-19 Hawk, post its enchanting journey across the city skies, returns to its original miniature size, along with its troop of diminutive passengers, and gently descends into Daryl's welcoming palms.
Amidst deafening cheers and the infectious laughter of the onlooking crowd, a triumphant Daryl and an out-of-breath Chloe make their jovial return home.
Their chaotic pursuit lasting an entire day which turned into an unexpected citywide entertainment.

Once back in the tranquility of their home, they decide to memorialize the day's adventure by strategically positioning the G-19 Hawk model alongside Daryl's meticulously crafted miniatures atop their mantle.

As the strange day finally comes to a close, it concludes with a merry audience still relishing the surprises thrown their way during the day, etching a memorable imprint on the fascinatingly entertaining day.

As the madness of the day finally subsides, Daryl and Chloe find themselves caught up in bouts of roaring laughter reminiscing about the ridiculous situations they encountered all courtesy of their mini-passenger packed G-19 Hawk, their laughter proving to be a fitting melody echoing throughout their apartment.

68183268.title: Konga TNT
synopsis: An F-15 Eagle sorties with orders to locate a target over 50 meters tall somewhere in the city below.
Flying low, the jet becomes easy prey for an enormous gorilla, who dispatches it with a swing of his hand.
One week earlier, an alien ship crashes in the Amazon.
After a local tribe take the ship's power source, General Mills dispatches famed tracker Skipper Smith and his assistant Marion Kind to retrieve it.
To Smith's delight, all of the members of the tribe are woman.
Distracted, he and Marion are easily abducted and taken before their queen, Peggy, who wears the power source as an amulet.
She shows them mercy, allowing them to stay for the night.
Smith seduces her, convincing her to take off the amulet, then dashes away with it.
Marion calls in a seaplane, and they bring the artifact to Professor Mills, the general's twin brother.
He dubs the substance inside it KTNT and attempts to splice its DNA with that of a houseplant, with dismal results.
Next he experiments on a monkey, who puts up a fierce fight before taking the KTNT in pill form.
As he observes the results, two terrorists break into his facility.
He sets the monkey free, but they shoot him before he can destroy his research.
Fleeing to the suburbs, the monkey rests in a shed.
General Mills is informed of his brother's death and the theft of the alien technology.
He orders a search for the escaped test subject, calling the retired Major Bummier back into the field.
Two boys, Chance and Grayson, discover the monkey after he eats their snacks.
Naming him Konga, they agree to keep him a secret from their mother.
Bummier, traveling door to door, asks her if she's seen an escaped ape.
The boys play in their backyard with Konga, who suddenly grows to enormous size and rushes past Bummier.
Konga terrifies a farmer before growing again, bursting through the roof of his barn.
Spotting a beautiful blonde woman in her bedroom, he abducts her just to give her a kiss on the head.
In Jackson Park, all of the fleeing citizens start to depress him.
Moving downtown, his clumsiness causes mass destruction, toppling buildings and cooling towers.
A passing airliner catches his attention, and he snatches it out of the sky.
Chance tries to lures him away by dressing up as a hot dog, but the military nonetheless assails the monster with tanks and fighter jets.
Suddenly, Konga returns to his original size, and the boys embrace him.
Charmed, Bummier reports to Mills that Konga escaped, and announces his second honorable discharge.
Professor Mills, miraculously alive, explains to his brother that Konga's body eventually rejected KTNT, allowing him to shrink.
Another drop of KTNT allowed him to survive being shot.
In a post-credits scene, Chance and Grayson discover a large egg in the woods.

87214240.title: Voyager vs. Terran
synopsis: Dr. Jane Reynolds, a globally recognized Astrophysicist, is focused on a series of telemetry feeds flowing from the Hubble Space Telescope.

She sits at the heart of the busy control room in NASA's Houston base, meticulously examining the multicolored array of fuzzy constellation maps displaying on the monitors, searching for any anomalous spectral signatures that might indicate uncharted territories in space.
Paul Thompson, a man of few words, is a former Marine Corps officer.
A stoic figure with a resilient demeanor, his aptitude for fending off cyber attacks is unsurpassed.
He is in charge of managing the security operations at the bustling NASA facility in Houston.
The perpetual hum of the control room is abruptly punctuated by a shrill alarm, as a red light starts flashing on the dashboard.
All anxious eyes turn to the satellite radar screen now displaying a fast-moving, unidentified object cutting through the Earth's atmosphere like a bolide.
The enigmatic object dives into the Earth and crashes in the vast open expanses of the Sonoran desert in Arizona.
Its shockwave can be felt as a seismic event, causing worldwide concern and sparking a media frenzy.

Thompson and Dr. Reynolds, due to their unique skills and experience, are called upon to assemble and spearhead an elite team, consisting of the top minds in evolutionary biology, quantum physics, and exceptional security personnel, all rushing to analyze the bizarre event.

Upon arriving at the crash site, they are greeted with a surreal spectacle: an avant-garde spacecraft, partially embedded in a sand dune, its glowing embers casting myriad ethereal shadows onto the desert night.
Fuelled by her scientific curiosity, Dr. Reynolds pushes aside Thompson's cautionary advice and persuades the team to venture into the mysterious, alien spacecraft.
Inside, they discover an unknown entity emanating a bioluminescent aura.
The alien being appears to be in a weird state of unconsciousness or stasis, ensconced upon a geometric pedestal, emitting eerie rhythmic waves of soft light.
Surprisingly, the alien entity, affectionately nicknamed "the Voyager" by the team, suddenly stirs with a high-frequency whir.
Its form begins expanding and contracting rhythmically, refusing to adhere to the norms of known physics.
Without warning, the Voyager explodes in a shockwave of frightening kinetic energy.
The force sends equipment and personnel flying like ragdolls, killing everyone in its vicinity except for Dr. Reynolds and Thompson who narrowly avert the lethal energy burst.
The shaken and barely surviving duo manage to return to Houston, carrying an urgent message about the rogue alien entity now loose on Earth.

While they relay the horror of their near-death experience to their colleagues, an unmanned drone captures alarming footage of the Voyager moving towards the metropolis of Phoenix, seemingly drawn by its dense energy grid, causing widespread panic.
Dr. Reynolds, in a desperate bid to halt the progression of the Voyager, proposes an audacious plan to render it incapacitated by manipulating its energy-absorption mechanism.
Simultaneously, Thompson begins assembling a formidable team of Delta Force commandos, briefing them for the impending confrontation with the extraterrestrial entity.
Ignoring the heavy artillery, the Voyager continues its sinister journey unscathed.
It unleashes devastating energy waves, causing extensive damage and significant loss of life in the outskirts of Phoenix.

In a hangar back in Houston, Dr. Reynolds and her dedicated team of engineers work round the clock to construct an electromagnetic pulse (EMP) device designed to disable the Voyager's energy-absorbing shield.

Halfway across the country, within the devastated landscapes of Arizona, Thompson and his team of Delta Force, armed with state-of-the-art weaponry, engage in battle with the Voyager, barely managing to stall its relentless march.
Upon receiving news of their unsuccessful resistance, Dr. Reynolds, wielding the prototype of the EMP device, boards a helicopter for a dangerous airborne ride to the heated battleground.
Bearing the hopes of humanity, Thompson leads his commandos equipped with the prototype EMP devices, charging into the dunes towards the Voyager.
Battling against immense odds, they successfully strike the Voyager with concentrated EMP bursts.
The powerful jolts visibly damage the alien, causing it to recoil and retreat back into the desert haze.
Amid fleeting relief of their hard-fought victory, the desolate ruins of Phoenix and the catastrophic loss of life wrought by the Voyager's onslaught cast a somber shadow on their victory.
As the dust finally settles, Dr. Reynolds, in a sweeping survey of the crash site, stumbles upon a disregarded fragment from the Voyager's spaceship.
An intense laboratory analysis of the fragment reveals a jarring truth - a multitude of similar spacecraft, possibly carrying more Voyagers, are heading towards Earth on an interstellar course.

As the narrative draws to a close, the camera pans to an ominous shot of the silent fleet of alien spacecraft - "the Terran Fleet" - suspended in the celestial backdrop of the Milky Way, planting the seed for "Voyager vs. Terran: Invasion."

67570226.title: Ape vs. Monster
synopsis: A space capsule crashes back to Earth near Roswell, New Mexico; Dr. Linda Murphy, answering to National Security Advisor Ethan Marcos, takes control of the investigation.
The craft is found to be from ELBE, a secret U.S.-Soviet space program that aimed to end the Cold War via establishing a joint first contact.
Linda's father, Noah, was a lead scientist on the project, but they became estranged when he sent Abraham, a chimpanzee the young Linda befriended, into space as the capsule's pilot.
The mission was declared a failure when Earth lost contact with the craft in 2007.
Marcos orders Linda to investigate the site before the Russians learn of the capsule's return.
Linda and her friend, Undersecretary Reynolds, lead a team to the crash site.
They discover that the capsule's occupant broke out following the landing, and the capsule is covered in a strange green fluid.
Abraham, having grown several times larger, appears and kills Reynolds and the soldiers.
Linda trips and is knocked unconscious, but sees another team led by her former classmate Eva Kuleshov, who is now a Russian agent, arrive and tranquilize Abraham.
Unnoticed by the humans, a Gila monster consumes some of the liquid at the site.
At the Langley Research Center, Abraham is confined while Linda, Eva and a team of scientists attempt to understand his mutation.
Back at the crash site, a group of soldiers left to guard the capsule are killed by the now-mutated, gigantic Dinosaur-like Gila.
Marcos sends Linda and her assistant Jones to pursue the creature.
Meanwhile, Eva discovers that the alien substance breaks down in Earth's atmosphere, leading her to covertly have the entire remaining supply injected into Abraham to stabilize it.
Linda and Jones witness the Gila destroy a bridge and a passenger train before heading underground.
Abraham grows even larger and escapes from Langley.

Linda, confused over his sudden further mutation, meets with Marcos and Eva, with Eva mentioning rumors that Abraham destroyed the Extraterrestrial Defense Initiative, a successor to the Strategic Defense Initiative.
It is found that Abraham inhaled the substance over time while in the capsule, while the Gila directly consumed it.
General Delaney, Reynolds' successor, orders the team to find the monsters as soon as possible.
They track Abraham to Huntington, West Virginia, where Linda discovers the substance breaking down in blood he left behind, forcing Eva to admit her deception.
Linda removes Eva from the team and joins a group of Special Forces soldiers who engage Abraham, but the men are all killed and Abraham flees.
Eva disappears with an Apache helicopter.
Returning to Langley, Linda and Jones discover beams of cosmic energy transmitted from the Andromeda Galaxy are remotely controlling both monsters via the substance in their bodies.
The Hubble Space Telescope discovers an alien ship approaching Earth, forcing Marcos to call Noah in to provide assistance.
Linda finds that Abraham may be able to resist the aliens' control, and she, Jones and Noah plan to jam the alien signal using a transmitter.
The transmitter is attached to the Washington Monument shortly before Abraham appears in the city, guided there to decapitate the U.S. government in preparation for a full-scale invasion.
Its jamming signal quickly frees him, but the Gila monster is unaffected and emerges to wreak havoc.

Despite Abraham no longer being a threat, Delaney orders a missile strike on him; this accidentally causes the Washington Monument to fall, killing Delaney and destroying the transmitter, thus allowing the aliens to regain control of Abraham.
Noah, having reconciled with Linda, discloses the existence of a prototype transmitter stored in a van in the city, and sends Linda and Jones to retrieve it.
They find it, but Jones is devoured by the Gila before she can repair it.
Upon its activation, Abraham is once again freed, and he battles the Gila to protect Linda.
The Gila eventually gains the advantage over Abraham, but Eva is able to disorient the Gila with a suicide attack.
Abraham recovers and beats the Gila, striking it several times before killing it by snapping its neck.
Marcos sends in gunships to terminate Abraham, but changes his mind and decides to place faith in Linda's trust of Abraham, calling them off at the last minute.
In the aftermath, the alien ship retreats from Earth, while the fallen Gila's energy is fully neutralized.
Abraham is sent to a facility outside Santa Fe, New Mexico, where he can live in peace.
Marcos gives Linda exclusive rights to study him, and she accepts Noah's offer to join her.

56405203.title: Bella's Getaway (2021 film)
synopsis: We begin the narrative with Bella, a young, ambitious woman waking up in her run-of-the-mill apartment in Manhattan, downtown New York.
Its plain white walls display an array of yellow post-it notes and dog-eared sketchbooks which showcase Bella’s dreams and aspirations.
The morning light streaming through the window finds Bella dragging herself to her unstimulating job as an administrative assistant at a local grocery store.
One gloomy afternoon, Bella stumbles upon a golden job opportunity posted on LinkedIn.
A luxurious Maldives resort, Sun Haven, is offering a position as an Operations Manager in their paradise-like surroundings.
Overwhelmed yet excited, Bella submits her application nervously.
To Bella's surprise and delight, the hiring team of Sun Haven acknowledges her potential and instantly offers her the job.
She accepts out of sheer joy.
Transitioning to her new role, Bella is introduced to her colleagues- Alex, a captivating DJ from Miami, and Liam, the Michelin star chef of Sun Haven.
Unluckily, the bright sunshine of Bella's life quickly gets covered by dark clouds when Sun Haven begins to crumble under financial strife.
The global pandemic wreaks havoc, threatening to close the resort.
The employees receive a disheartening notice imploring them to leave the islands.
Rather than succumbing to defeat, Bella, Alex, and Liam decide to fight back.
They unite to save Sun Haven, the place which has become home to their shared dreams and happiness.
Bella employs her dormant business acumen, devising and implementing an ingenious digital marketing plan, hoping to entice more international tourists to their resort.
Alex, capitalizing on his EDM industry connections, organizes mesmerizing music festivals which play a crucial role in increasing the popularity of the resort.
Liam, on the other hand, works to turn Sun Haven's restaurant into a gastronomical paradise.
Even as they tackle the financial troubles, Mason Corp., a corrupt multinational corporation, preys on Sun Haven's instability and plots to take over the resort.
Bella, Alex, and Liam bring together their resources, involving the local Maldivian community to counteract Mason Corp.'s exploitative actions.
A public hearing is announced in the capital city of Maldives, Male, where the outcome of this dispute will be decided.
The court hearing is intense, sparking an electrifying atmosphere with damning accusations and counter-responses flying across the courtroom.

With resolute support from the local community and Sun Haven's staff members, the verdict zings in favor of Bella's team, saving Sun Haven from being ravaged by Mason Corp.  Bella, Alex, and Liam rise as unexpected heroes, lauded for their steadfastness and resilience throughout the Sun Haven crisis.
Bella draws immense satisfaction from this success, realizing her deep passion for the dynamic, never-a-dull-moment hospitality industry.
Amongst this turmoil, a heartwarming love story blossoms between Alex and a local Maldivian artist.
Liam sees his popularity skyrocket as he enchants the world with his extraordinary culinary skills.
The narrative ends on a jubilant note, leaving the viewers brimming with inspiration, joy, and the courage to break free of an ordinary life and follow their passions.

63513044.title: Mayday (2021 film)
synopsis: Ana works at a hotel with her friends Dimitri, a DJ, and cook Max.
Ana and her coworker June comfort Marsha, a new bride who is experiencing cold feet.
Ana is abused by the cruel head waiter.
When a storm knocks out the power, Ana hears a voice spelling out "mayday" in a modified NATO Phonetic alphabet.
Following the voice, she crawls into an oven and falls into the ocean.
Emerging on an unknown shore, Ana encounters Marsha, now brimming with confidence.
She is in shock and realised she has no memories.
A man dressed as a World War Two aviator emerges from the sea and says that his plane crashed in the ocean and that there's a war on.
As the girls leave the beach the pilot is shot to death.
Marsha takes Ana to a beached submarine where she and two other girls, Gert and Bea, live.
Marsha explains that this land is a utopia where the girls can live without fear of male violence and predation.
Marsha tells Ana there are camps of women all over the island fighting and winning a war against the men trying to invade.
The girls show Ana how to shoot a rifle, something she proves adept at.
When the three others go swimming, Ana is too afraid to jump from a cliff and join them.
She is attacked by the head waiter, now dressed as a soldier, but manages to escape.
Marsha shows Ana her telescope and shows her how to view the stars.
Ana joins the girls in their ongoing mission: sending out fake distress signals to lure men to their death in the storm which surrounds the island.
When a group of men manage to make it to the island alive, Ana finds herself unable to kill them.
This alienates her from the bloodthirsty Marsha.
Ana begins having a recurring dream of herself driving a car through a tunnel.
While alone in the control room a distress call comes across the radio, Ana answers it and talks to the man, he tells her he isn't far from shore but they are having electrical problems.
Ana plans to go out and swim to their ship but he tells her he is in a submarine that can't surface because of the issue but he promises to come back for her when it is fixed.
Marsha catches her and knows she is lying when Ana says she was not talking to anyone on the radio.
Bea is captured by men and the girls run to rescue her.
They find her being forced to dig her own grave and Ana hesitates but in the end has no choice but to shoot the men to save her friend.
Gert speaks to Marsha and questions why Bea would be out in the forest by herself and Marsha says she told her to go out there, she knew Ana’s heart wasn't in it but now it is.

Ana goes out on patrol and finds a photographer and his squad Ana prepares herself to shoot them but bombs suddenly start to drop, she runs away but is knocked out by a blast, she comes to and stumbles into a field with a large camp of soldiers and they engage in a dance routine; this is likely a hallucination, as she has killed them all.
Ana wakes up on the ground and goes back to the submarine.
In the control room Marsha tells Ana she is a nobody and they scuffle.
Ana tells her she has stopped hurting herself and started hurting others.
Out on patrol, this time Ana has no problem shooting soldiers she finds scaling the cliffs.
Marsha is unhappy that she is losing control of the group, during an air raid she refuses to come inside to comfort a hysterical Bea.
On patrol Ana finds an older man peeling potatoes, the chef Max.
He tells her he is lost, she says she is too, they share a drink and he says he wants to be in a place where there is no war and suggests maybe they should go home.
Ana lays her head against his knee and falls asleep.
She dreams again about driving through a tunnel but this time she sees a light from the end of the tunnel.
Ana wakes up to find she is asleep on Marsha’s knee, they fight and Ana calls Marsha a monster.
Ana tells Gert she wants to leave the island that she doesn't think she is meant to be here, Gert agrees to help her.
Ana hears a radio broadcast by the man on the submarine, he says he's dying from the fumes and apologises for not being able to come back to save her.

He says he has ‘never had much luck with the ladies’ and tells her she should say goodbye; Ana replies, saying she’s ‘not that kind of girl’, echoing a conversation they had at the start of the movie.
The memory of the conversation makes her realise it is Dimitri, and she suddenly remembers everything.
Gert tells her she definitely doesn't belong here, and sends her to meet with  June, now a mechanic, who she tells about her plan to leave the island.

June warns her that she is like a star, and if she leaves it will be like a star dying; everything around it gets pulled in, and they all disappear, everyone on the island will be snuffed out of existence.
June also tells Ana that to get through the storm she will need precise calculations.
Ana returns to the sub and tells Gert and Bea she has changed her mind and isn't leaving, but Gert reveals they already know what will happen and they still want her to try.
Ana asks them to come with her but they tell her they can't.
They tell Ana she can go and protect other girls from becoming like them, victims of men.
They then show Ana that they have already spoken to all of the other camps on the island and they are all in support of Ana leaving.
Gert, Bea, June and Ana, with the help of the other camps via the radio, track the storms and formulate a plan to get Ana through the storm and back to the point she entered.
They think they have kept it all a secret from Marsha, but she has actually been listening to them via the radio.
She confronts Ana and tells her she can't believe that after everything she has given her, after making her a hero, she wants to go back to a kitchen.
Ana replies that she's made her into a psychopath and Marsha says it's the same thing.
She tells Ana that she is going back to so much darkness and Ana tells her that in the dark she will see the stars.
Ana and Bea lie in bed, Ana tells Bea she doesn't want to leave her, and Bea says she will go first and to close her eyes, Bea then disappears.
June, Gert and Bea check all of the perimeters are correct and tell Ana it's time.
They watch from the control room as Ana jumps into the sea and swims towards the storm but she gets caught in a rip tide, is pulled under and starts to drown.
Marsha gets on the radio and encourages her repeating the same message Ana heard on the radio in her dream.
Ana is able to float to where she needs to be and finds Dimitri floating there; as she reaches him, she is transported back to the hotel.
The film ends with Ana walking into the banquet hall where Dimitri is DJing.
She approaches the microphone and opens her mouth to sing.

4649154.title: Value of Life: The Legal Perspective (film)
synopsis: In the hallowed halls of Harvard Law School, David Wellington, a seasoned corporate attorney from the esteemed Wellington & Associates, captivates his attentive audience with an eloquent dissertation on the complexities of financial settlements versus the incalculable worth of human existence.
The lecture concluded, David retreats to the isolation of his steel-and-glass bastion located on the 23rd floor of Milton Towers.
The caller introduces himself as John Gallagher.
A name David recognizes as a former client, a hardy construction worker who had suffered a debilitating injury due to a tragically botched spinal surgery.
John, with hesitant words and forced breaths, pleads with David for guidance on an unsettling development involving the mighty medical conglomerate, MedCorp International.
Intrigued, David delves into the fresh developments surrounding John's moribund case.
David pays a visit to John's medical care facility, cuts across the echo-filled hospital corridors with a disarming show of empathy.
Shocked and disgusted by the meager $50,000 compensation being offered by MedCorp, David expresses his disdain for their callous appraisal of the worth of human existence.
Stirred at an emotional level by the connection he had built with John in their conversation and alarmed at the injustice, David agrees to become his legal representative without charging any fees.
The narrative next portrays David's relentless quest for retribution, as he resists the bullying mindset of MedCorp's powerful influence.
David meticulously uncovers MedCorp's shadowy past, revealing a chilling history of 37 recurrent allegations of malpractice skillfully veiled by the exterior of monetary settlements.

David is taken aback when MedCorp's legal heavyweights threaten to bring past professional discretions into the open, aiming to tarnish his decades-long career and threatening his professional standing.
John, consumed with guilt for dragging David into the adversarial situation, implores him to back out and abandon their cause.
Unyielding and resolute, David convinces John of the moral imperative guiding their cause, despite the imminent specter of professional disgrace.
David, engrossed in plotting his legal strategy late into the night, wrestles with the dilemma of balancing the high stakes against his own professional reputation.
Memories of his impassioned lectures at Harvard Law School well up in him, sparking a resurgence of conviction and resolve.
Overcoming his apprehensions, he girds himself for the legal combat awaiting him against MedCorp's battle-hardened lawyers.
David presents a passionately charged case in court.
With his vast legal knowledge and tactical maneuvers, he thwarts MedCorp's defensive strategies, convincing the jury with crystal clear facts.
In what seems an impossible battle, David's masterful rhetoric resounds throughout the courtroom, gradually tilting the scales towards justice.
The court ruling elevates the value of human life above monetary appeasements.
David's experiences have transformed him into a tempered steel, his insights now enriched with a newfound understanding of the myriad human life values.
His future lectures brim with practical wisdom and stark truths, exposing the frailties and moral inconsistencies of monetary judgments.
He enlightens his students about the fundamental values of integrity and empathy, inspiring a new generation of justice crusaders.
The concluding scenes depict John, embracing a fulfilling existence despite his harsh past.
David's hard-earned victory becomes a beacon of hope for the oppressed.
The film concludes with a solemn nod to the disastrous consequences of prioritizing financial gain over the sacredness of human life.

56587836.title: Worth (film)
synopsis: The film opens with Kenneth Feinberg detailing the law's recognition of the monetary value of a person's life to his class at Columbia University.
Some time later, the September 11 attacks occur.
Feinberg is appointed the Special Master of the September 11th Victim Compensation Fund while his law partner, Camille Biros, is appointed as his administrative deputy.

Feinberg develops a rigid formula for each payout based on the victim's income, and is instructed that if he cannot convince at least 80 percent of the 7,000 estimated victims to sign on then they will be eligible to file a lawsuit which they may lose (as well as the pressure from the political administrations to save the airlines from being sued, leading to financial disaster).
Feinberg is given until December 22, 2003 to accomplish this.
At an introductory meeting with victims in which he attempts to explain the rules governing the fund, Feinberg is perceived as insensitive to the losses suffered by attendees.
The hostile group is calmed when Charles Wolf, the husband of a woman killed in the attacks, demands that they listen to what Feinberg has to say.
After the meeting, Feinberg is confronted by Frank Donato, the brother of a deceased New York City Fire Department (FDNY) firefighter, Nick.
His brother had re-entered the tower to find him after communication, which may not have reached Nick, warned that the building would fail.
Frank demands that Feinberg includes this information in the report to remedy this flaw in the communication system for first responders.
Feinberg deflects that demand in lawyerly fashion.
Feinberg also is disturbed to learn that Wolf was offended by the callous nature of the fund's formula and has started a protest group.

Biros leads the staff in holding meetings with victims and is moved by the story of a gay man, Graham Morris, whose partner (whose parents vehemently denied that their son was gay) was killed in the attack.
Due to the rules governing the fund, he cannot be compensated as he is a resident of the state of Virginia, which does not recognize civil partnerships.
Feinberg also meets with several lawyers representing the loved ones of upper-class victims of the attacks, who want more money, which threatens the success of the group as a whole.

As the months drag on, the fund manages to attract only a fraction of the necessary applicants, leading Feinberg to hold a private meeting with Wolf in which the latter accuses Feinberg of serving only the interests of the Bush administration.
A lawyer representing Donato's extra-marital partner calls Feinberg to inform him that Donato has two daughters from that relationship who qualify for compensation.
This leads Feinberg to try to inform Donato's widow to convince her to sign on after she had earlier refused.
As the months drag on, Feinberg is increasingly unsuccessful in convincing victims to file for compensation from the government fund.

After Wolf approaches him one evening at the opera and recounts an anecdote from years earlier in which his deceased wife encouraged him to persevere in the face of failure, Feinberg finds his spirit renewed.
Feinberg and Biros begin to use the discretion government gave him to expand the rules to cover as many victims as they can under the fund.
Feinberg begins to meet victims.
He constructs a shrine in his office from the various mementos given to him by fund applicants.
When Wolf sees that Feinberg truly cares for the victims of the attacks, he is able to convince his fellow victims to trust Feinberg.
By the deadline, the vast majority of those eligible for compensation sign the forms, ensuring the success of the project.
Feinberg is visited by Donato's widow to sign on behalf of her husband's children.

Biros tearfully calls Morris to inform him that while she was unable to help him as the gay partner of a victim, because his state did not recognize their relationship, the fund did compensate many other gay couples who lived in states that recognized same-sex unions.
The film ends with a title card stating that Feinberg and Biros were able to distribute billions in government money to 97 percent of eligible victims and that they continue to work on similar cases.

49295197.title: Sweat It Out (film)
synopsis: The narrative starts around the pulsating energy of Westchester State University, painting a vibrant picture of college life which largely revolves around the life of a gifted student, Bailey Raymond.
Known for her idiosyncratic and unconventional demeanor, Bailey charms her peers and educators alike.
Paradoxically, Bailey who holds a notorious reputation for her complete lack of dancing abilities lands up as the de facto techno-manager of her university's acclaimed dance team, The Pelicans.
The Pelicans are well-regarded for an unbroken winning streak in the fiercely competitive annual 5-College Dance Showdown.
The following act brings into focus Bailey's hard-fought struggles to fit in with the rhythmically inclined Pelicans.
Her missteps and blunders during practice sessions transpire into a series of amusing and somewhat embarrassing incidents.
Meanwhile, the campus rivalry goes up a notch with the introduction of aggressive competitors from Eastchester University, known as The Hawks.
