Their unyielding desire to usurp the championship title from The Pelicans sets a challenging front.
Faced with the intense rivalry, Bailey steps up with innovative technological ideas for choreography and performance.
Unfortunately, The Pelicans exude indifference towards her suggestions and reject her proposals summarily.
Deeply dismayed by this dismissal, Bailey ends up evicted from the team.
Her ejection leaves her questioning the significance of her contributions and the influence of her advanced proposals on the dance field.
The audience is then drawn into a stark contrast showcased between The Pelicans' usual vibrant performances and their lackluster showcase at the preliminary competition rounds.
Recognizing the weight of their faltering performance, the once arrogant Pelicans come to understand the value and importance of Bailey's unique contributions in their success formula.
Realizing their folly, the team humbly reaches out to Bailey, beseeching her to rejoin the team.
They now recognize her precise technical expertise as an imperative variable in their formula to regain their championship status.
In an unexpected twist, Bailey presents a groundbreaking idea that melds wearable tech with modern dancing, paving the way for a sensational performance.
The next act glorifies the expected transformation of the Pelicans, who undergo grueling training sessions to perfect Bailey's technologically-enhanced dance routine.
This transition leads to a welcome departure from their familiar classical dance routines.
The viewer is then drawn into an escalating situation soon before the grand championship.
The "Sweat It Out" finale against their arch-rivals, The Hawks, receives prominence with underlying suspense.
At the climactic "Sweat It Out" dance-off, The Pelicans finally present an unparalleled dance performance.
Bailey's electronic music elements blend seamlessly with the team's traditional jazz routines to have the audience at the edge of their seats.
On the face of it, The Hawks seem to have an advantage with their flawless execution of intricate swing dance routines, putting The Pelicans in a precarious situation.
Pursuing a crowd-favorite approach, The Pelicans' innovative performance wildly excites the audience, resulting in a biased response in their favor, throwing the final verdict into uncertainty.
In an unexpected move by the contest organizers, they announce that the winner will be determined by the audience's cheer volume, escalating the suspense.
Against all expectations, The Pelicans incredibly seize a surprise victory.
Bailey's avant-garde choreography is acclaimed as a huge success and becomes a catalyst for their triumph.
Bailey's significant contributions are acknowledged finally, cementing her place within the team.
Her feats also gain her acceptance in the broader dance community and underscores the prime importance of technological innovation and cooperation in dance.
The narrative concludes with a glorious scene framing the ecstatic Pelicans, with the triumphant Bailey being their centerpiece.
Bailey emerges as the champion of innovation.

61199955.title: Work It (film)
synopsis: Quinn Ackerman, a quirky and intelligent high school senior, works as a technical director for the Thunderbirds, her high school's elite dance team, which is well known around the state as the reigning champions of the Work It dance competition.
When Quinn sets something on fire by accident, the ruthless leader of the Thunderbirds, Julliard Pembroke, fires her from the position.

Quinn's dream to attend Duke University, her late father's alma mater, is soured when the admissions counselor, Veronica Ramirez, informs that her chances of standing out to the admission's team are not good.
Quinn misleads Ramirez into thinking that she is a dancer on the Thunderbirds, even though she only worked the lighting.
Ramirez is instantly impressed, and vows to see her perform live at the Work It dance competition.
Though she considers confessing, Quinn instead decides to commit to it.
Quinn enlists the help of her best friend, Jasmine Hale, who is a dancer for the Thunderbirds herself, to teach her how to dance for the team's open auditions in two weeks.
Quinn's dancing skills improve substantially, but Julliard still rejects her.
After Jasmine stands up to him and defends Quinn, Julliard sarcastically suggests that the two start their own dance team, which Quinn does.
Jasmine reluctantly agrees to quit the Thunderbirds in favor of Quinn's new team.
Quinn and Jasmine research a former champion of the Work It competition, Jake Taylor, who stopped competing and vanished after a knee injury two years prior.

Quinn tracks him down and approaches him at the dance studio where he now works, and asks him to be a choreographer for her team, but Jake rejects her, insisting that dance is done with passion, not learned by thinking.
Meanwhile, the girls round up a group of unknown dancers at their school who all differ in style.
After seeing the team's potential during an informal dance meetup, Jake agrees to choreograph for Quinn's team, but only if they can win the upcoming qualifying competition by themselves.
Under the name "TBD", they cut qualifiers but on a technicality issue with an opposing team.
Jake and Quinn spend more time together, and one night, Jake takes her aside and decides to experiment with freestyle dancing with her.
As the two practice, Quinn's talent surfaces, and they kiss.
With newfound confidence, Quinn takes it easier on herself and puts more effort into her dancing and teamwork.
Quinn emails Veronica Ramirez and informs her that she has started her own team and that they will be competing at Work It.
However, when Julliard discovers that Jake is choreographing for the Quinn's team, he turns them in for using the studio to practice without paying, and Jake loses his job.
Quinn's grades drop due to her dedication to the team, and she receives an email from the Duke admissions team informing her that Veronica no longer works there.
Quinn confesses everything to her mom, and they agree that she should quit the dance team and bring her grades up before turning in her final transcript.
The team feels betrayed by Quinn's departure, especially Jasmine, who rejoins the Thunderbirds, and Quinn ends her romance with Jake.
She later rediscovers her own passion for dance and reconciles with Jake, and they both decide to bring the team back together.
Quinn reconciles with Jasmine, who quits the Thunderbirds and rejoins the TBDs.
The group begins to learn each other's unique dance styles, and Jake incorporates them into the choreography.
On the day of the competition, Quinn's mother discovers that she is still in dance and tries to stop her from leaving, but Quinn steals the car keys and leaves.
When Quinn arrives, the TBDs are already on stage, and she enters halfway through the act.
The TBDs narrowly win the competition over the Thunderbirds, and both Jasmine and Julliard are approached by a scout from the New York Dance Academy.
Quinn runs into Veronica, who is now working at NYU, and she invites her to apply for the fall semester.

42686812.title: Scripts on Locker Doors
synopsis: The film begins by introducing Jonathan, a tranquil teenager with an aptitude for computer programming.
His room is a tech haven filled with high-speed computers, multiple monitors, and peripherals where LED lights blink in the rhythm of some secretive code.

Amid an entangled web of colorful wires dripping from his high-end circuit boards, Jonathan spends his time engrossed in the world of Python coding, advanced mathematical algorithms, and under the veil of the mysterious dark web.

During the post-dusk hours, in the privacy of his techno sanctuary, he becomes an artist of puzzles, weaving challenging riddles infused with computational jargon and cryptographic codes, often obscured in Fermionic code and number theory.
As the morning light seeps through his room, he morphs drastically into an inconspicuous junior at Plainville High School.
His night-time activities become well-guarded secrets hidden beneath the cloak of an ordinary student's life.
He strategically places his riddles inside old lockers that stand like forgotten relics amidst an ocean of textbooks and discarded garbage, sparking curiosity and confusion.
The perplexing jigsaw of cryptic letters and numbers soon become the center of the high school grapevine, stirring up a whirlpool of speculation and second-guessing.
Both students and teachers find themselves engrossed in intellectual squabbles, unknowingly incorporating Jonathan’s cryptic lexicon into their everyday conversation.
Bitter doses of reality punctuate Jonathan's peaceful existence when his parents, locked in a corrosive marriage, engage in crushing verbal duels.
Jonathan digs through his father's attic filled with old, moth-infested war souvenirs and stumbles upon an antique trigger device, a relic from the Soviet-era.

As he examines the rusty contraption, he is haunted by disturbing memories of his father’s covert military past filled with top-secret missions and shadowy operations filled with danger and uncertainty.
With his proficiency in programming guiding him, Jonathan unwisely tinkers with the device, setting off a dormant countdown unbeknownst to him.
The device detonates within the school premises, severely injuring Ashley, the vivacious cheerleader, who becomes the victim of third-degree burns and smoke inhalation.
Overwhelmed with remorse, Jonathan makes a clandestine visit to Ashley's hospital room.
He stammers a confession and an apology, wrestling with the demons of fear and regret that torment him.
As they bear the sterile hospital environment and their shared pain, Jonathan and Ashley form an unlikely alliance forged by shared secrets and a profound understanding of the other's circumstances.
Inspired by this alliance, Jonathan writes Ashley a consoling note, full of heartfelt honesty and places it secretly inside her locker.
This note, dissimilar to his usual riddles, lays bare his emotions and guilt.
The uncharacteristically emotional message generates intrigue through the student body, fueling rumors about the secret identity of the riddle-maker.
Parallel to the escalating events at school, Jonathan's personal life spirals into chaos when his parents decide to separate.
This added turmoil puts further strain on his agitated mind.
Amidst this tumult, Ashley's companionship becomes his silver lining.
Her encouraging words filled with optimism serve as the buoy keeping him afloat amidst his life's tempest.
Inspired by this newfound hope, Jonathan blurts out a coded confession using his signature numeric cipher language etched on the school lockers.
Recognizing the familiar numerical pattern, Ashley savors the serenity of understanding and acceptance.
Upon deciphering the confession, the entire school body is left stunned.
The ensuing aftermath sees Jonathan expelled from Plainville High, throwing the small community into tumult.
Sensing a business opportunity in all of this chaos, Jonathan teams up with Ashley.
They channel this energy into a start-up, launching a business offering personalized, uplifting locker messages and deliver it to different high schools.
Jonathan, known till then as a lone nerd, reinvents himself as a creative writer and entrepreneur.
He painstakingly rebuilds his reputation while nurturing his blossoming friendship with Ashley.
As the narrative nears its end, Jonathan leaves behind one last heartfelt anonymous message.
A parting note, a farewell letter, written with emotive eloquence and hidden in the weathered lockers of Plainville High.
The piece sparks off a school-wide decoding effort.
In a final emotional showdown at an abandoned sports ground in Plainville, Ashley stands by Jonathan, vowing to stand with him in the face of future adversities.
The film ends with Jonathan and Ashley standing united, their mutual resilience against the harsh adversities life has thrown in their path.

56964263.title: Words on Bathroom Walls
synopsis: High school senior Adam Petrazelli experiences a psychotic break at school, accidentally burning someone's arm.
Diagnosed with  schizophrenia, he first self-treats by intensely focusing on cooking, which calms him.
His symptoms—chiefly hallucinations of three people—worsen until he is put on a drug trial.

At stressful times, his three regular "visitors" are Rebecca, a New Age hippie; Joaquin, the smutty best friend; and the overprotective and often violent "The Bodyguards"; as well as a "dark" threatening voice that represents Adam's fears of the unknown.
Adam transfers to St. Agatha's Catholic School.
There he meets Maya, a feisty, intelligent girl and class valedictorian.
Adam gets Maya to tutor him and finds she helps him feel better, so he takes his new medication regularly.
This reduces his visions, with only the side effect being muscle twitching.
He takes a romantic interest in Maya and the two become close, but he does not disclose his condition to her out of fear of stigmatization.
Adam also starts to regularly confide in Father Patrick, the sympathetic school priest, about his fears and anxieties.
When Maya doesn't show to a tutoring session, Adam visits her home.
He discovers that her family is struggling financially, and she is embarrassed and angry about his unannounced visit.
Once Maya realizes he doesn't care about her background, she continues tutoring him.
She invites him to her restaurant job where she has him cook for her, but a taste test leads Adam to the realization his medication is negatively affecting his taste buds.
Adam decides to stop taking his medications, unbeknownst to his mother Beth and stepfather Paul.
His moods become imbalanced and his delusions return.
The news that Beth is expecting a new baby with Paul also gives rise to Adam's insecurities about being unwanted and feeling like a burden.
Nevertheless, Adam's grades improve so much that his essay is selected to be read at graduation.
He asks Maya to the prom and she accepts.
Beth finds out Adam has stopped his medication and confronts him.
Sister Catherine, the school's headmistress, is informed about the incident and about what happened at his last school.
He is temporarily suspended, with the reasoning that it is for the students' safety.
Adam lashes out at Paul, believing that an email Paul wrote to Sister Catherine the previous night is behind the suspension.
The suspension bars Adam from attending the prom, but he goes anyway.
Before he leaves, he takes an overdose of his medication, believing it will help the night go smoothly.
He meets Maya there, but as they dance, the dark voice plagues him and he begins to act erratically.
Sister Catherine tries to kick him out, but his delusions cause him to push her to the ground, run to the catwalk, and fall over the edge.
Adam wakes in the hospital to see Beth and Paul.
Maya shows up to visit, but he breaks down when the visions overwhelm him.
He yells at her and tells her to leave.
He is expelled from St. Agatha's and placed in a psych ward.
Father Patrick visits and tells Adam he wasn't aware of his struggles, saying he will pray for him.
Beth brings Adam a printed copy of the email Paul sent to St. Agatha's.
Contrary to what Adam thought, Paul supported his stepson and wrote that suspending him would be cruel.
Realizing how much he cares, Adam runs to catch up with him and Beth, hugging Paul for the first time and accepting him as a fatherly figure.

Beth and Paul take Adam to St. Agatha's graduation ceremony, where, despite Sister Catherine's attempt to stop him, he gathers the courage to address the student body calmly, with the support of Father Patrick.
He quotes his essay in which he discusses both his condition and battle with schizophrenia, saying he wished he hadn't hidden his illness.
After he leaves the auditorium, Maya runs after him.
Adam apologizes for not telling her about his illness, at which point they express their mutual love and share a kiss.
Adam is able to receive his high school diploma and realizes his dream of attending culinary school.
As he celebrates the birth of his new sibling with his parents and Maya, it is shown that the voices are still present, but he has learned to live alongside them.

13284015.title: Conflicts at Checkout
synopsis: John, an elderly widower, who has always lived a modest life, finds himself in the comforts of his rustic lakeside home.
He's wrestling with the sleek, yet confusing remote to his new smart television - a far cry from the old knob that he was used to tuning.
His cumbersome interaction with touch screen mobile phones and tablets only amplify his alone-ness, glaringly revealing a man out of touch with the new world.
With the prospect of an adventure and a much-needed change of scenery in mind, John decides to venture to the bustling metropolis-like supermarket a few blocks from his home.
Inside, the supermarket presented itself as a daunting technological maze.
His slip-ups at the self-checkout machine accent his struggle with tech tools and his dire need for guidance.
With frustration mounting and his head in a whirl, he departs the chaos of the store, with a canister of French Vanilla ground coffee he mistakenly forgot to pay for.
His unintentional slight doesn’t escape the keen eyes of the supermarket supervisor, who, curt and stern, accuses him of theft.
The screen brightly illuminates the name 'Lisa', his daughter.
Lisa, unlike her father, is an urbanite who seamlessly navigates the torrent of technological advancements and digital age phenomena.
Fumbling and frantic, John struggles to accept the call.
In his confusion, he inadvertently places the call on speaker, broadcasting his situation to Lisa.
This troubling revelation prompts Lisa to call for an urgent family meeting.
The family, alive with concern, effortlessly agrees that John's days of fending for himself are numbered.
There's an overwhelming consensus that he needs to move in with Lisa and her family.
John, ever the rebel, reluctantly agrees to leave behind his old home for his daughter's bustling household.
John’s antics, which range from him accidentally microwaving metallic objects to struggling when left alone with voice-controlled appliances, create amusing family memories.
Meanwhile, his grandkids relish in these 'gramps moments'.
However, introducing John to the suburban setting of Lisa's house has its own set of challenges.
His lack of familiarity with the local Homeowners' Association norms leads to several hilarious confrontations.
The neighborhood's roped-off corners, excessive house-decor rules, and generally uptight atmosphere pose a unique challenge to John.
Determined to fit in and achieve harmony with his fellow residents, John embarks on a sincere yet wacky mission to improve his relationship with his on-edge neighbors.
His blunders have an upside though: they inspire his grandkids to take on the role of technological mentors, teaching him the A-Z of social media platforms.
This shared laughter, over the viral video, at both John's expense and delight, allows a unique family bonding: a truly human experience of love and strength.
The comedic friction with the neighbors necessitated a community gathering, serving as a platform to cultivate harmony and resolve misunderstandings.
In the ever-vibrant family backdrop, Lisa's work-life poses a roadblock in their peaceful narrative- a critical business presentation threatens to upend her successful career.
John, noticing his daughter fraying at the edges, steps in - against all odds, his newfound tech skills come to the rescue, saving Lisa from a professional debacle.
His internet popularity at an all-time high and his newfound confidence in technology in tow, John returns to the city supermarket, once a place of dread.
His sole aim this time is repentance; he wishes to pay for the can of coffee that he'd inadvertently stolen.
As the city life begins to make sense, adjusting with his modern, techno-freaky family seems more fun than a challenge.
He learns, he fumbles, he laughs - and so does his family.
John begins to interpret his digital struggles as personal challenges.
He takes them on, one at a time, with a happy heart and optimistic mind.
His consistency leads to improvement — he soon finds himself capable of essential tasks like using a laptop, browsing the web, and even managing his e-mail!
His marked progress peaks with a heartfelt e-mail to Lisa.
The email, deeply touching in its honesty, reeks of a heartfelt appreciation for her and her family.
He thanks them for standing by him, for being his guiding stars in the maze of technology.
Lisa, overwhelmed by an unexpected wave of emotion, savors her father's heartbreaking confession.
She reflects on their struggle, their victories, their bond.
Over a course of misadventures, their bond has solidified.
Their love deepened.
Their laughter, a common musical note in the cheerful family chaos.
With a sigh of contentment and a heart full of gratitude, the family comes together for a meal around their massive oak dining table.
It's a tender declaration of the healing power of love, of acceptance, and of family.

51896360.title: The War with Grandpa
synopsis: After accidentally stealing from a grocery store due to having trouble with the self-checkouts and causing a scene with the store manager, recently widowed Ed Marino (Robert De Niro) is visited by his daughter Sally Marino-Decker (Uma Thurman) who wants him to move in with her family.
Ed does not want to leave his house because he built it himself.
Sally convinces Ed to move in with her and gives him her son Peter's (Oakes Fegley) bedroom.
Peter is not happy about giving his room to his grandfather and being moved to the attic.
Ed is welcomed by Sally's husband Arthur (Rob Riggle) and two daughters, Mia (Laura Marano) and Jenny (Poppy Gagnon).
During his first day, Ed spends most of his time in his new room, sitting in his chair and looking at the sky while still thinking about his late wife.
Peter then tells his friends Billy (Juliocesar Chavez), Steve (Isaac Kragten) and Emma (T.J. McGibbon) about his grandfather moving in with his family and living in his room.
After a miserable first night in his new room, Peter decides to declare war.
Ed agrees, as long as they follow the rules of engagement: they cannot damage other people's belongings and cannot tell the family about their arrangement.
Peter pulls a series of pranks, including replacing Ed's shaving cream with quick-drying foam and damaging his record player.
Ed gets back at Peter with pranks including removing all of the screws from Peter's furniture and rewriting his school report.
Ed turns to his friends Danny (Cheech Marin) and Jerry (Christopher Walken) for some advice.
Over time, Ed begins to spend time with his granddaughters and son-in-law and learns how to use modern technology, such as self-checkouts and apps.
Sally learns that Mia is dating a boy named Russell (Colin Ford), whom she does not approve of.
Ed invites Jerry, Danny, and a store worker named Diane (Jane Seymour) who Ed has befriended to play dodgeball against Peter and his friends.
Peter and his friends win the first round, but Ed and his team manage to beat them during the second round.
However, during the third round, Danny's jaw is injured and the game is declared a tie.
Later, Peter pushes the button on Ed's emergency call necklace and Ed picks Peter up from school to take him fishing.
The two discover that it is illegal to fish there.
Ed then takes Peter to his old house and explains that he left some secrets in the walls.
Ed learns that Peter is being bullied, so he, Danny, and Jerry throw the bully in a dumpster.
At Jenny's Christmas-themed birthday party, Peter keeps his promise about not pulling any pranks.
Peter rigs up an ejector seat for Ed, who is supposed to be playing the part of Santa that night.
Unfortunately, a last-minute change results in Jerry being dressed up as Santa.
Throughout the party, Peter and Ed are asked to help out.
Instead, they continue to prank each other, including spraying bottles at each other and Peter plugging the cord to the lights as Ed checks them, shocking Ed.
As a result of their hijinks, they inadvertently reveal their war with each other to everyone.
Jerry gets ejected from his chair, resulting in further property damage and injuries to multiple guests.
During this, Jenny's Christmas tree prop falls onto the house, leaving a hole in Mia's room and revealing Mia's secret tryst with Russell.
Afterwards, Ed is injured and taken to the hospital.
As punishment, Arthur and Sally place Peter and Mia under "work arrest" for six months.
Russell shows up; Sally initially seems angry at him, but instead welcomes him.
Sally goes to pick up Ed from the hospital, but learns that he has already checked out and his Lyft driver Chuck (Joe Gelchion) has taken him to his old house.
Peter decides to make amends, and begs Ed to move back in with the family.
The two finally reconcile, as Sally listens.
As time passes, Ed and Peter seem to finally be getting along until Ed leaves one day to be with Diane, with whom he is now in a relationship.
Peter looks on angrily, declaring a war on both of them as they leave.

4390037.title: Manhattan Manor
synopsis: Tom Atkins, a suave, well-dressed man in his custom-tailored Armani suit, takes his spot high above the hustling, bustling New York City.
He carefully settles down on a plush armchair atop the gleaming glass Liberty Plaza in Manhattan.
With his eyes tracing the sprawling cityscape below, he meticulously evaluates every transaction and shift of his multi-billion-dollar investment firm.
Across this sprawling city, in a high-rise penthouse somewhere near Central Park, Sandra Atkins, his breathtaking and stylish girlfriend, indulges in her own routine.
Despite her exclusion from the endless hustle of the Wall Street, she holds a disinterest towards their glamourous life.
A talented artist and philanthropist, she primps in front of her vanity, preparing for a posh Met Gala-themed gathering.
With sunset around the corner, the Atkins duo make their way to an exclusive rooftop gathering at the renowned Guggenheim Museum.
Masterfully, Tom socializes and networks with top-tier CEOs, political leaders, and influential celebrities.
As the bonded Bourbon flows and the night deepens, they return home in their sleek black limousine to their ornate Manhattan penthouse at Trump Tower.
Next morning, as the sun floods their penthouse in warm gold, Richard – Tom’s less affluent, but emotionally wealthier oldest friend from his humbler past visits the penthouse.
Over a cup of coffee, Richard speaks passionately about his selfless work at ‘The Sunshine Community Center’.
His words hang heavy in the opulent apartment, recounting his efforts to support the marginalized individuals residing in the struggling Lower East Side of Manhattan.
His burning passion sparks a glimmer of intrigue within Tom, stirring him from his stoic indifference.
Richard's humble plea for financial aid for the community centre spins off an unexpected gut punch for Tom.
His nonchalant dismissal for the cause not only reveals his lack of concern for altruistic endeavors but also a cold disregard for his old friend’s dedication.
That night, Sandra confronts Tom, her face stern as she cajoles him to visit the community center.
Her harsh words have a measure of desperate hope, yearning to inject some meaningful substance into their arid life of opulence.
Reluctantly, Tom succumbs to Sandra's persistence.
In his expensive attire, he enters the modestly furnished community center finding himself transported to a world far removed from his.
Here, Tom meets Emily, a young woman barely out of her teens who, despite her tender age, runs the center with grace and resilience.
However, in the heart of his newfound dedication, a conflict bubbles up.
Sandra feels increasingly isolated as Tom, oblivious to her emotional needs, focuses on his newfound passion.
As weeks fade into months, he starts distinguishing between the superficiality of his past life and the real, impactful work at the center.
A sudden, tragic curveball finds its way to Tom when Richard dies in a car accident.
The grief rattles him badly, the unexpected shock shaking his understanding of mortality, purpose, and direction.
This devastating news has an unsettling effect on Tom.
Feeling abandoned and emotionally deserted, Sandra ruptures his grief further by confronting Tom about his negligence, an eruption that tears through their lavishly furnished living room.
In an emotional spiral, Sandra walks out of their gilt-edged life at Trump Tower, leaving Tom smothered in regret and loneliness.
As Tom grieves over Richard’s untimely demise and Sandra’s abrupt departure, he finds strange solace in his newfound cause.
He becomes an even more regular presence at the community center, his new refuge from a world that now feels alien.
With a hesitant knock, Sandra returns to their not-so-forgotten penthouse, acknowledging the person she failed to see before - the new Tom.
Their reunion ignites an honest discussion about their evolved identities, their mission, and the purpose they now share.
There are apologies, tears, and a shared understanding of the change they have both undergone, creating a newfound respect erasing all ill feelings.
United, they acknowledge the significant growth they have undergone.
With a shared vision, they make a pact, a commitment to utilize their wealth, influence, and luminary resources at their disposal to enhance their humanitarian endeavors.
Overcome by Tom's profound transformation and sincerely moved by his newfound principles, Sandra accepts his proposal with tears glistening in her eyes.
Moving forward, the couple work harmoniously together to shape up ‘The Sunshine Community Center’, propelling it to unparalleled levels of success and community outreach.
They conduct numerous charity galas, fundraisers, and outreach programs, tapping into their affluent network, exposing the elite to a world beyond their ivory towers.
Regardless of the challenges they face together, they unfailingly remember Richard.
Emily becomes an integral part, her expertise and dedication recognized and deeply valued in their revolution, further strengthening their connection to the center.
The narrative takes a leap into time, as months of hard work and dedication lead to the much-awaited day.

The movie concludes with an emotional, well-attended unveiling ceremony of the newly refurbished ‘Richard's Sunshine Community Center.’ As the grand opening comes to a close, Tom, Sandra, and Emily stand, arms linked, in front of their labor of love.
With the bustling community around them, they share a proud, paused moment, reflecting on the strides they have taken together.
As the crowd thins and the evening twilight sets in, the once-indifferent Tom takes a moment to himself at the center.

With the closing credits rolling in, there remains behind a profoundly moving portrayal of two contrasting Manhattans, one of dazzling skyscrapers, dressed men and women, endless parties, and the other of struggle and hope, laughter and tears.

67754909.title: Canaan Land
synopsis: Billy Gantry is an aging gigolo living in Beverly Hills in the house of his girlfriend, Connie.
He makes money giving telephone psychic readings.
Connie catches him bedding his clients and kicks him out, leaving Billy homeless.
He leaves with just his guitar and the clothes on his back.
Billy heads to the California Institute of Abnormalarts, a North Hollywood nightclub and sideshow.
Billy performs a song, singing and playing guitar with the house band.
The lyrics describe a street preacher, a persona Billy's therapist says is a manic side of Billy's personality, triggered by stress and loss.
As Billy sings, clowns from the freak show dance.
Billy asks patrons of the nightclub to put him up for the night, but they refuse, knowing him to be a petty hustler.
Finally, Billy spots Pary, a woman who he performed psychic readings for earlier, and she invites him back to her place.
He talks her into lending him her red Jeep Cherokee and clothes from her late husband.
Billy, a former preacher, listens to the YouTube sermons of Sister Sara Sunday, a sincere evangelist with a small church.
Billy charms his way into her life and ministry.
Brother Billy and Sister Sara become tag-team preachers and romantic partners.
When Sara has to temporarily leave the church to care for her aging spiritual mother and mentor, ("Mother Grace"), Billy takes over.
He builds the church with fake miracles, including a staged resurrection, and gold glitter he claims is from the golden streets of Heaven.
He is aided by his friends Rocco (a seedy private eye), Laz (a Compton, California street kid), and Laz's father.
Billy's broadcasts on radio and TV include cameos by Hollywood stars.
Billy preaches at the Hollywood Bowl.
At the peak of his popularity, Billy is investigated by student reporters from a skepticism magazine.
They collaborate with a group of Me Too movement women who reveal how Billy conned them in the past to get sex and money.
Their videotaped testimonies are organized by Billy's Beverly Hills ex-girlfriend Connie and Psychic Insight (his former boss at the psychic network).
The scandal devastates Sara.
She throws Billy out of the church and breaks up with him.
After the breakup, Sara focuses on her ministry, preaching, singing at large Christian gatherings, and riding down Hollywood Boulevard as the queen of the Hollywood Christmas Parade.
Billy is homeless once again, and more depressed.
He jaywalks in a tunnel with semi-trailer trucks and stretches out his hands in a death wish, imitating Christ on the cross.
He visits a chapel and confesses he doesn't believe in God because a pastor abused him when he was a boy.
Billy picks up a young prostitute named Angel who turns out to be his daughter whom he abandoned years ago.
She asks him to give faith one last chance.
Billy asks for a Christmas miracle to restore his faith.
He sincerely changes and wants to demonstrate his repentance by his actions.
He gives money back to the poor he conned into giving him "love offerings," assisted by Laz.
He returns Pary's red Jeep and gives her money to pay for driving her Jeep so long.
He visits an orphanage and prays for a little girl in a wheelchair but makes sure all cellphone cameras are off.
The girl experiences a miraculous recovery but Billy refuses to exploit it.
Billy dresses in white as a sign of purity and repentance and joins others from Sara's church at the Santa Monica beach.
Sara recognizes Billy is changing and forgives him, but is unwilling to reunite with him romantically.
She gives him her Bible and encourages him to stay on the right path.
Sara tearfully watches him walk away at the Santa Monica Pier and prays for Billy.

69643386.title: You Ought To Have Departed
synopsis: Albert Bennett, a stoic businessman renowned for spearheading a successful software company in the techno-cities of Silicon Valley, lives an apparently enviable life in the ever-bustling bay of San Francisco.

His beloved wife, Amelia, a literary scholar noted for her profound writings, and their ardent seven-year-old daughter, Lily, with her insatiable enthusiasm for life, completes their picture-perfect family.
However, this tranquil existence takes an ominous turn when Albert's past, teeming with disturbing secrets, intrudes upon their peaceful lives.
One fine day, while attempting to ignore his past, a classified newspaper ad catches his eye — the sale of an inherently Gothic mansion sequestered amidst the serene beauty of the Colorado mountains.
Albert rashly decides to relocate to escape his haunting reminiscences.
Amelia, initially skeptical about such a massive transition, finally trusts her husband's judgment and agrees to the relocation.
Their first encounter with the daunting mansion is a mix of fascinating adventure and chilling trepidation.
Unable to contain her curiosity any longer, Amelia embarks on a scholarly exploration of the mansion.
As Amelia sifts through the ancient paraphernalia, she senses an overwhelming surge of the house's antiquated history.
The eeriness of the mansion escalates rapidly as the family settles in; peculiar events begin to unfurl constantly.
Amelia can't help but sense a lurking presence, a phantom in the dark.
Albert, amidst all these mounting oddities, is gradually unraveling.
His usually composed demeanor morphs into erratic outbursts, causing a shift in their marital dynamics.
Lily introduces them to her delightful companion, an unnamed imaginary friend with stories as fanciful as their sprawling stone-towered abode.
Her tales start uncovering intimate details about the mansion, baffling even Amelia who relentlessly intuits the mansion's complex tapestry of tales.
Amelia, riddled with terror, bravely vows to uncover the mansion's backstories, ostensibly the root of their present predicaments.
Through her research, Amelia uncovers horrifying tales of dark rituals and murders enacted in the mansion, blending seamlessly with their current spectral experiences.
Most disturbingly, she uncovers ties between the mansion's history and Albert's veiled past, a revelation that shakes her to the core.
Embracing her fear, Amelia confronts Albert about the discrepancies in his past.
Yet, he skillfully evades her questions, driving a wedge between them.
Meanwhile, the spectral aberrations within the mansion evolve from eerily harmless to dangerously threatening.
Amelia attempts to persuade Albert to leave the mansion, but his resistance only intensifies her suspicion about his connection to their horrifying experiences.
A breakthrough occurs during a fiery confrontation when Albert admits his involvement in a crime that took place within the mansion years ago.
Amelia attempts a truce with the vengeful spirit, promising to ensure Albert faces the repercussions of his past deeds.
Overwhelmed by regret, Albert finally confesses his guilt, and the tension escalates to a climax that comprises Amelia, Lily, Albert, and a relentless spectral entity seeking justice.
The ghostly presence demands retribution — the life of Albert.
Albert, grief-stricken and defeated, yields his life to the vengeful spirit.
Stunned by the catastrophic showdown, Amelia and Lily barely manage to escape the haunted mansion, leaving behind the horrors of the house and the life they had known with Albert.
They muster the courage to build a new life from the ruins of their experiences.
Their harrowing ordeal imbues them with an unprecedented strength and resilience.
The mansion, once again left desolate, quiets down with the spectral entity seemingly placated, awaiting the arrival of unsuspecting inhabitants to disturb its momentary stillness.
The film draws to a close amidst an ominous silence broken only by a Sinister whisper echoing eerily through the vast mansion, "You Ought To Have Departed..."

59389913.title: You Should Have Left
synopsis: Theodore Conroy is a retired banker married to Susanna, a much younger woman, and they have a daughter named Ella.
Theo is a jealous husband and constantly fears Susanna, a successful Hollywood actress, is cheating on him.
The family books a vacation in Wales, but there is something strange about the house—time passes unusually fast, and everybody experiences nightmares while staying there.
The couple also discovers that neither one of them made the booking, each thinking the other did it.
One night, Ella sees the shadow of a man on the wall.
The next morning, she asks Susanna why people dislike Theo.
Susanna reluctantly explains that Theo's first wife drowned in the bathtub, and people suspected that he killed her, though he was acquitted at trial.
While in town for supplies, the shopkeeper asks if Theo has met Stetler, who Theo presumes is the home owner.
He mysteriously gives Theo a drafting triangle and tells him to measure the right angles, leaving Theo confused.
Theo wrestles with feelings of jealousy and mistrust toward Susanna.
One evening, while she is taking a bath, Theo checks the messages on her phone and laptop.
Theo has a dream that night and sees someone has written in his meditation journal: "You should leave.
Go now."
The following morning, as he watches Susanna and Ella playing outside, he texts her.
At the same time he sees Susanna look at her phone, he hears a text vibration on the kitchen counter and finds an identical phone with his messages on the screen.
Realizing that she has a secret phone, he suspects she has been cheating on him.
He confronts Susanna, and she admits to an affair with another actor.
Theo asks her to leave for the night, and she goes into town to stay at an inn.
He returns to his journal to see that someone has now written “You should have left.
Now it’s too late.” Upon discovering an anomaly in the angle between the wall and floor, they measure the kitchen and find that it is larger inside than outside.
Ella and Theo get separated; the two of them appear to be experiencing separate visions in the dream world.
Once reunited, Theo calls Susanna, wanting her to come back and take him and Ella away from the house, but her phone is turned off.
He then calls the shopkeeper, inquiring whether he knows of any cab services in the area.
The shopkeeper replies that there are none and speaks of the house cryptically, saying that the Devil collects souls from there.
Desperate to escape the house, Theo and Ella decide to go to town by foot, but see a shadowy figure observing them from inside as they walk away from it.
After some time, they find they have circled back to the house.
Seeing no other option, they stay there for the night, but Theo enters the dream world again and sees his and Susanna's past selves as they first arrived at the house.
He then meets Stetler, who has taken Ella captive.
He takes Theo's form to taunt him and says he will return Ella on the condition that Theo does "what he must."
Ella is returned, relieving Theo.
The next day, Susanna returns to the house, and Theo gives her Ella.

He finally confesses to the true circumstances surrounding the death of his first wife: he did not directly kill her, but did not help when she was drowning; he simply watched her die because he had been miserable with her for so long.
He accepts that he belongs in the house.

Theo's spirit is then seen trapped inside the house, revealing he had been the figure watching himself and Ella leave the night before, having tried to warn his past self by writing the messages in his journal.
The shopkeeper's voice says that some people do not leave the house and that "the place finds them anyway."

4267262.title: Rochester's Descent
synopsis: The narrative begins with David Rochester, a middle-aged loner grappling with a profound limp in his right leg, taking up residence in a charming, old-fashioned Victorian bungalow, nestled in the scenic town of Oakwood.
Seeking solace in the healing powers of solitude, he endeavours to mend his fractured spirit and escape from the shadow of a traumatic past.
The story narrates the circumstances of Rochester's present anguish - a horrifying car accident on a stormy night that cruelly claims the life of his vivacious young daughter, Lily.
The crash left him physically impaired with a limp and emotionally scarred by perennial guilt and grief.
Rochester takes up his coat and badge again, accepting a post as a detective in the small, tight-knit police department of Oakwood.
His quiet life takes an unforeseen turn as Emily, a teenage resident of the town, mysteriously disappears.
This unsettling incident prompts the deeply worried Chief of Police to delegate the investigation to Rochester, trusting him to unravel the mystery.
With every evidence Rocherster traces, he begins to hear distant whispers navigating him through his inquiries.
Initially dismissing them as phantoms of the traumatic past, Rochester trivializes their importance, trying to keep his gnawing guilt and grief from engulfing him whole.
He is sucked into a whirlpool of deceit and corruption stretching out within the quiet town.
His relentless pursuit of truth draws him into a politically windstorm, the eye being Emily's disturbing links to Oakwood's poster boy, Mayor Carlson.
Unnamed, faceless threats start arriving at Rochester's doorstep, demanding him to cease his inquiry or brace for unpictured peril.

Threatened yet resilient, Rochester, fuelled by vengeance and a deep-set belief in justice, refuses to back down and continues to unearth the grim secrets hidden beneath the tranquil veneer of Oakwood.
As the threats surge, so do the enigmatic voices in Rochester's head.
Despite his hard skepticism, Rochester lets down his guard.
He starts trusting the phantasmal voices.
Guided by their opaque revelations, he pieces together shattered telltales, exposing Mayor Carlson's secret domain.
Anchored firmly in his resolve and carrying irrefutable proof, Rochester tenaciously confronts Carlson, accusing him of orchestrating Emily's vanishing.
The narrative sparks into a deadly race against the clock.
Rochester, drawing on every ounce of his will, deconstructs Carlson's monstrous plan to exploit innocent citizens of the unsuspecting town.
With every passing moment, the mental toll visibly depletes Rochester's physical strength.
It’s a struggle to keep his investigation afloat.
In the height of this chaos, Rochester is paid a visit by the spectral version of his late daughter Lily, her appearance offering hope and rekindling his faltering resolve.
The emotional impact of Lily's vision fuels Rochester through a climactic confrontation with the merciless Mayor Carlson, testing his endurance and sanity to their utmost.
With steadfast resolve and indomitable spirit, Rochester gathers his last vestiges of strength.
He manages to expose Carlson's villainy, safeguard potential victims and uphold justice.
Once Mayor Carlson's tyranny ends behind bars, the grief locked within Rochester's heart finally overflows.
He lets go of his tormented past, and with it, the consistent voices in his mind cease.
The story gradually winds down as Rochester, his spirit lightened and brimful of hope, takes a leave from the quaint Oakwood.

A post-credit sequence uncovers an intriguing twist - the distinct echo of the guiding voices resonate once again hinting that the benevolent entity, having completed its mission with Rochester, might have found its next charge.
The narrative leaves off on an open-ended gesture, leaving audiences on the edge, fueling anticipation for a thrilling sequel.

61522357.title: Wander (film)
synopsis: Arthur Bretnik is a mentally unstable conspiracy theorist and private investigator whose daughter was killed in a vehicle accident.

Prior to becoming a conspiracy theorist, he was a detective who investigated the unusual death of an individual whose chest appeared to have something explode out of it, and whose body was later stolen from the morgue.
Bretnik and his friend Jimmy Cleats host a podcast that discusses conspiracy theories.
One of the podcast's listeners, Elena Guzman, hires Bretnik to investigate the death of her daughter Zoe in the small town of Wander, New Mexico, which she believes was a covered-up murder.

When he arrives, he meets Sheriff Luis Santiago and attempts to investigate the incident, but becomes convinced that he is being followed and that the death may be part of the same "conspiracy cover up" that caused the death of his own daughter years prior.

Bretnik's suspicions reach their peak when, after believing he is being followed by two men in an old Jeep Cherokee, he discovers it transporting a woman's body, which it moves into a derelict garage.
When Bretnik goes to investigate, he discovers an underground laboratory where people are trapped and implanted with microchips.
Cleats arrives to investigate with Bretnik, and they discover that Elena and Zoe's identities are fake and that they are actually Sofia and Martina Lopez, missing persons.
The two set out to investigate.
When Bretnik and Cleats arrive at Sophia's, she attacks Bretnik and claims Cleats is involved before her microchip suddenly explodes, killing her.
Cleats claims the "involvement" she mentioned is that he got her to report the death to Bretnik for money, and the two bury Sofia's body in the desert.
Bretnik and Cleats then decide to investigate the garage, but, before going, Bretnik places an envelope in a mailbox.
Bretnik and Cleats then sneak into the garage to record proof of the laboratory and expose it to the public.
Meanwhile, Bretnik's lawyer, Shelly Luscomb, discovers Bretnik's empty trailer and determines he has traveled to Wander.
As Bretnik and Cleats enter the laboratory, the film cuts forward to show Bretnik being involved in a shootout before being apprehended by FBI Agent Nick Cassidy, who arrives with Shelly.
Bretnik is questioned, where he explains what happened after he and Cleats arrived at the garage.
When Bretnik and Cleats entered the laboratory, Bretnik learned the microchips are being used to control immigrants, minorities, and the lower class.
However, the laboratory was attacked by one of the men from the Jeep, and Cleats was shot.
Bretnik was saved by a woman named Elsa Viceroy, apparently from the CIA, and the two met with Sheriff Santiago, who was revealed to also be working against the microchip operation.
Elsa and Santiago explained that the victim whose body was stolen from the morgue, as well as Martina, were both embedded with microchips.
Bretnik, Elsa, and Santiago planned to assassinate Victor Canton, the inventor of the microchips, who was on a rare visit to Wander.
Sheriff Santiago met with the inventor and the men from the Jeep at the garage, while Elsa and Bretnik moved to ambush them.
Elsa shot the others, including Sheriff Santiago, before allowing Bretnik to avenge the deaths of his family and Cleats; Bretnik shot Canton multiple times, killing him.
Elsa then told Bretnik to wipe the data from the computer inside the garage before leaving.
Upon exiting the garage, Bretnik was apprehended by Agent Cassidy.

In the present, Shelly informs Bretnik that the medication he takes for his mental trauma causes anxiety and delusions, and tells him that the garage was fully derelict and empty, the morgue he investigated and found bodies in was not in use for years, and that Cleats' decapitated body was found in Bretnik's car.
Bretnik, unable to believe whether the events in Wander were true or simply his own delusions, and faced with the possibility that he killed his friend, breaks down.
Bretnik is placed in a holding cell awaiting placement in a mental institution.
He is met in his cell by Elsa and an alive-and-well Cleats.
They explain to Bretnik that the entire investigation was part of their plan: Bretnik was being used all along as a way to tie up loose ends.
Bretnik's mental state ensured he would continue to investigate and allowed them to pin any blame on the events in Wander on him.
In the mental facility, Bretnik barricades himself in his room and digs in his chest with a stolen pen.
As he lies on the floor bleeding, he laughs and smiles; in his hand is his own microchip, proving his earlier fears that he had a microchip placed within himself.
Meanwhile, the envelope Bretnik mailed earlier is sent to Shelly.
Inside the envelope is all of the evidence and photographs Bretnik took of the laboratory, which could allow the conspiracy to be exposed.

25321152.title: Misdeeds: Paradox-22 (2021 film)
synopsis: Our adventure begins with Sam, a dauntless photojournalist originally hailing from Planet-49, nestled amongst piles of rusted parts within a decrepit warehouse.
Using his communal skills, he hid in plain sight, snapping high-resolution photographs of the dastardly Crown Prince and cunning Psycho Jester.
As Sam covertly documented the conniving pair, he shivered with the chilling realization that he must send an urgent warning to the Galactic Authority of Planet-49.
Determined to intervene against this impending disaster, Sam attempted to sneak out of the warehouse.
He was stopped in his tracks as the Prince deployed the devastating surge of his Electrifying Scepter, followed by an explosive flash - the Jester's deadly Card Arsenal.
While the planet continued unaware of this tragic turn, news of Sam's abrupt disappearance filtered into a press conference, where an intrepid reporter named Lily was in attendance.

Before Lily could begin unraveling this concerning news, a dark swirl of inexplicable shadows descended upon the dense crowd, enshrouding Lily within its folds, and whisking her away to an unknown destination – a treacherous aerial van with an ominous matte-black exterior.
Through narrow lanes, the stealthy vehicle maneuvered with impressive dexterity, disappearing into alleys before any alarm could be raised.
Unconsciousness faded, allowing Lily to wake within a large, dimly lit room.
Alarmed, her gaze fell on a foreboding structure standing silently in the corner – a pulse bomb linked to the thudding rhythm of her terrified heart.

As she absorbed her bleak situation, the cruel figures crafted an elaborate web of surveillance and control through their sinister Alien-tech security system, using a wall-sized holographic screen in their underground lair.

Meanwhile, chance led Planet-49's indigenous superheroes – Hawk with her impeccable sight, Starburst with his metamorphic skills, and Quicksilver, the embodiment of speed, to stumble upon Sam's lifeless body.
They were startled by his tight grip – still persistently clutching onto his camera, filled with revealing photographs of his murderers.
The images were chilling - grotesque snapshots of a friend's hard-fought struggle.
Sam’s camera revealed a clue - a unique insignia that unmistakably belonged to the Crown Prince and Psycho Jester, sending a surge of chilling realization through the brave trio.
The threat was closer than they imagined, wrapped in a shroud of grim sobriety.
Struck by the precariousness of Lily's situation, the trio was immersed in a disquieting silence.
Their contemplative expressions reflected their dread, solidifying their purpose to save their reporter friend.
Their headquarters, usually peaceful and serene, was now humming with a frenzied energy as the team scurried to devise an infallible invasion plan to infiltrate the daunting fortress.
Hawk employed her supernatural vision to trace the geographical layout of the villain’s hideout, and Starburst utilized his 'morphing' ability to recreate plausible attack strategies.
Quicksilver, on the other hand, used his unparalleled speed to sketch a blueprint dodging ancient traps and modern security layers.
Lily outwitted the villains as she faked a confession and infiltrated their local broadcasting facility to embed a coded message within their propagandist content, hoping for a miraculous rescue.
The scrambled distress signal reached the superhero's AI interface, stirring the tumultuous quiet of their anxious headquarters.
The signal was a beacon of hope, a confrontation between audacity and villainy.
Lily’s ingenious broadcast ushered crucial adjustments in the rescue mission, triggering a surge of momentum.
The heroes swiftly amended their strategy, incorporating her hidden cues pointing towards her location.
With burning determination fueling their collective strength, they stormed the villain’s lair, their war cries tearing through the subterranean darkness.
The villains retaliated with their robotic army, transforming the deserted lair into a ground of dreadful combat.
The heroes, a triad of formidable powers, moved in synchronized harmony despite the chaotic ambush.
Their telepathic link enabled them to predict and maneuver, thrashing the enemy forces with calculated precision.
As the fight raged, Starburst harnessed his energy to topple the villains’ formidable defense network.
Their spirits remained undefeatable - their synergy resilient under the relentless onslaught.
As defeat loomed, the villains, in an act of treacherous desperation, unleashed their lethal secret weapons, escalating the intensity of the battle to an unprecedented height.
In response, the heroes advanced with indomitable courage, rendering the vicious attack ineffectual.
The climactic showdown began as the heroes managed to breach the villains' impenetrable force field, their forces surged onward, eyes fixated on rescuing Lily.
Their relentless strategy started to overpower the villains, each tactical strike revealing their insurmountable unity.
Their hard-fought triumph was a poignant moment for the heroes, marred by the lingering lament of their fallen comrade.
Their victory tasted bittersweet as Starburst swiftly moved towards Lily, each tick of the bomb acting as a perilous background score.
His precise touch dismantled the pulse bomb bomb, Lily’s erratic heartbeat slowing to a steadier rhythm.
As the dreadful ordeal ended, the heroes stood tall, their unfailing resolve reflected in their steely stare at the defeated enemies.
The villains were finally tamed under their might, their reign of terror brought to a sudden halt.
A wave of newfound relief and order swept over Planet-49 as the heroes handed over the villains to be held accountable by the Galactic Authority.
Through loss, victory and sacrifice, the small unit of friends and survivors paid tribute to the brave photojournalist, Sam, who had played a pivotal role in their success.
Through the painful memories, also bloomed the seed of hope.
Months later, Lily gave birth to a baby boy.
The innocent smile hid a powerful secret – an extraordinary power reminiscent of the trio's collective might.
As the heroes watched the newborn peacefully sleep, they vowed to safeguard the boy.
As custodians of Planet-49, they would ensure he grows up surrounded by love, wisdom, and the spirit of bravery.

68815370.title: Injustice (2021 film)
synopsis: On Earth-22 (or even Earth-49), Joker and Harley Quinn kill Jimmy Olsen, kidnap a recently pregnant Lois Lane and steal a nuclear weapon, which they connect to a heart rate monitor attached to Lois' heart.
Upon hearing of Lois' capture, Batman calls the Justice League to find her.
The Flash finds the Scarecrow dead in his lab and his supply of fear toxin missing, before being killed by a trap laid by Joker.
Lois's husband, a panicking Superman, eventually finds Joker and Harley hiding on a submarine but is attacked by Doomsday, whom he punches into space.

As the other heroes arrive and apprehend the Joker and Harley, Batman realizes that they have mixed the fear toxin with Kryptonite and used it to make Superman hallucinate that he is fighting Doomsday; in reality, he has beaten Lois to death.
This causes the bomb attached to her to detonate, destroying Metropolis and killing 11 million people.
A grief-stricken Superman then kills Joker in revenge.

While Green Arrow takes Harley to his hideout to protect her from Superman, the latter reveals his identity before the United Nations and announces his intentions to bring peace to Earth, by force if necessary.
The Justice League is left divided over Superman's actions; some members, such as Wonder Woman, support his new methods, while others, like Batman, keep their no-killing vow.
Other heroes, such as Aquaman, Shazam, and the other magic users, refuse to choose sides and leave the League with Hal Jordan stating that he and his fellow Green Lanterns are being recalled to Oa.
Meanwhile, the United States government becomes concerned that Superman will interfere in their operations, and have Mirror Master kidnap Jonathan Kent as leverage against him.
Superman begins to question his actions, but Wonder Woman reassures him that he is doing the right thing and offers to help him find Jonathan.
Confronting Mirror Master, Wonder Woman learns Jonathan's whereabouts, allowing Superman to rescue him.
Elsewhere, Batman confronts the President and warns him that Superman will kill him if he finds out that he ordered Jonathan's capture.
Later, Superman visits Batman in the Batcave to make peace, but they get into an argument over their ideological views and Batman refuses to join Superman.
While trying to stop Superman from relocating Arkham Asylum inmates to a more secure facility, Batman and Nightwing are shocked to discover that Robin has joined Superman.
Harley, who escaped Green Arrow's capture and decided to become a hero, releases the inmates, forcing Batman and Superman to temporarily put their differences aside to fight them.
During the battle, Robin lashes out in anger and accidentally kills Nightwing, leading to Batman disowning him.
Nightwing then meets Rama Kushna in the afterlife, who transforms him into Deadwing.
Robin attempts to convince Superman to ally with Ra's al Ghul, who declines.
Batman forms an underground resistance and plans to steal a red sun cannon from the Fortress of Solitude.

During the break-in, Superman overpowers Captain Atom, Ra's kills the Atom and destroys the cannon, and Green Arrow accidentally kills Jonathan, whom Superman had been keeping safe at the Fortress, causing Superman to murder him in revenge.

After Superman transforms the Earth into a police state using surveillance drones, Batman has Plastic Man break Mister Terrific out of prison and leaks video footage of Superman killing a group of partying teenagers inspired by Joker to ruin his public image, shocking Wonder Woman as a result.
In response, Superman allies with Ra's and dispatches Amazo to enforce global peace, but the android quickly turns violent in Smallville as Ra's had secretly programmed it to kill Superman.
Amazo kills Hawkman and Cyborg, but Batman and his allies arrive and help Superman and Wonder Woman destroy the android.
Meanwhile, Robin, having had a change of heart, duels and defeats Ra's with Deadwing's help, sparing Ra's life.
Despite their aid, Superman prepares to have the Insurgents arrested and incapacitates Wonder Woman after she turns on him, but is confronted by Superman from Earth-1, whom Mr.
Terrific had summoned.
Earth-22 Superman defeats his counterpart as the latter was holding back, but surrenders after being met with a Lois from Earth-9 who lost her Superman after becoming pregnant with his child.
Earth-9 Lois reminds Earth-22 Superman that just like for Earth-9's, life is sacred.
Realizing how far he has fallen, a remorseful Superman willingly agrees to be imprisoned.
Although unsure of what will happen next, Batman makes preparations to rebuild the world and his life with Catwoman.

57318280.title: The Patriarchal Duties of the Wain Heir
synopsis: During the opulent era of the 1880s, when London's aristocracy greatly valued ancestral background and wealth, the aristocratic Wain family unquestionably held top sway.
Respected for his tactful business methods and expansive property that extended from the city suburbs to the beautiful countryside, Richard Wain, the family's head, held wealth and influence.
Richard, who was enjoying his prosperous years, unexpectedly passed away, extinguishing the prosperous glow that once surrounded the Wain family.

Learning about his father's demise amidst the bustling city's trading businesses, Charles Wain, Richard’s only son, had been enjoying a moment of serenity within the flourishing gardens of their grand mansion referred to as “The Wainhouse”.
The elderly, rigid attorney of Richard, Mr. Edmonds, later convened in the mansion's sombre drawing room, to disclose the last will which named Charles as the sole successor.
Act two broadcasts heightened concerns of Charles precipitated by the nosediving production rates and low morale in his inherited steel company.
To escape the pandemonium, Charles often sought refuge in his late father's office, where he would mourn privately.
In these troubled times, an unknown but charismatic man named Winston stepped in, presenting a potential disastrous debt claim against Richard’s grand estate.
Winston's unforeseen presence further exacerbated the ongoing disaster.
His audacious claim put the venerable legacy Charles was fiercely trying to protect at risk.
In the third act, Charles delved headfirst into his father's shadowy past to discredit Winston's claims.
As he deciphered his father's paperwork packed away in dust-covered wood chests, he stumbled upon sordid secrets, clandestine deals, and betrayed promises.
As a result, Charles was faced with a crisis of faith, forced to grapple with the tarnished image of the man he had admired.
Overwhelmed with uncertainty and distress, Charles was torn between preserving his family's reputation and unveiling the hidden truth.
The fourth act unveils a shocking revelation as Charles unravels damning evidence of his father's concealed lifestyle.
It was discovered that his late father had secretly indulged in unpredictable gambling games and illegal enterprises, connecting the esteemed patriarch with Winston, a clandestine offender.
Armed with newfound determination and irrefutable evidence, Charles bravely confronts Winston, exposing the inconsistencies in his claim of debt.
This clash heads towards a satisfying finale as Charles successfully revealed Winston's deceit, ultimately preserving his family's reputation.
As though emerging from a violent storm, Charles stood as a victorious figure, soaked in painful lessons but finally at the helm of his Wain destiny.
The final act documented Charles’s transformation from an angst-ridden son to a competent corporate stalwart.
Using the shrewd business strategies absorbed from his father, Charles breathed new life into the decaying Wain empire.
Slowly, he regained respect from business peers and vying competitors, his tangible actions reinstating faith in the resilient Wain heritage, steadily thriving under his wise leadership.
Despite damaged by his father's dishonourable actions, Charles chose transparency over cover-ups when addressing his employees and associates.
In the ensuing climax, Charles’ true leadership strength was put to the fore, shining brilliantly.
Sound agreements hammered out in oak-panelled boardrooms and legal victories marked the beginning of a new era for the Wain family.
Charles, realizing that leadership wasn't merely about displaying power but about demonstrating care and responsibility, assumed his role with a renewed perspective.
The closing scene illustrated Charles within the ambit of their century-old family estate, his firm yet empathetic leadership serving as a rock-solid protection for the Wain name.
Charles had reshaped the Wain trajectory towards a stable path, vowing for a future characterized by accountability and decency rather than maintaining pretences.
The narrative ends with Charles, now hardened with life's robust lessons, carrying out his patriarchal responsibilities with diligence and honour.
As Charles gazed over the sprawling Wainhouse estate towards the setting sun, he fully comprehended his transformation from an unseasoned heir to a mature, respected patriarch.

61345469.title: The Electrical Life of Louis Wain
synopsis: In 1881, 18 months after his father's death, Louis Wain, the only male and eldest of the Wain family, becomes the primary breadwinner.
He supports five sisters and his mother working part-time as an illustrator for The Illustrated London News under editor Sir William Ingram.
Ingram offers him a full-time job, but Wain declines in order to try his hand at composing music and playwriting; which he hopes will support the family but neither venture is successful.
Louis hires Emily Richardson to be the new governess for his sisters.
The two become instantly attracted to each other, much to the dismay of the eldest sister, Caroline.
Louis decides to take the full time position in order to keep Emily as the governess.
One night, Louis takes the family, and Emily to the theatre to see The Tempest as an educational trip.

She comforts Louis in the men's restroom after he has a recurring nightmare about drowning during the performance, but inadvertently causes a scandal when nosy neighbor Mrs. DuFrane tells people about the incident.
Embarrassed, Caroline fires her that night.
Before she can leave, Louis professes his love for her and they begin a courtship.
In 1884, the couple marry, which causes another scandal for the Wain family due to her being 10 years older than him; and her social status as a governess which is considered lower class.
They move into a house in Hampstead, where Louis takes additional work as a freelance artist to continue supporting his mother and sisters.
Months later, Emily is diagnosed with breast cancer.
While walking in the countryside, they take in a stray kitten they name Peter, to relieve the grief of Emily's cancer.
The practice of keeping a cat as a pet was unusual in the Victorian era.
Louis begins painting realistic pictures of Peter, but the paintings become more unusual as Emily's condition worsens.
He makes the cats more anthropomorphic, with them engaging in human behaviour.
A financial crisis in England causes the paper to cut staff.
Sir William tells Louis that he will have cut his workload, and advises him to use the extra time to spend with Emily.
After showing Emily his work, she encourages him to show them to Sir William who uses the drawings in two pages of the Christmas edition.
Although the edition becomes a success, Emily dies months later.
Louis begins drawing more cat pictures to cope with losing the love of his life, creating whole cat societies, but it also begins to show Wain's detachment from reality.
By 1891, Wain's cat pictures become enormously popular.
They are featured on postcards, greeting cards, and other print materials.
Wain also sends some of his drawings abroad.
The drawings change peoples' perception of cats, making them acceptable as house pets.
He hosts cat-themed events and is made chairman of The National Cat Society.
Despite the popularity of his work, the family remains in debt.
Wain fails to copyright his work, so he cannot profit from any reproductions of the art.
To make matters worse, Marie, the youngest, begins to show signs of mental illness.
The debt causes the family to be evicted from the Hampstead home.
Sir William allows the family to stay at one of his properties at a reduced rate.
Marie is admitted to an asylum, and Peter dies, causing Wain's own mental health to deteriorate.
In 1907, Wain travels to New York, on a trip sponsored by newspaper magnate William Randolph Hearst.
Wain hopes to forge a successful career in America to alleviate his debts.
He meets Max Kase, who tells him that people love the pictures.
Days after arriving, he receives news that his mother has died of influenza.
He has some success in NYC, but returns to England in 1914 at Caroline's request.
Upon arriving home, Louis is given the news that Marie, too, has died from influenza.
Sir William also dies, succumbing to his gout.
The family is evicted, and moves into a smaller flat in London.
Louis continues to work as Britain enters World War I.
He hits his head trying to jump off a double decker bus, and falls into coma; where he sees a vision of 1999.
Coming out of the coma, he is inspired to design futuristic themed cat toys.
The toys are manufactured, which looks to change the Wains' fortunes, but their hopes are dashed when a German U-Boat sinks the ship carrying the toys.
In 1917, Caroline dies.
The losses of Emily, his mother, Marie, Peter, Sir William and Caroline causes Louis to go on a series of violent mental breakdowns.
In 1924, his sisters are forced to have him committed to the Springfield Mental Hospital in Tooting.
Dan Rider, an official inspecting the mental institution recognizes Louis; in 1881 Louis drew his dog Cleopatra for free while they rode a train.

After speaking with Louis, he starts a campaign, along with Wain's three remaining sisters (who never married) to raise money that will place Louis in a better facility that allows cats and provides patients access to outdoors.
The campaign gets an enormous response, as thousands of admirers of Wain's art contribute.
The author H.G.
Wells, also a fan of Louis's work, along with other prominent British figures, assist with the effort.
After raising the money needed.
Louis is transferred to Bethlem Royal Hospital in Southwark, where he has a cat companion.
In 1930, he is admitted to Napsbury Hospital in St. Albans.
Guided by Emily's spirit, and with his journal and a cut-out piece of Emily's old scarf, Louis goes out to the painted countryside, where Emily once told him that he would find her.

25804332.title: Triumph and Sorcery: Chronicles of the Coastal and Highland Rulers (2021 film)
synopsis: The opening scene begins grandiosely with a magnificent high-vaulted hall.
Celebrating recent triumph over the wicked sorcerer king, Mathühr, are two noteworthy heroes, Arion and Brin.
Arion is a beloved monarch whose populace genuinely cherishes him.
An equally adored figure, Brin is a brave prince warrior.
Their camaraderie and celebration paint a warm picture of unity.
As dusky twilight takes the center stage, Arion's immense love for his kingdom shines prominently.
The golden chandelier casting intricate shadows and illuminating the lavish victory feast is a metaphor for his unwavering commitment.
On the other hand, Brin reciprocates with an approving nod, subtly showcasing their alliance.
The grand feast is marked by infectious laughter and inspiring tales of unbelievable bravery.
It is a manifestation of their joy of triumph, indicating a profound sense of camaraderie among companions.
As evening falls, painting everything with a soft, surreal glow, a spontaneous decision is made for a horseback ride.
Arion and Brin traverse the rugged coastline, heading towards an abandoned battleground surrealistically embellished with ghostly white wildflowers.
The serenity of the scene is abruptly shattered upon the appearance of three hooded figures- mysterious sorceresses.
Their identities secured behind worn-out black hoods, they proceed with a prophecy that makes the blood run cold.
The enchantresses speak of a powerful amulet entwined with dark magic.
Lying hidden in the complex maze of 'Drowned Mountain,' the warning states, if left untouched, the amulet might bring unprecedented chaos.
The hero duo could only quiver before the women's haunting allure.
The sinister prophecy leaves a lasting imprint on their minds.
Both Arion and Brin wear masks of unease, contemplating the sorceresses' chilling prediction.
Amidst the ebb and flow of daily duties and endless sunrises transformed into sunsets, their minds remain fixated on the grim forewarning, their hearts dreading the unforeseen future.
Their worst fears come true when a series of brutal assassinations engulfs their kingdoms, leaving the subjects in a pervasive shroud of fear and uncertainty.
Bound by their duties and a desperate quest for calm, Arion and Brin convene a covert council meeting, pledging to unearth the accursed amulet.
Upon entrusting their respective dominions to their competent generals, they take the plunge into the unknown, beginning a high-risk expedition.

The daring journey charts through a myriad of landscapes - gnarled forests echoing with the whispers of the night, rushing rivers with tumultuous white rapids, and freezing mountaintops blanketed under a pristine layer of snow.
Each location provides a new litmus test, challenging their bravery and tenacity.
Amid gripping tension and dangerous enigmas, an old parchment is encountered.
The manuscript reveals a shocking kinship between the sorceresses and Mathühr, their defeated adversary.
The alarming revelation motivates them to question the veracity of the prophecy, stirring a whirlpool of skepticism and a sense of deep-rooted betrayal.
Physically exhausted but mentally unyielding, the two heroes press on, their resolve bolstered by the ever-present threat looming upon their precious kingdoms.
Unbeknownst to them, the malicious Mathühr masterminds a deadly scheme, dispatching his ruthless legion to eliminate the ignorant duo.
Intense chase sequences ensue across the diverse terrains, each escape a thrilling example of survival of the fittest, with their pulsating heartbeats echoing the pervasive suspense.
After enduring harsh trials and tribulations, the duo finally uncovers the elusive amulet, setting free its potent magical abilities.
Their moment of triumph evaporates when Mathühr, flanked by his deadly accomplices, traps them in a cunning ambush.
Employing sharp tactical minds and the amulet's newfound powers combined with their boundless bravery, the duo orchestrates an escape from the adversary's clutches.
As they trudge back home, they begin to comprehend the treacherous deceit by the sorceresses and the amulet's potentially savior-like role in safeguarding their realms.
They victoriously return to their kingdoms, signaling the dawn of a new era of liberation and peace.
A captivating image of prosperity and tranquility exuding throughout their lands is the crowning testament to the prophecy coming to fruition.
Each king exudes an watchful aura, bearing the responsibility of guarding against hidden threats, their reign marked by constant vigilance.
As the climax nears, the screen is dominated by the silhouette of stoic Arion and Brin against a picturesque sunset.
They stand tall on a vantage point, overlooking their vast dominions.
Their silhouettes glow like silent beacons of resoluteness and determination, reminders of their strenuous journey and victory.

60355157.title: The Tragedy of Macbeth (2021 film)
synopsis: Macbeth, Thane of Glamis, and Banquo, Thane of Lochaber, having led King Duncan's army to victory over the traitorous Thane of Cawdor, are approached by three witches on the battlefield.
The witches hail Macbeth as the future Thane of Cawdor and proclaim that he shall some day be King and that Banquo shall father a line of kings.

Soon thereafter, King Duncan fulfills the first prophecy by ordering the Thane of Ross to execute Cawdor and reinvest the title upon Macbeth, but King Duncan names his own son Malcolm as the prince of Cumberland, which Macbeth sees as an encumbrance to his path to the throne.
When Duncan spends a night at Macbeth's castle, Lady Macbeth, aware of the prophecies, convinces her husband to commit regicide.
She drugs the King's servants, and a hesitant Macbeth murders the King.
At dawn, Macduff, Thane of Fife, discovers the body, and Macbeth ties up loose ends by summarily executing the servants, ostensibly as just punishment for their supposed betrayal of the King.
Fearing for his own life, Malcolm flees to England, and Macbeth assumes the throne as the new King.
Uneasy over the prophecy concerning Banquo, Macbeth arranges to have him and his son Fleance murdered.
Macbeth's assassins, accompanied by Ross as the Third Murderer, kill Banquo.
Ross then pursues Fleance through a field.An increasingly paranoid Macbeth becomes a feared tyrant.
At a royal banquet, he hallucinates and begins raving at an apparition of Banquo.
Lady Macbeth has the guests dismissed before sedating Macbeth.
During his trance, Macbeth is again visited by the witches.
They conjure a vision of Fleance, who tells him to beware of Macduff, that he shall be King until Great Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane Hill, and that he shall be harmed by no man born of a woman.
Macbeth orders the whole Macduff household to be slaughtered; only Macduff survives, having fled to England earlier.
A guilt-ridden Lady Macbeth gradually descends into insanity.
