The electrifying final act captures their maiden flight as the re-energized group embarks on their first official mission, marking the solemn transition of leadership from the old guard to the new.
A tantalizing post-credit vignette teases the presence of a hitherto unseen cosmic power, setting the stage for a formidable adversary for our heroes in the upcoming sequel.

Embracing her destiny, Lily, resplendent in her bespoke superhero attire, leads the united next-generation defenders towards future high-stake adventures, the charge around the globe and beyond resoundingly signaled.

62897087.title: We Can Be Heroes (film)
synopsis: Missy Moreno is at home with her dad, Marcus, when they receive word to come to the rescue of heroes where Missy has to go with her father and be with other Heroics' children.
Missy meets the other children there:   Wheels, who possesses super-strength, but his muscles are too heavy for his skeletal system to support.
Noodles, who can stretch his body.
Ojo, who is mute and communicates through art.

A-Capella, who can telekinetically manipulate objects by singing Slo-Mo, who is always in slow motion Face Maker, who can morph his face into anyone Rewind and Fast Forward, twins who can alter time Wild Card, who has immense powers but no control over it Guppy, who has "shark strength" and can shape water into anything she can imagineThe kids watch the battle between the aliens and Heroics on television, ending with the Heroics' capture.
Missy realizes that Ojo's drawings tell the future.
When a drawing shows aliens breaking into the vault, the kids hatch a plan to escape.
Face Maker tricks the guards into coming into the vault where Guppy subdues them, but not before one of the guards triggers an emergency lockdown.
Rewind sends them back in time, Wheels stops the guard from pushing the button, and Noodles steals their security badges.
Mrs. Granada spots Missy in the hallway and seals the doors, but A-Capella makes a staircase to the roof, allowing them to escape.
Noodles secure a vehicle, and the kids escape.
They land at the home of Missy's grandmother, Anita Moreno, who is the Heroics' trainer and helps the kids master their powers and work as a team.
The aliens arrive and Grandma sends the kids through a tunnel that leads to an empty field before she is captured.
The kids spot an empty alien craft and use it to reach the Mother ship.
Locating a room with a purple pyramid, they see the president and Ms. Granada speaking.
They are alien spies, sent to prepare Earth for a "takeover".
The kids are placed in a cell.
Guppy makes a replica of the key from the children's tears and opens the door.
A fight between the kids and the aliens ensues, and Wild Card is caught and taken for questioning while the others seek the pyramid.
Wheels hacks into the motherboard, but Ojo reveals that she can speak and is the Supreme Commander of the aliens.
Missy communicates with Wild Card in the control room; Face Maker has switched places with him.
Granada goes after Wild Card, but not before the protective shield around the motherboard is deactivated.
With the kids holding off the aliens, Wheels and Noodles remove the motherboard and swap it with a new one deactivating the alien's rocket and foiling the takeover.
To the kids' surprise, their parents emerge from the rocket.
Ojo reveals that she and Ms. Granada faked the "takeover" to train the kids to be the new Heroics.
The kids reunite with their parents and are soon ready to save the world.

47422292.title: Best Wishes to You, John Doe
synopsis: Jane Doe, a recently divorced woman coping with the fallout of a bitter separation, checks into 'The Ashwood,' an enchantingly quaint inn nestled in the untouched wilderness.
She hopes the idyllic ambience could help her heal the scars of her painful past.
At the inn, she encounters John Doe, an appealingly atypical bellman with a mysterious and intriguing aura.
Jane finds herself irresistibly drawn towards him.
As their paths cross repeatedly within the inn, Jane begins feeling a strange connection with John.
She develops an inexplicable attraction towards him, an emotion John reciprocates, creating an unsaid bond between them.
One stormy evening, the inn's stone fireplace casts an intimate, soft orange glow around them, creating the perfect backdrop for an honest exchange.
John opens up about his past, sharing stories of his nomadic lifestyle and the trust issues that stemmed from it.
Jane devises a solution for John, offering him a position at her law firm, 'Doe & Associates,' as a paralegal, choosing to overlook his lack of formal education in law.
When John initially refuses, Jane reassures him that she will provide all the support he needs.
Struck by her sincerity, John decides to take the opportunity and leaves for New York City.
Jane enrolls him in night classes at NYU’s School of Law.
Despite initial misgivings, John starts to make significant progress and finds a sense of belonging.
Jane and John often work late, coming closer through their professional interactions while navigating complex legal scenarios.
Jane recognizes the increasingly strong bond between them.
Unfortunately, her ex-husband Richard, who is a partner at the law firm, discovers John’s past and threatens to expose it.
Facing pressure, John considers reverting to his old ways, but Jane stands up for him, even confessing her love for him for the first time.
Despite the backlash, John decides to stay and fight for his place.
His unique approach towards a patent lawsuit leads the firm to a surprising victory.
Richard reluctantly acknowledges his prejudice and apologizes to John.
Jane expresses her respect and admiration for John through her heartfelt wishes signalling the strength and depth of their bond.
In the end, with past adversities weathered together, Jane and John stand together, their bond stronger than ever.

6914334.title: The Scarlet Badge of Silence
synopsis: Benjamin Mortimer, the lanky silhouette of a once vigorous detective now spends his days nestled in the serene coastal embrace of Dunbar in Scotland.
His days of solitude are harshly interrupted with the arrival of an enigmatic letter adorned with the insignia of the British Armed Forces.

The parchment bears an urgent appeal for his once-renowned sleuthing skills concerning the abrupt and seemingly implausible death of a promising cadet, Samuel King, from the esteemed Royal Military Academy.
Haunted by the spectral presence of unresolved cases and the gnawing clutches of whiskey-induced oblivion, Benjamin wrestles internally with the request.
But ultimately, the allure of the old chase wins, and he sets off on a lengthy voyage to the imposing grounds of Sandhurst, the cradle of the military institution.
Upon reaching the prestigious Royal Military Academy, Benjamin encounters blatant scorn from its dwellers.
High-ranking officers and cocky trainees alike scorn him, stubbornly arguing that Samuel's tragic end resulted from a moment of immense distress manifested as self-infliction.
Benjamin refuses to bow down to their persistent mockery.

Determined, he embarks on his investigation, meticulously collecting fragments of truth that gradually cascade into a chilling suggestion—Samuel's suicide might be a calculated homicide masquerading behind a veil of self-destruction.

As the seasoned detective dives deeper into the maze of secrets, sinister instances of intimidation surface—a menacing barrage of anonymous notes, violent encounters in underlit ghastly alleyways, and surreptitious attempts aimed at obstructing his relentless pursuit of truth.
During the ordeal, Benjamin forms an unexpected alliance with Sarah, the sharp-witted daughter of the innkeeper at The Weeping Willow, his temporary refuge.
Sarah, equipped with a razor-sharp mind, becomes a valuable asset to his investigation.
Sarah is a vivacious woman craving an escape from the mundane monotony of her village life.
She gets entranced by the complexity woven into the case and eagerly thrusts herself into helping Benjamin untangle the mystery.
As they encode the cryptic enigma shadowing Samuel's downfall, the unlikely pair display impressive synergy.
Her spirited enthusiasm serves as a torch in Benjamin's darkest days, allowing him to shrug off his addiction temporarily.
Their relentless search finally fortifies into a blood-curdling revelation—a crimson insignia, cunningly concealed among the trappings of the seemingly self-inflicted act.
The demonic emblem stirs a shadowy memory within Benjamin—he recognizes it as a macabre symbol of a brutal academy tradition, a sacrificial ritual known infamously as ‘The Scarlet Badge.'

Sarah supports Benjamin's unpleasant conjecture, adding layers of gloom to the unpalatable truth with more tales of this merciless rite that had extinguished promising lives with ruthless precision in the past.
The duo’s daring entrance into this labyrinthine secret triggers alarms within the academy, leading top brass to retaliate by placing them under stringent detention, hoping to bury the scandal.
Ensnared within the gory confines they sought to expose, Benjamin resorts to the wisdom forged in his past experiences, conceiving an audacious plan to effect their escape.
Sarah proves to be an astounding accomplice, effectively playing the distressed prisoner while surreptitiously learning the guards' daily routines—crucial data for their imminent escape.
The stakes skyrocket; their mere quest for justice morphs into an existential struggle for survival in the deadly theater of intrigue.
With a combination of on-the-fly strategy and a liberal dash of good fortune, they escape their prison just in time for one final courageous showdown.
This climactic confrontation transpires in the bustling heart of the city square, surrounded by curious onlookers gripped by trepidation and anticipation.
Benjamin, armoring himself with unassailable truths, unmasks the academy's darkest secret—the horrifying reality of The Scarlet Badge—and unearths the ethically compromised parties involved.
The explosive revelation ruptures the reputational edifice of the prestigious academy, marking a sensational victory for the unlikely heroes.
Completed with the mission, Benjamin retreats back to his serene haven in Dunbar, emerging from his hermitage not as an obscure retiree but as a nationally hailed hero.
The adrenaline-laced journey impels Sarah to break free from the confines of her village, inspired to establish her identity after playing a critical role in solving Samuel's murder.
Dunbar bids a tearful adieu to its local hero, Benjamin, even as another troubling case emerges, indicating the old detective's potential reentry into the grand theater of crime-solving.

66914834.title: The Pale Blue Eye
synopsis: In October 1830, alcoholic retired detective Augustus Landor is asked by the military to investigate the hanging of Cadet Leroy Fry at the United States Military Academy.
Landor is a widower whose daughter Mattie ran off a few years ago.
After Fry was hanged, his heart was removed from his body.
Examining the corpse, Landor finds a small fragment of a note in Fry's hand.
Marks suggest that he did not hang himself but was murdered.
Landor secretly enlists the help of Edgar Allan Poe, another cadet at the academy.
Poe and Landor deduce that the note was summoning Fry to a secret meeting.
After a cow and a sheep are found butchered with their hearts removed, it is suspected that the murder could be linked to black magic rituals.
Another cadet, Ballinger, is found hanged with his heart and genitals removed.
A third cadet, Stoddard, disappears; Landor presumes Stoddard had reason to believe he was next in line to be killed.
Landor and Poe suspect the family of Dr. Daniel Marquis, who performed the autopsy on Fry.
Particular suspicion is on his son Artemus and his daughter Lea, who suffers from random seizures.
Landor confronts Dr. Marquis, who admits that he resorted to black magic to cure Lea of her seizures.
Poe is drugged and finds Artemus and Lea about to cut out his heart in accordance with the ritual.
Landor rescues Poe, but the building catches fire and Lea and Artemus die.
Thinking that the case is solved, the military thanks Landor for his service.
However, Poe confronts Landor with his realization that the handwriting on the note fragment in Fry's hand matches that of Landor.
It becomes apparent that Landor was the killer of the cadets.
Two years earlier, Landor's daughter Mattie was raped by Fry, Ballinger, and Stoddard after attending her first ball.
Traumatized, she killed herself by jumping off a cliff.
Landor pretended that she ran away.
Distraught, he set out to avenge his daughter.
He left the note for Fry, luring him to a lonely spot before hanging him.
A patrol happened to walk by so he was forced to leave the body there.
Lea and Artemus stole Fry's heart for their ritual.
After killing Ballinger, Landor mutilated his corpse to make it appear that the cadet had been murdered by the same "madman" who desecrated Fry's body.
Poe tells Landor he has two notes with handwriting samples that link Landor directly to the murders, but burns them instead.
Landor later stands at the cliff where his daughter leapt to her death.
He lets her hair ribbon float away in the wind, saying "Rest, my love".

3325551.title: Stonewall: A New Beginning (film)
synopsis: Arlo Killian and Mara Bennet decide to start their journey of ‘forever’ by purchasing an enchanting Victorian-style house in a peaceful, upscale neighborhood on the outskirts of Charleston, South Carolina.
The young couple moves in to initiate the next chapter of their lives.
The couple embraces their new surroundings, forging new careers in the city- Arlo as a history teacher and Mara as a nurse.
Their house, a spectacle of old-world charm, enthralls them.
They dive into a meticulous investigation of their abode’s rich past.
In the course of their explorations, they uncover a hidden attic.
Among the contents, they unearth numerous antiquated documents which reveal their home's remnants of a significant Civil War battle, The Battle of Secessionville.
As the couple starts piecing together their home’s history, they begin to encounter inexplicable phenomena.
Digging deeper into their house's history, Arlo unearths a collection of aged relics neatly buried in their backyard.
These include rifles from the Civil War era and a soldier's helmet with a curious ’J’ etched onto it.
Arlo, driven by his love for history, finds himself drawn into the secrets their house possesses.
His fascination with the connection between their dwelling, the battle site, and General Stonewall becomes his sole focus, leaving Mara to seek comfort elsewhere.
Mara finds a confidante in Mrs. Rebecca Morgan, their elderly neighbor who resides in the same suburb.
The couple’s lives are increasingly dominated by the mysteries of their house when Arlo begins to receive a series of anonymous death threats.
Unwilling to bow down to the threats, Arlo and Mara make the bold decision to penetrate further into their home’s obscured past.
Their efforts bear fruit when they decode entries in General Stonewall’s journal, leading to the revelation that the revered soldier had hidden a Civil War artifact within their property.
However, their discoveries unearth a formidable nemesis, Robert Dawson – a ruthless businessman with unending means and greed.
Arlo and Mara persist in their quest to uncover the artifact’s location, unknowingly becoming threats to Dawson and his plans.
Dawson plots to eradicate Arlo and Mara to claim the artifact.
Arlo and Mara discover the hiding spot of the artifact, unearthing a diamond-encrusted ceremonial sword that symbolized General Stonewall Jackson's leadership during The Battle of Secessionville.
Dawson plots to eradicate the couple from his path.
An unforeseen alliance turns the tide in their favor when Mr. and Mrs. Goodwin, their neighbors, intervene.
In a surprising turn of events, the spirit of General Stonewall Jackson guides Arlo, Mara, and the Goodwins through a clandestine escape route within the house.
With Dawson out of the picture, Arlo and Mara can finally breathe a sigh of relief, safely tucked in their beloved home.
The restless spirits of the fallen Civil War soldiers find solace leaving a soothing change in the house’s environmental aura.
Arlo and Mara dedicate their lives to preserving the history and turning their home into a small Civil War museum.
As a golden sunrise bathes their cherished home, Arlo and Mara stand embracing each other, looking forward to the promising future in their historically-rich dwelling.
In a post-credit scene, Mrs. Rebecca Morgan looks into the camera with a secretive smile.
A figure materializes behind her - General Stonewall Jackson.
Mrs. Morgan turns towards him, nodding in understanding, indicating a secret pact to continue protecting the house and preserving its history.
The spirit of Stonewall Jackson, satisfied that his legacy is protected and his spirit finally at peace, fades away quietly, leaving the room filled with an eerie calm.

66821123.title: Karen (film)
synopsis: Malik and Imani Jeffries, a young black couple, move into a new house in the fictional affluent suburban Atlanta community of Harvey Hill, named after Confederate general Daniel Harvey Hill.

Harvey Hill Homeowners Association president Karen Drexler, their next-door neighbor and a widowed stay-at-home mother of two, quickly introduces herself to Malik; she refuses to shake his hand, callously comments about not "having any cash" in her home, and installs a security camera directed towards their house.
Although perplexed by her behavior, the couple decides to ignore their concerns and focus on settling in.

Unbeknownst to both, the virulently racist Karen has Neo-Confederate memorabilia in her home and a reputation for abusing her power as president to target local black residents, often recruiting her equally racist brother, Atlanta Police Department patrolman Michael Wind, to assist her.
She soon starts harassing and stalking the couple, trying to find something she can use to remove them from Harvey Hill.

She discovers that Malik secretly smokes marijuana and catches her seventeen-year-old son Kyle watching the couple have sex through an open window, but when she raises the issue at a meeting of the association's executive board, the other members, disturbed by her bigoted remarks about African Americans, decide against taking any action.
After learning that the couple is holding a housewarming party for their friends, Karen convinces Imani that she wants to make amends and is invited.

At the party, she quickly offends everyone present, including the couple, by insinuating that black Americans are being too angry and that if they dislike the country, they should just return to Africa.
The next day, she encounters three young black men, demanding that they identify themselves.
They refuse, and she calls Mike, falsely accusing them of harassment.
He arrests them, but they are quickly released after video footage of her phone call, recorded by the trio, and their subsequent arrest, recorded by Imani on her cellphone, surfaces.
The association then fires her as president after being sued by prominent civil rights lawyer Charles Wright, the father of one of the young men.
Growing more deranged and frustrated, Karen gets Mike to pull Malik over while driving home from work by revealing his past marijuana usage.
Finding no marijuana in Malik's car, Mike plants a bag of the substance in the trunk, subsequently arresting him following a physical altercation.

After his rookie partner, Officer Hill, accuses him of racism, Mike threatens to kill Hill if he ever double-crosses him again in the field, warning that a secret brotherhood within the police force shields him from any charges.
Malik manages to post his own bail and arrives home the following morning.
Karen then visits Imani, asking her and Malik to leave the neighborhood to avoid further trouble, but Imani defiantly declines.

The couple then hires Charles to represent them, who shows them a file suggesting that after a Black vigilante killed her police officer husband Ken Drexler and two other officers a few years earlier, Karen became unhinged and was later dismissed from her job as an elementary school teacher for making racist remarks towards her students.

That night, Mike, alerted by Karen of recent events, arrives with a falsified search warrant and arrests Malik again for owning an unregistered handgun, and Imani tearfully calls Charles, who calls the precinct and discovers Malik was not formally booked.
Meanwhile, Karen cuts the power to the couple's house and breaks in with a gun.
While Imani defends herself with a sword, Karen shoots at her several times, prompting a neighbor to call the police.
Mike immediately rushes to Imani's house, where the siblings threaten her at gunpoint before Karen shoots her in the shoulder, seemingly killing her.
Hill rushes in, and a standoff ensues until Mike and Hill shoot each other at close range; Mike is killed while Hill is only slightly wounded.
Karen prepares to finish him off, but a still-alive Imani grabs Mike's gun and kills her in self-defense.
After Malik's release from custody, he and Imani receive a full apology and compensation from the city for their ordeal.
Imani, now pregnant, assumes Karen's position within the Homeowners Association and successfully renames the community to John Lewis.

66720491.title: The Insurmountable Burden of Monumental Skill
synopsis: Our film swings open with a visually captivating tour of Joe's opulent past.
Clips of magazines and newspapers, most notably The New York Times, flash onscreen, headlining his astronomical success.
Footage from late-night shows like the popular "Late Night Show with Dave Letterman", feature Joe's charismatic presence, both loved and admired by cheering crowds.
Celebrity-filled premieres at the iconic Chinese Theater immortalize him on the silver screen.
Joe was the glittering epitome of Hollywood success.
Joe's persona was a beacon, magnetically drawing people in.
Cameras ceaselessly pursued him, documenting every instant, every emotion.
A sea of fans, entranced by his talent, faithfully followed his every move, making him an omnipresent fixture in pop culture.
But time mutated these triumphs into memories, faded and forgotten.
The narrative dramatically transports us into the present, revealing Joe's solitary existence.
His life, once brimming with applause and adulation, stands in stark contrast to his current reality of loneliness, silence, and a discouraging lack of enthralling movie roles.
As the grip of depression tightens, Joe seeks refuge at the bottom of a whiskey bottle.
In a drunken stupor, he conjures up Joey, his younger, victorious self.
Joey, the vibrant superstar who once headlined the hit "Summer of '87", surfaces in the gloominess of his derelict one-room apartment.
Joey embodies a past that Joe is attempting to forget.
Master of satire, Joey criticizes Joe’s life choices, incessantly jabbing at his lackluster present life, reigniting dormant insecurities in Joe.
This unexpected vision of his past self creates riveting comedic exchanges as Joe finds himself ferociously arguing with Joey.
Brucie Stevens, Joe’s elderly nosy neighbor, is often privy to these heated debates, her amused bewilderment only adding to the hilarity.
Desperate to disentangle himself from Joey, Joe confides in Dr. Ian Marvin, an eccentric psychiatrist known for his unconventional approach.
Dr. Marvin attempts to cage Joey by sketching an invisible box in the air, spewing a babble of Latin and gibberish, a laughably absurd technique that utterly confounds Joe.
Every session meant to sever ties with Joey spirals into a comedy of errors.
Joe exits each one with mortifying embarrassment, blushing under the amused gaze of Mrs. Stevens, and often nursing physical scrapes from clumsily tripping over Dr. Marvin's esoteric contraptions.
As word spreads about Joe’s bizarre predicament, a feisty paparazzo from TMZ attempts to capture him off guard.
The resultant unintentionally hilarious fall into a Hollywood Walk of Fame handprint leaves every viewer in splits and Joe a viral sensation.
Revelations and regrets come hand in hand with Joey, as he brings to light Joe’s missed career opportunities, like turning down the lead role in "The Phantom Vigilante".
Ironically, Joey’s candid insights force Joe towards confronting the mistakes that led to his fall from grace.
As Joe begins to appreciate Joey’s influence, he gathers the resilience to rekindle his acting career, often resulting in comical exploits as he navigates unfamiliar grounds.
He auditions for a local amateur theatre group, "Shakespeare's Puppets", receiving publicly amused responses due to his flamboyant interpretations of Macbeth's tragedies.
His pursuit for rediscovery eventually leads him to join "The Comedy Knights," a local improv group.
Despite the generational gap, Joe’s overly dramatic suggestions create hilarious misunderstandings, reaffirming his love for acting, albeit a new kind.
Joe’s newfound acting endeavors catch the eye of Leonardo McVincent, longtime competitor and notorious name in the Hollywood circuit.
Offered an endorsement contract, Joe’s competitive spirit re-ignites, taking his relationship with Joey to a new level.
By accepting Joey as an integral part of himself, Joe discovers that success doesn't lie solely in fame.
His performances, grounded in genuine emotion, start receiving recognition and increasing offers from various indie film directors.
As he aligns himself with the indie circuit, his performances, laced with authenticity and consistency, garner an Indie Spirit Awards nomination, a testament to his evolving talent.
Stepping onto the red carpet again at the Indie Spirit Awards, Joe delivers a refreshingly candid acceptance speech, acknowledging the valuable role that Joey played in his unlikely comeback.
The film’s final shot plunges the audience into silence as it slowly fades out on Joe and Joey, laughing wholeheartedly in reminiscence of their shared journey.

64300244.title: The Unbearable Weight of Massive Talent
synopsis: Hollywood actor Nicolas "Nick" Cage is struggling with his career after being passed over for several major film roles and is constantly pestered and tormented by "Nicky", who appears to him as his younger (and more successful) self.
His relationship with his ex-wife Olivia and daughter Addy is also marred by years of emotional neglect.
Losing a key film role and following an embarrassing event at Addy's birthday party, Nick plans to retire from acting.
He decides to accept a vague offer of $1 million from his agent Richard Fink that involves going to Majorca to meet billionaire playboy Javi Gutierrez and to be the guest of honor at his birthday.

Upon meeting Javi, Nick is initially annoyed by his neediness and insistence that they create an improvisational movie based on a script he wrote, but is soon inspired by Javi's determination, and the two of them quickly bond over their surprisingly shared love of films such as The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari and Paddington 2 (the latter of which Nick watches for the first time with Javi).
Soon after, Nick is confronted by CIA agents Vivian and Martin.

They suspect that Javi, who they claim made his fortune through arms dealing, is behind the kidnapping of Maria, the daughter of a Catalan anti-crime politician, with the hope that he will drop out of an upcoming election.
Nick insists that his acting instincts would've detected if Javi was a criminal, but he eventually decides to help the CIA with the mission.

After successfully rigging the cameras in Javi's compound, Nick attends a party where he announces his collaboration with Javi on a new movie, as an excuse to stay on the compound long enough to find Maria.
After a misadventure involving LSD, Nick and Javi decide that their movie should be about their relationship.
Nick later discovers that Javi keeps a shrine room dedicated to all of his movies, including a wax figure of his character Castor Troy from the film Face/Off, complete with identical golden pistols.
Vivian suggests that Nick includes a kidnapping in their script, to get Javi's reaction to it.
Nick explains his new idea to Javi, who believes that Nick is distracted by his family issues.
Vivian tells Nick to flee, or possibly kill Javi, as Javi has discovered their plot.
But Javi reveals he's brought Nick's family to his villa.
Nick tries to make amends with them, but they reject his appeal and accuse him of prioritizing his film career over his family.
Javi privately goes to meet with his cousin Lucas, who is revealed to be the true arms dealer and the one who kidnapped Maria.
Lucas warns him that Nick is working with the CIA and pressures him to kill Nick, or else Lucas will kill Javi.
Nick and Javi face off, but neither can bring himself to kill the other.
Lucas sends his men after both of them, and they race back to the house to discover that Addy has been kidnapped.

Nick takes Javi, Olivia and Javi's assistant Gabriela to the CIA safe house, only for the house to have been compromised; Martin has been killed, while Vivian sacrifices herself to kill Lucas's men before they can ambush the group.
With Javi's help, Nick and Olivia pose as a reclusive criminal couple to get close to Lucas.
He figures out their plan, but they still manage to escape with Addy and Maria.
Nick, Addy, Olivia and Maria race to the American embassy while Javi and Gabriela stay behind to delay Lucas's pursuit.
Upon arrival, Lucas holds Nick at gunpoint, but Addy tosses him a knife which Nick uses to kill him—transitioning into the movie that Nick and Javi completed, presumably based on their adventure.
Nick is applauded for his new film and congratulates Javi before going home with his family to watch Paddington 2, now with a better relationship.

92379396.title: Legacy of Alliance 127: Unveiled Secrets
synopsis: The beginning of the movie is showcased with a high-octane sequence featuring Alliance 127, a commercial Boeing 777, falling victim to a hijack.
The consequent turmoil that ensues as the ill-fated plane meets its tragic end in a devastating crash is presented through a series of heart-wrenching sequences.
Leapfrogging to 2020, the narrative presents John Decker, a veteran CIA agent, being handed a classified report about Alliance 127.
The case is being reopened, due to the revelation of fresh evidence discovered amidst the debris of the crash site.
John, intrigued by the persisting anomalies that had marred the initial investigations, delves deep into the buried case files, seeking connections that previously slipped attention.
Assembling a team of relentless pursuers from different CIA branches, John includes Sarah Wilson, an audacious and brilliant field operative known for her ability to thrive under pressure.
Their relentless probe yields disconcerting leads that suggest a premeditated hijacking, turning the narrative on its head.
A comprehensive background check of the passengers puts a spotlight on nefarious connections connecting some of them to notorious underworld figures and high-ranking government officials.
Unknown enemies target Sarah with brutal precision, culminating in a shocking personal tragedy - the suspicious car crash that claims her brother Robert's life.
As they bore deeper into the case, 'Legacy', an obscure anti-terrorism operation, emerges as a potential cipher, capable of shedding light on their gnarly quest for the truth.
The narrative takes a sharp twist when it's revealed that 'Legacy' was sabotaged from within.
It's revealed to be an inside job, with government tiers connected to the conspiracy.
As John and his team grapple with collecting evidence against the powerful traitors, a deadly cat-and-mouse game ensues.
Meanwhile, Sarah undertakes a daring mission to infiltrate a base camp operated by the enemy.
In what follows, Sarah engages in an adrenaline-pumping chase to dodge her pursuers, barely managing to escape with the crucial evidence.
However, a jarring plot twist waits as a bullet strikes Sarah before she can completely evade capture.
In her final moments, she hands over the evidence to John.
Armed with the retrieved evidence, John wages a relentless battle against the corrupt officials.
As the malicious web behind the Alliance 127 incident unravels, a chilling truth casts a grim shadow over the international political panorama.
Yet, the resolution offers some relief as the innocent victims of the flight are exonerated posthumously.

The movie wraps up with emotionally stirring scenes, etching Sarah's ultimate sacrifice in the hearts of the audience, whose valorous spirit is immortalized by John as he lays a single red rose on her grave.
Taking a vow by her grave, John carries forth their shared mission of justice and transparency, promising to honor her legacy.

65343667.title: All the Old Knives
synopsis: In early 2020, CIA officer Henry Pelham is informed by his boss, Vick Wallinger, that the CIA has reopened the case of Turkish Alliance 127, a 2012 terrorist hijacking which ended in tragedy.
Headquarters suspects there was a leak from the Vienna station, where Henry and Vick work.
Henry is sent to interview Celia Harrison, who also worked at the Vienna station at the time of the hijacking.
Henry and Celia were lovers, but she left him shortly after the event.
Celia, now retired, lives in Carmel-by-the-Sea, California with her family.
Henry meets her at an upscale restaurant, which is almost empty of customers and staff.
As Henry and Celia talk, she reveals that an Austrian intelligence agent named Karl Stein approached her shortly after she moved to Carmel.
He wanted her to inform on her coworkers, but she refused.
Henry has Celia recall the events of the hijacking.
In a flashback to 2012, Flight 127 is on the runway when it is hijacked by four armed militants belonging to an Islamic terrorist group.
The Vienna station jumps into action to address the crisis and learns that Ilyas Shushani, a Chechen and former informant for Henry, may be involved.
The hijackers threaten to kill the passengers unless several of their comrades are released from custody.
Ahmed, a CIA courier who happened to be on the plane, contacts the CIA and suggests an attack via the plane's undercarriage.
Celia connects with a possible source named Mohammed, but the meeting seems to yield nothing of value.

Henry tells Celia and her mentor, Bill Compton, that when Henry worked in Moscow his superiors forced him to betray Ilyas to the Russian government as a trade-off for intel on an imminent attack on a U.S. embassy.
The Vienna station receives another message from Ahmed saying that the terrorists have a camera mounted on the plane's undercarriage and the assault should be called off.
Celia notices differences in the language of Ahmed's messages and fears he has been compromised.
Checking the station's phone logs, she notices that a call to Iran was placed from Bill's office phone.
Then Ahmed is killed and thrown off the plane.
The next day, Celia leaves both Henry and Vienna.
In the present, Henry asks why she ended their relationship so abruptly.
Celia reveals that she saw a call on Henry's cellphone from the same Iranian number that she had found in the station phone logs.
It is revealed that when the terrorists' demands were not met, they released sarin gas, killing themselves, the crew, and all passengers.
The Vienna station is devastated by the outcome.
Realizing that Henry was the leak, she left him but did not divulge her discovery to the CIA.

She further confesses that, after Henry contacted her to arrange this meeting, she contacted Karl Stein, and he arranged the meeting place, the staff, and fake customers, with the aim of poisoning Henry via his wine.
As Henry begins to succumb to the poison, Celia tearfully asks why he betrayed everyone to the terrorists.
He explains that he was lured into a meeting with Ilyas, who had become radicalized and masterminded the hijacking.
Ilyas' people staged the meeting between Mohammed and Celia to create the impression that Celia's life was in danger.
This pushed Henry into revealing the plan for an undercarriage assault, and then the presence of Ahmed on the plane, in exchange for her life.
Henry comes to terms with his impending death, and Celia returns home to her husband and children.
Karl calls Vick to report that Henry has died, revealing that they had been working together the entire time.

49260198.title: Narcotics Falcon
synopsis: The tranquility of the night was punctuated by the roaring engine of the "Narcotics Falcon", a bright-red Cessna 172 aircraft.
This unusual scene unfolded on an isolated airstrip just outside the peaceful town of Prescott, Idaho.
Thomas Granger, a man of an otherwise uneventful life, stood beside the craft, his nervous-looking demeanor revealing his terrible secret life.
His intense brown eyes constantly darted to the fences, the tall trees, the endless sky, scrutinizing every passing shadow cast by the moon's eerie light.
The rustling of the leaves in the wind did not escape his notice as he swiftly completed his inspection of the aircraft.
Deftly managing to bamboozle the customs authorities with forged paperwork, Thomas embarked on the treacherous yet routine cargo delivery flight.
The Falcon purred into motion, lighting up the airstrip before ascending into the moonlit night skies.
Once safely cloaked by the chilling vastness of the Pacific Ocean, Thomas clumsily unloaded a gargantuan package of pure cocaine.
His heart pounded as it disappeared into the ominous depths, disturbing an ancient entity that lay dormant for centuries.
Cocaine mixed with the seawater, provoking the slumbering creature.
The once serene Pacific surface roiled and thrashed about, signaling the awakening of an inexpressible terror from the abyss.
Upon returning, Thomas landed the Narcotics Falcon deliberately on an unmanaged hangar in the outskirts of Prescott.
He folded the wings of the aircraft with practiced ease trying to bury the night's ordeal and resume his day job as the town's undiscovered drug trafficker doubling as a mechanic.
However, innocence was lost for Prescott.
Residents began to experience vivid hallucinations of terrifying intensity, turning their peaceful lives into monstrous nightmares.
Unexplainable self-inflicted harm and death cases started increasing, casting a grim cloud over the once cheerful town.
Sheriff James Ellison, a stern and reserved figure with an uncanny knack for observation, was not blind to the disturbing changes.
He grew suspicious of Thomas, the only person who seemed to retain his normalcy amidst the chaos, and discreetly initiated an investigation.
In the unchartered depths of the Pacific, the awakened entity feasted on the disarray unfolding in Prescott.
It thrived on and morphed with the fear and despair rippling through the town, taking a grotesque, shadowy form.
An oppressive gloom hung heavily over Prescott as the entity began manifesting physically.
The quaint town transformed into the disturbing playground for an unimaginable terror.
Weighed down by guilt and horror, Thomas confessed his illicit drug trafficking activities to the astute Sheriff James.
He recognized the possible connection between his cocaine drops and the dread consuming Prescott.
Joining forces, Thomas, James, and Martha Greene, a revered local historian deeply rooted in the town's folklore, dug deep into the historical records.
They found frightening similarities between the town's current plight and ancient tales of a monstrous force, strengthening their conviction about the horrifying cause behind the chaos.
Left with no choice, Father Mathew, a religious priest and an expert in archaic exorcisms, reluctantly lent his services to their desperate attempt to sabotage the entity and restore peace.
They hatched a strategic plan, marshaling the terrified citizens towards a battle for survival against the remorseless entity.
The decisive standoff occurred at the very asphalt strip where Thomas's crime and the town's horror had both taken flight.
Through an intricate plan involving well-timed scares and staged panic, they baited the entity towards the airstrip.
Falling for their ploy, the entity anticipates a grand feast at the chaos of the inescapable trap, inching closer and closer to the staged ambush.
At the pivotal moment, Father Mathew initiated a powerful exorcism,  manifesting a strong spiritual barrier around the vicinity.
Meanwhile, Thomas and James hurriedly prepared a fake cocaine package filled with powdered sugar, replicating the original cocaine package.
In the gripping climax, the entity's powers abruptly faltered due to Father Mathew's heaven-sent exorcism.
Simultaneously, Thomas and James sprung their trap, dealing the final blow.
The entity faltered, caught of guard.
Its terrifying form wavered, its power dwindling without the cocaine-induced fear to nourish it.
The combined strength of the exorcism and the trap brought the entity to its crushing defeat.
Its death cry echoed around the silent town, signifying the end of the living nightmare.
The aftermath bore witness to a repentant Thomas renouncing his criminal past, forever scarred by the consequences of his actions.
Sheriff James Ellison, who believed in second chances, forgave Thomas and granted him the opportunity to mend his life.
Slowly, a semblance of normalcy began to emerge over the quiet streets of Prescott.
The haunting memories of the Narcotics Falcon slowly started fading away to the reassuring rhythm of daily life.
Despite the gradual recovery, the horrifying memory persisted, casting a long, lingering shadow over Prescott.
A silent testament to the fear and chaos that once reigned, a chilling reminder of the nightmare they had barely survived.

67054916.title: Cocaine Bear
synopsis: In 1985, drug smuggler Andrew C. Thornton II drops a shipment of cocaine from his plane.
He attempts to parachute out with a drug-filled duffel bag, but knocks himself unconscious on the doorframe, causing him to fall to his death.
His body lands in Knoxville, Tennessee, where he is identified by Bob, a local detective.
He concludes that the cocaine is likely from St. Louis drug kingpin Syd White, and the remainder is missing.
Meanwhile, in the Chattahoochee–Oconee National Forest, an American black bear eats some of the cocaine, becoming highly aggressive and attacking two hikers, Elsa and Olaf, killing the former.
In northeast Georgia, middle schooler Dee Dee lives with her mother, nurse Sari.
Dee Dee skips school with her best friend Henry in order to paint a picture of the falls in the forest.
On the trail to the falls, they find a lost brick of cocaine and ingest some before they are attacked by the bear.
Sari ventures into the forest to search for the children with Liz, a park ranger, and Peter, a wildlife activist.
They find Henry clinging to a tree, hiding from the bear.
The bear attacks, sending Peter stumbling through a pile of cocaine and slashing Liz in the process.
The bear tries to climb a tree and attack Henry but gets attracted to a cocaine-coated Peter.
Ignoring Henry, the bear kills Peter.
Sari and Henry flee deeper into the forest, and Liz sends for help.
In St. Louis, Syd sends his fixer Daveed to recover the remaining cocaine.
Daveed travels to Georgia with Eddie, Syd's son, who has grown depressed following the death of his wife and has abandoned his own son.
They arrive in Georgia, as does Bob.
At the forest station, Daveed gets into a fight with the Duchamps gang, three delinquents who cause trouble in the forest.
After Daveed beats them, one of the members, Stache, agrees to take Daveed and Eddie to recover some of the cocaine he stashed in a gazebo.
Liz arrives back at the station, pursued by the bear.
Liz accidentally kills Ponytail, one of the Duchamps, before the bear slaughters Vest, another of the Duchamps gang.
Paramedics Beth and Tom arrive and collect Liz after a brief skirmish with the bear.
They leave with Liz in an ambulance, but the bear pursues and jumps into the vehicle.
In the ensuing chaos, Tom is killed by the bear, while Liz falls out of the ambulance and is dragged to death on the road.
Beth loses control of the ambulance and crashes into a tree, causing her to fly through the windshield to her death.
Sari and Henry discover that Dee Dee left a trail of paint which they use to track her.
Daveed and Eddie are taken to the gazebo but when they encounter Bob there with the stashed duffel of cocaine, Bob wounds Daveed.
The bear appears, but Bob distracts it with the bag of coke.
Bob is suddenly shot fatally by Syd, who reveals that he is under pressure from his superiors to retrieve the cocaine.
Sari and Henry find Olaf, who is mourning Elsa; Olaf leads them to Dee Dee's hiding place in the bear's cave which contains two cubs, revealing that the bear is a mother.
Olaf leaves and is killed by the bear.
Syd, Eddie, and Daveed find the cave, which leads out to a ledge behind the falls.
The bear returns to the cave.
Sari, Henry, and Dee Dee jump into the water below to safety, followed by Eddie and Daveed, who have chosen to quit the drug business together, and they all survive.
However, Syd refuses to leave the bag of cocaine found in the cave.
He shoots and wounds the bear but is unsuccessful in killing it and is disemboweled by the bear and her cubs.
Later, Stache hitchhikes to New York with a duffel bag of cocaine, while Eddie, accompanied by Daveed and Bob's dog, reunites with his son.

47938129.title: Rock Rulers
synopsis: The narrative unfolds with a snapshot of Hunter Mars, constantly churning out new compositions inside his modest suburban home.
Dialogues throw light upon Hunter's fragmented family life and his resolve to become a successful musician.
Hunter's world is interrupted with a vibrant scene transition to a high school musical parade, featuring Leo Rodriguez, a gifted drummer.
A chance meeting at Jefferson High Parade leads to an electrifying jamming session between Hunter's guitar riffs and Leo's drumbeats.
With Hunter's entrepreneurial spirit, he sees an opportunity to form a rock band with Leo, termed 'Rock Rulers'.
Their garage becomes a nexus of musical creation.
Their performances at house parties and local events grab the attention of residents.
However, the sudden escalation to fame becomes a stressor for Leo, who begins to exhibit severe signs of performance anxiety.
Tensions rise when Hunter impulsively secures a grand show in Fernville's neighboring town without considering Leo's discomfort.
The plot takes a dramatic twist when Eric Banner, a talent scout from Apollo Records, makes a surprise appearance at their performance.
Buckling under the colossal weight of performance pressure, Leo messes up the hit number on stage.
Eric retracts his rumored recording contract.
Hunter is left heartbroken, and Leo is consumed by failure.
The duo part ways.
Leo reverts to his high school parade ensemble, whereas Hunter blames Leo for squandering their big break.
As the date for the grand Fernville High Parade draws closer, Leo decides to confront his fear.
In contrast, Hunter grapples with regret.
The parade day dawns with a visibly anxious Leo ready to conquer his fears.
Hunter joins Leo on stage midway through the performance.
Their performance captures Eric's attention.
The renewed strength of the 'Rock Rulers' prompt Eric to reconsider his earlier decision and offers Hunter and Leo a new opportunity to rise in the music world.
This offer serves as an olive branch between Hunter and Leo, allowing them to rebuild their friendship stronger.
With their bond renewed, the 'Rock Rulers', now signed under Apollo Records, are ready to embark on their shared dream.
As a closing shot, the camera pans out, framing the daunted yet eager duo, anticipating their new journey.

70279342.title: Metal Lords
synopsis: Metalhead Hunter Sylvester jams with his best friend, introverted Kevin Schlieb, who as yet only plays a single drum in the school's marching band.

During marching band practice (featuring Chuck Klosterman as the sensitive band leader), Kevin witnesses sensitive Scottish student Emily having a full meltdown and quitting band because of her lack of skill with the clarinet.
Later that day, Kevin drags Hunter to a party at Clay Moss' house and tries to act 'normal' while Hunter feels misplaced.
Kevin gets drunk and flirts with the girl Kendall, while Hunter gets into an altercation with jock Rocky "Skip" Hoffman.
Afterwards, Hunter discovers the school is holding a "Battle of the Bands", prompting him to sign up his and Kevin's band Skullfucker.
Hunter steals his father's AMEX card and buys US$13,500 in gear, including a full drum kit.
Kevin adopts a grueling, daily practice schedule after school, learning Hunter's playlists by ear; he notices that Emily is a skilled cello player with equal dedication.
They become mutually interested, which prompts Kevin to give her a copy of the metal songs playlist Hunter assigned him as "homework".
Meanwhile, Hunter auditions bassists to complete the trio, but is unsuccessful, and has a series of run-ins with Skip.
Kevin unsuccessfully tries to pitch Emily as their new bassist to Hunter.
Afterwards, he calls her to apologize for Hunter's behavior and they end up having sex in her van.
Kevin and Emily become a couple, which enrages Hunter, who believes she will be their "Yoko Ono".

While Kevin struggles to meet Hunter's professional-grade demands, Clay hears Kevin practicing and immediately recognizes his highly advanced abilities and 'intense' drumming style; since Mollycoddle's drummer is in rehab, he recruits Kevin for a gig at his sister's wedding.
During speech class, Hunter mocks Emily until she attacks him, breaking his guitar in the process.
These facts lead to an argument between Hunter and Kevin, who leaves Skullfucker.
As Kevin is performing at the wedding, Hunter tries to crash it to get him back into Skullfucker, so is arrested for trespassing.
Afterwards, Clay praises Kevin for his exceptional contributions, in particularly mastering the material on short notice and elevating the original pop music with flair from his advanced techniques.
Clay invites him to hang out and permanently join Mollycoddle for the Battle of the Bands, which he reluctantly accepts.
Kendall invites a drunk Kevin into the pool and flirts with him.
While they make out, his conscience materializes as heavy metal musicians Scott Ian, Tom Morello, Kirk Hammett and Rob Halford.
Halford makes Kevin realize he loves Emily and goes back to her.
Also missing Hunter, he discovers he was sent to rehab by his father as punishment.
Hunter discovers the clinic is run by Dr.
Troy Nix, famed lead guitarist of metal band Killoton and former Battle of the Bands champion.
Nix explains that Killoton broke up partially due to his alcohol abuse, which prompted him to straighten out his life, become a doctor and help other addicts.
Although Hunter is fit for discharge, due to clinic policy it cannot be until Monday.
Kevin breaks Hunter and Mollycoddle's drummer out from the clinic.
Dr. Nix finds them during their escape, but lets them go after giving Hunter a better guitar pick.
Hunter and Kevin go to Emily's, Hunter apologizes and invites her to be their cellist, but she turns them down as she does not feel ready.
At the Battle of the Bands, Kevin apologizes to Clay and presents Mollycoddle's now sober drummer to replace him.
As Kevin and Hunter are getting ready to perform as a duo, Emily joins them with an electric cello and dressed in gothic metal gear.
Just before they take the stage, Principal Swanson warns them the name "Skullfucker" is inappropriate for the event, forcing Emily to quickly change it to Skullflower.
Despite initial skepticism, their performance wins over the crowd.
That is, until a drunk Skip stumbles out of a mosh pit, pushing Hunter into his amp stack in the middle of his solo.
His amplifiers crash down, breaking his leg.
Later, the band reads in the paper that their performance went viral, despite losing the Battle of the Bands and coming in second behind Mollycoddle.

They conclude they are the moral winners of the contest as they were headliners, the entire crowd loved them and sang the chorus of their original song, and they landed on the front page of the newspaper.
They begin to practice with renewed vigor and camaraderie.

16966659.title: Harmony Falling (film)
synopsis: In the vast universe, among the myriad of stars and planets, exists a clover-shaped, intergalactic settlement star known as the Unknown Realm.
This peaceful outpost is inhabited by settlers led by our protagonist, Sam, a steadfast, diligent farmer who excels at cultivating the galaxy's bounty.
The individuals on the star are unique in the way they do not only exist physically but also mentally enmeshed to one another, in an all-encompassing spectral network known as the Eidolon.
Like a cosmic timepiece, signaling another rotation of their star, Sam dutifully rises each dawn to tend to his responsibilities.
At the heart of their community, large tables under looming bioluminescent trees serve as the stage for daily communal meals.
Settlers gather around, their laughter orchestrating melodious symphonies, shared stories of ancient predictions and past experiences fueling a sense of togetherness that is perpetually renewable.
Even in their tranquil existence, a quiet unease lurks beneath the placid surface, attributed to a strange phenomenon known as the Echo.
The Echo periodically appears, traveling murky depths, propelled by an elusive spectral force that trespasses the minds of the male settlers.
It infiltrates their inner-most sanctuaries unearthing personal thoughts, locked away secrets, turning them into shared matters.
Sam, renowned for his ironclad emotional resilience and unwavering stoicism, unexpectedly falls prey to the Echo.
With vivid visions haunting him and alien secrets not his own clouding his mind, his mental stability begins to waver.
Random shards of thoughts, emotions, and experiences swirl inside him, as if caught in a psychic dust storm.
In his overwhelmed state, he stumbles upon thoughts far more ominous than personal indiscretions: an impending extraterrestrial invasion looming threateningly in the subconscious of a fellow settler.
With his mind reeling from this revelation, Sam turns to his most trusted ally, Leo.
Word of the looming danger spurs others into action.
Mia, an accomplished warrior never one to shun a fight, and Grandpa Eli, a wise elder whose knowledge of the Unknown Realm spans decades, readily join forces with Sam and Leo to address the threat.

Despite murmurs of unease cascading through the ranks of the community, the council's adamant refusal to acknowledge the severity of the Echo and the imminent invasion only bifurcates the settlers' unity further.
Their initial strategy sessions are far from smooth, with thought intrusions from the Echo causing interruptions.
Yet, amidst the tumultuous exchange of ideas and the challenge of overcoming Echo distractions, they manage to discover a method to concentrate and filter out the superfluous noise.
An uncomfortable quiet is abruptly pierced when ominous alien ships rupture the obsidian-like serenity.
Invaders, armed with vicious talons and grotesque, glistening scales, launch their long-foreseen assault causing mayhem, destroying structures, and felling majestic bioluminescent trees.
Amidst the escalating chaos, Sam and his team spring into action.
With their newly refined Echo communication, they predict invader movements and transform their unsettling foreknowledge into a finely-tuned counteroffensive.
Their minds wrapped in an iron resolve, they exploit the Echo to turn their collective vulnerability into a formidable weapon against the invaders.
Channeling their collective mental strength like never before, they begin projecting overpowering emotions of fear, confusion, and vulnerability into the invaders' minds.
This resonating force seeps into the invaders' consciousness, causing discord and division.
In the ensuing disarray, Sam and his team strike back with coordinated efficiency.
After a grueling standoff, the invaders finally retreat, disappearing back into the vast celestial expanse from where they descended.
Celebrations ensue, victory tastes sweet, not born out of physical prowess but the power of collective mental resilience and unity.
Recognizing his leadership, courage, and strategic acumen, the settlers overwhelmingly elect him the new head of the settlement council.
Under the fresh leadership, the defense team assumes center stage to share their arduous journey of conquering and taming the Echo, turning a once feared phenomenon into a potent ally.
Now fortified by their experience and renewed determination, the settlers initiate the formidable task of rebuilding their homes.
Leading the way, Sam guides the reconstruction - every brick laid and every beam erected a testament to their resilience.
Working tirelessly, under the thoughtful leadership of Sam, the settlement regains its strength, as the Council fortifies the clover-shaped star and reinstates the Eidolon network.
As the interconnected minds regain their strength, they transform into once again a nexus – a network of harmonious, resilient, unified consciousness.

The Echo that was once a disruptive threat exposed their collective vulnerability yet also revealed their immense mental strength, leaving them prepared for any challenges that may lurk in the future, fortified by their newfound unity.

Their final story reverberates throughout the Unknown Realm, a symbol of endurance, evolution, and rebirth that rose from the conflicts and stands as a witness of the resilient, peaceful society painstakingly reborn from the ashes of adversity.

50781870.title: Chaos Walking (film)
synopsis: In 2257 AD, on the colony planet New World, all the male colonists have been afflicted with a condition called the Noise, which causes everyone to see and hear each other's thoughts.
The colonists were at war with the native humanoid species referred to as The Spackle, which killed all the female colonists, while half the men survived.
Todd Hewitt lives in Prentisstown with his adoptive fathers, Ben Moore and Cillian Boyd.
Other residents include the preacher Aaron, the town's mayor David Prentiss, and his son Davy.
Prentiss has learned to control his Noise, making his thoughts difficult to see and hear.
A spaceship that lost contact with the First Colony approaches New World and a scout ship is sent to investigate the planet, but it crashes.
Todd discovers someone stealing something and chases the thief, only to come upon the crash site.
Todd returns to the town and tries to keep quiet, but the other men hear and see his thoughts about the crashed ship.
They head to investigate the crash scene but find no survivors.
While Todd is alone, he meets Viola, the ship's only survivor.
He is shocked to see a girl, as he has never seen one before.
The men from Prentisstown capture Viola and she is brought to the mayor's home, where she is questioned about where she came from.
Prentiss leaves to go speak to the men and leaves Davy in charge of keeping an eye on her.
Davy unwittingly toys with one of Viola's gadgets, which causes it to shoot large holes in the walls, allowing Viola to escape.

During her escape, Viola overhears Prentiss talking about preventing her from contacting the colony's mothership, intercepting their landing, killing them while they are still under cryosleep, and scavenging the ship.
Viola hides in Todd's family's barn, where Todd eventually finds her.
Todd tries to hide Viola when one of Prentiss' men arrives looking for her.
Ben tells Todd about another settlement called Farbranch and says Viola will be safe there.
Viola escapes while Todd chases after her.
Prentiss and the men arrive at the farm, demanding Viola back as they believe she is a spy.
Davy kills Cillian, and Ben is forced to join them.
Meanwhile, Todd catches up to Viola and the two begin a journey to Farbranch, accompanied by Todd's dog, Manchee.
During the journey, Viola reveals to Todd that she is from a large Colony Ship carrying over four thousand passengers and that her parents died during the journey from Earth to the New World.
When they encounter a Spackle, Todd attempts to kill it in self-defense, but Viola stops him because it does not appear to be dangerous.
They arrive at Farbranch, a town inhabited by men, women, and children, some of whom are displeased with Todd's presence because he is from Prentisstown.
Todd discovers his mother's diary, but Viola reads it to him because he cannot.
The diary reveals that the women were not killed by the native aliens, but rather by Prentiss and the men of Prentisstown.
The men could not stand not knowing the thoughts of the women when they could hear theirs, which drove them crazy.
Prentiss and his men arrive, again demanding Viola.
Ben tries to get Todd to surrender Viola, but Todd is upset with him for lying.
Ben uses his Noise to create an image of Viola to distract Prentiss and his men, while Todd and Viola escape.
Aaron chases after them.
They come upon a boat, and, as they escape, Aaron kills Manchee, further enraging Todd.
The next day, Viola and Todd arrive at the ruins of the first colony ship.
They enter it and try to send a signal to the colony ship, but the antenna is damaged, so Todd attempts to repair it.
When Prentiss and his men arrive, Todd surrenders himself, as Prentiss is holding Ben hostage.
Aaron goes inside to kill Viola, but she immolates him with one of her gadgets.
Todd appears, but Prentiss shoots Ben.
Todd goes to him and, unknown to Prentiss, Ben gives him a knife.
Todd engages Prentiss, but he uses illusions of himself to distract Todd and shoots him.
As he is about to kill Todd, Todd uses illusions of his mother and other women, calling Prentiss a coward.
Viola pushes Prentiss off the cliff ledge to his death.
The colony ship appears in the sky, causing Davy and the remaining Prentisstown men to flee.
Todd wakes up in the colony ship's medical room, almost fully healed.
Viola tells him she has learned to love his planet and shows him the new colonies her people are building there.

53430185.title: Project Might
synopsis: Project Might dives into a decaying world left by societal neglect, focusing on a dystopian New York City severely blighted by an atmosphere of brazen lawlessness, skyrocketing crime rates, and rampant desperation.
Beneath the city's shiny veneer, a thriving but hazardous criminal hub teeters on edge, violently seething under the burden of its own vice.

Into these bleak surroundings, we meet our protagonist: Adrian Chester Grady, otherwise known by his chilling moniker, "Gecko", who earns his living within the acute perils of the illicit narcotics trade.
As a pivotal operator in the drug commerce, Gecko dives deep into a moral struggle over his chosen path, ensnared in the intricate and unsettling web spun by the city's dark underbelly.
As Gecko busily grapples with his life choices, a clandestine drug supplier from the depths of South America entices him with an extraordinary business proposal.

The supplier, the sinister and commanding figure known as Raul, offers a novel substance, "Might", a potent substance with extraordinary implications - granting its consumers drastically enhanced physical and cognitive abilities.
The concept of superhuman potential seizes Gecko's cynical crew, who promptly concoct plans to flood their narcotics markets throughout Brooklyn and Queens with this new product.
As "Might" saturates NYC, public sentiment fractures between the exhilaration of enhanced capabilities and the dread of adverse societal impacts.

Riveting stories of superhuman individuals demonstrating astonishing strength and unprecedented agility, vanish from sight or run with bullet-like velocity rapidly become the city's primary source of buzz.
The hegemony of "Might" and the urban legends it spawns propel massive profits and newfound power into Gecko's operation, making him a major influencer within New York’s colorful underworld.
But as "Might" ensnares the city in a cult-like grip, the urban scape transforms into an unpredictable battlefield, brimming with potential devastation.

Staring into the dark side of “Might,” its surging addiction rates, and the imminent collapse of integral city structures, Gecko struggles to reconcile his uneasy conscience with the reality of his actions.
Conflicted, Gecko summons the courage to confront Raul.
The face-off leads to a horrifying revelation: Raul himself is a user of "Might", embodying the terrifying potentiality of the drug.
Inebriated by his own power, Raul unveils his monstrous vision of assembling a force of super-powered individuals.
He peels away further layers of deception, revealing their city was merely an experimental petri dish, a living laboratory for the potent enhancer.
Struck with fear and repulsion by Raul's perverse ambition, Gecko backpedals from their unholy alliance and pledges to halt the rampant spread of destruction.
The stakes mount as Gecko musters his underworld contacts, who, like him, have grown weary of the fallout "Might" generates.
This band of regretful outlaws, united by their shared disillusionment, forms a pact of secrecy to combat Raul's machinations and his twisted supremacy.
Their audacious strategy: to take down Raul's operations from the pulsating heart of his production facility.
But their covert mission is jeopardized when a traitor in their midst exposes their intentions to Raul.
With the element of surprise lost, Gecko and his unlikely comrades find themselves systematically hunted by Raul's fearsome corps of South American guerrillas.
As their ranks begin to dwindle, either imprisoned by the enemy or meeting untimely ends, Gecko is cornered into a desperate decision.
Accepting the likelihood of his doom, he consumes a "Might" pill, compelling his body to undergo a startling transformation into a superhuman version of himself with superior strength and agility.
Now equipped with enhanced abilities, Gecko faces off against Raul and his mechanically modified roster of hoodlums in an epic struggle to reclaim the city's spirit.
An explosive showdown convulses through the dilapidated high-rises of Midtown Manhattan, filtered through the ghostly luminescence of twilight.
Drawing on his gritty resolve, Gecko manages to overpower his superior adversaries after a bruising battle.
With most of Raul's army incapacitated, Gecko seizes their remaining cache of "Might" pills.
Determined to rid the city of the drug and its nefarious influence, he sets the stockpile of "Might" ablaze.
Raul’s drug manufacturing warehouse is thus swallowed by a roaring inferno, symbolizing the end of the corrosive reign of "Might".
Emerging scathed but nonetheless triumphant, Gecko retreats into the labyrinth of Manhattan’s maze-like alleyways, his crucial mission accomplished.
Taking stock of his actions, Gecko shuns his previous underworld links.
Having tasted the heady and corrosive strength of "Might", he swears to destroy any recurrence of similar terrors.

Blessed with a newfound wisdom of dual existence –— an ordinary life versus an enhanced reality,   Gecko navigates his path to realizing that the real strength and power flow from courage and determination.
He now profoundly grasps the monstrous damage unleashed by unabated greed and the ceaseless pursuit of dominance.
As he carves out a fresh life distantly removed from his past, Gecko drums up support for a narcotic-free society, preventing the incubation of similar drugs.
Bidding his past adieu, Gecko commits himself to nursing his scarred city back to health.
Embracing the ashes of his past, he contributes significantly to New York's recovery from the debilitating "Might"-induced era of mayhem.
The journey of Gecko from a feared criminal to the city's savior encapsulates the infinite potential for redemption and transformation, underscoring the possibility of a brighter future.
As the curtain falls, we see Gecko astride a skyscraper, contemplating the dawn of a hopeful new day.
The sunrise piercing the gradually resuscitating skyline symbolizes the dawn of a new and promising era, and the salvation of the city.
The camera zooms in to capture Gecko's weathered yet hopeful countenance against this backdrop, hinting at the bright, promising future for New York.

58725278.title: Project Power
synopsis: In near-future New Orleans, a mysterious distributor offers a free supply of "Power"—a pill that grants various superpowers for five minutes—to a group of drug dealers, including one named Newt.
Six weeks later, Newt's teenage cousin Robin, a dealer herself, is nearly robbed by customers seeking Power.
She is rescued by NOPD Officer Frank Shaver, one of her regular buyers.
Art, a man hunting for the distributor "Biggie", tracks down Newt, who dies after a struggle when he overdoses on Power.
Frank foils a bank robbery by a Power-enhanced thief, but is suspended for using Power himself.
His captain reveals that government personnel are pressuring him to terminate any investigation into Power, and gives Frank a picture of the man they suspect to be the source of the drug: Art.
Using Newt's phone to find and abduct Robin, Art forces her to take him to the drug cartel's safehouse.
He is shot while eliminating several of the cartel's men, and discovers that Power users throughout New Orleans are being monitored as test subjects for the drug.
Art bonds with Robin as they treat his wounds, and reveals that after leaving the military, he was recruited by Teleios, a private defense contractor who experimented on him to create superpowers.
His daughter Tracy, born after the experiments, exhibited powers without ever taking the drug, and was abducted by Wallace, a Teleios operative.
Art and Robin find Biggie hosting a private demonstration of Project Power for a potential buyer near the Superdome, where large groups of Saints fans are arriving for a home game.
Biggie claims that Power represents "the next evolution of the human species", with the pill's powers derived from the abilities of animals, such as the chameleon or the wolverine frog.
Art interrogates Biggie at gunpoint and learns of a ship, the Genesis, but Frank intervenes, having tracked other users to the demonstration.
Biggie takes a dose of Power, forcing Art, Robin, and Frank to flee as Art kills Biggie in an explosion.
Frank arrests Art and informs his captain, but Art explains that the Power epidemic in New Orleans is mass testing to stabilize the drug, and that Tracy is the source of the drug's powers.
Having convinced Frank that his captain is actually taking orders from Teleios, Art purposely has himself captured by Teleios and taken aboard the Genesis.
Frank and Robin infiltrate the ship, and Art persuades a guard to free him.
Frank and Art kill Wallace, while Robin finds Tracy and reunites her with her father.
As the four attempt to flee, Robin is captured by Dr. Gardner, the head of Project Power, who demands Tracy in exchange for Robin's life.
Art confronts Gardner, using Power, which gives him the ability of a pistol shrimp to finally kill Gardner and her men.
Despite this costing Art his life, Tracy ultimately resurrects him with her powers.
They all escape the ship.
Frank intends to expose Project Power to the press, while Art decides to move on.
He gives Robin his truck and a bag full of money to cover her mother's medical needs, telling her to use the greatness inside of her.
Art and Tracy depart, finally free.
Meanwhile, Robin begins a new career as a rapper.

66187144.title: Elephant Odyssey: Sahara Expedition (2020 film)
synopsis: The film opens with a breathtaking panorama encompassing the endless, stark landscape of the Sahara Desert.
In a striking transition, the scene shifts to the lush effervescence of the Nile Delta.
The camera captures a vivid montage of flamingos tiptoeing through the shallow waters of the Nile.
Without warning, the serenity of the scene is disrupted by a sudden submersion into the water, revealing the lurking, predatory presence of a crocodile.
The African elephants make their imposing entrance, their thunderous trumpets heralding their authority as the unchallenged queens of the habitat.
The scene transitions to a makeshift camp set up by a diverse group of biologists from across the globe.
The transformation of the usually tranquil herd into a restless, nervous group is palpable.
Asha, the matriarch of the herd, steps into her indispensable role as the leader.
The camera adeptly captures the raw tension building with each stride, peaking in a jaw-clenching confrontation with a pride of lions.
Towards the edges of the herd, aged elephants and juvenile calves struggle to keep up.
The herd’s inherent will to survive shoves away specters of threat and despair.
They muster their strength and press forward.
The film perfectly captures the puzzling navigational abilities exhibited by the herd.
Asha’s leadership leads them consistently to scarce water sources concealed in the desert's heart.
The narrative gradually melds with historical footage, revealing the ultimate goal of this arduous journey - an oasis resting peacefully at the base of Mount Kilimanjaro.
However, the journey doesn't remain a quest for paradise but transcends into a tale of survival against not only natural challenges but anthropogenic ones.
The deserted human settlement, its deafening silence served as a stark reminder of the catastrophic effects of climate change.
The camera now focuses on individual elephants, especially a calf playful in its innocent escapades under the protective gaze of its affectionate mother.
Tantalizing the viewer with a first glimpse of the formidable Mount Kilimanjaro in the endless horizon.
With the sight of their destination, the youngest elephants break into an endearingly excited trot towards their new home.
The film captures the shot from a bird's eye view as the elephants merge into the awaiting vegetation.
Months of arduous travel culminates in a sequence capturing the joy of reaching the refuge.
As the story climaxes, the narrative swings back to the Nile Delta again, but this time it is being drenched by the annual rains.
The biologists, having witnessed the harrowing yet triumphant migration, jot down their experiences.
The summarizing commentary focuses on the urgent need for conservation efforts.
As an epilogue, the film provides a sweeping panorama of Mount Kilimanjaro's majestic slopes, with the victorious herd embarking on their homeward journey.

63486764.title: Elephant (2020 film)
synopsis: In the Kalahari Desert in Southern Africa, many African bush elephants prepare to migrate from their home in the Okavango Delta to a grassy paradise near Victoria Falls until the rains return.
The Herd is led by their great matriarch Gaia and her younger sister Shani, who has helped keep their family safe.
Shani has also been raising her spirited son Jomo, a very energetic young elephant who just wants to play with the other animals, such as lechwes and baboons.
When the land is about to dry up, Gaia leads the elephants to an almost dry waterhole to enjoy the mud before leaving the desert.
They are soon joined by other elephants who visit, play, and drink from the water.
When the water dries up, Gaia notices a baby elephant suffocating and stuck in the mud, so she goes to its rescue, and the baby is reunited with its mother.
The herd leaves the desert to join the other elephants on the long journey, they take a lunch break to have a family reunion with other herds of elephants, with some not seeing Gaia for over a year.
Jomo starts making new friends with the other baby elephants, and for ages, Shani reunites with many of her long-lost cousins.

Gaia's herd and other herds of elephants have no luck trying to find food, but a male elephant (who is visiting his family) uses his trunk to drop a bunch of seedpods from trees, allowing everyone to feast.
Gaia's herd come across ancient paths that their ancestors created when they migrated.
When they reach a dry waterhole, they notice an elephant skeleton.
Shani shows a confused Jomo a life lesson.
The herd moves on and find another waterhole (this time with water).
As the elephants drink, Jomo plays with a group of warthogs.
The water has been ruined by its previous visitors, so the elephants munch on Mopani trees, but are chased off by caterpillars who are eating all the leaves.
The Herd continues their journey to a small little island.
There is no water for them to drink, but Gaia leads her herd to some baobab trees which they could drink water from its sap.
Shani teaches the young elephants how to get sap by ripping the thick bark.
The Herd rests on the island for the night.
Continuing their journey, the Herd trudges through sandstorms.
Shani and Gaia sense the ground trembling, which means a river close by, but they are despaired when they reach the river.
It is far below the cliffs where the elephants are, but thanks to the help of a flock of Quelea birds, the herd makes their way to Victoria Falls.
The Herd happily drinks but are soon confronted by crocodiles, but the Herd escape without any member getting hurt.
They reach the islands, and the Herd enjoy their times in Victoria Falls and even munch on palm nuts.
Meanwhile, in the highlands of Angola, rain starts to pour, which means the water is going off to the Okavango Delta, Shani and Jomo's home.
Soon after, Gaia starts to get tired and weak and finds the food hard to eat.
She and The Herd start making their way back to Okavango.
Shani helps Gaia gather the herd, with Jomo by their side.
Gaia realizes that the Angolan falls are early, and she and Shani immediately gather the herd to use the shortest route, but they soon find themselves confronted by a pride of lions.
As the elephants settle in for the night, the lions attack Jomo, but he is saved by Shani.
But by morning, Gaia dies, with the herd sharing a mournful goodbye to their matriarch, while the lions share their feast.
Shani finds her leadership to the other elephants difficult.
A week later, an elephant gives birth to a newborn baby calf.
Jomo is unimpressed, but soon lets go of being the baby of the family and warms up to his new playmate.
Shani soon uses Gaia's memories and begins to lead the herd back to the Delta.
They are soon confronted by a rival herd of elephants, who are going after the newborn calf.
Shani stands her ground at the rival matriarch, and the rivals retreat.
They make their way home to the Okavango, where the land is bursting back to life.
The Herd soon accepts Shani as the new matriarch, while Jomo teaches the newborn calf how to play with the other animals.

35302270.title: The Enigma of the Divine Female: The Silent Recordings
synopsis: The film masterfully begins its narrative with a sweeping panoramic view of the city of Hollywood.
We are swiftly guided into the chaos of an artist's creative haven where an assortment of literary paraphernalia is scattered haphazardly on a home office desk.
A particularly significant hardcover book, "Divine Female," attracts our attention.

An anonymous, haunting voice-over, presumingly from the film's narrator, cleverly hints on the intriguing life of an erstwhile admired Hollywood actress whose life met an abrupt end under enigmatic circumstances.
