A desperate desire for answers compels her deeper into John's cryptic operations, immersing her in a world of silent heroes and untold narratives.
Inspired by John's selflessness, she resolves to continue his mission, pledging her full support to Médecins Sans Frontières.
Despite overwhelming odds, Sarah remains steadfast, gaining an understanding of John’s relentless commitment in highly hostile environments.
She discovers that this mission is not merely about individual safety but about saving countless innocent lives.
As she delves deeper into her investigation, she stumbles upon a bone-chilling conspiracy by 'The Patriots' set to destroy refugee camps in Lebanon.
Without wasting a moment, she alerts federal agents about the catastrophe brewing on the horizon.
Her bravery in exposing the conspiracy bears fruit, leading to the arrest of 'The Patriots' by quick-acting federal agents.
In the chaos ensuing from the operation 'The Patriots' exact their revenge by abducting Sarah.
Relying on her sharp intellect and John's legacy, she manages to escape the dilapidated warehouse where she was held captive, outsmarting her captors in the process.
Now safe and more determined than ever before, Sarah stands tall, her recycled fatigue serving as a symbol of her somber mission.
Inspired by her resolve and her first-hand experience of the battle between good and evil, she decides to dedicate her life to carrying forward John's humanitarian work.
As the day draws to a close, Sarah gazes at the scenic New York City skyline from her Brooklyn Heights rooftop, reflecting on her transformative journey.
From a simple sketch artist who shared a blissful existence with her husband, she has evolved into a fearless woman championing a humanitarian cause.
The title ‘Final Sundown’ symbolizes Sarah’s remarkable journey of transformation.
As 'The Final Sundown' rolls its last frame, the audience is left with a powerful message of resilience, hope, and courage.

69443427.title: After Love (2020 film)
synopsis: Mary Hussain (Joanna Scanlan) and her husband Ahmed (Nasser Memarzia) return home one night only for Ahmed to unexpectedly die.
After looking through Ahmed's wallet some time after his funeral, she notices a picture of a woman named Genevieve (Nathalie Richard) whom she has never heard of before.
Probing further, she looks at Ahmed's phone and sees multiple text messages he sent to the same woman, with the two of them suggestively discussing meeting up with each other.
Suspicious, Mary takes a ferry across the English Channel to Calais to find Genevieve.
After meeting her, Genevieve mistakes Mary for a cleaning lady and invites her inside for work.
Genevieve lives with her son Solomon (Talid Ariss), who she appears to be on uneasy terms with, and both of them plan to move away in a few days.
They're both unaware that Ahmed has died.
Mary hides her true identity and poses as a cleaner so she can learn more information.
While at her house, she notices multiple articles of Ahmed's clothing.
After walking in on a home movie tape with Genevieve, Ahmed, and Solomon, Mary realizes Genevieve and Solomon were Ahmed's secret family for many years.
One day, Mary sneaks into Genevieve's house to search for more information when Solomon suddenly arrives and sneaks another boy into his room.
Mary looks into their room and sees them passionately kissing each other.
While leaving, Solomon hears her and catches up to her outside.
Mary tells Solomon she was in their house to get her bag and that she won't tell Genevieve what Solomon did.
The next day, Mary explains to Solomon that she and Ahmed used to keep their relationship a secret as well when they were younger.
At first, they sent letters back and forth, but when Ahmed moved to Pakistan, he sent cassette tapes to Mary.
Later, Mary witnesses an argument between Genevieve and Solomon.
Solomon accuses his mother of cheating on Ahmed with several other men and refuses to move away with her as he wants to live with Ahmed instead.
When Mary confronts Genevieve about their argument, Genevieve says she was aware that Ahmed had another wife throughout the time she knew him, but continued to see Ahmed anyway.
She also learns that Ahmed lied about her as he said Mary was Pakistani and that they never had a child (Ahmed and Mary had a son many years ago who died at four months old).
Later, Mary poses as Ahmed and texts Solomon from his phone, where Solomon asks if he can move in with him.
As Genevieve prepares to move away, Mary makes some food for Solomon.
When Genevieve walks in, she and Solomon get into another heated argument, culminating with Mary slapping Solomon and Genevieve scolding Mary for hitting him.
Later, Mary admits to Genevieve that she's Ahmed's wife and she came to their house to get information.
Furious, Genevieve demands to know where Ahmed is.
After Solomon walks in the room, Mary says that Ahmed died.
Solomon tries to call Ahmed, only for his phone to ring in Mary's handbag, confirming that Mary posed as Ahmed.
Genevieve then throws Mary out of her house.
Later, Genevieve, Solomon, and Mary happen to visit Ahmed's grave at the same time (and, in turn, Ahmed's and Mary's son's grave, who's buried next to his father).
The three of them then return to Mary's house.
Genevieve tells Mary that she was always jealous that Ahmed wouldn't ever leave Mary for her, but was fine with sharing as she believed she had the better half of Ahmed.
Shortly after Genevieve leaves the room, Mary hears one of the cassette tapes that Ahmed made for her and walks downstairs to see Genevieve and Solomon listening to it.
Solomon initially gives the tape to Mary, but she allows him to keep it instead.
The two tearfully embrace.
In the final scene, the three of them visit the White Cliffs of Dover and look out at the English Channel.

98976952.title: Global Pursuit: The Search for Future Champions (2022 film)
synopsis: The film "Global Pursuit: The Search for Future Champions" begins with a snapshot of Layla Adams' life.
She's a seasoned talent scout for the acclaimed New York Knicks but she's tired, working exhausting hours scrutinizing an endless stream of high school basketball games.
One day, Charles, her boss and long-time mentor, gives Layla an audacious assignment.
She is charged with the mission to scour the globe, looking for seeds of basketball genius hiding in unlikely places.
As he outlines her task in a meeting full of stern faces and doubting eyes, Layla can't help but fantasize about a different life.
Stirred by the monotony, Layla embarks on a bold path - she decides to look for talent in neglected and underprivileged territories.
The first leg of her adventure takes her to the lively, vibrant slums of Mumbai, India.
Here she encounters Sonu, a waifish 16-year-old street baller with fire in his eyes and a surprising agility on the court.
Spain is her next destination, and from the crowd of eager teenagers, she witnesses Diego.
The Spanish boy's wiry frame belies his incredible dribbling skills and his ingenuity on the court.
Her last stop is Nigeria, where she meets Stella, a young girl who exudes tenacity and fearlessness.
Back at the Knicks' headquarters, her choices are met with skepticism.
The superior expect tradition, expect protégés from the usual basketball-powerhouse countries.
Still, Layla’s resolute belief in her scouts doesn't waver.
With sheer determination, she convinces Sonu, Diego, and Stella to dream bigger, promising them a shot at a prosperous basketball career in America.
Despite the language barriers, culture shock, and logistic complexities, she forges onward with the trio's aspirations at the forefront of her mission.
Layla, in collaboration with the stoical yet empathetic retired coach, Roger, oversees the rigorous training of the trio at the Knicks' facility.
Over time, Layla grows a strong emotional bond with the budding talents.
Under the grueling training, the trio’s impressive progress begins to manifest.
Their performance gradually sparks an element of surprise and grudging respect among the doubting superiors.
After months of relentless training, Layla pulls off a coup.
She secures spots for Sonu, Diego, and Stella in a semi-pro basketball league.
On the day of the league matches, an anxious Layla watches from the sidelines as her protégés step onto the court.
Their performances exceed expectations, dazzling against the seasoned semi-pro players, silencing critics, and winning the hearts of spectators.
Impressed by the latent talent she unearthed, Charles offers Layla a promotion.
In a shocking twist, she turns down the offer, expressing her desire to retire from professional scouting.
Her explanation reveals a deep-rooted discontentment with the bureaucracy of her job, rather than any disillusionment with the sport itself.
With her protégés now signing contracts with the New York Knicks, the film wind down.
We see a contented Layla, retired but still deeply involved in her protégés' lives, joyfully watching them make their mark against well-established basketball professionals.

"Global Pursuit: The Search for Future Champions" concludes with a poignant scene- Layla, amidst a jubilant crowd during a Knicks' game, proudly watching Sonu, Diego, and Stella, now NBA stars, setting the court on fire.
Their exciting journey from humble beginnings to the global stage of professional basketball is a testament to her faith in them and the potency of unconventional decisions.

65592324.title: Hustle (2022 film)
synopsis: Stanley Sugerman, a jaded international scout for the Philadelphia 76ers of the NBA, lives life on the road searching for future stars.
His frequent travel takes a toll on his wife Teresa and daughter Alex.
While he is liked by 76ers owner Rex Merrick, he clashes with Rex's son Vincent.
Rex promotes Stanley to assistant coach, allowing him to remain at home with his family.
The same evening, however, Rex dies, leaving Vince in charge.
Three months later, Vince demotes Stanley again to scout, sending him overseas.
His former college teammate Leon Rich encourages him to leave the 76ers and also become a player agent.
When Stanley's plan to scout a player in Spain falls through, watching a local pick-up game, he is stunned by an incredibly talented unknown player.
Stanley attempts to speak with the man, Bo Cruz, but is rebuffed until he makes a FaceTime call to Dirk Nowitzki to prove his legitimacy.

Bo and his mother Paola recount his life story: he was a talented player from an early age and was invited to play in America at age 15, but stayed in Spain after his girlfriend became pregnant with his daughter Lucia.
Bo now works construction and makes extra money hustling at basketball.
After an impressive workout with members of the Spanish national team, Stanley urges the 76ers front office to sign Cruz immediately, but Vincent is unconvinced.
Taking matters into his own hands, Stanley pays to bring Cruz to the US, telling him he will be signed by the Sixers or enter the NBA draft.
At the airport, Bo is detained for an aggravated assault conviction he received in Spain.
He is released, but warned that he could be deported if he were to be arrested in America.
Stanley takes Bo to play at a showcase organized by Leon, which is also attended by the presumptive second overall pick Kermit Wilts.
Stanley advises Bo that if he shuts down Wilts, it will significantly raise his stock with the Sixers.
During the workout, Cruz shows flashes of talent, but struggles on offense and at guarding Wilts, who trash talks him and throws him off his game.
When Vince passes on Bo, Stanley quits the 76ers to prepare Cruz for the NBA Draft Combine six weeks away.
Telling Bo his only weakness is his sensitivity, he builds on his mental toughness.
Teresa and Alex assist with the training by preparing meals and taping workouts.
Bo improves dramatically through Stanley's coaching, but Leon cannot get him into the Draft Combine after Vince spreads information about Bo's assault charge.
Furious at Stanley, Bo eventually reveals the charge stemmed from a fight with Lucia's mother's boyfriend after she tried to claim sole custody of Lucia.
Stanley admits his injured hand was from a drunk driving crash while in college, derailing his basketball team's season and putting him in jail for six months.
Their trust renewed, Stanley works tirelessly to get Bo into the combine, without success.
To create interest, the Sugermans enlist Julius Erving to create a viral video of "the Boa Challenge", where people, including 76ers player Tobias Harris, attempt to score on Bo for money.
Cruz is eventually accepted into the combine, and Stanley flies Lucia and Paola to the US to support him.
Bo impresses in the physical elements of the combine, but faces off with Wilts again in a five-on-five exhibition game.
He initially performs well, but Kermit begins talking trash about Bo's daughter and mother, eventually breaking his composure as he pushes Kermit down the floor.
Bo then storms out of the combine.
Thinking that their journey is over, Stanley accompanies Bo to the airport.

However, before Bo's plane leaves for Spain, Stanley receives a call from Leon informing about a private game for players and front office members and that Bo and Kermit have both been invited to participate.
Playing without pressure, Cruz locks down Wilts defensively and demonstrates his offensive abilities.
Rex's daughter Kat, who recognizes Stanley's talent, reveals she is taking over from Vince and rehires him.
Five months later, the 76ers and Boston Celtics tip off for a game against each other with Stanley now the assistant coach of the 76ers and Bo playing for the Boston Celtics.

60396340.title: Suburban Shadows
synopsis: As the movie unfolds, we see John, a self-assured computer engineer, and Mary, a perpetually vibrant schoolteacher and newlywed wife, relocating to a delightful Victorian-style house.
Nestled in the serenity of Massachusetts's suburban landscape, their newfound residence looks every bit the charming home they'd always dreamed of.
As the couple acclimatizes to their new home, their bright faces beam with a profound sense of joy.
They look forward to cultivating their vegetable patch in the verdant backyard and inviting friends over to their quirky abode for intimate dinner parties.
However, their joyous reality slowly begins to intertwine with an unfamiliar, ominous undercurrent.
Buried beneath the façade of the picturesque home lie potential challenges and mysteries that elude the couple's knowledge.
Their excitement begins to oscillate between anticipation and unease as they meet with the house's enigmatic architect, Robert Smith.
Distinguished by his white, bushy beard and a curt demeanour, Smith imparts an unsettling presence that permeates the serene household.

Smith's peculiar behavior, accentuated by his avoidance of direct eye contact and his cryptic responses to their questions about the house, unleashes the first waves of suspicion in the couple's mind, consequently shadowing their initial enthusiasm.
A particular day turned pivotal when Mary stumbles on a newspaper clipping, aged and frail.
The piece hinted at Robert Smith's potential involvement in occult practices and his connection with a secretive, notorious society, shrouding him in an aura of mystery.
This revelation strikes Mary like a lightning bolt, triggering a whirlpool of curiosity intertwined with escalating apprehension.
John, however, brushes these allegations off as nothing more than small-town chatter, a classic case of the public's proclivity towards exaggerated tales and sensationalism.
Then follows a phase where they endeavor to retain normalcy in their enigmatic home until an antiquated wooden chest springs up amid the attic's dust.
This chest conceals antique curios and pale yellow letters, their antiquity echoing corresponding tales unspoken.
The letters, festooned with grotesque and unreadable symbols, hold an eerie gravitas.
Meanwhile, the curious trinkets bear an uncanny resemblance to the tools often associated with occult rituals.
The harsh reality of their situation dawns on Mary, spiraling her into a state of fear-stricken anticipation.

Their once idyllic house now transmogrifies into a hotbed of uncanny phenomena - inexplicable creaking sounds echoing in the dead of night, household objects migrating on their own, and fleeting shadows dashing across rooms, fostering an environment of discomfort.
As Mary wrestles with her mounting fears, John, spurred by resolve, plunges headfirst into investigating Robert Smith's past architectural endeavors.
His in-depth scrutiny into Smith's previous constructions reveals an unsettling pattern of otherworldly occurrences and riddles associated with Smith's other works.

The hair-raising accounts of Smith's past creations—events chalked up to accidents, mysterious happenings, and abruptly abandoned houses—force John to confront and reassess his initial dismissive stance.
As the narrative progresses, John and Mary develop a close bond with their neighbors, a pair of elderly folks.
This friendship unravels hushed whispers and shared fearful glances, reflecting parallel bizarre experiences in their neighbor's home.

Despite the fear clearly etched on their faces, the neighbors remain tight-lipped about their experiences, living under the constant threat of societal judgement and the possibility of social exclusion.
Accepting the supernatural presence as a grim reality, John and Mary seek guidance from Father Andrew.
A respected local priest, Father Andrew is revered for the profound wisdom he's accumulated over the years.
Father Andrew, a man of unwavering faith and remarkable spirit, agrees to perform an exorcism.
Yet, he warns of a potentially hazardous backlash, a response from the spirits at being banished from the premises.
The prospect of an impending exorcism instills a mix of fear and hope in the couple.
Yet, their anticipation is short-lived.
Father Andrew vanishes without a hint, plunging their community into a pit of shock and uncertainty.
Father Andrew's abrupt and inexplicable disappearance causes ripples in the local community, painting an atmosphere swirling with shock, fear, and insidious suspicions.
Now pressed into a corner by their circumstances, with increasing panic gripping their hearts, John and Mary engage Amelia Brown's services.
A reputed psychic, Amelia is revered for her bravery and keen intuition.
Amelia, a striking woman in her late forties with soul-searching blue eyes, arrives, radiating an aura of calmness.
Her serene presence offers a momentary respite to the harrowed couple.
Amelia's revelations force the couple to confront the alarming reality of Smith's malevolence.
He had intentionally ensnared anguished spirits within the confines of his architectural marvels, intending to weaponize them.
Amelia paints a daunting picture before the couple.
To rid their home of these long-lingering spirits, they would need to muster their deepest courage and prepare for massive psychological onslaught.
Notwithstanding the rising terror gnawing at their hearts, John and Mary stand resolute.
They pledge to rid their home of the tormenting spirits, come what may.
Moved by the couple's resolve, Amelia devises a risky plan.
Her strategy involves beguiling the restless spirit into revealing its existence.
Guided by Amelia's instructions, John and Mary recreate occult rituals, hoping to dupe the spirit into considering them part of its fold.
The spirit, intrigued by the couple's faux occult practices, reveals its presence, proving Amelia's theory to be accurate.
Seizing the opening, John and Mary doggedly continue their charade, emboldening the spirit to confide further into Smith's esoteric rituals.
Angered by their audacity, the spirit (now known to be a wrathful female specter) discloses the convoluted ritual necessary to sever its mystical bond with the house.
Sensing their duplicity, the spirits' skepticism manifests as furious tempests tearing through the house, flooding the interiors with icy gales.
The house throbs with the spirit's wrath, culminating in Amelia being forcibly hurled away by an indiscernible force, leaving a flustered John and Mary on their own.
Facing limited options, John and Mary scramble to enact the complex exorcism ritual as revealed by the incensed spirit.
Their frenzied attempts to complete the ritual, amid the relentless onslaught from the unseen spirit, form the heart-stopping climax of the movie.
Even as fear flutters in their gaze and sweat trickles down their faces, John and Mary exhibit unyielding unity, holding their ground against their spectral adversary.
Their tenacity eventually wins.
The mysterious bond crumbles with a resounding wail from the spirit, signaling her abrupt departure, leaving behind an eerily quiet house.
In the aftermath, the deafening silence fills the couple with a comforting sensation of victory as the once foreboding ambiance dissipates, replaced by peaceful calmness.
Word of their valiant stand and consequent triumph cascades through the neighborhood, creating waves of gratitude, relief, and awe among the townsfolk.
With the shadow of fear now replaced by a ray of hope, normalcy slowly creeps back into their suburban community.
Residents now feel brave enough to bask in the daylight, their children revelling in outdoor games.
Amid the unfolding events, John and Mary emerge resilient.
Their shared trials and turbulence had forged their bond, and the appreciation from their community further validated their courage.
Their lasting love took on a heroic hue after they stood undeterred in the face of the lurking terror within their home.
Their unwavering devotion to each other became their guiding light.
The journey from a naïvely happy couple to bravely confronting supernatural adversities had led them to reclaim their tranquil home.
Having emerged from their harrowing experiences, they dedicated themselves to assist others similarly tormented by Smith's malicious architectural designs.
They offered support, sharing their experiences and the knowledge they'd gained during their ordeal.
Their strength had evolved, no longer anchored in blissful ignorance, but stemming from their newfound wisdom and courage.
The dream of a peaceful domestic life they initially sought nods at them from a closer distance.
It was now a reality, albeit hard-earned through their relentless struggle against what was lurking unseen.
John and Mary now dwell in peace, treasuring their beautifully quaint suburban home.
They are ever aware of their eerie past, and the triumph they had won in claiming the house truly theirs.
While the tormenting spirits were banished, the bravery within John and Mary had sparked, equipping them to face any future challenges with a newfound resilience.
The film concludes with this resonant message: True heroes are not born pre-formed, they are molded and shaped in the fierce furnace of trials and adversities.
This couple's transformation from ordinary to extraordinary proves this ideology beyond doubt.

69310615.title: Mid-Century
synopsis: In 1963, Joanne and Anthony Waxen live in a home built by Frederick Banner, with whom the two have had concerning interactions.
Joanne, a stay-at-home housewife is given underwear as a gift by her husband.
After Joanne leaves to change, Frederick enters the house.
Joanne finds Frederick peeking on her while Anthony has been hanged from the ceiling with a belt.
In 2022, Alice is a doctor who is harassed by her superior and is traumatized from her time working during the COVID-19 pandemic.
She and her architect husband Tom go on a weekend getaway to San Diego and rent a mid-century modern home, the same that was built by Frederick, from a mysterious man named Eldridge.
While there, strange events occur including a bird crashing into the window, doors opening by themselves, and a shadowy figure watching the couple while they have sex.
As night falls, a delivery driver tells Tom about Eldridge, stating he freaks him out.
After driving away, his tire pops and a man stabs him in the chest.
Following dinner, Alice goes to interview at a hospital for a new job.
The delivery driver is sent to Alice's hospital but she is unable to save him.
After finding the receipt for the order in his pocket, officer Raquel and her partner interrogate her, inquiring if Tom had anything to do with the murder.
Meanwhile, Tom investigates the house and Frederick Banner.
Tom searches Frederick on Wikipedia but finds a lot missing, so he calls his co-worker Hannah who he is sleeping with to find a book on him in their office.
The book reveals that Frederick lost his first wife Alice and later remarried Joanne Waxen, and that he was also interested in polygamy and the occult with a painter named Emil Larson.
Hannah hangs up but is soon-after strangled by a security guard.
At the house, Tom is haunted by a woman who, after nearly drowning Tom in the pool, leads him to a book of the occult and later to a grave in the backyard with the bones of Graham Verdin.

When Tom touches the bones he sees visions which reveal that the woman is Marie Verdin and the wife of Graham, a woman who Frederick was manipulating at the same time as Joanne whom he later kills and takes her son as his own, now named Eldridge Banner.
She reveals to Tom that Frederick killed the husbands of the couples who moved into his neighborhood and that he still haunted the house where he died.
Eldridge returns to the home and Tom calls 911 before falling into a ditch outside.
The two officers arrive at the house and question Eldridge, but do not go further as he is a top fundraiser for the police.
Tom is then possessed by Alice and talks to her son through him before he drowns Tom and buries him in the yard.
Tom however still exists as a ghost and spends time with Marie.
The two discover a recording of Frederick and Emil discussing a prophesied blood "wolf" moon in which a woman can be impregnated with a spirit.
The police discover the delivery driver was killed by an architect's compass, narrowing the suspect down to Eldridge or Tom.
Alice returns to the house after work and finds Tom missing.
Eldridge confronts Alice and sedates her, preparing for the ritual.
Tom then possesses Eldridge and digs up his own body before officer Raquel arrives and arrests him.
Tom, speaking through Eldridge, admits to everything and asks to be arrested.
The chief of police arrives and kills Raquel, revealing he is one of Eldridge's brother possessed by Frederick.
The ritual begins with sons of Frederick surrounding Alice.
Alice, and Tom possessing Alice, kill the sons together and say their goodbyes.
After Alice is transported to the hospital, Tom sees every house in the neighborhood has ghosts of Frederick's victims inside.

51252736.title: Moroccan Horizon
synopsis: The film opens with vivid scenes of Paris, where Olivia, a lively 15-year-old Parisian girl, resides with her father, Benjamin.
Olivia's parents had recently divorced; an event that greatly affected both Olivia and Benjamin.
A lingering tension navigates the vast halls of their home, revealing a strained relationship between the two.
Benjamin, a once passionate traveler turned software mogul, decides to reconnect with his adventurous spirit.
He plans a trip to Morocco.
His stories of Moroccan escapades spark a kindle in Olivia's heart.
These stories awaken a plethora of feelings and subtle questions in the adolescent girl's heart.
Their journey begins as their plane smoothly lands in Morocco.
As they step down, the foreign land seems to welcome them with open arms.
They experience an exhilarating sensory overload traversing through the busy Moroccan marketplace.
Their journey converges with Rashid, a charismatic Moroccan guide.
Enchanted by Rashid's mention of the "Moroccan Horizon," they decide to venture into the country's mesmerizing depths.
The ethereal allure of the Moroccan Horizon captivates both of them.
Olivia forms an unusual kinship with local village children.
Olivia falls for the uncomplicated lifestyle, and Benjamin reflects over his obsession with a materialistic life back in the city.
Olivia struggles with internal conflicts.
Her newfound love for the village battles with her longing for city life and her mother back in Paris.
In a sudden impulse, Benjamin purchases an old, charming house in the center of the village.
Seeking an escape from his past and a clean canvas to restart his life, he barely gives this major decision a second thought.
Benjamin's abrupt decision shocks Olivia, who worries about leaving her familiar life and her mother back in Paris.
The impromptu purchase amplifies the underlying tension, pushing Olivia to confront Benjamin.
Benjamin apologizes, aware of his oversight, and assures her that in the future, her emotions will be his primary concern.
Amidst the turmoil, a turning point arrives when Olivia uses her connection with the local kids to set up a basic English language school.
She aims to overcome the language barrier and create deeper bonds.
She leverages her Parisian education to teach the village kids English, finding a lost sense of purpose and happiness that her luxurious city life could never provide.
The villagers reciprocate this gesture by imparting their traditional rituals and customs to Olivia and Benjamin.
Watching Olivia flourish, Benjamin realizes the need to mend ties with Olivia's mother.
The story reaches its climax when Benjamin brings Olivia's mother to Moroccan Horizon.
The invitation signifies his readiness to address his past mistakes and unite their fractured family.
The film's final scenes show Olivia's mother stepping into the serene Moroccan village.
With the sunset over the beautiful Moroccan Horizon, the arrival presents a second chance for their fragmented family.

70850736.title: Aftersun
synopsis: In the late 1990s, 11-year old Sophie travels to a Turkish holiday resort with her father Calum, who moved to London after having separated amicably from her mother.
Sophie records the holiday on a MiniDV camera, the footage of which is interspersed throughout the film.
Over the course of the holiday, Sophie befriends and observes various English tourists at the resort, often meeting and playing arcade games with a boy named Michael.
Calum exhibits signs of depression, anxiety, and internal turmoil, which he tries to hide from his daughter beneath a façade of contentment.
During his time alone, he is seen engaging in Tai chi patterns and reading self-help books; he is also shown smoking, which he hides from Sophie.
Despite Sophie's observant nature, she is oblivious to the signs of her father's increasingly obvious signs of depression.

One day, they go scuba diving and she loses her expensive scuba mask; while Calum feigns nonchalance, Sophie senses her father's actual feelings and expresses that she understood the mask was expensive and comforts her father; Calum is taken aback by this.
Calum then tells the diving instructor next to them that he is surprised to have lived to be 30.
Soon after, Calum and Sophie go to a rug merchant and she observes him grapple with the cost of purchasing one he likes.
Calum initially declines purchasing the rug while Sophie is with him, later returning without her to buy it.
The following night, they attend a karaoke night and Sophie signs herself and Calum up for a song.
Calum curtly refuses to sing with Sophie despite her insistence, and Sophie ends up singing "Losing My Religion" alone as Calum watches on.
Upset by being left alone by him, Sophie refuses to join Calum in returning to their hotel room and hangs out with the strangers.
Michael creeps up on Sophie from behind, frightening her.
They later kiss beside a pool.
Meanwhile, Calum goes to the beach and submerges himself in the water.
When Sophie returns to the hotel room, she finds Calum asleep and nude; she gently covers him with a sheet.
The two reconcile the next day while travelling to the mud baths, and Calum apologises for the previous night's behaviour.
Sophie surprises him by having other tourists sing "For He's a Jolly Good Fellow" for his birthday, while Calum stoically watches on.

In a flashback to the previous night, a nude Calum is shown sobbing in the hotel room alone, with letters that apologise to Sophie strewn across the floor, presumably in reference to his planned suicide.
On the last night of their holiday together, Calum and Sophie share a dance together to "Under Pressure" in a loving embrace.
The next morning, Calum and Sophie are at the airport, where Calum waves goodbye and sends Sophie off on her flight back home to her mother.
In the present day, the now-adult Sophie lives with her wife and young child, with the rug Calum purchased on display.
She is shown looking through the camera footage from the holiday in Turkey, prying through her memories in an attempt to understand what happened to her father.

Interspersed throughout the film are abstract, dream-like sequences where the adult Sophie stands in the middle of a crowded rave, catching glimpses of Calum dancing frantically through strobing lights.

Throughout the sequences, Sophie attempts to get closer to him multiple times, eventually briefly embracing him; with their hands wrapped around each other, Calum ultimately falls from Sophie's grasp.
In the final scene, Calum packs away the camera and walks down the airport hallway after having waved goodbye to Sophie, opening the doors to the room of the rave.

73801890.title: Custodians (2021 film)
synopsis: A spirited group of youthful archaeology scholars from the esteemed Timeless University stumble upon an obscure, dust-covered ancient Greek manuscript hidden in a forgotten nook of the university's vast library during a routine archival clean up.
They carefully peruse the manuscript, discovering an enthralling account of Athena - the divine Greek goddess of wisdom and warfare known for her strength and strategic prowess.

As they delve even deeper into the lyrical text, they uncover a vaguely encrypted clue within the manuscript's aged pages that directs them to "The Entrance" - an intriguing concept believed to protect Athena's uniquely powerful cognate stone.
Besieged by an overpowering academic excitement, the scholars unanimously agree to embark on a mission to unravel the tightly woven secrets concealed within the mysterious clue.

The ensuing weeks are filled with grueling effort, with the scholars dedicating countless hours to scrutinize ancient maps resembling faded parchments, meticulously study historical files brimming with cryptic information, and painstakingly decode cryptic archaeological records - each piece of information painstakingly piecing together the route to The Entrance.

Exhausted yet exhilarated at the end of weeks of relentless research, they successfully manage to triangulate The Entrance to a silent, entropy-ridden castle hidden on the outskirts of Athens, seemingly untouched by time.

Armed with the tools of their trade – powerful flashlights cutting through the darkness, leather-bound notebooks filled with their observations, the scholars, their faces alight with anticipation, embark headlong into their potential life-altering quest.
On entering the castle, they find uncanny shadows stretched grotesquely across the cracked, ancient stone walls, distorting their appearances and defying the natural laws of light.
Despite the bone-chilling environment, the scholars show commendable courage, attributing the sinister phenomena to the long years of neglect, and commence their exploration unhindered.
They painstakingly document every architectural detail, every relic peeking through the dust-covered floor, and every paranormal occurrence encountered in their haunting expedition.
Suddenly, one of the scholars trips over a nearly buried stone slab, its true form hidden by grime and etched with perplexing ancient hieroglyphics.
Wiping away centuries of accumulated dirt, they unveil the intricate carving of Athena's symbol—an owl—rooting their previous suppositions in firm scientific observation.
However, their euphoric celebration soon turns into dread-filled revelation as they comprehend that their intrusive activity might have stirred a long-dormant curse bound with the ancient castle.
The once silently imposing castle undergoes a petrifying transformation, converting from a peaceful testament to Medieval architecture to a formidable, deadly death trap.
As the ancient curse seizes its stronghold, the scholars are drawn into a series of inexplicable and horrific accidents that ruthlessly claim their lives one by one.
Each unanticipated death sends shockwaves of abject terror and crushing remorse through the scholars, their comrades' demise a grim reminder of their impending, gruesome fate.
Amidst the escalating chaos, a spectral figure shrouded in luminous white ethereal robes materializes—a spirit from the distant past tethered to the owl-carved stone.
Introducing herself as Althea, the spectral figure reveals she is the immortal guardian of Athena's wisdom stone, a revelation that sends a collective gasp through the remaining scholars.
Althea unveils the chilling truth—that damaging the protective stone seal had awakened an ancient demonic entity sealed away by Athena herself.
Stricken with the realization of the horrifying implications of their scholarly curiosity, the scholars express profound remorse to Althea for their grave actions.
Moved by their genuine expressions of regret, Althea extends a dangerous but redeeming solution; a ritual that might imprison the demonic entity back within the owl stone.
However, performing the chilling ritual involves high stakes—it demands a human sacrifice willing to act as bait, to draw the demonic entity into its stone prison.
After heart-rending deliberation, the eldest scholar, driven by a sense of responsibility, volunteers to face the perilous consequences, thereby potentially sealing his fate.
United by terror and determination, they undertake the ritual, adhering strictly to Althea's instructions, their every move accentuated by the perceptible tension in the air.
The volunteer scholar fearlessly moves forward, his expression resolute amidst his teammates' chant of sealing incantations, his eyes reflecting firm resolve and silent goodbye.
Although the scholars manage to complete their dire mission, their victory is marred by the bitter loss of their brave comrade.
Once the supernatural pandemonium subsides, the surviving scholars, fraught with emotional trauma and relief, hastily retreat from the ill-fated castle.
Their escape, although a narrow one, leaves them both remorseful for their reckless exploration and relieved at surviving and rectifying their grave mistake.
Chastised, the scholars return to their university campus, psychologically scarred by their chilling adventure and perpetually burdened by the memory of their lost companion.
Their reckless exploration into the secret realms of history transforms into a formidable lesson, serving as a stern reminder to generations of scholars to respect the sanctity of historical sites.
Decades later, a new wave of young explorers, their hearts afire with the thrill of potential adventure, unearths the same ancient manuscript within their metropolitan library.

The legend of Athena and the tantalizing concept of The Entrance ignite their imagination, their hearts pulsating with a never-before-experienced excitement as they contemplate the legendary adventure that possibly awaits them.
Existing in a bubble of excitement and anticipation, they remain blissfully unaware of the cruel fate that claimed their predecessors, oblivious to the true nature of The Entrance they seek.

The menacing shadow of a familiar, timeless castle looms ominously in the misty distance, serving as a monumental testament of errors made by a group of scholars just as passionate as these young explorers.
The allure of mystery and legend that once enticed their predecessors stands ready to ensnare these innocent adventurers in its insidious trap.
The ominous scene concludes the film, setting the stage for yet another horrifying sequence of events.

70706211.title: Barbarians (2021 film)
synopsis: A video is shown advertising a property called the "Gateway" property, named after the nearby Gaeta stone – known as a sacred site to historical druids.
Going on a morning jog on his birthday, Adam, the current leaseholder of Gateway, comes across a wounded fox snared in barbed wire.
He attempts to free the fox, but backs off when the animal hisses at him before resuming his jog.
Returning home some time later while his girlfriend Eva works on a large replica Gaeta stone in the property courtyard, Adam discovers the dying fox in his kitchen.
Eva and worker Dan come inside and, after expressing horror at the sight of the animal, Dan quickly euthanizes it.
Meanwhile, Lucas (the owner of Gateway and presenter of the advertisement) and girlfriend Chloe drive to the Gateway property to celebrate Adam's birthday.
While on the way, they stop at the Gaeta stone as a neopagan celebration takes place.
While there, Lucas is attacked by a celebrant while recording a video lamenting the death of Alan Wickes, his former partner.
Lucas and Chloe arrive at the property, and Eva takes Chloe to her art studio after learning of the latter's interest.
Eva remarks that her largely dark and disturbing art has been focused towards pagan imagery since her move to Gateway.
At the same time, Lucas gifts Adam a mysterious drug contained in an eye dropper.
Later during dinner, Chloe admits to being pregnant.
After she goes to the bathroom, Adam confronts her with worries that the child could be his.
They return to dinner, and Adam spikes Lucas's drink with the drug in revenge for Lucas's taunting behavior.
Lucas attempts to renegotiate the sale of the property, and a fight breaks out between him and Adam.
Adam reveals his prior affair with Chloe as the doorbell rings.
Eva opens the door to reveal two assailants in animal masks.
The invaders take Adam, Lucas, and Eva hostage while Chloe drives off, but is run off the road by another masked individual who takes her hostage with the rest of the group.
The bird-masked invader, seemingly the leader of the group, performatively vandalizes the house before seating Lucas in a chair and dousing him in blood.

Lucas is forced to read a confession letter in the style of his advertisement for Gateway, but shortly after begins to suffer from a bad trip and is able to break free from his restraints, killing the bird-masked invader.
One invader chases Lucas outside while the other is overpowered and is revealed to be Dan.

Lucas is overpowered and killed by his assailant Neil, who reveals that the invaders are the sons of Alan Wickes, and that they blame Lucas for their father's death and the loss of their family property.
Adam convinces the two invaders that he will sign the property to them.
A conflict ensues in which Chloe stabs Dan who shoots her in retaliation, killing her.
Eva and Neil fight before Adam tackles him out of a window, seemingly killing them both.
Eva pursues Dan but is unable to bring herself to kill him.
Adam is revealed to be alive, and decisively kills Dan with a captive bolt pistol before embracing with Eva.

89209043.title: Breaking Lanes
synopsis: Jake is a wealthy financier known for his hardened disposition and remains emotionally impenetrable until he engages in a heated argument with Angie, his empathetic girlfriend, and a dedicated nurse working in a local hospital.
Their disagreement flairs, fueled by pent-up emotions, longstanding grudges, and misunderstandings from both sides.

This tumultuous argument ends putting a halt to their long-time relationship, driving them apart, and leaving Jake wallowing in a stew of guilt and regret, bitter memories of their shared moments haunting him.
Feeling lost and needing a respite from the constant reminder of his broken relationship, Jake decides to embark on a solo voyage across the country, trying to make sense of his turbulent emotions.
After navigating through forgotten towns and desolate landscapes, he pulls over at a dilapidated roadside shop, the only semblance of a structure for miles around on a remote Arizona highway.
Feeling an alarming sense of dread and unease, Jake hastens to extract himself from the eerie surroundings and resume his solitary journey.
However, his growing apprehension is driven into a frenzy as he hears hushed, ghostly whispers enveloping the silence.
As he maneuvers his sleek black Mercedes-Benz onto the empty highway, the car abruptly stalls due to an unexplained engine malfunction, stranding him in the desolate vastness.
Alone under the pale moonlight, Jake observes shadowy figures hovering at the edges of his peripheral vision, their formless and sinister bodies shimmering ominously.
With no help in sight, Jake's only choice lies in returning to the forsaken service station, his heart pounding with anxiety and fear.

Back in the once-vacant shop, he stumbles upon an ancient leather-bound diary, its worn-out pages filled with blood-curdling tales of haunting spirits and paranormal incidents reported on this lost stretch of the road.

As he peruses these spine-chilling narratives, familiar whispers of Angie's voice fill his ears, and horrifying stories of past wayfarers disappearing on this eerie highway echo in the pressing silence.
It dawns on Jake that his journey now encompasses more than incubating self-realizations; he has to deal with the spectral presence and dismantle the haunting hex shadowing the road.

Using his emotional vulnerabilities against him, the malignant spirit takes on Angie's form, horrifying Jake with spectral manifestations of his guilt, reminding him brutally of their tumultuous past.
Over the span of the haunting nights and phantom-filled days, Jake begins to comprehend the depth of his feelings.
He recognizes the importance of reconciling with Angie and securing her forgiveness to mollify the restless ghosts.
Gathering all his fortitude, he confronts the spectral apparition resembling Angie, pleading for understanding and forgiveness.
Guiding the trapped spirits restless on the desolate highway, Jake directs them on their journey towards salvation and liberation.
As dawn creeps upon him, darkness retreats, leaving Jake alone in the stark reality of the Arizona desert, but with an unusual feeling of peace welling within him.
He attempts to resuscitate his stalled car, and the engine roars back into life.
Breathing a sigh of relief, he drives back onto the highway, leaving behind the spectral horror.
He reaches Phoenix with a clearer mind and newfound wisdom.
Gathering his resolve, Jake sets his course for the local hospital where Angie works.
He confronts her with an apology for his past mistakes and earnestly implores her forgiveness.
This freeing act of submission releases Jake from the heavy chains of guilt and remorse that he had been enshackled within.

70944703.title: Glorious (film)
synopsis: Wes, distraught over his breakup with his ex Brenda, stops his car at a roadside rest stop.
That night, he gets blackout drunk and burns all his possessions, including his pants and box of photos.
The next morning, he stumbles into an empty restroom to vomit.
The man in the stall next to him starts up a conversation and reveals his name to be Ghatanothoa.
As the conversation becomes uncomfortable, Wes realizes the door is sealed shut.
Ghatanothoa explains that it is a demigod created by his primordial god father who accidentally created the universe, including humanity.
Incredulous, Wes attempts to peek through the stall's glory hole and over the stall door to see it, despite Ghatanothoa's warnings not to, as glimpsing its true form would destroy Wes.
Exerting its power, Ghatanothoa punishes Wes by giving him visions of Brenda.
Wes attempts to escape through the air vent but finds himself back in the restroom.
Ghatanothoa explains that its father created Ghatanothoa as a tool to destroy humanity.
However, Ghatanothoa's older siblings sealed their father away to stop him.
But now, the god is free and Ghatanothoa, having developed affection for humanity, has hidden itself away from its father to avoid being used to destroy the universe.

Ghatanothoa tells Wes that in order to permanently hide, it must transcend into the ethereal plane, but can only do so if its physical form is "satisfied" by a mortal, which must be done through the glory hole.
While corporeal, Ghatanothoa's powers are weakened, further exposing its location to its father.
Ghatanothoa is apologetic for what must be done and pleads with Wes to help it, arguing that humanity is precious.
Wes counters with his own experiences of his abusive father and how he never felt anything for anyone, except for Brenda.
A maintenance worker arrives and Wes screams for help, despite Ghatanothoa warning him that this will end badly.
The man also becomes trapped in the bathroom, and to prevent him from telling anyone about this, Ghatanothoa explodes him into blood and body parts.
Wes uses his dismembered leg to try to bash down the door but eventually gives up.

Wes inserts his penis into the glory hole, only for Ghatanothoa to be shocked, clarifying that "satisfaction" means offering a piece of his liver, and passes him a shard of broken glass, causing Wes to once again back off.
The stress eventually causes Wes to scream for Ghatanothoa's father to find them.
The rest stop begins to crumble away as the god tears through reality.
Desperate, Ghatanothoa removes Wes's memories of Brenda to show him what universal annihilation will mean.
Wes relents and begs to see Brenda one more time in exchange for doing the deed.
Ghatanothoa restores his memories, and with Ghatanothoa's father in sight, Wes cuts a hole in his abdomen, and allows Ghatanothoa to pull his liver out.
In excruciating pain, Wes' thoughts reveal that he is a serial killer who murdered Brenda after she discovered the photos of his victims in his box.
With Wes' offering, Ghatanothoa transcends into the ether, foiling its father.
Wes weakly asks if this makes him a hero.
Ghatanothoa departs, stating that he is no hero, and that as entities of destruction, both of them deserve to be forgotten and die.
Wes soon dies just outside the restroom, holding a teddy bear Brenda had given him.

46495342.title: Flat 302: The Uni Journey
synopsis: Sara and Lilly, two lively freshmen attending Manchester University, are brimming with excitement as they prepare to move into Flat 302, an animated Victorian apartment in the bustling student district.
The flat’s stark white walls become an artistic canvas as they transform the space into a radiant home.

Their curiosity is aroused when their elderly neighbor, Mr. Roberts from Flat 304, subtly hints about the notorious past associated with Flat 302, detailing several former student occupants who met dramatically tragic circumstances.
Deciding to ignore his ominous warnings, Sara and Lilly decide to focus their energies on imbibing student life, settling into the unique charm of their new home.
The girls, however, struggle to ignore certain peculiar occurrences in their home: the crystal chandelier exhibits strange swinging motions, and the in-built LED lights flicker erratically.

Before they know it, the girls are caught up in the vigour of university life, grappling with intensive law courses, while also endeavouring to form lasting friendships within the campus' vibrant student union.

Yet, they find the recurring oddities at Flat 302 increasingly unsettling: volatile radiator noises, inexplicably chilling cold spots around the bay-window, and relentless network interruptions disrupt their daily life.
Soon, Lilly begins experiencing recurrent nightmares featuring a threatening shadow.
Sara grows concerned as Lilly display sleepwalking tendencies, escalating the eeriness that pervades their apartment.
Alarmed, Sara decides to delve deeper into the mysteries surrounding their flat.
She digs through the local library archives excavating the chilling rumors associated with students who had formerly lived in Flat 302.
She reels in shock as she discovers an old newspaper article detailing the mysterious disappearance of two prior tenants who seem to have experienced eerily similar circumstances.
A routine day turns dire when Lilly, usually an effervescent spirit, begins to act strangely distant.
This disconcerting behavioral change culminates abruptly as Lilly mysteriously goes missing following the Christmas holidays.
Desperate and fearful, Sara finds an ancient diary hidden under the loose floorboards in Lilly’s room.
As she immerses herself in the frantic entries, a dreadful realization dawns upon her: the past occupant’s horrific experiences bear a startling similarity to Lilly’s nightmares.
Stricken by this chilling revelation, Sara resolves to extricate Lilly from the relentless grasp of any malevolent entity that may have taken up residence in their beloved Flat 302.
Seeking assistance, Sara turns to their academic colleagues from the university, disclosing the grim reality of Flat 302's haunting past to her confidantes.
United, they resolve to perform a séance, a desperate attempt to establish communication with what they suspect is a malevolent spirit holding Lilly captive within the flat.
As the search for Lilly escalates to city-wide proportions, the local Manchester police force gets involved.
Their inquiry intensifies as they grapple with the enigma of Lilly’s inexplicable disappearance.
Unfazed by the cynicism, Sara and her cohort proceed to hold the séance.
They gather under the soft glow of vanilla-scented candles strategically placed in the antique drawing room.
A pervasive silence engulfs Flat 302 as they brace themselves to wrestle with the malevolent force that seemed to possess their home.
In this confrontation, they uncover the gruesome past embedded within the walls of Flat 302 and unmask the countless innocent lives ensnared by its sinister clutches.

Through a combination of sheer mental willpower and using a treasured family talisman, Sara succeeds in exorcising the malicious spirit, thereby freeing their quaint student apartment from a frightening paranormal presence.
Following this draining episode, the police locate Lilly in the concealed depths of the apartment's cluttered basement.
Her pulse is weak but defiantly persistent.

Amid the flood of relief, Sara and Lilly have a tearful reunion in the clinical confines of the Manchester Royal Infirmary, a testament to the unbreakable bond of friendship that has weathered an extraordinary ordeal.
Having emerged from a harrowing experience, the girls wisely decide to vacate Flat 302.
Instead, they opt for a sleek modern flat, looking to start anew, far removed from the disturbing past.

Once again vacant, Flat 302 retains its allure, its façade betraying no hint of the secrets it harbors within its charming Victorian architecture; patiently awaiting the arrival of its next unsuspecting tenants.

71255260.title: Room 203
synopsis: Kim White is a young woman about to start her college education and has decided to move into a newly rented apartment with her best friend, Izzy.

Kim’s parents, however, are not at all supportive of this idea, owing to Izzy’s past history with drugs and cases of overdose, and they warn their daughter that they would not keep any contact with her if she does actually move in.
She ignores them and goes inside where she and Izzy meet Ronan, the landlord of the apartment who gives them a tour and tells them to stay out of the basement.
Kim and Izzy are mesmerized by a large stained-glass window depicting medieval knights killing each other.
Kim also sees a small but noticeable hole on the wall of her room and tries to cover it up by hanging a mirror over it.
This does not work, as the mirror either keeps tilting or falls to the ground.
Izzy finds an amulet in the hole and begins wearing it, at the same time she begins sleepwalking.
As Kim reaches college late on her orientation day but the tour guide Ian, gives her a private tour.
They bond over their shared passion for journalism.
Kim decides to write a paper in her course on Izzy's life but doesn't ask permission from her before doing so.
One night Kim is woken up by a fluttering noise and sees a crow slither into the hole in her wall, which has now grown and somewhat resembles a decomposing wound.

She had also earlier found a heavy metal music box with the names of a couple written inside it, and now, on this very night, Izzy walks into her room holding the music box in her hand, with blood spilling down from her head.
Kim takes care of her and keeps her company that night, and Izzy seems to be normal again the next day.
Her sleepwalking episodes continue and get even scarier when she walks down into the basement one night and Kim has to bring her back.
Kim had often seen the landlord, Ronan, watching them and behaving strangely.
She finds him in their apartment one day staring at the stained glass.
He reprimands them harshly for having gone down to the basement.
Kim shares all this and also Izzy’s sufferings with Ian, and he suggests she investigate the history of the building.
Together they read up on the internet about a bank manager named Liam McNally who had murdered his pregnant wife, Karen, before killing himself in apartment 203.
They realize those are the names inscribed inside the music box that Izzy had carried around during her sleepwalking.
Kim meets up with Milton Briggs, the janitor who had reported the murder so many years ago, and the man reveals that the baby survived.

Ian does his own research into the images present on the stained-glass mural in apartment 203, and he connects them to Celtic pagan symbols and finally to the Irish mythology figure Morrigu, who often appears in the form of a crow and symbolizes death.
Meanwhile, Izzy stumbles across Kim’s paper about her and angrily confronts her before storming out.
Kim rips open the hole on the wall, and a shriveled-up, nasty old hand from a dead body falls out of it.
Ronan enters the apartment and abducts Kim, revealing that he is the baby that survived, and the amulet Izzy wore belonged to his mother.

The curse chooses its victim through the necklace with the cursed amulet, and compels them to kill both others and themself, but Izzy had been successfully resisting, likely due to her resilience from her troubled past.
Ronan has decided to take matters into his own hands out of fear that Morrigu will come after him if she does not get her offerings.
Ian meanwhile rushes to Kim’s apartment where he is killed by a possessed Izzy.
Kim manages to escape Ronan before finding Ian's body and following Izzy into the basement as she herself is pursued by Ronan.
He manages to catch up to her but before he can kill Kim he is possessed and turns the gun on himself.
Izzy shifts between her real self, who asks for Kim’s help, and her possessed self, who grins and laughs scarily, and asks Kim to kill her.
Kim tries to refuse, and Izzy attacks her, but just as she is about to finish her off, Kim rips off the cursed amulet from Izzy’s neck.
The two friends now walk up to their apartment with the intention of breaking down the stained-glass window, but are spooked by hundreds of crows flying right outside their window in an eerie manner.
Kim does finally gather up the courage to shatter the window by throwing the dead-body hand that had earlier fallen out of the hole in the wall.
The two quickly escape the apartment, and Izzy rushes her friend to the hospital, where she is treated for her physical wounds.
Right at the end the camera moves back into the empty apartment 203 and closes in on the hole in the shattered glass window.
In pitch darkness, a faint figure of Morrigu herself makes an appearance.

58901651.title: More the Merrier: The Thompson's Tale (2022 film)
synopsis: Startled awake in the Thompson family's warm, inviting kitchen, father John and mother Emily, their daughters Lily, an inquisitive nine-year-old, and Madison, their perceptive ten-year-old are gathered around their aged oak breakfast table, embarking on the day with the usual family dialogue.
In the middle of their laughter and gentle rebukes over the breakfast table, a shrill ring from John’s latest iPhone model disrupts the tranquil morning.
The familiar, gruff voice on the other end is unmistakably John's brother, Rob.
Rob, sounding both surprised and defeated, reveals his plan to move in with the Thompsons following a public and intense divorce from his wife of fifteen years.

Subsequent scenes depict the transformation of the Thompson's stately, 4-bedroom colonial-style family home, typically ordered meticulously by Emily, to accommodate the intrusion of Rob's somewhat chaotic lifestyle.
Rob's arrival is far from discreet; he stumbles over the porch steps and lands spectacularly into the towering rose bushes that front the perfectly groomed yard.
Rob's lack of organisation, showcased by his anti-social meal times and sprawling laundry, proves to be a hurricane in the calm waters that was the Thompson residence.
For Lily and Madison, however, their uncle’s carefree lifestyle becomes a source of fascination and entertainment, leading to an unexpected camaraderie between the unlikely threesome.

Just as the family finds a rhythm to Rob's zany lifestyle, another shocker arrives in the form of Emily’s bossy elder sister, Margaret with her two noisy kids barging unannounced into an already crowded residence.
Margaret, coupled with her pair of quarrelsome twins, exacerbates the already burgeoning chaos, converting the Thompson household into a full-blown circus.

However, the laughter dies down when Margaret, in a dramatic turn of events, nonchalantly reveals her intent to sell her share of the cherished countryside villa they had inherited from their late grandmother.
This shocking revelation escalates tensions in the Thompson household, leading to a series of heated disagreements.
But the story takes a hilarious twist when Rob, in a mock-worthy blunder, mistakenly shreds the villa’s legal papers in a whirring kitchen blender intended for his morning smoothie.
The ruined documents trigger yet another episode of pandemonium causing uproar among the family members.
This unexpected blip, however, gives the Thompsons a breather to reconsider Margaret's rash intentions.
A poignant turning point occurs when their judicious grandmother pays a surprise visit for a family potluck.
Swallowed by the festivities, they chance upon a faded letter hidden in their Grandmother’s antique chest.
It reveals a clause previously overlooked that might just dissolve their desperate fears of Margaret selling the family villa.
Margaret, taken aback by the new development, is compelled to swallow her pride when she realizes her family outsmarted her unthoughtful plan.
Inspired by Margaret's newfound humility, her twins too undergo a change of heart, their softened demeanor providing a welcome touch of warmth to the familial atmosphere.
Following the hectic experiences, Lily and Madison find a renewed sense of balance in their lives.
Their journey of self-discovery and the realisation of maintaining their unique personalities amidst the domestic turbulence offers them a sense of accomplishment.

Approaching the climactic scenes, the Thompsons recognize that resilient as they are, their unorthodox family dynamics which might seem like a weakness to outsiders, is in fact their great strength, binding them closer.
Margaret, humbly acknowledging her mistakes, offers a heartfelt apology for her impulsiveness and the turmoil her ruthless assertiveness wreaked.
Her heartfelt confession met with a gracious acceptance by John, Emily, Rob, and the girls, marking a promising beginning.
As the movie segues into a peaceful end, and the Thompsons heave a sigh of relief, the doorbell rings once again.
The entire family exchanges knowing smiles of readiness, their eyes sparkling with anticipation, knowing full well that the next storm was inevitable.
Their shared laughter rings through the house, promising a myriad of future misadventures.
By now, they wouldn't have their lives unfold any other way- the chaos is what makes them the Thompsons.

64762204.title: Cheaper by the Dozen (2022 film)
synopsis: The Bakers are a blended family that began with Paul Baker and his wife Kate who together had daughters Ella and Harley.
They had friends who died in a car accident causing them to take in their godson Haresh.
Kate eventually divorced Paul, but they remained friends with Kate acting as an occasional, though slightly inattentive, babysitter.
Zoey married football player Dominic "Dom" Clayton and had daughter Deja and son DJ.
Due to Dom's celebrity life, Zoey divorced him and took custody of the kids.
Paul met Zoey after she visited his small restaurant and suggested that he make the entire menu breakfast themed all day.
The two eventually got married, expanded the restaurant, renamed it Baker's Breakfast and had two sets of twins: Luca and Luna, and Bronx and Bailey.
Dom continues to be active in Deja and DJ's lives which slightly intimidates Paul as he was rarely there to begin with.
While Deja prepares for her basketball scholarship to the University of Southern California, DJ feels that he connects with Paul more than Dom and would rather speak with him.
Paul gets a meeting with a large company to expand his restaurant.
He succeeds and has his famous sauce sold on shelves.
He decides to use the money to move the family and their dogs Bark Obama and Joe Bitin' from Los Angeles to Calabasas, in a bigger house in a gated community.
Upon arrival, Zoey begins to feel the effects of racial profiling, especially after meeting her neighbor Anne.
Paul suddenly gets a call informing him that his sister Rachel has checked into rehab, forcing him to take in his nephew Seth, who Ella and Harley claim is a criminal.
Seth bonds with Haresh when he discovers that he is being picked on at the new school because of his ethnicity and teaches him to defend himself while making monster spray for his younger cousins.
While not being used a lot on the Calabasa Hornets basketball team, Deja begins seeing a boy named Chris and sneaks out of the house to see him.
Paul finds himself having to travel to look for new places to expand his restaurant.
The investors Melanie and Michele also insist on altering some of his business ideals to cut costs.
He starts to miss out on being with his family which upsets Zoey as this was the reason she divorced Dom.
Haresh and Seth are suspended from school for a week after starting a fight with the kids who bullied Haresh causing Zoey to ground them.
On DJ's birthday, Paul rushes to get home.
During the party, things start to get out of hand as DJ changes his look to impress a girl.
Anne profiles Zoey's family for a series of recent break-ins.
Upon Paul arriving, Deja reveals that she quit the basketball team and that the entire family has been unhappy since arriving in Calabasas.
Feeling that Zoey can no longer handle their kids, Dom announces that he wants full custody of Deja and DJ.
Harley and Ella accuse Seth of the break-ins after Haresh pointed out that he saw him stealing from the restaurant cash register, though he returned it and he angrily leaves.
After telling Paul and Zoey they explain the money is from DCFS and they have been giving it to Seth and that someone broke into Anne house during the party while Seth was grounded.
Upon realizing their mistake, the Bakers, Kate, and Dom all go out and find Seth.
They apologize and admit that he is part of the family and he rejoins them.
Back at home, Paul and Dom discuss their different upbringings.
While Paul will never know what it is like to be at a disadvantage, Dom has to understand that being away from his kids has made him distant and that he needs to be more attentive.
Realizing how much his family means to him, Paul breaks his deal with the company so that he can run the restaurant himself.
The Bakers move back to Los Angeles and buy a new house while the children returned to their old schools as Deja returns to the Elysian Park Wildcats which beat the Calabasa Hornets.
While having breakfast for dinner at the newly named Baker's Dozen Breakfast, Paul reveals the design of the sauce bottle has changed to reflect the entire family.
A postscript states that Dom, Paul, and Zoey were able to invest their sauce and went national.
Kate invented bird yoga which only birds liked.
Seth moved back in with his mom after she got out of rehab, but still spends lots of time with his cousins who haven't had any monster problems since.
Deja and Chris soon started their freshman years at USC.
Ella became the social manager for Harley's punk band and a video of her band playing at her school talent show broke the internet.
Luna and Luca won the tennis national under 12 division becoming like Venus and Serena.
DJ, Talia, and Dom went to Comic-Con and bonded while Dom realized he liked Thor.

55873309.title: Unexpected Visitors at Dinnertime
synopsis: The life of young Jesse originates as an ordinary routine, featuring laborious farm work, hours within the confined wooden structure of a local single-room schoolhouse, and playful roughhousing with his siblings in the fields of corn near their home in the rural heartland of Kansas.

His parents, like twin suns radiating love and a gentle kind of strength which Jesse readily admires, are fundamental influences that shape his character, teaching him the importance of hard work, the ties of family, and the value of humility.
A routine family dinner, enhanced by the sweet aroma of freshly baked apple pie, is interrupted by an unexpected noise, abrupt and intrusive.
Two strangers appear at their threshold - mysterious Buddy with his cunning smile and clever eyes, and Hank, who despite his initially intimidating demeanor, has an undercurrent of rustic charm.
Despite initial reservations towards these unfamiliar visitors, Jesse is drawn towards them, an unquenchable curiosity and the allure of promised adventures igniting within him.
The barn's wooden planks groan beneath his curious gaze as he subtly observes the strangers.
He discerns the shape of Buddy's hidden revolver and the Bowie knife discreetly concealed within Hank's clothing.
His interest is further piqued by their guarded demeanors and unspoken stories.
Brushing aside any timidity, Jesse questions them boldly, touching on the topic of these hidden weapons and their unspoken purpose with an uncanny bravery.
In response, Buddy and Hank decide to reveal their secret identities, exposing themselves to Jesse as seasoned bounty hunters.
The revelation sends Jesse spiraling into a realm of newfound excitement and intrigue.
As he listens to their recounts of dangerous missions featuring notorious criminals, high-risk captures, and adrenaline-charged expeditions, he pleads to be included in their perilous journeys.

Buddy and Hank, observing the undeniable spark of bravery and interest blossoming within Jesse's ocean-blue eyes, finally decide to take the undeterred young boy under their toughened wings and introduce him to the thrilling world of bounty hunting.
Soon, the tranquil monotonous life of the town is disrupted when unfamiliar faces arrive, their menacing presence blatantly declaring them as criminals on a mission to capture a fugitive outlaw.
Jesse, utilizing his honed observational skills common to a farmer's life, documents the actions of these new elements, thoroughly detailing their behavior in a detailed report to Buddy and Hank.
Impressed by Jesse's initiative and innate smartness, the bounty hunters decide to step up the training, formally enveloping him into their exhilarating world.
Under the careful tutelage of Buddy and Hank, Johnny evolves rapidly, maturing from naive curiosity to expertly controlled professionalism, showing the promise of becoming a skilled bounty hunter.
Working in tandem, they expose several illegal activities within the town, confounding the culprits into a retreat and thereby restoring a small piece of the fragmented peace back to the community.
Jesse's courageous nature introduces itself during a dangerous pursuit, as he rescues the blacksmith's daughter from an immediate threat, earning the respect and admiration of the local townsfolk.
As the story unfolds, a shocking truth surfaces - the town's respected and trusted Sheriff is, in fact, the very outlaw they seek to apprehend.
Buddy and Hank disclose their mission objective - to capture the corrupt Sheriff.
The evidence against the trusted Sheriff becomes undeniable, causing divisions among the townsfolk.
Cornered and desperate, the Sheriff turns sinister, taking Jesse's parents hostage, enraging Jesse and escalating the situation to an alarming degree.
Faced with this dire circumstance, Jesse puts his sharp mind to work, carefully designing a plan to rescue his family.
His intricate knowledge of the town's secluded alleys and abandoned barns becomes the linchpin of their daring rescue operation.
As a new day dawns over the horizon, Jesse, Buddy, and Hank put aside fear and uncertainty, preparing to face off against the Sheriff and his minions in an intense showdown.
With a coordinated attack, they outsmart the Sheriff and his followers, revealing the Sheriff's malevolent plans and freeing Jesse's parents.
Confronted and outnumbered, the Sheriff crumbles under their onslaught, leaving Jesse to rescue his parents without a scratch.
With the fall of the Sheriff, a tangible relief washes over the town, as peace and tranquility return.

Recognizing Jesse's accelerated growth and newfound resilience, Buddy and Hank extend a tempting offer as they prepare to embark on their next grand adventure, inviting Jesse to accompany them as a full-time member.
Yet, Jesse is torn between his adventurous spirit urging to accept the offer and his duty to protect his hometown from future threats.
Eventually, he makes a life-altering decision, prioritizing his commitment to safeguard his town and family rather than chasing the thrilling and dangerous life of bounty hunting.
The story draws to a close at Jesse's family dinner table, where the usual peace and normalcy echoes, but an irrefutable shift in dynamics is sensed.
No longer the innocent young farm boy, Jesse now stands tall in their midst as a reliable protector of his beloved town.
Buddy and Hank leave, off to new adventures, but their teachings and experiences continue to shape Jesse as he takes up his new role – a guardian of his small town.
His younger siblings look upon him with newfound respect and unbounded admiration, seeing their older brother as a rising hero they aspire to emulate.
Jesse's parents, while relieved by the return to normalcy, also understand that their son's role has drastically changed, becoming the town's protective barrier against future threats.
Despite the serenity of a peaceful farmhouse life, there lies an undertone of excitement intimating the likelihood of thrilling adventures lurking just around the corner.
The final shot captures Jesse’s steely gaze, emphasizing his willingness and readiness to face the trials yet to come.

65289054.title: The Harder They Fall (2021 film)
synopsis: Eleven-year-old Nat Love is eating dinner with his parents when Rufus Buck and his associate Cortez arrive.
Nat's father begs Buck to spare his wife and son, but Buck shoots and kills both of Nat's parents and then carves a cross into his forehead.
Twenty years later, Love finds and kills Cortez.
Meanwhile, his partners, sharpshooter Bill Pickett and quick draw Jim Beckwourth, ambush the Crimson Hood gang and steal their haul from a recent bank robbery.
The lone survivor tells them the $25,000 they have stolen belongs to Buck.
Love travels to meet his former lover Mary Fields, who runs a chain of saloons.
Pickett brings news of the heist to Love.
Buck's gang, led by Trudy Smith and Cherokee Bill, forcefully free Buck from a train leaving from Yuma Territorial Prison.
They reveal Buck has been pardoned, and they have been paid to kill the corrupt U.S. Army soldiers guarding the prison car.
After slaughtering the soldiers, Buck and his gang arrive in their former stronghold of Redwood City, now run by Buck's associate, Sheriff Wiley Escoe.
Learning that Escoe has used the position to profit at the expense of the town, Buck brutally pistol whips him and orders him to leave town.
Buck gathers the townspeople and after killing a naysayer, demands that they raise $50,000 to save Redwood, threatening to kill and burn the property of any who resist.
U.S.
Marshal Bass Reeves arrests Love after a standoff in a saloon.
However, Reeves reveals to Love that Buck has been released, and he offers him a chance for revenge.
Love's gang, accompanied by Fields and her friend and enforcer, Cuffee, arrive and insist on joining.
They encounter Escoe, who tells them Buck has returned to Redwood.
Fields volunteers to scout Redwood under the cover of offering to buy Smith's saloon.
Love proposes marriage to Fields, but she turns him down.
When Fields arrives in Redwood, Smith takes her prisoner and beats her.
Love's gang arrives, and Love joins Fields in captivity to save her life.
Smith has Love beaten, and he in turn asks Buck to release Fields.
Buck demands Love return the money he stole plus $10,000 as 'interest', requiring him to rob a bank in a white town.
Love and Cuffee rob the bank without killing anyone and escape.
However, the group recognizes that Buck is unlikely to release Fields willingly, so they devise a plan to rig a decoy wagon with dynamite.
They enter Redwood and the decoy wagon is destroyed, killing some of Buck's gang.
Love prepares to hand over the money, but is interrupted by Cherokee Bill preparing to shoot him in the back.
Beckwourth intervenes, challenging Bill to a quick draw showdown.
Bill shoots and kills Beckwourth before he can finish counting down, causing a gunfight to erupt.
Love, Reeves, Pickett, and Cuffee kill most of Buck's gang, and the money is destroyed in another explosion.
Escoe infiltrates Buck's house but is killed by Buck, while Pickett and Love are wounded.
Fields is freed by Cuffee and pursues Smith, who she defeats in a hand-to-hand fight.
Pickett is shot in the back by Bill, who is subsequently killed by Cuffee in a quick draw confrontation.
Love finds Buck, who is unwilling to defend himself.
Buck reveals that they are half-brothers, and that their father was once an abusive outlaw who killed his first wife (Buck's mother) when she tried to protect her son.
After leaving Buck, their father eventually repented and married another woman and had Nat.
He further indicates that driving Love to outlawry was his true act of revenge against their father.
Love reluctantly kills Buck and closes his eyes out of respect.

Love and his companions bury Pickett and Beckwourth, alongside another grave marked "Nat Love" (implied to be the resting place of Rufus Buck), as Reeves states that the law will now consider Nat to be "dead."
Cuffee joins Reeves as a deputy.
Cuffee and Reeves ride off in one direction and Love and Fields in another.
A woman holding a bowler hat looks at them from a distance.

16671137.title: George & Emma's Tranquil Journey
synopsis: Nestled in the verdant expanses of Greenville, Idaho, encircled by extensive stretches of golden wheat fields and towering barley stalks, lies the modest yet endearing country home of the elderly couple - George and Emma Miller.
