As Jane is escorted into the age-old courthouse, a wave of shock spreads amongst the once trusting locals of Whitfield.
They watch, horrified, as the notorious reality of Jane's actions unfolds threatening to shatter the quiet simplicity they’d built over the years.
The courtroom is abuzz as Sam, with an unexpected burst of confidence, uncloaks the crimes committed by Jane and her conspirators one by one.
Jane's facades crumble as the accusing voice from the audiotape resounds within the courtroom, years of her carefully crafted manipulation uncovered.
She sits in the defendant's chair, watching her empire of lies crumble in real-time.
The sigh of justice echoes through the once deceived crowd as Jane is stripped of her ruling title of legal guardianship.
Sam emerges a clear victor, his past misdeeds silently forgiven in light of his triumphant exposure.
The accusations on his integrity rolled back, leaving in place a newfound respect in the wary eyes of Whitfield’s citizens.
Emily releases a sigh laden with the relief of victory as she sets about to rebuild her relationship with her estranged mother who now sees her daughter in a brave new light.
With Jane's toxic presence gone, Emily begins to clear the cloud of deceit, reinstating a sense of security in Mrs. Parker’s life.
Emily makes a heartfelt promise to restore all of her mother’s life savings that had been deceitfully snatched away by Jane.
She proves herself to be a beacon of hope for Mrs. Parker who sees the unwavering love of her daughter finally casting away her troubles.
All the while, Jane, dejected and stripped off her grandeur, faces the shocking reality of her fall.
She is no longer the puppeteer, her strings handed over to those she once denigrated.
Sitting in the corner of the room, Jane watches as her past victims rise against her.
Her vast network of lies, like sand, slips through her clenched fist, giving rise to a sense of remorse that’s too late to redeem herself.
With Jane's conviction, the gates to her malicious network are thrown open.
The vast network is expunged, leaving behind a sense of restored justice and a newfound resilience within the hearts of Whitfield’s residents.
Sam remains aware of the lingering traces of Jane's influence and the stronger possibility of other similar guardianship rackets operating under the cover of legality.
He vows to maintain his vigilance against such malpractices.
Sam, inspired by his victory, pledges to expose more rigged schemes.
His past experience and present victory fuel his determination to shine light on the darker elements hidden within the guardianship systems.
The film draws to a close on a hopeful note, hinting at Sam's continued efforts towards maintaining the peace of the town and his dream of eradicating the society off such vices.

61076187.title: I Care a Lot
synopsis: Marla Grayson is a con artist who makes a living by convincing the justice system to grant her guardianship over elders who she pretends cannot take care of themselves.
She places them in an assisted living facility, where they are sedated and lose contact with the outside world.
She then sells off their homes and assets, pocketing the proceeds.
She and the court deny a man, Mr. Feldstrom, access to his mother after he attempts to force his way into the assisted living facility.
He later threatens her outside the courthouse, saying that he hopes she is killed.
Dr. Karen Amos informs Marla about a potential case, a wealthy retiree with no apparent partner or close family named Jennifer Peterson.
A judge appoints Marla guardian after she and Dr. Amos falsely testify that Jennifer suffers from dementia, confusion, and loss of mobility.
Marla moves Jennifer into assisted living and immediately gets to work selling Jennifer's furniture, car, and home.

While rooting through Jennifer's possessions, Marla discovers the key to a safe deposit box and finds that it contains a watch, gold bars, bank notes, and hidden, loose diamonds, which she takes and stashes away.
As Marla's girlfriend and business partner, Fran, oversees the renovation of the house, a cab arrives driven by Alexi Ignatyev, who says he is there to pick up Jennifer.
Fran says that Jennifer has moved.
Alexi returns to his employer, Roman Lunyov, greatly distressed.
Roman, a crime lord, is revealed to be Jennifer's son.
He threatens Alexi and orders him to find his mother and report back.
Mafia lawyer Dean Ericson offers to pay Marla $150,000 in cash to release Jennifer but she refuses, willing to do it only if she is paid $5 million.
He threatens Marla and takes her to court.
The judge dismisses the case as Ericson cannot prove Jennifer hired him.
Fran discovers "Jennifer Peterson" is an identity stolen from an infant who died of polio.
When Jennifer refuses to tell Marla her real identity, Marla teams up with property manager Sam Rice and withdraws filling many of Jennifer's basic needs.
Finding his mother's safe deposit box rifled, Roman sends three thugs to Jennifer's facility to take her.
This violent effort fails, and Marla helps police apprehend Alexi, who is one of the men.
Fran's police contact tells them that Alexi is the sibling of two other mafia bosses who supposedly died in a fire.
Having failed to rescue his mother, Roman has Dr. Amos killed at her office.
After hearing this news, Marla and Fran move into an unsold property of a previous victim.
Jennifer is baited into attacking Marla when she visits the facility and is moved to a psychiatric ward.
Marla is kidnapped while Fran is attacked in their home.
Marla is taken to Roman, where she demands $10 million to arrange Jennifer's release.
He refuses, and his associates knock her out with chloroform and send her in a car into a lake.
She escapes and returns home to find Fran beaten unconscious as gas fills the house.
They narrowly escape an explosion and flee to another unsold property.
Marla shows Fran the diamonds she has hidden there.
She offers Fran a choice: they can use the diamonds to start a new life elsewhere, or they can get revenge.
Marla and Fran track down Roman and kidnap him.
They force drugs into his body, burn his car, and leave him on a forest trail.
He will be discovered high on drugs and with no identification.
Roman is discovered by a jogger, and is rescued.
With no identity, Roman is designated a "John Doe" by a judge, who appoints Marla as Roman's legal guardian.
Marla visits Roman and offers to release him and Jennifer from her guardianship for $10 million.
Instead, Roman offers her a partnership in a global business based on her scam.
She accepts and, using his money and connections, quickly becomes a powerful, extremely wealthy CEO.
Roman is reunited with Jennifer, while Marla marries Fran.
While leaving a TV interview, Marla is shot by Feldstrom.
He says that his mother died alone in the assisted living facility because no one would let him see her.
As Feldstrom is arrested, Fran cries out for help as Marla bleeds to death in her arms.

83670910.title: Endless Shore (film)
synopsis: John Greene, an esteemed author who captured the world's attention with his gripping suspense novels, and his wife Eli, a renowned surrealist painter, admired for her vivid and thought-provoking body of work, find themselves stepping off a boat onto the blissful island of El Paradiso.
The Greenes have left behind their bustling New York life, seeking a serene retreat.
The couple finds their paradise within a paradise in the secluded Coconut Palm Resort.
The El Paradiso Samba Carnival is their first foray into the island's vibrant social scene.
However, the captivating beauty of the carnival takes a spine-chilling turn as a savage ritualistic murder, shrouded in the jubilation of the carnival, unfolds before their eyes.
The writer within John instantly pries into the shocking graffiti of violence that was so oddly painted amongst the carnival merriment.
The local people, sensing the Greenes' discomfort, and the police, rather frivolously dismiss the incident as a random act of violence.
Still, John, ensnared within his writer's instinct, cannot disregard the scene that is now permanently etched in his memory.
With patient and careful inquiry, he unveils old fables of a haunting curse.
Slumber becomes a dark realm for John as the narratives he uncovered infiltrate his sleep.
He experiences terrifying nightmares, a sinister waltz between his unfolding manuscript and the repressed reality of El Paradiso, blurring the lines between the two.
As they try grappling with this unsettling turn of events, they come across the upcoming 'Endless Shore Festival.'
The sinister saga associated with the festival prompts them to cut short their serene stay at the resort.
Back at the Coconut Palm Resort, unsettling events begin to unfold around them, piling onto the existing dread.
Tourists inexplicably start disappearing one after another, raising an uproar.

Fear escalates to terror when the Greenes discover all modes of escape – the airlines and ferries – have indefinitely stopped their services without any sound reason, effectively turning their hideaway into an unnerving cage.
Amid this storm of rising chaos and trepidation emerges an unlikely ally.
An island historian, an expert in deciphering the local folklore, presents a glimmer of hope in this dark hour.
He shares the knowledge of a specific ritual, performed only during the 'Endless Shore Festival' and reputed to hold the strength to lift the island's haunting curse.
With a heavy heart and the desperate need to protect Eli and the other panic-stricken visitors, John makes the monumental decision to carry out the ritual.
It was a fight against time, against invisible shadows, against his inner turmoil.
As the anticipation electrifies the air, John prepares himself mentally.
Fear courses through his veins, yet he finds courage in the loving gaze of Eli amidst the festival's raging crowd.
With the climaxing of the 'Endless Shore Festival', a hush descends over the crowd as John, wrought with fear, plunges into performing the fearsome ritual.
With anxious resolve, John adheres to the cryptic instructions.
Despite the flurry of ominous shadows that seem to be closing in around him, he manages to perform the ritual to its completion.

As the last echo of the incantation dies down, a wave of inexplicable tranquillity blankets the island, replacing the carnival's uproar with a chilling silence that freezes the crowd into eerie statues.
It's as if El Paradiso itself lets out a sigh of relief, the heavy burden of a centuries-old dread lifting and dissipating like a specter at daybreak, causing every heart to mirror its tranquility.
The remaining shaken visitors, including John and Eli, grab this hasty chance to escape the nightmarish experience that had so callously invaded their blissful retreat.
As John and Eli bid a final farewell to El Paradiso, they feel an odd mixture of relief and apprehension.
The harrowing memories drawn by El Paradiso, the Coconut Palm Resort, and the Endless Shore Festival, etch deep marks into their spirits, unmistakably altering their perspectives forever.
Their boat moves sluggishly away from the ghostly coastline.
John and Eli share a silent understanding, bearing the weight of an unpleasant terror.
A dream vacation had morphed into a nightmare, giving them a saga they'd recount with a shudder.

As they leave behind the festival echoes, a haunting phrase, "Beneath the Festivities, Lurks an Endless Fear", whispers around them, a grim tattoo that would mark their souls long after they have docked their boat safe at New York.

69649844.title: Infinity Pool (film)
synopsis: Novelist James Foster and his wife Em spend time at a resort in the fictional seaside country of Li Tolqa, where a local festival is underway.
The couple's chronic marital strife is exacerbated when Gabi, a fan of the only novel James has published, invites them to spend time with her and her husband Alban.
The four have dinner and spend the next day driving in the countryside, even though they have been warned that tourists are to remain on the resort grounds at all times.
At a beach, as James urinates behind a tree, Gabi unexpectedly grabs him from behind and gives him a handjob.
After a long day of sunbathing and cooking, the tourists drunkenly drive back to their hotel.
En route, James accidentally hits a local man, killing him.
Gabi insists that they cannot call the police as the country is corrupt and they will not be safe.
The next day, James is arrested and told that the penalty for his crime is death at the hand of his victim's firstborn son.
However, the country has a unique system of justice whereby the guilty, for a hefty fee, can be cloned and have their duplicates killed in their place.
James, who married into money, pays the fee to escape execution.
However, as part of the deal, he must watch the execution of his clone.
While Em is horrified by the entire affair and wants to leave immediately, James is titillated by the spectacle and doesn't share her urgency.
He discovers that his passport is missing but encourages Em to return to the United States.
James extends his stay by a week and encounters Gabi and Alban again.
They introduce him to a small group of Western tourists who all have been convicted of serious crimes and have paid to watch their doubles killed.
These people return to the resort annually, commit heinous crimes, and pay to watch their doubles get slaughtered.

Over the next several days, they encourage James to transform into a libertine criminal, encouraging him to kill locals, engage in intoxicated orgies (as he uses a local hallucinogen with Gabi, it's unclear how much of the orgy is real), and abuse other resort guests.
One night James is tricked into brutalizing a clone of himself he had been led to believe was the detective who initially arrested him.
In a moment of clarity and panic, James retrieves the passport he had hidden in order to stay in Li Tolqa and attempts to flee.
However, the tourist group abducts him from the bus transporting him to the airport.
Gabi reveals that she finds him pathetic, that she never read his book, and that he was targeted by the group, which is abusing him for their own amusement.
The accident James and Em had with Gabi and Alban made their plan easier to implement.
James runs off into a nearby wilderness, but Gabi shoots him in the leg.
After hours of wandering, James collapses at a farm, where a local family takes him in to recuperate.
In his drugged state, he experiences another series of hallucinations.

Once he has regained his strength, he is again confronted by Gabi's group, who order him to kill a leashed duplicate of himself they refer to as "the dog" to complete his transformation into a murdering tourist.
He initially refuses, but when the clone attempts to kill him, James beats him to death.
Gabi consoles James by exposing her bare breast, covering it with the warm blood of "the dog" and inviting him to simulate breastfeeding.
The next day, as they head back to the United States, the other tourists casually chat about upcoming errands, while James is visibly traumatized.
Waiting in the airport for his flight, he resolves to remain behind instead.
He returns to the closed resort, where he sits alone amidst the downpour of the monsoon.

38506394.title: Metropolitan Chronicles
synopsis: Michael, a jaded journalist from the humble Daily Gazette, spends his days wrestling with his wavering talent within the four gloomy corners of his faded New York apartment.
Amidst the disarray of failed articles is a once cherished photo of the vibrant Elizabeth, his former lover and an esteemed columnist for the prestigious national newspaper, The Chronicle.
The door creaks open, and Oscar strides in, his lively demeanor dissipating the gloomy aura that wraps Michael's living space.

Studying the evident deflation in Michael's spirit, Oscar presents a beacon of hope: a piece of autographed baseball memorabilia and an invitation to a social event hosted by the illustrious Douglas Richard, a well-known publisher.
Doubtful of the proposition but constrained by his dwindling career, Michael agrees to the plan, girding himself for a night that promises a mix of discomfort and prospective triumph.
In the midst of this charming chaos, Elizabeth stands out, clothed in a sleek black dress, her witching allure leaving a lingering impact on Michael.
Catching sight of her revives dormant emotions, but Michael masks his sentiments under layers of reserved pleasantries, concealing the indomitable memories threatening to surface.
Returning home, Michael is torn between his unfinished exposé's weight and the heart-wrenching bump into Elizabeth.
As the city sleeps, Michael's peaceful night is interrupted by disturbing anonymous calls warning of a catastrophic conspiracy primed to strike at the city's heart.
Overwhelmed by the danger indicated in the calls, Michael discloses the matter to Oscar, pouring out the dark threats beating in their midst.
Oscar, despite sensing the inherent dangers dancing at the doorstep, firmly decides to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with Michael.
Simultaneously, Elizabeth, nestled in her cramped cubicle at The Chronicle's headquarters, receives an anonymous tip-off about a deep-seated political deceit.
Her weathered journalistic instincts propel her to delve unabashedly into the dirty world of power and politics, determined to unearth the truth behind the impending disaster.
As Michael and Elizabeth commence their separate investigations, they unexpectedly cross paths again at a secret meeting point designated by an unknown informant.
As they find themselves investigating the same corruption-driven scandal, their lives are forced together again, unavoidably compelling them to confront their unresolved romantic history.
As their investigations converge, a shocking truth emerges - the involvement of the city's beloved social reform icon, Henry Bennett, in the concocted conspiracy.
The revelation sends shockwaves through the city, their philanthropic superhero exposed as a fraud shakes the city's core in disbelief.
Events escalate when Elizabeth vanishes into thin air, leaving behind a cryptic clue that leads to Bennett's heinous deeds.
Her last communication is a tear-stricken call to Michael, her tremored voice indicating she has been drawn too deep into the scandal's whirlpool.
Motivated by his sense of duty and rekindled love for Elizabeth, Michael, backed by Oscar's courageous support, pledges to uncover the truth and rescue Elizabeth.
The climax unfolds when Michael and Oscar ingeniously infiltrate Bennett's formidable, high-security penthouse office.
Inside, they find a cache of implicating documents providing unmistakable proof of Bennett's wicked conspiracy designed to exploit the city.
And there, in a chilling revelation, they find Elizabeth, held captive by Bennett's menacing, muscle-bound guards.
A nail-biting standoff begins, with Michael and Oscar greatly outnumbered by Bennett's heavily armed henchmen.
But, just as all hope seems extinguished, whirlwinds of NYPD's tactical unit storm in, acting upon an anonymous tip, and bringing an end to the alarming stand-off and successfully freeing Elizabeth.
Drained yet resolute, Michael pens down the harrowing events, crafting a ground-shaking exposé that earns him a well-deserved spot on The New York Times front page.
The explosive article catapults him back into the limelight of American journalism.
In the stark sanctuary of her minimalist apartment, Elizabeth mulls over the life-risking adventures her job unexpectedly brought to her.
The unnerving experiences force her to question whether her high-profile reporting career's unforeseeable dangers are worth the prizes they bring.
Oscar, having discovered his unexpected bravery during the dramatic rescue operation, decides to step out of Michael's shadow.
He gathers the courage to abandon his banal job at a local grocery store and pursues his dream of managing a community center in Brooklyn.
The winds of transformative change blow through the lives of this improbable trio.
Their intermingled lives, now venturing onto distinct paths, echo the unyielding spirit of the Big Apple and its unfailing ability to shape new tales in its unchanging cityscape.

67453324.title: Italian Studies (film)
synopsis: Opening on the protagonist going with her partner to a party with young people in NYC, the scene then cuts to daytime.
She bums a cigarette from a young girl who recognizes her but she can't recall knowing her.
One ordinary day, the protagonist goes into a hardware store, leaving her dog tied up outside.
She steps out, and suddenly she's disoriented and has forgotten everything.
She then wanders through the city aimlessly for an unclear period of time.
Finding some steps she vaguely recognises, she sits, recalling having spoken to some young people there.
As this character walks the streets with her seemingly endless stride, her memory seems to fail her.
She remembers snippets of conversations.
At a diner she meets one, and we observe that she's not even sure  of her diet even but believes she may be a vegetarian.
As she's talking with the diner teen, she confesses that she can't even answer basic questions about herself.
She argues in a corner shop with the attendant as she has no money to pay.
In another, she takes a few things and bolts.
Going to a small hotel, she tells the receptionist she misplaced her key for room 234 but, as she can't even provide a name he can't give it to her.
Outside, she finds somewhere desserted to pee and sleeps in a stairwell.
A woman approaches her, asking if she's the author Alina Reynolds, author of Italian Studies.
She saw her do a reading from the book two years ago, and describes it as a anthology of coming-of age stories.
With this information, she is able to find the book in the library.
Alina reads a chapter from the book, and she sees a reference to room 234.
With a faint smile on her face, she borrows a pen to sign it.
A man in the library tells her off for defacing the book, but apologises upon realising she is the author.
Reading the chapter Lucinda, more of Alina's memory returns.
We see the interviews with the teens was with a younger version of herself, in her early 20s.
The teen from the diner was Simon, who tells the story of his first love.
Various teens in the group tell Alina their perspectives and anectdotes.
At a fast food restaurant, the older version of herself had mentioned she is writing a novel based on ideas she gets from them, so they hand her the check.
Explaining she hasn't got any money, the teens pool together their dollars after exchanging incredulous looks.
Going to a party with more youth, Alina doesn't connect with them like she had.
Receiving open hostility, she finds herself swearing and defensive.
Alone with Simon, she says they are both broken.
She kisses him and he leaves.
Cutting to a beach, Alina catches up to Lucinda.
As they talk, she suddenly remember she lost her little white dog.
She hurries back the city, returns to the hardware store and recovers it.
In the present day, the girl who had offered Alina a cigarrette encourages her to look up Simon, whoo is a college student.
She thinks it's a bad idea as she prefers to preserve the memory, implying it would needlessly stir things.
Now married, Alina alludes to some mental difficulties she had passed through, which she believes her husband fears may return.
Alina heads home with her husband, and we are shown the images of the main interviewees she had interviewed.

60294239.title: Aikido: Guardians of Earth
synopsis: Beneath Kyoto's brilliant pink cherry blossom trees lies the tranquil Heian-kyo Temple, a silent reflection of past eras, brimming with age-old tales and solemn customs.

Over this calming backdrop, a soothing voice narrates the prominence of unseen Aikido warriors - the "Guardians of Gaia," who have pledged their existence to preserve Earth from unidentified celestial threats.
These skilled warriors, endowed with extraordinary strength and knowledge, vigilantly safeguard Earth against imminent alien invasions, often predicted through ancient mystical scripts.
During one such moonlit night, absorbed in a prayer ceremony, the ancient Amulet of Hikari housed within the temple's sacred sanctuary bursts into a brilliant glow.
The illumination, a signal of looming alien encounter - a prophecy foreseen in ancient scrolls.
As the amulet's radiance disrupts the tranquil temple atmosphere, Master Hiroshi, blessed with wisdom and resilience, rises, visibly unperturbed by the unfolding chaos.
Far beyond Earth's comforting blue atmosphere, a grim reality unravels.
An alien fleet, monstrous and terrifying in all its cosmic grandeur, hurtles down, spearheaded by Commander Zorgon.
The hideous alien overlord is resolute on this destructive course, to claim Earth for his extraterrestrial Zeta Reticuli species.
Amongst humiliated laughter and savage vows echoing ominously through the massive fleet, the intent is chillingly clear.
The alien species is hell-bent on Earth's ruthless takeover.
Back within the ancient temple confines, Master Hiroshi discloses the Guardians' intricate relic legacies to his fellow warriors.
He speaks of past warriors, their courage, wisdom, and unyielding will to protect Earth, their stories woven into the tapestry of the guild's illustrious past.
The warriors then familiarize themselves with their powerful armory - an amalgamation of traditional Samurai craftsmanship and advanced alien technology, tokens from previous alien incursions.
As anticipated, the eerie calm preceding the storm is disrupted when the Zeta Reticuli fleet lands, wreaking unimaginable havoc amongst the unsuspecting human population.
The ensuing chaos and expanding terror ultimately mobilize the Guardians.
There are no embedded warriors in every corner of the world, their valor enkindling hope amid the spreading despair.
But despite their desperate defense, the initial skirmishes against the extraterrestrial invaders result in a tragedy, casting a pale shadow over the Guardians' fighting capabilities.
Beaten, bruised and mourning their losses, they retreat to their temple, their spirit untouched.
Driven to regain their ground, they meticulously reevaluate their combat strategies, identifying their shortcomings, and uncovering novel Aikido techniques to exploit their adversaries' weaknesses.
This moment of reflection reignites a spark of hope and fortitude, a conviction that their mission is attainable, undimmed by the encompassing despair.
As the first rays of sunlight pierce the horizon, Master Hiroshi leads his rejuvenated warriors, deeply rooted in unity and fortitude, to brace against the forthcoming wave of invaders.
Together, they venture into the impending battleground, armed with their sharpened combat skills and potent weaponry, beneath the royal blue canopy of a hopeful morning sky.
The ensuing faceoff is of epic proportions, extending across continents, blurring temporal boundaries, and plunging Earth into an eerie state of timelessness.
Observing the relentless defense from his Mothership Vraxis, Commander Zorgon, infuriated yet fascinated by the Guardians' persistence, offers a grand duel.
"Surrender or fight till fall," he taunts.
Accepting the challenge with a steadfast gaze, Hiroshi mobilizes his groundwork, seizing an opportunity to truncate the alien reign of terror.
The colossal duel emerges as a choreographed display of sheer strength and technique.
Hiroshi encapsulates his well-honed Aikido skills, wisdom, and unwavering will against the blatant alien power.

Leaping forward, striking with conviction, dodging with agility, Master Hiroshi delivers a defining blow, overthrowing Zorgon, marking a victory of human courage and perseverance amidst inhumane conditions.
The remaining regiment of aliens, taken aback by their leader's defeat, unconditionally surrender, bringing the brutal warfare to an unforeseen finale.
The triumphant guardians, carrying the burden of an averted catastrophe, become heroes in their right.
These warriors return to their temple abode, shouldering the gratitude of a world they have just saved, echoing profound stillness and relief.
They solemnly remember and pay homage to their fallen comrades, their names carved as immortal symbols of bravery.

As time passes, the film concludes with the Guardians commencing their continual training sessions, hinting at potential future threats, their ever-vigilant eyes scanning the placidly cascading cherry blossom petals above the Heian-kyo Temple.
The day subtly transitions into night as Master Hiroshi's assertive voice promises Earth's relentless defense, the temple once again cloaking the stalwart warriors in its tranquil ambience.

65355241.title: Jiu Jitsu (film)
synopsis: Every six years, an ancient order of expert Jiu Jitsu fighters faces a vicious race of alien invaders in a battle for Earth.
For thousands of years the invaders have lost to Earth's defenders, up until now.
Earth's future is in jeopardy.
In a jungle in Burma (Myanmar), Asia, Jake Barnes, a celebrated war hero, is running away from shuriken under the command of Brax, the powerful invader leader.
Jake ends up on an oceanside cliff, where he is hit by the stars, falls into the ocean, hits his head and blacks out.
Wylie, a senior Jiu Jitsu fighter, rescues Jake from the water and gives him over to the care of two Burmese fishermen.
They stitch up Jake's cuts and take him to a nearby military outpost, assuming that he came from there.
After foreboding miscommunication between an inexperienced translator and one of the fisherwomen, Jake is left at the outpost and starts to regain consciousness.
But he must regain his strength!
Puzzled by the mention of a comet that comes every six years and a hole in a temple opening, the operatives set about figuring out where Jake came from.
An intelligence officer, Myra, tries to interrogate Jake but he appears to have amnesia, with no recall of events leading to his being found in the water.
After a fight sequence Myra injects Jake with a truth serum, but this proves ineffective on what he divulges.

She decides it is probable that he actually does not remember, but while discussing this with other operatives, Keung, advanced Jiu Jitsu fighter, begins to work his way through the base, besting fist and gun alike.
Keung is unfazed by repeated attacks by men in balaclavas and fatigue uniforms, who he lays flat.
Gunfire and the sound of feet against chests, heads and the like alert Myra and the others that indeed something is up.
After more fighting, Keung approaches Jake who he recognizes with a special handclasp.
Keung exclaims "We gotta go" and Jake accepts this chance to leave his captors.
Their departure from the base confirms that Jake, too, is skilled in the art of using his limbs in defense against others.
Jake then reunites with three other fighters who seem to know him but he does not remember who they are or what his mission is.
As they try to leave to head back to their base, soldiers turn up again.
The three other fighters defeat the entire unit easily but Jake gets grabbed by Myra.
She tried questioning him again back at the military base but he simply tells her she should leave.
They then decide to move out from the army base as they try to escape but they are hunted down by an alien called Brax.
The group confronts Brax at the temple and fight him.
During the fight, it is revealed that Brax has a weakness to fire and uses that to his advantage.
Jake manages to cut down Brax with a sword and shove a grenade in his gut before it heals up.
He kicks Brax into the portal and it explodes finally ending the alien race.

96269308.title: Emerald Sojourn: An Irish Journey (2022 Film)
synopsis: In the peaceful and serene county of Kerry, Ireland, we meet a melancholic teenager, Peter, grappling with the pain of the untimely loss of his mother, who to him, was a beacon of unwavering affection.

The narrative explores Peter's life at St. Patrick’s High School, where he blends into the background, and his aimless wanderings around the cobblestone-paved streets of Kerry, each step heavy with solitude and despair.
His emotional turmoil prevents him from forming bonds with his peers, leaving Peter to navigate the torrential tides of his grief, largely alone and unsupported.
Concurrently, the story unfolds in the heart of bustling Dublin, where we encounter Siobhan, a city woman with stalwart determination.
She masterfully strides through the arenas of formidable corporate law while simultaneously nurturing her newborn daughter, Aisling.

One day, on a nostalgic exploration of her late father's belongings, Siobhan stirs up a hidden secret within an antique oak chest—a cryptic letter hinting at previously undiscussed family ties in Kerry, where Peter resides.
Fueled by a thirst for closure and intrigue sparked by the ambiguous letter, Siobhan decides to embark on a journey to Kerry, taking baby Aisling along for the ride.
Once in Kerry, they experience the breathtakingly simplistic beauty of rural life—so contrasting from the frenzied hustle-bustle of their previous city existence.
Siobhan and Peter's worlds unknowingly intertwine at O'Malley's local grocery store—the town's prime social hub.
Peter finds himself drawn to Aisling's raw, untainted innocence, experiencing a flicker of elusive joy that pierces through his shroud of melancholy.
As Siobhan delves deeper into her father's past in the idyllic town, she unearths enchanting tales through her conversations with the inevitably charming and wise townsfolk.
Stories of her father's profound camaraderie with Peter's mother assemble bit by bit, like the pieces of an intricate jigsaw puzzle.
Siobhan discovers the deep bonds shared between her father and Peter's mother—expressed as tales of unconditional friendship, and unyielding loyalty.
The townspeople reveal to Siobhan that Peter’s mother, with a matching loyalty to her father, had kept the secret of her birth hidden under oath.
This earth-shattering revelation ignites an emotional whirlwind within Siobhan, invoking an empathic understanding of Peter's sorrowful solitude.
Conversely, Peter begins to find solace in Siobhan's and Aisling's quiet yet comforting presence.
Peter starts learning to confront his grief through the unwavering support of the tightly knit Kerry community, gradually making peace with the fact of his mother's physical absence.
As Peter starts to reintegrate himself into town activities, Siobhan painstakingly disentangles the mysteries of her obscured past.
Acknowledging Peter’s mother's sacrifices and the secrets she kept, Siobhan develops an intense admiration for her own unexpectedly fortunate roots.
Siobhan, irrevocably touched by the town's genuine warmth and harmony, decides to renounce her high-stress city life and make Kerry her permanent residence.
She starts her own small, locally-focused law practice and begins using her professional capabilities to advocate for the town's inhabitants.
Siobhan gradually adjusts to her new tranquil life, while Peter evolves into a caring, big-brother figure for the adorable Aisling.
He takes on responsibilities including walking her to the local kindergarten, regaling her with delightful bedtime stories, and looking after her as Siobhan shoulders work duties.
Peter's life undergoes a remarkable transformation, paralleling his emotional journey from bleak despair to hopeful acceptance.
The annual town harvest festival, embodying unity, rejuvenation, and life, applauds and celebrates Peter's inspiring journey.
At this festival, Peter’s journey of healing reaches its highpoint, and Siobhan discerns a sense of belonging and family that was previously unknown to her.

67595934.title: Joyride (2022 film)
synopsis: Set in County Kerry, Ireland, this road movie follows 13-year-old Mully, whose mother Rita has recently died of cancer, and Joy, a solicitor, and her newborn baby.
Mully's father James has stolen the cancer hospice money from the collection jar at Rita's wake, to pay off his debts.
Mully takes back the cash and drives off in a taxi to return in, but then realises there are passengers in the back seat.
Joy, overwhelmed by her needy newborn, seeing Mully's ease at caring for her child, proposes they travel together.
They swap the taxi for a car in a used car lot.
Joy and Mully take the backroads to remain undetected as he is an unlicensed driver, and they could be stopped by the police.
They quarrel at first but later bond.
The car runs out of fuel.
As they walk to get more petrol, Mully proposes that they take turns asking and answering questions.

When queried, he explains about the hospice money, and Joy shares her plans to give up the baby to her friend Mags and then fly to Lanzarote, as she has not bonded with the baby and does not know who the father is.
Calling James from the petrol station, Mully is convinced by his father to head for a ferry, which Joy initially rejects.
However, when a police checkpoint goes wrong, she changes her mind about the ferry, swapping for another car.
While waiting for the ferry, Mully helps Joy learn how to breastfeed Robin (she thought up the name upon seeing a robin alight nearby), as he observed with his infant sibling.
She tells him that she and his mother were in the same class at school, Joy one of the brightest and Rita extremely beautiful.
Mully’s father catches up with them, and Mully convinces him to let Joy and Robin go with them in the car.
They go to a B&B when Joy haemorrhages, so she can get cleaned up and rest.
In the meantime, his father has thought up a lie, wanting Mully to lie to them at the pub, saying he stole the money then got robbed.
Joy calls up her childhood friend Mags, letting her know she had the baby one week early, her name is Robin and she has breastfed her.
She then tells her about a repressed memory from her childhood.
One day, she and her mother saw her father cheating; afterwards, Joy had gone into the sea.
When she was caught by an undertow, she saw her mother hesitate to save her.
Joy tells Mags she will be there soon.
The next morning, before leaving, Joy gives the hospice money back to Mully so he can return it.
Hurt that she is leaving him and going through with giving away Robin, he lashes out, insulting her.
In a daze and with an emotional crisis, she drops Robin off on Mags's doorstep, then drives on to Kerry airport in deep denial about her own nascent feelings.
Joy boards the Spain-bound plane but immediately has a change of heart.
Insisting they let her off, she races back to find Mully.
Locating him, he initially tells her off, but James appears, demanding the money.
Joy tries to protect Mully from his father, but he races to the water, throwing the cash over his shoulder.
His father retrieves the cash, while she fishes him out of the water.
The film ends with Mags calling Joy to pick up a distraught Robin, and she drives by the pub with Mully to return the stolen money and then to collect the baby.

60815538.title: Echoes in the Lodge
synopsis: Lily, brimming with the ferocious excitement of a risk-taking 12-year-old and her two endlessly loving fathers, celebrated lawyer Peter and high-profile architect Mark, arrive at the unspoiled gem tucked into the heart of Ohio, the Friendly Pines Lodge.

The idyllic, old-world charm of the place, with its ageing beauty quietly shielded by the enveloping arms of Shawnee Forest, offers them an unexpected oasis of tranquility from their concrete jungle in Columbus, Ohio's bustling capital.
Awed by the mesmerizing serenity of the lodge, nestled among the towering and comforting pine trees, they soak in the unbridled joy that the charming structure offers them.
Fearless and adventurous Lily, whose spirit resonates to the energetic vibes of legendary Amelia Earhart, decides to unravel the unseen corners of the rustic lodge.
On one of her exploratory expeditions, she stumbles upon the source of an eerie, whispering sound bouncing off the walls of the dimly illuminated attic.
Unsettled, she shared her intriguing discovery with Peter and Mark.
Undeterred by her fathers' dismissal, Lily's explorations lead her to a hidden recess behind a vintage wine rack in the lodge cellar.
To her exhilaration and confusion, she unravels a collection of age-old, dust-ridden diaries tucked away carefully.

The diaries, marred by time, unfold grotesque chronicles that plunge her into a labyrinth of questions about the eerie happenings and disappearances associated with Friendly Pines Lodge from the early 1900s.
The curiosity initially ignited in Lily's mind turns into fixation, leading her further into the spine-chilling accounts found in the diaries.
However, as she delves deeper into the ghostly stories, a sense of threat starts to congregate, replacing her exhilaration with a gripping fear.
Peter and Mark observe a drastic change in her demeanor.
Lily, once confident, has now transformed into a restless spirit frequently beholden to flurries of inexplicable anxiousness.
One night, Lily startled her parents, narrating vague dreams about a phantasmal child she had been witnessing.
As the days unfurl, the abnormal occurrences that Lily had anticipated, start manifesting themselves.

Peter and Mark encounter the inexplicable displacement of antique porcelain figures, whispers emerging from the empty corridors at twilight, and an antique chandelier that flickers without any plausible cause.
They seek counsel from Mrs. Green, a seasoned local historian in the vicinity.
Mrs. Green embarks upon the chilling revelations associated with Friendly Pines Lodge.
The tale emerging from Mrs. Green's memories narrates the malevolent destiny of the Browning family.
The family mysteriously disappeared from the Friendly Pines Lodge, leaving behind their traumatized daughter, Abigail.
The abandoned girl, left deserted in the massive lodge, plunged into madness.
Peter and Mark resolve to confront the inconsistencies of their lodge and decide to endure whatever terror the lodge throws at their family.
But the subsequent course of events reveals a relentless surge of paranormal activities centered around Lily.
Overwhelmed with horror, Peter and Mark are paralyzed as they watch their daughter wrestle with the aggressive spirit.
Amid the swirling chaos of the supernatural occurrences, they discover that the spirit influencing Lily is not vengeful, rather a mournful soul yearning for her long-separated family.
Accompanied by Mrs. Green, they embark upon a courageous battle to reclaim their daughter from the spirit's grasp.
This journey proves a real test of their familial ties, pushing them into a whirlpool of fear and uncertainty before they finally manage to liberate Lily from Abigail's clutches.
Not just content with freeing Lily, the family decides to guide the sorrow-laden spirit towards closure of its unfinished chapters.
By helping the spirit reconcile with her lost past, they achieve the ultimate liberation of the lodge from Abigail's mournful presence.
Exhausted but relieved, they breathe sighs of peace, soaking in the hard-fought victory.
Peter and Mark collaboratively approach Mayor Johnson and the local historians, advocating for the tragic tale and historical significance of the Browning family.
Their efforts culminate in the erection of a stone memorial at Friendly Pines Lodge that honors the long-departed inhabitants.
The lodge is transformed into an educational historic site.
Surviving the unnerving ordeal has strengthened the family, and they leave the lodge behind.
Protected within their rugged SUV, the tranquility of their journey home is interrupted when they drive past an old gothic farmhouse nestled against a sunny, yellow sunflower field.
The film leaves its audience hanging precariously on the brink of a sequel with a close-up shot of Mark and Peter’s expressions in unmasked terror.

68388340.title: Knock at the Cabin
synopsis: Seven-year-old Wen is vacationing with her fathers, Eric and Andrew, at a remote cabin in rural Pennsylvania.
She is approached by a stranger named Leonard, who explains that he needs Wen and her parents' help to save the world.
Three other individuals break in with makeshift weapons and tie them up.
Struggling to fight them off, Eric sustains a concussion.
Leonard and his companions—Sabrina, Adriane, and Redmond—claim that they have no intention of harming the family.
However, in the past week, they have been driven by visions to find the family.
They foresee an impending apocalypse in which oceans will rise, a pandemic will spread, and the sky will fall.
The only way to prevent this is for the family to sacrifice one of their own.
If they do not make a choice, they will be the last people standing.
When the family refuses, the intruders sacrifice Redmond by fatally striking him with their weapons.
Eric sees a figure of light as Redmond dies.
On television, news reports show devastating megatsunamis.
Andrew believes Redmond is Rory O'Bannon, a man who had been arrested after assaulting Andrew in a bar years prior.
He thinks Rory tracked him down for revenge.
Leonard, Sabrina, and Adriane grapple with guilt, but reveal that Redmond's death has unleashed the first judgment of humanity.
The next day, the intruders sacrifice Adriane.
Meanwhile, a deadly variation of the flu virus spreads across the world.
Andrew escapes and shoots at Sabrina with his gun until she flees.
As Leonard is being held at gunpoint, Sabrina breaks in and is fatally shot by Andrew.
Leonard decapitates Sabrina, and afterwards Andrew finds Redmond's wallet and proves to Leonard that he was Rory.
Andrew confronts Leonard in the bathroom, but Leonard overtakes him and grabs Andrew's gun.
A TV broadcast reveals that hundreds of spontaneous plane crashes have occurred around the world.
Realizing their time is nearly over, Leonard informs the family that after his death, they will only have a few minutes to make a decision.
He then slits his throat.
Upon his death, lightning causes fires and more planes to crash.
Eric now believes the events are real, and that the intruders represent the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse.
Not wanting Wen to grow up in a destroyed world, he offers himself as the sacrifice and envisions an older Andrew and an adult Wen thriving in the future.
He feels that their family was chosen to make the sacrifice because their love is so pure.
Andrew reluctantly shoots and kills Eric.
Andrew and Wen find the visitors' truck with belongings that corroborate their stories.
They drive to a crowded diner, where they watch news reports confirming that the disasters have subsided.
The radio plays "Boogie Shoes" by KC and the Sunshine Band, coincidentally the song that Eric had played for them before.
The duo drives off.
As the closing credits fade out, seven distinct loud knocks are heard at the very end of the film.

72626278.title: Let Them All Write (film)
synopsis: The film "Let Them All Write" begins its story in the opulent setting of the Nobel Museum in Stockholm, where celebrated English writer, Amanda Brown, is lauded as the Nobel laureate in Literature, marking an apex in her illustrious writing career.

Her achievement sends seismic waves throughout the global literary community, the undercurrent of which translates into a vibrant anticipation for her purported next book, speculated to be her finest creation, her magnum opus.

Upon her triumphant return to England, she finds an ally in the likes of Bloomsbury, a foremost publishing giant known for fostering literary talent, which is eager to ride the momentum of her recent success.

A highly-charged conference is convened at the impressive Bloomsbury headquarters in London, wherein every editor, publication executive, and literary enthusiast congregates to decipher, decode, and understand Amanda's creative vision for her much-anticipated masterpiece.
As Amanda partakes in the dialogue, an unexpected bout of creative blankness cripples her.

Her once fertile mind, which played host to an array of vividly diverse characters and narratives, now feels like an empty desert, bereft of any coherent plan or structured narrative for her upcoming magnum opus.
Burying the weight of sky-high expectations, Amanda chooses to take a sabbatical.
She retreats to the peaceful, idyllic settings of her childhood town of Yorkshire, seeking solace and inspiration among familiar surroundings.
At Yorkshire, she embarks on a profoundly nostalgic journey to the red-bricked structures of the University of York, her alma mater.
She roams the long untouched corridors, hoping to rekindle the sparks of inspiration from her formative years.
In her quest for renewed creativity, Amanda turns to her revered old literature professor, Prof. Whitaker.
It’s during this introspective journey that Amanda crosses paths with John Bennett, a brilliantly talented yet notoriously arrogant upcoming writer, known more for his ego than his evocative prose.
John, completely indifferent to Amanda’s commendable achievements, scornfully criticizes her creative stagnation and openly questions the authenticity of her acclaimed skills.
Thousands of miles away in London, the incessant delay of Amanda's novel starts to cast its ominous shadow over Bloomsbury, threatening their reputation and financial stability.
Despite her unwavering determination and attempts to reignite her creative flame, her muse remains an elusive entity.

In a desperate bid to salvage their position, they turn to Sarah, a prodigious ghostwriter with a reputation for mirroring the style of the authors she's worked with, to clandestinely produce a novel under Amanda's name.
The editor-in-chief at Bloomsbury, with his keen editorial insight, identifies anomalies in the drafts.
He grows suspicious of their overwhelmingly disparate quality and the conspicuous absence of Amanda's subtle stylistic elements.
Amid the pressure, Amanda staunchly refuses to succumb and continues to maintain her focus on resurrecting her creative charm.
Back at the University of York, Amanda engages in intellectually stirring debates with the brash and confrontational John.
Their polar opposite viewpoints on matters of inspiration, style, and creative process serve as a reinvigorating feast for Amanda's thought-starved mind.
Unexpectedly, Amanda's shattered inspiration finds a strange source for revival - her sharp-tongued critique, John.
With her rejuvenated creativity, Amanda, now fueled with a fresh lease of determination, begins to weave captivating tales that once made her a beloved storyteller.
Just as Amanda successfully starts regaining creative momentum, the literary world is rocked by a scandal.
Sarah’s secret role in ghostwriting for Amanda is exposed, leading to public outrage and the inevitable questioning of Amanda’s creative authenticity.
Amanda, having journeyed through an intense creative struggle and finally completed her long-awaited novel, is devastated by the exposure of these dishonest practices.
In an assertive move to maintain her integrity, Amanda withdraws her manuscript from the scandal-ridden Bloomsbury.
The film then transitions to a crucial turning point, as Amanda, inspired by her academic roots, accepts a position as a literature professor at her alma mater, the University of York.
Meanwhile, John, after witnessing Amanda’s struggles and her steady resurgence, begins to perceive her in a new light.
Amanda's masterfully crafted novel, a self-reflective narrative rich with emotional depth, resonates with HarperCollins, a publishing house renowned for its ethical practices.
Their recognition of the sophistication and artistic brilliance in Amanda's work reinstates her reputation.
When Amanda’s deeply personal narrative finally gets published, it garners widespread appreciation.
The narrative resonates with readers, particularly mirroring Amanda's own narrative of hope and perseverance.
The influence of John's encounters with Amanda ignites a transformative spark within him, altering his previously dismissive approach to writing.
John, deeply influenced by Amanda's creative journey and resilience, evolves as an author, infusing Amanda’s teachings into his writing.
Amanda's courageous decision to prioritize academia over published work is lauded in the literary community, signifying yet another distinguished chapter in her prolific career.
The closure of the film reveals Amanda in her new classroom, surrounded by her avid students, lighting up their paths with her collective wisdom around the writing.

After the rollercoaster of disruptions, viewers are left contemplating about the facets of authenticity, the unspoken struggles of creativity, and Amanda’s relentless battle to safeguard her individuality as a celebrated author.

61523994.title: Let Them All Talk (film)
synopsis: Alice Hughes is a Pulitzer Prize-winning author working on her latest manuscript, which her publisher hopes will be a sequel to her best-known work, You Always/You Never.
Alice is due to receive a literary award in the United Kingdom but is unable to fly due to her health, leading her agent Karen to suggest she make the transatlantic crossing on the Queen Mary 2.
Alice invites her nephew Tyler to assist her while on the voyage, and her university friends Roberta and Susan, with whom she has lost touch.
Alice and Roberta have a difficult relationship stemming from Roberta's belief that Alice used details about her in You Always/You Never, which Roberta feels derailed her life.
Unbeknownst to Alice, Karen joins them on the ship, hoping to learn details about Alice's new book.
Once on the ship, Karen strikes up a friendship with Tyler, using him to gain information from Alice.
Alice tells Tyler that the book is about "trying to catch lightning in a bottle for a second time", possibly implying that it will be a sequel to a previous work.
She spends the majority of her time writing, only taking breaks to eat and swim.
Roberta attempts to attract wealthy men on board, while Susan begins interacting with Kelvin Krantz, another writer; Krantz writes popular mystery and thriller books, which Alice dismisses.
Krantz also knows Karen, and advises her not to pry into the details of Alice's work.
Roberta attempts to meet with Alice to seek an apology and acknowledgement of Alice's use of her life details – a fact that Alice has never admitted to – but the two fail to connect.
Alice runs into Tyler and Karen together, and learns that Tyler has a romantic interest in Karen.
Tyler and Karen have dinner, where Tyler's romantic advances are rejected.
Alice invites Karen to dinner with the foursome, where tensions come to a head between Alice and Roberta after Karen asks about the new book.
They are interrupted by Susan, who accuses them both of being selfish and holding onto their bitterness.
Alice decides to delete her book, implied to be a sequel to You Always/You Never as both Karen and Roberta expected.
After disembarking the ship, Alice and Roberta have a conversation about their estrangement.
Roberta tells Alice that she will provide her with the life details Alice would need to write a sequel to You Always/You Never, but wants a share of the profits in return.
Alice rejects this offer and they part with Roberta telling Alice "I loved you when you were Al."
That evening, Alice begins work on a new writing project.
The next morning, a man that Tyler saw frequently coming out of Alice's room on the ship greets him at Alice's door.

He reveals that he is Dr. Mitchell, Alice's personal physician, and that Alice has died in the night from deep vein thrombosis; Dr. Mitchell was aboard the ship to administer injections of a blood thinning medication to Alice.
Tyler, Roberta, and Susan visit the grave of 19th century author Blodwyn Pugh, as Alice had intended them to.
Back in the United States, Roberta gives Alice's writing, which she took from Alice's room after her death, to Karen in the hopes of profiting from it.
Karen maintains that the work is unfinished and cannot be published, but encourages Roberta's idea of writing a book about her life experiences.
Susan works with Krantz on a new book based on an idea of hers she shared with him aboard the ship.

Tyler receives Alice's unfinished writing from Karen and returns it to her apartment, recalling a talk Alice made celebrating the existence of consciousness and the ability of people to affect each other.

23888236.title: Flight from the Love-struck Monarch
synopsis: The movie begins in an idyllic setting – a tranquil countryside village nestled in the heart of Medieval England.

Here, we meet the captivating Isabella, a maiden of extraordinary beauty, and her spirited seven-year-old son, Alfred, living a quiet life in a two-roomed, thatched-roof cottage, their world brimming with rustic simplicity and harmonious joy.
Their peaceful existence is abruptly disrupted when King Witherwood, a physically imposing ruler with dangerous ambitions, becomes smitten by Isabella's bewitching charm and radiant emerald eyes.
He presents her with a lavish proposal of matrimony, a promise of riches and royal comforts soaked in the undercurrents of relentless duties and unwanted obligations.

The sudden intrusion of young Alfred into the king's luxurious palace sparks a flurry of hushed whispers and snide glances, leading to growing doubts and speculations about Isabella's virtues due to her prior motherhood.

The plot descends into a darker realm as it's revealed that King Witherwood, a staunch believer of cryptic prophecies and a seeker of boundless power, plans on offering Isabella and Alfred as sacrificial lambs to the terrifying Aezorgoth, an ancient supernatural entity known as the Unseen Titan of the Endless Void.

As whispers of the King's malevolent intentions seep into her knowledge, Isabella, filled with primal fear, tiptoes around castle corridors, formulating a perilous escape plan with her innocent son, aiming to leave behind the gilded cages and set sails towards the promising horizons of freedom.
This perilous journey takes them through ominous, thorny woods and treacherous mountain trails steeped in ancient folklore.
They encounter grotesque goblins, vindictive witches and their twisted servants, each threat spiking their journey with spine-chilling terror and moments of courageous defiance.
Amidst their grim journey, fate smiles upon them as they stumble upon a band of rebellious peasants.

These rugged men and women, simmering under the weight of King Witherwood's oppressive rule, become unexpected allies in Isabella and Alfred's desperate escape, weaving a network of camaraderie and mutiny.
Finding a haven of safety and companionship among the dissenters, Isabella and Alfred bolster their collective defense, strengthening the peasants' rebellion and inspiring the spirit of defiance.
Pushed by his raging obsession, King Witherwood turns to his dreaded necromancy, calling forth spectral hounds of the shadowlands, aiming to hunt down the fleeing mother and son.
In his bid, the fearful Aezorgoth is invoked into physical existence, its bone-chilling roars reverberating through the castle walls amplifying the story's mounting tensions.
The plot spirals into heightened anxiety with the unleashed demonic forces and paranormal apparitions, casting an ominous shadow.
The climax nears as Isabella, Alfred, and the intrepid band of peasants find themselves engaged in a brutal struggle against Witherwood's hellhounds.
They navigate a cursed forest shrouded in fog and dangerous creatures, setting the stage for a sprawling, nail-biting chase.
As they delve deeper into the chaotic darkness, they uncover ancient folklore that speaks of a cosmic talisman - the Aegis of Light.
This mythic artifact, known for its divine radiance, might have the power to obliterate Aezorgoth's deathly magic, providing a sliver of hope in their dire circumstances.
Guided by this newfound knowledge, they set off on an exciting, danger-steeped quest to secure the fabled Aegis of Light, stirring a sense of anticipation in the narrative.
The final act opens with a thrilling mission.
The Aegis of Light is rumored to be hidden in the ancestral St. Ethelred Cathedral, a fortress-like structure maintained by King Witherwood's fierce knights.
Isabella and the peasants, driven by a desperate sense of courage, stage a daring heist under the mellow dusk light.
Despite the odds stacked against them, they triumph over Witherwood's knights in a storm of sword-clashing, adrenaline-inducing battle.
Their spirit remains undeterred even in the face of grave danger.

The story reaches a peak of intensity as the hallowed Aegis of Light crackles to life, its divine illumination casting out the terrifying influence of Aezorgoth, freeing our heroes from his tyrannical reach.
They seize the glowing Aegis, making a heart-pounding, moonlit escape across the cathedral roofs, hurtling towards the safety of the rebel ranks.
King Witherwood, aghast at their audacious success, orders his elite soldiers into a relentless pursuit of the defiant group.
The narrative hurdles towards an electrifying climax.
The thrilling finale unfolds within the imposing walls of King's Keep Castle.
A bloody confrontation between the peasants and the king's soldiers sets the throne room astir.
Amid the chaos, Isabella musters her deepest courage, raising the vibrant Aegis of Light against the weakened Aezorgoth.
The titan is banished into the vortex of the abyss, giving our heroes a long-awaited victory.
Aezorgoth’s departure creates a power vacuum, causing seismic shifts in King Witherwood's rule, effectively toppling the pyramid of old world power.
The era of Witherwood's tyranny ends, releasing a wave of relief across the kingdom as the promise of peace and justice lingers in the air.
The final scene unfolds amidst a grand celebration where Isabella, Alfred, and the brave peasants celebrate their momentous victory, ringing in a fresh epoch of fairness and tranquility.
The once feared King Witherwood becomes a fading memory.

68850089.title: Little Vampire
synopsis: Pandora, a beautiful young woman and her son seek to escape from a prince, who is in love with Pandora; he is furious to see that she already had a child and seeks to deliver them to the God of Nothingness, a gigantic slimy monster.
When all seems lost for Pandora and her son, a skeleton pirate, the Captain of the Dead flies to their rescue because Pandora promised to give her life to whoever would save her child.

Once on board the Captain's boat, whose mermaid acts as a figurehead named Boisdormante and is populated by monsters of all kinds, Pandora and her son transform into vampires and become living dead who will never age, but the God of Nothingness, furious at not having had his fresh flesh to eat, devours the soldiers.

Prince begs to spare him and the monster accepts; after having swallowed him, transforms him into a being with a head of moon baptized the Gibbous and allows him to seek revenge on Pandora and the Captain of the Dead.

Since Gibbous is capable of killing the undead, the Captain of the Dead has no choice but to flee with Pandora and her son who has taken the name of "Little Vampire" through the world and the different eras, during which they meet the monsters Marguerite (a creature inspired by Frankenstein's monster), Claude (a radioactive crocodile), Fantomate (a tomato-dog) and Ophtalmo (a monster inventor) who join them, before ending up hiding in a mansion on a small hill in town where the Captain creates a dome making them invisible to everyone.
300 years later, Little Vampire begins to get tired of the film club where he goes daily with the other monsters as well as their incessant arguments.
He then decides to run away with Fantomate to go to school where he wants to meet children.
Little Vampire meets Michel, an orphan who lives with his grandparents and believes in monsters, through a mathematics notebook.
Little Vampire begins to do his homework for him without any fault and corresponds with him who ends up wanting to meet him.
He then goes to Michel's without noticing that he has taken with him a kawai (humans turned into bugs by the Gibbous) stuck in the notebook.

Once at Michel's, Little Vampire wakes him up and the two boys get to know each other, but on returning, Little Vampire and Fantomate come across the Gibbous (which Fantomate thought they had managed to get rid of) and manage to escape him.
Little Vampire then confides in Pandora about the Gibbous, keeping the fact that he visited a human.

Taking advantage of a game with Marguerite, Claude and Ophtalmo, Little Vampire decides to go to Michel's to ensure his safety against the advice of Fantomate who no longer wants to go out because of the Gibbous.
The dog then decides to go and confess everything to Pandora and the Captain of the Dead; the latter orders Fantomate and the monsters to bring Michel back in order to "ensure his silence".
Michel and Little Vampire go outside, where they are joined by the other monsters that the vampire passes off as his cousins.

Michel is then invited to meet the Captain of the Dead who, finding him sympathetic, makes him swear with a pirate oath to be a faithful friend to Little Vampire and never to reveal his existence to anyone.
At first, Michael and the monsters get along well, but Little Vampire is disappointed that Michael isn't a monster.
Ophtalmo then proposes to transform Michel into a monster but the operation proves to be very dangerous, and Michel flees home.

At night, he is surprised by the appearance of Gibbous who, knowing that Michel has been dating his prey for a long time, blackmails him: if he does not reveal to him where Little Vampire and Pandora are hiding, he will kill his grandparents.
While Little Vampire, Fantomate, Marguerite, Claude and Ophtalmo are arguing about Michel, they later see him on a surveillance camera in Little Vampire's room where he leaves a message from Gibbous.

Fantomate accuses him of betraying his oath and tries to hurt him but Michel gives up protecting his grandparents and withdraws the message but he falls into a trap door which leads him to Little Vampire and the monsters.

Little Vampire then decides to go and confront the Gibbous so that he can no longer terrorize them; after having awakened Boisdormante, he leaves with Michel, Marguerite, Claude and Ophtalmo on the Captain's boat in search of that of the Gibbous which is moored in Michel's garden.
When they arrive at their destination, they are captured: Michel and the monsters are stuffed in a bag while Little Vampire is brought to the Gibbous.
Worried, Fantomate warns Pandora and the Captain of the Dead that the Gibbous have captured Little Vampire, Michel and the monsters.
The latter, followed by the Captain's crew, come to their rescue, meeting Michel's grandparents on the way.
Finding his boat, the Captain finds that the Gibbous has put Boisdormante to sleep.
It is then that the latter arrives and kidnaps Pandora under the eyes of Fantomate and the Captain.

Transformed into a mouse, Little Vampire frees his friends with whom he faces the Gibbous kawais while the Captain and the Gibbous engage in a duel that Pandora, out of patience, ends up interrupting.
The latter declares that it cannot go on like this but the Gibbous bursts into tears at the idea of having to stop wanting revenge and admits that he needs company, otherwise he becomes mean.
Little Vampire explains to him that he was also bored until he met Michel and that in order to be loved by another person, he must agree and must not be forced.
The kawaïs come to confirm it because they like the Gibbous even if he likes to crush them.
Gibbous, convinced, recognizes that Pandora loves the Captain because he saved her but he does not know what to do because the sleeping princesses who must be awakened are rare.
It is then that Little Vampire shows her Boisdormante and the Gibbous ends up waking her up; Boisdormante frees herself from the ship and takes the hand of the Gibbous who becomes the prince again.
Under the moved gaze of Little Vampire, the prince and Boisdormante decide to flee death in turn with love while the kawais decide to build their democracy.

The next day, Michel reveals to his teacher and his class the trickery of Little Vampire and promises to get back to work, then he goes to the beach to find Little Vampire, Fantomate, Marguerite, Claude and Ophtalmo and they start playing under the eyes of Pandora and the Captain of the Dead who can now leave their mansion without fear.

85069015.title: Dash to Midnight (2021 film)
synopsis: Alex, who dedicated his heart and soul to the intricate world of Marvel and DC comics, found himself confronted with yet another lonely New Year's Eve celebration.
His kinship sprung from the curious mix of wanderers and pragmatists that formed his co-workers at the small-town bookstore.

Responding to his situation, they forged a profound plan to host a spontaneous celebration to welcome the new year, generously offering Alex a reprieve from his impending solitude and sowing in him a new glimmer of expectancy.

As the discourse in the breakroom ebbed and flowed around the exhilarating turns of 'The Amazing Spiderman series', Alex found the courage to extend an invitation to Emma, his long-standing crush who tended the travel section.
To his absolute delight, she surprised him by accepting the invite.
The prequel to the party played out like a comic strip of its own, as Alex and his band of friends scrambled to curate a truly unforgettable New Year's Eve gathering.
A particularly memorable moment ensued as one of Alex's friends, notorious for his culinary disasters, attempted to bake a sumptuous New Year's Eve cake.
The resulting near-fire fiasco ended up as a comic blot on their preparations.
Add to this chaos, another friend from their motley crew was consumed by the fervor to create the perfect party ambience.
His wrestling match with an army of unruly fairy lights culminated in a blackout, adding to the laughs.
Amidst all this bedlam, they found themselves embarking on an unanticipated adventure of securing an eleventh-hour DJ, thereby escalating comedic tension with their antics.
As she dove deeper into her thoughts, Emma found herself smitten by Alex's effortless humor, genuine kindness and his refreshingly uncomplicated nature.
The grandeur of the gathering on New Year's Eve didn't fail to be as eventful as the lead-up.
The fun-filled skirmishes and harmless pranks set an entertaining rhythm in the room.
Alex, now cloaked in a polished navy-blue suit, delighted the crowd with an audacious karaoke tribute for Emma.
His rendition of Madonna certainly did leave a mark, mostly due to the ensuing furniture-toppling fiasco.
Alex became the star of a liquor-laden game of charades.
His overzealous attempt resulted in a diving spectacle straight into the punch bowl.
His follies, instead of being embarrassing, only served to elevate his offbeat charm.

Meanwhile, Brad, the bookstore charmer who had consistently shown interest in Emma, saw his efforts to woo her foiled time and again by Alex's dedicated troop of friends, who were rooting for their comic connoisseur confederate.
Brad's underhanded attempts to meddle with the budding relationship between Emma and Alex met with slyly timed drink spills and strategically abrupt changes in the DJ's play list.
As the party reached a fever pitch, the clock announced ten minutes to midnight.
Cake frosting smeared Alex, with his ever-faithful friends in tow, began weaving his way through the exuberant crowd to reach Emma standing across the room.
His journey across the cramped room underlined the hilarious chaos the party had dissolved into.
At one point, he had to navigate through an enthusiastic mosh pit of tipsy partygoers and inadvertently found himself meandering into a plate of spaghetti, prompting an impromptu food fight.

To add to the farcical scenes, a hyperactive poodle named Polly, belonging to one of the guests, suddenly decided that Alex's trousers were her chew toy for the night, and became yet another amusing hurdle in his path.
Emma, shining like a star in her sequin black dress, began her own determined quest to meet him halfway.
She was ready to reveal the affection she had discovered for Alex.
Dodging her work friends from the periodicals department who tried to shepherd her into a round of Twister, she remained single-minded in her objective.
As the countdown clock neared the last minute, Emma and Alex were locked in a race against time to find each other amidst the bustling crowd.
The climax saw the room dissolve into a riotous laughter as a disheveled Emma and an exhausted Alex ran head-on into each other just as the countdown ended.

Amidst the backdrop of cheering friends, multi-hued confetti raining from the ceiling, and the reverberating clamor of the clock striking midnight, Emma and Alex held each other's gaze and leaned in for their first heart-poundingly exhilarating kiss.

Their friends, who had watched this romance unfold with collective enthusiasm, erupted into euphoric cheers and applause, while Brad, the jilted lover, slunk into a shadowy corner, brooding with his half-empty glass of punch.
As the shimmering confetti settled on the worn-out floorboards, Emma and Alex held each other close, looking ahead to a year strewn with unscripted moments of absolute hilarity.

Their future seemed a vivid tapestry of eclectic friendships, shared passion for comic tales, and a newfound love for each other, promising each approaching year to be filled with laughter, high-jinks and perhaps, an annual comic tribute to their first ever New Year's Eve run to midnight.

66665348.title: Long Story Short (2021 film)
synopsis: At a New Years' Eve party, Teddy races to kiss his girlfriend Becca by midnight.
By mistake, he kisses another woman named Leanne who is wearing the same dress.
Leanne helps Teddy when he goes into anaphylactic shock from inadvertently consuming a peanut that was in Leanne's mouth, and the two begin a relationship.
A few years later, Teddy and Leanne visit Teddy's father's grave to give him the news that Teddy has proposed using the ring he personally crafted for Teddy's mother, though they haven't set a date.

A strange woman overhears them and cautions Teddy against wasting his life and gives him a wedding gift of a tin can, with the instruction not to open it until his tenth anniversary, for which the traditional gift is tin.
The morning after the wedding, Teddy wakes up to discover that exactly one year has passed and Leanne is 18 weeks pregnant.
A few minutes later, time shifts to their second anniversary and he is the father of a baby girl who, much to his shock, is named Talullah.
Teddy realizes that time is passing normally for everyone but him, and asks his best friend Sam to meet him in one year with an anniversary present, which he does.
They theorize that Teddy's predicament is similar to that in the film Groundhog Day, and that Teddy must have a "perfect day" to break the curse.
In the intervening year, Teddy and Leanne have begun couples' counseling and their therapist has asked them to write letters to each other.
Leanne feels that Teddy isn't the man she married, as he spends all his time at work.

Teddy promises he can change, but the letter he wrote betrays the resentment he feels at being forced to be the family breadwinner instead of pursuing his dream of photography, while Leanne chases a "pipe dream" of being a writer.
On Teddy and Leanne's fourth anniversary, Teddy is shocked to find Leanne gone; they have agreed to a trial separation.
Worse, Sam has been diagnosed with skin cancer, and Teddy is shocked by his weight and hair loss.
On their fifth anniversary, Teddy wakes up from a night with his ex Becca, whose marriage has also fallen apart and who Teddy has been seeing casually for a few months.
Teddy rushes Becka onto the terrace when Leanne drops by wanting to get back together.
They almost have sex, but Leanne walks out upon finding Becca's bra on the couch.
Becca vows to stop seeing Teddy, but they are still together a year later.

Teddy wonders what keeps bringing them together when they're clearly wrong for each other, and Becca sadly notes that she would have been able to save her marriage if she had the knowledge then that she has now.
Teddy visits Leanne and is surprised to learn that she is the owner of a Great Dane puppy (a dog Teddy disliked) and is dating a man named Patrick.
He suggests they get a kiddie pool, which, as time shifts again, he falls into.
Leanne and Patrick help him out and Teddy is shocked to see Leanne is no longer wearing his ring.
She shamefully admits that she lost it at the beach, and couldn't find it even after hours of searching.
Teddy takes the dog on a walk to the beach, where another year passes.
He finds a chocolate bar containing peanuts in the sand and considers suicide.
His daughter, Tallulah, whom he doesn't remember seeing since infancy and is now seven, tries to cheer him up.
Another year passes.
Teddy tries to call Sam but is heartbroken when he realizes that he has died.
He visits Sam's grave, where he again encounters the strange woman who gave him the "gift" of fast-forwarding through his life.
She explains that she was given a similar gift shortly before her own wedding; her experience made her realize that she didn't love her fiancé, and was in fact a lesbian.
She often visits her lover's grave to show her how she's using the years she never got to give other people the same gift.
On their tenth anniversary, Teddy rushes to Leanne's house and asks her to find the old tin can.
Upon opening it, Leanne miraculously finds Teddy's father's ring.
Teddy and Leanne finally reunite, and Teddy wakes up the day after the wedding.

Now with a new outlook on life, Teddy calls his boss to inform her he will be cutting down his hours at work and studying photography, encourages Sam to get screened for skin cancer, and resolves to give the tin can to Becca so she can save her own marriage.

4364802.title: Vanished Women & Love Ryokans
synopsis: With a mix of trepidation and determination, Susan disembarks from the sleek Shinkansen train and steps onto the platform of Tokyo Station.
Surrendering to the vibrancy of Tokyo, she gasps in the crisp city air.
This bustling landscape, vastly different from the skyscrapers of New York, now becomes her refuge from a turbulent past she hopes to forget.
Fortune smiles on Susan when she lands a job at 'Heiwa no Ie', a tranquil ryokan, packed with history that spans over several centuries.
The delicate tranquility of her new workplace soothes her frayed nerves and offers a stark but pleasing contrast to her hectic past life.
She finds her guides in this unfamiliar territory in the form of her co-workers at the ryokan.

Aiko, with her piercing onyx eyes unfolds the stoic layers of Japanese grace; Yumi, the embodiment of absolute joy, projects a neon smile as inviting as a blossoming sunflower; Miki, full of childlike wonder, infuses endless curiosity into their shared experience.
Confronted with the strangeness of traditional customs, from the process of wrapping a kimono to the meticulous ritual of tea ceremonies, Susan initially feels overwhelmed.
However, through quiet observation and relentless patience, she weaves herself into the tapestry of her paradoxical life that blends moments of tranquility with laborious work schedules.
Sheltering within the distinctive personalities of Aiko, Yumi and Miki, she finally feels gaps in her own story closing.
