Intriguing stories unravel, about Aiko, the oppidan widow seeing the ryokan as a living memory of her departed husband; Yumi, a daring spirit who fled an oppressive household in Osaka; and lastly, Miki, nurturing a hidden aspiration for a life beyond the kyokan's rigorous conventions.
Over time, a robust bond entwines each of these women, their unique stories creating a shared narrative of unrealized dreams, unspoken expectations, and dark secrets lurking in shadows.
During an errand to clean the ryokan's attic, Susan stumbles upon an eerie pattern hidden in the old records and personal notes.
Unsettling traces of female employees who strangely disappeared over the last decade, all of whom harbored dreams strikingly similar to theirs, send shivers down her spine.
Fear subtly enters their world, distorting the ryokan's image from a sanctuary to an ominous fortress.
The once comforting walls now seem burdened with untold secrets.
Faced with reluctance from her colleagues, Susan forges on with her quest for truth.
Each missing woman's tale echoes with their own dreams of sanctuary in the ryokan, triggering an uncontrollable urge within her to reveal their fate.
As she delves deeper into the ryokan's history, Susan grapples with her own fear of a past marked by scandal and alleged crime, threatening to resurface and shatter her newfound peace.
Alongside the sordid history of the ryokan, Susan's past rears its head once again.
She finds herself forced to confront pain that she thought had been buried in her escape to Japan.
Summoning immense strength, she reveals her scandalous exit from America - a series of misguided decisions, leading to scandal, immense losses, and her consequent self-imposed exile to Japan.
Her colleagues - Aiko, Yumi, and Miki - struggle with these revelations against the backdrop of their own introspection and the shocking truths Susan uncovers about their beloved ryokan.
As personal battles and persisting fear amplify, so does their need for each other.
The quartet finds unity in their shared grief, emerging courage, and intertwined destinies.
Emboldened by Susan's bravery, the women continue their pursuit of truth.
A charged atmosphere of deep respect and shared goals surrounds them as they step forward.
Learning to absolve herself from remorse and shame, Susan finds solace in the unwavering support of her peers.
She no longer feels like an outsider, instead identifying as an integral part of their collective strength.
Their journey reaches a chilling climax as they uncover horrifying secrets tangled amidst Heiwa no Ie's historical allure.
The previously dismissed pattern of staff disappearances gnaws at their guts, now making horrific sense.
Fear, rage, and fierce determination merge within them, galvanizing them into a formidable force of justice.
Determined to tear apart the cloud of malevolence lingering over the ryokan, they turn to face the storm.
With the menacing truth laid bare, they battle against the odds, advocating justice for the vanished women and reclaiming their residential ryokan as a sanctuary once more.
Once a woman fleeing from her past, Susan now bravely walks the path of reconciliation.
Her painful history aligns with her peaceful present, guided by the strength of the women whom she now calls family.
Under the attentive stewardship of Susan, Aiko, Yumi, and Miki, the ryokan thrives.
Unified and stronger than ever, their spirit infused in every corner of the historical gem.
Their journey, grappling with shared secrets, forged resilience and powerful unity, casts a metaphorical sunset upon the once troubled ryokan, symbolizing a tale of survival, redemption, and triumph.
Conquering adversity, they breathe new life into the Heiwa no Ie.
The inn that once catered to weary travelers now also warmly welcomes those fighting personal battles, providing a sanctuary under the watchful eyes of the triumphant quartet.

64508008.title: Lost Girls & Love Hotels
synopsis: Margaret is an American expatriate living in Tokyo.
She works at a Japanese academy during the day teaching prospective flight attendants how to speak English.
She spends her nights getting drunk with fellow expatriates Ines and Liam, and seeks out submissive sexual encounters with random men in the city's numerous love hotels.
Her misadventures cause her to sometimes show up to work in a daze and disheveled, drawing the concern of her manager, Nakamura.
However, Nakamura sees something of her younger self in Margaret and is sympathetic.
One day, Margaret crosses paths with a Yakuza enforcer named Kazu, and the two begin a relationship.
Margaret is at first taken aback by Kazu's revelation that he is about to get married, but she continues with him after he admits that his marriage is more out of duty than love.
Margaret confides to Kazu that she does not have a family: her father left when she was a child, her mother died from cancer, and she has a schizophrenic brother.
She came to Japan to be alone.
On the day of graduation for Margaret's students at the flight academy, Kazu asks Margaret to spend the entire day with him in Kyoto.
Initially reluctant to skip graduation, Margaret agrees when he says he will not get another day, and they take the train.
He brings her to the Kiyomizu-dera temple and shows her the "Buddha's womb", a stone illuminated at the end of a pitch-black tunnel.
Kazu explains the symbolism of being reborn by reaching the stone and says that he has brought Margaret there hoping to help her let go of her trauma; but Margaret seems unaffected.
On the train ride back to Tokyo, Kazu leaves the train while Margaret is asleep, leaving her despondent and desperate to find him when she wakes up.
When she returns to work the next day, she finds that she has been dismissed and replaced.
Margaret spirals down further when Ines reveals to her that she is leaving Japan.
Following numerous meaningless sexual encounters, Margaret spots Kazu with his family by chance one day and follows him into a love hotel.
Kazu reprimands Margaret for following him, telling her nothing can happen between them.
When Margaret insists that she loves him, they have sex one more time before he sends her away, leaving him saddened and conflicted.
When Margaret returns to her apartment she finds an eviction notice.
She desperately takes a job as a bar hostess for drunken businessmen, but finds herself unable to participate and leaves without getting paid.
Now homeless and at rock bottom, Margaret is found on the street by Liam's girlfriend Louise, who reveals that Liam has been deported.
After sharing a drink with Louise, Margaret gets drunk and begins wandering around Tokyo aimlessly at night until she notices of a strange man following her.
She asks him to take her to a love hotel.
She tells him that she likes to be submissive.
On his orders she strips naked and lies down, the stranger then tying her hands and feet to the bed.
When he suggests that he could kill her, she begs him to do it, but Kazu comes into the room to rescue her, having followed her.
Grateful for being rescued, Margaret decides to start anew by leaving Tokyo.
On the plane, Margaret notices Tamiko, one of her former students, as one of the flight attendants and they smile at each other while Tamiko demonstrates safety procedures before the plane takes off.
Margaret calls Kazu to tell him she now understands the symbolism of the "Buddha's womb" and finally feels reborn, saying goodbye to him for good.

15303181.title: Parisian Love Flight
synopsis: Meet our protagonist, John, a hard-working banker devoured by the relentless pace of New York.
His dream of an alleviating break is manifested in the form of a long-awaited trip to the charming city of Paris.
His artistic cousin, Ava, resides there, painting her days towards success.
His plane lands smoothly at Charles de Gaulle Airport, where he is welcomed with warmth by the radiant Ava and her eccentric Parisian roommate, Lily.
Lily's effortless charm, abundant energy, and unparalleled zest for life fascinate John from the very first encounter.
Struck by enchantment, John often finds himself lost for words in Lily's presence.
The task of articulating his sudden affection turns into a peculiar struggle he hadn’t been prepared for.
In the meantime, Ava, completely oblivious of this nascent romance, humorously tries to pair off John with her colorfully diverse circle of friends.

However, Ava’s innocent meddling brings about a chain of laugh-out-loud moments and potently awkward situations, turning John's attempts to confess his affection into a series of regrettable blunders.
Despite the numerous obstacles, John is valiantly determined to win Lily's heart.
His journey spirals into a whirlwind of hilarious capers and absurdities, burlesquely magnified by the French setting.
In a humorous endeavor, he finds himself in a chaotic situation of becoming a reluctant participant in a disgruntled mime's performance at the renowned Café de Flore.
In another misadventure, he unintentionally offends a dignified French chef at the prominent restaurant, Le Meurice.
An innocently misplaced critique of Escargot soon escalates into a theatrical fiasco.
The art enthusiast in John leads him to the Louvre, where he gets lost among the captivating, history-infused corridors.
This promptly triggers a comedy of errors that leaves visitors and tour guides agape.
Amidst the mirthful chaos, Lily's fondness for the diffident yet captivating John grows.
His endearing personality and heartwarming clumsiness tug at her heartstrings, making her slowly fall for him.
Their relationship engenders several raw and heartfelt encounters that sensitively enforce a deep connection, paving a path into an unexpected romance.
After an emotional journey, John musters enough courage to divulge his feelings for Lily.
However, his declaration is preempted by devastatingly ill-timed intervention.
Lily's ex-boyfriend, Pierre, an impeccably polished Frenchman, makes an unexpected return.
His entry sends unforeseeable shockwaves through John's hopeful plan.
Lily, unaware of John's deep feelings, neutrally distances herself from him.
She erroneously assumes John’s affection towards Ava’s friends, a misunderstanding engineered unintentionally by Ava's constant setups.
Disillusioned and heartbroken, John decides to escape the emotional cyclone stirring within him.
He disguises his sorrow with practiced humor and impulsively decides to cut short his Parisian endeavor.
He books a rushed flight back to New York, abandoning his hopes and dreams of a love-filled Parisian adventure.
Ava stumbles upon a heartfelt letter John had penned for Lily but never delivered.
The unsent letter reveals the depth of his feelings, along with Ava's accidental hand in John's heartache.
Ava, confronted by the colossal misunderstanding, implores John to confess his love before abandoning it entirely, forcing the disheartened lover into a frenzy.
Carmaggedon ensues as a frantic John chases time through the labyrinth of the narrow, winding streets of Paris in his rented Peugeot.
Witnessing an opportunistically available hot air balloon, he quickly ascends into the Parisian skyline.
With a love-powered courage, John throws caution to the wind.
In a fervent act of desperation, he shouts his love for Lily across the picturesque Parisian panorama, announcing his suppressed emotions into the open world.
Lily fortuitously hears this dramatic display of affection and is profoundly touched.
John's declaration resonates deeply within her, inciting a rush of emotions she couldn't possibly ignore.
Excited yet fearful, she makes her way to the airport, with the desperate desire to meet John before he departs, etching a potentially tragic end to their affectionate escapades.
As Lily's dramatic arrival unfurls with the Eiffel Tower standing benignly in the background, John finds himself at the verge of his return flight.
Caught off-guard, John stands frozen as Lily expresses her reciprocated feelings in front of the bustling terminal crowd, epitomizing their moment with a passionate farewell kiss.
Lily vows to follow John back to New York, bidding her lover a temporary goodbye at the brink of his departure, imbuing the airport scene with a palpable romantic tension.
Back to his mundane job in New York, the resilient John re-enters his old life with a heart brimming with Parisian memories.
His monotonous routine is abruptly disrupted by a delightful surprise.
Lily, true to her word, strides into John's Wall Street office.
Her entrance rekindles their adventurous romance, promising an exciting continuation of their love story, which seems to have just begun.

60527595.title: Love Wedding Repeat
synopsis: While in Rome visiting his sister Hayley, Jack tries to muster up the courage to kiss her roommate Dina before returning to London.
However, they are interrupted by his old schoolmate Greg, and after Jack and Dina awkwardly say their goodbyes, a frustrated Jack leaves with Greg.
Three years later, Jack is at Hayley's wedding.
She informs Jack that Dina has come to the wedding and is newly single.
After the ceremony, he and Dina meet for the first time in three years.
They admit that they used to ask Hayley about one another.
Marc, Hayley's former school classmate, arrives uninvited while high on cocaine, confessing his love for her.
She demands that he leave, but her husband Roberto appears and invites Marc to stay for the celebrations.
Hayley asks Jack to drug Marc with her sleeping drops and he reluctantly agrees.
Shortly after Jack places the drops into Marc's empty champagne glass, a group of children playfully rearrange the seating order.
The narrator comments on the many variations eight people can sit at a table.
The drugged glass ends up with Bryan, the "maid of honour", who quickly drinks it all.
While Jack and Dina reconnect, Marc blackmails Hayley by threatening to tell Roberto they had sex three weeks earlier.
She again asks Jack to handle Marc, so Jack locks Marc in a cupboard.
A sedated Bryan mumbles through his maid-of-honour speech before destroying the cake.
The mayhem is exacerbated by the presence of Jack's vindictive ex-girlfriend and her current insecure, jealous boyfriend.
After a guest releases Marc from the cupboard, he grabs the microphone and exposes his affair with Hayley in front of all the guests.
Upset, Roberto abandons Hayley, but when she tries to stop him, he accidentally falls over a balcony.
The scene freezes as the narrator reminds the audience of how the wedding can be affected by endless seating arrangements.
In fast-forward, the film depicts a number of alternate scenarios where different guests are drugged each time, all ending in chaos.
In the last scenario, Jack is finally seated beside Dina, though he is the one that ends up drugged.
Unable to regurgitate the sedative, he asks Bryan to insert his fingers down his throat.
Dina walks in on them, much to Jack's embarrassment.
They try to move past it back at the table, but as Dina tearfully opens up about her mother's death, Jack struggles to stay awake, upsetting her.
Things soon begin to look up for Jack and the other guests.
Bryan gives a successful speech, impressing Vitelli, an important film director also in attendance, and hooks up with another guest, Rebecca.
Following a conversation with Jack, Marc decides against exposing the affair.
Instead, he wishes Hayley and Roberto the best and leaves.
As Dina is leaving the wedding due to a work emergency, Jack attempts to connect with her for the last time.
She says that, although their feelings were mutual, they missed their moment and she leaves.
Having finally landed an opportunity with Vitelli, Bryan inspires Jack to take chances when they come.
He chases after Dina, catching her at the end of the street.
They are nearly interrupted by a man passing by who claims to know Dina, but Jack turns him away and they finally kiss.

28616335.title: Broken Bonds: An American Tale (2020 film)
synopsis: Our initial protagonist, John Doe, is introduced as a captivating figure in the world of Manhattan, both revered and reviled as one of New York City's most powerful real estate tycoons.

He navigates through a life underscored by opulence, residing within the towering luxury penthouses, rubbing shoulders with Manhattan's elite, and accompanied by his equally successful wife, Mary Doe, an influential banking executive.
Beneath the veneers of their polished lives, the couple's overwhelming disconnect and emotional aloofness infuse a toxic skepticism within their marriage.
The constant glare of the public eye and the overriding pressure to maintain a facade of an ideal couple, despite festering private woes, creates an uneasy tension between the two.
Unable to bear the burden of his crumbling marriage any longer, John confides his distress to his oldest friend - Ben Stevens.
A respected psychologist by profession, Ben has faithfully upheld his role as John’s confidant and mentor since their childhood.
John broaches the idea of divorcing Mary, revealing his fear of public scandal and the overwhelming cost it would mean, considering their shared assets running into millions.
Ben initially tries to dissuade John from taking such a tumultuous step, mindful of the consequences it would entail on a public and personal level.
However, as John's emotional distress grows irrefutably apparent, Ben reassesses his stance and begins to look beyond societal implications.
Ben recommends John to seek out the guidance of Robert Goodman, a divorce attorney of eminent standing, known for maintaining the interests of his clients amidst an emotional whirlpool.
On the flip side, Mary remains unaware of John's internal turmoils and is engrossed with orchestrating their silver anniversary.
In a dramatic turn of events amidst the pompous celebration, John announces his decision to divorce Mary, inducing a gasp of shock from their astounded companions.
The news hits Mary, who is left visibly taken aback and red-faced underneath the sparkling party lights.
The public humiliation left her dumbstruck, standing in disbelief in front of their crème de la crème friends and acquaintances.
Despite the widespread condemnation and bitter backlash, John remained steadfast in his decision.
His unwavering determination showcased his desperation to break free from their emotionally draining marriage and pursue a personal sense of joy.
Ensuring his interests were safeguarded during the legal turmoil, he appointed Robert Goodman as his divorce attorney, instructing expedited proceedings.
Breaking his ties with long-term friends who openly disapproved of his choice, he parted ways to ensure zero interference in his decision.
Meanwhile, Mary, struggling to comprehend John's sudden announcement, starts questioning the rationale behind the abrupt itinerary their marriage had taken.
Mary, known for her stoic demeanor, showcases an unfamiliar side of vulnerability in the aftermath of John's decision.
Her act of maintaining a composed front falls apart as the reality of their ruptured relationship settles in.
The divorce proceedings drag on, marked by intense battles of negotiation and their shared struggle to keep their emotions under control.
From a one-time power couple, they now found themselves specifying terms for parting ways - a heartbreaking testament to their once shared dreams.
The potential scandal lurking ahead, threatening to further tarnish their reputations, leads the estranged couple to decide upon finalizing their divorce in an amicable manner.
They accept the path of mutual respect, putting their shared history at the forefront of their negotiation.
Acceptance finally sinks in for John and Mary as they grudgingly acknowledge the role of their career-centric choices in propelling their marriage towards its terminal end.
After a series of exhausting and emotionally taxing negotiations, the judgment arrives, presenting them with the bitter reality of their dissolved marriage.
The divorce, although having freed John from his failed marriage, left him with an unexpected loneliness.
His freedom came with an unforeseen cost - solitude amidst the bustling Manhattan crowd.
Armed with a reinvigorated spirit to rediscover himself, John broke away from his luxury penthouse located at the heart of Manhattan, moving towards a simpler lifestyle to foster personal growth.

His journey down the introspective path led him to understand the underlying truth of life: The real essence of living lies not in accumulating wealth and status, but nurturing love and fostering sincere emotional connections.
Gradually, his priorities shift.
Away from the relentless chase of wealth and influence, he focuses on cultivating deeper relationships with others and pursuing personal contentment.
This newfound perspective fuels his zeal for a more modest lifestyle.
Similarly, Mary embarks on her journey of self-discovery and personal growth within the confines of her penthouse overlooking Central Park.
She skillfully navigates through her journey, gradually detaching her identity from the societal image she had been upholding until now.
Mary seeks solace and companionship in her newfound interest in arts, attending painting classes, learning the intricacies of the piano, and focusing on her mental well-being.
Both John and Mary undergo a transformative phase, reshaping their lives to incorporate a healthier work-life balance, while striding on their separate paths.
Their journeys bring a renewed focus on their individual development, marking a stark deviation from their earlier quest for collective happiness.
Despite their independent lives, they maintain a sense of respect and understanding for each other, a remarkable testament to their emotional growth.

60722362.title: Made in Italy (2020 film)
synopsis: Jack Foster is getting divorced from his wife Ruth.
Her family is selling the art gallery where he works as a manager, which devastates him.
He decides to buy the gallery by selling the old Italian home he owns with his estranged father Robert, a famous artist.
The house belonged to Jack's mother and Robert's wife, an Italian woman who died in a car accident when he was young.
Jack takes Robert with him to Italy and tells him he needs the money to buy the gallery from Ruth's parents.
When they arrive, they find it is completely rundown.
Kate, an estate agent, comes to survey the home.
She tells them the house is in a bad condition, but if they fix the house, it could be worth more.
Jack tries to clean but then decides to sell the house as is.
Jack meets Natalia at her restaurant.
Robert looks at photos of his deceased wife and the whole house reminds him of her.
He decides to help Jack renovate the home.
Robert and Jack befriend some of the locals including Natalia and invite them to a party at the house.
She tells Jack that she has an eight-year-old daughter and is divorced.
As her husband lied about her, she only gets partial custody.
A buyer comes to look at the house but is not satisfied.
Kate tells Robert that the house needs more work, so he asks Natalia to help.
After Natalia and her daughter help with the renovations, Robert tells her that after his wife died, he sent Jack away to boarding school to keep him away from all the reminders of his mother.
Ever since she died, he could not drive or paint.
Kate comes over and sees the house almost fully done.
A couple arrives to look at the house, and decide they want to buy it.
Meanwhile, Jack tells Natalia about his impending divorce and how Ruth has taken everything from him, which she can relate to.
He tells her how he could not paint like his father but thought he could make the gallery a success, but his father never supported him.
Later, he enters his father's workspace and sees painting after painting of his mother, and of himself.
When Robert finds him, Jack wants to know why he locked away all his memories and his childhood.
Robert says he thought it was the fastest way to get him out of pain, and Jack screams at him that he never let him in and never talked to him.
He begins wrecking the space, and Robert holds him as they collapse onto the floor.
Later, they talk about her for the first time, sharing memories of her, and Robert begins crying, recounting what happened the day she died.
He was so wrapped up in painting that he let a young Jack walk to school.
He blames himself for her death as he kept on painting.
Jack hugs and comforts him, and tells him about his divorce from Ruth.
Robert is relieved to hear this news, and reveals that he was expecting it to happen.
The next day, at the house, the couple who decide to buy the house disrespect it and in response Robert tells them that he will not sell them the house, which angers Jack.
Robert admits he cannot give up the house, and Jack accuses him of never having any intention to sell, and returns to England.
Robert comes to see Jack, telling him he sold his London home and has enough to buy Jack out of his share of the Tuscany villa.
He urges him to buy the gallery back.
Jack asks him why he never came, and Robert says Ruth told him Jack did not want him to, that it was too much pressure.
Robert says he will live at the Italy home and host painting holidays.
Jack goes to the gallery, and when Ruth says she has changed her mind and will not sell the gallery, he instead presents her with the signed divorce papers.
In Italy, Robert leads a painting class where Kate is a student.
Jack arrives and tells Robert it was never about the money, and all he wants is his father.
He then meets with Natalia, who wants to know why he did not say goodbye.
He tells her that he saw her with Marzio, and she explains as he is the father of her child she has to maintain some relationship with him.
They decide to start over.
The film ends with Jack painting a wall with Robert.

27185118.title: Wed Me Not (2022 film)
synopsis: Hollywood’s celebrated star Jane Smith, renowned for her roles in box office hits such as "Golden Dreams" and "City of Shadows," finds herself standing at the peak of her illustrious career.
Despite her grandeur, Jane finds herself disillusioned by the concept of love.
Her past had been dotted with high-profile relationships with her equally famous co-stars, but their bitter conclusions had repeatedly left her nursing a sore heart and a sense of cynicism.
This longing for a touch of real love leads Jane to a charity event for underprivileged children in Los Angeles.
There she encountered Carlos, a dedicated teacher from a low-income community.
Carlos was a man indifferent to Jane's fame, a stark contrast from the men of her past.
His simplicity ignited an unforeseen attraction in Jane Smith, the Oscar-winning proverbial queen of Hollywood.
Their covert romance, intentionally shielded from the vultures circling the paparazzi skies, blossomed.
However, this idyllic quietude abruptly ended when a photo capturing their secret intimacy—hand in hand on Santa Monica Beach—got leaked, instantly becoming sensational news.
Carlos decided to distance himself from Jane and the impending onslaught.
Barely disguising her breaking heart, Jane watched as Carlos vanished in the glorious sunset of Los Angeles.
Bereft and on the verge of a public outroar over her private life, Jane sought refuge from Hollywood, decisively prioritizing her mental health.

Taking solace in a tranquil beach house in Malibu, Jane surrendered to the ebb and flow of her past relationships—each memory sparking a revelation that guided her towards understanding her romantic follies.
Jane welcomed a change, not just of her surroundings but also of her mindset.
As leaves turned hues around her, she immersed herself in mindfulness and therapeutic practices.
This transformative journey awakened a new definition of happiness in Jane.
A concept that had been subjectively distorted by her past, happiness now became a cozy feeling of comfort in her own company.
Now brimming with newfound strength, Jane decided to stride back under the dazzling Hollywood spotlight.
Her powerful public announcement of her decision to remain unmarried marked her comeback, sending a wave of shock and awe through Hollywood.
A groundbreaking press conference at the Beverly Hills Hotel had Jane challenge deeply ingrained societal expectations.
Jane’s unexpected courage baffled Hollywood.
Her transformation into an advocate for prioritizing individual happiness reverberated within the industry, forcing discussions about its archaic norms.
This milestone was inked forever into Jane’s life through an intricate henna tattoo on her forearm reading, 'Love Self First'—a symbol of her newfound commitment to herself.
Jane soon became Hollywood's sensation.
Not for her past movies or failed relationships, but for her single-handedly altering the narrative of her life and the unapologetic stance against entrenched stereotypes.
This intense attention did not sway Jane from her path, though.
She wielded her influential platform, steadfastly promoting self-fulfillment and mental well-being.
A year down this life-altering journey, fate reunited Jane with Carlos at the same charity event for underprivileged children where they first interacted.
Instead of the intense love that once defined their interactions, a mature resonance saturated their meet.
Carlos and Jane shared warm smiles as they remembered their shared past with a touch of nostalgia and acceptance.
Overwhelmed by her transformation, Carlos hesitatingly applauded Jane for embarking on such a brave journey of self-discovery.
His confession that he’d never been prouder of her traced the periphery of the closure Jane had been seeking.
With newfound confidence, Jane returned to Hollywood, her spark amplified.
Her affirmations radiated through screens worldwide.
Jane leveraged her fame to raise awareness about the importance of mental health and promote gender equality, her personal journey serving as the beacon of inspiration for millions.
Jane's leap towards self-growth proved as monumental as her filmography.
She had replaced the quest for love with the pursuit of self-love, putting her peace and happiness at the pinnacle of her priorities.
Bathed in the euphoric glow of self-satisfaction, Jane reveled in personal victories that fueled her relentless journey towards complete self-acceptance.
Jane continued carving a path for herself, leading a crusade for mental health awareness and gender equality.
Her story became a beacon of hope, inspiring others to seize their happiness.
Jane's evolution, from a love-jaded actress to a woman confidently controlling her narrative, left an unforgettable imprint on society and its perception of personal growth and self-validation.

61892187.title: Marry Me (2022 film)
synopsis: Superstar Kat Valdez is a long-known star of the Latin community who has had three failed high-profile marriages.
After "Marry Me", a song by Kat and her fiancé, Bastian, becomes a chart-topper across the world, they plan to hold their wedding ceremony in front of a streaming audience at one of Kat's concerts.
Charlie Gilbert, a divorced math teacher, is guilt-tripped into attending the concert with his friend Parker and his daughter, Lou, who has lately been less than enthused with her father.
Just as Kat prepares to go to the altar, a showbiz gossip website publishes video of Bastian's infidelity with her assistant Tyra.
Kat's manager shows her his phone, revealing the fast-spreading news to her.
In distress, Kat sees Charlie in the crowd holding Parker's sign reading "Marry Me"; to the surprise of the entire venue, she impulsively decides to do so.
Unsure, Charlie goes onstage and marries Kat in front of the world.
After the ceremony, Kat refuses to speak with Bastian or Tyra as she and Charlie leave.
The two are awkward and polite to each other before Kat goes home with a broken heart.

The following day, needing to respond to the frenzied media coverage and speculation about her mental state, Kat decides to stay married to Charlie for a few months to put a positive spin on the situation.
He reluctantly agrees, not wanting to cause a stir in either of their personal lives.
Charlie poses for media appearances, though he is uncomfortable with the scrutiny.
They eventually begin to grow close after spending time together away from the media and her management.
Kat meets Charlie's students and Lou.
Charlie eventually asks Kat to his school dance as a date, and she accepts.
That night they kiss and sleep together.
They spend the next few weeks together in a real romantic relationship.
Charlie prepares his math team for a mathalon with Kat's encouragement to the students.
She teaches Lou, who has stage fright, to dance to take her mind off her anxiety.
Bastian shows up to announce that "Marry Me" has been nominated for a Grammy, Kat's first nomination.
Charlie is wary of the fact that Kat and Bastian will have to perform together again, but Kat insists it is over between them.
However, Charlie becomes unsure that he can compare to Bastian and fit into Kat's world.
He breaks up with her, reasoning that their marriage was not real.
Kat writes a love song, "On My Way", that becomes more successful than "Marry Me".

While filming an appearance on The Tonight Show with Bastian, Kat realizes it is the night before the mathalon, where she promised to support Lou and Charlie; she corrects rumors, stating that she and Bastian are not back together and she did not write "On My Way" for Bastian but for Charlie, before abruptly departing the show to reunite with Charlie, who is helping Lou overcome her stage fright with the dance Kat taught her.
Kat holds up a sign asking Charlie to marry her again, to which Charlie agrees.
Kat, Charlie, and Lou become a happy family with their dog.
In the credits, a series of couples and their stories of how they met are shown.

73065741.title: Evelyn the Ant: The Dawn of Spring
synopsis: The film begins with enchanting, whimsical narration that introduces us to a bustling ant colony and its intricate ecosystem, ensconced within the intertwining roots of a mighty oak tree.
Amidst the seemingly labyrinthine corridors, overcrowded with diligent, industrious ants, we find our protagonist - an energetic young worker ant named Evelyn.
Out of all her kin, Evelyn is unique due to her insatiable curiosity and a fondness for exploration.
One day, the first warm breeze of springtime delicately wafts through the twig lined tunnels of the colony.
As Evelyn stirs from her slumber, she senses the shift in the season, bringing new hope and renewed vitality.
Joyful and excited, she hastens through the winding corridors of her subterranean home, keen to share the news of spring's imminent arrival with the rest of the colony.
Sensing her eager rush, Joe - another worker ant who harbours a secret fondness for Evelyn, takes notice.
Undeterred by their apathy, Evelyn decides to prove her claim and gather evidence of the season change.
Courageously, she decides to embark on a daring, unprecedented journey to the earth's surface.

Concerned for her safety, as well as spurred by his camaraderie and affections, Joe decides to accompany the eager Evelyn through the complex maze of root-laden catacombs leading to the world beyond their sheltered existence.
As they journey through unexplored parts, they stumble upon ancient murals and inscriptions on pebble walls, depicting ant lore that plays a significant role in predicting the arrival of spring.
Excited, they perceive this as a positive omen reaffirming Evelyn's belief in the changing season.
Inadvertently, they overhear a malevolent mole scheming to infiltrate their home colony to store his sizable springtime cache.
The threat to their home strangles their joy of exploration, replacing it with a pang of fear and anxiety.
As comprehension dawns on the brave ants, Evelyn and Joe realise that they are the only ones who can save their home.
The urgency of the situation is exacerbated by the fact that their kin and their colony are blissfully ignorant of the impending danger looming just around the corner.
Galvanized by their newfound responsibility, their return journey becomes a frantic race against time.
These trials serve to solidify their resolve to rescue their family, only strengthening their determination.
She utilises every lesson from her journey, every tidbit from the ant lore, as she devises a shrewd strategy to deter the approaching mole.
Armed with unwavering determination and razor-sharp intellect, she prepares for the urgent battle ahead.
Amid escalating tension, the valiant ant confronts her fears head-on, promoting courage and wit over sheer power to thwart the unfolding challenges.
Defying all odds, Evelyn teams up with Joe to outwit the mole using clever tactics and fast thinking.
Their ingenious ploys successfully thwart the mole invasion, averting an imminent disaster that would have threatened their existence.
Accepting Evelyn's warnings, which they once dismissed cavalierly, the ant colony rejoices in the afterglow of their successful defence.
They are awestruck by Evelyn's dedication, her act of lone bravery that preserved their home, showering her with praises and lauding her as their protectress - a heroine in the truest sense.
Her solitary joy becomes a collective celebration vibrating through every corner of their underground abode.
Evelyn, once a lone voice advocating for the acceptance of change, becomes the colony's guiding beacon towards spring preparations.
Throughout the course of the narrative, Evelyn metamorphoses from a curious worker ant into the colony's courageous protector.

Her adventurous exploration, comprehending the cryptic ant lore, outsmarting malevolent threats, and selflessly preserving the colony, all add layers to her courageous persona, making her no less than a legendary heroine.
Her immense bravery resonates with viewers across age groups.
Her story provokes a sense of awe and admiration, leaving an indelible mark in their hearts.
The film subtly engrains core values into the minds of its viewers, immortalizing lessons that were once indifferently overlooked, within their consciousness.
As the narrative weaves into its thrilling denouement, it fills viewers with a sense of fulfilment.
Leaving them yearning for more such ventures, it keeps their excitement ignited even in its conclusion.

As the tale of Evelyn and her bustling ant kingdom concludes, the audience exits the theatre with a warmed heart and a lesson etched in their minds; offering a fitting end to an enlightening subterranean adventure.

67306995.title: Maya the Bee: The Golden Orb
synopsis: Maya is full of the joys of spring as she tries to wake the hive and Willy to let them know that spring has finally arrived, but the others went back to sleep.
Maya and Willy went to the glow worms, but they took Maya and Willy up to wreck the hive and the precious sunstone, much to the displeasure of the Queen.

Maya overhears that she and Willy are to be separated because of their calamitous partnership and she needs no further invitation to get away from the hive ‘to do something special’ in order to prove her and Willy’s worth to stay together.
This opportunity comes in the unexpected guise of a passing green ant who is on the run from the muscle-bound beetle boom-bugs, who are after the golden orb he’s carrying.
The ant names him Chomp and hands the golden orb to Maya and Willy.
They meet up with Arnie and Barney to take the orb back to Bonsai Peak.
It turns out this golden orb is the egg of the ant princess whom she calls herself Smoosh, the heir to the ant kingdom.
Willy at first thought Smoosh is too squishy.
Maya holds Smoosh to greet him.
But Smoosh doesn't understand Maya’s name, until it lets out a fart to Willy as a gift.
Meanwhile at the hive, Crawley tries to fix the sunstone, but to no avail, much to his dismay.
Miss Cassandra calls out that Maya and Willy has left the meadow.
Smoosh begins to cry so Willy tries to sing in panic until they were frightened by the ants again, Willy doesn’t think they can keep going and decided to stop and rest.
Meanwhile, the hive is over the place trying to find Maya and Willy.
Arnie and Barney make something to cool them down, Maya sings Smoosh a lullaby while placing a diaper on her, It was too dark and Smoosh was afraid.
Willy sings a lullaby to her just like Maya did earlier, but feeling tired.
Chomp knows about Maya and Willy and follows Flip and Miss Cassandra to find Maya and Willy while Crawley stays behind.
Arnie and Barney complain about their hatred of spiky trees with Maya joining in until they found Loggy Hollow, but they were caught by the beetles again.
Maya and Willy found a wanted poster and Willy is ready to give up.
They argued until they saw Smoosh disappeared.
Maya throws a ball then grabs Smoosh and quickly flies away, she then found Willy, Arnie and Barney, until the beetles came back.
They quickly rode on a leaf to get away until Rumba is caught in the river and needs saving quickly.
Maya and Willy reconcile their arguments and decide to take Smoosh back to Greenleaf.
Until Bumbulus, Henchie, and Boof blocks their path and sends them to a dark cave where they can't escape.
Maya becomes crestfallen when she realizes that they have failed their mission until Miss Cassandra, Flip and Chomp arrive to rescue them.
Rumba make amends with Maya and Willy and they warn the ants of Greenleaf about Bumbulus' plan to dispose of Greenleaf and the only way to stop him is to sing a little song.
Then a bird arrives and the fight began.
Bumbulus was inside when Willy appeared.
When the sun finally rises, they join together into a huge spider in the shadow, scaring away the birds.
Afterwards, Maya and Willy reunite and Smoosh finally says Maya’s name.
Bumbulus apologizes for his selfishness and Bonsai Peak is saved, thus protecting it from further threats.
Maya and Willy are returned to the hive and the Queen congratulates them for their journey and decides to not separate them, and thus the spring festival finally now begins.

58220971.title: Imperial Thrones: A European Dynasty in the 1300s
synopsis: The film unfolds with a splendid, ornate coronification ceremony, where our central character Prince Adrian is crowned amidst jubilant applause and royal fanfare.

Despite the extravagant ceremony, Adrian wrestles with his new position, taking the throne in the wake of his beloved father, King Edward's, untimely death— a traumatic incident that had no forewarnings leaving him with little time for mental preparation.
Now a young and inexperienced ruler, Adrian grapples with court procedures and social protocol that seem as simblingly unreachable as a labyrinth.

His world takes an unexpected turn when Lord Hampstead, a dignified envoy from the frost-bitten Northern Kingdom, drops a gob-smacking revelation: Adrian's ingenious lineage makes him the legal heir to the North due to an ancient inheritance law.
Shocked and burdened by this sudden dual responsibility, Adrian is thrown into another whirlpool of pressure—now facing the challenge of ruling two diverse kingdoms at once.
With tensions escalating, Adrian's determination is put to the test.
He fights a grueling battle to uphold his reign over both Brindon and the Northern Kingdom, refusing to let the obstacles break his iron-willed resolve.
The plot thickens with the dramatic entrance of Pope Gregory, who in a lead-heavy strategical move, proclaims Adrian as the Holy Roman Emperor.

Suddenly, Adrian finds himself at the center of a political maelstrom, balancing the incessant demands of Brindon, the Northern Kingdom, and the Holy Roman Empire, facing hidden betrayals and rising rebellions at every juncture.
His reign is continuously put to the test with deadly assassination attempts, perpetrated by power-hungry nobles who wouldn't spare a thought before drawing blood.
Rebellions, uprisings and coup attempts start to bubble up in all his territories—the sinister outcomes of these power-craving nobles's malicious plans, casting an ominous shadow over Adrian's reign.
Amidst this spiraling chaos, Adrian's journey intertwines with Lady Elise of York, a noblewoman possessing a brilliant mind, gentle compassion, and surprisingly bold demeanor.
They find a haven in each other amidst the storm, their clandestine meetings acting as sweet respites from the raging responsibilities of their respective kingdoms.

As Adrian wades through his ever-expanding geopolitical responsibilities and palace intrigues, his fleeting yet tender moments with Elise become his sanctuary—a temporary respite from the kingdom's overwhelming demands.
A quaint love story begins to bloom between hurried whispers, secret letters and stolen glances, amidst the backdrop of the political upheaval—their romance, a rose among withered thorns.
Act three begins with thundering cries for rebellion, as disgruntled nobles from Adrian's dominion band together to hasten his downfall.
Thirsty for chaos and anarchy, these nobles trigger destructive wars, ripping apart the harmony and testing the resilience of Adrian's rule from its seams.
Despite facing odds of colossal magnitudes, Adrian begins to embrace his leadership role—not as the flamboyant prince he once was but as a sensible and astute king, zealous yet unruffled.

Displaying an intuitive knack for warfare, Adrian leads his troops with strategic precision, countering the spreading rebellion with superior military strategies that turn the tide in favor of his reign.
Adrian's decision to consult trusted allies for counsel, further depict his wisdom and the willingness to accept guidance from a league of loyal comrades—significantly fortifying his leadership.

Adrian's bid for ultimate victory doesn't stop there as he secretly instigates minor sabotages within the rebel camps, weaving an intricate web of strategic moves conceived to dismantle their treacherous schemes.
With Adrian at the frontline, his courageous leadership propels the armies into an epic battle against the united forces of the rebellious nobles.
His tactical brilliance and unyielding bravery become the beacon of hope for his loyal soldiers.
A gruesome battle unravels on screen, a dance of swords and searing flames.
Despite the storms of opposition, Adrian's forces gradually overcome the rebel onslaught—chanting a hard-fought victory for their determined monarch.
The rebellion, now effectively quelled, gives way to the once again titanic task of mending the torn seams of Adrian's kingdoms.

Act four rolls out, showcasing Adrian's adeptness at juggling his personal life and demanding political duties– highlighting his rapid maturation and his ability to deftly steer his kingdoms with a firm yet sensitive hand.
He negotiates peace treaties, catalyzes rebuilding practices, and keeps his subjects reassured of a tranquil, prosperous future.
Lady Elise stands by Adrian's side through it all—supportive, relentless, and ceaselessly loving.
Their intimate, evolving love story adds a refreshing contrast to the tensions of kingdom restoration.

Blending political strategy with personal elation, Adrian proposes to Elise, outlining plans for a grand ceremonial marriage that would serve as a beacon of unity and resilience for his recovering realms.
Through their marital bond, Elise and Adrian usher an era of harmony and peace in their realms.
Their combined leadership, characterized by strength, innovation, and understanding, echoes across their dominions.
While challenges continue to loom on the horizon, the royal couple tackles them with a shared resilience.
Adrian's journey culminates in their grand wedding, a fête symbolising renewal and hope amidst the vestiges of adversities.
The joyous celebration of their union fills the kingdom with jubilant hopes of an enthralling reign—one built on shared dreams, enduring love, and thriving hope.
United by a vision for peace and prosperity, they commit to a lifetime of mutual support, leadership and partnership—their eternal vows solidifying these promises.
Their royal wedding marks the beginning of Adrian's reign—a reign underpinned by strategic alliances, a love that promises a future, and a shared aspiration for peace and prosperity.
Adrian continues to secure the unity of his diverse territories, his reign a testament of strength and devotion, admired by citizens and statesmen alike.
Under Adrian and Elise's compassionate leadership, war-ravaged Europe converts into a golden age of prosperity.
The narrative draws towards its climax, their reign ushers an era of blissful peace and prosperity that envelopes Europe.
The narrative employs a time-leap in the conclusion, presenting an older, dignified Adrian, ruling over a culturally diverse and economically robust Europe.
This united Europe, basking in prosperity and progress, is a stark contrast to the turbulent land that existed at the commencement of Adrian's reign.
The narrative concludes by tracing Adrian transition from an unsure prince to a universally respected emperor.
Adrian's journey as a monarch is exquisitely portrayed—marked by unyielding courage, relentless determination, and a heart that remains warm and full of love in the face of grim trials.
The blossoming love affair between Adrian and Lady Elise captures aptly the idea of a beautiful lotus blooming amidst murky waters—symbolizing hope and resilience in the midst of adversity.
Moments of shared laughter and intimate whispers, scattered thoughtfully in between scenes of political crisis and maneuverings, underline the eternal bond of love they share amidst the turmoil.
The narrative leaves a lasting sense of triumph, underpinned by Adrian's exceptional growth as a character, and his acceptance of destiny marked by unflinching courage and strength.
The climax boosts the cinematic journey by providing a hopeful ending that underpins Adrian's phenomenal transformation into a universally beloved and respected Emperor.

53677315.title: Medieval (film)
synopsis: In the 14th century, Wenceslas IV from the House of Luxembourg is the king of Bohemia, King of Germany and Roman emperor at the same time.
Wenceslas has received the throne after his father Charles IV, but his reign is not as successful, and the kingdom seems to fall apart under his weak rule.
The country is actually ruled by Henry III of Rosenberg, the most powerful nobleman in the country.
The film follows Jan Žižka, a knight, mercenary, and future leader of the Hussite army who leads a mercenary group.
Žižka is tasked by Lord Boresh to kidnap Rosenberg's fiancée Katherine which would force Rosenberg to keep his word and help Wenceslas IV to be crowned the emperor of the Holy Roman Empire.

This gets Žižka involved with high politics and brings him into conflict not only with Rosenberg but also with Wenceslaus' brother King Sigismund who sends soldiers led by Žižka's mentor Torak to get Katherine back.
Torak and his men burn Žižka's home, kill his nephew and kidnap his brother Jaroslav to swap him for Katherine.
Torak sets up a trap but Žižka uses the help of local peasants and great tactics to defeat Torak's men despite being outnumbered.
Žižka and his men manage to escape with Jaroslav and Katherine.
They hide in a nearby cave but are ambushed by Torak and Žižka barely escapes losing his eye in a fight with Torak.
Katherine nurses him from his injury.
Torak is searching for Žižka while terrorizing local peasants.
His men eventually manage to kidnap Katherine who meanwhile had fallen in love with Žižka.
Katherine is taken to Rosenberg's castle while Žižka and his men find mortally wounded Boresh.
Boresh reveals that Sigismund kidnapped King Wenceslas.
As he dies he notes that the world can't be changed for the better if kings can do such things.
Žižka decides to save Katherine.
He and his men get into the castle and Žižka faces Torak.
Torak gets the upper hand but Katherine throws herself off the castle wall to the river to save Žižka.
Žižka jumps after her while pulling Torak with him.
He kills Torak while underwater and brings Katherine to the riverbank.
She gives him her ring after they kiss and she dies.
Žižka brings her body to his men.
An epilogue states that Sigismund became king of Bohemia after his brother's death but the people revolted against him.
Sigismund then orchestrated crusades to Bohemia while Žižka led outnumbered peasants.
The film ends during the Hussite Wars with Žižka leading a Hussite army in wagon fort facing a large army.
It is shown that he is still keeping Katherine's ring.

70884080.title: The Valiant Savior and the Metropolis of Liberation
synopsis: Our tale begins with Sarah, a young woman brimming with spirit, hidden away in the dusty, isolated desert town of Sierraleone.
Upending the monotony of her everyday life, she stumbles upon cryptic documents concealed deep in the confines of her basement.
These parchment papers unravel the history of an ancient kingdom—The Metropolis of Liberation, believed until then to be a mere legend.
Across the distant mountains in the land of Zephyria, tales of Sarah and her discovery spark the interest of Orion, known as the Valiant Savior.
He embarks on a quest driven by curiosity and a steadfast belief in Sarah's unearthed secrets.
Sensing the wealth and power potentially up for grabs, vile bandits lay siege on the peaceful town of Sierraleone, jeopardizing Sarah's existence.
Orion, the Valiant Savior, arrives just in time to thwart the marauders, saving Sarah from the imminent peril.
A profound kinship betwixt Sarah and Orion begins to bloom.
They pledge together to emancipate the enslaved citizens of the Metropolis.
Thus begins an arduous preparation period filled with exhaustive training, decoding of ancient documents, stockpiling of necessary supplies, and bracing for the inevitable dangers lurking ahead.
Their expedition, fraught with peril at every turn, tests their mettle against treacherous sandstorms, backstabbing allies, and intricately complex traps imposed by the city's ancient protectors.
The duo finally finds themselves standing before the mythical Metropolis, a city oppressed by a cruel dictator's rule.
The callous ruler, Emperor Zarkon, reveals a personal grudge against Orion, escalating their mission's stakes.
Dumbfounded, Sarah and Orion pull back to regroup and formulate a refined approach to their daunting task.
Together, they concoct a plan to dethrone the remorseless Emperor Zarkon.
Embracing her royal ancestry, Sarah unlocks latent powers, transforming into an indomitable force.
Simultaneously, Orion prepares strategically, relying on his vast combat experience.
The grand showdown begins as Orion goes toe-to-toe with the malicious Emperor Zarkon and Sarah stretches her newly-acquired powers to free the entrapped populace.
In this war of attrition, a newly empowered Sarah successfully liberates the oppressed citizens while an injured, yet determined Orion manages to subdue Emperor Zarkon's tyranny.
Vanquished and defeated, Emperor Zarkon is dethroned, thus bestowing the Metropolis's royal heirdom upon Sarah, its true and rightful queen.
The city rejoices, its streets brimming with happiness as Sarah's coronation unfolds, marking the dawn of a new era.
Orion, now hailed as the Metropolis's guardian, devotes his life to the city's defense.
Their extraordinary odyssey and thrilling adventure become the bed-time stories for generations to come, inspiring courage and bravery.
The Metropolis rises again, symbolizing liberation and endurance—a befitting tribute to the valorous deeds of Sarah and Orion.

58844569.title: Miss Fisher and the Crypt of Tears
synopsis: Phryne Fisher helps to rescue a young Bedouin girl called Shirin from imprisonment in 1920s Jerusalem.
While doing so she is suspected of having died.
Shirin is reunited with her uncle Sheikh Kahlil Abbas and they travel to Lofthouse Manor in England where a memorial is being held for Miss Fisher by her friends Lord and Lady Lofthouse.
DI Jack Robinson travels to England from Australia to attend the memorial and is just about to deliver her eulogy when Miss Fisher arrives in her biplane.
Shirin discusses with Miss Fisher about how she came to be in Jerusalem.
As a child, a sandstorm had wiped out her village and she was the only survivor, having been rescued by a mysterious stranger.
This stranger has now sent her a letter asking to meet at All Saints' Church at midnight.
Miss Fisher notices that the letter had already been opened so volunteers to attend the meeting on Shirin's behalf as it could be dangerous.
On her way to the meeting, she asks DI Robinson to accompany her to the meeting.
At the church, she approaches a British man called Wilson.
He is shot by an unknown assailant.
Before dying, he gives Miss Fisher an emerald amulet which he asks her to give to Shirin.

Miss Fisher and DI Robinson are arrested at the scene and the police reveal that Wilson was a felon who had deserted the British army with fellow soldier Captain Harry Templeton who has already been executed for desertion.
Miss Fisher and DI Robinson visit antiquities expert Professor Linnaeus, who explains that the amulet is engraved with the inscription "Crypt of Tears".

Linnaeus explains that legend says that during Alexander the Great's last campaign through Palestine, he suffered a horrible loss and was so bereaved that his very tears created a desert spring, really a tomb.
It is also said that Alexander placed a curse on the tomb where anyone who disturbs it, they and their loved ones will be cursed.
Linnaeus warns Phryne that the amulet is proof that the tomb has been disturbed, which has triggered the curse.
While there, the unknown assailant attempts to steal the amulet from DI Robinson who manages to fight them off.

The following morning, Miss Fisher sneaks into the Sheikh's bedroom at Lofthouse Manor where she discovers that the Sheikh had signed an agreement with Lord Lofthouse and businessman Vincent 'Monty' Montague involving the British Palestine Railways.

However, after learning from Shirin that it was British soldiers who murdered their family, Kahlil angrily breaks off the contract and loudly denounces the British during a party at Lofthouse's manor.
Later in the night, he is shot dead by the unknown assailant.
DI Robinson visits Captain Templeton's widow who gives him an astrolabe which had been owned by her husband.
He also learns that after Templeton's execution, and the supposed disturbance of the tomb, his at the time pregnant widow went into early labor despite there being no complications before then.
The baby didn't survive.
Miss Fisher finds a large emerald in a pot in the Sheikh's room which is verified by Professor Linnaeus as being linked to the amulet.
DI Robinson, Miss Fisher, Jonathon Lofthouse (the younger brother of Lord Lofthouse), and Shirin all travel to Negev and find a tomb in the desert using the astrolabe.
There they find an ancient corpse preserved in honey.
The body is that of Alexander's secret desert bride who died, leading to his grief.
Another corpse is found near the coffin, which had been stabbed by a dagger carrying Jonathon's insignia.
Jonathon reveals that he had accompanied Captain Templeton and Wilson to Shirin's village a decade ago in search of the jewels.
While Shirin's mother, the guardian of the tomb, showed them inside, Captain Templeton went mad and shot and murdered the villagers.
Shirin's mother upon hearing the gunshots, lashed out at Johnathon.
There was a struggle in which he accidentally killed her.
He returned with them so that he could return the jewels as he believes that he is cursed.
Miss Fisher therefore figures out that the unknown assailant is someone trying to protect Jonathon—whom she identifies as his real father, the Lofthouse's butler, Crippins.
He emerges from the shadow of the tomb and attempts to steal the jewels but is stopped by Jonathon who holds him hostage while the others escape from the collapsing tomb walls.
Miss Fisher tells Lord Lofthouse the truth about Jonathon and later says goodbye to Shirin.
After pretending to shoot a spider to appease Miss Fisher's fears, Jack has a heart-to-heart talk with Phryne about their relationship.
He tells her that he doesn't need to marry her, he just needs her heart and she declares she had already given it to him.
They spend the night together.
In a mid-credits scene, Phryne receives a letter announcing that her husband, whom she married to help him secure his kingdom (while he was in love with someone else), has been murdered.

25295009.title: Friday Night in Madrid
synopsis: As the narrative begins, we are introduced to Jordan in the midst of his New York apartment - a blink-and-you'll-miss-it studio in the heart of towering skyscrapers.

Worried yet excited, he hurriedly stuffs his worn-out suitcases, his belongings evidence of a man preparing for a consequential overseas work assignment - a gigantic skyscraper project to be erected in the sprawling expanse of Madrid.
Meanwhile, halfway around the world in Madrid, Emily, a struggling and yet unrecognized oil painter, is grappling with her latest streak of rejections.
Numerous high-profile art galleries in the bustling city, gatekeepers of artistic prestige, dismissed her captivating artwork, leaving her in a crushing wave of disappointment.
Meanwhile, Jordan gets his first intoxicating taste of Madrid.
He is quickly enraptured by the city's vibrant street life, its medieval architectural masterpieces, and lively public squares teeming with life.
The city captures his heart almost instantly, its raw, intoxicating charm in stark contrast to his steel and concrete home in New York.
One balmy Spanish evening, in a bustling tapas bar packed with chattering locals, fate pulls the strings, causing the lives of Jordan and Emily to intersect.
Their casual conversation evolves into a mutual affinity for avant-garde art and neoclassical architecture - a spark of unspoken resonance is ignited.
As their rapport deepens, a new tradition is spontaneously forged.
Every Friday, abandoning their solitary routines, Jordan and Emily plunge into the raw and authentic heart of Madrid's thriving art scene.
However, a harsh phone call from his pragmatic, New York-based engineering manager one day forces Jordan to confront the nearing end of his temporary Madridian life.
This presents him with an unnerving dilemma - to choose between his high-stakes skyscraper project in his homeland and the enchanting life he has woven together in Madrid.
Simultaneously, Emily receives an empowering invitation - a chance to present her artwork at Museo Reina Sofia, Madrid's preeminent contemporary art museum.
But, the haunting memories of past rejections still linger like stubborn stains, casting doubt over her decision to accept this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.
As both their worlds teeter on the brink of unsettling change, the narrative shifts to heartrending scenes of Jordan wrapping up at the buzzing construction site.
Simultaneously, Emily seen lost in a world of oil paints and blank canvases.
Their once shared experiences give way to solitary battles, each grappling with their struggles.
Despite their individual turmoil, they find ephemeral solace in each others' comforting presence.
Their shared moments of vulnerability offer them glimpses of a safe haven where they can lay their troubles bare and seek much-needed solace from one another.
However, calamity soon strikes when a sudden flaw in the skyscraper blueprints endangers Jordan's project at the work site, potentially delaying his project indefinitely.
Finally, the day of Emily's long-anticipated art exhibition at Museo Reina Sofia arrives, bringing with it a whirlwind of nerves and frenzied preparations.
Alas, on this momentous evening, Jordan finds himself shackled to the construction site, his imminent departure barred by the escalating crisis in the blueprint.
Heart heavy with regret, he resigns himself to his responsibilities at the site, apologetically dialing Emily's number only to regretfully inform her of his absence from her momentous night.
Emily, although disappointed, pulls up a brave smile.
She reassures him, pushing disappointment into the recesses of her heart and focuses all her energies into the impending public exhibition.

Following her tremendously successful event, Jordan views photos on social media of Emily's triumphant night and feels a profound pang of regret for not being there to witness her shine in her moment of deserved glory.
The realization grips him with tenacity - the monstrous skyscraper project back in New York is no match to the magnitude of missing vital life moments with Emily.
He begins questioning his priorities, his heart longing for Emily and the life he had started to love in Madrid.

Emily, despite the fresh waves of compliments and newfound respect from the art community, still feels a void, a gnawing incompleteness without Jordan – her confidant, best friend, and strongest cheerleader.
The following morning, defying a fierce inner battle, Jordan decides to confront his engineering manager about his decision.
He opts to resign from his role, choosing to extend his time in Spain.

Prioritizing his personal happiness, he chose the tranquility of his relationship with Emily and the beloved lifestyle he had stumbled upon in Madrid over any professional obligations back in his homeland.
On learning about Jordan's steadfast decision to stay in Madrid, Emily feels a taut thread of unease in her heart relax.
His sacrifice reassures her of his commitment, offering a comforting promise of a shared future with him.
On a star-studded Friday evening, Jordan and Emily reunite.
Their hearts echo with love as they walk into the rustic Tapas bar where their story had initially unfolded.
Their excited features, glowing under the soft lighting of the bar, hint towards a hopeful anticipation for the evening to come.
As they settle into the familiar rhythm of their Friday nights, an openhearted, earnest conversation begins to take shape.
Over shared glasses of Spanish wine, they pledge their undying love and unwavering support for one another.
Their expressions mirror a shared adoration, and just as it all started, their evening culminates in a dance.
As the pulsating flamenco music reverberates through the air, the couple dances with wild abandon, letting their movements tell their story, offering a visual testament to their love.
Their hands tightly intertwined, their destinies wrapped as closely together as their fingers.
They eagerly anticipate the chance to craft their unique love story on the magnificent canvas of Madrid with strokes of shared memories, trust, and relentless love.

63632818.title: Monday (2020 film)
synopsis: Meeting at a party in Athens, Mickey and Chloe instantly connect.
They wake up naked on the beach Saturday morning surrounded by families - and police, who take them downtown.
They are let go with a warning.
Chloe is leaving in two days because her toxic relationship ended, but must recover her purse from the party.
Mickey invites her to his DJ gig on an island, until he can get it.
They get to know one another, spending the day there.
By the night's end, Mickey asks Chloe to stay.
She refuses, so when her things arrive, they part awkwardly.
Argyris (Mickey's friend and business partner) realizes Mickey has fallen for Chloe, so they chase her to the airport.
The gesture works, and soon they move in together.
They fall in love… although they are polar opposites.
Mickey’s old bandmate tries to convince him to join her on the road.
Mickey seems tempted, but when he sees Chloe he decides against it.
Mickey and Argyris's freelance advertising jingle gig isn’t going well.
They placate their client in the living room, while Chloe meets with an immigration client in the dining room.
Chloe and Mickey plan a party for all their friends.
They’re meant to meet Aspa, his son's mother, beforehand but she ends up going alone, while he takes care of the party food.
Aspa tells Chloe Mickey is a terrible father who's never bothered with Hector.
When she returns home, he has not done as promised.
Upset, she then unhappily discovers she's pregnant.
Takeout arrives ahead of the guests.
Chloe is unimpressed, as Mickey had obviously forgotten.
It is a disaster as their friends clash.
Chloe and Mickey try to laugh about it afterwards however, it affects them.
A social worker informs them that Aspa has stipulated the visitation and guardianship must be shared between Chloe and Mickey, which troubles her more than Mickey.
Chloe secretly has an abortion, pretending to have the stomach flu, so puts him off when he wants to have sex.
Chloe's ex Christos intimidates them both at a wedding, so Mickey gets drunk and belligerent.
Argyris tries to stop him from sabotaging his relationship with Chloe, as she loves him.
Unfortunately, Mickey embarrasses Chloe by drunkenly, halfheartedly proposing.
At Christmastime, the Friday before Hector’s first visit, they argue because Chloe is nervous.
They joyfully learn a Greek song together to sing to Hector, then go out for one last carefree night before becoming responsible parents.
At a club they have tequila, and Chloe insists they do cocaine, then they get bounced.
Chloe encourages Mickey to pull over so they can have sex immediately.
She begins to cry and confesses to the abortion.
He is not upset, which angers her.
Their arguing alerts a security guard, so they must run.
Back at the motorcycle, remembering their first night together naked on the beach.
Chloe convinces Mickey to relive it.
They get on the cycle naked, then pull up next to a cop car at a red light.
Chased, Mickey wants to pull over, but Chloe insists he keep going.
Eventually they are cornered and stopped.
Mickey complies, but Chloe resists arrest.
Like before, they are arrested naked and in the back of a police car.
But now, Chloe is belligerent and assaults an officer, so they will not be treated so lightly.
Taken to the station and charged, the court date is on Monday, so they will miss Hector’s visit tomorrow.
Aghast, both beg to be let go until Monday, but to no avail.
They are separated, and Chloe spends the weekend sleeping in a cell.
On Monday, Chloe's attorney gives her clothes, telling her everything will be fine.
She's found guilty, but receives a suspended sentence and a fine.
Chloe then discovers Mickey's case was dismissed.
Returning home she confronts Mickey, there since Saturday.
Christos got him out and the charges dropped.
Chloe rages, but Mickey points out she is not innocent.
She cries quietly to herself.
In the last scene, Mickey and Chloe are waiting outside a school for the doors to open.
Small children come out and run into their parents' arms.
Our last view is of Mickey and Chloe's smiling, expectant faces.

73858173.title: Our Blood Ties in the Shadow
synopsis: Our protagonist is Alex, a dedicated and seemingly tireless nurse employed at the modest St. John's Hospital, who takes on double-shifts frequently as a means to barely scrape by and provide for his fragile family.

The axis of his world revolves around his frail younger brother, Matthew, whose incredibly rare medical condition and his constant need for healthcare have become ingrained in Alex's daily life, adding layers of complexity to his life’s struggle.
Despite being housebound due to an inexplicable allergy to sunlight, Matthew gallantly fights against the odds in face of the bewildering medical enigma encompassing his life.
Providing solid support to them is their resolute elder brother, Peter, trusted and respected by the township of Silver Oak for his role as the deputy sheriff.
Tirelessly, he ensures law and order, striving for harmony in their small community.
However, a constant internal conflict gnaws at him—a precarious balance between being an authority figure and his innate brotherly instinct propelling him to safeguard his family from jeopardy.
Amid the cheerful bustle of Silver Oak's annual harvest festival, hushed conversations circling the elusive Matthew's nocturnal lifestyle begins to stir up whispers and questions.

His peculiar condition and weather-resistant lifestyle evoke intrigue among the small-town folks, raising questions about the brothers' secretive comings and goings, and their tight-knit, quite secluded, existence.
As the narrative unfolds, a sudden and alarming downturn in Matthew's health sends their life into a whirlwind of disarray, marking the second chapter of their saga.
Out of sheer desperation to keep his brother from the brink of death, Alex resorts to the ethically questionable act of secretly siphoning blood supplies from his employer, St. John's Hospital.
Ironically, this act of compassion wedges a rift among the siblings, deepening Matthew’s anxieties about being discovered and causing a visible strain in their relationship.
Peter, utilizing his impeccable investigative skills, stumbles upon Alex's covert actions.
He finds himself battling his conscience on whether to hand his own brother to the law or to uphold family above duty.
The unexpected revelation ensues simmering discord between the two older brothers, leading to hushed arguments and awkwardly avoided confrontances.
Sensing the tension, Matthew retreats into his solace—painting.
Simultaneously, an alarming wave of thefts targeting blood banks across the neighboring towns further heightens the risk of their family secret getting unveiled.
The townsfolk, growing increasingly wary, begin to weave a web of suspicion that gradually unfurls towards the brothers' doorstep.
Bound by his deputy sheriff duty, Peter feels the heat to crack the case without letting the investigation's spotlight fall on his own household.
Amidst this storm, a dazzling ray of light and further complication simultaneously appears in the form of George Darnell, a renowned art curator from New York, vacationing in their town.

Stumbling upon one of Matthew's profoundly expressive paintings, Darnell finds himself enchanted and intrigued by the skill behind the imagery, placing Matthew under the demanding lens of art world limelight.
With budding fame, however, comes the relentless scrutiny of curious eyes, intensifying their already existing challenges.
Alex’s subterranean exploits at the hospital suddenly surface in the wake of Matthew's heightened notoriety.

The ever-looming confrontation between Peter and Alex eventually comes to a head, revealing the profound depth of their love for their little brother and the lengths they are willing to go to protect him.
Amidst their turbulent argument, a visibly weakened Matthew suddenly collapses, requiring immediate medical intervention.
This chain of events threatens to dismantle their meticulously devised facade of normality, making their exposure an imminent possibility.

As their world begins to crumble, Peter sees an opportunity to buy some time—shouldering the blame for an unrelated administrative error and submitting himself for court-marshall, successfully creating a smokescreen.
This bold sacrifice allows Alex a critical reprieve, a chance to search for an enduring solution to Matthew’s unique health dilemma.
Immersing himself in multiple medical journals, Alex starts to dig for groundbreaking treatments that could rewrite Matthew's cursed fate.

Eventually, Matthew's condition starts to stabilize, allowing the brothers to breathe a collective sigh of relief and paving the way for a sliver of hope to focus on maintaining their fragile guise of normality.
Seemingly against all odds, the brothers solidify their unity, vowing to safeguard their family at all costs despite the prying eyes and the relentless scrutiny of the public.
With Matthew’s situation somewhat under control, Peter embarks on a personal journey of redemption, aiming to wash off his tarnished reputation and regain his hard-earned position of deputy sheriff.
Seeing a ray of light, Alex continues his relentless pursuit, fueled by newfound hope to find a permanent solution to Matthew's condition.
Together, the brothers forge an uneasy alliance against the town’s wary inspection.
Matthew ventures into the moonlight, immortalizing this pivotal moment through his speculative brush-strokes.
Observing his transformation, the town's inhabitants start to appreciate the brothers' resilience in facing adversity.
They gradually dispel their suspicious whispers, welcoming Matthew back into the community and recognizing his inspiring spirit.
Finally, Peter manages to shake off the shackles of false blame and is reinstated into his rightful position as Silver Oak’s honorable deputy sheriff.
Meanwhile, Alex’s tireless efforts yield fruition when he stumbles upon a sustainable regimen that could potentially manage Matthew's condition without robbing him of normality.

St. John's Hospital, recognizing the desperate measures taken by Alex as acts born from the selfless love for his brother, decides to pardon him, paving the way for his return to his beloved nursing profession.
The art curator, Darnell, touched by Matt's deeply personal journey and captivated by his talent, arranges for a solo art exhibition in his honour at the buzzing heart of New York City.
Initially apprehensive, Matthew finally succumbs to the art-world's admiration, showcasing his journey through the vivid paintings, his visual diary documented in color and canvas.
As the dust settles, Alex and Peter, their secret safely buried and family bond stronger than ever, stand by Matthew's side, their hearts filled with a mixture of relief, pride and unspoken love.
After the magnificent exhibition, the brothers celebrate their survival, breeding dreams of breaking out from their past's cage, looking forward to a promising dawn of a new life.
The final scene unfurls with Matthew's strikingly beautiful moonlit painting as a backdrop, symbolizing their acceptance, courage and the unwavering resilience reflecting off their strengthened bond.

62990658.title: My Heart Can't Beat Unless You Tell It To
synopsis: Siblings Jessie and Dwight, care for their chronically ill younger brother, Thomas, who is unable to venture outdoors during the day and must regularly drink blood to survive.
Dwight and Jessie provide blood for Thomas by routinely murdering strangers, mainly homeless people and drifters.

Jessie works as a waitress in a local diner, while Dwight spends his days pawning items he finds around town or takes from victims, and visiting Pam, a prostitute whom he pays extra for a few minutes' conversation after their liaisons.
After a particularly grisly murder, Dwight begs Jessie to get real medical help for Thomas.
She refuses and instead orders Dwight to procure a new victim.
He lures a Spanish-speaking migrant named Eduardo into his car, but Eduardo escapes and wounds Dwight with a screwdriver when Dwight attempts to strangle him.
Dwight subdues Eduardo after a fight in the forest, but his desperate pleas for mercy convince Dwight to spare him.
He restrains Eduardo in a shed in the yard.
Angered when Dwight returns home without a blood source, Jessie kills Pam, leaving him distraught.
That night, Thomas complains of loneliness at the dinner table and implores Jessie to let him socialize with the local children he hears outside his window.
When she refuses, he overturns his bowl of blood, infuriating her.
Eduardo escapes the shed and attempts to kill Dwight, but he fights back and kills Eduardo as Thomas looks on.
The next day, in an attempt to make contact with the outside world, Thomas writes a note on a paper airplane and opens the front door to hurl it at a group of passing teenagers.
