PG returns the now powerless gem to Mimi, stating that after witnessing the family's affection for each other, he is now powered by love.
He will use that love to destroy the galaxy, but promises to spare the family.
The family bids farewell to PG and watches as he begins to destroy their town.
The news shows PG in giant form devastating the Earth, and in deep space the Planetary Alliance debates killing themselves before he can reach them.

48675850.title: Tropical Awakening (2020 film)
synopsis: Our tale takes off in the bustling hubbub of Wall Street, introducing our protagonist, Jack, a high-powered broker.
Exhaustion plays across his features as he finds himself buried under towering stacks of financial reports and intricate equity analysis documents in his disorderly office.
The ensuing conversation is an intense dispute over a $2 million financial discrepancy, further highlighting the relentless pressure he faces.
In this contrasting scene, we come across Jenna, Jack's girlfriend—a high-end criminal defense attorney.
Her face betrays her exhaustion as she steps out of the imposing Manhattan city courthouse after a grueling and drawn-out trial.
With his nerves frayed and intelligence challenged, Jack welcomes the end to his punishing day.
At his psychologist's office, he seeks the calming influence of his long-time therapist, Dr. Stanley.
The discussion takes a dive into Jack's persistent anxiety, which primarily stems from the unbearable pressure at work and its repercussions on his already strained relationship with Jenna.
Sensing the need for a drastic change, Dr. Stanley recommends a relaxed retreat.
Jack mulls over the advice and, on impulse, makes a reservation at the opulent Tropical Bliss Resort in the Maldives—a complete departure from his concrete jungle.
With both anticipation and apprehension, he surprises Jenna with two first-class tickets to the Maldives.
Soon, they swap their high-pressure New York-state-of-mind for the tranquility of an Emirates A380 soaring towards sunnier climates.
Jack's strategies to rekindle their dwindling romance suffer repeated setbacks, causing mounting frustration.
In his desperation, Jack turns to Marley, a local shaman known for his unconventional wisdom and unique take on life.
Marley, a kaleidoscope in his tie-dyed attire, guides Jack through quirky healing practices.
These never before imagined trials result in many amusing misadventures, providing much-needed comic relief.
Act three heralds a transformed Jack, now seen meditating under radiant waterfalls and carefully hugging spiny Maldivian cacti, all under the close scrutiny of Marley.
Drawing closer as they immerse themselves in the natural beauty of the island and adapt to the slower-paced lifestyle, Jack and Jenna start to see a flicker of hope for their relationship.
Act four introduces an unexpected hitch in their road to recovery.
An urgent call from Jenna's office disrupts their leisurely vacation.
An unexpected complication in her ongoing case requires her immediate attention in New York.
Their once-in-a-lifetime retreat is abruptly ended by Jenna's provocative decision, and tension fills the air between the couple.
Jack, who had just started to appreciate the slower pace of life, decides to stay behind.
Jenna departs, feeling misunderstood and fearing that Jack was downplaying the importance of her career.
Her departure creates a chasm between them, torching their once fiery relationship.
With nothing going as planned, Jack finds himself unwittingly signing up for the island's quirky annual event- The “King Mango” contest.
The surprising twist changes the trajectory of their tropical tryst.
Grasping the unexpected opportunity, Jack throws himself into the challenge, discovering novel aspects of island life and further distancing himself from his previous Wall Street image.
Jenna's timely arrival is rewarded with the sight of Jack, adorned in a traditional Maldivian sarong, being crowned the “King Mango”— a jubilant shock that is mirrored on both their faces.
Both physically and emotionally reunited in the warm embrace of the island, Jack and Jenna engage in a heartfelt conversation about the significance of work-life balance.
They make a pact to ensure a harmonious blend of their professional and personal lives in the future.

Surrounded by the multicultural island crowd, Jack, Jenna, Marley, the quirky toucan, and all the friendly islanders they've connected with on their journey commemorate Jack's unexpected victory and toast to their shared life-altering realizations.
This uplifting narrative concludes with an inspiring lesson; a commitment to prioritizing mental health, personal development, and casting away the burden of the fast-paced city life.

60289181.title: Palm Springs (2020 film)
synopsis: On November 9, in Palm Springs, Nyles wakes up and fails to consummate sex with his girlfriend Misty.
That evening, Nyles and Sarah bond at a wedding reception for Sarah's sister Tala and her fiancé Abe.
They leave the party to have sex in the nearby desert.
As he undresses, Nyles is shot with an arrow fired by an assailant.
Nyles, injured, crawls into a cave, warning Sarah not to follow him.
Concerned for Nyles, Sarah follows him and is sucked into a vortex.
Sarah wakes up and realizes that it is November 9 again.
She confronts Nyles, and he explains that by following him into the cave, Sarah has become stuck in a time loop with him; falling asleep or dying resets the loop, repeating November 9.
Sarah tries various methods to escape the loop, but is unsuccessful.
Nyles, having already been in the loop for a long time, has become complacent and carefree, abandoning hopes of escape.
Nyles and Sarah become close, and Sarah adopts Nyles' carefree and reckless lifestyle.
They both begin excitedly looking forward to their next adventures together.
Nyles reveals that the man who shot him, Roy, is from the wedding and that Nyles inadvertently trapped him in the time loop.
In revenge, Roy sometimes hunts Nyles, torturing or murdering him.
One night, Nyles and Sarah camp out in the desert, get high, and have sex.
The day after, Sarah sleeps in and is woken up by Abe, who she had sex with on November 8, the night before the wedding.
Guilt-ridden, Sarah refuses to talk to Nyles about their previous night, expressing nihilism about their life in the loop.
After being pulled over by Roy disguised as a cop, Sarah runs him over.
Sarah and Nyles argue, leading Nyles to admit that he had slept with Sarah many times in the loop, something he previously lied about.
An angry Sarah starts avoiding Nyles.
Nyles feels lost without Sarah and spends multiple days aimlessly moping, discovering Abe and Sarah's affair in the process.
One day, Nyles visits Roy at his home in Irvine and they reconcile.
Meanwhile, Sarah, resolved to escape the time loop, spends her days studying to become an expert in quantum physics and general relativity.
After some experimentation, she believes that exploding oneself in the cave will break the time loop.
Sarah offers Nyles a chance to escape with her, but he confesses his love for her and asks if they can stay in the loop together forever.
Sarah refuses, resolved to try her escape plan without him.
Sarah attends the wedding one last time, giving a heartfelt speech to her sister, the bride, and then travels to the cave with explosives.
Nyles, in a change of heart, rushes to the cave to leave with Sarah.
He admits that he would rather die with her in an explosion than remain in the loop alone.
Sarah reciprocates his feelings, and they kiss in the cave, as she presses the detonator.
It is revealed that her plan has worked, and that it is now November 10.
The two are relaxing in the pool of a nearby house, which Nyles showed Sarah during one of their loops, when the residents return and catch them in the pool.
In a mid-credits scene, Roy, having gotten a voicemail from Sarah explaining her plan to escape the loop, returns to the wedding and asks Nyles if the plan would work.
A confused Nyles does not recognize Roy.
Roy smiles, realizing that Nyles is out of the loop and Sarah's escape plan works.

68281313.title: Sundresses and Seashells (film)
synopsis: For Sarah, the anticipation of summer’s freedom courses through her veins vividly, making her indulge in a whimsical idea.
What better way to enjoy the balmy season than to invite her quirky and adventurous childhood friend, Emily, to bask in the liberating sunlight at her sprawling Cape Cod-themed beach house in Malibu!

With a picturesque setting and idealistic mood, Sarah and Emily concoct a dream of their perfect summer equation: rejuvenating sunrise swims in the sparkling ocean, soul-soothing sunsets painting the sky in hues of coral and crimson, and time seemingly frozen on comfortable sunbeds gracing the long stretch of sandy shores.
The girls first encounter with the beach house leaves them enchanted.
Captivated by the breathtaking sight of the ceaseless Pacific Ocean reflected in the wide expanse of panoramic French windows, they are drawn into the heart of tranquility.
And so commence their idyllic, sun-splattered days.

The holiday comprises of excessive sun-soaking on the house's exclusive beach, indulging in coastal delicacies during beach picnics, and delighted exploration of the enchanting corners of Malibu town.
As Sarah immerses herself in these golden sunny days, she finds herself irresistibly drawn towards Adam - a charismatic local surfer, who's piercing blue eyes are as captivating as the ocean itself.
Amid the crackling beachside bonfires under the velvet blanket of stars, Sarah and Adam’s friendship unknowingly begins to tread on the path of budding romance.
Emily, however, always the practical one, casts a wary eye at the escalating summer romance.
She advises Sarah against nurturing any deeper feelings for Adam, reminding her of the ephemeral nature of their vacation.
But driven by the compelling force of her blooming love for Adam, Sarah chooses to set Emily's cautionary words adrift and surrenders herself to this blossoming romance.
But as Sarah indulges in her newfound love with Adam, Emily faces a whirlwind of emotions, coming face to face with a startling revelation - she's fallen in love with Sarah.
Struggling with a myriad of emotions, Emily gathers her resolve and, against the stunning backdrop of a moonlit shoreline, reveals her deep affections to Sarah.
The confession hits Sarah like a tidal wave, sweeping her off balance as she attempts to grapple with her burgeoning emotions for Emily, all while maintaining her mercurial romantic ties with Adam.
The unexpected turn of events sends Sarah spiraling into a sea of emotional turmoil.
She is dumbfounded, unsure about which course to take.
During a tranquil morning stroll by the beach, Sarah's eyes alight upon a perfectly-shaped conch seashell, washed ashore.
Its graceful complexity, bathing in the morning glow, is a stark symbol, urging her to introspect and evaluate her tangled relationships.

After spending hours under the cool shade of their beachfront palm tree, Sarah decides to prioritize her childhood friendship over an uncertain summer romance, leading her to break off her relationship with Adam.
The news of their breakup shatters Adam's heart, causing visible turmoil amidst the carefree local surfer's community, marring their rosy existence.
Concurrently, Emily finds herself in the midst of a fierce internal battle, juggling her newfound self-identity and her fear of a shattered platonic bond with Sarah.
The complex emotions, coupled with fear of rejection, push Emily to hastily buy a ticket for an early flight back to their bustling hometown, New York.
Wracked with pain and fear, Emily begins packing her well-worn, vintage suitcase, not bearing to inform Sarah of her impending departure.
The daunting prospect of losing their once-unbreakable friendship has Emily tormented, her tears staining the cloth of her hastily-packed belongings.
The sight of Emily, overwhelmed, and packing an absurd amount of clothes, triggers a protective instinct in Sarah, who decides to reciprocate Emily’s earlier candidness.
With Emily at the brink of boarding her early morning flight from LAX, an unexpected farewell awaits her.
Sarah, with a determined expression, surprises her friend at the terminal.
Mustering all her courage, with the bustling airport as their witness, Sarah reveals her dormant feelings for Emily.
Amid the rush of travelers, the sudden revelation of deep-seated emotions makes the busy terminal a stage for a heartfelt confrontation between the two best friends.
In the heart of the bustling airport, the two friends find themselves at an emotional crossroads, their destinies hanging in the balance.
Overwhelmed, Emily is doused in an intermingling sense of fear and relief at Sarah’s confession, her heartbeat resonating in her ears.
Sarah, amidst her own turmoil, assures Emily of the solidity of their friendship, appealing to her with a plea to reconsider her impulsive departure.
Amid teary gazes and heartfelt confessions, Sarah and Emily decide to put the romantic possibilities on hold to prioritize their enduring friendship.
They vow to explore the depth and possibility of their love when the time is right while assuring to prioritise their time-tested camaraderie before any potential romantic complications.

69704561.title: Palm Trees and Power Lines (film)
synopsis: Lea is a 17-year-old girl spending the last few weeks of her summer hanging out with her best friend Amber.
She lives in suburban Southern California with her emotionally absent single mother, Sandra.
Lea's father is not present in her life and lives in Arizona with his new family.
Lea and Amber hang out with boys their age, and Lea has a casual relationship with one of them, Jared.
However, Jared only values Lea for sex and their hookups are not satisfying for her.
One night, as the group of friends eat at a diner, Lea makes eye contact with an older guy sitting at another table who winks at her on his way out.
Lea's friends run out on the bill, but Lea is left behind when she hesitates to follow them.
When she does try running out, a cook accosts her, but the same man from earlier intervenes and Lea is able to get away.
As she walks home, the older man drives his truck alongside her and coaxes her into getting in and giving her a ride home.
He introduces himself as Tom and tells Lea he is 34 years old, while Lea shares her age.
Before she departs, he adds his mobile number into her cell phone.
Lea is charmed by Tom and confides to Amber that she has met someone, but doesn't disclose the details and says the guy is a boy at another school.
Lea's relationship with her mom becomes further strained when she welcomes an ex-boyfriend back into their house.
Lea turns to Tom for attention and validation, and he acts sympathetically to her problems, telling her that he too does not have a close relationship with his parents.
When Lea asks Tom what he does for a living, he vaguely responds that he runs his own small business doing home repairs and remodeling, a job that grants him complete freedom.
Lea soon enters into a romantic relationship with Tom.
When she agrees to spend the night with him, he takes her to a motel, reasoning he is temporarily staying there until he finds a new place.
Lea senses something is wrong when Tom must leave the room to attend to a domestic dispute upstairs, but he insists to Lea that he was just helping out a female neighbor with her drunk boyfriend.
On a day out with Tom at the beach, Lea is spotted by a friend from school, and Tom introduces himself to her.
Word gets back to Amber, and Lea makes her promise not to tell anyone about their relationship.
Tom also asks Lea not to see other guys, telling her affectionately, "You're mine".
Lea appreciates feeling wanted and desired.
Lea and Tom are at a restaurant one day and the waitress suspects Lea is in a coercive relationship.
When Tom steps outside to take a phone call, the waitress covertly tells Lea that if she needs to get away, she can help her.
Confused and unaware that she is being groomed by Tom, Lea asks why she would need help, and the waitress mentions that Tom frequents the eatery with other young girls.
When Tom returns, he can sense Lea's unease and gets her to talk about what's troubling her.
When she confesses the waitress said she's seen him before with other girls, he plays it off and claims she must have him mistaken with someone else.
Later, while Lea is out drinking and smoking with friends, Jared mockingly jokes she has been seen "hanging out with the geriatric".
Lea, angry that Amber is the one who told Jared, storms off and shows up distraught at Tom's motel room.
Tom comforts Lea by telling her he loves her and reassuring her that her friends and family's opinions don't matter.
He also gifts her a bracelet inscribed with an inside joke they share.
When he asks if she wants to go on a vacation with him, Lea agrees without hesitation and the two head to a hotel.
On their second night at the hotel, Tom sits Lea down and asks her if she can do something for him.
He says she needs to sleep with another man for money, and if she loves him she'll do it for him.
Having coerced her into prostitution, he leaves her with a middle-aged man.
The unnamed man coaxes a reluctant Lea into oral and vaginal sex.
While the man is in the shower, an emotional Lea packs her things and leaves the room, but Tom catches her in an embrace before she can leave the hotel.
Tom takes her to get food at a restaurant, and Lea uses an excuse to go to the restroom as an opportunity to leave, walking to a nearby gas station by herself.
She tearfully calls Amber to come pick her up, and when she arrives the two reconcile.
At home, Lea makes an effort to spend more time with her mother and returns to her usual activities with Amber.
After Amber compliments Lea's bracelet, she feels compelled to try and phone Tom several times, but his mobile number is disconnected.
She goes to the motel and knocks on his door, but it goes unanswered.
She inquires about Tom's whereabouts from an upstairs tenant she had seen Tom helping out before, and the girl reluctantly dials his number and puts her through to Tom.
Lea sobs into the phone and asks why Tom abandoned her.
The film ends with Lea's affirmations of her feelings for Tom and she smiles hearing him reciprocate his love for her.

72246852.title: Radio Rascals: Echoes from the Countryside
synopsis: The opening scene of the film treats the viewer to a passel of aged newspaper clippings and jumpy b&w footage depicting the Radio Rascals during their heyday in the 1990s.
The film then backpedals through the trio's timeline, embroiling the audience in their downfall from grace.
We are introduced to our lead, Kinetic K, once a gear-turning part of the music machine, now relegated to the uneventful life of postal delivery in Marleyville, his hometown.
DJ Cosmic, another vital cog of the Radio Rascals, now leads a solitary existence in a cramped apartment in NYC.
Meanwhile, the band’s manager, Slick Jump, also a key character, has retreated into an obscure corner of the Texas countryside, completely cut off from the world that once idolized them.
A chance reunion takes place at Kinetic K’s childhood home, where they stumble upon a floundering local radio station, WRR 101.9.
Kinetic K, rebranding himself as ‘Mailman’, takes to his new dual role with gusto; delivering mail while collecting local anecdotes, vibrant tales ultimately serving as the soul of their radio shows.

DJ Cosmic, in an effort to tune into the rustic musical landscape of Marleyville, immerses himself in the local music scene, joining a country music club and soaking in the rich cadences of bluegrass and country rock.
The former manager, Slick Jump, leverages social media to rekindle the flame of Radio Rascals.
Armored with new tales, the sound of emerging musical genres, and clever digital marketing, they breathe new life into WRR 101.9.

Meanwhile, a rival radio station, NYC Live, sensing a threat to their monopoly, plots to torpedo the Radio Rascals’ comeback ambitions by spreading damaging rumors of their return to scandalous lifestyle.
With a threatening possibility of their comeback crumbling, the stakes rise sharply for the Radio Rascals, pushing them onto thin ice.
Jolted by the adversity, the trio quickly pivot their strategy — they realise that to truly resonate with the Marleyville audience, they must adapt their content.

Kinetic K, showcasing his old ingenuity, starts delivering smooth verses anchored on local events like cattle auctions and potluck suppers, shaping the snoozy rural life into punchy, relatable comedy that begins to gain traction.
DJ Cosmic explores new musical territory, mixing the pulsating city pop with the heart-rending ballads of country rock.
The result — a new, unique sound, a musical melting pot that resonates with the rural society.
The trio orchestrates a grand relaunch, hosting a dynamic, live radio show designed to blend their reformed, edgy urban persona with rural charm.
The skeptical Marleyville audience approaches the extravaganza with apprehension.
Techniques relying on authenticity, humility, and empathy strike an ideal chord with the locals.

Turning out to be a game-changer, Edna, a ardent Marleyville listener, exposes NYC Live's disruptive tactics during a live broadcast — an unexpected twist that solidly goes in favor of the Radio Rascals.
Edna’s revelations end up turning the tides as locals rally behind the now sympathetic Radio Rascals, victims of a bitter sabotage.
Bolstered by this unexpected momentum, the trio manages to bridge the cultural gap between the skyscrapers of New York City and the expansive farmland of Marleyville.
They reestablish not just their stature but also reimagine the norms of rural radio broadcasting along the way.

The town echoes with joyous laughter, heartwarming country music, and the bright bursts of celebratory fireworks as Marleyville braces to embrace the unique blend of city glamour and rustic simplicity.

In the closing scene, the Radio Rascals stand atop a hill overlooking the seemingly endless spread of Marleyville’s verdant fields, a potent symbol of their newfound love and acceptance for their rural life.
The film wraps up on an optimistic note, with the trio accepting their quiet lives and their commitment to the slow-paced simplicity of Marleyville.
Their journey, richly told, serves as a testament to adaptability, the embrace of an abrupt change and subsequent transformation.
The once sceptical citizens of Marleyville evolve, becoming an integral part of their journey, standing as avid followers advocating for their favorite radio show.
Despite initial culture clashes, stubborn opposition, and scandalous obstacles, the Radio Rascals dance past their adversities and regain their former glory in an unforeseen setting.

The narrative concludes with the camera sweeping over the serene Marleyville countryside, over rolling hills and tranquil rivers, where the former city celebrities, the Radio Rascals, have now found a humble and inspiring new home.

62452934.title: People Just Do Nothing: Big in Japan
synopsis: Three years after the final transmission of Kurupt FM and the crew moving to Essex (series 5 of People Just Do Nothing), Anthony "MC Grindah" Zografos works as a postman, Kevin "DJ Beats" Bates works in a bowling alley, and Steven "Steves" Green is still based in the Brentford flats.
However, their dead-end lives are changed when Chabud "Chabuddy G" Gul announces the news that their song, "Heart Monitor Riddem", has found phenomenal success in Japan on a popular game show.
Furthermore, the company responsible for the show wishes to invite them to Japan for a record deal.
With this in mind, the crew reconcile and travel to Japan.
Miche, Grindah's wife, later joins the crew after obtaining a ticket.
In Japan, the Kurupt FM crew are assigned a manager, Taka, and a translator, Miki.
The introduction of Taka proves antagonistic for Chabuddy, who notices Taka trying to replace him as their manager, which is further proved when he is ejected from a club.
With Steves' eccentric behaviour and Miki acting as a weed dealer for him, the two become very close.
While in Tokyo, the company plans Kurupt FM's debut to the Japanese audience, with a concert featuring them planned within a week of them arriving and a record deal.
However, the exact terms and conditions regarding their deal are unknown, as Chabuddy deleted the email regarding the small print.
The Kurupt FM crew's first day in action proves disappointing.

Instead of visiting a recording studio as they anticipated, the crew are led to a dance studio to perform a dance commonly featured on the game show, associated with their song, much to their chagrin.
After being covertly manipulated by Taka, Grindah insists to the crew that the dances are necessary and are needed for their success in Japan.

Later on, the crew go for a photo shoot in their outfits for the concert, and it becomes clear that Taka is publicising Grindah as more important than the rest of the members, prompting an argument within the crew.
During dinner with Miche and Taka, a jealous Chabuddy breaks in and berates Grindah for choosing Taka over him, offering Grindah an ultimatum between him or Taka.
Grindah refuses to acknowledge the situation, leaving Chabuddy defeated.
The feud between Beats and Grindah comes to a climax when they are expected to appear on the game show under their new stage name "Bang Boys".
Shortly before the show, Beats lambasts Grindah for not sticking to their garage roots and accuses him of selling out.
This results in a scuffle between Beats and Grindah, leaving the latter in tears and the rest of the crew abandoning him.
Grindah appears solo on the game show, feeling humiliated as he watches himself fail on the obstacle courses and later on with a disastrous recording session with a J-pop artist.
Meanwhile, Steves has become attracted to Miki but struggles to express his feelings for her.
A drunk Chabuddy buys rounds for Japanese salarymen, thinking he is spending Taka's money, until he discovers from Yuta the barman that Taka's tab has been closed.
Having spent several hundred pounds on drinks, Chabuddy flees from the hotel to avoid paying and is left homeless.
The day of the concert arrives, and only Grindah is there to perform.
His nervousness from not having his former crew around and him realising that he has led himself astray from his roots leads him to lock himself in the bathroom.
When Chabuddy G arrives after tracking a Bang Boys van to the concert, Grindah has fled.
When the Bang Boys' turn on stage arrives, Chabuddy and Miki convince Taka's managers that he knows the dance routine and promptly leave.
What is left of Kurupt FM crew are sulking in a karaoke bar.
Suddenly, Grindah enters and reaffirms his friendship with Beats, saying it is the "best thing to happen" to him.
The rest of the gang arrive and do an emotional karaoke performance to "Heart Monitor Riddem", whilst Taka embarrasses himself at the concert.
During the credits, Kurupt FM is set to release their first album, Miche is looking to publish a book, and Steves and Miki become domestic partners.
However, it is unknown how Steves will return to England.

17938868.title: Frozen Contact (1987 film)
synopsis: In the remote expanses of Siberia, bordered by a blanket of snow and defined by its unforgiving ice-cold winds, a strange night falls under an eternal winter twilight.
Beneath this icy veil, amidst the echoing silence, a resilient middle-aged miner named Paul endures in the diamond mines.
Day in and day out, Paul navigates the perils of his profession while isolated within Siberia's vast wilderness.
One such night, illuminated by the faint glow of an old lantern and punctuated by the rhythmic clanging of his pickaxe against the hardened rocks, Paul encounters an unfathomable phenomenon.

Unseen energies disrupt the comfortable darkness of his toil; lights of eerie, iridescent hues flash in the mine's abyss, followed by whispers in an unknown language and shadows dancing like phantoms.
Suddenly seized by a pull stronger than gravity, Paul's feet leave the frozen ground, and he is whisked away into the unknown, leaving behind his familiar world.

Mute with disbelief, his loyal companion, Ivan, can only gaze helplessly from his hiding place behind a snow-covered dune as Paul vanishes into the mine's eerie glow, triggering a dread-filled silence.
When consciousness returns to Paul, he finds himself inside an alien spacecraft, replete with intricate machinery and strange lifeforms whose existence extends far beyond human comprehension.
These beings, their biological constitution as bizarre to Paul as their home—a dying star system millions of light-years away, find themselves locked in a battle for survival.
Their existence teeters on the edge, held back only by an exceedingly rare mineral found exclusively in Siberia's tundra.
Overwhelmed by their desperate plea yet moved by their yearning to survive, Paul volunteers to mine the crucial mineral despite being light-years away from Earth.
Meanwhile, on Earth, a panic-stricken Ivan spills tales of the incident to the local authorities.
Words spread, concern escalates, and soon, the world is thrown into conniptions over the disappearance of Paul.
Isolated in the cosmos, in an environment that is as bizarre as it is fascinating, Paul commits himself to the task of securing the mysterious mineral from alien terrains.
His sole companion in this quest is Zya, an alien linguistics expert, whose mission is to decipher and communicate alien utterances, thereby acting as a bridge between Paul and the alien crew.
Through shared meals and deciphering cryptic alien commands, Zya introduces Paul to their customs while absorbing nuances of human behavior and values.
These profound interactions nevertheless foster empathy and camaraderie, illuminating that bonds can thrive even in the unlikeliest of places—millions of miles away from home.

Amidst the unclear skies, on their isolated blue dot, human authorities rally together, devising an audacious plan to bring Paul back from the clutches of what they fear might be a hostile alien invasion.
Unaware of the unfolding chaos on his home planet, Paul, with steadfast assistance from Zya, finally uncovers the crucial mineral, shining with an unearthly glow.

However, their mining operation triggers a seismic event that streams across the vast cosmos, reaching the advanced monitoring systems on Earth, alerting the authorities about an unidentified spacecraft in the Earth's atmosphere.
As the spacecraft discreetly hovers near Earth's stratosphere, apprehension mounts among Earth's defense forces, creating an air of potential conflict.
Alarmed by these developments, Paul and Zya scramble to formulate a peaceful resolution, an assurance to the apprehensive terrestrial forces.
They manage to broadcast a carefully constructed message, asserting their peaceful intent, Paul's safety, and a promise not to harm Earth.
This unexpected communique relieves the anxiety on Earth, with the authorities allowing the alien spaceship to land safely.
Landing marks a tearful reunion for Paul and his companions on Earth, a tumultuous blend of relief and disbelief.
Simultaneously, the aliens, having acquired the rare mineral necessary for their survival, prepare for their long journey back to their dying star system.
The heartfelt farewell between Paul and Zya embodies the first peaceful interaction between humans and extraterrestrials, serving as a beacon of hope for future cosmic relations.
Life resumes for Paul, but his everyday routine is no longer mundane - a changed man after an extraordinary interstellar journey.
Gazing dreamily at the starlit sky as he labors in the frozen mine, everyday experiences remind him of his cosmic adventure, with his bond with the aliens being a constant reminder of his journey.
The narrative concludes with Paul standing in the vast expanse, his gaze lost amongst the stars where his newfound friends embarked for.
Paul's incredible journey demonstrates the power of unity in the face of impending extinction, leading to the formation of unusual bonds.
High-stakes encounters and tense dilemmas bring to light how individuals can rise above all odds when faced with possible annihilation.
From a baffling beginning to a progression towards a resonant conclusion, the story draws a compelling narrative arc.
The narrative skillfully connects vastly different worlds and uncovers the potential of empathy, understanding, and unity in the limitless cosmos.
As an epilogue, Paul's enduring connection with his extraterrestrial friends and the distant stars leaves a touching remnant of his journey.

67008472.title: Proximity (2020 film)
synopsis: In 1979, Carl, a Lumberjack working in Alaska, is abducted by aliens.
In the present day, a computer engineer named Isaac starts a video diary.
After a hike in the woods, he encounters a flying saucer and encounters an alien.
Three days later he wakes up near the water.
He discovers that he is having hallucinations.
He visits the doctor and discovers his bone broken with a precise cut.
He got the abduction on camera and uploads it to the internet, and it goes viral.
The news, media, and government question Isaac.
Isaac realizes mysterious signs of alien life throughout history prove that aliens exist.
He finds a post on the internet by a girl his age named Sara that includes a similar story.
The two meet at a local diner.
Isaac is asked to do a lie detector test for proof of the abduction and he passes it, leading to him being apprehended by men in black run by Agent Graves.
The government discovers that Sara and Isaac have an alien tracker in their arms and Isaac refuses to cooperate in the government's procedure.
Isaac escapes with Sara and they're chased by androids.
They realize that they have been taken to Costa Rica and find a hacker named Zed who helps them and admits that he knows about the United Nations agency behind the kidnapping.
Zed helps them locate an elderly Carl, and they Video Chat with him.
The group discovers that the aliens will come to British Columbia in five days.
Zed, Sara, and Isaac travel to British Columbia and find Carl living in a cabin.
Carl disables the United Nations trackers, allowing them to stay with him for the next two days.
In two days, the aliens arrive and explain that they are studying humans, believing that Jesus Christ is important to the creation of the universe.
They remove Sara's tracker as the men in black surround the cabin.
Agent Graves demands an answer about his father's death from Carl, who refuses and is shot by laser guns.
Sara walks out of the cabin and is shot as well.
The aliens remove Isaac's tracker and he unleashes telekinetic and chronokinetic powers which he uses to escape by saving Zed and carrying Sara and Carl to safety as the cabin is destroyed.
The aliens save Sara and Carl and the group escapes in a flying saucer.
Six months later, Isaac and Sara are living a normal life in Costa Rica.
Zed and Carl are running a new science program and Agent Graves has been fired.

46699511.title: Gilded Salvation (2022 film)
synopsis: In the mining town known as Double-Dice, we meet our heroine, Seraph, a waitress maneuvering through life amidst miners and their brawls.
Raised as the daughter of a deceased miner, Seraph's past is filled with tales of struggle.
She serves whiskey to the miners to scratch out a living in this harsh town.
One night, an enigmatic stranger named Everett walks into the tavern.
Everett's past is a mystery, adding to his allure.
Seraph serves him a drink and strikes up a conversation.
Everett, dreaming of escaping the mining cycle, and Seraph with her wisdom developed from hard-fought survival, display a stark contrast between their characters.
Everett works tirelessly in his mining claims, driven by a dream of a richer life beyond Double-Dice.
His evenings are spent in the comforting company of Seraph, developing a bond over shared dreams of a life beyond their present circumstances.
A dispute over mining claims involving Everett and Seraph's past with Byrne, the owner of the local brothel, threaten their growing bond.
The townsfolk ensnare their relationship further with their scorn and speculation.
However, things abruptly change when Everett strikes gold in his claim, sending them from a struggle to survive to suddenly wealthy.
This stirs up the greed of their fellow miners.
In the face of adversity, Everett and Seraph's love for each other grows.
They plan an escape from Double-Dice, dreaming of a life far from the mining town.
Utilizing the distraction of the town over Everett's gold, they gamble their way into acquiring a ship called the 'Golden Sunrise' for their escape.
However, the town retaliates violently to their departure, causing a gunfight.
In the face of danger, they board their ship and leave Double-Dice.
Stories of their daring escape echo around the town, becoming legend among the miners.
The story ends with Seraph and Everett living out their dreams by the sea, far from Double-Dice.

64454495.title: Redeeming Love (2022 film)
synopsis: During the California Gold Rush, a beautiful young woman called Angel works as a prostitute in the fictional town of Pair-a-Dice.
Despite being the object of desire for the local men, she survives through hatred and self-loathing.
Meanwhile, a visiting farmer named Michael Hosea prays for God to send him a wife.
Later that day, he sees Angel walking through town and falls in love at first sight.
Flashbacks reveal that Angel's real name is Sarah and that she knows only abuse from men.
As a child, she overhears her father, Alex Stafford, saying that she should never have been born.
Sarah learns that her father is married and her mother, Mae, is his mistress.
Alex eventually cuts off support for Mae, obliging her to become a prostitute and eventually become sick and die.
Distraught, Sarah rejects her mother's Catholic faith.
Afterward, Mae's pimp sells an 8-year-old Sarah to a man named Duke, who renames her "Angel" and forces her into prostitution.
One night, when Angel is a teenager, one of her customers is her father, and she knowingly has sex with him to punish him for how he treated her mother.
He does not recognize her, but when he finds out the next morning, he commits suicide.
This prompts Angel to escape from Duke.
She arrives in California with hopes of beginning a new life but, penniless, once again becomes a prostitute at a brothel there.
In the present day, when Michael enters Angel's room and tells her he wants to marry her, she is thrown off-guard but remains aloof toward him.
It is not until after she is nearly beaten to death by a brothel guard, that she agrees to marry Michael and leaves with him.
He nurses her back to health at his home, despite her continued aloofness toward him.
Michael continues to surprise her as he claims to love her as his wife, and refuses to have sex with her.
Afraid to trust him, she runs away at her first opportunity, but Michael finds her and convinces her to come home.
As the two begin their life on the farm, Angel develops feelings for Michael but runs away again when she realizes that he wants children, as she believes herself to be sterile.
She gets a ride with Michael's brother-in-law, Paul, who resents her because of her past and demands that she pay him for the ride by having sex with him.
Back in Pair A Dice, Angel reluctantly returns to the brothel to get the gold she is owed, from Duchess.
She finds that the brothel had been burned down by Macgowan with the Duchess, Lucky and Mei Ling inside.
With no money and no place to live, she reluctantly goes back to prostitution with one of the town's bar owners.
When Michael arrives to rescue her from her employers, she is relieved to return home with him.
He forgives her, and their relationship begins to blossom based on honesty and affection.
As Angel falls in love with Michael, she becomes convinced that he will be happier married to someone else who can have children, leading her to leave him once more.
Having learned to cook while with Michael, she is able to get a job at a cafe in the city rather than returning to prostitution.
However, by chance, she encounters Duke, who has relocated to California.
He compels her to return to prostitution by threatening the life of her employer.
He places her on a stage in his new establishment for his patrons to view.
There, in a moment of desperation, she regains the faith she lost after her mother's death and tells the audience about Duke's sexual trafficking of young girls.

Duke denies the allegations and attempts to murder Angel, but an African American man, implied to be an old friend of Michael's, subdues him and the captive girls escape into the audience, resulting in Duke being lynched by an outraged mob.
Afterward, Angel starts a successful mission to help rehabilitate other young prostitutes.
Three years later, Paul finally comes to find her and tells her that Michael still loves her.
Angel returns home to Michael, offering her love and telling him that her real name is Sarah.
They reunite and are shown to eventually have children.

31748970.title: Ancestral Search (2020 film)
synopsis: The narrative initiates with the chilling ambience of a neglected Tudor-style mansion, entrapped in the consuming darkness of its advanced years.
In this solemn darkness, the gentle radiance of a scantly steady kerosene lantern held in the shaking grip of Carol pierces through.
She discovers the untouched sewing room of her Grandma Eleanor.
As the mystery about Eleanor's absence grows, Carol's old confidant, Michael, unveils the cryptic conditions revolving around Eleanor's unexpected vanishing.
Struggling under the weight of Eleanor's unexplained absence, the pair – Carol and Michael – decide to direct their energies in unraveling the intertwined layers of this fateful mystery.
Their journey leads them towards their family mansion, resting in the distant corners of Rochester.
They navigate through the labyrinthine corridors of the mansion, their exploration culminating at a secluded study room.
The room, reeking of decayed scrolls and generations-old family documents, unravels an unfamiliar narrative of their family's past.

Amid the room's dust-ridden copies of Bram Stoker's novels and delicate parchment records, they stumble upon tales of their ancestors caught in forbidden practices of occultist magic and nefarious rituals.
This chilling revelation of their family's unsettling heritage sends jolts of icy dread down their spines, yet compels them further into the mystery.

Ghostly whispers echoing through cold crypts, fleeting figures flitting along decaying wallpapers, and disconcerting incidents start to crawl out from the mansion’s darkest corners to confront their resolve.
An impending sense of deep-rooted dread starts to permeate their hearts, yet it is their unwavering logic and reasoning that propels them to push the bounds of understanding.

The webbed theory begins to unravel itself, forcing them to confront a horrifying truth—their lineage is shackled with an ancestral curse, one that can be traced back to the days of their great-great-grandmother.

The curse's underlying details– coded intricately within the timeworn family journal– suggest a visceral connection between Eleanor's abrupt desertion and the cyclical resurgence of the dreaded curse.
The pair slowly comprehend that the curse, a menacing presence hanging ominously in the backdrop, had been leading the chain of mysterious happenings concealed within the mansion's confines.

As the narrative proceeds, they are engrossed in a decisive moment, characterized by fragmented debates and silent pledges, with a firm objective to cleanse their lineage from the tormenting grip of the ancestral curse.
Fueled by new-found hope and relentless tenacity, they gear up for a spectral showdown.
A heightened vigour grips the narrative as they handpick ancient texts and sacred scriptures, endowing themselves with knowledge and courage to finally confront the enigmatic horror.
Preparation ensues rapidly: they rehearse potent Gregorian chants sourced diligently from archaic Roman manuscripts, and acquire sacred water and silver crucifixes endorsed by the local cathedral.
The real confrontation ensues during a hair-raising ouija board session.

The film's scenes fluctuate in intensity, alternating between the stern duo employing their knowledge and guts to fend off horrifying spirits wrapped in Victorian garb, and the mysterious might of their exorcist verses.
Amid the battlefield, the unanticipated arrival of Eleanor's spirit, casting an otherworldly blue luminescence, surfaces as the unexpected ally who vindicates her rightful place in their lineage.
Her melodious lullaby-like whisper, guides Carol and Michael through this spectral adversity.
The narrative inches towards its climax as dawn approaches, symbolizing victory, catharsis, and above all, liberation from the curse that had held them captive.
Their unwavering spirit and unyielding struggle finally shatter the age-old familial curse, exorcising their bloodline from the confining spectral purgatory.
As the curse breaks, Eleanor's spirit, now free from her nefarious chains, elegantly transitions towards the pacifying serenity of the afterlife.
The formerly haunted mansion, now vacant of its spectral inhabitants, stands as a silent testament of Carol and Michael's victorious struggle.
Victors of this supernatural combat, Carol, and Michael, make their exit from the mansion.
Their departure marks the onset of a new beginning, an alleviated chapter for their lineage.
Even as they move on, the burden of victory and fear intermingle.
Leaving the de-haunted mansion behind, they cast one last lingering glance at the edifice that had tested their courage and conviction.
Slowly, but surely, the duo blend back into their routine, indelibly affected by their ancestral engagement and yet, elevated by their triumphant encounter.
The narrative concludes, leaving Carol and Michael standing under spots of their evolved identities, unchanged superficially yet profoundly mutated within.

63342411.title: Relic (2020 film)
synopsis: When Edna, the demented, elderly, and widowed matriarch of the family, goes missing, her daughter Kay and granddaughter Sam travel to their remote family home to find her.
They discover the house locked from the inside, and a strange black mold-like substance on an upstairs wall.
Much of the furniture has been adorned with Post-it notes of reminders for Edna.
That night, Sam is visited by their young neighbour Jamie, who states that he had not been to visit Edna for a while after his father had told him not to go back to the house.
Sam and Kay grow increasingly disturbed by a loud creaking from inside the walls and the appearance of more black mold throughout the house.
Kay experiences nightmares of a withered rotting corpse in an old shack in the woodlands.
The next morning, Kay finds Edna has returned, barefoot and muddied, and unaware of her own disappearance.
Following a visit from a doctor, Edna is found to be mostly of sound mind and without injury with the exception of a large black bruise on her chest (resembling the mold).
Kay tells Sam that she plans to move Edna into a retirement home, given her self-neglect.
That night, Kay awakes to find Edna sleepwalking toward the front door, whispering, "It's nothing."

After being brought back to bed, Edna is convinced there is something hiding in the room and urges Kay to check under the bed; Kay sees something breathing but is distracted before she can investigate further.
The next day, Sam and her grandmother share a tender moment until Edna suddenly grows cold and accuses Sam of stealing from her.
She snatches the ring off Sam's finger, not remembering that she had gifted Sam this ring.
Following another violent event involving Edna, Sam visits Jamie's father Alex to ask why he stopped letting Jamie visit.

Alex reveals that the last time Jamie visited, the pair played hide-and-seek, however, Edna mistakenly locked Jamie in his hiding space and left him there for hours, forgetting she had even seen him that day.
Back at the house, Kay follows Edna into the garden, where she finds her tearing pages from the family photo album and frantically eating them.
When Kay tries to intervene, Edna bites her and storms off, attempting to bury the album in the soil, claiming it will "be safer there".
Fearing that something may come to get her, Edna softens and agrees to let Kay take care of her.
Sam discovers a hidden passageway to another part of the house.
She enters but becomes lost as the corridor begins to loop.
Disorientated and afraid, she resorts to screaming and banging on the walls.
Edna's condition seems to have worsened again; she now glares at Kay mistrustfully, refusing to eat and wetting herself.
Kay notices that her mother's urine is stained black.
As Edna bathes, she scratches what was once her bruise but is now rotting black flesh.
The bathwater overflows and shorts out an electric heater, causing the house's power to go out.
Sam travels deeper into the corridors.
The ceilings slope lower, forcing her to crawl.
She eventually escapes by knocking holes through the mold-covered walls.
Kay finds Edna, much to her horror, picking at her rotting face with a knife.
Kay and Sam flee into the passageway when they hear Edna approach.
Edna, now disfigured and physically contorted, crawls towards them.
Sam and Kay break through the wall and fall into the lounge room, followed by Edna.
She attempts to pin down Sam before being beaten down by Kay.
Wheezing, the decaying Edna gestures toward a post-it note on the floor, labelled "I AM LOVED?
", and smiles.
As they escape the house, Kay realises that the walls are no longer rotting and returns to her corpse-like mother to carry her to bed.
She helps Edna peel away the last remnants of her hair and flesh to reveal her final form, a withered rotting corpse (like the one in her nightmare).
Kay and Sam then lie on the bed with Edna until she peacefully falls asleep.
The film ends with Sam noticing a very small black bruise on the nape of Kay's neck, resembling Edna's initial bruise, suggesting that in time Kay will suffer a similar fate to her mother.

77273752.title: Oppression: The European Struggle (2020 film)
synopsis: The cinematic lens opens to a war-torn Prague under the suffocating grip of the Nazi regime during World War II, revealing an everyday life steeped in desolation and paranoia.
Our protagonist, Martin Kratochvíl, is introduced laboring in a claustrophobic government office.
Martin's personal life unveils a cruel dichotomy to contrast his high-ranking job.
A narrow cot in a sparse, tenebrous room is his sanctuary, shared with his ailing mother who coughs up her existence battling tuberculosis.
The plot deepens when Martin converses fervently with the intimidating figure of Colonel Gunther Hoffman.
Their terse exchange trims the air, hinting at shared, hidden narratives deeply intertwined with the dark webs of wartime quizzes.
An audacious observation has Martin following a reticent trail to a dilapidated bookstore, its significance hidden behind musty tomes.
Secretive meetings take place within its timeworn walls, drawing an audacious throng clutching at the straws of freedom in the besieged city.
The bookstore's crepuscular atmosphere births legends like Sara Adler, a resolute Jewish woman with fire in her veins.
Her fervor challenges the suppressive Nazi regime, her defiance sparking whispers of rebellion.
As war atrocities whisper around him, Martin is drawn towards the flame of Sara's rebellion.
It also pulls him into a complex emotional maelstrom with loyalties split between Sara, his imbroglio with Colonel Hoffman, and the ailing mother he seeks to protect.
The rebel's daring scheme to steal classified Nazi blueprints unfolds in chilling whispers passed around the shadowy bookstore.
A sudden turn presents a betrayer in their midst, causing Josef Adler, Sara’s persistent brother, to fall into the clutches of the Nazis.

Martin is torn between his growing fealty to the rebel cause, his burgeoning love for Sara, the debilitating worry for his sick mother, and the unexplained bond with Hoffman that challenges his tenuous moral compass.
Torn with internal conflict, Martin painfully extracts a confession from Hoffman, revealing his abhorrence of Nazi atrocities.
A vein of unlikely redemption runs through this revelation.

A resultant tirade followed by Hoffman's dramatic martyrdom mark the tipping point of a formidable inner battle over Martin’s divided loyalties, cementing his ultimate allegiance to the clandestine rebellion.
The plot spins into a high-stakes rescue mission, masterminded by Martin, to liberate Josef from the impregnable Nazi prison known as The Gestapo Headquarters in Prague.
But Sara, the fiery core of the rebellion, meets with a dire fate, captured and tormented by the Nazis.
Martin, driven by Sara's desperate situation, tempts fate by daring to release her from the chilling dungeons of Nazi custody.

Despite an atmosphere thick with dread and disarray, Martin skillfully navigates the chaotic labyrinth and delivers Sara from her captors' clutches, marking a symbolic victory against the feared Nazi regime.
The film’s climax crescendos as Martin and Sara successfully leak intelligence about the Nazi concentration camps to the Allied forces.
The inevitable downfall of the Nazi regime seals the rebellions' consequential victory.
Martin, the unsung hero threaded intricately through the narrative, perishes in the cataclysmic final showdown with the Nazis.
His sacrificial demise underscores the tragic cost of their freedom.

The closing scenes capture heartfelt reflections of surviving members of the stoic rebellion and Martin’s grief-stricken mother, the narration echoing the searing reality of war and the indomitable human spirit that rises from the ashes of conflict.
The film wraps up on a deeply moving note, saluting those valiant spirits who chose to rise against their oppressors.
It depicts the untold narratives of countless wartime heroes, and the hollow victory that bespeaks their tragic, noble legacy.

58917347.title: Resistance (2020 film)
synopsis: The film opens in Munich, Nazi Germany.
It is 1938 and Nazi Brown Shirts invade the home of a young Jewish girl, Elsbeth, and kill her parents.

The film continues in Strasbourg, France (near the German border), where Marcel Marceau works unfulfilled in his father's butcher shop, disconnected from Nazi atrocities and eager for the arts, especially mime and painting.
During 1939, as Nazi power consolidates and World War II approaches, Marceau performs a cabaret impression of Charlie Chaplin, using the narrow moustache also favoured by Adolf Hitler.
Visual similarities between Chaplin and Hitler frequent the film.
Marceau's passion for theatre strengthens further after discovering his father secretly performs opera.
While Marcel's cousin, Georges, involves himself with a Jewish arm of the French Resistance, Marcel and Emma fall in love.
Marcel's father, who had fled Poland years earlier, supports his son and Emma joining the anti-Nazi resistance.
It is a decision that defines Marceau's wartime experiences and brings tragic consequences for Marceau's father: arrested in 1944 he dies in Auschwitz during 1945.
A Scout troop which Emma and Georges lead rescues 123 Jewish children whose parents were killed by Nazis.
Marceau's mime skills improve as he helps entertain the orphans in a nearby castle.
Bonds with Emma also strengthen.
After Germany invades Poland in autumn 1939 their involvement deepens with the French Resistance.
Adults distribute the Jewish children into smaller groups to minimise their visibility, some to local churches and others to Jewish families.
Marcel and Emma maintain contact with Elsbeth.
After 1941 Marceau's story intertwines with the menacing Klaus Barbie, who is seen beating to death a Nazi homosexual in Berlin.
Barbie portrays the murder as Aryan purification.
Barbie arrives in Lyon in 1942 during the Nazi occupation of southern France.
His aim is eliminating the French resistance.
Barbie operates by bribing collaborators and brutal executions in an empty swimming pool at Gestapo Headquarters.
Later, Barbie gains notoriety as "The Butcher of Lyon".Marcel and Emma also move to Lyon, with Alain, who narrowly evades capture during a Nazi sweep of Lyon's train station.
Marcel helps Alain escape by burning a German soldier.
Emma and Mila, her sister, are less fortunate.
Captured during another Gestapo roundup, Barbie tortures Mila to death while extracting information from Emma about the resistance.
Emma survives by collaboration but later attempts suicide-by-train.
Marceau saves her and they resolve to help Jewish children escape to Switzerland.
Pretending their Scout troop is hiking, Marcel and Emma, accompanied by Alain plus a dozen children including Elsbeth, travel by SNCF train to the French Alps.
Barbie and SS troops patrol the last train station before the Franco-Swiss border, forcing the petrified Emma into hiding as they search the train.
Barbie fails to discover Emma or the children's true ambition to reach Switzerland.
Marcel and Emma continue their journey towards Switzerland with the children.
Barbie's SS meanwhile learn from a tortured priest the children are escaping Jews.
Barbie, angry at his mistake, mobilises SS troops to pursue Marceau and the children into the icy forests of the Swiss border.
Barbie gets close enough to discharge his handgun, mortally wounding Emma, but cannot prevent their escape.
Marcel is devastated at Emma's death but comforted the children reach Switzerland.
The film closes in 1945 at Nuremberg, Germany.
Marceau is now a Liaison Officer with the United States Army, also an actor, entertaining troops of the American occupation of Germany.
Introduced by General George S. Patton, troops learn that Marceau crossed the Alps many times to save hundreds of children, mostly orphans, and indirectly saved thousands more children.
Patton lauds an "incredible story... of one of those unique human beings that makes your sacrifices and your heroism completely worth it."
The film closes with an evocative mime by Marceau in his famous white face and blue and white shirt.
It ends with a series of "where are they now" captions that neglects saying that Barbie escaped to Bolivia aided by US intelligence.

45134474.title: Beat the Drum
synopsis: Bathed in the tangerine glow of the rising sun, the cracked hatch of a rustic loft resting precariously in the grit of the Mission District of San Francisco, drinks in the day's first light.
The loft is home to Davis, the impassioned drummer of an alternative rock band, the Underdogs, embarked on an arduous journey to the spotlight.

Davis' loft, a swirling kaleidoscope of vivid hues amidst clutter, is shared with his loyal childhood companion Fred, a talented bass guitarist, and Max, their energetic German Shepherd providing the boisterous background score for their lives.
When the city's pulse slows down during the calm afternoons, Davis indulges in whimsical attempts to coach Max in drumming, resulting in comedic episodes of endearing failures.

Suddenly, one clear, bright Thursday morning, the neighborhood wakes to the sight of posters announcing a city-wide Battle of the Bands competition, with the grand prize of a headline tour and invaluable exposure to industry giants capturing everyone's eye.
Invigorated with newfound hope, Davis and the Underdogs devote each waking hour to rigorous practice in their makeshift home studio, letting the neighborhood resound with their fervor.
When Sarah, a sharp and trendy concert manager from New York, enters their band's rhythm, she brings a precision and modernity, causing noticeable shifts.
After some initial discord, Davis and Sarah discover a blooming affection amidst the fiery California sunsets, their shared passion for music knitting them closer.
This unexpected romantic twist triggers a title wave of comedic misunderstandings and heated disputes within the band, fueling their narrative.
Throughout it all, Davis tenaciously pursues his absurd ambition to train Max, the German Shepherd, to master the drums.
While appearing somewhat perplexed initially, Max surprisingly begins to display incredible synchronicity with the drums, evoking incredulous laughter and wonder from the band.
As the day of the fateful Battle of the Bands races closer, an atmosphere of heightened anxiety clouds over San Francisco.
Tragically, Davis falls prey to a severe bout of food poisoning from ill-prepared sushi on the eve of the competition.
Thrusting their haphazard fallback plans aside, the Underdogs finally adopt a desperate solution; they place their faith in Max to handle the drums on the grand stage of the Fillmore.
Adorned with a festive bandana, Max, on stage, induces nervous chuckles from the audience, his innocent confusion tugging at their hearts.
Nevertheless, Max manages to drum out an impeccable rhythm, capturing the audience's fascination and securing the Underdogs an astounding victory, against all odds.
The unforgettable sight of Max drumming spreads like wildfire across various digital platforms, catapulting the Underdogs into dizzying internet fame overnight.
Glued to their modest loft's TV, a weakened Davis takes pride in Max's performance and their band's unimaginable rise to fame, his weariness momentarily forgotten.
Upon Davis' return to health, his unwavering determination and passion earn him newfound respect from Sarah, strengthening their relationship.
Their internet success captures the attention of a leading record label, leading to a lucrative national tour deal featuring Davis and the remarkable German Shepherd.
Davis permanently seats Max alongside him in the band, marking the onset of a thrilling musical adventure filled with enchanting performances and unexpected deviations.
The journey commences with a contemplative Davis, gazing out of the glass-enclosed tour bus, bidding adieu to his humble loft dwelling for an unknown but promising future.
Their first performance in Seattle goes down in an album of memories, featuring an ecstatic crowd and a surprising star—Max.

The narrative seamlessly transitions into documenting their tumultuous road life, filled with overflowing hotels, thunderous concerts, high-profile talk shows, impromptu recording sessions, and Max's irreplaceable charm dominating every frame.
Their journey ends on a poignant note, with Davis, Sarah, Max, and Fred, now united more strongly than ever, celebrating their well-earned conquest amidst laughter and cheers.

67701577.title: Ride the Eagle
synopsis: Leif, a 40ish, perpetually adolescent man working as a band percussionist, lives in his friend Gorka's shed in Los Angeles, and is devoted to his black labrador Nora.
One day, he is informed that his hippy mom Honey has died of cancer.
He greets the news with an indifferent shrug: she abandoned him at 12 to join a cult and had not contacted him since.
She had tried to reach out toward the end, but he had rebuffed her.
Honey has left him her wood cabin in Yosemite – under the condition of completing a to-do list, explained on a pre-recorded video.
The point of the tasks is to make a numbed Leif feel something, a final last effort to mend fences with him.
Leif goes to the cabin and discovers the cabin's cabinets are stashed with marijuana.
At first, it seems that she is just messing with him—one request is to row across the lake and sneak into a house to drop off what turns out to be a kiss-off note.
He almost gets caught after leaving it, forcing him to sneak away.
Another charges him with catching a fish for his dinner using his bare hands.
So, he spends most of a day in a nearby stream, trying to catch one.
Another request is to call "the one that got away" and apologize for his mistakes, leading him to reestablish contact with former girlfriend Audrey.
They turn out to still have some chemistry over the phone, but she is hesitant to do anything about it as she is recovering from a recent breakup.
They try to have phone sex, but Leif has no idea how to, so Audrey soon gives up.
She agrees to visit him at the cabin.
The next day, Gorka calls Leif to give him bad news.
Not only does the rock band of youngsters for which he plays bongos wants him out, but the shed where he was living at the back of his property has been deemed illegal, and has to be destroyed.
Leif looks out to see someone has gutted two rabbits and smeared them over the windshield of his van.
So, after he cleans it up, he sees the next task which is to play a song from the heart on the bongos.
After doing so, Audrey calls back to say she is not coming.
Leif goes for a walk, leaving a reluctant Nora behind.
On his return, she has disappeared.
Frantic, he contacts the police and finally leaves a note in the cabin he had left the original note in, asking him not to hurt her.
That night, the mysterious angry neighbor breaks into Leif/Honey's cabin and, similarly to calls he had made earlier, insults him in a jealous way.
The neighbor, Carl had believed Leif was her lover, not her son.
Carl explains they had been on a break, so had no idea she had passed.
He tells him she had felt terrible when Leif had refused to speak to her as an adult.
Carl lists everything he will miss about Honey, finally offers Leif an olive branch and departs.
The last request is to hike to Green Lake.
There, he is directed to find her ashes and read a note written by her.
When he returns to the cabin, Nora is back, the huge stashes of pot are gone, and the last of her video tells him to reconsider and live his life.
Leif and Audrey text again, and he decides to take the eight-hour drive to see her.

41631921.title: Endzone Triumph (2020 film)
synopsis: Our story begins with the electrifying scene of high school football sensation, Kyle Carter, scoring a victorious touchdown in his final regional championship match.
Kyle belongs to a blue-collar family, their dreams and aspirations glistening in Kyle, embodying his full ride football scholarship.
One cozy evening, Ada and Joe Carter, Kyle's loving parents, celebrate his remarkable achievements.
In an emotional farewell, Kyle packs his bags, biding goodbye to his parents and childhood home, stepping into the bright future at the esteemed University of Texas.

Upon his arrival at the university, Kyle doesn’t take long to realize the fierce rigors of balancing a demanding academical schedule and the grueling daily workouts of the Longhorns, the college football team he was eager to join.
His struggles become evident - his concentration split between academics and sports, his performance starts to wane.
He loses sleep, his grades dip, his football magic seems to fade, and he feels like an alien entity, cut off from the community he used to belong to.
Travis, the unparalleled star quarterback, takes an instantaneous disliking towards Kyle.
This leads to regular heated arguments on the field, with Travis using every opportunity to berate and belittle Kyle.
During a match against Baylor University, Kyle is handed the crucial responsibility to make a decisive pass.
However, he fumbles, and the pass fails.
The Longhorns suffer an unexpected loss, and Kyle is blamed for the failure.
In his period of isolation and gloom, Kyle stumbles upon an unlikely friend and mentor.
Lester, the carefree janitor of the Longhorns training complex, offers hope and solace to the dejected soul.
The deserted football stadium, under the cloak of moonlight, turns into a sanctuary of wisdom for Kyle.
Lester shares life lessons, strategic football insights, and enlightens him on the power of unity amongst teammates.
Kyle finds a companion in Peter, his studious and introverted roommate.
Peter supports Kyle in his academic turmoil.
Kyle begins to step beyond the boundaries of his comfort zone.
He joins a book club, volunteers at a local animal shelter, and makes efforts to establish connections within the community.
During one of his visits to the university library, Kyle meets Abby, a sociology major whose humility and kindness instantly tug at his heartstrings.
Their bond strengthens - encapsulating those moments of their blossoming love story.
Simultaneously, his enhanced performance on the field due to Lester's teachings catches everyone's eye.

61807863.title: Safety (2020 film)
synopsis: Set in South Carolina in the 2000s, Ray McElrathbey is a freshman at Clemson University, having been accepted on a football scholarship for their team, the Tigers.
He is quickly thrust into campus life as he tries to balance his school work and football career.
He begins to receive numerous phone calls from his younger brother Fahmarr, but tries to ignore him to study.
He quickly takes an interest in sports journalist student Kaycee Stone while also butting heads with football captain Keller.

One day, Ray learns that Fahmarr is not at home with their mom, Tonya, and races back home over the weekend to find that their mother has relapsed and Fahmarr has been staying with a former acquaintance, presumed to be a dealer.
Ray takes Fahmarr to child services and, faced with the prospect of losing Fahmarr to the system, decides to take him in, albeit temporarily so that Tonya can recover in a month.
Ray hides Fahmarr in his dorm with his roommate Daniel Morelli discovering him.
He promises to keep him a secret while also helping him out.
Ray soon becomes close with Kaycee though she begins to suspect that he is hiding something from her.
Fahmarr also gets enrolled in a new school, though the different environment becomes slightly alienating for him.
Eventually, studying, practice and caring for Fahmarr begin to take its toll on Ray and Daniel brings in the rest of the freshman squad to help with keeping Fahmarr out of trouble.
Unfortunately, team captain Keller discovers Fahmarr and forces Ray to come clean about it.
Coach Bowden and Simmons reprimand him and Ray tells Fahmarr that he must leave as Tonya's program is almost over.
Tonya informs the boys that she will be staying in the program much longer, meaning that Fahmarr must go into the system.
Ray becomes depressed and tells Kaycee about why he has been acting so strange.
After some encouragement, Ray speaks with Simmons about Fahmarr and he helps him go out and retrieve him.
They must live off campus while Ray holds side jobs to keep themselves afloat.
Fahmarr goes back to school and begins crushing on a girl named Shannon.
Ray's relationship with Keller and Kaycee improve and becomes a better player.
Fahmarr sits-in in one of their classes and helps the team with one of their games.
Kaycee, impressed with the changes, offers to print Ray's story in the paper, despite him not wanting to come off as a charity case.
Soon, everyone in the community begins offering help to the McElrathbeys as their relationships improve.
Shortly before the Bowden Bowl, Ray is informed that the NCAA is investigating his situation as they believe that he is receiving irregular benefits.
Despite the support of Bowden and Simmons, they are informed that it seems impossible that they will be waived.
Ray begins to prevent any more charity to himself or Fahmarr and shuts himself off from everyone.
He soon discovers that Fahmarr has run away and everyone goes searching for him; eventually finding him at a diner.
Ray promises that he will continue to look after him no matter what and he reluctantly forces Tonya to hand full custody of Fahmarr over to him.
Ray and Fahmarr head to the hearing at the NCAA, along with his coaches, his team, Kaycee and the community.
After giving a heartfelt speech, the board ultimately decide to allow Ray and Fahmarr all the necessary benefits needed.
Fahmarr is seen with the rest of the Tigers and is given his own jersey as he joins his brother on the field to prepare for the big game.
During the credits, it is revealed that Ray successfully graduated as he and Fahmarr reunited with their completely sober mother.
Real footage is played of their appearance on Oprah as well as Ray playing football.

10048722.title: Virtue's Flight (film)
synopsis: We commence our story in the quaint village of Stone Town.
We meet the protagonists, Virtue and Rival, identical twins, distinctive for their awe-inspiring supernatural abilities.
Their uncanny capabilities, bait an air of intrigue, making them the hot topic of village whispers, and at times, they develop into fear-induced stares from the village folk.
Malicious conjectures suggesting witchcraft and dark sorcery associated with the twins seep into the village vein.
A horrifying incident taints the semblance of peace.
Their ancestral stone-cottage home turns into a fiery furnace at the hands of a panicking mob.
Falsely accused for sparking the disaster, Virtue and Rival are forced to flee from Stone Town.
Long winding trails lead them to Orion City, a densely populated metropolis bustling with activity.
They grapple to blend with the city crowd while also trying to grapple with their extraordinary abilities.
The pain of their loss refuses to subside, acting as a splitting wedge in their relationship.
Rival, while plunging deeper into bitterness and rancor, hones his powers to form a formidable alter-ego—the 'Phantom of Orion.'
Rival thrives in the city outskirts, routinely executing illicit activities, inciting panic and unease across Orion city with his uncontrolled supernatural powers.
In stark contrast, Virtue, longs for normalcy.
She attempts to suppress her abilities and immerse herself in an unassuming life.
Living incognito, Virtue can't escape from the unsettling whispers and horror tales circling the city, which spoke of fearsome encounters with a mysterious supernatural entity.
It's a bitter pill to swallow but through closer inspection, Virtue identifies this terrifying entity as none other than her own brother, Rival.
Struggling with guilt and remorse over her passive stance till now, Virtue decides it is high time to intervene in the escalating situation.
Accepting her latent abilities, Virtue is hopeful that her powers could possibly cease Rival's reign of terror.
Her mission starts by finding a mentor in Obsidian, an ancient supernatural entity, who had managed to coexist peacefully among humans.
Under Obsidian's guidance and wisdom, Virtue aspires to control her inherent powers and save her brother from spiraling into total anarchy.
Training with Obsidian gives her the ability to harness her talents.
Virtue evolves into an impressive supernatural entity, fearlessly encountering her powers and preparing for a final showdown against Rival.
The inevitable day arrives when Virtue confronts Rival, leading to an epic clash of supernatural powers amidst the crumbling ruins of Orion City.
In the throes of this dramatic battle, their once unified past is laid bare.
The battle reaches its peak, resulting in Rival facing defeat.
Virtue emerges victorious, but not without sacrificing the quiet life she had learned to cherish.
Embracing her newfound reality, she pledges to heal the damage caused by Rival.
Virtue makes her way back to Stone Town, where she is initially greeted with apprehension, but also with intrigued and wide-eyed stares.
Virtue, buoyed by her newfound strength and mastery over her powers, begins reconstructing the burnt stone cottage and damaged buildings.
Her continuous efforts and unwavering resolve eventually soften the skeptical townsfolk, gradually replacing fear with trust and understanding.
Utilizing this breakthrough, Virtue begins creating a blueprint for a harmonious co-existence between humans and supernaturals.
The story concludes with a beautiful portrayal of Virtue's courageous journey.

62537103.title: Samaritan (film)
synopsis: Superhumans Samaritan and Nemesis were antagonistic twin brothers who lived in Granite City, where the residents at the time burned down their home in an effort to kill them, only for the twins to escape, while their parents died in the fire.

Samaritan grew up to become a superhero as a way to show the world that he is nothing like how they originally viewed him in the past, whereas Nemesis, consumed by revenge, became a supervillain that wanted the world to suffer the same fate as their parents.
Evenly matched, the villainous Nemesis crafts  a mystical sledgehammer that gave him an edge over the heroic Samaritan.
However, the hammer could hurt both brothers.
During a confrontation at the city's power plant, both were apparently killed as the plant exploded, blacking out the city.
Many people remain fans of Samaritan, and there are constant rumors that he is still alive.

Twenty five years later, thirteen-year-old Sam Cleary tries his best to help his mother with their financial crisis, and, after being threatened with eviction, he accepts a job from a gang headed by Reza.
The plan goes awry and Reza tries to blame Sam, but the real gang leader, Cyrus, is impressed and personally gives Sam $110.
Reza and his friends later attack Sam as payback but are stopped by Joe Smith, a garbage collector who lives in an apartment across from Sam's.
Joe displays super-strength in fighting off the gang members, and Sam suspects that he is Samaritan.

Meanwhile, Cyrus locates Nemesis' hammer at a police station and sets himself up as the new Nemesis, sparking riots and chaos throughout the city, using EMP grenades to black out and disrupt the city infrastructure.
After Sam confronts him, Joe denies that he is Samaritan, but Reza - still looking for revenge - hits him with his car.
Joe is badly injured but heals before Sam's eyes, overheating so much he has to be cooled down in a cold shower and by eating ice cream.
Joe and Sam build a friendship, while at the same time Cyrus invites Sam to work with his gang.
However, Sam is disturbed when he witnesses their violent activities.
When Joe saves a young girl from an explosion caused by the gang, the media claims that Samaritan is back threatening Cyrus' plans.
Reza recognizes Joe as being the same person he "killed" with his car and thus his identity and connection to Sam.
Finding Joe's apartment empty, they kidnap Sam and his mother to lure Joe to their headquarters as a trap.
Joe breaks into the headquarters, and decimates the gang before being confronted by Cyrus, now dressed as Nemesis and wielding the hammer.
Despite his strength, Joe is weakened from the gang fight, and at a disadvantage against the hammer giving Cyrus the upper hand.

As they fight, with Cyrus calling himself Nemesis, and Joe "the good guy", Joe reveals that Samaritan did die during the power plant fire, and Joe is actually Nemesis, who survived but left his villainous life behind, having been freed from his need of revenge.
It is shown in flashback that Samaritan had effectively won the fight, but refused to kill Nemesis, instead tossing the hammer away, still viewing him as his brother.
The roof subsequently gave way, leaving Samaritan hanging precariously above the flames.
Despite his best efforts and a change of heart, Nemesis was unable to save his brother, instead tossing both of their masks into the same fire that Samaritan fell into.
Destroying the hammer, Joe kills Cyrus by knocking him into a burning abyss - the same way Samaritan died - but almost overheats from his healing abilities and the spreading fire.
