Evelyn, unable to bear the weight of her secret any longer, reveals her dual identity as the artist behind the groundbreaking collection and the modest gallery assistant simultaneously.

Following the highly successful exhibition, Lucas and Evelyn enjoy a tranquil moment on the museum's deserted rooftop, basking in the glow of their shared love story and mutual achievements in their respective fields.
Evelyn’s fiery passion for art ignites a flame in Lucas, leading him to perceive the world of art and his role as an art critic through a fresh lens.
As the dust settles, Evelyn discovers the harmony of cohabitating with her dual identities—the determined artist and the reserved assistant.
This revelation brings with it newfound inner peace.
Evelyn achieves her dream of leaving an indelible imprint on the world of art.
Hailed as a groundbreaking artist, she luxuriates in the success that she had only fantasized about.
She understood that her journey through personal struggles formed the pinnacle of her art exhibition, the very essence of the “Shattered Dreams Exhibit”.
The narrative continually reminds the audience that dreams, regardless of how fragmented, can be pieced back together to create a remarkable image of unprecedented beauty.
The story drives home messages of hope, perseverance, risk-taking, self-belief showing the potential of cherishing shattered dreams and nurturing them to unimaginable success.

62378924.title: The Broken Hearts Gallery
synopsis: Lucy is a young assistant at the Woolf Gallery in NYC.
Idolizing her boss, Eva Woolf, she readily provides info about her to her boyfriend and colleague, Max.
Her friends and roommates, law student Amanda and model Nadine, hear her talking non-stop about him.
At the gallery opening, instead of Max asking her to move in, she is both dumped for his ex Amelia and fired.
Drunk and despondent, Lucy climbs into Nick's car, believing it's her Lyft.
The kind Nick takes her home while she describes the gallery fiasco.
For weeks, she wallows in her room, with her roommates’ support.
Finally, they urge her to clear out her cave of memorabilia from past relationships.
Unable to sell her mementos, Lucy follows Max and Amelia into a restaurant.
Nick sees her and steers her outside before she can cause a scene.
Lucy and Nick end up at the Chloe hotel, an old YMCA.
Renovating his dream boutique hotel for five years, he is out of money and needs help to keep the project going.
He encourages her to hang Max's tie on an old nail.
Inspired, she writes a caption, and they jointly come up with the concept of Broken Heart Gallery.
Nick shows up at Lucy's, inviting her to see something added to the wall.
Excited, she envisions a chance for New Yorkers to connect over shared loss and humanity.
Meeting and bonding with Marcos, Nick's friend on the building project, they convince Nick to give her gallery space in exchange for work.
Lucy shares photos with their stories on social media #BROKENHEARTGALLERY, then posts short videos of people parting with their memorabilia.
She sees first-hand how freeing it is for people to give up their baggage.
Seeking furniture and decorations for the gallery-hotel, they pound the streets, reclaiming pieces as they go.
On the way, they chat about themselves.
The money to start the hotel came from his grandma's inheritance.
Lucy's mom sees art everywhere.
Browsing in a secondhand-book shop, Lucy sees Max, follows him to a café, and meets Amelia.
Nick rescues her again, saying they're off to a meeting about their hot new gallery.
They leave, Max looking intrigued.
While Lucy is alone one day in the hotel-gallery, a cold, blonde woman arrives looking for Nick, and declines to leave a message.
Shortly thereafter, the three roommates invite Nick, Marco and his wife to a karaoke night birthday bash.
Lucy shows Nick New York Magazine mentioning their project, and she tells him about her idea for a ball opening.
They sing a ‘Don’t Go Breaking My Heart’ duet.
Marco (like her roommates) suggests Nick ask her out.
Arriving home at 3 am, they find Max out front.
After railing on him in Lucy's defense, Amanda and Nadine head up.
Max is telling her he wants her back when Nick shows up with birthday cake and the men butt heads.
She and Max stay out, talking, and she agrees to a lunch.
As Nick's loan falls through, he tells her to rehome her exhibit, so Lucy approaches every gallery she knows.
At lunch with Max, he suggests Eva Woolf, who surprisingly offers gallery space.
Seemingly about to take it, as she and Max leave together, she has an epiphany.
She asks Nadine for help in breaking up with him.
He tells her Amelia dumped him, and she concludes that they were not meant to be together, as she's the hero in his love story, and he's the villain in hers.
She tells Nick, who informs her that now he has a mystery backer providing the finance to complete the venue.
They all work to get the opening ready.
Lucy opens up to Nick, introducing him to her mom Cheryl, who is in a home due to dementia.
Later on, Nick and Lucy are intimate.
Then Chloe appears (the cold woman from weeks ago).
Lucy leaves, hurt.
Finding her, Nick tries to explain that it's over with Chloe, and he only kept Chloe's name on the hotel because changing it would be too expensive.
He says he'll stay away from the gallery opening, so as not to distract Lucy from her triumph.
Eva Woolf unexpectedly contributes an item to Lucy's exhibition, donating the box of the wedding ring used to fund her own gallery, saying, ‘Pain is inevitable.

It’s what you do with it that matters.’ Before the opening, Marco and his wife find Nick, who claims to be ill. Marco tells him it's heartbreak, and that Lucy organised his mystery backer (who is Eva Woolf).
During Lucy's opening speech, Nick bursts in with a neon sign, with the new name, The Broken Hearts Hotel.
As he professing his love for her, she descends from the balcony and tells him she reciprocates his love.

80842772.title: The Sphere (2022 film)
synopsis: Nestled below the glitter and glamour of Hollywood lies a run-down apartment, its peeling wallpaper echoing the faded reputation of its inhabitant, Jane, a former A-list actress, whose star-studded career diminished as swiftly as the setting sun.

A shrill ring snaps the somber silence with another cruel reminder of her fall from grace, as Jane holds back the sting of yet another rejected audition, gracefully ending the call, with a bitter "Thank you for considering me."
Kenny, her charismatic yet mysterious manager, presents a script entitled "Mountain Monsters 6: Struggle for K2."
However, skepticism paints Jane's face as she recalls her last significant project, "Bayou's Curse."
Weighed down by exhaustion yet provoked by Kenny's robust confidence in her, Jane steps onto the chaotic set of "Mountain Monsters", welcomed by the familiar warm smiles of the crew members.
A newfound wave of self-assurance nudges Jane to accept the high-stakes character of Dr. Rachel Starling, a bold beast-chaser known for her fearlessness.
However, her initial enthusiasm dwindles as visceral panic seeps in, her debut day clogged with tangled lines, brusque dealings with wardrobe staff, and frosty run-ins with the modern, hip co-stars.
Amid the turmoil on-set, Jane and Max, the film's prodigious leading male, develop an unexpected camaraderie via a series of side-splitting mishaps.
Disaster strikes when Jane unwittingly crashes an essential prop, the sleek ‘sphere’ into smithereens, sending shockwaves of chaos across the set.
Determined, she resolves not to repeat her past mistakes and cooks up a cunning plan to repair the 'sphere' under the shroud of twilight.
Jane forms an unorthodox band of misfits, enlisting the initially reluctant Max, her enduring anchor Kenny, and some empathetic crew members ready to forego a night's rest for her cause.

This ragtag crew embarks on an audacious and hysterical midnight mission to mend the sphere, encountering a zealous security team, maneuvering through an abrupt power outage with absurdly unfit equipment, all while sorting out a hilariously over-inflated monster prop.
With dawn as their time limit, they somehow manage to piece together a replacement sphere, though its absurd craftsmanship resembles that of a foil beach ball rather than an ultra-modern movie prop.
Amidst the escalating tension, Jane, taking center stage with a poignant monologue, instead erupts into a fit of uncontrollable laughter upon seeing their makeshift sphere.
The director, in an unexpected twist, decides to incorporate this humorous interlude into the film's final cut, giving Jane due credit for the much-needed dash of comedy.
Jane's tenacity and unexpected flair for comedy endear her to the team, fortifying her place within it and earning their hard-fought respect.
On premiere night, the quirky sphere scene, intended to be a disaster, instead unleashes bursts of laughter from the audience.
Critics laud the film; Jane's unique blend of comedy and charm is cited as the unexpected delight that propelled the movie to unforeseen heights.
Jane's star is on the rise again, as her phenomenal performance in the film skyrockets her back onto Hollywood's typically fickle radar.
Embracing her unforeseen comedic charisma, Jane signs numerous contracts featuring roles certain to spotlight her newly discovered comic abilities.
The story concludes in the warmth of Jane's recently refurbished, now lavish, apartment.

They cheerfully raise toasts to their forthcoming projects, with vibrant discussions simmering around potential sequels promising to transport the audience on more riveting, laughter-filled journeys in time to come.

66691193.title: The Bubble (2022 film)
synopsis: Following a problematic film role that nearly destroyed her career, actress Carol Cobb is offered the chance to revive it by reprising her role as the heroic Dr. Lacey Nightingale in the sixth installment of the wildly popular Cliff Beasts franchise: Cliff Beasts 6: Battle for Everest – Memories of a Requiem.
Having turned down appearing in the fifth film in favor of doing the aforementioned panned role, Carol initially fears that her former Cliff Beasts castmates may still hold a grudge against her.
One of the first major film productions to resume amidst the COVID-19 pandemic, the Cliff Beasts cast arrive at a swanky English hotel and must self-quarantine for two weeks.
Afterwards, a welcome back party is organized for the cast and crew.
Here, Carol happily reunites with co-stars Dustin, Howie and Sean but has an awkward meeting with Lauren, the only Cliff Beasts co-star appearing bitter about her absence.
There are two series newcomers, Dieter, a respected, but indifferent veteran actor, and Krystal, a young TikTok sensation to attract a younger demographic.
The latter quickly bonds with Carla, a deadpan on-set production assistant who's her age.
Director Darren Eigan, an enthusiastic, but frazzled indie filmmaker, tries to boost morale and make the shoot special, coming off as pretentious.
He clashes with leading man Dustin, who constantly bombards him with revised versions of the script to fit his own vision.
Dieter has a crush on Anika, the hotel's sweet front desk clerk, but she wants to build a proper relationship first before jumping into sex.
Shooting begins and for the first few days, everything appears to be okay.
However, a series of events delay the production even more.
During a group meditation session, Howie becomes paranoid and quits the film in a panic - in response to this, his Cliff Beasts character is killed off gruesomely.
Bored in the hotel, Krystal and Carla sneak out to party in the city.
This gains traction online and gets Krystal cancelled for her behavior, losing many of her followers.
Later the cast tests positive for influenza, linked to a delivery girl who had given them all their morning coffees.
Despite being ill, the studio forces them to film.
Introduced is the mysterious Mr. Best, the head of a new security team from the studio to oversee the cast and film's production, making some of the cast grow suspicious.

When the shoot starts back up again, Carol realizes that most of her character's dialogue and actions have either been given to Krystal or omitted entirely making her suspect this is how the studio is getting back at her for leaving the franchise.
Carol has a heart-to-heart with Darren, telling him of her concerns, but when he talks to the higher-ups about giving back her dialogue it backfires.
Lauren tries to escape from the hotel in a frenzy one night.
Mr. Best's men graphically shoot one of her hands off, leaving her in the hospital for the remainder of the shoot.
Infuriated, Carol tries to rally together her castmates and fight for their rights.
Shortly afterwards, while filming an elaborate dancing TikTok with Krystal, Dieter collapses.
They quickly work together to revive him, however, it's Anika who does it, cementing their relationship.
This event inspires the team, and they plan a getaway.

As they shoot the climax, Dustin creates a distraction by clashing with Darren about the script revisions while the rest of the cast leave the set and try to avoid getting caught by Mr. Best and his men.
The cast meets up at the helipad, calling upon an unsure Sean to fly them out.
A furious Darren tries to stop them from leaving, but is knocked out by Dustin.
Inside the helicopter is Anika, who hopes to run away with Dieter, who happily accepts.
Sean gets the helicopter up off the ground but doesn't know how to fly it forward.
The rest of the crew encourage Sean to fly the helicopter away from the hotel as the Cliff Beasts cast celebrate their victory.
Two years later, a behind the scenes documentary detailing the troubled production and crazy antics on the set entitled Beasts of the Bubble is released to rave reviews and praise from the public.
While Carol is described as "the villain" of the film, she's proud of the project.
Dieter and Anika's relationship is still strong.
Lauren is in good spirits, having a robotic hand.
Meanwhile, Darren is signed on to direct a movie based on Skittles.

10920181.title: Festive Blues: Mexican Holiday
synopsis: The film commences with the brash 17-year-old Lola, visibly annoyed as she aggressively packs her suitcase, at the prospect of her upcoming Christmas holiday with her newly blended family to Cancun, Mexico.

Lola is seen spending time with herself, her teen angst apparent on her face as she lounges on her bed, expressing her resentment about the trip through sarcastic jibes at unsuspecting family members and angered diary entries.
Next steps into picture, Ben, her new 16-year-old stepbrother.
He is energetic and excitable, his happy demeanor marked by his wide smile and intense enthusiasm about the upcoming trip and the opportunity to build a new friendship with his step-sister.
Upon landing in the sunny Cancun, Lola tries her best to literally hide from her new family, but Ben's relentless energy and numerous attempts to befriend her fail to let her escape.
Lola's subtle plans to distance herself from her family become amusingly unsuccessful.
Ben continues his pursuit of their friendship, going to great lengths to befriend her.
Their parents, particularly her bubbly stepfather Paul, continue their efforts to engage the duo in holiday activities.
Lola continually finds ways to escape these family bonding attempts.
One such escapade leads them to an odd, old-looking book while being dragged around Cancun's famous Mercado 28 flea market, which reveals a weathered pirate map when opened.
This prompts them into a comedic expedition across the city.

They find themselves in various unexpected situations and their journey introduces them to peculiar characters, who give Lola and Ben encrypted clues and riddles which lead them to popular tourist attractions like the Xcaret Park and the Scenic Tower.
Their epic hunt lands them in various tight spots— situations that force them to cooperate and start relying on each other.
Act 4 begins with their map leading them to a shabby, dusty souvenir shop.
Disappointed and feeling somewhat ridiculous, their shared embarrassment brings them closer than their shared adventure.
Returning to the resort to find their family frantically searching for them, they realize the depth of the concern their family holds for them.
Lola's rebellious streak starts to fade as she acknowledges her stepfamily's genuine worry and care.
A clear shift in Lola's perception towards her stepfather and her new family is evident as she exchanges relieved smiles with them.
The entire family, now closer and fond of each other, participate together in the local Mexican festivities.
Lola and Ben's adventure becomes part of their holiday story.
They incorporate local elements for a fun twist during the celebrations and create excitement.
The film concludes with the family, now truly connected, celebrating Christmas Eve.

Lola, finding common ground with Ben, no longer sees him just as an annoying stepbrother but a partner-in-mischief and a friend, and he reciprocates this feeling, seeing her as his sister rather than a stranger.
The movie ends on a euphoric note, capturing a beautiful candid shot of the family under twinkling fairy lights, embracing and laughing together.

62534522.title: The Christmas Chronicles 2
synopsis: Two years after the events of the first film, Kate Pierce is a cynical 13 year old, unhappy about spending Christmas in Cancún, Mexico with her mother Claire, her brother Teddy, Claire's new boyfriend Bob Booker, and his son Jack.
Wanting to be back home where it is snowing, Kate tries to secretly fly back early to Boston.
Unbeknownst to her and their stowaway Jack, the shuttle is driven by Belsnickel, a nefarious Christmas elf, who sends them unepectedly through a wormhole to the North Pole.
Kate and Jack are found and saved by Santa Claus, who brings them back to his and Mrs. Claus's house.
The Clauses give them a grand tour of their village, then dinner.
Jack and Kate go to bed as Belsnickel and his follower Speck attempt to destroy the village.

Mrs. Claus tells the kids the origin story of Santa in Turkey, how he saved the elves from extinction, and received the Star of Bethlehem, a magical artifact that stops time in and provides power to Santa's Village.
The Clauses adopted Belsnickel, but as he grew up and they had less time for him, he became unruly, transforming him into a human as a curse, so he ran away.
Belsnickel releases the yule cat Jola into the reindeer pen, injuring Dasher.
He then releases a potion into the village that makes the elves go insane and steals the Star of Bethlehem from the top of the Christmas tree.
11 Santa and the others confront Belsnickel.
The two struggle over the star, and it is accidentally destroyed, causing the power to go out in the village.
So Santa and Kate leave for Turkey to get the forest elves, led by Hakan, to build a new one.
The maddened elves start a snowball fight that allows Jack to escape.
He leaves to get a root to cure them while Mrs. Claus stays behind to heal Dasher.
Meanwhile, Kate and Santa successfully find the elves and Hakan who give them a casing for a new star and Santa captures the power of the Star of Bethlehem inside it.
While flying back to the village, Belsnickel catches up to them on a sleigh pulled by jackalotes (a hybrid of a jackal and a coyote which he created).
He steals the star to stop himself from aging until he can figure out how to replace Santa, and transports them back to 1990 Boston via a time-travel device he planted on Santa's sleigh.
Jack finds the root and brings it back to Mrs Claus.
Kate attempts to buy AAA batteries for Belsnickel's time travel device at Boston airport so she and Santa can return to the future.
However, she is detained by airport security as the bill has the modern redesign so seems counterfeit.
Kate is taken to a locked lost kids security room.
When she laments about her wrongdoings in Cancun, another kid named Doug Pierce comforts her and helps her escape.
After Kate joins Santa, she realizes Doug is her late father.
With help from airport worker Grace, Santa gets everybody singing a Christmas song so the weather clears.
With Christmas spirit high enough for the sleigh to fly, he puts in the batteries and they transport back and recover the star.
Mrs. Claus makes the root into a powder, which Jack manages to load into the snow cannons.
He shoots it onto the elves, curing them.
Santa and Kate race back to the village evading Belsnickel as he chases them.
Mrs. Claus throws an explosive gingerbread cookie between the sleighs before they can collide in a game of chicken.
Dasher recovers and assists Santa in defeating Jola, who is hurled out of the village.
Kate places the star on top of the tree, restoring power to the village.
Santa gives Belsnickel the first toy that they built together, they reconcile and he is transformed back into an elf.
Santa flies Kate and Jack back to Cancún where they tell an excited Teddy about their adventure.
Kate also becomes more accepting of Bob.
At the end, Kate, her Mom, and Teddy, along with Bob and Jack sing "O' Christmas Tree" as everyone in the North Pole Santa also sing it.

65342026.title: Sorcery Time-Stop: Unfulfilled Prophecy
synopsis: In a realm of unmatched beauty where floral forests of lavender and jasmine perfume the air, a world teeming with magical beings residing in majestic, radiant castles.
Inside one of these magnificent castles resides our unlikely trio of heroine sorceresses.
Alexis, armed with her fiery, vibrant red hair that flickers with a life of its own.
Bella, whose doe-like brown eyes hold an air of innocence and wisdom far beyond her years.
Gabriella, best known for her captivating black curls, is the final member of this enchanting triumvirate.

Together, they have devoted their lives to unravel the mysteries of the arcane, performing mystical rituals involving languages of the long-lost rune, deep within the grand library nestled in the heart of their castle, framed by towering mahogany bookshelves.
One fateful day, their lives take an unexpected turn as they stumble upon a faded prophecy concealed within an ancient, leather-bound tome.
The prophecy detailed a celestial ritual involving alignment of the stars and moons.
According to the old scripture, performing this ritual correctly could suspend the linear progression of time.
Fueled by an insatiable curiosity and desire for knowledge, they threw themselves into extensive research.
Consulting forgotten grimoires of diverse mythologies and magical theories, they sought to piece together the perplexing ritual detailed in the prophecy.
Meanwhile, in the mundane human world, Chelsea, an ordinary librarian leads an unassuming life.

Despite her mundane profession, she struggles to understand her sporadic involuntary manifestation of unexplained magical abilities—peculiar instances when she could move objects without touching them.
In their castle cloaked in the hues of the enchantment, the girls make a startling discovery.
An ancient obelisk, etched with rune symbols, holds the answers they seek.
The ritual requires a fourth sorceress, someone burgeoning with magical power—someone like Chelsea.
Without wasting any moment, the trio perform an intense summoning spell.
Encapsulated in a flurry of vibrant glyphs and a crescendo of powerful incantations, they weave a portal through time and space.
From her normality in the nine-to-five librarian job, Chelsea is whisked away into their wondrous, magical realm.
Arriving in this magical world, Chelsea is initially shaken.
Her old life's simplicity now replaced by overwhelming magic leaves her anxious and fearful.
However, as she begins to learn about her ancestral lineage of powerful sorceresses, her fear starts to subside and morphs into fascination and curiosity.
Over time, a montage of the girls' shared experiences illustrates their growing bond.
Filled with laughter, knowledge-sharing, and arduous training sessions within the castle's grand training hall, the previous trio metamorphosed into a united quartet with Chelsea's inclusion.
The original triumvirate offers their guidance, teaching Chelsea to wield and control her hereditary magic.
As they study the prophecy further, it reveals its true purpose.
The unity of the quartet is destined to protect an invaluable, ancient magical artifact of unimaginable power—a power which can alter the very fabric of their realm.
However, their lighthearted journey takes a dark turn when Mordak, a malevolent ancient sorcerer with an insatiable lust for power, discovers their plans.
With his scarred eyes glowing maliciously, he drowns in his wickedness.
Learning about their intention to perform the time-standstill ritual, he furthers his nefarious plot.
Employing dark necromantic spells and twisted magic, he plots to seize control of the time-warping ritual and thus, the power-laden artifact.
The girls, through a scrying spell, unveil Mordak's malicious intentions.
With the stakes raised, the sorceresses know they must extinguish his impending threat, causing tension within their once harmonious group.
Amidst the mounting pressure, Chelsea's confidence starts to waver.
She questions her worth and relevance in a world where she feels outmatched by more experienced magic-users.
Seizing this opportunity of vulnerability, Mordak wages a fierce assault on the castle.
He bypasses its magical defenses and traps Alexis, Bella, and Gabriella within an oppressive dome of shadowy enchantments.
Meanwhile, in the human world, Chelsea is alerted to her friends' perilous situation via an enchanted mirror, one connecting both worlds.
Torn between her newfound responsibility and debilitating fear, she confronts her insecurities.
Her previous life holding no allure anymore, she makes a daring choice, embracing her magical ancestry and stepping into her destined role.
Armed with newfound grit and determination, she returns to the magical world, casting a rift-opening spell to infiltrate the sorcerer's stronghold.
Harnessing her raw telekinetic abilities, Chelsea manages to break Mordak’s shadow dome, freeing her friends from his malicious grip.

Together, they transcend the limitations of their individualities, realizing the prophecy's deeper interpretation—it was not about halting the flow of time, but the unearthing of the strength ensconced within their shared bond.
Forming a united front, the evolved quadrumvirate of sorceresses squares off with their adversary, Mordak.
His nefarious attempts to divide them are futile, amplifying his frustration.
Together, they perform the celestial ritual—but not to suspend time.
They warp it to their advantage.
Using their seamlessly coordinated magic, they consign Mordak to a timeless dimension, nullifying his threat.
Choosing her magical heritage and the bond with her friends over her former human life, Chelsea decides to stay permanently in the mystical realm.
The adversity they faced solidifies their bond preparing them for more magical trials they may face in the future.
The girls stumble upon another prophecy, veiled within a gilded scroll.
It hints at the emergence of another antagonist—a power-hungry dragon, foreshadowing future battles.

62010614.title: The Craft: Legacy
synopsis: Three girls, Frankie, Tabby, and Lourdes, are trying to freeze time with magic, but failing as they require a fourth member.
Lily Schechner moves into the town with her therapist mother, Helen, to live with Helen's new boyfriend Adam Harrison and his three sons, Jacob, Isaiah, and Abe.
The girls befriend Lily after she begins her period and bleeds through in class, then is mocked by her other classmates, particularly by the school bully Timmy Andrews.
They are amazed when she telekinetically pushes Timmy into the lockers.
When Lily responds to them using only her mind, the girls confirm her to be their fourth member and invite her to join their coven, to which she agrees.
As a result, they succeed in freezing time.
To seek revenge on Timmy, the girls cast a spell on him.
The next day, Timmy behaves sensitively, confirming the girls' success.
They continue to experiment with their powers, including levitation.
Adam learns of the incident in school and scolds Lily, but Helen defends her.
Lily overhears them arguing and goes outside where Abe talks to her about his father's authoritarian beliefs.
Timmy hosts a party, inviting the coven, and apologizes to Lily, eventually becoming friends with the coven.
When Timmy is at Lily's home for a project with Jacob, he admits to the girls that he had sex with Isaiah, Jacob's elder brother and that he is bisexual.
Later, Lily places a love spell on Timmy, using his sweatshirt, and the two kiss.
The next morning, during class, the coven is told by their teacher that Timmy allegedly committed suicide the night before.
Lily opens up to her friends about her kiss and love spell.
They sever ties with her and bind themselves from magic.
Lily suspects Adam to be dangerous and asks her mother for them to move out, but she does not agree.
In hopes of finding something against Adam, she searches his office only to find her own adoption papers, forcing Helen to admit to her that Lily is actually one of her psychotherapy patient's child.
After Timmy's funeral, Helen tells Lily she agrees to move out.
Helen also admits that she knows about her powers of telepathy, telekinesis, and magic.
The conversation prompts Helen to ask Lily to give her powers to Helen.
When Lily grows suspicious of her, Helen shapeshifts into Adam who had disguised himself with his own magic.
Adam tells her he is a member of a pagan cult and that he has been after her powers since the beginning, before knocking her unconscious.
Lily awakens in a forest at night with Adam, who confesses that he murdered Timmy and threatens to kill her too.
When Timmy's spirit contacts Lily's friends through a Ouija board and tells them about being murdered by Adam, they arrive to save Lily.
They try to freeze time, but Adam subdues them quickly.
The girls then work together and use their elemental powers to defeat Adam, burning him to death.
Later, Lily continues her friendship with the girls and Helen takes her to a mental health hospital to meet her birth mother, who is revealed to be Nancy Downs.

79596177.title: Hellfire Across the Pacific (film)
synopsis: Nestled within the South Pacific's sapphire blue expanse lies the pristine archipelago of Fiji, where tranquility and isolation reign supreme in untouched glory.
However, the serenity is abruptly pierced as crisp footprints imprint on the sandy island shores.
The saga unfolds with Jack Carson's arrival, a newly appointed army lieutenant, who brings with him a maelstrom of changes and a gust of unforeseen events.
Without missing a beat, Jack leaps headfirst into his new role, dedicating his earliest moments to bond with his freshly assigned crew.
He is soon introduced to Staff Sergeant Smith Johnson, a man whose chest is a canvas of numerous commendation medals.
As Jack immerses himself in the foreign surroundings, a fascinating mentor-mentee dynamic starts unraveling between him and Johnson.
Just as Jack begins to see the depth of Johnson's experience and insightful mentoring, disaster threatens their budding relationship.
The discovery of Johnson’s brutally murdered body near their base's perimeter sends shockwaves through the platoon.
Jack, in particular, is profoundly affected, and a pulsating thirst for justice starts brewing within him.
The military discipline ingrained in him nudges Jack to wait for official orders before taking any action.
However, his loyalty towards his fallen comrade urges him to embark on a personal, non-sanctioned quest for justice.
Abandoning the safety of the fortified sand barricades, Jack plunges into the hostile jungles of the island.
Exploring more, he discovers scattered remnants like a shredded uniform and spent shell casings – telltale signs of a clandestine enemy lurking within the heart of the wild, untamed island.
His mission expands beyond avenging Johnson’s death to unmasking and intercepting any broader implications related to war crimes happening under the veil of this concealed enemy.
As Jack ventures deeper, the quiet dangers of the rainforest come alive in a clear display of adversity.
Pushed to his limits, Jack's resilient spirit surfaces more prominently, proving the extent of his unwavering determination and bravery to seek justice despite the rising odds.
One humid afternoon, during his daring penetration deeper into the rainforest, he exposes a chilling scheme.
While aggressively investigating Johnson’s murder, he stumbles upon evidence that hints at treachery within his platoon.
Unwavering in his dedication, Jack employs his tactical brilliance to trace the traitors' steps methodically, further solidifying their connection to Johnson's brutal murder.
Armed with irrefutable proof, he reveals the traitors' deeply rooted, sinister motives to his commander.
His audacious bravery surprises the enemy, allowing him to launch a victorious counterstrike that effectively knocks the traitors off balance.
Amid the chaotic stage of urgent battle, Jack gradually gains the upper hand against the enemy forces, pushing them towards a demoralized retreat.
His triumphant reprisal changes the course of the unfolding war.
Despite the shower of accolades and praises, the mental scars etched deep within him from the war refuse to fade, their existence evident in his haunted eyes' depths.
Amid the grandiose parades and elaborate welcome, his mind remains inexorably tethered to the war's gruesome memories he left behind.
The residual guilt, regret, and trauma gnaw at Jack’s very being, slowly shaping him into a man scarred and hardened by the brutalities of war.

58419210.title: The Devil All the Time (film)
synopsis: During World War II, while serving in the Solomon Islands, U.S. Marine Willard Russell finds Gunnery Sergeant Miller Jones skinned and crucified by Japanese soldiers.
Willard ends Jones's agony by shooting him with a nearby Luger pistol.
After the war, on his way home to Coal Creek, West Virginia, Willard passes through Meade, Ohio, where he meets Charlotte, a waitress at a diner, and a photographer named Carl Henderson.
Willard and Charlotte marry and move to Knockemstiff, Ohio, where they have a son, whom they name Arvin.
In 1950, Helen Hatton marries Roy Laferty.
Roy is a bizarre, albeit charismatic, evangelical preacher who pours venomous spiders over his head while giving sermons to demonstrate his faith in God.
Helen and Roy have a daughter named Lenora.
During a sermon, Roy is bitten by a spider on his face and has a severe allergic reaction that affects his grip on reality, coming to believe that he can resurrect the dead.
Roy takes Helen out in the woods and stabs her in the neck with a screwdriver before trying and failing to resurrect her.
A distraught Roy hitchhikes and is picked up by Carl Henderson and his wife Sandy, that met at the same time and place Willard and Charlotte did.
Carl and Sandy are revealed to be serial killers who pick up male hitchhikers and encourage them to have sex with Sandy while Carl takes photographs before murdering them.
Roy refuses to have sex with Sandy but Carl kills him anyway.
In 1957, Charlotte is diagnosed with cancer.
Willard believes he can influence God with fervent prayer to remove the cancer from his wife's body.
He prays to God and sacrifices Arvin's dog on a rustic cross he had erected in the woods behind his house.
Charlotte dies despite his efforts, and Willard commits suicide by slitting his throat; his death is investigated by Sandy's brother, corrupt Sheriff Lee Bodecker.
Arvin, now orphaned, goes to live with his grandmother Emma, who has also adopted Lenora.
In 1965, Arvin - now a young adult working manual jobs around town - is given Willard's Luger as a birthday present.
He is fiercely protective of high school-aged Lenora who is bullied by some local greasers, prompting Arvin to one day attack and beat them all mercilessly.
Lenora grows close to the new, narcissistic Reverend Preston Teagardin, whom Arvin resents for previously ridiculing Emma.
The pedophilic Preston grooms Lenora and she becomes pregnant.
When she informs Preston, he denies her.
Overwhelmed by her bullying and pregnancy, Lenora hangs herself, though she briefly reconsiders.
After the autopsy, Arvin is told that she was pregnant and deduces that Preston was the father.
He follows Preston and sees him grooming another girl.
Alone at church together, Arvin confronts Preston about Lenora and shoots and kills him with the Luger before fleeing.
Arvin decides to hitchhike to his childhood home in Knockemstiff and is picked up by Carl and Sandy, whose relationship has become acrimonious.
Realizing Carl's intentions, Arvin kills them both in self-defense.
He finds evidence of their serial killings and takes some of it with him.
Lee learns about her murder and, to protect himself and his coming reelection, goes to Carl and Sandy's apartment where he finds and burns Carl's photo collection.
Investigating Carl's and Sandy's deaths, Lee eventually concludes it was Arvin, who has gone to bury his dog at Willard's cross.
Lee tracks Arvin there and, armed with a shotgun, attempts to kill him and get revenge.
A shootout ensues and Arvin shoots Lee in the stomach with the Luger.
As Lee dies, Arvin plants his copy of the evidence of Carl and Sandy's killing spree so it can be revealed.
As Preston's death is also uncovered, Arvin hitchhikes out of the area with a hippie headed to Cincinnati.
As they drive off, Arvin falls asleep and contemplates his future, which he imagines will be very similar to Willard's.

55684595.title: The Iron Vein of Boulder Ridge
synopsis: As the first rays of the sun pierce the sky, etching streaks of gold against the predawn grey, the bustling activity at the Boulder Ridge Iron Ore Quarry resumes.
A group of rugged miners, their faces obscured by dust and grit, strap on their hard hats and adjust their safety harnesses.
Jack, the foreman, a man who wears his years in the industry on his weathered face, stands huddled over the sprawled-out blueprint of the mine.
As the drills begin their relentless assault into the terracotta-soaked earth, they unexpectedly run into a resisting structure.
The workers retrieve a shimmering vein of iron ore under the incandescent light of their headlamps.
Sam, the resident geologist of the team, inspects the unusual iron ore.
While Sam dives into his research, the rest of the crew continue the drilling operations, hoping this find might be valuable.
When the first chisel pierces the silver vein, an eerie howl echoes through the quarry followed by a chilling gust that rustles past the miners, causing their lanterns to flicker.
Following this, a series of unexplainable events unfold.
Key mining equipment disappears only to reappear in unlikely places and unnerving sounds echo throughout the mine.
Heightening the miners' anxiety, Fred, a weathered mining fixture who had spent most of his life at Boulder Ridge, disappears without a trace.
Jack and Sam decide to investigate the strange occurrences by descending into the lesser-explored sections of the mine.
They discover a worn-out journal covered in layers of dust.
Under the shaky light of their torches, they decipher the fading, archaic text and a ghost story unfolds from within those pages, detailing the mine's eerie past.
The journal spins a tale of a malevolent ethereal creature imprisoned within the unusual iron vein they've accidentally disturbed.
Overwhelmed, they seek the counsel of Agnes, an elderly local woman known for her knowledge of the paranormal.
Agnes confirms their worst fears and gives them instructions for ancient protective rituals.
Meanwhile, the haunting intensifies and the once thriving mine is now a chilling abode of dread.
The miners form a united front, assisting Agnes in setting up the protective barriers to ward off the invisible foe.
Despite the escalating threat, they devise a plan to trick the vengeful entity back into its iron prison.
United in purpose, they chant incantations and together, they manage to imprison the spirit back into the vein of iron.
With the vein once again quiet, the surviving quarrymen are left grappling with a whirlwind of conflicted feelings from their harrowing ordeal.
They solemnly swear to respect the seal forever, safeguarding against any future disruptions.
Whispers of their horrific plight echo through their mining community and flow into neighboring towns, carried by waves of awe and terror.
The tale of Boulder Ridge's Gleaming Iron Vein outlives its protagonists, becoming a haunting reminder echoing through time.

67947600.title: The Devil Below
synopsis: A mining crew is leaving the Shookum Hills Coal Mine.
A man named Schuttmann and his son Derek are talking about a coworker who is not being safe.
Derek is attempting to persuade his father to give their coworker another chance when he is suddenly attacked by an unknown creature.
Schuttmann attempts to save Derek, but the creature stabs him in the shoulder, paralyzing him.
A bloodied Derek is taken away as he screams.
Years later, a team of scientists—Darren, Shawn, Terry, and Jaime—led by an adventurer named Arianne, are searching for Shookum Hills and its coal mine.
The town hasn't been placed on maps since the 1970s, and its population has also seemingly vanished.
It's believed that the disappearance is related to an underground coal fire that resulted in sinkholes opening up around the town.
Darren, the team leader, believes that the fires were started by a rare mineral.
The group stops at a store and Arianne goes inside to buy supplies and ask for directions to Shookum Hills.
The proprietor claims that he has never heard of Shookum Hills; when Arianne presses the issue, he tells her to go back the way she came.
As the team leaves the store, the proprietor warns an unknown party that there is a problem.
As the team leaves the store, another car begins following them.
Arianne successfully eludes the pursuers, and the team finds a dirt road blockaded by an electrical fence.
They break through the fence and discover the abandoned Shookum Hills Mine.
Though delighted by their find, they are puzzled to discover a sinkhole covered by an improvised electrified fence.
They break through the barrier and lower sensors into the hole to establish a picture of the tunnels beneath.
Terry is suddenly dragged into the sinkhole.
Arianne and Jaime descend into the sinkhole to try and find Terry, but cannot locate him.
Darren and Shawn are confronted by an angry local named Dale, who demands to know why they opened the sinkhole cover.
Frightened, they knock him unconscious.
Once Arianne returns, she tells them that there are monstrous creatures in the tunnels.
The group flees into the woods, losing Shawn in the process.
Dale is also killed, after reporting that the sinkhole has been breached.
Darren, Arianne, and Jaime are rescued by a group of locals led by Schuttman, who used to own the mines.
He reveals that the mines are home to monsters that are the true reason the town disappeared.
The surviving townsfolk have remained behind to keep the creatures contained.
Arianne volunteers to go back with two locals, Ellroy and Shelby, to show them the sinkhole they opened.
Darren and Jaime choose to accompany her.
The creatures ambush them, and Ellroy sacrifices himself to draw them off.
The rest of the group escapes into the tunnels.
Shelby also chooses to distract the creatures, telling Arianne and the two men to flee.
Jaime attempts to kill some of the creatures with a grenade, only for one of them to attack him and knock the grenade out of his hand.
He is killed when it detonates.
Exhausted and distraught, Darren tells Arianne that this expedition was not to map out the geographical area as he had led her to believe.
He is being paid by a coal mining company that wants the rare mineral in the caves.
He refuses to go on and Arianne leaves, promising to bring help back.
She reaches the surface, but is surprised and captured by one of the creatures, which knocks her out with a paralytic venom.
She awakens briefly to see that she is on a raft being steered by one of the creatures, along with Shelby's corpse.
When they reach the creatures' lair, she is reunited with Darren and Shawn, both of whom have also been captured.
Shawn notes that the creatures are a species which breeds and colonizes like ants or bees.
He is then fed to the queen creature, which is a bloated, immobile hulk.
The creatures attempt to feed Arianne to the queen, but she recovers from the venom and uses a grenade Darren gave her to kill the queen.
She and Darren escape and begin to climb up a rope at the entrance, but one of the creatures follows them and attacks Darren.
Arianne gives him a knife to fight back, but the creature manages to poison him.
He chooses to cut the rope instead, saving Arianne at the cost of his own life.
The locals arrive, and one of them is about to cut the rope and doom Arianne, only for Schuttman to stop him and help her escape.
The locals use a flamethrower and rifles to drive the creatures back into the tunnels.
Afterwards Schuttmann is driving Arianne back to the outside of the fence.
He tells her about the death of his son and asks her to help them keep the creatures from escaping.
While she's unsure that they can overcome the monsters, she reluctantly agrees to help.

33340059.title: Guardian in Bucharest
synopsis: The film commences within the debriefing room nestled in the heart of the Federal Government's massive Central Intelligence Complex, where Lieutenant Julia Thompson is given a manila envelope containing critical mission documents relating to her next assignment - the arduous task of safeguarding the life of a diplomat's son.
Having reviewed the orders, Julia boards the international flight UA50 heading out to Bucharest, Romania.
As the plane takes flight, her mind is filled with details of the mission and the individual she's charged with protecting.

Stepping foot into Bucharest, she spearheads a rendezvous with the local police chief and the diplomatic liaison officer who equip her with crucial insights into the city's political and security situation.
Absorbing the city's nuances, Julia makes an earnest effort to learn rudimentary Romanian and understands the political factions governing Romania to ensure her acclimatization.
Julia's initial rendezvous with ten-year-old Alex Petrovic, the diplomat's son and her assignment, marks the core of her mission.
Initially wary of Julia's presence, Alex gradually succumbs to her amiable calmness, and a bond begins to form between the officer and the protected.

The screen also witnesses the introduction of other notable characters - the strict chief of local police, Julia's stern and no-nonsense boss back at the CIA, and a swath of unknown figures looming in the shadows.
The second act gets a dramatic momentum as Alex's convoy journeying to a secure location faces an ambush.
Amid the chaos of this sudden wave of violence, Julia's agile command over the situation is highlighted as she manages to safeguard the convoy and prevent harm to Alex.
Though Julia manages to stave-off the dire attack, the incident underlines the potent threat that Alex faces, turning Julia's inherent protective instinct towards the child into an impervious armor.
Holding duty close to her, Julia reviews the mission at hand, her determination hardening at the thought of future harm befalling Alex.
A high-speed chase winds through Bucharest's streets, with Julia maneuvering a black Range Rover.
One of Julia's trusted team members, Victor, jeopardizes their mission through a shocking assassination attempt on Alex, instability and tension within the team.
Victor's unexpected treachery induces tension within the team, gnawing away at their established mutual trust, and putting the mission at risk.
Susception festers as the team's dynamics begin to sway perilously, with Julia caught under the crosshairs of doubt and skepticism.
Act three introduces a strained atmosphere within their covert safehouse, a meticulously preserved century-old Villa hidden in Bucharest.
Julia, now alone in her fight, grapples with pervasive untrustiness towards her team members.
Throughout these trials and tribulations, Julia's companionship with Alex grows stronger.
As the climax draws near, Julia stumbles upon a potent piece of evidence that potentially reveals a traitor within her ranks.
As suspicions begin narrowing due to the mounting evidence, the team unifies under Julia's leadership.
In the backdrop of escalating tensions, Julia plans a secretive operation to transport Alex beyond Bucharest's city limits to the security of a fortified NATO base.
The culmination of her efforts is evidenced during an epic showdown between Julia and Victor in the heart of Bucharest.
Due to Julia's strategic finesse, Victor's escape routes are blocked leading to his imminent capture.
After her teammate Jack's untimely death, Julia ensures Alex's successful extraction from the city, completing her mission.
The film edges towards an end with parting scenes, including Julia's bittersweet goodbye with Alex.
Upon returning to the U.S, Julia receives a warm welcome from her superior, director Harrison.
News reports about Operation 'Protector' reveal Julia's achievements in Bucharest.
Julia's superiors laud her persistent courage and strategic brilliance.
Returning to her high-tech briefing room, Julia exudes a sense of experience and wisdom.
She receives another classified mission named 'Phoenix'.
Julia's comrades regard her with awe.
As Julia walks down the agency hallway, the silent respect from her colleagues palpably follows her.
The film concludes with an image of Julia.
A note scribbled in a child's handwriting, a heartfelt 'Thank you, Julia', lies on her desk against a stack of mission documents, serving as a memento of her mission in Bucharest.
The screen fades off showcasing Julia's silhouette against the monumental background of the CIA Headquarters.

64652289.title: The Doorman (2020 film)
synopsis: In Bucharest, U.S. Marine Gunnery Sergeant Alexandra “Ali” Gorski is tasked to protect a convoy carrying the daughter of the ambassador.
Armed mercenaries ambush them, and although Ali fights fiercely and effectively, the mercenaries are still able to kill the ambassador, his wife and their daughter.
Ali leaves the Marines and returns to New York City.
Her uncle, Pat, tells her of a job in The Carrington Hotel in New York City where he works.
Ali is hired, working alongside another doorman, Borz.
She finds out that her late sister’s husband, Professor Jon Stanton, and his two children, Max and Lily, live there.
Jon and Ali had an affair during the marriage, which she fled by joining the Marines.
She is invited to their Easter dinner.
Over the Easter holiday, Borz kills Pat with a sledgehammer, revealing that Borz has been disguised as a doorman to search for valuable paintings hidden in the hotel.
A group of mercenaries led by Victor Dubois arrive and initiate a lockdown.
Dubois, Borz, and his men invade the apartment of Bernard Hersch, who suffers akinetic mutism.
Dubois knew Bernard as Erich Dreischler and asks where the paintings are.
When Bernard does not speak, Borz stabs him in the hand, finally bringing Bernard around, even though he cannot recall the whereabouts of the paintings.

When Bernard’s wife explains that they moved from 10 C after Bernard's stroke seven years earlier, the mercenaries leave for 10C — now occupied by the Stantons — before Borz kills Bernard and his wife.
Dubois and his men arrive at 10C and hold Jon and Lily hostage, while Max, seeing the men already inside, runs away.
Dubois eventually discovers the hidden safe containing the paintings and has Martinez use a water cooled drill to bypass the combination code.
Jon attempts to distract Dubois by having a glass of wine to allow Lily to use Dubois’ laptop to call for help via Facebook, but Borz catches her and Dubois forces her to delete the message.
After discovering the Hersch couple's corpses and Borz’s betrayal, Ali kills one henchman and runs into Max.

Ali and Max activate the fire alarm to summon the fire department but as Ali tries to alert them, two other henchmen catch the two and the firefighters find nothing amiss and leave after Borz explains that it was a false alarm.
After Ali kills another henchman, Max is separated and is recaptured and brought to 10C.
Dubois calls Ali on PA system, ordering her to surrender herself.
Seeing the water hose is connected to the drill bit, Max surreptitiously sends the Morse code on PA system to message Ali to disable the main valve of the water supply.
Leo is killed by the nail bomb set by Ali while attempting to turn the water back on, destroying the main valve as well.
Dubois radios her and threatens to kill the family if Ali refuses to restore the water supply.
Ali agrees and, with corrupt NYPD officer Olsen (Dubois’ cohort) holding her at gunpoint, connects a hose to the rooftop water tank.
The safe is opened, revealing the paintings.

After Jon mentions that the art is worth hundreds of millions rather than $5 million Dubois had told them, Borz renegotiates that 50% of the proceeds will go to Dubois while the remaining men, Martinez and Borz, will each receive a share of 25%.
Ali kills Olsen and rushes to 10C, where she holds Martinez hostage.
Borz wounds Jon and kills Martinez to increase his share to 50%.
As the police arrive at the scene, Borz dresses as a doorman to walk past the police and pins the blame on Ali, who incapacitates the officers and chases Borz.
As they walk through a sewer, Borz turns on Dubois and kills him.
Ali fights Borz and finally kills him with a grenade.
Sometime later, Ali bids farewell to Jon and the children, who are heading to London.

10473018.title: The Standby Stanford
synopsis: Luke, the celebrated valedictorian of Jefferson High School, felt a rush of exhilaration as each acceptance letter from the nation's premier Ivy League universities – Harvard, Yale, Princeton, among others – arrived in the mail.
Each envelope, embossed in gold lettering, served as an evidence of Luke's earnest studious dedication.
However, upon tearing open the Stanford University envelope - his first preference all along - he found himself relegated to the position of waitlisted candidate.
His heart plunged into an ocean of disappointment, dishearteningly eclipsing his array of impressive acceptances.
The sting of this letdown was intense, like the fury of a menacing thunderstorm, threatening to overshadow his otherwise remarkable achievements.
His jubilant parents - Paul and Martha - planned to throw an extravagant celebration at their tasteful suburban home, a feast to honor Luke's extraordinary academic victories.
The party was an opulent event, replete with ornamental decorations, overflowing with champagne, a gourmet buffet, and a generous sprinkling of well-wishers – family, friends, neighbors.
Each attendee heaping praises upon Luke.
Yet, even amidst the fanfare, Luke couldn’t discard the despair of his Stanford setback.
Immersed in his solitary corner of challenging calculus problems, intricate physics theories, and leading his treasured debate club, Luke felt isolated.
The weight of the expectations - from his parents and the community, felt increasingly burdensome on his slender shoulders.
The amalgamation of societal pressure and his unfulfilled Stanford aspiration ignited an internal struggle in Luke, forcing him to question his self-worth beyond his academic prowess.

In a desperate yearning to escape the demanding environment of Jefferson City, Luke suggested an impromptu road trip to his closest allies - Sarah, an eloquent, budding journalist, and Jake, a proficient and ambitious athlete.

The idea was welcomed with open arms, and their old, faithful Ford was hastily packed with essential supplies, setting a promising foreground for an odyssey that would carve their personal transitions.
Along their course, they halted at a minimalist homestead in the rustic backwoods of Wyoming.
The inhabitants were an industrious family subsisting entirely off the grid, rejoicing in the simplicity of their self-sustaining farm and solar-paneled dwelling.
They seemed blissful, lacking high-speed internet, advanced technology, or even suburban comforts that Luke unconsciously considered necessities.
He found their lifestyle intriguing.
The journey continued to unfold unexpected events.
In Hailey, Idaho, they found themselves helping out in a charming diner, 'Idaho Golden Pancakes', after their skillful cook had been put out of commission by the seasonal flu.

Luke found unexplainable joy, flipping fluffy pancakes and indulging in pleasant casual conversation with the cozy, inviting diner's regulars, a way of life that sharply contrasted with his previous stress-inducing academic environment.
These impromptu detours and experiences brought about a radical change in Luke's perception, making him question his previous notion of what was truly important in his life.
Back in their now too empty house, Paul and Martha deeply contemplated and acknowledged the undue pressure they had unintentionally inflicted on their son.
Resolved to rectify their parenting style, they committed to become a more supportive and understanding safety-net for Luke, fully appreciating their own shortcomings in the process.
The fruits of this self-introspection led them to solemnly vow to change their approach, a shared journey they were ready to embark upon, much like their son's voyage of personal development.
In an ironic twist of fate, their road trip unintentionally led them to Stanford, coincidently on the very day their waitlist was releasing.
Luke logged into their online portal, albeit surprisingly calm, unflusteredly prepared to accept whatever outcome awaited him.
He carefully scrolled down the list of admitted candidates, finding his absence met his preconceived assumptions.
His parents arrived, breathless and distressed, prepared to assuage his disappointment, only to find his serenity surprisingly soothing.
Luke acknowledged their words of solace, however, his newfound contentment didn't crave approval or validation any longer.
Describing his chance encounters, the road trip experiences and his transformed emotions, he detailed the liberation he felt while learning from life itself.
This heartfelt revelation inspired valuable insights for both his parents and Luke himself, redefining their collective understanding of their own definitions of success.
Touched by their son's experiences, Paul and Martha committed themselves to evolve, learn, and grow – for their own betterment, and more importantly for Luke's benefit.
Embracing a renewed perspective towards education and life, Luke entered the venerable corridors of Harvard University.
He indulged in his academic interests, signed up for various events and initiated new friendships.
Each aspect of his life at Harvard brought joy, contentment, and a newfound enthusiasm to Luke.
As the summer break approached, Luke decided to honor the tradition he unwittingly began.
He dialed Sarah and Jake, extending the proposal for another summer road trip across the country.
They immediately accepted, their reminiscences of their previous adventure adding to their excitement for another summer filled with exploration and self-realization.
His parents bid him farewell, reminding him to treat his life as an open book, to learn, to experience, to grow.
Their words of encouragement echoing in his mind, Luke eagerly awaited the adventures that lay ahead.
Luke, appreciating the subtleties of life more maturely now, recognized that the end destination often mattered less than the invaluable experiences picked up along the journey.

The movie closes with the iconic shot of their car disappearing into the vastness of the Nevada desert, symbolizing the boundless aspirations that lay before them - their laughter, camaraderie, and the anticipation of an unforgettable summer echoing into the nothingness.

69502739.title: The F**k-It List
synopsis: Brett Blackmore's pushy parents are excitedly celebrating his acceptance into 7 out of 8 Ivy League schools (including bragging to their friends, the school, the local paper) with Harvard being the only one he is wait-listed for.

When his friends—Nico (Karan Brar), Clint (Marcus Scribner), Les (Tristan Lake Leabu), and Stacy (Amanda Grace Benitez)—take him to break into the school to play a benign prank, they accidentally blow up one of the buildings.
He is the only one identified from this and, as a result, he loses his acceptance.

After sharing a brief kiss with Kayla (interrupted by the brash Ted) he records a video ranting about being forced down a path he didn't choose, including a 'fuck-it list' of things he wishes he had done if he wasn't scared it would affect his future.
He posts it to his friendship group but accidentally posts it publicly.
The post goes viral on a small scale (1000+ views overnight).
His parents scheme to get him accepted by Harvard, including making advances to their friend (Peter Facinelli) who is also a board member of Harvard.
Kayla appreciates Brett's list and says that she needs his help to start checking items off of the one she's made as a result.
This involves smashing the expensive Mustang belonging to her mother's alcoholic and abusive boyfriend, which she says she never had the guts to do before Brett's post.
The boyfriend spots them and they drive off and spend a cute day together, including discussion of their mutual lists and Brett's public performance of "Wild Thing" on Venice Beach.
Kayla is signed to Ted's dad's modeling agency, where she will be working in Europe over the summer to afford school, but she has to entertain the annoying Ted as a result.
Kayla reveals she has nowhere to go after smashing the car, and Brett refuses to help her in service of getting 'back on track.'
She storms off but does later post a good-luck message to him.
His list continues to gain traction online in the meantime, which affects his meeting with the principal and results in his inability to graduate high school.
His parents berate him and he drives off in his dad's car to the Rocks to meet his friends.
They spread the word and a large number of other teenagers turn up to burn their school books together.
The fire builds attention for the list and he is called by a PR representative (King Bach) to help him monetise it.
The police turn up to reveal he could be considered as inciting crime.
The dean of Harvard calls Barry to say that she wants to offer him a place as an iconoclast and disruptor.
Meanwhile, Kayla finally agrees to see Brett and they make up.
Brett has to write an essay to gain entry to Harvard, but he seems uninspired by it.
He drops in on his friends' graduation to learn that Kayla's mother's boyfriend pressed charges for smashing up his car.
Upon learning from Les that Dee was previously a valedictorian, he turns his Harvard essay into a new rant about the education system and success, rejecting them.
His mother opens up to him, apologizing for pushing him and saying that they are on board with his decisions.
Brett hits 3 million followers and Harvard says they loved his essay, offering him a place.

Shortly after Kayla is told that in order to work in the industry she will need to attend to rich clients, Brett arrives in Spain to persuade her to travel with him instead (after rejecting Harvard again) which she is happy to do—both subscribing to the 'fuck-it' attitude.
Brett tells Kayla that he was offered a visiting professorship.

20266107.title: The Distressed (2021 film)
synopsis: Our first introduction to Officer John Smith portrays him as a seasoned NYPD veteran, with an extensive service record and a proven reputation for his astuteness and bravery.
Smith is a respected figure in New York's 45th Precinct, an idol for the fresh-faced rookies and a go-to guy for the most perilous tasks.
However, his mental strength is severely tested following the tragic demise of his partner, Officer Darren Richards, a man who was his closest confidant and friend for over a decade.
Officer Richards' untimely death wasn't just another consequence of New York's rampant crime scenes.
He lost his life right in the line of duty, during an aggressive crack down on a notorious drug syndicate, casting a somber hush in the previously frenzied precinct.

However, whispers of fresh evidence and possible discrepancies associated with his death soon begin to echo through the silent halls, prompting the reopening of his case and prompting a meticulous inquiry.
As the probe unfolds, slowly and steadily, Smith finds himself entangled in a web of doubt.

With each unearthed detail contradicting the original narrative of Richards' death, Smith's conviction in the justice is system is mightily shaken, breaking him away from the reality he had for so long believed in.
Smith's professional life takes a treacherous turn as Officer Daniel O'Reilly, his superior and a notoriously skeptical Lieutenant, takes the reins and repositions Smith.
His energetic outdoor patrol routines are replaced with monotonously quiet, graveyard shifts in the NYPD's 911 communication center.
During a predictably quiet midnight shift, a jarring call pierces the silence.
The distressed voice at the other end belongs to an unidentified teenage girl from Brooklyn, who hints at a possible grave danger.
The raw panic in the girl's voice, her deliberately vague location information, and her cryptic conversation sparks a fierce suspicion in Smith.
It triggers a dormant part of his investigative instincts, long diluted by the lingering horrors of Richards' death.

Engaging with his rekindled detective senses, Smith starts drawing connections between the mysterious caller and the infamous "Grimm Reaper"; a serial killer that had been terrorizing the city's back alleys without ever leaving enough clues for an identification.
Smith becomes engrossed in a self-set mission, tailing the faint imprints left behind by the disturbed call and connecting them to the broader case.
Ignoring the limitations of his isolated duty, he delves deeper into the territory of the Grimm Reaper, aided by the countless unsolved crime case files lying untouched in his new makeshift office.
As he meticulously combs through the chilling tales scribed within these files, Smith uncovers a frightening correlation.
The seemingly random victims chosen by the Grimm Reaper hold uncanny similarities to the circumstances surrounding Richards' tragic shooting.
This fresh revelation whirls Smith's world into a vortex of doubt and distrust.

He begins to believe that the perpetrators could be from within his cherished department, staging an intricate charade to camouflage their deeds, painting the unsuspecting criminal world as the culprit.
Smoldering with a determination to discern the shadowy truth, Smith goes beyond his limited authority and indulges in an impassioned investigation mired in uncertainty and danger.

Leveraging his cordial relationships with young rookies and rookie officers within the NYPD, Smith embarks on a dangerous whirlwind of events, trying to unravel the convoluted conspiracy haunting the precinct.
However, snooping around for the truth in an environment rippling with deceit doesn't go unnoticed.
The senior officers within the department soon raise an eyebrow at Smith's activities.
Consequently, Smith's unsanctioned investigation is exposed by an unexpected internal affairs probe, threatening his otherwise untarnished service record.
His colleagues now reject and ridicule him, alienating the once-revered officer.
Despite the professional setback, Smith's spirit remains unbroken.
The suspension only serves him with more time, allowing Smith to delve deeper into the controversial investigation.
Smith finds a brusque ally in his dreaded dispatch duty.

The countless hours of combing emergency calls, coupled with the freedom offered by his current suspension, afford him the unique advantage of linking the reported incidents to the ongoing murder spree.
In an awe-inspiring display of masterly analysis, Smith tracks down the mysterious caller to a neglected apartment building concealed within the forgotten corner of Brooklyn.
Being no stranger to peril, Smith ventures alone into the intimidating, dilapidated apartment complex.
With each creaky step deeper into the building's ominous belly, Smith hopes to expose the icy anonymity of the Grimm Reaper.
Confronted by the grim reality of the apartment's inhabitable condition, Smith is hit by a sense of familiarity.
As the chilling details begin to weave together, he finally encounters the shadowy figure responsible for the escalating citywide panic.
His spine feels a chilling wave of fear and recognition as he confronts the murderer; his trusted confidante, Officer Jack Carter, stained with the guilt of Richards' unfortunate demise.
Overwhelmed by the horrifying realization, Smith's usual composure crumbles, and he finds himself face-to-face with Carter, in a tense standoff fueled by a surge of grief and anger.
Despite the alarming situation, Smith manages to subtly retreat from this confrontation.
He walks away from Carter, believing it vital to strategize his next move rather than bring the battle to an inconclusive head.
Armed with the ugly truth and a resilient will to expose it, Smith painstakingly assembles an array of irrefutable proof against Officer Carter, aiming to bring him to justice.
Over a painstaking fortnight, Smith toils day and night, putting together shreds of evidence, all pointing accusingly at Carter's heinous actions.
With an admirable display of patience and tenacity, Smith successfully lifts the shroud obscuring the truth.
The mystery that framed him for Richards' death and exonerates him from the false allegations, and implicates Carter as the prime suspect for the serial murders terrorizing the city.
Armed with the monumental evidence, he takes a bold step, presenting his findings to the shocked NYPD.
The incriminating proof against Carter leads to his immediate arrest, leaving the precinct in a state of shock and regret.
Despite being absolved from all damning accusations, Smith makes a surprising decision.
He elects to continue his service at the quiet dispatch center, now with a renewed sense of purpose, using his sharp instincts to aid distressed New Yorkers.

Having battled against vile criminals in the city's chaotic crime scene, Smith finds a newfound purpose in the subdued light of the dispatch office; offering solace and comfort to frightened callers in their most vulnerable moments.
As we bid farewell to our resilient hero, Smith exhibits a sense of tranquility despite his changed role.
He retains his hardened resolve, continuing to serve the city that has seen so many ups and downs alongside him.
However, this brief moment of respite is disrupted when another cryptic 911 call brings Smith back into action; a subtle hint of another potential threat brewing within the city’s underbelly.
The story concludes on an anticipatory note, suggesting a thrilling sequel.
We leave Smith, ready to unraveled the latest sinister challenge threatening the city he swears to protect.

Finally, the film ends on an ingenious cliffhanger, effectively setting the stage for a promising sequel, hinting at more thrilling disclosures and high-stakes confrontations in Smith's undeterred quest for justice.

65825243.title: The Guilty (2021 film)
synopsis: Troubled LAPD officer Joe Baylor works the night shift at a 911 call center while awaiting a court hearing for an incident that occurred on duty eight months prior.
He answers a call from Emily Lighton, a woman that reveals she has been abducted.
While traveling in a white van, Emily is forced to hang up before she can provide more details.
Joe relays the information to the California Highway Patrol, who cannot locate the van without a license plate number.
Joe calls Emily's home phone and speaks with her six-year-old daughter Abby, who tells him that her mom left the house with her dad, Henry Fisher.
After getting Henry's cell phone number from Abby, he is able to retrieve the van's plate number.
Joe also learns that Henry has a record of assault, so he calls Sergeant Miller to send a patrol unit to Emily's home to do welfare check on Abby and her baby brother, Oliver.
He also requests he send another to investigate Henry's apartment.
Miller refuses to send anyone to Henry's without a warrant.
Reminding Joe of his legal issues, Miller suggests he stop investigating.
Afterwards, Joe calls Henry and demands to know where he is taking Emily.
Henry hangs up after Joe starts asking questions in an accusatory tone.
Joe then calls his former partner, Rick, who is off-duty.
Joe asks him to go to Henry's house.
Rick complies, but also expresses concern about Joe's upcoming hearing at which he is set to provide testimony.
Joe receives a panicked call from Abby when two officers arrive at her home; he instructs her to let them in.
The officers notice blood on Abby and, upon searching the property, find Oliver in the bedroom either gravely injured or dead.
Joe calls Henry and accuses him of killing his son.
Henry hangs up again.
On the line again with Emily, Joe tells her to try to crash the van.
Emily makes an attempt, to no avail.
Meanwhile, Rick breaks into Henry's apartment and finds documents showing that Emily had recently been a patient in a psychiatric treatment facility in San Bernardino.
Back on the phone with Emily, she admits she thinks she will die and does not want to be locked up again.
Emily goes on to say that she believed Oliver had "snakes in his stomach" and that she "took them out."
Joe realizes that Emily was the one who hurt baby Oliver, and Henry is trying to have her readmitted to the psychiatric hospital.
Outside of the van, Emily hits Henry with a brick and runs away.
On the phone with Joe, Henry explains that she had been off her medication for a number of weeks, as they could not afford them.
Henry feels guilty about having left Emily, believing this triggered the psychotic episode during which she hurt Oliver.
Henry does not trust the police and the criminal justice system due to his own legal troubles and because of the many failed attempts by various government agencies to "help" his mentally ill wife.
Emily does not know what she has done and Henry fears what she will do after she finds out.
Eventually, Emily calls Joe back from a freeway overpass, while preparing to commit suicide.

Joe directs the CHP to her location while attempting to talk her down; he tries to distract her by revealing that he killed a 19-year-old while on duty because he was angry with him for hurting someone.
Joe tells Emily that Abby needs her and that he promised Abby she would come home.
As officers arrive, Emily hangs up.
After repeated attempts to call her back, Joe calls the CHP dispatcher who conveys that Emily is alive.
He then learns that baby Oliver is alive and in the hospital, recovering from his injuries.
An overcome Joe calls Rick and asks him to tell the truth at the hearing, even if it means he will spend years in prison.
Joe then announces to the media that he will plead guilty to a charge of manslaughter.

75979258.title: The Prankster's Triumph (2022 film)
synopsis: Nestled in the serene landscape of Falls Creek, a bespectacled 12-year-old cocoa-haired boy named Arthur Johnson finds his solace at his grand oak desk.
Surrounded by shelves brimming with age-old encyclopedias and expansive textbooks, he dives dutifully into the boundless ocean of knowledge, his dedication and thirst for learning almost tangible.
Arthur’s cerulean eyes light up with a vibrant spark, intensifying with every line he consumes from his treasured books, the written words, a delicious feast for his ever-curious mind.

Residing in a household helmed by two distinguished scholars lovingly known as "The Professors," owing to their esteemed doctoral degrees, Arthur is ingrained with the profound significance of academic excellence.
Bearing the weight of his parents' lofty expectations coupled with his personal ambitions, Arthur nurtures a dream of earning the esteemed title of valedictorian at the Falls Creek Middle School.
In stark contrast to Arthur's tranquil scholarly world is the flamboyant life of 13-year-old Scott Reed.

With a mischievous twinkle in his eyes and an infectious laugh, Scott, the school's resident master prankster, pulls off an ingenious stunt, trapping the principal's silver convertible in a swimming pool overflowing with a cascade of multicolored bouncy balls.

As the hilarious spectacle unfurls, the eruptive peals of laughter and enthusiastic applause from his classmates only further ignite Scott's innate appetite for mischief, solidifying his reputation as the unmatched class entertainer.
Upon catching wind of Arthur's escalating academic recognition, Scott senses a fun challenge and conceptualizes a humorously ingenious prank aimed at taking the scholarly Arthur down a peg or two.

On an exciting day at school, the unsuspecting Arthur delivers his rehearsed speech at the bustling cafeteria, which quickly succumbs to uproarious laughter as Arthur stands perplexed, drenched head to toe in fluorescent green slime, an unforeseen climax in Scott's masterful prank.
This public spectacle sparks a uniquely contrasting rivalry between the academically inclined Arthur and the light-hearted prankster, Scott.

As the Fall Creek Middle School gears up for the annual student council election, both Arthur and Scott add a thrilling twist by announcing their candidacy for the coveted position of student council president.

Arthur eloquently advocates the need for bolstered tutoring programs and a more intellectually stimulating environment, while Scott, true to his playful spirit, promises to saturate the school with more elaborate, laughter-provoking pranks.
Amidst the mounting anticipation, Scott's relentless practical jokes, while amusing to most, start disrupting the school's routine, causing a mild uproar.
The once orderly events, such as school assemblies, spiral into chaotic scenes of hilarity and confusion under Scott’s rule of mischief.

In a move marked with audacity, Scott takes his pranking spree up a notch and takes aim at his rival, Arthur, managing to hang Arthur's professionally designed campaign banner, a symbol of his earnest dedication, upside down in the school's main hallway.
Determined to reclaim his dignity, Arthur, always the strategist, meticulously plans a brilliant counter-prank to impugn Scott without resorting to physical harm.

The next day, the school ambience is filled with chuckles and gasps as Scott, in an unexpected role reversal, finds himself the victim of his own game, squirting water uncontrollably like a malfunctioning pipe.
The combined shock and laughter tip the rivalry in Arthur's favor as he begins to earn accolades for his clever, non-harmful retaliation to Scott's prank.
The ingenious prank gives a much-needed boost to Arthur's popularity, subtly changing his peers' perception of him from a conventional bookworm to an inventive, strategy-oriented individual.

Unable to resist, Scott aims to pull off another hilarious prank on Arthur but in a humorous twist of events, becomes the unsuspecting victim of his booby-trapped locker filled with explosive confetti, painting himself in a vibrant mess.
