Both Mary and Dickon hatch a plan to bring Colin to the garden, hoping to heal his immobility, but upon returning, Mrs Medlock confronts Mary for stealing the pearl necklace and she is punished by being signed up for a boarding school.
Later, confined and locked in her room, Mary finds letters between her mother and aunt in a rocking horse.
She persuades Colin to read them and the three continue reading letters in the garden.
A depressed and distracted Lord Craven, while lighting a candle, sets the desk on fire.
The next morning, Mary, Dickon and Colin are in the garden when they see black smoke coming from the house.
Colin persuades Mary and Dickon to run to check it out.
Mary enters the burning house to find Lord Craven frantically looking for his son in the fire.
She tries in vain to convince him to escape as his son is safe outside, but he resists until the ghost of his wife guides them out safely as the fire brigade arrives.
An anxious Lord Craven and Mrs Medlock go with Mary and Dickon to Colin in the secret garden.
Lord Craven gazes in awe at his son's mobility as they rekindle their relationship.
The film ends with Lord Craven rebuilding the estate and Mary, Dickon and Colin having fun in the secret garden.

37889357.title: The Absent Sanctuary
synopsis: John Thompson, a man haunted by stubborn traces of alcohol dependency, seeks refuge in his daughter's abandoned treehouse.

Despite being trapped within the iron claws of his addiction, he finds semblance of serenity in the noiseless whisper of the treehouse's worn-out wooden walls, which bear the desolate scars of time and neglect.
During an ordinary, aimless exploration of the treehouse, John’s worn-out boot scrubs against a concealed trapdoor.
Instantly, the secret doorway gives way plunging him into an icy labyrinth beneath the old oak tree’s hardened roots.
As he navigates the darkness of the underground maze, he stumbles upon ancient symbols carved with unnerving brutality into stone walls, revealing the silent whispers of past occult practices.

The sudden disappearance of Bethany Dunhill, the well-liked cheerleader of Stillwater High, rings the alarm bell within the quiet town, sowing seeds of icy fear and distressing uncertainty within the community.
Frank "Stoneface" Mendez, the toughened ex-marine-turned-local sheriff, zeroes in on the enigmatic John as the primary suspect.
Stillwater is soon blanketed in a chilling fog of suspicion, as the citizens begin questioning John’s unexplained solitude and mysterious lifestyle.
Disregarding the whirlpool of mistrust and finger-pointing, John unveils the dark secrets of the underground maze by following its haunting twists and turns.

The horrifying evidence of the cult’s atrocities and its spine-tingling connection with the town’s missing children starts to emerge from the obscure shadows of the labyrinth, establishing both a gut-wrenching horror and a tenacious resolution within John.
As the painful echo of his daughter’s abduction amalgamates with the innocent face of Bethany, John embarks on a personal mission to unearth and expose Stillwater’s chilling truths.
John stands on the precipice of two grueling wars: an embittered battle against his self-imploding addiction and an impending confrontation with the clandestine cult.
In a bid to expose the cult's horrifying reality, John hatches a dangerous scheme to infiltrate one of the cult's secret moonlit rituals.
However, his meticulously laid plans crumble to dust, revealing his covert presence to the cult's menacing members.
Almost instantaneously, John transitions from hunter to hunted, as the cult members mark him as their prey, seeking vengeance for his audacity.

Mustering every drop of courage from the core of his shattered spirit, John manages to set Bethany free from her nightmarish captivity, initiating a pulse-racing escape through the labyrinth's winding passages.
The relentless pursuit of the cult members echoes through the cold stone tunnels, their ominous footsteps amplifying the tension.
Meanwhile, Stillwater's local police force, now aware of the hidden horrors beneath the treehouse, storms into the oppressive abyss of the underground.
An explosive hostility unfurls in the underground battleground, as John, the police force, and the cult cross swords in a life-or-death confrontation blanketed by palpable tension.
Despite the overwhelming odds, John's unyielding bravery coupled with the police's steadfast dedication, triumph against the nefarious cult.
The horrifying revelation of the oak tree, the chilling tales of abducted children, and the cryptic resurgence of the cult jolts Stillwater into a muteness of shocked silence.
The unholy labyrinth beneath the treehouse is permanently sealed, closing the monstrous chapter of Stillwater's chilling folklore.
A cruel wave of closure washes over John as he encounters the haunting etch of his daughter's name on a cold, unfeeling stone.

Despite the heavy weight of personal loss, John renews his quest towards sobriety, vowing to pay homage to his dearly missed daughter by transforming his own life into a testament of survival and redemption.

62918772.title: The Silencing
synopsis: Alcoholic Rayburn Swanson is the owner of the Gwen Swanson Sanctuary, named after his missing daughter.
The sanctuary is an act of penance, both because Gwen disapproved of his trapper lifestyle and because she had disappeared from his car five years earlier while he went into a store to buy whiskey.
Rayburn keeps hunters out by using surveillance cameras.
Sheriff Alice Gustafson is the sister of a troubled young man, Brooks.
While examining the body of a young girl found by a lake, Alice notices a scar on the girl's throat, along with the point of a spear-head (marked with an “MB”) buried in a tree.
After learning about the body, Rayburn arrives to make a positive ID, but it is not Gwen.
Alice learns that the spear was used with a rare weapon known as an atlatl.
Rayburn sees a man in a ghillie suit stalking the woods; when Rayburn attempts to confront the man, he is wounded by a thrown spear.
While fleeing, he comes across a black pickup truck with the license plates removed.
He marks the truck by scratching a small 'x' on the fender.
After returning home and stitching his wound, he reviews his surveillance footage and observes a girl being hunted in the sanctuary by the same man.
Rayburn returns to the sanctuary and rescues the girl, Molly, then keeps her safe in an unused spike trap overnight.
She was rendered mute, having a throat scar similar to the one on the dead girl.
They make it back to the cabin the next evening but are ambushed by the hunter.
The hunter injures Rayburn and stabs Molly with a spear.
Alice arrives and, after seeing that Molly has been stabbed, immediately suspects Rayburn, until the hunter appears behind her.
Still disguised, his mannerisms cause her to believe it is her brother.
Alice shoots Rayburn, wounding him, and causing him to flee so that her brother can escape.
Alice searches for Rayburn and steps on a bear trap he had set, injuring her ankle.
He escapes in her patrol car and calls an ambulance for Molly; Alice calls for Rayburn's arrest.
He flees to the home of his former wife, Debbie, and her husband, Karl Blackhawk, Sheriff of the local Indian tribal police.
They take him to the "Factory", an abandoned mill where the homeless stay, and call Dr. Jon Boone to treat him.
Brooks coincidentally arrives and is arrested by Karl, although he has an alibi to establish his innocence.
Alice, realizing her moral failure, promises Molly, now hospitalized, that she will catch the killer.
She also noticed the same throat scar on Molly.
Rayburn decides to clean up and throw out his liquor, except for the still unopened bottle he bought on the day Gwen had gone missing.
He remembers the marked truck and locates it.
After breaking into a house, he finds the same weapons and clothes worn by the killer, along with a trove of "missing" posters, including one for his daughter.
After finding a still-living girl under a sheet with her throat surgically cut open, the killer appears and captures Rayburn by knocking him unconscious.
Alice notices issues with the autopsy report by Dr. Boone.
While waiting for him in his office, she sees a photo of the doctor with his daughter Melissa wearing a necklace with the initials "MB".
Alice realizes that Boone is the killer and immediately calls for backup to raid Boone's home; the same home Rayburn had found.

Boone explains to Rayburn that while grieving his own daughter, who had been killed by a drunk driver, he began kidnapping and killing teen girls to "save" them from bad parents, including Rayburn; he operates on the larynx so they cannot call for help while being hunted.
Boone takes Rayburn to the wildlife sanctuary and forces him to flee so that he can be hunted.
Alice sees Rayburn on the surveillance.
Rayburn overpowers Boone and is beating him severely as Alice arrives; she attempts to stop Rayburn, but he ignores her and throws Boone into one of the spike traps, mortally wounding him.
Alice looks on as Rayburn closes the doctor in, telling her that they are even (he had lied earlier, saying the intruder shot him instead of Alice).
She later sits in a patrol car, listening to the radio about the ongoing manhunt for Dr Boone.
Rayburn and his ex-wife have a funeral for Gwen, which Molly attends, providing him closure.
He then empties his last bottle of whisky into the lake in memory of his daughter.

52799304.title: The Manhattan Encounter
synopsis: Amelia Bennett, a reserved yet highly accomplished editor-in-chief of the influential 'Manhattan Herald', settles into her spacious luxury office when a noteworthy parcel arrives.
It is an eye-catching, meticulously wrapped package carefully bound by a lustrous silk ribbon supplies a stark contrast to the endless piles of news scripts on her desk.

A sense of intrigue washes over Amelia as she cautiously unravels the luxurious package, revealing an ingrained invitation to a grand New York soirée at an extravagant penthouse situated on the opulently prestigious Fifth Avenue.
The cryptic closure "Ethan Rodriguez" at the end of the invitation, kindles a flame of curiosity in her, nudging her to explore the enigma.

Her initial apprehension gives way to mild excitement as she shares the mysterious invitation with her vivaciously outgoing best friend and work colleague, Peter, who buzzes with infectious enthusiasm about attending the hailed event.

Finding herself intrigued by this sudden twist of events and Peter's determined eagerness, Amelia concedes to attend the gathering, leaning heavily on Peter for his unwavering support and bravery in social interactions.

Embracing the evening, she swathes herself in a captivating black dress, finishing her look with a daring touch of red lipstick, and inhales deeply, gathering her courage before stepping into the bustling penthouse with Peter amiably by her side.
Despite the increasingly chaotic scene, Amelia dives into the sea of faces, resolutely beginning her quest to locate the elusive Ethan Rodriguez.
Her relentless pursuit inadvertently triggers a tidal wave of hilarious misunderstandings, converting the high-end gala into an absurdly entertaining saga.
The misadventures unfold relentlessly, each hilarious mishap hammering laughter out of the shocked guests, adding to the peculiar charm of the ongoing soirée.
Ethan Rodriguez, the elusive host she pursued throughout the night, is unveiled as a figment of an elaborate prank planned by Peter who aimed to coax Amelia from her comfort zone.
Taken aback by the revelation, Amelia feels an initial rush of disappointment, which quickly dissipates when she hears the penthouse behind her erupt into uncontrollable laughter.
Her stern exterior crumbles, replaced by a joyous smile, as understanding of the humorous situation finally dawns on her.

As dawn approaches and the extravagant party starts to wind down, Amelia leaves the penthouse with a sense of satisfaction and a spring in her step, her heart abuzz with memories of the wacky adventures and unexpected laughs.
Settling into a yellow cab back to her place, Peter musters the courage to express his guilt over the prank.
But before he gets the chance, Amelia bursts into a fit of chuckles, forgiving him wholeheartedly and thanking him for pushing her boundaries.

Energized by a fresh outlook on life and armed with an amusing tale, Amelia pours forth her experiences into a riveting cover story for 'Manhattan Herald', capturing all the sweet and salty moments of the memorable soirée.
Finding a new lease of fun in her life, Amelia decides to concoct a surprise twist for Peter during their customary morning visit to 'Coffee Central'.
In a spirited turn of tables, she picks the perfect moment to ask Peter if he would like to accompany her for an outing that evening.

Returning from their funny escapade at the café, the story concludes as Amelia’s narration of her own ‘Manhattan Encounter’ sets the daily newspaper office abuzz causing employees to cherish the rippling laughs.

61637637.title: The Sleepover
synopsis: In Boston, Clancy Finch is invited by her crush Travis Schultz to a party at his house.
Her brother Kevin is caught dancing in the restroom by some older students who record him and bully him, but Clancy's and Kevin's mother Margot, the lunch monitor, scares them away.
The bullies upload a remix video of Kevin dancing and Margot admonishing them to YouTube, where it quickly goes viral, gaining over two million views.
Kevin, Clancy, and her friend Mim are picked up by their father Ron, an awkward pastry chef.
Clancy asks her parents if she can go to Travis's party and they both say no, leading to her insulting her mother and getting grounded.
Later, Kevin's friend Lewis comes over for a sleepover in a tent in the backyard.
That night, Clancy and Mim sneak out.
On their way to the party, they first scare the boys, causing Lewis to run into the house to pee.

While in the bathroom, he notices a man and a woman break into the house, force Ron at gun point and Margot (whom they call "Matilda") to come with them under threat of Ron's death to get their group back together.
Margot agrees, removing her necklace as a clueless Ron is brought along.
Lewis runs back to the tent and tells the others what happened.
Not believing him, the four run back inside until they notice United States Marshals Agent Henry Gibbs sneaking into the house.
An intruder, they attack him, tying him to a chair.
He tells them Margot was in the Witness Protection Program because she turned in the boss of the crime syndicate she was in, but has been located due to the viral video.
In another location, Elise and her associate are briefed on the mission.
Also present is Margot's criminal ex-fiancé Leo Bouchot, who had been in the Witness Protection Program before he was found.
The kids follow clues Margot left them in the flour and her necklace when she was taken away, leading them to a storage unit, a secret spy center.
They take a self-driving spy car to Travis's party.
Travis agrees to take them to Downtown Boston in his family's boat, but they are stopped by the U.S. Coast Guard and he has a revoked license.
The four jump off and swim away, then reach the building where they believe their parents are located.

They instead find a secret passageway behind a painting of Margot's favorite poet W. B. Yeats leading them to the hideout of Margot's best friend Jay, who tracks Margot's GPS chip to an extravagant gala.
Jay tells them to stay, but Clancy handcuffs her to a pipe so they can all leave.
At the gala, Ron, Margot, and Leo plan to steal Queen of Moldana's crown by giving her a non-lethal poison.
Upon meeting her, Ron accidentally ingests the poison and vomits everywhere, so gala security detains them.
When they are about to be sent to the FBI, Margot and Leo knock out all the security guards.
They go with Ron to the main floor, where they find the four kids, who got in by pretending to be live musicians.
The seven escape to Leo's safe house.
There, they discover Leo was never in the Witness Protection Program, but is actually the new head of the syndicate.
Elise holds them at gunpoint and calls the police, framing them for the theft.
Ron throws a wolf spider at her so she drops her gun and then shoots the chandelier so it subdues her.
Margot hot-wires a car that Ron uses to drive Leo into a bunch of construction barrels, then Margot kicks the crown out of his hands and Clancy catches it.
The Boston Police arrest Leo and those involved.
Henry drives everyone back to the Finch house where Travis returns Clancy's jacket and Lewis's mother picks him up.
Everyone returns to their normal lives.

8367095.title: The Harmonic Chronicles of Jacob Spencer
synopsis: The film introduces our protagonist, Jacob Spencer, in the energetic atmosphere of a high school concert, where he is seen doing a splendid rendition of Rachmaninoff on a grand piano.
After the concert, Jacob returns to his suburban home.
His parents, while loving, are not aware of Jacob's musical advancements.
Theo, Jacob's best friend, tirelessly supports Jacob during his recitals.
One day, Jacob stumbles upon an old man named Mr. Reynolds – a master of Rachmaninoff, charming passersby with his performance on a worn-out public piano.
A new chapter begins in Jacob's life when he starts composing a harmonious tune under Mr. Reynolds' tutelage.
As his passion for music further intensifies, Jacob's academic performance takes a hit.
Amidst the chaos of upcoming exams and looming deadlines, Jacob finds solace in music.
Jacob's slip from his academic duties comes to his parents' attention when they overhear a conversation about Jacob's performances from a gossiping PTA parent.
They confront him.
A heated showdown develops between Jacob and his parents.
Jacob longs for his parents' approval but also feels intense emotion when playing the piano.
Sensing Jacob's turmoil, his confidant Theo consoles Jacob.
Simultaneously, Mr. Reynold's deteriorating health becomes a subject of concern.
This change strengthens Jacob's resolve to excel in his craft and honor his ailing mentor.
To keep his passion alive amidst parental pressure, Jacob secretly starts rehearsing in his basement.
He is unintentionally caught by his parents.
Theo manages to convince Jacob's hesitant parents to attend the upcoming school recital.
At the grand recital night, Jacob steps on the stage and delivers a heartfelt performance of his original composition, enthralling the entire audience.
The performance leaves Jacob's parents in awe, allowing them to comprehend their son’s musical talent.
They validate their son’s passion for music.
Subsequently, they apologize for their earlier neglect and promise to support his desires and dreams in music.
In an intensely emotional scene towards the end of the story, Jacob visits his ailing mentor Mr. Reynolds in a hospital.
He presents him with a CD recording of his school performance.
Mr. Reynolds thanks Jacob and encourages him to continue on his artistic path, reminding him to always stay true to his love for music.
With his mentor's words of wisdom set in his heart, Jacob decides to continue to pursue his passion for music wholeheartedly.
The closing scenes of the film depict Jacob applying for the esteemed music program at the Juilliard School.
The film lastly shows a hopeful Jacob receiving an acceptance letter from the Juilliard School's program.
He places the letter beside a cherished framed picture of him and Mr. Reynolds on his piano.
The film ends with a determined Jacob engrossed in playing his piano, with each note symbolizing his journey marked by struggle and triumph.

69594858.title: The Ultimate Playlist of Noise
synopsis: Marcus Lund is a high school senior who is very music and sound obsessed.
As a child, his older brother Alex saved him from their burning home, perishing in the process.
Marcus listens to all of the music Alex left behind.
At a music gig, he falls for the singer who opens the show, but she takes off before he can introduce himself.
Simultaneously he has a seizure.
After testing, Marcus is told he has a brain tumor requiring surgery that will render him deaf.
Depressed at the idea that he soon won't be able to hear beloved sound, he compiles a playlist of 50 sounds he wants to record.
After giving a presentation of his plan to embark on a cross-country road trip to record the playlist, his mother rejects his plan.
Marcus takes off in the car.
A short time later, Wendy jumps in front of the car, and he knocks her off her feet.
She jumps in, urging him to hurry.
Wendy's angry ex follows close behind on his motorcycle, trying to get the guitar from her.
He breaks two windows and half jumps through the passenger window before Marcus drives through the red light, and Wendy pushes him out.
At a diner, Marcus and Wendy introduce themselves, he tells her saw her opener at the gig, telling her one day she'll make it.
He shows her his 50 item playlist, and she shows him her limited edition 1959 Starling Gold Fender Stratocaster.
On their way to NYC, they record many of the items on the list, including a thunder storm, a multitude of wind chimes, fireworks, a perfect strike in bowling...
Arriving in NYC, they go to Wendy's aunt's place.
Wendy heads off to her audition, while Marcus heads to the recording studio.
There, he discovers that the fire had actually been started by Alex, that he had committed suicide.
Marcus confirms with his mother what happened at the fire then, returning to Wendy's aunt's he finds out Wendy headed for Penn Station.
There, he discovers that she lied, there was no audition, she was there to sell the guitar.
Marcus leaves, getting someone to buy him liquor.
He empties his anti-seizure medication bottles randomly on the street.
As he falls, his recording equipment ends up getting smashed by a passing car.
As he's taken to the hospital.
Wendy finds the pills and the smashed tape recorder.
When Marcus' mother catches up with him in the hospital, he finds out that Alex had been bipolar.
She drives him back home.
Back in New York, Wendy struggles to get the tape recorder fixed, finally getting it done at Alex's friend's studio.
Back home, Marcus awaits the operation, a box with the repaired tape recorder and his brother's demo arrive from Wendy.
She records her well wishes to him.
The day of the operation comes and Marcus cherishes every last sound.
Sending out his 'Ultimate Playlist of Noise' to all his contacts, he says he's now learning to appreciate the world with his other senses.

2553549.title: The Encounter: Jazz Royalty vs. The Radio Lord
synopsis: During a time when jazz music stirred the soul of New York City, a striking voice echoed through the jazz clubs, captivating countless jazz aficionados.
This mesmerizing voice belonged to Louis Armstrong, an African American jazz musician who had uniquely cultivated an impeccable reputation for his soulful singing.
In a period characterized by racial segregation, Armstrong endured racial discrimination every single day.
He remained resilient, asserting his powerful presence in a predominantly white-dominated music industry and promoting his liberating jazz music.
In the throbbing nucleus of the WNYC radio station, Harold Roberts meticulously curated his popular radio show, "The Roberts Hour."
One evening, out of curiosity, Roberts frequented the famed Birdland Jazz Club and was utterly mesmerized by Armstrong's captivating performance.
Intrigued by Armstrong's audacious public stance on a pervasive issue, Roberts turned sinister and invited Armstrong to his radio show.
Unbeknownst to Armstrong, Roberts was plotting an on-air confrontation to challenge and undermine his beliefs, thinking this would fortify his influence.
Alerted to Roberts' less-than-noble intentions, Armstrong's friends fervently urged him to reconsider accepting the seemingly harmless invitation.
Armstrong, however, saw the broader picture.
He understood the power and reach of Roberts' radio platform and accepted the invitation.
On the other hand, Roberts meticulously plotted his tactics like a military strategist, intending to exploit the prevalent racial prejudices among his listeners.
The day of reckoning finally arrived.
Roberts' radio show started- the crackling of the airwaves symbolizing the tension that was palpable to the vast number of listeners who had eagerly tuned in.
Roberts commenced the verbal duel by probing Armstrong's music and beliefs in an unnervingly calm manner, aimed at unsettling his opponent.
But Armstrong, unfazed, parried right back.
Armourstrong responded fervently to every antagonistic question, displaying courage and resolve that left both Roberts and the critical listeners profoundly dumbfounded.
Sensing the direction of the wind changing, Roberts tried to regain control but couldn't match Armstrong's impassioned and irrefutable stand on racial equality.
However, not everyone looked at this development positively; Armstrong started receiving a torrent of threats from Roberts' followers.

In the aftermath of his impressive performance, Roberts found himself questioning his beliefs and regretting his role in fostering racial discrimination, his mind filled with a newfound admiration for Armstrong.
An internal struggle began to brew in him- should he continue to adhere to long-standing biases or acknowledge Armstrong's undeniable talent and moral courage?
In an unprecedented move, Roberts decided to issue a public apology during his live radio segment.
This bold on-air confession sparked a firestorm of negative reactions, leaving his professional reputation effectively in tatters.
Despite the crushing public backlash, a sense of relief surged through Roberts.
The radio apology turned out to be the end of an era - Roberts' entrenched radio career.
This marked the beginning of a challenging journey of self-reformation and the unlearning of deeply ingrained biases.
Roberts' sweeping broadcast initiated a paradigm shift in the radio journalism industry which changed it forever.
Meanwhile, in the wider world, Armstrong commenced a nationwide tour using his music as a catalyst for societal change.
Having retreated into privacy and self-reflection, Roberts introspected deeply on the harm he caused by wielding his radio platform irresponsibly.
Acknowledge his past transgressions, Roberts vowed to dedicate the rest of his life towards rectification of the racial biases he had propagated and towards promoting equality.
The film ends with a scene depicting a touching human moment- Roberts reaching out to Armstrong, suggesting a potential beginning of an unexpected but profound friendship.

While the road to change was just beginning and attitudes did not change overnight, the radio incident had sparked a citywide chain reaction that initiated a period of transformation in societal views.
The incident, etched in history as 'The Battle of the Airwaves,' was a turning point in music history.

It triggered fundamental shifts in attitudes towards race, music, and the role of radio journalism, and laid the groundwork for an era that would eventually lead to a breakthrough in the media industry.

61802475.title: The United States vs. Billie Holiday
synopsis: In 1957, Billie Holiday meets with a radio journalist, Reginald Lord Devine, for an interview.
He asks her what it is like to be a "colored woman" and about the trouble she keeps getting into because of her hit song "Strange Fruit".
Billie says it is about human rights, something the government often forgets.
In 1947, Billie's husband Monroe and her manager Joe Glaser try to get Billie to cut "Strange Fruit" from her set list, saying people high up in the government do not want to hear her sing it.
Lester Young, Billie's sax player, supports her in playing it.
In the 1940s, FBN chief Harry J. Anslinger tells agents that Billie is a threat, her song promotes the wrong ideas, and she has not stopped singing it.
Unable to arrest her for singing, they decide to go after her on drug charges.
After Billie's next show, Agent Jimmy Fletcher, disguised as a soldier, witnesses her doing drugs.
The FBI arrest Billie and her lover Joe Guy for drug use and possession.
The judge sentences Billie to a year in jail.
It is later revealed that Anslinger paid off Guy.
Anslinger tells Jimmy that they need to make sure Billie never sings again.
Jimmy questions why Billie is such a problem.
Anslinger tells Fletcher to go to the prison to get back in with Billie.
Instead, he tells her to not trust anyone and warns her the FBI will continue to try to set her up.
After Billie is released from prison, she does a Carnegie Hall show, where an audience member asks her to sing "Strange Fruit" and she sadly declines.
Billie meets John Levy, who tells her that he will pay off the right people to make sure she can keep singing in his clubs.
They begin a relationship.
Levy proposes to her, then slips drugs into her pocket just in time for the FBI to enter.
In court, Fletcher admits that Billie was possibly framed, and she is freed.
Anslinger sends Fletcher to follow Billie on her tour.
In 1949, Jimmy comes to see Billie after a successful tour stop and tells her the agency wants her to think he was fired.
Suspicious, the whole crew has Jimmy do heroin to show he can be trusted.
Over the course of the tour, Jimmy and Billie fall in love.
One day, after the bus breaks down, Billie breaks up with Jimmy, telling him he needs to find a nice girl, and that is not her.
Jimmy returns to work, where he finds he has been replaced.
Billie marries Louis McKay, later returning to Jimmy.
Later, Billie tells Jimmy she has liver failure.
In the hospital, Anslinger tells Billie and McKay that if she cooperates, she will never see them again.
Billie tells him that his grandkids will be singing "Strange Fruit" one day.

8744871.title: The Monster Hunter: Shadow of the Woodland Spirit
synopsis: Eldric, a revered monster slayer seasoned with thirty summers, stands at the edge of the grim and dark Dreadwood Forest.
His gaze pierces the slightest wind ruffles, attests to his readiness to hunt the elusive Voracious Viperwolf.
His eyes, fashioned to eagle-like precision from years of tireless training, are now latched onto the shadows behind the alien forest-trees.
He flickers between them, his agility akin to a panther, each stride more silent than the wind, affirming his mastery of coping with cryptic threats.
Prince Alfred rests in his affluent domain, Moonstone Nordhelm.
He indulges in a royal feast, gorging on culinary delights, gallivanting with jovial courtiers, blinded by the opulence at play.
His path intersects with that of Seriphia, a notorious Dryad spoken of in hushed whispers around the outskirts.
Drunk on his royal blood, Alfred recklessly bellows, ordering Seriphia to kneel before his noble lineage.
A gross display of arrogance, he becomes unknowingly responsible for triggering her wrath.
Seriphia's reply resonates in an echoing laughter, defying royal command.
This clash of status sparks a hostile clash, casting a heavy shroud of dread over the cheerful murals of Nordhelm.
Seriphia, in a cruel twist, turns to drain Alfred of his pride-induced energy.
A ruthless act that saps him into a pity-stricken state of physical and mental exhaustion.
On seeing the Dryad raise her arm to deliver a lethal blow, Eldric selflessly intervenes, launching his celestial Moonsteel blade against her.
An intense, whitening confrontation ensues.
Seeing a chance to salvage his honor, Alfred approaches Eldric with the olive branch of friendship and alliance.
Following this pact, Alfred endures a rigorous combat training regime under Eldric becoming adept in clashing steel, outwitting foes, and learns to coexist with Nordhelm's monstrous population.
Their combined forces successfully deter the minor beings lurking on the outskirts of Elderwood, inching closer every day towards Seriphia's wood-knotted abode.
They stumble upon an old, tarnished copper crown, stuck in the roots of a thousand-year-old Yggdrasil tree, an uncanny link to a forgotten Nordhelmian monarch.
Stoked by an overwhelming resolve to protect Nordhelm, the duo confronts Seriphia, triggering a final showdown that ripples the very essence of the kingdom.
Eldric's Moonsteel blade meets Seriphia's spectral energy, pushing each other to the brink of their combative abilities.
In an unprecedented move, Alfred swings a devastating blow against Seriphia.
Under Moonsteel's raw power, she splinters into sparks of dissolving ether.
But not before leaving Eldric with a grievous wound.
Eldric uses his waning breath to entrust the protection of Nordhelm to Alfred.
Alfred attempts to reconcile with Eldric's sacrificial death.
He pledges to shield Nordhelm from inevitable threats, honoring the memory of the brave hunter.
Alfred ushers an era of tranquility in Nordhelm.
A peaceful beginning signifying the dawn of a revitalized realm in his command.
A haunting howl slices through the serene night, spelling out the advent of a nerve-wracking chapter in the saga.
Standing atop the castle's highest tower, Alfred's shadowy presence forms a daunting silhouette against the moon.
A resounding royal decree reverberates across the dimly lit alleys of Nordhelm, rallying the kingdom folk to prepare for an impending assault.

66354923.title: The Witcher: Nightmare of the Wolf
synopsis: In 1165, the witcher Vesemir saves a noble child from a leshen in a forest in Kaedwen.
Before dying, the creature says something in an archaic elven dialect to Vesemir, leading him to think it was under someone's control.
Vesemir is visited by the elf Filavandrel, who thinks the leshen was controlled by Kitsu, one of many elven girls who have gone missing.
Meanwhile sorceress  Tetra Gilcrest tries to convince the Kaedwani king to wipe out the witchers, but Lady Zerbst, another courtier, is sympathetic to the witchers and speaks in their favor.
Vesemir reminisces about his youth when he, along with his best friend Illyana, were servants for a noble whose mistress was saved from a mahr by a witcher named Deglan with Vesemir's help.
Enticed by promises of coin and riches, Vesemir traveled to Kaer Morhen and underwent the training and mutations to become a witcher.
In the present day, Vesemir and another fellow witcher, Luka, are arrested for killing two knights in a bar fight.
Lady Zerbst persuades the king to send Vesemir along with Tetra to rid the forest of Kitsu.
She personally delivers the mission order to Vesemir who recognizes her as the now 70-year old Illyana.
Vesemir and Tetra set out and she tells him the story of a young sorceress wrongfully killed by a witcher as part of a con, and that she is convinced that all witchers are corrupted.
They find Kitsu, mutated and now able to cast powerful illusions, and fight her basilisk.
They kill the monster, but Kitsu escapes.
Following Kitsu, the pair come across an old and abandoned elven school where they find the bodies of the other missing female elves.

They rescue the captured Filavandrel, who explains that Kitsu tried to replicate the experiments that were done on her, and they come to the conclusion that witchers were responsible, creating new monsters to keep them in business.
Vesemir surmises that the monsters he encountered were probably created in Kaer Morhen and leaves to confront Deglan.
As he departs, Tetra destroys Kitsu's den, finds Kitsu later surveying the destruction, and blames the witchers.
Back at court, she likewise tells the king of the witchers' responsibility in the recent monsters attacks and is given authorization to lay siege to Kaer Morhen.
The King has Luka wrongly executed despite Lady Zerbst's protests.
She then escapes to warn the witchers.
Deglan admits to Vesemir to creating the monsters, including Kitsu, to protect their way of life and are alerted by Illyana of Tetra's assault.
Tetra and the local townsfolk attack Kaer Morhen with Kitsu and her monsters.
Illyana helps the witcher recruits flee into the mountains.
Vesemir confronts Tetra, who has captured the mages and is holding them hostage in the basement.
Kitsu arrives and plunges Vesemir into an illusion where he married Illyana and had a family.
However, Vesemir is able to break out of the illusion and engages in a fierce battle with Tetra and her forces.
He seemingly kills Tetra and Kitsu, only for it to be revealed as another illusion.
He had instead mortally wounded Illyana and killed the mages, meaning that the art of creating more witchers died with them.
Tetra reveals she is the daughter of the sorceress killed by the swindling witcher from her story before being killed by a dying Deglan.
He asks Vesemir to find the recruits and make them into "better men" before succumbing to his wounds.
At the behest of Illyana, Vesemir allows Kitsu to flee, and he carries a dying Illyana from the burning castle.
Vesemir takes Illyana to a lake, where she always dreamed of living by.
The two share a brief moment before she peacefully passes away.
He then sets out and catches up to the recruits, including a young Geralt, taking them under his wing as the last batch of witchers.

84637427.title: The Storm of Frost Valley
synopsis: Alex McKinley and Emily Stone, documentary filmmakers from New York, embarked on a journey away from city life.
They were committed to filming a groundbreaking nature documentary featuring the untouched landscapes of Frost Valley, located in the heart of Colorado.
Leaving behind the constant buzz of New York, they sought solace in the tranquil serenity of frost-kissed trees and the towering peaks of Colorado mountains.
Their residence for the filming duration was an antiquated log cabin.
During one of their supply runs to the rustic-general store in a neighboring town,they chanced upon two local inhabitants - Warren Smith and Cheyenne Mitchell.
Both were renowned elk hunters and had spent their lives in the embrace of Frost Valley.
They recounted tales of severe snowstorms and the unwilling spirits believed to be responsible.
Unfazed by the local folklore, Alex and Emily armed with their state-of-the-art filming equipment, ventured into the snow-blanketed landscape to commence their ambitious project.
As darkness fell on their first filming expedition, an unexpected blizzard descended upon them.
The soft snowflakes whirled around them in a frenzied dance, encasing them in a thick blanket of frost.
As they immersed themselves deeper in the valley, eerie incidents began to manifest.
Enigmatic frost patterns started forming on the glass-paneled windows of their cabin.
Alien yet somehow sentient, these patterns resembled symbols from an unknown language.
Reviewing their filmed footage revealed ghostly apparitions barely visible amidst the snowfall.
The revelation sent waves of panic and fear through them, but their curiosity remained.
When the tension escalated, Alex accused the native duo, Warren and Cheyenne, of organizing the spectral apparitions, creating an elaborate hoax in conformity with their superstitions.
Warren and Cheyenne, under increasing suspicion, confessed about an ancient seal.
For generations, locals believed this seal contained the spirits of the valley, confining them to their ethereal world.
With their safety hanging on a fragile thread, Alex and Emily temporarily ceased filming.
They shifted their focus to understanding more about the ancient seal and how they could fortify it to appease the spectral entities.
Relying on the local duo's expertise and the legends they had grown up with, they embarked on a quest.
Their objective was to understand the mysterious seal better and to discover a way to reinforce it to guarantee their survival amidst the spectral presence.
Equipped with age-old ritual tools provided by Warren and Cheyenne, they embarked on a risky mission.
Battling the bitterly cold winds, they trekked across the snow-covered valley.
Their bodies shivered, driven by the hope to neutralize the energy of the spectral entities lurking in the shadows.
Pushing their mental and physical limits, they performed the ancient ritual amidst the merciless storm.
As the last word of the incantation left their lips, the spectral figures receded, their ghostly figures blending into the white backdrop of the snowy valley.
Warren, moved by a divine sense of duty, volunteered for the final sacrifice.
With Warren's sacrifice, the blizzard subsided.
The extraordinary occurrence left an indelible mark on Alex and Emily.
They meticulously created a photo mosaic.
Having packed their filming equipment, they bid a mournful adieu to the majestic Frost Valley, carrying in their hearts their fallen comrade and memories to last a lifetime.
Back in their city loft, Alex and Emily found it challenging to merge back into mundane routines despite their newfound fame.
Their supernatural experience had left a powerful imprint, casting an ominous aura they carried within themselves.
Unlike before, they initiated a documentary project to honor Warren's sacrifice.
They painstakingly compiled raw footage from their time in Frost Valley, weaving it into a compelling narrative.
The film captured the paradox of the serene valley beautifully, depicting the tranquil wilderness and underlying mystery through artistic visuals and compelling storytelling.
Seizing the opportunity garnered by their documentary's success, they initiated a dialogue about untouched places like Frost Valley.
They emphasized conserving nature and respecting indigenous beliefs.
The film concluded with a panoramic shot of Frost Valley, its untouched allure now paired with an underlying sense of artificial tranquillity, with the echo of untold terror still lingering.

65418323.title: The Wolf of Snow Hollow
synopsis: PJ Palfrey and his girlfriend Brianne vacation in Snow Hollow, Utah, where PJ gets into a verbal altercation with two local hunters.
At their rental house that night, Brianne is attacked.
PJ discovers her mangled body and a paw print in the snow.
John Marshall, a deputy sheriff struggling with anger management issues and alcoholism, is called to the murder scene.
His father, Sheriff Hadley, and fellow officer Julia Robson have discovered Brianne's genitalia and other parts missing from her corpse.
A snowboarding instructor is killed next, in a struggle in which her head and an arm are torn off.
Wolf fur is discovered on her body.
John gets into a fight with an officer who leaks to the press that the killer could be a wolf.
Under stress, John begins drinking again.
While John and Julia drive to work the next morning, someone throws a beer bottle at her car.
Paranoid tips from all over the community roll in.
Townie Liz Fairchild has a strange encounter with a tall man at a diner and reports it to the police.
Hadley is diagnosed with a heart murmur, and John urges him to seek medical treatment.
They argue, with John declaring that Hadley should work from home.
Hadley refuses to go for treatment.
Later that night, Liz and her three-year-old are killed.
John, growing increasingly agitated and angry, combs through the town's records to determine if there is a connection between the victims and looks up werewolf lore.
While investigating, they discover the tall man called Liz's workplace asking for her.
A curfew is imposed, and an active watch for the creature begins.
After another cardiac event, Hadley agrees to retire and seek treatment.
At night, Jenna sneaks away to see her boyfriend.
They are attacked in his SUV by the wolfman, wounding Jenna.
John answers a neighbor's 911 call and shoots at the creature, which escapes.
It later kills a sheriff's deputy, stuffing his body in a trash can.
When John yells at Jenna for breaking curfew, she shouts that his lack of care is the reason why she is going away to college on a gymnastics scholarship.
After visiting her and Hadley in the hospital, John breaks into Jenna's boyfriend's house and attacks him.
Meanwhile, Hadley passes away from heart complications.
Grieving for his father and frustrated with the case, John is banned from his support group meetings at Alcoholics Anonymous.

The body of a man living in a camper outside town is found dead of a heroin overdose and the police believe he is the killer due to multiple factors including his height, his knife collection, the presence of a pet wolf-dog, and the discovery of the body of a missing woman in his backyard.
The coroner later insults John's intelligence and threatens to tell the press about his difficulties in finding the murderer.
John deduces the coroner was responsible for the vandalism of Robson's car and fires him.
While John is out distributing evidence from the closed case back to its original owners, PJ contacts Robson and tells her that his belongings contained a seam ripper that was not his.
Deducing that the ripper is for taxidermy, Robson realizes that Paul Carnury, the town's taxidermist, must be investigated, just as John stops by Paul's house.
Paul seems eager for details of the case and asks John about his daughter, something he could not have known unless he was present when Jenna was attacked.
John asks Paul to stand up to his actual height, revealing himself to be nearly 7 feet tall.
He slams the door on John and runs.
John breaks into the house, discovering a workstation containing Hannah's head.
Paul stabs John in the stomach and lifts him off of the ground.
Hearing sirens, he drops John, changes into a homemade wolf costume and flees into the woods.
John overcomes his wounds and pursues Paul.
A fight ensues until Paul is shot and incapacitated by Robson.
John then shoots Paul repeatedly in the head before collapsing.
Sometime later, Robson becomes Snow Hollow's new sheriff.
She and John help Jenna move into her college dorm.
John leaves Jenna condoms and his gun for protection.
As he walks out of the dorm, he passes two students making sexual comments about the gymnasts in the dorm.
He stops for a moment but then just walks away.

12316026.title: The Lady in the Townhouse (2021 film)
synopsis: We meet Julie, a distinguished child psychologist who had made a comfortable home for herself in a tastefully designed townhouse situated in Chicago's upscale Gold Coast neighborhood.
Even after separating from her ex-husband, James, a celebrity chef known for his inventive culinary creations, she maintained a cordial relationship with him.
This arrangement was made more peaceful by their shared love for Amelia, their six-year-old daughter.
However, the faultless orderliness of Julie's life began to waver with a series of small incongruities happening inside her home.

A perfectly arranged shelf disturbed, a favorite toy of Amelia's forgotten in an unlikely place, a puzzle book supposedly misplaced – initially, these were shrugged off by Julie as random occurrences.

On an icily cold night, an out-of-place anomaly grabbed her attention: the latch on her Victorian-style master bedroom window – an antique that she hardly ever opened – was broken, an occurrence she had no memory of causing.

Creeping discomfort slithered into her life as belongings she held dear - a particular pair of pearl earrings her grandmother had given her, the hardcover mystery novels she loved - began disappearing one by one, seemingly swallowed by thin air.
Her anxiety was compounded by strange noises coming from the basement in the dead of night.
As the frequency and intensity of these incidents escalated, Julie found pathways in her mind that she hadn't tread before.
She began doubting herself, questioning her memory, her sanity, even the fabric of reality in which she was living.
Overwhelmed, she decided to drown herself in her work.
The young minds that she helped navigate through their trauma provided a respite from her own burgeoning fear.
Julie's dedication did not go unnoticed.
As she tackled increasingly intense cases with her characteristic commitment, her reputation at the children's psychology department of the prestigious Northwestern Hospital skyrocketed.
On a cool, rainy evening, she discovered an unmarked note on her oak-wood doorstep.
There were clear similarities that linked the notes to Tom's unique handwriting and artistic style.
Desperation driving her, she decided to engage David, a former F.B.I.
agent who had turned private investigator.
Her mentor from her days at Harvard, Henry, had suggested David could help navigate her mysterious predicament.
A camaraderie flourished between Julie and David, built on their shared dedication towards the cause of child trauma recovery.
A certain case involving a distressed adolescent named Tom began to stick out as they dug deeper.
Tom's committal to the institution had been decided by a court, and Julie's testimony had played a significant role in it.
The chilling timeline added to their suspicion: Tom had been released from the institution for good behavior just a few weeks before the queer disturbances had first started at Julie's home.

Equipped with the state-of-the-art surveillance tools, David was able to gather indisputable evidence confirming their growing suspicions - Tom had a personal vendetta against Julie and was the source of the disturbances.

Devising a stratagem of their own, David and Julie turned the tables on Tom by setting a trap for him within the historic walls of her townhouse, leaving not a single stone unturned to ensure Tom’s capture.
The confrontation with Tom that followed was akin to a tempest, escalating to a level of violence neither of them had anticipated.
Struck with a newfound fear for Amelia's safety, Julie had a heart-wrenching discussion with James late into the night.
Reality opened their eyes, and for their innocent six-year-old's sake, they decided to bury their differences.
Shaken, Julie sought the guidance of her wise and trusted mentor, Henry, one last time.
She needed his wisdom to decide her life's new course in the wake of recent events.
With renewed resolve, Julie began the task of packing.
Saddened but committed to her newfound path, she finalized the paperwork that would transfer Amelia to a local pastoral school nestled amidst sprawling farmlands.
Simultaneously, she accepted an attractive job offer from 'Healing Horizons,' a renowned therapy center situated in the same pastoral landscape.
Throughout her remaining days in Chicago, she worked tirelessly to wrap up all pending cases at the Northwestern Hospital.
On the eve of her departure, David stopped by for a final meeting.
Their goodbye was bittersweet.
The severity of her traumatic experiences had left Julie bruised but not broken.
It had in fact, strengthened her resolve to start afresh.
When the sale of her modern, riverfront townhouse to an ambitious young couple was finalized, she felt an odd mixture of sadness and relief wash over her.
Spending her final night in the once treasured confines of the townhouse was overwhelming.
Leaving was harder than she'd imagined it would be.
With a nod of gratitude to the bricks and mortar that had once been her safe haven, she stepped out of the front porch, never looking back.
Stepping into an entirely different phase of life, Julie, James, and Amelia embarked on their journey totheir new home in Alpine Grove.
Their new abode was a cozy country-style cottage.
In the soothing cocoon of her new surroundings, Julie surprisingly found herself comfortably fitting in.
She found solace in penning a heartfelt letter to David.
She detailed how their first week in Alpine Grove had been, also assuring him that she would keep him updated abouttheir new life.
The movie ends with a serenely beautiful scene of Julie, sitting on her porch swing.
For the first time since the ordeal had started, she was genuinely smiling; as Amelia and James, in the distant, were trying their hand at fishing.
With a heart ready to mend, she let go of her haunting past and embraced the promising tranquility the future held for her.
A firm goodbye to her harrowing past, marked the beginning of her journey towards a better, safer tomorrow.

57233370.title: The Woman in the Window (2021 film)
synopsis: Child psychologist Anna Fox lives alone in a Manhattan brownstone after separating from her husband Edward; he lives away with their daughter Olivia, but she talks to them on a daily basis.
Anna suffers from agoraphobia and her housebound state leads her to observe all of her neighbors from a second-storey window, including the Russell family who recently moved in across the street.
She also takes a large number of medications and drinks heavily.
One evening, Jane Russell visits Anna and they befriend one another.
She also meets Ethan, Jane's teenage son, who suggests his father Alistair is abusive.
One night, Anna witnesses Jane being stabbed to death in the living room.
She contacts the police but they do not believe her, claiming everyone in the family is fine.
Alistair arrives along with "Jane" who, to the shock of Anna, is a different woman from the one she met.
She begins spying on the Russell family.
Anna's tenant David, who lives in her basement, claims he did not hear or see anything, though she learns David was once in prison and broke his parole conditions.
She receives an anonymous e-mail with a photo of her sleeping.

She again contacts the detectives, who are joined by the Russells and David in Anna's house, and Anna breaks down when it is revealed by a detective that Edward and Olivia are dead as a result of a car crash that Anna accidentally caused.
Anna is now agoraphobic as a result and her medication has caused her to have hallucinations and conversations with people who are not there.
Anna apologizes to the Russell family and stops pursuing her suspicions.
She records a video on her cell phone, planning to commit suicide by overdose.
She then discovers a photograph she took of her cat and, in the reflection of a wine glass, sees the original Jane, proving she is real.
Anna shows David the photo and he confesses the original Jane she met is a woman named Katie Melli, Ethan's biological mother.
Katie had been stalking the Russell family, trying to get close to Ethan.
David refuses to help Anna prove the truth; he is then suddenly attacked and killed by Ethan, who had been lurking inside the house.
Ethan reveals to Anna that he murdered Katie and is a serial killer, having also killed Alistair's secretary in Boston, and now intends to kill Anna.
He had been letting himself into her house all week with a stolen key, and he was the one who took the photo of her sleeping.
Anna flees to the roof, where they fight until she pushes Ethan through the skylight to his death.
As Anna recovers in the hospital, Detective Little visits and tells her they have arrested Alistair and Jane for helping Ethan cover up Katie's murder and that they have found Katie's body.
Little admits he watched Anna's suicide video, but hands back her phone to allow her to delete it before she has to return it for evidence.
He apologizes for not believing her.
Nine months later, Anna, now sober and healthy, says goodbye to her house before she moves out and on with her life, now no longer afraid of the outside world.

42227480.title: Echoes Uncovered
synopsis: Laura is our protagonist, a devoted art conservator currently employed by the Louvre.
Her passion for preservation is shared by none other than her spouse, John — an esteemed professor of the art histories that breathe life into each masterpiece — at the Sorbonne University.

Together, they have a six-year-old daughter, Lily, whose pristine innocence is like an untouched masterpiece; a blank canvas graced with the charm of sunflower eyes that reflect her vibrant surroundings.
On a biting winter day, the mansion welcomes an addition to its collection.

Laura brings home a painting; a peculiar piece captivating with its Gothic allure, bearing the cryptic signature of an artist known as Adramelech and whispers of a mysterious cult called the Blood Moon.
The artwork is a whirlpool of unease — its frames inscribed with archaic symbols and eldritch runes.
The subjects of the painting, a gathering of robed figures amidst an otherworldly ebon forest, draw the viewer deep into the limbs of its unsettling beauty.
One silence-laden night, the house seems to transform.
Deep in its tranquil quietude, Laura begins hearing murmurs — soft yet eerie sounds resonating eerily as though coming from the painting’s inscrutable depths.
Meanwhile, Lily begins to display an alarmingly unfamiliar behavior.
She speaks of an unseen friend, an invisible playmate who seemingly frequents her interactions.
This revelation shifts a shiver of fear through the heart of the parents.
As days progress, their once peaceful abode begins mirroring scenes from a tenebrous tale.
Struck by the unfolding peculiarities, Laura and John dive into the dark depths of the painting's obscured past.
They work tirelessly in hope of unmasking the unsettling aura surrounding Adramelech's creation and its alleged camaraderie with the virtual cult.
Their research unearths a spine-chilling history pregnant with sinister rites and a dreadful fate that had once met previous owners.
The painting, it seemed, breathed a curse.
Nightly torment ensues for the family.
Haunting dreams featuring grotesque shadows chanting in an indecipherable tongue infiltrate their subconscious.
As inexplicable occurrences continue, they feel the tendrils of terror tighten around them.
With despair looming, Laura turns to an exorcist — a reputed figure sanctioned to grace their home with an enquiry into the unexplained hauntings.
His ominous speculations further curdle their blood.

The expert believes the painting a portal, a spiritual gateway with ill-intent; a mystical abyss for perturbed spirits of the foregone Blood Moon Cult to cross into their world — a means to awaken an ancient demon.
A turning point envelops when Lily's behaviour undergoes a chilling transformation.
She speaks in unearthly tongues, her innocence replaced with an unsettling change that sends a tremor of terror through Laura.
Desperation sets in, and the family delves further into the world of occult knowledge.
They scour through ancient tomes, attempting to decode cryptic symbols that lace the painting, hoping to close the spectral gateway that has tainted their lives.
What follows is a climactic whirlpool of suspense.
Guided by the exorcist, the weary family endeavours to recite ancient incantations, their hearts held captive by mind-numbing terror, their spirits determined to protect Lily.
Each trial leaves them drained, their fears exacerbated.
The tension crescendos in an electrifying finale — their relentless efforts finally yield result.
They watch as the spectral glow of the portal starts to dim.
In unthinkable rage, the spirits retaliate — an unnatural force shreds the painting, severing their ties with the mortal sphere and leaving behind a damaged, hollow canvas.
With danger averted, an exhausted but relieved Laura opts to change her career path.
She steps away from her position at the Louvre, seeking professions away from the mystical world of artifacts.
Heavy-hearted, the family packs up their foregone lives.
They relinquish their antique collectables and the mansion housing memories of their harrowing ordeal.
With one last lingering look at the mansion that was once their haven, the family steps into an unfamiliar future.
They say their goodbyes to the horrifying past, closing this chapter of their lives hitherto.

62000460.title: Things Heard & Seen
synopsis: In 1980, Catherine Claire, an art restorer, lives in Manhattan with her husband George and daughter Franny.
When George lands a job teaching art history at a college, the family moves into a large farmhouse in upstate New York.
Catherine, who suffers from bulimia, feels isolated in the house.
She finds an old Bible containing a family tree of the previous owners, the Smits; some of the names are scratched out and marked "Damned."
She senses a spirit and sees strange lights leading her to an antique ring, which she begins wearing.
Franny sees a female spirit in her room and insists on sleeping with her parents.
Catherine employs brothers Eddie and Cole Lucks as handyman and babysitter while George starts an affair with Eddie's cousin Willis.
Catherine befriends George's colleague Justine Sokolov.
George invites Floyd DeBeers, the head of the art history department, to his home.
Floyd feels the presence of a soul but assures Catherine that the spirit is benevolent and offers to hold a séance.
George and Catherine throw a party, where Catherine finds out the previous owners, who died in a murder-suicide, were Eddie and Cole's parents, and that her ring belonged to their mother Ella.
She confronts George about the house's violent history.
As they argue, a radio begins playing, only stopping when George smashes it.
Catherine asks George to take Franny to his parents' house.
While George is gone, Catherine and Floyd hold a séance and the ghost of Ella is summoned.
Floyd tells Catherine that there is another spirit in the house and that she should be careful.
Catherine discovers George's affair with Willis.
On a class trip, Justine overhears a conversation between George and his dissertation advisor, who asks how he was hired without a letter of recommendation.
Floyd confronts George, who admits to forging a recommendation.
At a family dinner, Catherine learns that the paintings George claimed were his work were actually painted by his cousin, who drowned in a boating accident.
Her trust shattered, Catherine begins an affair with Eddie.
On a boat ride, George fails to dissuade Floyd from reporting him.
Later, a soaked George returns to campus (with Floyd nowhere to be seen), where Justine confronts him about his affair with Willis.
George follows her car and runs her off the road, putting her into a coma.
Catherine learns of Floyd's death and Justine's accident.
In George's classroom, a mystical painting of death and a Christian cross from a book that Floyd gave him is suddenly projected on a screen.
George can't make it go away, which infuriates him and sends him running from the class.
Back home, Catherine prepares to leave with Franny.
George drugs her and murders her with an axe.

In the morning, Cole comes to babysit, finding instructions from George not to disturb Catherine as she is ill. George returns home from campus, where he has been given Floyd's office and position, and pretends to discover Catherine's body.
The police suspect he is responsible but have no proof, so they release him.
He takes Franny to his parents' home in Connecticut.
Catherine's soul joins forces with Ella's.
They awaken Justine and show her what George did.
Justine speaks to the police.
To avoid being arrested, George tries to escape on his cousin's boat.
A storm arrives and George's boat disappears in flames, a scene that resembles the painting seen earlier.
However, the cross in this painting is upside down, indicating that George is damned.

78370590.title: Falling Through Flames
synopsis: We meet Paul, a seasoned firefighter with the New York Fire Department, renowned for his unwavering courage and exceptional rescue skills.
He's introduced amidst one of the most ferocious forest fires anyone has ever witnessed - the "Great Sierra Blaze."
His face, hardened by the inferno’s warmth, reflects the determination and resolve he's known for.
Paul commands a squad of the department's most outstanding firefighters, cutting through the sea of flames threatening every inch of the Sierra forest.
They have one aim: saving a trio of stranded teenagers and a trapped colleague named Ben, trapped right in the heart of the fiery chaos.
Despite their best efforts, as darkness falls, a thick canopy of smoke blankets the forest while fierce winds fan the raging fire, causing it to intensify dramatically.
The forest transforms into an unstoppable inferno, a beast threatening to swallow everything in its path.
Struggling against the relentless onslaught and failing to escape the rapidly approaching firestorm, a wave of devastating heat engulfs Ben and the teenagers.
They tragically succumb to the ruthless blaze's destructive fury, a scene that scars the surviving heroes for life.
Consumed by survivor’s guilt, Paul begins questioning his actions, his decisions, and his worthiness as a seasoned firefighter.
He berates himself endlessly for their loss, reliving every moment of their grim fate.
The misfortune profoundly affects Paul, distorting the once renowned firefighter into a haunted shadow of his past.
The persistent trauma begins to infiltrate his work, making a formidable task even more difficult.
Chief Thompson, from the NYFD, registers his concern for Paul's emotional wellbeing, witnessing the toll the tragedy had taken.
The jovial, dedicated firefighter he knew was now a man burdened by guilt and regret.
Believing a change of environment could potentially aid his healing, Chief Thompson decides to transfer Paul to the fire investigation department, housed in their Brooklyn office.
It's a drastic move intended to remove him from the fiery front lines and immerse him in less frenzied work.
The radical shift from the field to the office doesn't sit well with Paul.
Long accustomed to battling real, raging fires, facing a desk and paperwork every day feels exhausting in a monotonous way, dismantling his stamina and spirit bit by bit.
As Paul investigates numerous fire incidents in New York City, he uncovers a tormenting correlation echoing facets of the once catastrophic "Great Sierra Blaze."
This chilling discovery sends ice-cold shivers down his spine.
Driven by a mounting concern, he allies with Sarah, an exceptionally sharp and dedicated fire investigator from his department.
They begin an intense chase, delving into patterns, motives, and culprits associated with the string of fires.
They unearth a series of blazing catastrophes sharing uncanny resemblances in their spread pattern and fierce intensity.
The blazes aren't just accidents - they're the product of calculated arson.
During his relentless pursuit for the truth, Paul's guilt resurrects.
Comprehending that the fatal fires were results of deliberate actions and not just freak accidents fuels the self-blame he was battling.
Could an earlier detection have saved the innocent lives lost?
His guilt remerges stronger, distorting reality and convincing him that he could've changed the outcome if he had identified these sinister patterns sooner.
Self-doubt clouds his mind more than ever before.
With Sarah, they finally zero in on their prime suspect.
Marcus, a notorious pyromaniac known for his terrifying love affair with fire, stands beneath their scrutiny's spotlight.
Sensing the tightening noose, Marcus preemptively plots an intimidating, fiery assault within the iconic Empire State Building.
Paul and Sarah find themselves imprisoned within the high-rise building, as a ruthless fire threatens to consume everything around them.
Their escape routes diminish as the threatening blaze intensifies.
Surrounded by savage flames, Paul's ghosts from the Sierra rescue operation resurface, amplifying his guilt and regret.
He’s back within the familiar wrath of an inferno, battling the same terrifying enemy.
Refusing to succumb to despair, Paul moulds his guilt into unwavering resolve.
With a firm mission to save Sarah and himself, he summons the strength that had once defined him so boldly.
As the Empire State Building's structure begins to crumble, Paul leans on his extensive knowledge and firefighting abilities to protect Sarah and devise a way out.
His instincts and strategies stand against the time bomb, lending them a glimmer of hope amidst the terrifying chaos.
The spreading news pulls in the entire New York Fire Department, with a visibly anxious Chief Thompson commanding a desperate rescue operation.
Amid the instability and danger, Paul finds the courage to face Marcus, a fierce wrestling dance in the fire-lit backdrop.
His hardened eyes reflect the desire for justice, overshadowing the flames' threatening glow.
In a dramatic turn of events, Paul disarms Marcus, pitting him defenceless against the arriving NYPD officers.
With Marcus captured, Paul's mission nears successful completion.
Upon surviving through the hair-raising rollercoaster of events, Paul and Sarah are rescued, culminating in the arrest of Marcus - the mastermind behind the series of horrifying citywide fires.
Through his gut-wrenching journey, Paul's metamorphosis is tangible.
He manages to reshape his guilt, once crippling, now a driving force of resilience and strength.
Having extinguished his internal angst, an invigorated Paul gears up, ready to serve his city once more.
The firefighting suit adorning him now symbolizes not just duty, but also courage, resilience, and hope.
The film ends with Paul triumphantly rejoining his NYFD unit, a shining testament to healing and resilience.
His colleagues' smiles mirror the triumphant return of the hero they always believed in.

60620058.title: Those Who Wish Me Dead
synopsis: Hannah Faber, a smokejumper, is struggling after failing to prevent the deaths of three young campers and a fellow smokejumper in a forest fire.
She is now posted in a fire lookout tower in Park County, Montana.

Owen Casserly, a forensic accountant in Florida, learns about the death of his district attorney boss and his family in an apparent gas explosion; believing that their deaths were actually a contracted killing and that he is the next target, Owen goes on the run with his son, Connor.
He intends to seek refuge with his brother-in-law, Ethan Sawyer, a deputy sheriff in Park County.
Reaching Montana, they are ambushed by the assassins "Jack" and "Patrick", who force them off the road and down a cliff.
Trapped in the car, Owen gives Connor the evidence against the assassins' employer.
Connor flees before the assassins kill Owen.
Lightning strikes Hannah's tower, frying her communications equipment.
As Ethan discovers Owen's car wreck, Hannah stumbles upon Connor while out on patrol.
She takes him back to the tower to contact help.
The assassins meet their boss, who instructs them to hunt down and kill Connor.
As a diversion to preoccupy the police, they use flares to start a forest fire.
They go to Ethan's isolated house searching for Connor and find and interrogate Ethan's pregnant wife, Allison.
When they force her to call Ethan, she gives him a duress code; she then fights off the assassins and escapes.
Hannah attempts to take Connor into town on foot but they are forced to turn back when the fire blocks their path.
Following the radio call, Ethan returns home with the sheriff, aiming to protect Allison.
However, the assassins ambush them; they kill the sheriff and force Ethan to guide them through the woods.
The assassins arrive at Hannah's fire tower and force Ethan to search it as they observe from a tree.
Hannah and Connor hide while Ethan attempts to make it appear as if the tower is empty.
After Patrick sees that Ethan seems to be talking to someone, the assassins shoot up the tower.
Ethan is injured, but Hannah and Connor manage to escape.
The assassins try to follow them but are stopped when Allison, having tracked them down, starts shooting at them.
Patrick and Jack split up, with Patrick pursuing Hannah and Connor while Jack stays behind to fight Allison; Allison gains the upper hand and kills Jack.
Connor runs ahead while Hannah fights Patrick but returns after Patrick threatens to beat Hannah to death.
As Patrick is about to kill Connor, Hannah severely injures Patrick with a climbing axe and leaves him to burn to death in the approaching fire.
Allison reunites with Ethan in the tower, but the fire traps them as they put on oxygen masks and hold each other.
Hannah and Connor jump into a stream and watch from under the water as the fire engulfs the forest.
In the morning after the fire has burned out, Hannah's old smoke-jumping team arrives and rescues her, Connor, and Allison.
Ethan has died from his gunshot wounds.
Connor later prepares to give his father's evidence to the media.
Hannah promises to help him through his uncertain future.

12035112.title: Bound by Regret (2022 film)
synopsis: The film begins in the picturesque DeLune Vineyard.
Thomas, an austere figure, is issuing hurried instructions to Eleanor, who is painstakingly pruning the last row of Merlot grapevines.
Their heated conversation reveals years of repressed bitterness and resentment, echoing the strained relationship between the two.
Their latent anger gradually rears its ugly head, turning each retort more acidic.
The tension, icy and palpable, reflects how their marriage turned sour over a decade.
A series of flashbacks remind the audience of Thomas and Eleanor’s rose-tinted past.

It unfurls the progression of their tumultuous relationship, drifting from the first bloom of romance to harsh, screaming fights, a heart-wrenching separation, and finally, their pressured attempts at co-running the vineyard post-divorce due to a crippling, high-interest loan.
Their bickering halts abruptly as they spot the family attorney, Jackie Sullivan, making his way across the vineyard.
Sullivan reveals that their frugal Aunt Roberta, a distant relative known for her wise investments, has left them a substantial inheritance.
It comes with an absurd clause that they must act like a happily married couple for a year to claim the treasure.
A solitary man, Thomas and the vivacious Eleanor recoil almost in sync at the ludicrous suggestion of living a lie of marital bliss for an entire year.
A quick, reluctant glance at the stack of pending bills and the wearied degradation of their beloved vineyard convinces them to stomach their resentments and give the preposterous plan a shot.
Thus, they embark on a comedic journey of rehearsing and staging numerous scenarios of domesticated joy.
These performances are filled with forced candlelit meals and enthusiastic love-filled banter.
The challenges of the charade take a hilarious turn as they move into sharing the same bed and navigate the awkward moments that follow.
Their banters never fail to remind them of their actual fragmented relationship.
Close relatives, especially the intuitive Aunt Patty, begin dropping in without notice, forcing them to up their act.

Striving to maintain their deception under the prying gaze of their kin, they arrange elaborate romantic scenes, including heart-shaped chocolates and scenic boat rides, which turn astonishingly farcical.
Amid all these staged pretences, old resentments creep up unexpectedly.
Trivial arguments over a burnt toast or the choice of throw pillows escalate quickly into heated verbal spats.
To escape this brewing tension, they hit upon the idea of hiring seasoned actors to play the part of their joy-filled family.
The auditions held in their rustic vineyard barn call forth an assortment of uncanny characters.
Surprisingly, amidst all unveiled chaos, they manage to assemble an amusingly incongruous family, including overexcited children and a robotic dog who seems too perfect for reality.
Their hard-earned comfort gets toppled when the stern vineyard inspector, Mr. Higgins, arrives unannounced.
Grasping with this unexpected development, they fumble through coming up with a convincing family backstory.
It leads to a series of hastily orchestrated cover-ups and wild fabrications.
Ironically, their hired family, in their effort to earn their pay, exaggerates each of their roles to an absurd extent.
Amidst the madness of these high-tension scenarios, Thomas and Eleanor unexpectedly share many light-hearted moments that soften their hardened exterior, offering glimmers of their old camaraderie.
A climactic 'family' dinner featuring a gigantic roasted turkey centerpiece unravels when the hired actors veer off their scripts, raising the vigilant Mr. Higgins's suspicions.
The fourth act dives into the repercussions of their failed act that, despite their tireless charade, almost costs them their fortune.
Even with this monumental stumbling block, they feel an unexpected wave of relief.
Their once strained relationship now reflects a kinder understanding and camaraderie born out of their shared escapade.
Their world flips sideways with the revelation that Mr. Higgins was an imposter all along, and their old friend Mike Stinson was the mastermind of this unraveled deception.
This shocking twist stirs a muddle of emotions within them, a blend of relief, betrayal, but most importantly, an undeniable bond born out of a shared ordeal.
Reflecting upon their chaotic journey, they share moments of genuine laughter - a refreshing change after years of seething resentment and anger.
With a newfound understanding and a deep respect for their turbulent history, they decide to give their relationship another shot.
The concluding scenes depict Thomas and Eleanor re-engaging in their usual routine of taking care of their vineyard.
The difference - this time, their partnership is underlined with a sparks of understanding and rekindled affection.
Together, they breathe new life into the deteriorating DeLune Vineyard.
The film concludes with them basking in the fruit of their labor, the thriving vineyard.

66913521.title: Ticket to Paradise (2022 film)
synopsis: David and Georgia Cotton are a divorced couple who hate each other and regret their marriage, which ended 20 years earlier.
Their daughter Lily graduates from college, and goes on vacation to Bali with her friend and fellow graduate Wren.
While snorkeling off the coast, their tour boat leaves them behind, and they are rescued by a young Balinese seaweed farmer named Gede.
That night, Lily and Gede hit it off.
A month later, Lily emails David and Georgia to let them know that she and Gede are getting married and are staying in Bali permanently, giving up her legal career before it begins.
David and Georgia form a truce to try and convince Lily that she is rushing into things and making the same mistake they did.
Their pilot on the flight to Bali turns out to be Paul, Georgia's boyfriend, who arranged to work this flight, and returns to visit Georgia in Bali a few days later as a surprise.
David and Georgia give their verbal blessing to Lily and Gede, but secretly plan a "Trojan horse" strategy to sabotage the wedding from within.
Their scheme includes stealing the couple's wedding rings, which the couple quickly replaces.
Gede immediately suspects David and Georgia, but hides his suspicions from Lily.
While carrying out this plan, David and Georgia begin to mend fences with each another.
They also get to know Gede and his large extended family and see that he really cares for Lily.

Paul shows up and surprises Georgia with a series of marriage proposals, the first of which is interrupted by a snake bite at the temple of Tanah Lot, and the second is prevented by an accidental head-butt.
When Lily discovers the stolen rings, she demands that they get on board with the wedding or go home.
She also confronts Gede, who simultaneously confesses his harbored suspicions toward David and Georgia stealing the rings.
David and Georgia realize that they will lose Lily forever if they do not support her decision and offer their support.
The wedding proceeds in accordance with Balinese custom.

As the couple prepares to ceremonially stab a dagger through a pandan-leaf mat to complete the bond of marriage, Gede pauses the ceremony to ask David and Georgia to give their blessing sincerely this time, offering not to go through with it unless they agree.
