The two "Barbie"-named girls then made a pact to not let stardom ruin their friendship.
Meanwhile, at the Handler Arts Academy, Emmie appears in disguise so she can be treated like a normal student.
Dean Morrison announces that the annual Spotlight Solo will be livestreamed from Times Square.
Malibu and Brooklyn meet a costume student named Rafael (who wants to be known simply as Rafa) and his dog Gato.
He gives them sequinned dresses that are supposed to sparkle, but the remote control he uses to light up the dresses malfunctions.
During her first week at the academy, "Malibu" Barbie struggles in all of her classes.
Ken calls her to ask how she's doing, but she has mixed feelings.
Later, the "Barbie"-named girls and Rafa discover that Emmie is attending the school in disguise.
When they confronted her, Emmie explains that she lost contact with "Brooklyn" Barbie because of her strict manager-father.
With this, Emmie and "Brooklyn" Barbie rekindle their friendship.
The "Barbie"-named girls and Rafa then sworn to keep Emmie's disguise a secret.
The "Barbie"-named girls go to Central Park and donned on the dresses Rafa gave them.
"Brooklyn" Barbie tells "Malibu" Barbie that her mother is a pilot and her father is worried about her.
"Malibu" Barbie can relate because her father is also uneasy about her being in NYC.
They take photos to send to their fathers, then dance and twirl in front of a fountain, making their dresses sparkle.
Later, Emmie's father, Mr. Miller, comes to Handler Arts Academy to observe the students.
He wants Emmie to have the Spotlight Solo, even though Emmie just wants to learn.
Rafa records the class as Mr. Miller observes.
While Malibu is dancing, she accidentally knocks "Brooklyn" Barbie into an orchestra pit.
"Brooklyn" Barbie lands on a percussionist's drum and sprains her ankle.
"Malibu" Barbie feels guilty about the accident, but she and her friends keep a positive attitude and share their struggles.

According to a witness, Dean Morrison calls "Malibu" Barbie into a meeting and expels her from the academy for sabotaging "Brooklyn" Barbie, who would later be called by the dean to explain her expulsion.
The two "Barbie"-named girls confront each other, break up their friendship and lament over it.

Rafa and Emmie discover that Mr. Miller is behind the hullabaloo, leading the latter to confront her father, with Rafa forwarding his recorded class video to "Brooklyn" Barbie, who in turn shows it to Dean Morrison.
"Malibu" Barbie goes back home to California devastated about the thought of "Brooklyn" Barbie sabotaging her.
With the truth and guilt feeling dawned on her after seeing it all for herself, Barbie decides to give up music.
However, "Brooklyn" Barbie and her mother follows her home route to California so that the former can apologize to "Malibu" Barbie and bring her back to the academy.
They reconciled and when they return to the academy, they find out they had obtained the Spotlight Solo.

On the big night, the MC Emmie reveals her identity during the livestream and introduces the "Barbie"-named girls, who appear in their now-lit-up sequinned outfits Rafa gave them earlier and perform a song about their friendship journey (known as "See You at the Finish Line") while their family and friends watch live in Times Square.
After their performance, Barbie "Malibu" and Barbie "Brooklyn" held each other's opposite hand high to signal their unison whiles fireworks go off above the Times Square's skyscrapers.

77080663.title: The Undercover Strategist (2024 film)
synopsis: As the lights dimmed within the tightly secured, clandestine operations center of the Pentagon, CIA officials John Doe, Sam Smith, and Agent Johnson leaned forward in their chairs, consumed by the projection screen.
It unveiled a terrifying spectacle: a relentless, incipient cyber-attack on America's crucial defense satellites.
A grim understanding, fortified by the sinking sensation of deep dread, dawned on them.
With each successful penetration of the firewall, their alarm increased, culminating in an urgent decision to request assistance from a former colleague, a seasoned operative named Alex Turner.
Known for his unorthodox, maverick methodologies in the world of cybercrime, Alex had once been a pivotal element within CIA ranks.
Now, he was a secluded figure, having chosen a life of distant solitude in the tranquillity of a remote farmhouse in Idaho.
Aware of the gravity of their predicament, John, Sam, and Johnson embark on their mission to extract Alex from his peaceful abode.
Using earnest persuasion peppered with patriotic sentiments, they aimed to entice their once loyal compatriot into service once again.
Alex Turner, quietly nestled in his peaceful hermitage, found himself at life's crossroads.
His tranquillity was thrown into a whirlpool of his chaotic past.
A battle of reason and emotion ensued within him, where the call from his previous duty won over the sweet serenity of his present.
Back in their high-tech cyber centre, they disclosed the specifics of the strategic cyber assault to Alex.
His once dormant, yet ostensibly rusty skills, re-surfaced, reminiscent of a retired warrior skillfully wielding his weapon after years of peaceful oblivion.
His astute understanding of the human psyche coupled with technological prowess worked wonders.
Infiltrating their systems, he managed to gain the adversary's trust.
As Alex delved deeper into his risky operation, he encountered morally challenging situations.
The line between friend and enemy blurred as he found acquaintances amidst the adversaries, bound by common military experiences and paradoxically similar political ideals.
He managed to uncover a much more sinister scheme.
A hair-raising plot to create global economic instability was in motion, causing Alex's adrenaline to spike.
His sympathetic portrayal of the enemy, however, raised eyebrows among his superiors back at the operations centre, sparking questions about his loyalty and intentions.
Suspicion rested heavily within the agency as whispers of doubt spread.
Torn between trusting their former comrade or questioning his loyalty, a schism developed, threatening to shatter the unity of the CIA ranks.
Despite mounting doubt and anxiety, the CIA directors endorsed Alex's warning of the looming financial crisis with cautious understanding.
In the lead-up to D-day, as they braced themselves for an explosive confrontation, the atmosphere vibrated with anxiety and apprehension between the two factions.
The climactic moment spiralled into an intense face-off between Alex and his former allies, igniting a fierce ideological battle coloured with personal betrayals.
Against the backdrop of chaos and confrontation, unexpected alliances emerged.
Deception gave way to sacrifice as individuals gave up their positions in a bid for overall victory.
Once the storm of the mission abated, Alex returned to his rustic Idaho sanctuary, the echo of his traumatic mission causing profound sadness to shadow him as he ventured back into solitude.
Physically unscathed but emotionally scarred, Alex wrestled with the haunting memories of his audacious decisions and the grim reality of espionage.
Taking refuge in the tranquil Idaho wilderness, he aimed to erase the shadows of his recent past.
The mementoes from his mission, however, continued to haunt him, a heavy burden he struggled to shake off.
His once idyllic life now bore the marks of bittersweet victory, grief, and regret, a stark contrast to his previous peaceful existence.

74141436.title: The Bricklayer (2024 film)
synopsis: To fight against Victor Radek, Kate Bannon and O’Malley decide to seek the help of a retired agent Steve Vail, off the books.
O’Malley wants Vail to go to Greece with Kate to find Radek.
Initially, Vail refuses to go on this mission.
He reveals that he has moved on in his life and has become a bricklayer.
But soon, a couple of shooters attack him.
Naturally, this makes him change his mind.
Eventually, he reaches Kozani with Kate and meets his old friend Patricio.
With Patricio’s help, Kate and Vail put on disguises, get armed, and head to Thessaloniki.
They check into a hotel.
While Kate goes to take a shower, Vail sneaks out to rekindle some memories, related to Radek and his family.
Later, he enters a fancy party and meets his old flame, Tye.
He tells her that O’Malley sent him to find Radek who is not dead as they thought.
She warns him about Kostas.
That night, Vail enters a pool party to meet Sten and Crystal to know any details about Radek.
Sten does not reveal anything.
Instead, he threatens Vail, who takes it badly and fights Sten’s pawns.
Luckily, Kate arrives there in time because she had put a tracker on him.
Once in the car, she starts asking him about his history with Radek.
Radek was performing assignments for them.
He joined the CIA for asylum.
But once his cover got blown, the Russians killed his family.
So, he went on a killing rampage.
As a result, the CIA asked Vail to track down Radek and neutralize him.
Back in the US, the CIA receives a threat message from a person who wants to punish them for their wrongdoings.
In exchange for not killing people, he expects a huge payment in Bitcoin.
In Greece, Vail decides to follow Sten with Kate.
They break into Sten’s house and look for any signs of his connection to Radek.
Kate finds Greta Becker’s phone.
Sten’s pawns enters the house.
Vail and Kate fight back and escape after Vail kills him.
Kate apologizes that she froze during the fight.
Vail asks her not to be so hard on herself.
Patricio tells them where they can find the next target Alekos Melas.
They reach the location and see a peaceful march turning into a fight.
Vail suddenly receives a call from Radek.
Radek believes the agency blew his cover because he couldn’t complete one of their assignments.
That’s why he started blackmailing the CIA.
Before Vail can catch him, Radek kills Melas and drives away.
Kate fears that Radek’s list of active targets will antagonize the agency.
Vail thinks that O’Malley is the mole, working with Radek and leaking information to him.
Because of this, Vail finds it difficult to trust the agency.
His accusations make Kate angry.
Still, he firmly believes them.
He goes to meet Tye and reignite their old spark.
She wants him to return home to protect himself from Kostas.
But he doesn’t let that change his mind.
On the other hand, Kate finds two burner phones in Vail’s bag.
So, she suspects he is working with Radek.
He accepts that he is in contact with Radek but does not disclose why.
Later, they both reach Patricio’s storehouse to meet.
Unfortunately, by that time, he was killed by Sten’s men.
Vail starts shooting them one by one.
However, they find Kate and blackmail him to act as per their needs.
He offers himself in exchange for her safety.
Moments after, a bomb goes off leaving all of Sten’s crew dead, whereas Vail walks out safely.
Suddenly, O’Malley decides to remove Vail from their mission.
Then, he sends Kate to finish what they had started.
When in Greece, she reunites with Vail.
He enters a room to transfer the money online and speaks with Radek.
Vail asks Radek to meet in person.
Radek tells him about his one final assignment, a hit on Kostas.
He plans to broadcast the dark truth of the agency on a big scale.
By the time he reveals this, the money transfer is over.
Right after, a bomb explodes.
Vail escapes and immediately starts driving to the venue where Kostas is giving a speech.
As Vail suspected, Radek had reached the spot and put a target on Kostas.
So, Vail finally manages to find Radek in person.
He notices Radek on a stage with other journalists.
He immediately picks up a hammer, destroys the stage, and stops Radek from getting hold of his gun.
Vail apologizes to his old pal for not protecting his family.
Then, Vail shoots Radek.
O’Malley saves Vail from getting incriminated by saying he was working for the agency.
Turns out, the Bitcoin wallet transfer wasn’t done.
Vail most likely made Radek believe that.
However, thanks to his efforts, the CIA finds Radek’s manifesto with all his targets.
Vail meets Tye in her hotel room to learn she worked against him and helped Radek with the list.
While Tye’s men come outside to kill Vail, Tye leaves and starts driving.
Luckily, Kate reaches there and shoots her dead.
Later, O’Malley offers Kate a promotion.
Instead, she decides to stop working for the CIA.
She hopes to work for the country but not for the agency.
After his retirement, Vail returns to his as a Bricklayer.
Vail says that a brick’s form gives him purpose.
O’Malley considers that to be just an incoherent rambling.

54546736.title: Crossroads Collision
synopsis: We meet Emma Bradford, a high-powered lawyer, known for her impressive record of taking on complex corporate cases with grace and skill in New York City.

On her morning route to court for a significant case involving a pharmaceutical company, she collides with a car driven by Jake Morris, a horticulture enthusiast visiting for an Urban Farming convention.
This encounter causes Emma to miss her court hearing, resulting in a crucial loss in the case.
Upon hearing about Emma's missed court appearance, Jake's attitude shifts to deep remorse and he offers to help Emma navigate the city's chaotic streets, sparking a strained friendship.
Jake invites Emma to his hometown Maple Hollow, Connecticut, where his trusted friend owns a renowned automotive repair shop.
In Maple Hollow, Emma becomes enchanted by the town's quiet landscape, the close-knit community and a slower pace of life.
As Emma adjusts to town life whilst Jake works on her car, Emma gets involved in a land dispute threatening Jake's community garden.
Their shared endeavors see their friendship evolve into unexpected romance.
However, as Emma becomes enchanted with her new life, her Manhattan law firm offers her a career-defining promotion which threatens her newfound happiness.

Torn between her legal ambitions and the tranquillity of Maple Hollow, Emma decides to remain in the small town when the land dispute she had volunteered to help with, becomes a serious threat to its harmony.
Emma sets about defending the town, putting her legal skills to good use.
As she defends the residents of Maple Hollow, Emma's bond with Jake strengthens and turns into undeniable attraction.
On the day of the trial, Emma successfully defends the townsfolk ensuring the preservation of the town's peace.
The town celebrates, and Jake confesses his feelings for Emma, who reciprocates.
Emma decides to stay in Maple Hollow, decisions that shocks her Manhattan law firm as she sets up a local law advisory firm in the town.
Emma embraces the rhythm of small-town life, the community bake-offs, peaceful evenings under the Connecticut sky and her romance with Jake.
The townsfolk organize a grand welcome feast for Emma.
Their relationship deepens, and they become integral to the community.
Towards the end, Emma reflects on her journey, her consequential decisions made at literal and figurative crossroads of her life.
She acknowledges the joy and peace she’s found in Jake and the small town.
Standing hand in hand at a crossroad in Maple Hollow, they promise each other an adventurous journey ahead.

66890675.title: The In Between
synopsis: Opening scene: a traffic accident.
Two young people lie on the road, the girl barely moving, the boy, motionless.
Tessa wakes up in the hospital.
In a flashback set 182 days before, Tessa spends the morning taking photos in the coastal town, wandering into the local theater to watch a classic French film.
Skylar, another person watching it, offers to translate.
He is a true romantic, he and Tessa have very different views.
80 days later, Tessa is encouraged to apply to RISD for her photography skills.
Later, while shooting a rowing meet, she finally finds Skylar again.
They both obviously had been searching for each other.
Spending the day together, Tessa shows him the world through her eyes.
At the Empyrean, an abandoned honeymooners hotel, Skylar teaches her to waltz and they kiss.
He tells her he'll return at the end of the month to stay for the summer.
In the present, Tessa is back at school, and is reminded of the RISD deadline.
Later, going home, she throws out her developing materials.
Her adoptive dad reminds her that her mother never stuck to anything.
Dreaming of Skylar, she wakes up to see her Robert Doisneau print of Le baiser de l'hôtel de ville.
Flashback: July 4.
After the fireworks, Tessa shows Skylar her darkroom, portfolio and opens up about her mother's abandonment, forcing her into the foster care system.
They go out on a boat during the day, he teaches her to row, declares his love and they make love on the shore.
Tessa tells her friend Shannon about the In Between, the concept of a window of time in which a recently deceased person needs final contact before moving on.
Sitting the SAT, weirdly Skylar moves her hand on her answer sheet to draw what seems to be a non-sensical scribble.
Then their song, 'Never tear us apart' comes up simultaneously on everyone's silenced mobiles.
Flashback: 11 days before the accident.
Skylar angers Tessa for putting a photo she gifted him in an exhibit to show her talent.
Her inability to express her feelings comes up.
He wants her to realize they could have a future but she continues to hold back.
Photographing her adoptive mother, she suggests expressing her feelings out loud.
Shannon helps Tessa try to channel Skylar after reading several books.
First they try with a planchette, scrying, and instrumental trans-communication Electronic voice phenomenon.
The built-in GPS in her adopted mother's car shows Tessa the same route she had scribbled on her SAT sheet.
So, she blows off returning the car to follow it, arriving to 'The In Between' author Doris she met in the hospital.
She suggests Tessa seek him where they had their strongest connections.
Flashback: 5 days before the accident.
Tessa discovers Skylar is going to Oregon to support his father for the year, leaving her on the East coast.
Taking it as a sign, as she finally has applied to RISD and was about to express her love, she breaks it off.
After buying special photography equipment, Shannon drives Tessa to the places she and Skylar had most closely connected, hoping to reconnect.
Finally they do connect at The Empyrean, but not completely, and he shatters a mirror trying to reach her.
The police catch up with her there, traced through her mobile.
At home, Tessa's adoptive parents are on top of her, she collapses, and in the hospital she's told her heart needs to be repaired the next day.
Shannon sneaks her out, with Skylar's help (he manipulates some electronics, distracting the nurses, then guides them to the site of the accident).
In a flashback to the night of the accident, Shannon convinces Tessa to catch Skylar before he leaves.
The timelines overlap.
As paramedics attend Tessa's collapsed body, reunited with Skylar briefly, they are in Paris, in black and white, like the Doisneau print Le baiser.
They are back at a house on the beach, and she hears from far off her adoptive mom calling her back.
Tearfully, she reminds him that 'love never dies', and decides to go back to live.
In a mid-credits scene, Tessa and Skylar are wandering around the beach, tracing their silouettes in the sand.

38692246.title: Complete Remembrance (2084 film)
synopsis: John Smith, a dedicated construction worker known for his diligent attention to minuscule details and his unusually philosophical nature, was haunted every night by colorful dreams about an aquatic planet, similar to Neptune.
In those dreams, a spectral woman with captivating teal eyes would always appear, seeming to plead desperately for his aid.
Fuelled by those strange dreams and his intense curiosity, John trudged through his daily routine on the construction site.
He felt a constant sense of bewilderment, perplexed by the vivid nature of the recurring dreams that he couldn't shake off.

One day laden with unexpected occurrences, John was handling an earth-boring drill among the clamorous chaos of the construction site, when he discovered an incredible secret hiding just beneath his feet.
As his machine relentlessly burrowed into the depths of the Earth’s crust, it exposed an ancient artifact.
The artifact bore the weight of eons, encased in an impenetrable shroud of dust and hidden under a cloak of intriguing enigma.
John was strangely drawn to the artifact.
Its unusual appearance and the alien glyphs etched onto it in an intricate pattern astonished him, breaking the droning monotony of his mundane life filled mostly with concrete and hard hats.
With a hand trembling from anticipation, he toggled a switch on the strange device, sending a cascade of holographic light into the construction site.
Astonishingly, he had unwittingly unlocked a mesmerizing three-dimensional projection.
The air around the construction site started swirling with radiant hues as the woman from his dreams materialized in front of him.
Her holographic figure maintained that earnest plea from his dreams that had haunted him nightly.
Rocked to the core by the surreal turn of events, John was left confounded.
A dream had intertwined itself with his reality, unearthing a mysterious artifact.
It was then John resolved to undertake a daring journey to the aquatic planet he'd been seeing in his dreams—Neptune.
Rallying his tight-knit group of friends–each with skills in diverse fields and united by a longing for challenging adventures–John unfurled his audacious blueprint towards Neptune.
Pooling their collective construction expertise, John and his teammates erected a makeshift spaceship from salvaged materials.
They worked tirelessly using discarded mechanical components and surplus steel and aluminum to fuel their ambitious endeavor.
Their night-time toiling was not without observers, and they soon attracted the unwanted attention of the unyielding mega-corporation for which they worked.
The corporation, notorious for its ironclad grip on potential profit sources, identified their clandestine project and the ancient artifact as potential avenues of interest or threats to neutralize.
The workers soon found themselves transformed into prey, a dangerous game of cat-and-mouse commenced between them and the relentless corporate forces.
Their hunting grounds: a patchwork of concrete and steel towers scraping the skies.
Backed into a corner, John spearheaded the successful launch of their makeshift spaceship, flickering hope starkly against the incoming menace of the corporation’s tyranny.
Journeying to Neptune was one fraught with trials.
It was a grueling test of nerves, resilience, and technical skills beset on all sides by unforeseen hurdles and disruptions.

Frustrating glitches within their assembled spaceship's system threatened to derail their progress, and random meteor showers pummeled their path, forcing them to face survival trials on an astronomical scale.
In the faceless vastness of space, with the Earth reduced to a simple speck, the unity of John and his team was strained.
Differences fueled by fear and the stress of their situation simmered, igniting sparks of dissent that threatened to dissolve their unity.
Amid the crew's internal strife, John managed to decode the alien script etched into the artifact.
The antiquated artifact metamorphosed into a cosmic key, revealing the ability to interface with and control an advanced technology hidden deep beneath Neptune's icy surface.
The monumental revelation injected a newfound significance into their journey, helping them press on, strengthened by the shared enthusiasm of unknown territories.
Upon setting foot on Neptune’s frosty surface, they were bewildered by the surprisingly inhabitable conditions, courtesy of the advanced alien tech that regulated the environment.

As John and his team traversed the mesmerizing alien landscape, they made a fascinating discovery: the woman from John's dreams, Eris, was not an illusion but a tangible entity—a breathtaking human-alien hybrid who was far less alien than they had anticipated.
Eris, living in self-imposed exile to escape the clutches of power-hungry corporations on Earth, took refuge on Neptune.
She substantiated every dream that John had seen, bringing the phantom to reality.
She explained the lethal potential of alien technology in the hands of unscrupulous humans, painting a grim picture of a dystopian future.
Eris also had dangerous news for John and his team—a corporate fleet, hell-bent on exploiting her and her secrets, was hot on their trail, determined to claim Neptune as its own.
United against the common enemy, John and Eris, along with his friends, cadged together a concrete plan to outwit the incoming pillagers.
Marshaling the overwhelming potential of alien technology, they also relied heavily on their shared resolve, and strategic manoeuvres, as they steeled themselves for the impending battle.
As predicted, the corporate fleet launched their offensive in a merciless display of power.
Their meticulously outlined strategies, however, began to crumble under the sustained and resilient opposition from Eris, John, and his friends.
Utilizing the alien technology expertly, John and his team gained the upper hand in their struggle against the corporate mercenaries.
Facing the threat of a crushing defeat, the corporate troops were left with no choice but to retreat.
The victory marked a decisive moment in favor of John and his rag-tag team of cosmic rebels.

They now custodians of alien technology sufficiently advanced to appear as magic, John and his friends made a pact—they’d keep this tech a secret from humanity’s unrelenting grasp, relinquishing any possibility of turning a profit.
Life irrevocably transformed, John Smith—who was once a mere construction worker—now stood as a guardian of the cosmic order, dwelling on a planet where no human had set foot before.
John chose to remain on Neptune with Eris, leaving his past life behind.
He carved out a new life for himself, embracing his responsibilities as a sentinel of the unknown and a consistent influence maintaining the delicate balance in the cosmos.
Over time, his bond with Eris grew stronger while his ties with his old life back on Earth grew fainter, turning him slowly into a stalwart guard of a universal secret.
Their shared experiences and the adversity they overcome had forged a bond of friendship within the team, which would forever relate them to one another.
Their journey had turned them from simple construction workers into celestial protectors.
They took on their new role with a sense of reverence.
They were now the guardians of cosmic secrets, the pioneers of a new era, a beacon for any misdirected or lost kickstart in the universe.

Their journey from Earth to Neptune, from turmoil, conflict, and near-annihilation to triumphant survival, stood as a testament to the indomitable spirit and resilience of humankind—even in the face of alien worlds and formidable, unknown technology.

Back on Earth, the conglomerate that had pursued them with dogged determination continued to loom in the background, representing a constant reminder of the insatiable human hunger for power and control that was unchecked back home.
Neptune, flourishing under its new guardians and the secrets they guarded, didn’t seem to care much about the crises unravelling on Earth.
Tales of John's extraordinary voyage reverberated within the confines of construction sites on Earth.
His daring adventure sparked a sense of boundless possibilities in the hearts of many.
John and Eris, in their outpost on the farthest edge of the known universe, continued their cosmic watch.
Their bond deepened with each passing moment, bringing them closer in their mission to guard the expansive cosmos.
John had shown remarkable grit and determination in his journey, embracing his role as the new "Cosmic Guardian" readily.
The man who once was limited to the tough, mundane life of manual labor had found a higher purpose.
He was now tasked with the exclusive duty of protecting unseen parts of the universe from known threats.
The journey that John embarked on, one that he thought was a one-off, had left a formidable imprint on human history, marking the first successful human voyage to Neptune.
The tale of John's ordinary beginnings—as a diligent construction worker—the friendships he crafted during his odyssey, and the victorious result redefined the essence of true heroism.

It was the story of an unassuming man who, driven by his dreams, risked all odds to protect an alien secret and left a powerful message for those inspired to dream beyond the sphere of human existence.
A legend in his own right, John Smith had lived the extraordinary tale, transitioning from the life of an ordinary construction worker to the guardian of a divine cosmic secret.
His story was an exemplary tale of an unlikely hero, etched firmly in the annals of history and in the hearts of those who dared to dream.

55325.title: Total Recall (1990 film)
synopsis: In 2084, Douglas Quaid is an Earthbound construction worker having troubling dreams about Mars and a mysterious woman there.

His wife Lori dismisses the dreams and discourages him from thinking about Mars, where the governor, Vilos Cohaagen, is fighting rebels while searching for a rumored alien artifact located in the mines.
At "Rekall", a company that provides memory implants of vacation, Quaid opts for a memory trip to Mars as a secret agent.
However, during the procedure, Quaid violently reacts before the memory is implanted.
The company re-sedates him, wipes his memory of the Rekall visit, and sends him home.
On the way home, Quaid is attacked by his co-workers and is forced to kill them.
He then is attacked by armed thugs led by Lori and Richter, her real husband and Cohaagen's subordinate.
After evading his attackers, Quaid is given a suitcase containing money, gadgets, and a video recording.
The video is of Quaid, apparently called "Hauser", who explains that he used to work for Cohaagen but learned about the artifact, and underwent the memory wipe to protect himself.
The "Hauser" instructs Quaid on removing a tracking device, before ordering him to go to Mars and meet "Kuato".
Quaid makes his way to Mars and follows clues to Venusville, the colony's red-light district populated by a people mutated by poor radiation shielding.
He meets Melina, the woman from his dreams, but she spurns him, believing that Quaid is working for Cohaagen.
Quaid later encounters Lori and Rekall's President, Dr. Edgemar.
Edgemar insists Quaid is living out the implanted memories, and offers Quaid a pill that would wake him from the dream.
Quaid however sees Edgemar sweating in fear, and kills him instead.
Richter's forces capture Quaid, but Melina rescues him with Quaid killing Lori in the process.
The two race back to the Venusville bar and escape into the tunnels with their taxi driver Benny.
Unable to locate Quaid, Cohaagen shuts down the ventilation to Venusville, slowly suffocating its citizens.
Quaid, Melina, and Benny are taken to a resistance base, and Quaid is introduced to Kuato, a deformed humanoid conjoined to his brother's stomach.

Kuato reads Quaid's mind and learns that the artifact is a turbinium reactor that will create a breathable atmosphere for Mars when activated, eliminating Cohaagen's abusive monopoly on breathable air.
Cohaagen's forces burst in, led by Benny, and kill most of the resistance, including Kuato, who instructs Quaid to start the reactor.
Quaid and Melina are taken to Cohaagen, who reveals the Quaid persona was a ploy by Hauser to infiltrate the mutants and lead Cohaagen to Kuato, thereby wiping out the resistance.
Cohaagen orders Hauser's memory to be reimplanted in Quaid and Melina to be programmed to be Hauser's slave, but Quaid and Melina escape into the mines where the reactor is located.
They work their way to the control room of the reactor, killing Benny, Richter, and the rest of his men.
While running away in the reactor, Cohaagen confronts them in the control room with a bomb.
but Quaid accidentally sets it off, blowing out one of the walls of the control room, causing an explosive decompression.
Quaid grabs on the wall, but knocks Coohagen out, which causes him to land on the surface of Mars.
Due to the low atmospheric pressure, his internal fluids boil out, killing him.
Quaid manages to activate the reactor before he and Melina are also pulled out.
The reactor releases air into the Martian atmosphere, saving Quaid, Melina and the population of Venusville.
As humans walk onto the surface of the planet in its new atmosphere, Quaid takes a moment to wonder whether he is still living the memory before turning to kiss Melina.

63336851.title: Suburban Scholars: The Saturday Class
synopsis: The movie curtains rise to reveal a sweeping, picturesque scene of Elmwood, a sophisticated, well-manicured suburban enclave ensconced in the heartland of Naperville, Illinois.

Stepping into Elmwood, we are introduced to five discernible, distinct teenagers who come from different walks of life, each with their own unique characteristics and challenges, forming the nucleus of our story.
First, we are introduced to Jake, a rebellious teen recognizable from his worn, tattered leather jacket and wild hair.
Crossing town, we enter the practice grounds of Naperville High, where we find our next character.
Matt, the school's adored quarterback, is practicing under the sun.
From the muscular football player, we shift to Grace, engrossed in perusing "A Brief History of Time" by Stephen Hawking.
Moving to Elmwood's local thrift store, Violet, the town's identified eccentric is found exploring the rows of vintage records.
Next, the narrative takes us into the school's state-of-the-art gymnasium, where Emily, the school’s perceived embodiment of perfection and cheerleader captain, is seen practicing her routines.
The plot twists when each of the main characters receives a cryptically ominous note from an unexpected courier - the steely eyed and often intimidating Frank, the school's janitor.
The subsequent Saturday unfolds within the confines of a seemingly mundane detention classroom.
The first interaction amongst them rings with undisguised hostility, animosity bristling through their terse exchanges, and acerbic observations.
However, as they spend time together, the surface-level discussions of why they have landed in detention evolve into poignant stories of their personal battles and unseen tribulations.
Jake reveals his unruly behavior is a mask for his challenging home life.
Following suit, Matt provides insight into his life off the field, revealing the burden he carries to maintain his status as a leading athlete.
Grace reveals her constant battle with being intellectually superior in an environment where this makes her a target.
Emily uncovers the relentless pressure she experiences in maintaining her position as a popular cheerleader.
Lastly, Violet sheds her quirky facade and admits to the often stifling loneliness she experiences as a non-conformist amidst a crowd of predictable patterns.
Finding common ground through their individual struggles they decide to band together to outsmart their rigid principal, Mr. Chandler.
In a strategic whisper, each member contributes to an elaborate scheme, crafting a meticulous plan to escape the stifling classroom of detention.
Displaying tangible audacity, they stealthily maneuver through the unfamiliar maze beneath the school, evading patrolling janitors.
As they navigate their way to freedom, they realize their experiences have kindled an emergent friendship, undermining their earlier misconceptions of each other.
They slip back into detention just as the imposing thump of Mr. Chandler's steps reverberate ominously through the quiet hallways.
The shared adventure fosters a deeper, more understanding dialogue about their dreams, fears and secrets, strengthening their nascent bond.
Solidifying their new friendship, they shake hands to seal an agreement, promising respect, understanding, and support to every member of the group.
This pact induces an emotional catharsis, where they accept both their and their peers' flaws and imperfections.
The narrative returns to the ensuing Monday, where the newly formed clique confidently strides through Naperville High.
Together, they challenge inherited norms and expectations, refusing to be boxed into their preconceived characters anymore.
As the final bell rings, amidst astonished gazes, a haunting voiceover crowns them as “The Suburban Scholars”.
The story reaches its climax, cataloging their journeys of self-discovery, acceptance and the solidification of a solid camaraderie.
The movie ends leaving viewers with the potent message of breaking societal norms and acknowledging authentic friendships above all else.

29943.title: The Breakfast Club
synopsis: On March 24, 1984, five students — "criminal" John Bender, "athlete" Andrew Clark, "brain" Brian Johnson, "basket case" Allison Reynolds, and "princess" Claire Standish — report for Saturday morning detention at Shermer High School in the Chicago suburb of Shermer, Illinois.
While not complete strangers, each of them comes from a different clique, and they seem to have nothing in common.

They gather in the high school library where they are instructed by the assistant principal, Richard Vernon, not to speak, move from their seats, or sleep for a period of eight hours, fifty-four minutes (from 7:06 AM to 4 PM).
He assigns a 1,000-word essay to the students in which each must write about who he or she is.
He then leaves, returning only occasionally to check on them.
Bender, who has a particularly antagonistic relationship with Vernon, disregards the rules and constantly riles the other students, mocking Brian and Andrew and harassing Claire.
Allison is initially quiet except for the occasional random outburst.
The students pass the hours by arguing and smoking marijuana that Bender retrieves from his locker.

Gradually, they open up to each other and reveal their deepest personal secrets: Allison is a compulsive liar, Andrew hates his father, John comes from an abusive household, Brian has contemplated suicide, and Claire is a virgin.
They discover that they all have strained relationships with their parents and are afraid of making the same mistakes as the adults around them.
However, despite these developing friendships, the students are afraid that once the detention is over, they will return to their very different cliques and never speak to each other again.
Towards the end of the day, the other students ask Brian to write the essay that Vernon assigned earlier.

Brian does so, but instead of writing about the assigned topic, he writes a letter objecting to Vernon's request to describe who they are, stating that the man has already judged who they are (an athlete, basket case, princess, brain, and criminal), and that he will not accept any different accounts from them.
Brian signs the essay as "The Breakfast Club" and leaves it at the table for Vernon to read after they leave.
Before the students part ways outside the school, Allison and Andrew kiss, as do Claire and John.

23320969.title: Warrior: Scheme Orion (American film 1998)
synopsis: Located in the isolated expanses of the wilderness, highly camouflaged under the guise of an innocuous electrical power plant, Spark Eye Corporation houses a state-of-the-art, clandestine underground facility of unprecedented technological marvel.
This high-tech labyrinth hosts a veil of darkness over sinister operations that lurk in the shadows, led by the enigmatic Brigadier General Mars.
These operations involve the chilling kidnapping of newborn infants from blindfolded and unsuspecting parents, executed with utmost precision and absolute secrecy.
Jack Thompson, a former marine living a quiet, retired life amongst the tranquility of the small country town of Ramsgate, unwillingly gets snared in this spiderweb of uncertainty.
His placid existence is brutally upturned like a whirlwind when his newborn son, Ethan, inexplicably disappears.
His life of peace abruptly diminishes, replaced by a ferocious storm of despair and an unyielding resolve to reunite with his vanished son.
As Jack embarks deeper into the confounding abyss of Ethan's missing case, he unraveled the enigma of Project Orion - an ultra-secretive operation spearheaded by the Spark Eye Corporation.
The mounting evidence pointed towards Project Orion being the likely culprit behind Ethan’s sudden abduction.
Jack plunges further into the gloomy labyrinth of Project Orion.
Feeling isolated and aiming to bolster his forces, Jack reaches out to his old military comrades, who express disbelief but eventually resolve to assist him.
Jack enlists a band of dedicated individuals including combat specialists, tech wizards, stealth experts, and a few undercover operatives camouflaged within the ranks of Spark Eye.
Grave Patterson, a former surgeon turned fugitive, becomes Jack's closest ally and support system.
Jack and his team uncover essential details about the Spark Eye Corporation, forming the backbone for their large-scale infiltration planned for the imminent future.
Each successful mission invigorates them, fueled by their commitment, they become a beacon of hope to save the helpless lives ensnared in the corporation’s clutches.
Amid the dawn, Jack and his team initiate their final, most daring operation infiltrating the fortified confines of the heavily guarded Spark Eye facility.
Grace uncovers the bone-chilling truth behind Project Orion: Spark Eye Corp. had a terrifying agenda of militarizing the kidnapped infants as superhuman child soldiers.
This revelation expands Jack’s responsibility beyond saving his child to combating a concealed threat that could wreak havoc on a global scale.
Strengthened by a call from his wife Linda, who implores him to return with their child safely.
Jack and his team infiltrate the fortified confines of the corporation, reaching the core of the facility where the kidnapped children were held.
As they fight their way through genetically enhanced soldiers, their path is laden with deadly encounters.
Jack overpowers Brigadier General Mars, locates Ethan and the other children, the innocent, young victims subjected to Project Orion's inhuman exploitation.
He takes Ethan into a comforting embrace, promising safety.
This moment resonates with the other children, ready for their imminent evacuation.
Their retreat triggers retaliation from the Spark Eye Corporation.
Evidence regarding Project Orion covertly secured by Grace finds its way to the public, pushing the Spark Eye Corporation into an irrevocable scandal.
Consequently, an immediate shutdown of the corporation and all its operations is commissioned.
Jack's tearful reunion with his wife Linda marks a raw, emotional moment.
Jack pledges to transform the abandoned facility into a sanctuary for the children rescued from its clutches.
Against all odds, Jack's vision of optimism takes concrete shape turning the barren vestiges of Project Orion into a beacon of hope.
Jack's continuous efforts to provide Ethan with emotional support and care begins to show positive effects.
The ex-soldiers find a new purpose in life as mentors, caregivers to the children at the center.
Grace, assuming the role of the center's head, uses her medical expertise and compassion to drive the center's operations.
Official recognition and public support towards the rehabilitation center soon follow, becoming a symbol of resilience and restoration.
The narrative jumps forward to the yearly celebration at the center, a testimony to their indomitable spirit, courage, and the triumphant future that lies ahead.

730819.title: Soldier (1998 American film)
synopsis: In the near future, as part of a new military training program ("Project Adam"), a group of infants are selected at birth and raised as soldiers.
Undergoing extreme mental and physical training, they become virtual sociopaths, extremely disciplined, but with no understanding of anything except military routine and war.
The soldiers are conditioned to never speak unless spoken to, to completely ignore physical pain, and to address whomever they are speaking to (women included) as "sir".
At the age of 49, Sgt.
Todd 3465 (Kurt Russell) is a hardened veteran of many battles, but his unit is about to be replaced.
Colonel Mekum (Jason Isaacs) introduces a new group of genetically engineered soldiers, designed with superior physical attributes and a complete lack of emotion, except aggression.
Todd's unit's commander, Captain Church (Gary Busey) insists on testing the "new" soldiers' abilities against his own.
But Todd, the unit's best soldier, is no match for Caine 607 (Jason Scott Lee).
In the final trial, a fight between Caine and three "old" soldiers, two of Todd's comrades are killed, though Todd manages to gouge out one of Caine's eyes before he is defeated.
Todd seemingly dies when he falls from a great height; but the body of a dead soldier cushions his fall, and he is simply knocked unconscious.
Mekum orders their bodies dumped like garbage, and the remaining "old" soldiers are demoted to menial support roles.
Meanwhile Caine gets an artificial blue eye to replace the brown eye he lost.
Todd and his dead comrades are dumped on the surface of Arcadia 234, a waste disposal planet with dangerously high winds.
Though badly injured, Todd limps toward a colony of humans who crash-landed there twelve years earlier, and have managed to survive and build a society from the planet's mountains of trash.
Though they try to make him welcome, Todd has difficulty adapting to the community due to his extreme conditioning and their extreme pacifism.
Todd's training, and subsequently stunted social skills, make it difficult for him to answer in anything more than curt replies.
Many of the settlers are afraid of him, but he is accepted and sheltered by Mace (Sean Pertwee) and his wife Sandra (Connie Nielsen).
Todd develops a silent rapport with their mute son, Nathan (Jared and Taylor Throne), who had been traumatized by a snakebite earlier in his life.
In a later conflict with a coiled snake, Todd teaches Nathan how to face it down and strike back to protect himself.
His parents misinterpret the lesson, unsure of how to deal with Todd.
However, Todd soon begins to experience flashbacks from his time as a soldier and mistakes one of the pacifist colonists (Michael Chiklis) for an enemy, nearly killing him.
The pacifists decide that Todd is too dangerous to live among them, so they give him supplies and democratically vote him out of the colony.
Outside the colony, he sheds tears, but appears confused, implying that this is the first time in his life that he has ever cried.
A short time later, Mace and Sandra are almost bitten by another snake while sleeping, but are saved by Nathan, who used Todd's technique.
Mace then realizes that Todd taught their son how to protect his parents from the snakes.
He also realizes that Todd has an important role to play in their community, and decides to search for the soldier on his own and bring him back.
The colonists object, saying that they had voted him out democratically, but Mace insists that "We voted wrong."
The new genetically engineered soldiers arrive on the garbage planet for a training exercise.
Since the world is listed as uninhabited, Colonel Mekum decides that the pacifists' presence is unlawful and, for practice, orders his troops to slaughter them.
Frightened children hide underground and hope not to be seen.
Mace is spotted by the troops and killed just after he finds Todd.
Though outmanned and outgunned, Todd's years of battle experience and superior knowledge of the planet allow him to return to the colony and kill the advance squad attacking the pacifists.
Nervous that an unknown enemy force may be confronting them, Colonel Mekum orders the soldiers to withdraw and return with heavy artillery.
Using guerilla tactics, Todd outmaneuvers and defeats all of the remaining soldiers, including Caine 607, who is defeated in hand-to-hand combat.

Panicking, Mekum orders the transport ship's crew, composed of Todd's old squad, to set up and activate a portable nuclear device powerful enough to destroy the planet, then orders the ship to lift off, leaving the squad behind.
When Captain Church objects, Mekum shoots him in cold blood.

Before they can take off as planned, Todd appears, and his old comrades recognize him as the ranking officer due to their conditioning and silently side with him over the army that has discarded them.
Todd and his comrades take over the ship, leaving Mekum and his aides on the planet, then evacuate the remaining colonists just before the bomb detonates.
Mekum wets his pants as he realizes he is helpless.
Todd orders the ship to set course for the Trinity Moons, the colonists' original destination, then picks up Nathan and points to their new destination, while looking out upon the galaxy.

74819072.title: Proletarian Prodigy: Journey to Triumph
synopsis: Our cinematic journey begins with an expansive panorama of the city of Kolkata, India.
Among these slums, lives our boy-hero, Aadi.
Trapped in the labyrinth of the city's streets and bustling marketplaces, we encounter Aadi, an eager young boy of humble birth.
From the earliest light of dawn, Aadi embarks on his daily routine of scavenging through mounds of refuse.
His clothes, little more than tatters barely covering his thin frame, his feet bare and dirt-coated from walking on grimy city pavements, fail to suppress his passion for learning.
Every street corner, every alley, becomes a classroom in Aadi's inspiring vision of his city.
His already sparked interest blazes further when the local radio broadcasts a trivia contest, fashioned after the global phenomenon, 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire.'

The chance to participate in such a contest pricks his imagination and Aadi begins to fantasize about the potential of showcasing his knowledge and hopefully transform his own reality from his stringent existence to something more promising.

In his solitary preparation for the big quiz, Aadi's mind wanders into the corridors of his painful past — the early demise of his parents, his relentless pursuit of his education in an environment devoid of the bare minimum.
The contest day finally arrives and we find Aadi, our champion-in-making, cozied up on the trivia's hot seat, face an embodiment of pure fear mixed with stark excitement.
As the contest kicks off, each right answer from Aadi steadily amasses increasing awe from the engaging audience and his contemptuous competitors.
The nail-biting suspense climbs higher and higher as Aadi sturdily moves to the final rounds, asserting his dominance and resilience in the competition.
A riveting plot twist occurs when the quiz host, out of the blue, brings forth an accusation against Aadi of rigging the game just before the final life-changing question.
Amidst overwhelming objections and in spite of Aadi's earnest protest, he is abruptly ousted from the show, a cloud of disgrace hanging over his dreams.
Dejected and heartbroken, Aadi finds solace in Nilam, another fellow scholar living in the same underprivileged circumstances, yet refusing to bend to them.
In a heartfelt and intense dialogue, Aadi shares with Nilam his crushed ambitions, but reasserts his unbroken resolve to uncover the truth and prove his innocence.
Touched by his unyielding spirit, Nilam pledges her support and promises to aid him on this challenging path.
Their struggle unfolds in an invigorating sequence where both Aadi and Nilam meticulously scour the city and libraries for each trivia question and its corresponding answer.
Gradually, they realize a startling revelation - Aadi's answers matched accuracy with the obscure episodes of his own life.
An astonishing realization evolves: Aadi did not cheat; the experiences of his life, gleaned from various unnoticed sources, simply prepared him to answer the contest's questions correctly.
Gathering their meticulously collated evidence, Aadi and Nilam make their case public and challenge the earlier accusation in a high-tension legal debate.
Astonished, the audiences watch as their extensive evidence successfully unveils the host's concealed intentions.
Recognizing Aadi's earnestness, the general public starts fervently rallying for him, demanding justice for the slandered boy.
Silenced watchers transform into vehement protestors, their dissent against the injustice growing louder and unyielding.
Consequently, Aadi is warmly reinstated to the trivia show amidst pulsating applause, assuring him a second chance to fair victory.
A renewed and confident Aadi courageously answers the final question correctly, scripting an unprecedented victory in the history of the quiz.
His victory spawns uncontained joy among friends, neighbors, and even strangers, bringing everyone into unison to celebrate his success.
Epilogue sees the establishment of a learning center, financed from the prize money Aadi won at the trivia show.
The newly erected learning center, rooted in Aadi’s aspirations, stands firm amidst Kolkata’s desolate poverty, radiating hope.
The narrative concludes with a shot of Aadi’s serene countenance, triumphantly signifying the transformative power of knowledge and the indomitable spirit of human tenacity.

15233369.title: Slumdog Millionaire
synopsis: In Mumbai in 2006, eighteen-year-old Jamal Malik (Dev Patel), a former street child (child Ayush Mahesh Khedekar, adolescent Tanay Chheda) from the Juhu slum, is a contestant on the Indian version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, and is one question away from the grand prize.
However, before the Rs.
20 million question, he is detained and interrogated by the police, who suspect him of cheating because of the impossibility of a simple "slumdog" with very little education knowing all the answers.
Jamal recounts, through flashbacks, the incidents in his life which provided him with each answer.

These flashbacks tell the story of Jamal, his brother Salim (adult Madhur Mittal, adolescent Ashutosh Lobo Gajiwala, child Azharuddin Mohammed Ismail), and Latika (adult Freida Pinto, adolescent Tanvi Ganesh Lonkar, child Rubina Ali).
In each flashback Jamal has a point to remember one person, or song, or different things that lead to the right answer of one of the questions.
The row of questions does not correspond chronologically to Jamal's life, so the story switches between different periods (childhood, adolescence) of Jamal.
Some questions do not refer to points of his life (cricket champion), but by witness he comes to the right answer.

Jamal's flashbacks begin with his managing, at age five, to obtain the autograph of Bollywood star Amitabh Bachchan, which his brother then sells, followed immediately by the death of his mother during the Bombay Riots.
As they flee the riot, they run into a child version of the God Rama, Salim and Jamal then meet Latika, another child from their slum.

Salim is reluctant to take her in, but Jamal suggests that she could be the third musketeer, a character from the Alexandre Dumas novel (which they had been studying — albeit not very diligently — in school), whose name they do not know.
The three are found by Maman (Ankur Vikal), a gangster who tricks and then trains street children into becoming beggars.
When Jamal, Salim, and Latika learn Maman is blinding children in order to make them more effective as singing beggars, they flee by jumping onto a departing train.
Latika catches up and takes Salim's hand, but Salim purposely lets go, and she is recaptured by the gangsters.

Over the next few years, Salim and Jamal make a living travelling on top of trains, selling goods, picking pockets, working as dish washers, and pretending to be tour guides at the Taj Mahal, where they steal people's shoes.

At Jamal's insistence, they return to Mumbai to find Latika, discovering from Arvind, one of the singing beggars, that she has been raised by Maman to become a prostitute and that her virginity is expected to fetch a high price.
The brothers rescue her, and Salim draws a gun and kills Maman.
Salim then manages to get a job with Javed (Mahesh Manjrekar), Maman's rival crime lord.
Arriving at their hotel room, Salim orders Jamal to leave him and Latika alone.
When Jamal refuses, Salim draws a gun on him, and Jamal leaves after Latika persuades him to go away (presumably so he wouldn't get hurt by Salim).
Years later, while working as a tea server at an Indian call centre, Jamal searches the centre's database for Salim and Latika.
He fails in finding Latika but succeeds in finding Salim, who is now a high-ranking lieutenant in Javed's organization, and they reunite.
Salim is regretful for his past actions and only pleads for forgiveness when Jamal physically attacks him.
Jamal then bluffs his way into Javed's residence and reunites with Latika.
While Jamal professes his love for her, Latika asks him to forget about her.
Jamal promises to wait for her every day at 5 o'clock at the VT station.
Latika attempts to rendezvous with him, but she is recaptured by Javed's men, led by Salim.
Jamal loses contact with Latika when Javed moves to another house, outside of Mumbai.
Knowing that Latika watches it regularly, Jamal attempts to make contact with her again by becoming a contestant on the show Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?
He makes it to the final question, despite the hostile attitude of the show's host, Prem Kumar (Anil Kapoor), and becomes a wonder across India.
Kumar feeds Jamal the incorrect response to the penultimate question and, when Jamal still gets it right, turns him into the police on suspicion of cheating.

Back in the interrogation room, the police inspector (Irrfan Khan) calls Jamal's explanation "bizarrely plausible", but thinks he is not a liar and, ripping up the arrest warrant, allows him to return to the show.
At Javed's safehouse, Latika watches the news coverage of Jamal's miraculous run on the show.
Salim, in an effort to make amends for his past behaviour, quietly gives Latika his mobile phone and car keys, and asks her to forgive him and to go to Jamal.
Latika, though initially reluctant out of fear of Javed, agrees and escapes.
Salim fills a bathtub with cash and sits in it, waiting for the death he knows will come when Javed discovers what he has done.
Jamal's final question is, by coincidence, the name of the third musketeer in The Three Musketeers, a fact he never learned.
Jamal uses his Phone-A-Friend lifeline to call Salim's cell, as it is the only phone number he knows.
Latika succeeds in answering the phone just in the nick of time, and, while she does not know the answer, tells Jamal that she is safe.
Relieved, Jamal randomly picks Aramis, the right answer, and wins the grand prize.
Simultaneously, Javed discovers that Salim has helped Latika escape after he hears Latika on the show.
He and his men break down the bathroom door, and Salim kills Javed, before being gunned down himself at the hands of Javed's men.
With his dying breath, Salim gasps, "God is great."
Later that night, Jamal and Latika meet at the railway station and kiss.
The movie ends with a dance scene on the platform to "Jai Ho".

41996238.title: Echoes of Deception
synopsis: The aroma of burnt wood and despair hangs heavily over the village that was recently razed by the British onslaught.
The expressions on the faces of the American revolutionary soldiers are grim, their hearts heavy with the aftermath of the devastating battle.
The once lively streets are now ghostly, abandoned, echoing the profound loss inhabitants of the village have experienced.
Amid the discouragement, Bea, a female soldier renowned for her wits, stands tall.
She lights up the dimly lit cabin with her strategy, elaborately detailing plans to ensnare Captain James "Jim" Bristow - a distinguished and notorious British officer.
Bea never banks on men's underestimation of women, drawing strength from her courage instead of relying on society's misplaced assumptions.
Tonight, though, she consents to don a guise of feigned vulnerability, trusting her intelligence to keep her safe.
Using her feminine charm, she is determined to win Jim's trust.
With a well-crafted lie on her lips and a believable backstory, Bea embarks on a risky venture.
Accompanied by a seemingly besotted Jim, they set off on a river journey down the Potomac, their boat bobbing along under the pretense of a romantic escape.
However, beneath the tranquillity looms a chilling plot of entrapment.
Arriving at their supposed romantic retreat, Bea reveals her ruse.
Expertly tripping hidden alarms in the wilderness, she ensnares a stunned Jim with the help of her rebel comrades waiting in silence.
In the face of relentless questioning from Bea, Jim remains composed.
Then, amidst the hostile interrogation, Jim sees through Bea's hardened exterior and in an unexpected turn of events engages her in deep conversations about life, war, and loss.
Through this moment of weakness, Bea's past is unveiled.
Images of her childhood marred by war, the relentless determination that took her through countless trials and tribulations, and the burning resolve for her cause, all surge to the forefront.
Bea's concurrent past and present create a whirl of emotions.
She experiences a wrestling match between her staunch dedication to the American cause and the awkward understanding she seems to be developing towards her British captive.
Breaking her reverie, the watchman's birdcall shatters the silence.
It is a warning sign, a coded message signifying the imminent approach of British troops towards their hidden base.

Bea is thrust back into reality as the rebel leader, sweating and fidgety, confronts her with a morose proposal - to execute Jim immediately to avoid his plea for reinforcements when the British inevitably find them.
Bea, now engulfed by sympathy for Jim, intertwines her newfound feelings with her strategic prowess, creating a audacious plan to free him.
Every decision she makes here comes with consequences that could radically alter her standing with her fellow rebels.
Under the cover of a moonless night, Bea sabotages the lone watchtower, plunging their hideout into darkness, subsequently assisting Jim's daring escape.
Jim reaches the safety of his camp, disappearing into the fortified barriers, leaving Bea amidst the ensuing chaos, a memory imprinted in his mind.
Branded a traitor, Bea finds herself deserted by her rebel comrades.
Unyielding, she uses her solitude to strengthen her resolve, preparing herself to confront the inevitable rebel attack.
As dawn breaks, the bitterness of the prior night's treason, loss, and retribution hangs in the air.
As the sun rises, illuminating the aftermath of the prison break, it mirrors the relentless cycle of war.
Although Bea's journey ends, her tale continues to resonate through Jim.
Reflecting on Bea's stubborn resilience and sacrifice, Jim finds his perception towards his enemies shifting.
Bea’s legend sparks a change in perception in Jim.
He is compelled to reevaluate his stance on the revolutionary war, her selfless act disrupting his lifelong beliefs.
No longer is the enemy faceless for him.
The image of Bea, the rebel turncoat who risked everything for him, humanizes the colonists he’s been trained to despise.
As Bea’s actions leave a lasting impact on Jim, he contemplates the human cost of war, striving for peace in a world torn apart.

30581.title: The Crying Game
synopsis: The film opens as a psychological thriller – IRA foot soldier Fergus and a unit of other IRA fighters, including a woman named Jude and led by Maguire, kidnap Jody, a black British soldier after Jude lures him to a secluded area with the promise of sex.
The IRA demands the release of other gaoled IRA members, threatening to execute Jody in three days if their demands are not met.
While the amiable Fergus guards Jody, they develop a bond – much to the chagrin of the other IRA men.
During this time, Jody tells Fergus the story about the Scorpion and the Frog.
Jody persuades Fergus to promise to seek out his girlfriend, Dil, in London, to tell her he loved her, and protect her after Jody has been killed.
The deadline set by Jody's captors passes and Jody is to be executed.
Fergus takes Jody into the woods to carry out the sentence.
However, Jody knows that Fergus is no murderer at heart, and makes a break for it.

Sure enough, Fergus cannot bring himself to shoot the fleeing Jody in the back, but Jody is instead accidentally run over and killed by British Saracen armoured personnel carrier as they suddenly move in to assault the IRA safe-house.
With his IRA companions seemingly dead after the attack, Fergus hides from the main body of the IRA in London, where he takes a job as a day labourer, using the alias "Jimmy".
While in London, Fergus seeks out and meets Jody's attractive girlfriend Dil at a hair salon.
Later they talk in a bar, where the next evening he sees her singing "The Crying Game".
Fergus still suffers from guilt about Jody's death and sees him in his dreams bowling a cricket ball to him.
He continues to pursue Dil, protecting her from an obsessive suitor and gradually falling in love with her.
Later, when he is about to make love to her in her apartment, he discovers that she is in fact a transgender woman.
His initial reaction is of revulsion.
Rushing to the bathroom to throw up, he accidentally hits Dil in the face, leaving her with a nosebleed.
He then leaves the apartment.
A few days later, Fergus leaves Dil a note, and the two make up.
Despite everything, Dil is still attracted to him.
Around the same time, Jude unexpectedly reappears in Fergus' apartment.
She tells him that the IRA has tried and convicted him in absentia.
She forces him to agree to help with a new mission to aid in assassinating a judge.
She also off-handedly mentions that she knows about Fergus and Dil, warning him that the IRA will kill her if Fergus does not co-operate.
Fergus, however, cannot overcome his feelings for Dil, and continues wooing her.
Fergus shields her from possible retribution by giving her a haircut and male clothes, as a disguise.
The night before the IRA mission is to be carried out, Dil gets heavily drunk and Fergus has to escort her to her apartment, where Dil asks for Fergus to stay with her.
Fergus complies, then admits to Dil that he had an indirect hand in her former boyfriend's death.
Dil, drunk, appears not to have understood, but in the morning, before Fergus wakes up, Dil ties him to the bed.
Dil unwittingly prevents Fergus from joining the other IRA members and completing the planned assassination.
Holding Fergus at gunpoint, Dil forces him to tell Dil that he loves her and will never leave her.
Dil unties him, saying that, even if he is lying, it is still nice to hear his words.
Dil then breaks down in tears.
Meanwhile, Jude and Maguire gun the judge down, but Maguire is shot dead by one of his bodyguards.
A vengeful Jude enters Dil's flat with a gun, seeking to kill Fergus for missing the assassination.
Dil takes several shots at Jude, hitting her, whilst stating that she is aware that Jude was complicit in Jody's death and that Jude used her sexuality to trick him.
Dil finally kills Jude with a shot in the neck.
Dil then points the gun at Fergus, but lowers her hand, saying that she cannot kill him, because Jody will not allow her to.
Fergus prevents Dil from shooting herself, and tells her to hide out in the club for a while.
When Dil is gone, he wipes Dil's fingerprints off the gun and allows himself to be arrested in place of Dil.
The epilogue takes place a few months later – Fergus, in prison serving a sentence of over six years, is visited by Dil.
Dil, after talking with Fergus about plans once he gets out of prison, asks him why he took the fall for her in the first place.
Fergus responds, "As a man once said, it's in my nature."
He then tells her the story of the Scorpion and the Frog.

96956140.title: Pop Star's Solo Journey
synopsis: The buzzing Madison Square Garden is drowned in the hypnotic tunes of pop sensation Emma Lee.
She pivots on the towering stage, mesmerizing her ocean of admiring fans with a charm that is nothing short of spellbinding.
Behind the stage and away from the blinding lighting and roaring applause, Emma confesses to her closest friends her deep-seated loneliness.
Emma had recently endured a brutal breakup with a Hollywood sweetheart, an occurrence that was as public as it was heartbreaking.
She yearns to forge real emotional bonds, to experience the carefree happiness and warmth of a family that is her own.
During a vulnerable conversation, abundant with raw emotion and honesty with her inner circle, Emma takes the monumental decision to start her journey towards motherhood.
She chooses in vitro fertilization, a decision that is life-altering and empowering at the same time.
Emma then decides to share this journey with the world.
During a candid interview with TMZ, she announces her decision.
The journey takes a wild spin when Emma learns that she is pregnant with twins.
From only anticipating one child, she is now faced with the arrival of two, throwing her world into an exhilarating whirlwind.
Emma first announces her twin pregnancy during a heartfelt OB-GYN appointment.

However, the morning sickness that accompanies her pregnancy unexpectedly strikes at awkward times – during concerts and high-stakes interviews, compromising her professional commitments, making her temporarily step back.
Struggling to keep up with the relentless demands of her hectic celebrity life and physical strains of being pregnant with twins, Emma finds her stress levels escalating.
Adding to her strains is the omnipresent scrutiny of the reality TV cameras.
In a refreshing twist, Emma finds herself gravitating towards Ray, a die-hard fan and humble bookstore owner surprisingly unaware of her publicised pregnancy journey.
This secret relationship, filled with humorously clumsy communication mixups, adds an extra layer of excitement to her already turbulent life.
Amid this rapid-paced existence and hormonal upheavals, Emma experiences an emotional breakdown on camera.
All eyes are on Emma during her extravagant, star-studded Hollywood baby shower, rendered more momentous by her twin pregnancy reveal and her secret relationship with Ray.

Amid the glittering party, under the festive disco lights, Emma, surrounded by her confidantes, indulges in a deep discussion, realising that she doesn't need another partner to feel whole, that her upcoming family is enough to fill her heart.
When Ray learns about Emma's pregnancy, he reacts unexpectedly yet heartwarmingly.
His support and understanding hint at a possible future together, sparking hope.
The culmination of Emma's journey comes with the arrival of her twins.
From the humorous challenges of labor to the overwhelming joy of motherhood, each moment is caught on camera.
As she navigates her new life with twins, cameras follow her journey juggling changing diapers and composing hit songs, adding a hilarious touch to ordinary chores.
The final scenes capture Emma backstage, desperately multitasking between cooing babies and her vocal warmups, demonstrating her extraordinary resilience.
In her comeback post-delivery concert, Emma is seen stronger and happier.
With cascading lights and an outpouring of has joy, she emerges transformed - a single mother and an idolized pop sensation.
In the grand series finale, Emma introduces her twins to her fans.
The conclusion speaks volumes about her personal growth and the beautiful unpredictability of embarking on motherhood as a solo parent.

23335172.title: The Back-up Plan
synopsis: Zoe (Jennifer Lopez) has given up on finding the man of her dreams and decided to become a single mother and undergoes artificial insemination.
The same day she meets Stan (Alex O'Loughlin) when they both try to hail the same taxi.
They run into each other twice more at a farmers market and a pet store.
Stan convinces Zoe to go on a no-obligations date.
Zoe is still uncertain whether she is pregnant or not and if she should tell Stan.
The night she takes the test and Stan takes her for a romantic dinner in a garden.
Things don't turn out as well as planned when he spills the wine and a fire occurs.
At the end of the night Stan asks her to come to his farm during the weekend and Zoe finds out that she is pregnant.
She goes to the farm determined to tell him that she is pregnant.
They make love and afterwards Stan is confused and angry that she didn't tell him before and Zoe leaves the next morning believing that things are over between them.
However, Stan decides he still wants to be with her and they reconcile.
They go to the doctor and find out that Zoe is actually carrying twins.
Overwhelmed, Stan goes to a children's playing area to figure out what it means to be a father, but is suspected to be a pervert; this is soon cleared up.

He finds a friend there that he can talk to about the pregnancy throughout the movie, while Zoe gets little support from her Single Mothers and Proud group when the group members discover she is no longer single.
Stan takes the next step to becoming a father and orders a stroller for the twins.
After many misunderstandings and comedic revelations, Zoe and Stan are walking into the Market when they run into Stan's ex-girlfriend.
Due to Stan's remark that the twins are not his, Zoe believes that he is not ready to become a father to them, and breaks off the relationship.
Later, the stroller that Stan ordered arrives and Zoe figures out that Stan was never planning to leave.
At her grandmother's wedding, Zoe's water breaks and on the way to the hospital they make a pit stop at the Market.
Zoe apologizes to Stan and they begin to work things out.
He pulls out the penny that she turned over when they first met and Zoe promises to trust him more.
In the end, Stan opens a store/restaurant next to Zoe's pet shop and after the Grand Opening speech Stan asks Zoe to marry him and she says yes.
On their way home, she spontaneously throws up into a rubbish bin and realizes that she may be yet again pregnant.

29471905.title: The Final Seduction of Faith
synopsis: John, a successful attorney of high repute, indulged in the splendour of his wealthy lifestyle.
Despite these materialistic achievements, he often found himself ensnared in a persistent inner conflict.
The unfamiliar unfamiliarity of this longing proved to be taxing.
However, his seemingly perfect life was disrupted when a severe financial crisis erupted.
His life partner, a woman enamoured by materialistic luxuries and societal impressions, found herself unable to cope with the weight of their sudden financial downfall.
Stripped of the pride of wealth, the respect of his clients, and the company of his wife, John was left alone, staring at the stark reality of a humble existence devoid of any superficial charm.
Amidst this solitude, the voice he had once dismissed echoed louder, underscoring the harsh reality of his vulnerabilities and the severe blow to his self-worth.
Lost and aimless, John serendipitously encountered Paul during one of his routine wanderings.
Paul's simple living and modest exposure starkly contrasted the luxurious life John had once savoured.
Sensing John's turmoil, Paul kindly extended his hand to lead him towards a path of spiritual awakening, promising him solace and tranquillity.
Longing for an antidote to his pain, John graciously welcomed Paul's assistance and embarked on a journey wherein he poured over various spiritual scriptures and dived deep into religious teachings.
His quest for spiritual understanding acquired a social dimension when he began attending religious gatherings at the local church.
At one such congregation, he met Susan, a woman whose compassionate nature bore the evidence of suffering that echoed John's own.
Their relationship evolved beyond a mere acquaintanceship.
Their shared experiences led to a bond that offered them mutual peace and understanding.
However, their flourishing association was hit with an unexpected tragedy; Susan confided in John, revealing her battle against a life-threatening illness.
Torn by the impending doom, he sought refuge in relentless prayers for Susan's well-being.
Despite her impending mortality, Susan's faith remained unbroken.
As her body deteriorated, her spirit remained strong, offering John an inspiring illustration of bravery.
Susan's remaining days were marked by physical suffering, but her final moments were met with courageous serenity, her faith standing unwavering against the cruel hands of fate.
Susan's demise left John grappling with unsettling void, yet her unwavering spirit and brave acceptance had indelibly altered his perception of life and faith.
After battling with his grief, John wholeheartedly surrendered himself to his newfound spirituality.
The once-ignored voice within him now functioned as a guiding light on his spiritual journey.
His perspective altered by his trials, he resolved to spend his remaining life serving others, helping them navigate through their struggles.
The film culminates with John delivering an invigorating sermon to the reverent church congregation as a newly-ordained pastor.
"Our true journey begins within," he asserted, embodying his deep understanding that true peace and satisfaction stem from unfaltering faith.

7832768.title: The Last Temptation of Christ (film)
synopsis: The film begins with a man whispering in despair, "The feeling begins.
Very tender, very loving.
Then the pain starts.
Claws slip underneath the skin and tear their way up.
Just before they reach my eyes, they dig in.
And I remember.
First I fasted for three months.
I even whipped myself before I went to sleep.
At first it worked.
Then the pain came back.
And the voices.
They call me by the name: Jesus."
Jesus of Nazareth (Willem Dafoe) is a carpenter in Roman-occupied Judea, torn between his own desires and his knowledge that God has a plan for him.
This conflict results in self-loathing, and he collaborates with the Romans to crucify Jewish revolutionaries.
Judas Iscariot (Harvey Keitel), originally sent to kill Jesus for collaboration,[1] instead suspects that Jesus is the Messiah and asks him to lead a revolution against the Romans.
Jesus replies that his message is love of mankind; whereupon Judas joins Jesus in his ministry, but threatens to kill him if he strays from the purpose of a revolutionary.

Jesus also has an undisclosed prior relationship with Mary Magdalene (Barbara Hershey), a Jewish prostitute, who asks Jesus to stay with her, a request that he considers before leaving for a monastic community.
Jesus later saves Mary from a mob gathered to stone her for prostitution and working on the sabbath.
Jesus compels the mob to spare her life, asking "Who here has never sinned?
", with Jesus offering two stones.
[2] Later, Jesus preaches to the crowd using many of the parables from the Sermon on the Mount.
Jesus acquires disciples, but remains uncertain of his role.
He visits John the Baptist, who baptizes Jesus, and that night the two discuss their differing theologies and political views.
John believes that one must first gain freedom from the Romans to achieve their end, while Jesus maintains that love is more important and people should tend to matters of the spirit.
