She decides she is being foolish and goes to New York to meet Walter for Valentine's Day.
With Jessica's help, Jonah flies to New York without his father's permission, and goes to the Empire State Building in search of Annie.
Jonah goes to observation deck and asks every unattached woman if she is Annie.
Sam, distraught, follows Jonah and finds him on the observation deck.
Meanwhile, Annie has seen the skyscraper from the Rainbow Room where she is dining with Walter and confesses her doubts to him.
They amicably end their engagement.
She rushes to the Empire State Building but is told that the observation deck is closed.

Annie convinces the guard to allow her to go to the observation deck (An Affair to Remember is the guard's wife's favorite movie) and arrives just moments after the doors to the down elevator close with Sam and Jonah inside.
In spite of the observation deck being deserted, Annie convinces the elevator operator to let her take a quick look around.
She discovers a backpack that Jonah has left behind.
As she pulls out Jonah's teddy bear from the backpack, Sam and Jonah emerge from the elevator, and the three meet for the first time.
Annie asks Jonah if the teddy bear is his, and he says it is.
"Are you Annie?"
Jonah asks.
She nods yes, and Jonah smiles.
"You're Annie," says a stunned Sam.
The elevator operator clears his throat.
Sam indicates they should go, momentarily making it unclear what his intentions are, until he says "Shall we?
", offers his hand to Annie, and the three go down the elevator together.

55956687.title: The Ledger (film)
synopsis: The cinematic journey commences in the hushed atmosphere of a deserted office, bathed in the sterile light of the late evening.
Amid the ocean of empty seats and lifeless screens, we find our protagonist, Paul Smith from Essex, England.
He is seated at the corner desk dealing with a swarm of paperwork, working tirelessly.
Paul serves as a stoic and highly principled accountant at Gold Leaf Bank, a globally renowned banking powerhouse stationed at the resounding heart of London's financial district.
As a classic introvert, Paul finds solace in the methods and precision of financial calculations.
One fateful evening, while scrutinizing the myriad ledger entries of the annual financial documents, he is pricked by an anomaly, an anomaly that forcefully grabs his attention.
The irregularities point to financial transactions tethered to offshore accounts.
This unexpected discovery intrigues him, and he finds himself modifying his routine, shifting his professional priorities to scrutinize every inch of the unusual books.

Paul, a seasoned accountant with over two decades of experience, channelizes his sharp eye for detail and analytical prowess in tracing the origins and final destinations of these inexplicable transfers.
As he plunges deeper into the labyrinth of financial documents and complex transactions, the conspiracy starts shaping itself into a grandeur, as confounding as it is shocking.
With each passing night, Paul peels away the layers of a massive internal conspiracy, a sinister plot that implicates the very core of the esteemed Gold Leaf Bank he had devoted years serving.

His tireless pursuit of truth leads to a shocking revelation; the mastermind behind this elaborate ploy is none other than his immediate superior - Mr. Arthur Henderson, a figure revered for his pioneering financial acumen and steady leadership.

This revelation sends shivers down his spine and casts a looming shadow of paranoia over his regular routines, but his steadfast moral compass impels him to amass irrefutable evidence before taking any sudden steps.
As Paul ventures further into this perilous journey, he realizes that the fraudulent trail thickens with every step, casting a dense net of corruption and deception.
Mr. Henderson, feeling the pressing heat of scrutiny, grows increasingly paranoid, threatening to detonate this volatile situation.
Despite the mounting sense of danger, Paul's resolve crystallizes, surrounded by a singular mission of exposing this pervasive scam.
On his path, he discovers an ally in Emma Thompson, a fellow accountant whose cynical demeanor about the organization's dealings mirrors his own.
Finding camaraderie in their mutual contempt for the virulent corruption poisoning their profession, Paul and Emma gradually form an unwavering alliance.

Working silently like covert operatives, the unlikely pair collaborates, assembling indispensable evidence against the scheming superior whose actions have morphed Gold Leaf Bank into a center for underhanded operations.
Bolstered by strength from their newfound bond, Paul and Emma orchestrate a bold confrontation against Mr. Henderson, the monstrous puppeteer of their once trustworthy organization.
Their quiet expose escalates into a hair-raising climax when the local authorities barge into the confrontation, acting upon an anonymous tip-off most likely orchestrated by our heroes.
The authorities quickly apprehend the shocked Mr. Henderson, thus triumphantly concluding Paul and Emma's venture.
In the aftermath of the scandal, independent financial auditors engulf Gold Leaf Bank.
Paul's unwavering courage and commitment to truth are rewarded with a much-deserved promotion, now the Director of Compliance.
Standing tall beside him, Emma too reaps the fruits of their shared victory.
Her promotion to Senior Auditor paves the way for a more accountable and transparent Gold Leaf Bank.
Their bond, forged in the searing heat of their shared ordeal, motivates them to establish an organization advocating for transparency and upholding employee rights.
Transparency Watch, their nascent organization, resonates with their harrowing experiences.
From an inconspicuous accountant to a celebrated whistleblower, Paul's transformative journey beautifully intersects with Emma's resilient spirit.
Their tale leaves viewers with a profound sense of optimism and a renewed faith in the extraordinary power of truth and integrity.

442333.title: The Mask (film)
synopsis: Shy and luckless clerk Stanley Ipkiss (Jim Carrey) works at an Edge City bank.
He is tormented by nearly everyone except for his Jack Russell Terrier Milo and his co-worker Charlie Schumaker (Richard Jeni).
Meanwhile, gangster Dorian Tyrell (Peter Greene) operates a nightclub called the Coco Bongo while plotting to overthrow his Greek boss Niko (Orestes Matacena).
Tyrell sends his singer girlfriend Tina Carlyle (Cameron Diaz) into Stanley's bank to record its layout, in preparation to rob the bank.
Stanley is attracted to Tina, and she seems to reciprocate.
After being denied entrance to the Coco Bongo, he finds a mysterious wooden mask near the city's harbor.
Placing it on his face transforms him into a zoot-suited, green-faced, bizarre trickster known as The Mask, who is able to cartoonishly alter himself and his surroundings at will.
The transformed Stanley exacts revenge on some of his tormentors, including the auto mechanics who had ripped him off the night before and his bullying landlord Mrs. Peenman (Nancy Fish).
When a street gang attempts to rob him, he scares them by turning a balloon into a Tommy gun.
The next morning, Stanley encounters Lieutenant Kellaway (Peter Riegert), Detective Doyle (Jim Doughan), and newspaper reporter Peggy Brandt (Amy Yasbeck) investigating The Mask's activity.
Despite being sought by the police, he again becomes The Mask in order to steal money targeted by Tyrell and attend Tina's performance.
At the Coco Bongo, The Mask dances exuberantly with Tina, whom he ends up kissing.
Following a confrontation with Tyrell, The Mask flees, leaving behind a scrap of cloth belonging to himself.
Kellaway suspects that Stanley is behind the bank robbery, but Stanley dissuades him.
Stanley consults an expert on masks named Dr. Arthur Neuman (Ben Stein), who tells him that the object is a depiction of Loki, the Norse god of darkness and mischief.
Still later, Stanley transforms into The Mask again and meets Tina at the local Landfill Park.
He is interrupted by Kellaway and Doyle, who attempt to arrest him.
However The Mask distracts them by tricking a large group of Edge City police officers into joining him in a mass performance of the Desi Arnaz song "Cuban Pete".
Stanley flees with Peggy, but he is betrayed to Tyrell for a $50,000 bounty.
Tyrell tries on the mask and becomes a malevolent green-faced being.
Forced to reveal the location of the stolen money, Stanley is kept hostage in one of the mob's cars while Tyrell's henchmen reclaim the money.
Stanley is later handed over to Kellaway and Doyle, along with a green rubber mask, to be detained.
When Tina visits Stanley in his cell, he urges her to flee the city.
Tina thanks Stanley for treating her with respect and tells him that she knew that he was The Mask all along.
She tries to leave the city, but is captured by Orlando and Tyrell.
They take her to a charity ball hosted by Niko and attended by the city's elite, including the city's mayor, Mitchell Tilton (Ivory Ocean).
At the ball, the masked Tyrell kills Niko and prepares to destroy both the club and Tina.
Milo helps Stanley escape from prison, and bringing Kellaway as a cover and hostage, they go to the club to stop Tyrell.
After briefly securing the assistance of Charlie, Stanley is spotted by Orlando and captured.
Tina tricks Tyrell into taking off the mask, which is recovered and donned by Milo, turning the dog into a cartoonish pitbull who defeats Tyrell's men while Stanley fights Tyrell.
After recovering the mask, Stanley uses its abilities to save Tina by swallowing Tyrell's bomb and flushing Tyrell down the drain of the club's ornamental fountain.
The police arrive and arrest Tyrell's remaining henchmen, while Kellaway and Doyle try to arrest Stanley again claiming his real identity as The Mask.
Mayor Tilton arrives and debunks Kellaway's claims by announcing that Tyrell was The Mask the whole time because he was one of the victims that was taken hostage by the thug at Coco Bongo.
He tells Stanley that he is a hero, thanks him for saving lives, and orders the police to release him.
In a desperate attempt to prove Stanley was The Mask, Kellaway and Doyle try to claim off Milo for assisting in his escape, but Tilton is not in the mood for their antics.
He goes on to say that he will need to meet with both men in his office the next morning to discuss their early retirement.
All charges against Stanley are dropped, while Kellaway and Doyle must face Tipton's judgment.
The next day, as the sun rise, Stanley, Tina, Milo, and Charlie take the mask back down to the harbor.
Tina throws the mask into the water, and she and Stanley celebrate their victory with a kiss.
Charlie tries to retrieve the mask for himself, only to find Milo swimming away with it.

93336689.title: 5 Aspects I Dislike About Technology
synopsis: A singularly tech-savvy 17-year-old high school student, Benjamin Miller, caused quite a stir as he transferred to Central Secondary School.
His arrival was hardly inconspicuous, for he brought along a state-of-the-art triple-screen ASUS Gaming computer setup.
On his first day, Benjamin boldly featured a unique accessory - multi-function eyeglasses created by Zungle that tracked his sleep metrics.
His Fitbit wristband tirelessly calculated his heartbeat, recording each step he took.
Parallel to Benjamin, the story introduces Andrew Larson.
A 16-year-old youngster working as a part of the school's technical staff, his humbleness and fondness for old-style methods provided a starkly different narrative.

His soft spot for classic artifacts, like rotary dial phones and film projectors, enveloped him in a nostalgic world that buzzed with the rhythmic clatter of vintage Royal typewriters and the unique, almost comforting smell of old film reels stored away in wooden cabinets.
Benjamin's encounter with a traditional compass and old-fashioned paper map during a geography class resulted in a comical series of attempts to locate Italy.
Andrew's reactions to modern technology, through technophobic lenses, astounded many.
His obstinate refusal to open emails and his panic attacks while attempting to handle a Canon laser printer generated moments of humor.
An unforeseen crisis at the school required the two stark opposites to reluctantly collaborate for a computer science project.
Despite the difficulties, each saw the project as an opportunity to learn from the other.
As their cooperation progressed, their contrasting styles caused numerous miscommunications and misunderstandings.

Benjamin’s journey into the past began with Andrew's guidance, carefully writing a thank-you letter with a quill pen, squinting at a generation-old world map, and entertainingly twirling the dial of an antique telephone.
Meanwhile, Andrew's entry into the world of digital technology was not without issues.
Under Benjamin's patient guidance, he grappled with frequent “page not found” errors and the wild chases of the mouse pointer on the computer screen.
The duo celebrated a moment of comic success when, after numerous attempts filled with embarrassing errors, Andrew managed to send his first successful email to the school's principal.
Amidst this newfound enthusiasm, Benjamin experienced some unexpected issues with his digital aids.
One incident occurred during a solemn "No bullying" pledge at the school assembly, when all his devices decided to buzz simultaneously, making Benjamin the center of attention.

The third act witnessed a reformed Benjamin taking a calmer approach towards his project, abandoning his flashy PowerPoint presentation in favor of a rustic hand-made flipchart titled "5 Aspects I Dislike about Technology".
On the other hand, Andrew's newly acquired digital skills were put to test as he successfully upgraded the school's old overhead projectors and chalkboard systems.
Benjamin presented his project on the school’s annual day.
His personal revelations regarding technology left his peers quite surprised initially, but soon his sincerity was rewarded with hearty applause.
His project emphasized the need for a balanced engagement with technology.
The climactic sequence saw Benjamin getting his first paper cut from an origami creation, causing playful chaos in the classroom.
At the same time, an overflow of emotions led Andrew to slip-up and send a heartfelt confession of his infatuation to his secret crush.
In a comical twist of fate, the email was accidentally sent to the entire school network!
In the closing moments of the story, Benjamin was seen introspectively penning an entry in a vintage leather-bound diary, while Andrew bravely booted up his brand-new MacBook laptop.
The narrative comes to a heartfelt conclusion as the contrasting worlds of technology enthusiast Benjamin and traditionalist Andrew find balance.

398934.title: 10 Things I Hate About You
synopsis: Cameron James (Joseph Gordon-Levitt), a new student at Padua High School, is given a tour of the school by Michael Eckman (David Krumholtz), an A.V.
geek.
During the tour, Cameron notices the beautiful and popular Bianca Stratford (Larisa Oleynik) and he is immediately smitten with her.
Michael warns Cameron that Bianca is shallow and conceited, and that her domineering father does not allow her to date.
However, Michael does inform Cameron that Bianca is looking for a French tutor.

At the Stratford residence, Bianca's outcast older sister, Kat (Julia Stiles), is in conflict with their overbearing father (Larry Miller), who wants Kat to attend college nearby despite her acceptance to Sarah Lawrence College.
Bianca is also fighting with their father regarding his strict no dating rule.
Kat's aversion to dating prompts their father to come up with a new rule, to Bianca's fury: Bianca can only date if Kat is also in a relationship.
Cameron starts tutoring Bianca (despite knowing little French himself).
After Cameron makes a failed attempt to ask her out on a date, she informs him of her father’s rule.
This motivates Cameron and Michael to find a boy who is willing to date Kat.
Cameron suggests Patrick Verona (Heath Ledger), another outcast who is just as ill-tempered as Kat.
Cameron tries asking Patrick for his assistance, but Patrick scares him off.
Michael suggests that Joey Donner (Andrew Keegan), an affluent student and model who also wants to date Bianca, pay Patrick to take Kat out.
Patrick agrees, but Kat wants nothing to do with him.
After a little effort, Patrick gets Kat to attend a party with him.
At the party, Bianca sees Cameron but is dragged away by Joey.
He poses and tries to please her when Bianca realizes he is just obsessed with himself.
Kat starts table dancing after getting drunk and hits her head on the chandelier, collapsing off the table and into the arms of Patrick who takes her outside.
They talk on the swingset; however after throwing up on his shoes, Patrick takes Kat home.
She unsuccessfully attempts to kiss him after he drives her home, then slams the car door in his face and storms off.
Cameron admits his feelings for Bianca, and they kiss in the front seat of his car.

The next day, Patrick attempts at apologising because he realises he is starting to like Kat but fails, but eventually wins Kat over with a performance of "Can't Take My Eyes Off You" in front of her entire soccer team.
After sneaking Patrick out of detention, the two go paintballing and fall into a haystack, where he kisses her; however, when Patrick later asks Kat to prom, she becomes suspicious and the two fight.
Bianca tries to convince her father to let her attend the prom, but he refuses because Kat is not going to the prom.
When Bianca confronts Kat, it is revealed that Kat previously dated Joey and they slept together once since "everyone was doing it."
She tells Bianca that her feelings of isolation from her fellow students dated from that incident and that she would never again do anything just because it was the popular thing to do.
Bianca and Kat end up going to the prom with Cameron and Patrick, respectively.
Joey is furious to learn that Bianca has gone to the prom with Cameron, and confronts Patrick about the "arrangement" in front of Kat.
Kat is very angry at Patrick when she discovers the truth and leaves him at the prom.

Joey subsequently confronts Cameron about manipulating the "deal" for himself and knocks him to the floor, but Bianca punches Joey numerous times for using her, for hurting Kat's feelings, and for punching Cameron.
Bianca and Cameron share another kiss and leave Joey lying on the floor in pain.
The next morning, Kat and Bianca's relationship appears to have improved drastically as Bianca attempts to comfort her older sister.
Their father allows Kat to go to Sarah Lawrence College, she is extremely grateful and hugs him with happiness.
Later at school, Kat reads a poem which she wrote for English class, titled "Ten Things I Hate About You," revealing her true feelings for Patrick.
After school, Kat finds a guitar in her car for the band she told Patrick that she wanted to start, that Patrick bought her with the money that Joey paid him.
He admits the truth and says that Joey paid him to take out a "really great girl", but he messed up because he fell for her.
Kat forgives Patrick and the two reconcile with a kiss.

25255772.title: Individuals in Dark Attire (film)
synopsis: Our tale begins unfolding in the scenic serenity of Friendlyville, a small town treasured for hosting positive, motivational self-help conferences.
A jovial seminar in the town attracts an intriguing range of participants, all starkly unique yet bound by a single thread – their attire, all in black.

The group comprises Tom, a scornful Mortician, quirky Goth teenager Lily, Jack, a disciplined Blacksmith, Ana, a lively Zumba instructor, and Peter, a Wall Street investor whose emotions seldom surface.
Their distinct professions do little to hinder the bond they forge.
Bound by their attendance at the seminars, their trust in each other deepens, and camaraderie blooms.
Friendlyville's inhabitants, accustomed to a laid-back lifestyle, can't help but be drawn in by the mystery shrouding the new arrivals.
As the group's black attire becomes a known trait, whispers begin that they are agents of a legendary spy network known as the Individuals in Dark Attire (I.D.A.).
Initially, the group takes the townsfolk's suspicion lightly, laughing about the absurd notion and brushing the gossip aside.
As time passes, they sense a change in the attitudes of the townsfolk.
Their bemusement along with the awe-infused respect of the villagers not only amuses them but sparks intrigue.
The town Mayor, cunning opportunist Phineas Schultz, eavesdrops on these widespread rumors, his calculating mind starting to work overtime.
Schultz sees an unexpected opportunity amid the speculation.
He decides to employ the misconceptions about the group's affiliation with the I.D.A.
to bolster his re-election campaign.
Mayor Schultz takes it upon himself to endorse this unique affiliation of the group, assigning them with the responsibility of enlightening the locals about self-defense and community safety.
This task catapults the group into a whirlwind of events, filled with comedic twists and surprising turns.
Ana, with her Zumba instructor prowess, cleverly repurposes her rhythmic dance steps as self-defense techniques.
Jack, applying his blacksmith's skills, provides a masterclass in turning traditional tools of his trade into improvised weapons.
Yet, every attempt they make to peel away the rumors is misinterpreted as further evidence of their spy identity, thickening the comedic chaos.
Meanwhile, in their headquarters nestled in Zurich, the real I.D.A spies take note of the peculiar situation unfolding in Friendlyville.
Intrigued by the bizarre turn of events, they decide to keep a close eye on the town's activities.
Finding the whole situation amusing, they subtly play along with the town's outlandish beliefs, reinforcing what they believe to be a fantasy.
Amidst the comedic frenzy, our unsuspecting group accidentally stumble upon several pieces of proof highlighting corruption within Mayor Schultz's office.
Hidden documents reveal the Mayor's fraudulent plan to divert public funds for his personal gain, under the guise of building a spy defense system.
Unintentionally, they trigger an alert signal that gets picked up by the observing I.D.A agents in Zurich.
The town folks, caught up in their adventure, challenge the alleged I.D.A members to unveil Mayor Schultz's underground operations.
Surprised and unsure of their new found responsibility, the group takes a moment to digest their peculiar situation.
With quick thinking, they formulate a plan, leveraging each member's individual strengths.
Peter's meticulous analytical skills, Jack's raw strength, and the others leading to a well-rounded strategy.
Propelled by an uncanny sense of duty and the town's faith, they evolve into the heroes no one, including them, expected them to be.
Through a series of hilarious yet harrowing incidents, they manage to unravel Mayor Schultz’s shady plot with striking conviction.
Seeing his well-orchestrated plan crumble in front of his eyes, Schultz finds himself being arrested by the actual I.D.A agents.
Their silent vigilance finally highlighted.
Their unexpected triumph incites a joyous celebration across Friendlyville, spontaneously renaming them the town's heroes.
In honor of their triumph, the townsfolk, to mark their hero's proclaimed affinity, adopt their iconic black attire.
They institute 'Hero’s Day' in celebration of their indisputable courage.
The comedic journey comes to an exhilarating halt when the real I.D.A agents, amused by the group's harmless impersonation, bestow the honorary title of 'Agents in Dark Attire'.
As the narrative reaches a sweet conclusion, the entire town gathers for a memorable group photograph, sealing their momentous adventure.
The group that once felt alienated amidst unfamiliar faces transformed into celebrated heroes of a town that’s not theirs but feels like home.
Over time, their training continues, and the once peaceful town now brims with newfound fortitude and serenity.
Initially unsettled by their rumored identities, the group gracefully embraces their unexpected roles.
Circumstances turned a group entwined in confusion into true heroes, proving the power of community.
Their saga ignites a spirit of resilience and camaraderie within the town, that was unexplored before their arrival.

31984428.title: Men in Black (film)
synopsis: Men in Black (M.I.B.)
is a secret non-government agency that polices extraterrestrial alien refugees that are residing on Earth and are disguised as humans, created in 1961 after the first contact.
The agency operates from an underground base at a Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority ventilation station in Battery Park.
MIB members use neuralyzers on witnesses' memories of alien sightings, therefore the secrecy of the presence of aliens and the MIB itself is extremely secretive.
MIB is monitoring about 1500 aliens around the world, most of them in the vicinity of New York City.

One night, Agent K (Tommy Lee Jones) and his partner, D (Richard Hamilton) intercept a truck containing illegal immigrants, and allow everyone to cross into America except for an extraterrestrial, who is disguised as a human because he is an intergalactical fugitive.

When a suspicious United States Border Patrol agent, who saw K and D pose as fellow Border Patrol agents, sees the alien without its disguise, the alien attacks him, forcing K to destroy it and use the neuralyzer on the agent and his colleagues, claiming that the alien remains splattered all over them are from when the agent shot an underground gas main with his gun.
D, feeling too old, asks K to use the neuralyzer on him.
Meanwhile, James Darrell Edwards III (Will Smith) is a New York police officer pursuing a man on foot while his out-of-shape colleagues can't catch up.
While chasing the incredibly fast and agile fugitive, he corners him and the man throws an odd looking gun away, which disintegrates, and escapes.
When Edwards corners the man again at the top of the (Guggenheim Museum), he sees the man blink with a set of secondary eyelids before jumping over the roof and killing himself.

K arrives at the precinct station, (where no one believes Edwards's incredible story), questions Edwards about the incident, then takes him to a pawnshop run by a man named Jack Jeebs (Tony Shalhoub), an MIB informant who Edwards knew for dealing stolen goods, to identify the strange weapon the criminal drew on him.
While questioning Jeebs, K reveals Jeebs is an alien by blowing his head off with a weapon, which grows back immediately.

After Edwards finds a weapon identical to the one he saw among Jeebs' hidden stash of alien technology, K realizes that the gun was meant to be used in an assassination, but Jeebs is unable to provide any further information.
K uses the neuralyzer on Edwards, takes him to dinner, and leaves him an MIB business card.
Later, Edwards goes to the MIB's secret headquarters and competes with several others to qualify to join the agency.
During one part of the test, a written exam, the candidates struggle to complete the test due to the oddly shaped chairs, until Edwards pulls a table over for him to use.

at another part involving a shooting gallery, Edwards refuses to shoot several aliens because he thinks that they are doing normal everyday things, but shoots a little girl for carrying suspicious quantum physics textbooks.
After the tests, K takes him aside (while Zed uses the neuralyzer on the others for failing the tests) and offers him the position.

Edwards accepts and his identity is erased, becoming Agent J, and explains the nature of MIB and tells him that he will have to distance himself from any human contact to maintain secrecy, and that he will get his own neuralyzer when he learns.
Suspicious of why extraterrestrials are suddenly leaving the planet, the M.I.B.
investigate a farmer named Edgar (Vincent D'Onofrio), who has been acting strangely after an alien craft crashed on his farm and destroying his truck.
Edgar has been killed and his skin used as a disguise by a "Bug", a member of a giant cockroach-like species that are at war with several other alien races, including the Arquillians and the humans.
An Arquillian prince hiding in Brooklyn who is disguised as a human jewelry store owner is attacked by the "bug" and appears to die along with his friend.
The body is taken to the city morgue and investigated by Dr. Laurel Weaver (Linda Fiorentino).
During the investigation K and J arrive at the morgue posing as Doctors.
The head of the dead Arquillian "opens" while being examined by Dr Weaver and J reavealing the actual Arquillian prince.
While dying the Arquillian tells J that "the galaxy is on Orion's belt".
M.I.B.
informant Frank the Pug (Tim Blaney), a Remoonian disguised as a small lapdog, explains that the missing galaxy is a massive source of energy housed in a small jewel.
The Bug figures out the galaxy is hanging on the collar of Rosenberg's cat Orion, which refuses to leave the prince's body at the morgue.
Orion has been taken care of by Dr. Laurel Weaver (Linda Fiorentino).
J arrives at the morgue just as the Bug kidnaps Weaver and grabs the galaxy.
The Arquillians deliver an ultimatum to M.I.B.
to secure the galaxy within an hour, or they will destroy Earth.
The Bug arrives at the site of two disguised flying saucers, the observation towers of the New York State Pavilion at Flushing Meadows.
K and J are close behind and destroy one saucer, causing it to crash through the Unisphere.
The Bug sheds Edgar's skin and swallows J's and K's guns.
K tells J to stop the Bug from getting onto the other ship, then taunts the Bug until K too is swallowed.
J infuriates the Bug by crushing cockroaches and taunting him.
The Bug is blown open from the inside by K, who located his weapon in the Bug's stomach.
As J and K sit on the ground covered in slime, the mortally wounded insect tries to attack again, but is killed by Weaver using J's weapon.
The three return to M.I.B.
headquarters and K tells J that he has not been training him as a partner, but rather as a replacement, as he is tired of a life as an agent.
J reluctantly uses the neuralyzer on K, using a story that he has been suffering in a coma for 35 years to allow him to return to his civilian life and the young woman he left behind.
A few days later, it is revealed that Weaver also joined M.I.B.

and is now J's new partner, Agent L.  As a coda, the camera rapidly pulls back, showing that Earth and the Milky Way galaxy are also inside an alien marble being used in a cosmic game, revealing that, like the galaxy in a necklace, we are tiny.

41403368.title: City Shadows
synopsis: Guided by the early morning frosty light, the beautiful city of San Francisco stirs from its tranquil and serene charm into a bustling hub of life.
A series of vivid and captivating shots showcase the leisurely journey of the sun's first rays, gently casting long shadows across "Joe’s Classic Diner".
Inside the diner, the camera lingers on the daily rituals of eight contrasting individuals immersed in their hearty breakfasts.
We delve a little deeper into this tableau.

It includes an intellectual librarian, lost in the enticing mystery of Agatha Christie's "And Then There Were None"; a burly mechanic with roughened palms, an imprint of a hard day's work, stirring his black coffee; a humble street cleaner, enjoying his crispy bacon and scrambled eggs, carrying the toil of the city on his shoulders.

Next, we find a charismatic bartender, world-weary from his late-night shifts, a spritely primary school teacher primly checking a pile of math tests, a bank employee in chic attire poised with her calming green tea, a formidable security guard grudgingly staring at his healthy dish of Caesar salad, and lastly, a seasoned, earth-loving gardener, inspecting his lush green fern plant religiously.
But when the humble light of the morning gives way to the glaring hustle of daytime, the mundane outward appearances peel back to reveal concealed identities.
Feeding off the energy of the bustling city, they are clandestinely immersed in meticulous preparation for an audacious plan.
Our characters are unveiled as resilient risk-takers, convincingly disguising beneath their everyday personas.
Their collective fixation gravitates towards an alluring prize - "The Dawn's Tear," a dazzling, priceless, 60-carat diamond, valued at a staggering 500 million dollars.
Its sparkling glory rests in the illuminated spotlight of the city's prestigious Morrison Art Museum.
As they coordinate their preliminary groundwork, surprising skills and tactics surface.

Sudden expertise in dexterity, advanced computer hacking, safe-opening techniques, agile acrobatics, stealth strategies, disguising artistry, explosive handling, strategic planning, and groundbreaking deception come to the fore.
As evening wraps the city in darkness, the group gathers at the monumental sandstone structure of the museum.
Cloaked in anonymity, they converge, poised for action.
Under the dim streetlights, recognition crosses their faces as they identify familiar features from the diner.
The brewing suspicion adds a fascinating layer to the surroundings.
They set in motion a covert operation; an intricate game of cat and mouse, with each player pining for the same dazzling prize - The Dawn's Tear.
As their scramble for the jewel turns reckless, a deadly scuffle ensues in the grand hall.
The kerfuffle accidentally triggers the much-dreaded, cutting-edge laser-based security system of the museum.
In the ensuing chaos, panic fuses with the acrid scent of smoke from burst grenades.
The once serene museum is now a battlefield.
Shattered shards of glass from the damaged display fall like tiny shards of crystal around them as the harsh siren's cry cuts through the disarray.
As the security system retaliates with ferocious warnings, the group's personal wants give way to a desperate need to escape the escalating situation.
Despite their initial mistrust, they form an instant, unlikely alliance, pooling their diverse skills to evade the rapidly closing in SWAT team.
Their united dash for freedom propels them through the city’s hidden underworld- a labyrinth of abandoned subway lines, antiquated sewage pipes, and dilapidated warehouses.
As they navigate the city's unnerving underbelly, they start revealing unexpected motivations behind their daredevil venture.
Stories are shared; we hear accounts of a common nemesis in their past - the formidable mob boss, Samuel "The Snake" Sullivan.
As they share their grievances against Sullivan, they unknowingly weave a web of empathy and camaraderie.
This remarkable kinship, forged by necessity and fueled by a shared adversary, starts forming a cohesive team.
In the grip of a life-threatening chase, their loyalty fleetingly switches from self-preservation to thwarting Sullivan's plot to obtain the diamond.
As dawn breaks once more, the unlikely team finds themselves far from the reach of the relentless SWAT team.
Collectively, they agree to a risky proposition; to turn the gem into bait, to trap Sullivan.
Their ingenious plot gradually unravels, leading to unearthing not only a baited trap for Sullivan but also revealing his nefarious deeds.
In a daring move, an anonymous dossier compiled with damning evidence against Samuel, including the diamond, is discreetly delivered to the San Francisco Police Department.
Sullivan, once a fearsome figure, now finds himself cornered by the unforgiving grasp of justice.
In the gripping aftermath, the group reconvenes at Joe's Diner, now a sanctuary, sharing a peaceful meal as they reminisce over the whirlwind events.
As if adhering to an unspoken pact, they resume their regular lives.

They each retreat to their familiar roles; the mechanic crippled by the city’s growth, the teacher shaping young minds, the street cleaner subsumed in city grime, the bartender succoring the city’s nocturnal creatures, the librarian in a world of words, the guard watching over sleeping giants, the bank employee in factions of finances, and the gardener tending the city’s green heart.
The extraordinary caper dissolves in the city's bustling rhythm, unseen beneath the majestic shadow of the Golden Gate.
Their shared adventure, unlike their glittering prize, is carefully packed away, only revisited during quiet introspective moments.
The once lost and feared "Dawn's Tear" reappears, neatly packaged in a nondescript box, in the SFPD station.
Rumors circulate laden with speculation, yet the true identities of the audacious thieves remain shrouded in mystery.
The reclaimed gem is returned to its protective casing at the Morrison museum, remaining silent amidst the galleries, a testament to the city's untold secrets.
Confounded city officials are left wondering, puzzled over the unresolved enigma of the audacious diamond heist.
The city quickly regains its rhythm, the once electrifying escapade gradually fading into a barely visible thread in San Francisco’s rich tapestry of urban legends.
Beneath their unassuming roles, each individual shoulders a burdening secret, their nondescript appearances masterfully disguising an extraordinary past.
Furtive glances exchanged, fleeting smiles and silent secrets shared over mugs of hot coffee hint towards an unspoken past.
The routine morning chatter cleverly disguises the adrenalized roller-coaster they once embarked on together.
The familiar ambience of the diner, with its vintage walls, silently guards yesterday's secrets.
Lives once lived in obscurity now seethe beneath the surface, tales of suspense, peril and camaraderie hidden out of sight.
An unbreakable bond, formed amidst gunfire and danger, adds invisible threads to their day-to-day lives.
Their collective vow of silence, committed to protect the purity of San Francisco's vibrant dawn, remains unbroken, held sacred within the hallowed space of Joe's Diner.
Another day meets dawn in San Francisco as the city pulsates tirelessly, indifferent to the untold and unheard tales of patrons at Joe's.
The city continues its song, unfazed, narrating the untold tales to its unwitting inhabitants.
The closing scene showcases the panoramic view of San Francisco at dawn.
The first sun rays illuminate Joe's Diner, paying tribute to their silent bond.

297111.title: Reservoir Dogs
synopsis: Eight men eat breakfast at a Los Angeles diner before their planned diamond heist, and none of them knows who they really are.
Six of them use aliases: Mr. Blonde, Mr. Blue, Mr. Brown, Mr. Orange, Mr.
Pink, and Mr. White.
With them are gangster Joe Cabot, the organizer of the heist and his son, "Nice Guy Eddie".
After they discuss the plan, they leave to the heist.
The action abruptly cuts to a speeding car, in which Mr. White comforts Mr. Orange, who has been shot in the abdomen and is bleeding profusely, revealing they just performed the heist.
Shortly after they reach an abandoned warehouse.
Mr.
Pink arrives and angrily suggests that the job was a setup due to the rapid police response.
Mr. White tells Mr.
Pink that Mr. Brown was killed during the heist, and the men discuss Mr. Blonde, who murdered several civilians after the alarm triggered.
Mr. White is angered that Joe, an old friend of his, employed such a "psychopath" and agrees about a possible setup while Mr.
Pink reveals that he escaped with the diamonds and hid them in a secure location.
They argue over whether to take the now unconscious Mr. Orange to a hospital.
Mr. White also reveals that he has told Mr. Orange his name and home town.
Mr. Blonde, having watched them from a distance, steps forward and ends the dispute regarding Mr. Orange.
Mr. White berates him for his deadly rampage, but Mr. Blonde dismisses the criticism.
He tells the others to wait as Eddie is on his way there.
Mr. Blonde has also taken a police officer, Marvin Nash, hostage and the three men beat Nash in an attempt to find out if there is an informant.
Eddie then arrives and orders Mr.
Pink and Mr. White to assist him in retrieving the stolen diamonds and dispose of the hijacked vehicles, while Mr. Blonde stays with Nash and the unconscious Mr. Orange.

Alone with Mr. Blonde, Nash denies any knowledge of a setup, but Mr. Blonde is uninterested and tortures Nash for his own amusement, slashing Nash's face with a straight razor and severing his right ear.
He then douses Nash with gasoline, but before he can ignite it, Mr. Orange shoots and kills Mr. Blonde.
Mr. Orange then reveals to Nash he is an undercover cop, reassuring Nash that, upon Joe's arrival, a large police force is in position to raid the warehouse.
Eddie, Mr.
Pink, and Mr. White return to the warehouse to find Mr. Blonde dead.
Mr. Orange claims that Mr. Blonde was going to kill all of them and take the diamonds for himself.
After impulsively pulling out his gun and killing Nash, Eddie rejects Mr. Orange’s claims, saying that Mr. Blonde was a close personal friend who had always remained loyal to his father.
Then Joe arrives and reveals that Mr. Blue is dead.
He confidently accuses Mr. Orange of being an informant, forcing Mr. White to defend his friend.
Joe, about to execute Mr. Orange, is stopped when Mr. White points his gun at him, and Eddie in-turn takes aim on Mr. White.
Joe eventually shoots Mr. Orange, wounding him again; Mr. White shoots and kills Joe in response; Eddie shoots Mr. White, wounding him; and Mr. White shoots and kills Eddie.
Mr.
Pink, who was hiding during the melee, takes the diamonds and flees.
Badly wounded, Mr. White crawls to Mr. Orange and cradles him in his arms.
However, Mr. Orange reveals that he is in fact an undercover cop.
Devastated, Mr. White points his gun at Mr. Orange's head.
The police storm the warehouse, demanding that Mr. White drop his gun.
The frame zooms in on the face of Mr. White and a hail of gunfire is heard.

71862304.title: The Titan Enigma (film)
synopsis: The movie opens in the bustling, space-age city of Titan Town.
Pastel hues of the fading evening sun reflect off the monumental facades of towering structures like the colossal Titan Tower.
Bold, pulsating neon lights illuminate the night sky, casting surreal reflections on the overhead hyperloop lines.
The Riddler, a figure shrouded in notoriety in the enticing world of cyber espionage, forms the protagonist of the story.

Accompanying the Riddler, are three other indomitable whistle-blowers; a tech prodigy known for his groundbreaking strides in artificial intelligence, a phantom-like master of stealth, and a man once loyal to Titan Corp's cybersecurity detachment, now using his knowledge of their systems against them as they plan a daring digital heist.
Under Riddler's expert guidance, they infiltrate the electronic vaults of Syndicate Bank, the financial lifeblood of a dangerous mob.

Upon completion, they deliver a crippling blow to the syndicate by uploading the stolen financial transactions and clandestine deals online, explosively exposing the syndicate's global empire of money laundering and illicit weapons trading, consequently stirring the public's indignation.
Whispers of an uprising quickly spread amongst the oppressed citizens of Titan Town.
As the group continues their digital rampage through the syndicate's data, they stumble upon a mysterious file named "Titan Enigma."
Intrigued but wary, the crew dedicates great time and effort to decrypting this piece of the puzzle.
Upon successful decryption, the data uncoils to expose a spine-chilling conspiracy.

Unbeknownst to the innocent dwellers of Titan Town, the Mayor of their city, in collusion with the secretive tech giant Titan Corp, has orchestrated a massive scheme to establish absolute control over the city.
The realization of Cipher's capture, and the disaster it spelled for their mission, hit the team like a ton of bricks.
The Riddler makes a daring decision.
They would infiltrate Titan Corp's towering, impregnable 200-story strong headquarters.
Retribution came thundering down from the Syndicate, outraged and embarrassed at its scandalous exposure by them.
Titan Corp jumped into action as well, aligning itself with the city's robotic law enforcement - the unyielding, powerful Titan Enforcers - with a single mission of capturing these cyber rebels.

Pursued relentlessly by both the syndicate's ruthless bounty hunters and the formidable Titan Enforcers, the team finds themselves on the run, racing against the clock towards unveiling the deeply enigmatic "Titan Enigma."
Upon successful decryption, the data uncoils to expose a spine-chilling conspiracy.
A sinister blueprint of a city-wide surveillance grid emerges from the decrypted files, threatening to deprive the citizens of Titan Town of any semblance of privacy and personal freedom.
The clandestine activities of the Riddler and his crew did not go unnoticed.
The omnipresent digital Worm logo that mysteriously started appearing on their computer screens signalled the danger brewing ahead.
Retribution came thundering down from the Syndicate, outraged and embarrassed at its scandalous exposure by them.
It placed a staggering bounty of 500 million credits on the capture or demise of the Riddler and his team.
Titan Corp jumped into action as well, aligning itself with the city's robotic law enforcement - the unyielding, powerful Titan Enforcers - with a single mission of capturing these cyber rebels.

Pursued relentlessly by both the syndicate's ruthless bounty hunters and the formidable Titan Enforcers, the team finds themselves on the run, racing against the clock towards unveiling the deeply enigmatic "Titan Enigma."
During a high-speed chase through the city's neon-lit lanes, Cipher, their stealth specialist, was captured by a squadron of cyborgs masquerading as ordinary citizens.
The realization of Cipher's capture, and the disaster it spelled for their mission, hit the team like a ton of bricks.
The danger of Cipher spilling their secrets under interrogation or advanced brain hacking techniques was looming large.
In the face of this adversity, the Riddler makes a daring decision.
They would infiltrate Titan Corp's towering, impregnable 200-story strong headquarters.
A rescue mission for Cipher was under plan while simultaneously intending to uncover the "Titan Enigma" in its heartland.
The stakes raised, the daring team penetrated the fortress-style headquarters under the cover of the night.
Tension rises as they confront Titan Corp's formidable defense mechanisms, fighting off advanced combat robots in the digital maze of its corridors.
Their survival is constantly on the line, their mission hanging by a thread amidst the chaos.
Amidst this relentless action, they successfully locate Cipher who has been held captive in an advanced high-security, digital prison, and orchestrate an exhilarating escape.
Within the secured confines of the hidden control room of the base, they make a chilling discovery that adds a new, dangerous dimension to the "Titan Enigma".
Titan Corp sought not just control but absolute dominion, intending to launch a city-wide digital attack with 'Virus X'.
This would cripple the city's systems and make its citizens sitting ducks for Titan Corp's oppression while simultaneously erasing any evidence of their sinister designs.
As they reel under this terrifying revelation, the team splits responsibilities.

Some members frantically work on aborting the launch of Virus X while others simultaneously upload all the incriminating evidence they have gathered against Titan Corp's dastardly plans on Titan Town's public network, Titan Web.
As the truth gets unveiled, Titan Town is thrown into pandemonium.
Every citizen, glued to their holographic screens, watch the revelations unfold in real-time, leading to a thunderous uproar and widespread dissent against Titan Corp.
Simultaneously emboldened and enraged, the people rise against Titan Corp in an unbeatable wave of defiance.
The corporation's iron grip on the city begins to loosen.
As the corporation's plans crumble, the domino effect extends to the robotic law enforcement entities which had been remote-controlled by the corporation.
The robots malfunction en masse, causing their systematic obliteration and freeing up advantageous opportunities for public uprising.
As Titan Town seethed in rebellion, Riddler and his team stealthily exited the scene, leaving behind a city on the precipice of a monumental democratic transition.

As the first streaks of dawn break through the city’s brooding skyline, the Titan Tower, a once-inescapable reminder of oppression, stands a mute spectator to a city’s resurrection from the ashes of a sinister autocratic regime.
Hope, at last, takes flight.

4276475.title: The Dark Knight (film)
synopsis: In Gotham City, The Joker and his accomplices rob a mob-owned bank.
The accomplices kill each other off one by one in a sequence masterminded by the Joker, who escapes alone with all the money.
Batman and Lt. Jim Gordon decide to include the new district attorney, Harvey Dent, in their plan to eradicate the mob.
Although Dent is dating Rachel Dawes, Bruce Wayne is impressed with his idealism and offers to throw him a fundraiser.
Mob bosses Sal Maroni, Gambol, and The Chechen hold a videoconference with Lau, a Chinese accountant who has hidden their funds and fled to Hong Kong.
The Joker interrupts the meeting, warning that Batman is unhindered by jurisdiction.
He offers to kill Batman for half their money, but the mob bosses refuse, and Gambol puts a bounty on him.
The Joker kills Gambol and takes control of his men.
Batman captures Lau and delivers him back to Gotham to testify against the Joker and the mob.
The Joker announces that people will die each day unless Batman reveals his identity.
He then kills Commissioner Gillian B. Loeb and the judge presiding over the mob trials.
He also targets Dent at the fundraiser, but Bruce hides Dent.
Gordon foils the Joker's assassination attempt on Mayor Garcia, apparently sacrificing himself in the process.
Bruce plans to reveal his identity, but Dent instead names himself as Batman to protect the truth.
Dent is taken into protective custody and pursued by the Joker across the city; Batman rushes to Dent's aid.
Gordon, who faked his death, helps apprehend the Joker and is promoted to Commissioner.
That night, Dent and Rachel disappear.
Batman interrogates the Joker and discovers that Dent and Rachel are held in two separate buildings filled with explosives.

The Joker reveals their locations, and Batman goes to Rachel's, only to realize that the Joker has tricked him into finding Dent moments before both buildings explode, killing Rachel and scarring half of Dent's face.
The Joker detonates a bomb in the police station and escapes with Lau.
Coleman Reese, an accountant at Wayne Enterprises, deduces Batman's true identity and plans to reveal it.
The Joker kills Lau and The Chechen, then threatens to bomb a hospital unless Reese is killed.
Gordon and Bruce protect Reese, who changes his mind.
The Joker visits Dent in the hospital and convinces him to seek revenge.
The Joker then blows up the hospital and escapes with hostages.
Dent starts to go after people responsible for Rachel's death, deciding their fates by flipping a coin.
He kills Maroni and a cop who had helped kidnap Rachel.
It is revealed that the Joker rigged two ferries with explosives to escalate chaos; one ferry is full of citizens, the other full of prison inmates and guards.
He then gives the passengers of each ferry the choice to blow the other up before midnight — otherwise, both ferries will explode.
The passengers ultimately refuse.
Batman asks a reluctant Lucius Fox to use a city-wide tracking prototype device to find the Joker; Fox agrees, but says he will resign immediately afterward.
The Joker dresses up hostages as his men, luring Gordon's SWAT team to strike them.
Batman fights off the SWAT team and the Joker's men, then rescues the hostages.
Batman apprehends the Joker, but the Joker gloats that he has won, as Gotham will lose hope once Dent's rampage becomes public.
The Joker also reminds Batman that their conflict will be eternal before the SWAT team arrives to take the Joker into custody.
Dent lures Gordon to the building where Rachel died and holds Gordon's family hostage.
Batman confronts Dent, who judges the fates of himself, Batman, and Gordon's son with three coin flips.
He shoots Batman, spares himself, then flips again to determine the boy's fate.
Batman, who is wearing body armor, tackles Dent off the building, killing him and saving the boy.
[13] Batman then convinces Gordon to frame him for Dent's murders so that Dent will remain a symbol of hope for the city.
Gordon destroys the Bat-Signal and launches a manhunt for the Batman.
Alfred Pennyworth burns a letter written by Rachel to Bruce announcing her engagement to Dent, and Fox watches the signal tracker self-destruct.

77308067.title: At Second Glance
synopsis: Sarah Thompson, an award-winning designer hailing from the prestigious Montage Wellness Center in Aspen, Colorado, feels a sudden urge to leave her bustling city life behind.
With a mixture of excitement and apprehension, she chooses to swap her city lifestyle for a simpler existence closer to nature.
Sarah's new home takes form as the captivating village of Laurel Canyon, a picturesque hideaway just outside the ever-energetic city of Los Angeles, California.
Coming from a cosmopolitan background, Sarah struggles to fit into her new bucolic life.
Her metropolitan habits, deeply ingrained over the years, challenge her attempt to assimilate into this novel rural environment.
Sarah's budding country life reveals complications that she didn't anticipate.
She bears the brunt of the daily inconveniences that remind her of the stark difference between her past urban life and the rural existence she currently inhabits.
Amid this whirlwind of change, Sarah frequently stays up into the wee hours of the night, reflecting intensively on her life's path.
She grapples with feelings of solitude and questions if she cherishes her past or current lifestyle.
One morning, during a solitary walk at sunrise, Sarah stumbles upon a shabby, neglected bookstore named "Second Glance".
Inspired, Sarah pledged to revive this literary haven into a thriving hub.
She harnessed her financial prowess and abundance of energy towards rejuvenating "Second Glance" and thereby, leave a signature mark on the village life.
During her energetic venture to revive "Second Glance," she crosses path with John, the enigmatic local carpenter known for his unique woodwork.
John offers his skilled craftsmanship to Sarah, aiding her in her mission to revitalize the neglected bookstore.
The initial silence between them gives way to a sincere connection, flourishing with mutual respect and admiration.
Her growing friendship with John acts as a salve to her burgeoning feelings of displacement and loneliness.
As time passes, Sarah's respect and affection for John deepen.
Shepherd grapples with the allure of a high-status job and re-entry into the glitzy design world which wrestles with her newfound affection for her rural existence.
John, despite being aware of Sarah's predicament, respects her autonomy, and steps back, allowing her to independently decide on the course of her life without his influence.
After countless sleepless nights spent on contemplation, Sarah decides to return to Aspen, to succumb to the familiar pull of her former influential role.
However, as Sarah prepares to leave, she experiences a sudden and powerful revelation.
It stops her in her tracks, making her realize what truly matters to her.

Sarah acknowledges the truth; the love she has cultivated for "Second Glance," her unspoken affection for John, and the peaceful life she painstakingly curated in Laurel Canyon, far outweighs the glamour of her past life.
Displaying immense courage, Sarah declines the glamorous job offer she once aspired to have.
She chooses to embrace her peaceful bookstore, her budding relationship, and the tranquillity of her village life.
Under the starry village night sky, Sarah finally confesses her unconditional love for John and her irrevocable decision to stay back.
John, deeply moved, reciprocates his suppressed emotions.

Together, Sarah and John enjoy the peaceful life in Laurel Canyon, their days filled with the raw beauty of the village, the intellectual exchanges in their bookstore, and the warmth of their shared affection.
Sarah finally finds the peace she yearned for during her expedited professional journey.
She has learned to appreciate the joy of living each day in its fullness.

As they start a fresh chapter of their lives, Sarah and John journey together, their shared love and vision serving as the guiding star, with innumerable narratives waiting to unfold in their quaint bookstore.
Sarah's attachment to her former city life begins to fade as she acclimates to her village life.
The simplicity of their daily routine, combined with small joys and accomplishments, grows ever more appealing.
The ups and downs of her village life shape an incredible evolution of Sarah's character.
Every twist brings forth new wisdom, experiences, and delightful surprises.

2399430.title: At First Sight
synopsis: Amy Benic (Mira Sorvino) takes a break from working as an architect at a spa in Pinecrest, a small town outside New York City.
Virgil Adamson (Val Kilmer) is a masseur at the spa and gives Amy a massage.
Amy breaks down and cries, later falling asleep as Virgil leaves the room.
When she wakes up, she runs after him to compliment the massage, only to realize that Virgil is blind.
Virgil asks her out, and the two eventually fall in love and begin a relationship.
Virgil lives alone, though his over-protective sister, Jennie (Kelly McGillis), who lives next door, takes care of him.
During an intimate session with Amy, Virgil reveals that he went blind when he was three and that the last thing he saw was something fluffy.
Amy describes the horizon to Virgil as something that you "can see but can never reach."
While researching Virgil's condition, Amy learns of Doctor Charles Aaron, a specialist in eye treatment who suggests to Virgil that, with surgery, he could restore his sight.
Virgil refuses.

To understand Virgil's reaction, Amy seeks out Jennie, who reveals that their father left the family years ago after putting Virgil through several kinds of treatment in an unsuccessful attempt to restore his sight.
After waking up with Amy one morning, Virgil decides he will give the operation a try.
It is a success, but after Virgil regains sight for the first time, he becomes confused and disoriented, unable to perceive light and distance.
Dr. Aaron suggests that he should visit Phil Webster (Nathan Lane), a visual physiotherapist.
Webster in turn suggests that Virgil needs to learn everything from scratch himself, through experience.
Virgil and Amy begin living in New York City, with Virgil finding his feet with his new-found sight.
The pair begin drifting apart, as Virgil finds it hard to decipher the look on Amy's face at times.
Amy finds herself constantly having to explain basic things to Virgil.
While at a party, Virgil sees Amy kiss her ex-husband for his birthday.
While trying to leave the party, Virgil walks into a glass pane due to his poor perception.
Virgil's father sees him on television and arranges a reunion; Virgil goes to his father's workplace, but decides at the last minute that he cannot face him yet.
On one of the regular consultation visits with Webster, he brings Virgil to a strip club.
They engage in a deep conversation, where Webster notes that instead of just "seeing", Virgil should instead "look"; there are a lot of things that sight alone cannot solve.
Virgil confesses that he and Amy are drifting apart, but insists that Amy is the most important thing in his life.
Upon returning from a work trip to Atlanta, where she and her ex-husband shared a sensual moment, Amy decides to save the relationship.
She finds Virgil in a park looking for "the horizon" in the city.
Virgil's sight begins deteriorating.
He begins experiencing vision blackouts.
After consulting with Dr. Aaron, Virgil realizes that he is losing his sight.
He decides to look for his father.
Virgil reveals to him that he is going blind again, and asks him why he left.
His father tells him that he felt he was a failure when he did not find a way to help his son regain sight.
Virgil states that he should not have left because his mother and sister suffered greatly after his father walked away.
Virgil looks for Amy, who tells him about her plans to travel with him to places like Egypt and Europe.
Withholding the fact that he is again going blind, Virgil tells her there is one thing he really wants to see, and brings her to a "New York Rangers" game.
At the game, Virgil realizes that the "fluffy cloud" he last remembers seeing was cotton candy.
As he buys some, he suffers a lengthened vision blackout and admits to Amy that he is going blind, which Amy refuses to accept.
Back home, Virgil and Amy argue.
He asks if she wants to spend her life with him if he is going to be blind forever.
Amy hesitates, and Virgil decides to return home.
Virgil is welcomed by Jennie and eases back into his old way of life.
While losing his sight, Virgil spends his remaining time with sight to look at as many things as possible, going through magazines and pictorial books in the library.
He stays up to watch the sunset, seeing the horizon for the first and last time.
After he has been blind again for some time, Virgil is at a park with a guide dog.
He takes a seat, finishes a sandwich, and tosses the wrapping into a bin.
Amy has found him and says, "You missed."
Virgil takes a moment then realizes it is Amy.
She sits down and they reconnect; then she reveals that she finished a significant sculpture that he broke during their argument.
Amy apologizes to Virgil for trying to change him and for moving too fast, which led to their problems together.
Virgil puts his hands on Amy's face and touches her tenderly.
She asks if he wants to take a walk and "see what they see".
They leave the park together.

25070744.title: Path to Freedom: The Heist
synopsis: John, a battle-hardened robber, and his former partner Peter, a master forger, find themselves serving long sentences with hardened criminals in the most notorious and brutal Russian prison, the Black Dolphin.

Over intense games of chess and mundane shared meals, the two form a deep bond, reminiscing about their past daring exploits, exhibiting their skills in robbery and forgery, and yearning for their shared dream of safeguarding their families' financial futures.
Out of the blue, they are visited by Sergei, a feared Russian Mafia boss, who, lured by their legendary reputation, presents them with a once-in-a-lifetime proposal.
Tempted by the idea of a final, audacious job which could secure them and their families for a lifetime, John and Peter agree to play a pivotal role in Sergei's high-risk heist operation.
They receive detailed blueprints in a clandestine meeting, wherein Sergei informs them of their targets – the impregnable Central Bank of Russia and a major Swiss bank in Zurich.
After securing conditional release on parole due to their exemplary in-prison behavior, they split ways to put together their teams and lay down the plans for their respective heists independently.
In the grimy nest of Moscow's underworld, John reconnects with his past cohorts and courts a motley crew of skilled thieves for his daring mission.
Close to a thousand miles away, Peter, leveraging his knowledge of automobiles and repair, taps into his network in Europe's murky black market to build a robust team of seasoned criminals.
Reading between the lines of Sergei's cryptic notes, they unearth the plan's crux – the robberies need to be executed concurrently for maximum possibility of success.
Simultaneously, Agent Smith of Interpol, a dogged sleuth, begins noticing patterns in the criminal underground, hinting at an impending multi-national bank heist.
Swiftly and discreetly, Smith increases security at vulnerable banks across Europe and Russia, putting high-risk criminals and financial institutions under strict surveillance.
Peter, while operating from an illegal black-market workshop in Budapest, narrowly escapes a sudden police raid, barely getting out with everything needed for the heist.

Back in the belly of Moscow's underground, a team member of John, a self-serving hacker looking for a golden parachute, betrays their plan to the local authorities, placing their operation under intense scrutiny.
The inexorably heightening police cards and vigilance begin to squeeze both the teams, the palpable tension escalating with each closing hour till the day of the decisive heists.

The narrative diverts into unforeseen territories as the teams are forced to adapt to unexpected challenges and obstacles while trying to crack the code of the sophisticated soviet era security measures.

The D-day of the heist unravels with a beautifully choreographed montage, presenting an array of slick, synchronized maneuvers, primed to breach the formidable structures of the Russian and Zurich banks.
The tension is palpable as both teams, armed with their wit and tools, attempt to outsmart the intricate security systems, dealing with impenetrable lasers, coded locks, and advanced biometrics.

In Zurich, Agent Smith, putting his deductive skills to the test, identifies one of the targeted banks, joining the fray to halt the heist; however, Peter's team, already on the move, eludes him just in time.
In Russia, John's team, although under immense stress, successfully extracts an astronomical amount of cash and gold, precisely timed to avoid an imminent law enforcement response.
Amidst the victorious cheers and celebratory cigars, John and Peter, holding their hefty spoils, plan to meet Sergei at a concealed bunker in Siberia to partition the stolen booty.
The plot takes a shocking turn - rather than a smooth division of loot, Sergei reveals a sinister plan to double-cross John and Peter, intending to seize the entire haul for himself.
All three hardened criminals face off in a hefty standoff, with each man's trust in the other hanging by a thread.
The standoff unravels with an unexpected arrival – Agent Smith, hot on the trail of Sergei, swoops in and apprehends the treacherous mafia boss.
Quick to seize the ensuing chaos as an opportunity, John and Peter covertly flee with their shares of the loot, comprising of untraceable bills and a small arsenal of gold bullions.
Agent Smith, left to deal with the aftermath and faced with the frustration of John and Peter's escape, vows to capture the audacious men for their unprecedented crimes.
Despite successfully pulling off the ambitious double heist, John and Peter are all too aware of the looming danger they're yet to face.
The sight of Sergei being marched off in cuffs, splashed on national news, darkens their mood; They know the mafia's downfall could trigger an investigation leading directly back to them.
During a gripping press conference, Agent Smith openly commits to catching the elusive duo, stating that their crimes won't go unpunished.

John and Peter, isolated in their respective hideouts - John nestled in the harsh, bitter cold of Russian mountains, and Peter hiding in plain sight in the brick laden streets of Amsterdam, watch the news in anticipation.
As Smith's promises of relentless pursuit echo from their television sets, their eyes lock through the screens.
The narrative ends with a tacit understanding between them - their fight for freedom is far from over.

3390263.title: 15 Minutes
synopsis: After getting out of prison, ex-convicts Emil Slovak (Karel Roden) and Oleg Razgul (Oleg Taktarov) travel to New York City to meet a contact in order to claim their part of a bank heist in Russia (or somewhere in the Czech Republic).
Within minutes of arriving, Oleg steals a video camera.
They go to the brownstone apartment of their old partner Milos Karlova (Vladimir Mashkov) and his wife Tamina, and demand their share.
When Milos admits that he spent it, an enraged Emil kills him with a kitchen knife, then breaks Tamina's neck as Oleg tapes it with his new camera.
The couple's neighbor, Daphne Handlova (Vera Farmiga), witnesses everything, but she escapes before they can get to her.
To cover up the crime, they douse the bodies in acetone, carefully position them on the bed, and burn down the apartment, intending to pass it off as an accident.
Jordy Warsaw (Edward Burns), an arson investigator, and NYPD detective Eddie Flemming (Robert De Niro) are called to the scene.
Flemming is a high profile detective who frequently appears on the local tabloid TV show Top Story.
Flemming and Warsaw decide to work the case together.
They eventually determine that Milos was stabbed so hard that the knife's tip broke off and lodged in his spine.
While checking out the crowd outside, Warsaw spots Daphne trying to get his attention.
When he finally gets to where she was, she is gone, but Warsaw manages to produce a sketch of the witness.
Emil, who got hold of Daphne's wallet when she fled the apartment earlier, realizes that Daphne is in the country illegally and will be deported if she calls the police.
He contacts an escort service from a business card he found in Daphne's wallet.
He asks for a Czech girl hoping she will arrive.
When Honey, a regular call girl, arrives instead, he stabs and kills her, but not before getting the address of the escort service from her.
Oleg tapes the entire murder.
In fact, he tapes everything he can; a wannabe filmmaker, he aspires to be the next Frank Capra.
Flemming and Warsaw investigate her murder, determine the link to the fire, and also visit the escort service.

Rose Heam (Charlize Theron) runs the service and tells them that the girl they are looking for (Daphne) does not work for her but rather a local hairdresser, and she just told the same thing to a couple other guys that were asking the same questions.
Flemming and Warsaw then rush to the hairdresser but get there just after Emil and Oleg warn the girl not to say anything to anyone.
As Flemming puts Daphne into his squad car, he notices Oleg taping them from across the street.
A foot chase begins, culminating in Flemming's partner getting shot and his wallet stolen.
Emil finds a card with Flemming's name and address in it.
He gets very jealous of Flemming's celebrity status and is convinced that anyone in America can do whatever they want and get away with it.
On the night that Flemming is to propose to his girlfriend Nicolette Karas (Melina Kanakaredes), Oleg and Emil sneak into his house and knocks him unconscious, later taping him to a chair.
While Oleg is recording, Emil explains his plan - he will kill Flemming, then he will sell the tape to Top Story, and when he is arrested, he will plead insanity.
After being committed to an insane asylum he will declare that he is actually sane.
Because of double jeopardy, he will get off, collecting the royalties from his books and movies.
Flemming starts attacking them with his chair (while still taped to it) and almost gets them but Emil stabs him in the abdomen, and putting a pillow on Flemming, killing him.
The entire city is in mourning and Emil calls Robert Hawkins (Kelsey Grammer), the host of Top Story, to tell him he has a tape of the killing and is willing to sell it.
Robert pays him a million dollars for the tape.
Warsaw and the entire police force are furious with Robert and can not believe he would air it, especially since his main reporter is Nicolette.
At the same time, Emil and Oleg try to kill Warsaw and Daphne by booby-trapping Daphne's apartment.
The two narrowly escape the resulting fire.
On the night it is aired Emil and Oleg sit in a Planet Hollywood to watch it with the rest of the public.

As the clip progresses, the customers react with horror at the brutality of it, and a few begin to notice Emil and Oleg are right there with them, Oleg actually smiling at the results of his work, and panic takes place.
Emil explains his betrayal to Oleg and as he about to execute Emil with a gun, Oleg stabs him in the arm.
The police come in and arrest the wounded Emil, while Oleg escapes.
They put Emil in Warsaw's squad car but instead of taking him to the police station, Warsaw takes him to an abandoned warehouse where he is going to kill him.
The police arrive just in time and take Emil away.
Everything goes as planned as Emil is now a celebrity and is pleading insanity.
His lawyer agrees to work for 30% of the royalties Emil will receive for his story.
Meanwhile, Oleg is jealous of the notoriety that Emil is receiving.
While being led away with his lawyer and all the media, Warsaw gets into an argument with the lawyer while the Top Story crew is taping the whole thing.

Oleg gives Hawkins the part of the tape where Emil explains his plan to Flemming, proving he was sane the whole time (Oleg presumably kept this part of the tape on hand as part of an "insurance policy").
Hawkins shouts out to Emil and explains to him the evidence he now has.
Emil pushes a policeman down, takes his gun and shoots Oleg.
Emil grabs Flemming's fiancée, who is covering the news story, and threatens to shoot her.
He is finally cornered by the police and Warsaw.
Against orders, Warsaw shoots Emil a dozen times in the chest in order to avenge Eddie's death.

An officer shouts that Oleg is still alive, and Hawkins rushes to him to get footage just as Oleg says the final few words to his movie he is taping just before he dies (with the Statue of Liberty in the background).
Shortly afterward, Hawkins approaches Warsaw and tries to cultivate the same sort of arrangement he had with Flemming, suggesting the power an arrangement would give him.
In response, Warsaw punches out Hawkins and leaves the scene as the police officers smile in approval.

35137398.title: Half Hour or No Charge
synopsis: Jake is a jovial pizza delivery man who, instead of constantly worrying about delivery deadlines, thoroughly enjoys his time amidst the busy New York City sights, sounds, and people, making light banter with his co-workers, and loves to end his day unwinding the stress with a relaxing joint of marijuana.
Be it bright sunny mornings or cold rainy evenings, Jake could always be seen riding his familiar red scooter, with a hot and steaming box of pizza strapped firmly behind his back.
Jake's boss, Paul, a middle-aged man with expressive grey hair and a stern countenance, is the antithesis of him.
He manages "Pizza on the go" with no-nonsense regulations and maintains a work environment that pressed on punctuality.
Paul believes in sticking strictly to timing information and this kept his pizzeria's reputation pristine.
His tagline for the pizzeria sternly dictated - "Half Hour Or Your Pizza is Free."
Paul often rebuked Jake, warning him about his continuous tardy pizza deliveries to the customers.
He even threatened to sack him if he failed to maintain delivery schedules, even once.
Often, Jake would find himself lost between the mounting scoldings coming from Paul and the comforting aroma of Margherita pizzas baking away with loads of extra cheese.

Underestimating Paul's warnings, Jake would frequently daydream on his next pizza delivery assignment when the boss handed the pepperoni pizza for the next delivery, thinking it all as a quite amusing joke.

Jake had a few regular customers in his delivery area, including a grumpy, yet good-hearted Vietnam war veteran who liked to order Hawaiian Pizzas and a mischievous English Bulldog that would always tip him with used tennis balls, much to Jake's amusement.
During his daily errands, Jake came across a woman named Lucy.
Lucy worked as a night-shift nurse and usually ordered pizzas when her shifts ended.

Jake found himself hopelessly falling in love with Lucy’s infectious laughter and he made his feelings obvious by consistently sending her extra garlic breadsticks and writing romantic notes on the pizza boxes meant for her delivery.
Jake’s crush for Lucy became so severe that he started losing track of his delivery timings.
His frequent chats with Lucy started leading him away from his duty schedule.
Trying to juggle between Lucy and his job, Jake often found himself delivering pizzas that weren’t as fresh as they should’ve been, leading to a few complaints from the customers.
Stress was starting to pile on Jake as he struggled to balance everything.
The climax hit when Jake messed up an extremely important order.
He had been assigned the delivery of a pizza to Judy, a powerful food blogger with millions of followers online.
Totally absorbed in arranging a surprise candlelit date for Lucy on the Brooklyn Bridge, Jake completely forgot about Judy's pizza delivery.
Having waited for an hour, Judy, the food blogger, threatened to post a harsh review of "Pizza on the go", damaging their reputation.
After returning from his surprise date with Lucy, Jake was greeted with Paul’s furious yelling for his failure in making the delivery on time.
Throughout the chaos, the only anchor for Jake was his growing fondness and strong emotional connection with Lucy.
Realizing how dire the situation was, Jake planned to save his job and also his love life with all his might.
To aid his damage control efforts, Jake’s friends - Tommy, a techie, Streetz, a street art enthusiast, and Coco, a hilarious talking parrot, pitched in.
They banded together to rectify the situation and win back the food blogger’s favor.
Despite their combined and tireless efforts, they missed the half-hour pizza delivery deadline.
Quickly, they resorted to innovative solutions.
They made a fresh delivery including a box full of extra-large pizzas.
The box was accessorized with a vibrant street art portrait of Judy on the lid and a side splitting skit performed by Coco, causing outright laughter.
Judy received the pizza half an hour late, but she was certainly intrigued by their humorous goodwill gesture.
Judy ended up writing positive reviews about the pizzeria, sharing the fun-filled delivery experience which brought an unexpected twist in their usual pizza delivery.

Jake missed his boss's deadline again, but Paul was pleasantly surprised to see the sudden surge in new customers and the increased online attention their pizzeria received due to the blogger's review.
Jake's passion, creativity, and determination made Paul rethink his obsession with strict timelines and dedication to work, helping Jake to keep his job.
Lucy had been observing all these events from afar and had fallen deeper for Jake’s carefree and loving nature.
Jake began to build stronger relationships with his customers, started understanding their unique pizza preferences and made sure they always received what they really liked.
He indulged in a long story-telling session from the Vietnam war veteran, while the English bulldog sat next to him, waiting for his share of crunchy pizza crust.
The deliveries became far more engaging with these interactions and mucho quicker than before.
Lucy was highly impressed by Jake’s carefree attitude towards life and his new sense of responsibility, which made her grow closer to him.
The whole city took notice of Jake’s unconventional pizza deliveries, and he struck a friendly rapport with his previous delivery rivals.
Over time, Jake and Paul’s relationship evolved.
