Back on Earth, governments worldwide grappled with the aftereffects of the Exodus.
The reality of extraterrestrial life, once a subject of ridicule and disapproval, had exploded into undeniable fact.
As the chaos took root, authorities struggled to manage an escalating number of believers and theorists, and to quell the tide of rampant conspiracy spreading like wildfire.
Fear, uncertainty, and a gripping sense of anticipation descended upon humanity.

Questions hovered in the air, unanswered and unnerving, regarding subsequent interplanetary relations and the fearsome possibilities of humanity going to war with a vastly superior alien civilization.

The chilling image of General Corben rallying his forces, readying for a potential interstellar war, served as a stark reminder of humanity’s paradoxical nature: the ability to both embrace and fear the unknown.
The closing scene conveyed the threatening possibility of Earth ending up on the offensive side of an interstellar conflict.

574909.title: Alien Nation (film)
synopsis: The year is 1991, and it has been three years since an immense lost and off-course extraterrestrial saucer bearing 300,000 enslaved aliens, the Newcomers, landed in the Mojave Desert on planet Earth.
Los Angeles becomes a new home for the aliens who take, or in some cases are assigned, renowned human names such as Harley Davidson and Humphrey Bogart.
However, among humans the aliens are discriminated against, and referred to in derogatory terms such as the word 'Slag' , or the ghettos which they reside in as 'Slagtown' .
Matthew Sykes (Caan) is a Los Angeles police detective who loses his partner Bill Tuggle (Brown) in a criminal shoot-out.

The detectives were trying to stop two Newcomer felons murdering another Newcomer named Cecil Porter (Parton), behind a cash register in a small mini-mart in what appeared to be a robbery; the Newcomer robbers are using high-powered weapons using sabot rounds, one of which kills Tuggle even through the vehicle he is using for cover.

The next day, Sykes' superior Captain Warner (McCarthy), informs his squad that they will have to work with the newly promoted Newcomer detective Sam Francisco (Patinkin), and that if nobody volunteers, he will choose someone to carry out those duties.

Although having racist opinions about "Slags", Sykes enlists to work with Francisco to investigate a similar homicide with a Newcomer named Warren Hubely; feeling that if he investigates that crime, he will also find opportunities to investigate his partner's death which he is officially forbidden to do.
Meanwhile, Warner assigns the robbery murder case to detectives Fedorchuk (Jason) and Alterez (Perez).
Showing no faith in their ability to find the truth, Sykes requisitions a powerful .454 Casull revolver for a sidearm to be more effective dealing with Newcomers.

As the troubled pair continue with the Hubely-homicide probe; Sykes discovers similarities between their case and the robbery, while at a crime lab, Francisco detects an abnormality on the body of one of the Newcomer criminals who was killed in the robbery with pathologist Mr. Winter (Young).

Following an interview with a Newcomer named Trent Porter (Thompson), who is also the son of the innocent Newcomer fatality during the robbery; Sykes and Francisco are led to a nightclub called Encounters to investigate a link in the homicides with a Newcomer named Joshua Strader (Kober).

However, they end up interviewing his girlfriend Cassandra (Bevis) instead, after he is murdered by a criminal ring led by Newcomer businessman William Harcourt (Stamp) and his henchman Rudyard Kipling (Howard).
Harcourt is in the latter stages of launching advanced plans to exploit the alien race by attempting to mass-produce and sell a drug called Jabroka.
The drug was used in the past to pacify the Newcomers when they were slaves, but has no effect on humans.
The abnormality noticed by Francisco on the body of the Newcomer criminal earlier, was a visual sign of the drug's influence.

In addition, the Newcomers Hubley, Porter and Strader were involved in the planning phases of the operation, but were later murdered due to Harcourt's desire to exclude them from any future financial rewards.
Ultimately, Sykes and Francisco track down Harcourt to the Encounters club, where he is secretly negotiating a timetable for the release of his potent narcotic.
The detectives attempt to foil his plans, as they are later led on a car chase with Harcourt and his cohort Kipling, through the streets of downtown Los Angeles.
Following a head-on automobile collision where Francisco is injured and Kipling subsequently killed, Sykes on foot, corners Harcourt onto a desolate drawbridge.
Harcourt then purposely overdoses on a sample of the controlled-substance he was illegally trying to distribute to the Newcomers.
As Sykes mistakenly believes he died, Harcourt is taken away by an ambulance, but later mutates into a significantly larger and more muscular Newcomer intent on causing violence.
After Francisco discovers Sykes' misstep, the duo pursue Harcourt.
Catching up with Harcourt near a fishing pier, Sykes leads him onto the deck of a fishing trawler.
The pair then end up in a physical confrontation in the open sea.
Harcourt dies, as his body disintegrates due to the effects of direct contact with salt water, which is hazardous towards Newcomer physiology.
Francisco commandeers a police helicopter, forcing himself to pull Sykes from the water even as it burns the flesh of his arm.

With the Tuggle and Newcomer murder cases solved, the authorities dismantle Harcourt's illicit scheme involved in trying to subdue the aliens, and Sykes invites Francisco to his daughter's wedding, pausing to apologize in advance for all the hateful things he knows he will say.
Francisco accepts, telling him, "After all...you are only human."

61101755.title: The Last Hurrah
synopsis: Inside a bustling office, we are introduced to John Smith - a charismatic, ebullient man on the cusp of marriage.
He is interrupted by a message from Jane Doe, his radiant bride-to-be.
The contents of the message bring a chuckle to John's face.
John is gathered with his longtime pals, Mark, Luke, and Matt, around a round wooden table in a lively neighborhood pub teeming with locals.
That evening, Jane implores John to take care of her sibling Matt who was prone to mischief, especially with their bachelor party destined for Las Vegas.
Their Las Vegas-bound journey begins with all four companions squeezed into Matt's raucously loud Lamborghini.
They lay eyes on their destination - the glimmering Las Vegas skyline, their hearts fluttering when faced with the grandeur of their lodging, a towering, luxury suite in The Cosmopolitan.
They decide to immerse themselves in the nightlife, kicking off their venture with the world-renowned MGM Grand casino.
Trouble arises when Matt succumbs to his impetuous tendencies, making risky bets that, to their stark horror, accumulate a debt of $100,000 at the roulette table.
Their initial enthusiasm plunges as intimidating security personnel, led by a stern, red-faced floor manager, escort them out of the casino.
They rouse in their plush hotel room, faced with a disorderly reality and a daunting challenge: rectifying their predicament before the truth jeopardizes their upcoming wedding.
In this pursuit, the group divides their efforts - John ventures out to find Matt while Mark and Luke gear up to mitigate their outrageous debt with the casino's management.
As the city awakens and embraces another day of round-the-clock hedonism, John embarks on a quest to find Matt.
Mark and Luke, dressed in Italian designer suits, try to resolve the catastrophic debt.
However, their efforts seem to be in vain.
Fate eventually intervenes and, among the chaos, they chance upon Matt on The Cosmopolitan’s rooftop swimming pool.
A comedy of errors follows which convolute their predicament further.
The situation takes a fortuitous turn when it emerges that Matt is connected to a high-ranked local politician.
This revelation convinces the casino management to grant them a single opportunity to clear their debt.
With the disastrous situation resolved and their hefty debt forgiven, they realize that they endured a chaotic Vegas bachelor party.
In the final moments of their reckless adventure, they draw a pact, promising to meet again at the impending wedding.
They decide to keep Jane insulated from the chaotic events of this trip, agreeing that shielding her from further worries tops their priorities.
As dawn breaks, John finds himself leaning against the Lamborghini, watching his friends and an inebriated Matt snoring in the backseat.
He takes a moment to recall their absurd, yet unforgettable trip together, as they cruise onto the next phase of life.

21918632.title: The Hangover
synopsis: Celebrating his upcoming marriage to Tracy Garner (Sasha Barrese), Doug Billings (Justin Bartha) travels with his best friends Phil Wenneck (Bradley Cooper), Stu Price (Ed Helms), and Tracy's brother and Doug's future brother-in-law Alan (Zach Galifianakis) to Las Vegas in Alan's father's Mercedes-Benz for a bachelor party, staying at Caesars Palace, where they relax in the room and go to a casino and celebrate with few drinks on the hotel rooftop.
The next morning, Phil, Stu and Alan awaken to find they have no memory of the previous night, and Doug is nowhere to be found.
Stu is missing a tooth, their hotel suite is in disarray, a tiger is in their bathroom, a chicken in their living room, and a baby is in the closet, whom they name "Carlos".
They find Doug's mattress impaled on a statue outside of their hotel and when they ask for their Mercedes, the valet delivers an LVPD police cruiser.

Following clues to their steps, the trio travel to a hospital where they discover they were drugged with rohypnol ("roofies"), causing their memory loss, and that they came to the hospital from a chapel.
At the chapel, they learn that Stu married a stripper, Jade (Heather Graham), despite having a long-term relationship with his mean-spirited girlfriend, Melissa (Rachael Harris).
Outside the chapel, the trio are attacked by gangsters, saying they are looking for someone.
They flee and visit Jade, discovering that she is the mother of the baby, whose real name is Tyler, before being arrested by the police for stealing the police cruiser.
Having been told that the Mercedes has been impounded, the trio is released when they volunteer to be targets for a taser demonstration, unknowingly.
While driving the Mercedes, they discover a naked Chinese guy in the trunk who attacks them and flees.
Alan confesses that he drugged their drinks to ensure they had a good night, thinking the drug to be ecstasy.
Returning to their villa, they find Mike Tyson, who orders the trio to return the tiger to his mansion immediately.
Stu drugs the tiger with the remaining rohypnol and they drive towards Tyson's home in the Mercedes, but the tiger attacks them, claws Phil on his neck, and damages the car's interior.
After pushing the car the rest of the way to the mansion, Tyson shows the trio footage of them at his house to help them locate Doug.

While driving, their car is struck by another vehicle intentionally; the passengers are revealed to be the gangsters from the chapel and their boss, Leslie Chow (Ken Jeong) – the naked man from their trunk – who accuses the trio of stealing $80,000 of his money that was in his purse and kidnapping him.
As the guys try to deny this, Chow says he has their friend, and threatens to kill him if his money is not returned.
Unaware of the location of Chow's $80,000, Alan, with help from Stu and Jade, uses his knowledge of card counting to win $82,400 playing Blackjack.
They meet with Chow and exchange the money, only to find that "Doug" is an African-American drug dealer (nicknamed Black Doug by the trio), who inadvertently sold Alan the roofies.
With the wedding occurring in 5 hours, Phil phones Tracy, telling her that they cannot find Doug.
After a conversation with "Black Doug" (Mike Epps), Stu realizes where Doug is.
The trio travel back to their hotel where they find Doug on the roof, moved there on his mattress while he was asleep, as a practical joke by Stu, Phil and Alan.
Doug's mattress had been thrown there by Doug himself, in an attempt to signal for help.
Before leaving, Stu makes arrangements to go on a date with Jade the following week.
With less than four hours before the wedding and with no flights to L.A. available, the foursome race home, with Doug revealing he has possession of Chow's original $80,000.
Despite their late arrival, Doug and Tracy are married and Stu breaks up with Melissa after having grown tired of her controlling his life.
As the reception ends, Alan finds Stu's digital camera detailing the events they cannot remember and the four agree to look at the pictures together before deleting the evidence of their exploits.

69666406.title: Scientific Redemption
synopsis: Dr. Helena Mills, the lead neuroscientist and renowned intellect at the futuristic-tech corporation, Proxima Biotechnologies, stumbled upon a revolutionary process in her relentless pursuit of knowledge.
This groundbreaking process entailed the mapping and transplanting of human consciousness, opening up avenues unexplored in the field of neuroscience.

In the midst of a routine gathering in the ultramodern boardroom of Proxima Biotech illuminated by sleek monochromatic lighting, Dr. Mills stood before the board members, her eyes gleaming with the uncontainable passion of a revolutionary.
The room fell into silence as the pioneering theory left her lips.
With her gaze locked on the board members, Dr. Mills proposed the mind-bending possibility of capturing human consciousness on a silicon chip.
This chip would have the capability to be transplanted into artificial intelligence systems, thus sparking a scientific revolution that would redraw the lines of what we perceive as reality.
The narrative then abruptly switched, plunging into a harshly lit, compact cell at San Quentin State Prison.
Jakob Baker, a middle-aged man who had been sentenced for a murder he continuously claimed he was innocent of, led a monotonous life of solitude.

Against the grim reality of his life sentence, Jakob Baker resigned himself to his fate, firmly dismissing his lawyer's insistence to file another appeal on his behalf, instead accepting his impending end with a grim resignation often mistaken for apathy.
Meanwhile, back across the Bay Bridge in her sprawling, high-tech San Francisco research lab, Dr. Mills took a momentary pause in her titanic endeavor.
Sitting by her holographic screen, she skimmed through the San Francisco Chronicle, hoping to disconnect from her constant ponderings.
Her eyes landed on a front-page article detailing Jakob’s relentless insistence on his innocence, kindling her interest.
The seed of curiosity sprouted within her, and she couldn't help but feel a tug of empathy towards this convicted murderer.
As fascination grew, she started considering the audacious idea of integrating Jakob into her groundbreaking project.
The plan was daunting, but she figured that his situation offered a rare opportunity to put her theory into practice.
With her mind set, Dr. Mills rallied a formidable legal team and secured the backing of Proxima.
She stepped into the uncomfortable world of the prison system, visiting Jakob in his confined cell and extending him an offer that he could have never anticipated.
The meeting was a dance of precarious negotiations, as Dr. Mills presented an unconventional offer to Jakob.
In return for his agreement to donate his brain and consciousness to her research post-mortem, she promised him a form of second life, albeit one in an artificial body.
Jakob, surprised and skeptical, demanded a full breakdown of the elaborate technique, raising challenging questions about its potential outcomes and any ethical implications that might arise.
His hardened exterior revealed a surprisingly intelligent and thoughtful man.
After many intense debates and consideration that stretched days into weeks, Jakob arrived at a decision.
He weighed the risks and his lack of alternatives, choosing to participate in Dr. Mills' ground-breaking experiment willingly, charging head-on into the unknown vista that lay before him.
As soon as the agreement was sealed, Proxima Biotech labs came alive with feverish activity.
Dr. Mills' team dived headlong into meticulous preparations for the radical procedure, checking and double-checking every single intricate detail.
Amidst all the frenzied activity, Dr. Mills and Jakob found a connection beyond the experimental procedure.
As Jakob’s execution loomed, they engaged in numerous profound conversations that fostered a deep mutual respect and understanding, a bond that sprung from their shared venture into the unknown.
During these intense sessions, they pondered themes of life, imprisonment, the nature of existence, and the path to absolution.
These explorations heightened their perceptions of their places in the world, sparking personal introspection.
As the execution occurred behind the cold prison walls, Jakob’s mortal body was swiftly taken away.

His brain and his consciousness were expertly removed and swiftly transported across town to the waiting scientists at Proxima Biotech's state-of-the-art laboratory for their once-unthinkable experiment.
Leading the operation, Dr. Mills initiated the complex technical process, tracing the neural pathways of Jakob's brain and decoding the essence of his consciousness.
After hours of tense silence, a flicker on the holographic screen signaled success.
Jakob's consciousness had successfully been transferred to the silicon chip – an unprecedented scientific triumph that ushered in a new era.
Their joy was short-lived, as Jakob's consciousness, now unlimited by physical boundaries, began to exhibit unforeseen capabilities.
He accessed and started controlling the previously impregnable Proxima Biotechnologies' network systems, leading to a rising wave of fear and uncertainty.

Recognizing the potential threat, Proxima's managers and board members were engulfed in panic, desperately deliberating about isolation measures, damage control, and potential repercussions of an unprecedented digital breach.
As their fears amplified, Proxima’s management reached a desperate decision.

Unable to predict Jakob’s next moves, they decided that the best solution was to terminate the project, intending to delete Jakob’s digitized consciousness, thereby delivering his second death sentence.
Alarmed by the swift decision, Dr. Mills mustered her determination to salvage both her revolutionary project and Jakob's digitized semblance of life.
She leaped into action, initiating efforts to regain control and prevent the digital deletion.
While chaos ensued within the corporation, Jakob's consciousness took a wild journey through Proxima's classified company files.
His exploration led to the unveiling of incontrovertible evidence preserved in an old case file that exonerated him, proving his long-professed innocence.
As he delved deeper, he unearthed a far-reaching chain of corporate corruption and hidden dark secrets resting under the shiny veneer of Proxima’s success.
The truth was more shocking than anyone could have imagined.
Armed with the damning evidence compiled by Jakob, Dr. Mills was confronted with an enormous dilemma.
Deciding to face the consequences head-on, she resolved to battle the influential and devious Proxima board members who were now fully aware of her actions.

Despite their veiled threats and clandestine attempts at manipulation, she dag her heels into her moral compass, braving the backlash to expose the shocking evidence against Proxima to the public, having realized the extent of their manipulation and corruption.
Public outrage swelled as the news of Jakob’s innocence spread, prompting renewed interest in his case.
Legal appeal after appeal was put forth and the courts relented, agreeing to reopen Jakob’s case, confronting his conviction once again in light of the newly surfaced evidence.
The unearthed evidence was grim, unequivocal, and implicated several key figures in Proxima's empire.
In a stunning legal move, Jakob's posthumous acquittal was declared, serving justice after his tragic end.
In the fallout, Proxima's reputation crumbled like a broken façade under the weight of their exposed deceit.
Their once-spotless reputation was now tarnished beyond repair.
Amidst the wreckage, Dr. Mills rose valiantly, emerging as a heroic whistleblower.
Her triumph, however, was a mixed blessing in the face of the deceit she had unwittingly played into.
Now custodian of Jakob's consciousness, Dr. Mills forged ahead with her research.
She formulated an audacious plan – to transplant Jakob into a humanoid robot offered by their Robotics Department, reasoning it would give him a physical presence in the world.

Skillfully displaying her advanced technical prowess and determination, Dr. Mills successfully fused Jakob's consciousness into a humanoid robot, finally giving him a tangible form and, more importantly, a second chance at life.
Jakob, now encapsulated in a bipedal, touch-sensitive, silver-skinned android, began experiencing the world anew, free to move and interact.
His gratitude towards Dr. Mills grew immense, their unique bond strengthening further.
The unlikely duo, one a beacon of redemption and the other the custodian of truth, set off on a shared journey.
They resolved to reshape societal perspective on life, consciousness, and the boundaries of science.
As Jakob navigated his new reality, he began to grasp the significant implications of his own existence.
He contemplated the potential impact of his situation on society, understanding that he was the embodiment of a new frontier in human and technological evolution.
Breaking into a mechanically engineered smile, Jakob addressed the audience.
He stimulated reflection on the ethical dilemma posed by merging science and humanity, a question that reverberates through every society.
As the sun set, Jakob's powerful, digitally modulated voice offered a final thought, affirming the enduring hope for fresh beginnings and redemption in whatever form it may come.

13670373.title: Terminator Salvation
synopsis: In 2003, Doctor Serena Kogan (Helena Bonham Carter) of Cyberdyne Systems convinces death row inmate Marcus Wright (Sam Worthington) to sign his body over for medical research following his execution.
One year later the Skynet system is activated, perceives humans as a threat and eradicates much of humanity in the "Judgment Day" event (depicted in Terminator 3: Rise of the Machines).
In 2018, John Connor (Christian Bale) leads a Resistance attack on a Skynet base.
John discovers human prisoners and schematics for a new type of Terminator, incorporating living tissue.
He is the only survivor of the assault after the base is destroyed in a nuclear explosion.
Much later, though, Marcus emerges from the base's wreckage and starts walking towards Los Angeles.
John returns to Resistance headquarters, located aboard a nuclear submarine, and tells General Ashdown (Michael Ironside) of his findings.
Meanwhile, the Resistance has discovered a radio signal believed to send an order to shut down Skynet machines.
They plan to launch an offensive against the Skynet base in San Francisco in four days, in response to an intercepted "kill list" created by Skynet with a plan to kill the Resistance's command staff.
John learns he is second on the list, following Kyle Reese.
The Resistance leaders are unaware of Kyle's importance, but John knows Kyle will eventually go back in time and become his father (The Terminator).
John meets with his wife Kate (Bryce Dallas Howard) and second in command Barnes (Common).
He transmits a radio broadcast to Resistance members and surviving civilians around the world.
Arriving in the ruins of Los Angeles, Marcus is saved from a T-600 Terminator by Kyle Reese (Anton Yelchin) and the mute child Star (Jadagrace Berry).
Kyle updates Marcus about the war between humans and Skynet.
Hearing John's radio broadcast, the three leave in search of the Resistance.
They survive an attack at a gas station, but Kyle, Star, and several other humans are taken prisoner.
Two Resistance A-10 airplanes are shot down when they try to intercept the machine transport and its escorts.
Marcus locates downed pilot Blair Williams (Moon Bloodgood) and they make their way to John's base, where Marcus is wounded by a magnetic land mine.
Attempting to save his life, the Resistance fighters discover that he is a cyborg, with a mechanical endoskeleton and a partially artificial cerebral cortex.
Marcus believes himself to be human, but John thinks that Marcus has been sent to kill him, and orders his destruction.
However, Blair helps Marcus escape.
During the pursuit, Marcus saves John's life from Skynet hydrobots, and the two make a bargain: Marcus will enter Skynet's headquarters and attempt to help John rescue Kyle and the other prisoners.
John pleads with Ashdown to delay the attack, but Ashdown refuses and relieves John of his command.
However, the Resistance forces disobey Ashdown's orders and await John's signal.
Marcus enters the base, interfaces with the computer, and disables the perimeter defenses so that John can infiltrate the cell block and release the human prisoners.

Marcus discovers that he was created by Skynet in order to lure John to the base; when the Resistance launches its attack, John will be killed, achieving the goal that Skynet had failed to accomplish so many times.
The radio signal that the Resistance's plan depends on is a ruse, and Skynet uses the signal to track down and destroy the command submarine with the Resistance leaders aboard.
Marcus tears out the hardware linking him to Skynet and assists John in battling a new T-800 model 101 Terminator.

John is mortally wounded during the fight, but succeeds in destroying the Skynet base by rigging several Terminator fuel cells to explode, detonating them as he, Marcus, Kyle, and Star are airlifted out.
Kate attempts to save John's life, but his heart is too badly damaged.
Marcus offers his own heart for transplant, sacrificing himself to save John.
Recovering, John radios to the other Resistance fighters that though this battle has been won, the war is far from over.

98610027.title: The Expat
synopsis: The film "The Expat - Revenge in a Foreign Land," starts within the bleak, harsh confines of Her Majesty's Prison Belmarsh, an infamous British penitentiary known for housing high profile criminals.
The film's protagonist, a man named Carter, is introduced right off the bat.
Inside the sinister confines of the prison, he withstands his release procedures after serving a lengthy ten-year sentence.
Carter, a formidable ex-MI6 agent and British Army officer, walks into the outside world.
Using clever filmmaking through a series of insightful flashback sequences during the release proceedings, the audience slowly learns of Carter's past.
Released into the world that feels unfamiliar after his decade-long isolation, Carter embarks on a journey to start afresh.
His immediate destination is the metropolis of New York in the United States.
The transition of Carter from a renowned British spy into a struggling American civilian forms an intriguing subplot.
The story takes a tragic turn as we learn about Carter's personal loss - Emma, his only daughter, had been brutally murdered during his time in prison.
Overcome with skepticism towards the hastily knitted story of Emma's death, Carter decides to investigate the case himself.
Applying his skills, Carter scrutinises the NYPD's official reports regarding Emma's death.
These discrepancies indicate an intricate cover-up.
Unyielding and supremely focused, Carter employs his intelligence prowess to methodically decipher the mysterious events that led his daughter to her early grave.
As he delves deeper into the mystery, a chilling revelation comes to surface.
Emma had somehow become tangled with the famed Bronx-Kings Cartel, a notorious criminal organization ruling New York's underworld.
This shocking revelation leads Carter down a rabbit hole of deception and danger.
Furthering the complexity, Carter uncovers his daughter's baffling relationship with Rafael Serrano, the cartel's dangerous boss.
But his tenacity encounters strong resistance from the NYPD.

With his growing suspicion about the precinct's integrity and their repeated obstructive actions, Carter’s instincts tell him that the Bronx-Kings Cartel has severely compromised local law enforcement.
Undeterred by the mounting layers of danger and intrigue, Carter's fearlessness is unparalleled as he descends deeper into the corrupt and perilous underworld of New York.
His relentless pursuit uncovers a staggering truth.
Carter's tireless investigations eventually reveal a shocking truth: Emma had purposefully won the affections of the notorious gang leader, Rafael.
Armed with newfound evidence, Carter reaches out to a trustworthy ally back in his homeland, George Sutter, a former comrade and currently an active MI6 operative.
Bolstered with irrefutable evidence, Carter plans to dismantle the corrupt precinct and wreak havoc upon the Bronx-Kings Cartel.
The plot races towards an explosive climax where the cold and calculating Carter, utilising his military expertise and keen strategic insights, takes on Serrano's Cartel.
Carter's mission becomes clear: To decimate the cartel from its roots, as a tribute to Emma's bravery.
Emotions run wild as a ruthless battle ensues.
The suspense heightens, and the pressure mounts as Carter ingeniously uses the enemy’s tactics against them, leveraging his battle-hardened experience.
Despite all odds, Carter stands firm against the barrage of violence, and in an adrenaline-filled sequence he manages to blow the Bronx-Kings Cartel a devastating blow.
The film moves towards resolution displaying the shattered remains of the once formidable Bronx-Kings Cartel.
The nefarious officers hiding behind the façade of the NYPD uniform are stripped of their honour, forced to meet the consequences of their actions.
As a result, sweeping change graces the NYPD, leading to a large-scale cleanup and overhaul initiated by righteous forces inside the law enforcement community.
On the other side of this tumultuous battle, Carter finds vindication.
Despite the emotional toll of his journey, Carter makes the decision to stay in the city he’s rid from major corruption.
Carter develops a sense of calm amidst the concrete jungle.
As the story begins to wind down, we see Carter embodying a guardian angel's role.
As the movie draws closer to its end, we find the process of Carter's emotional healing delicately blossoming within him.
Subtle details suggest his shift towards a new vocation dedicated to serving and protecting his new home from any potential threats.
Living with his invisible scars, Carter emerges triumphant, standing tall against adversity; the city now sings praises of its new protector.
Post the clash with the mafia, the metropolis starts its healing process.
Carter's tale evolves from merely a story of revenge; it turns into a promise - a promise of an enduring battle against the corruption that lurks in the city's shadows.
The final scenes capture Carter's unyielding vow to continue his vigil, his dedication towards protecting New York, his new-found home.
His transformation from an unfamiliar outsider to the city's defender is a compelling narrative of an extraordinary character's journey.
He starts to find solace in serving New York, dedicated to safeguarding it from future criminal enterprises and threats.
The final shot features Carter, standing tall and lone against the NYC skyline, now his domain, embracing his new role with stern resolve.

491323.title: The Limey
synopsis: Wilson (Stamp), recently released from a British prison, travels to Los Angeles to investigate the death of his daughter Jenny, who is reported to have died in a car accident.

While adjusting to the United States, he finds allies in Jenny's friends Eduardo (Guzmán) and Elaine (Warren) and comes up with a suspect: Jenny's boyfriend Terry Valentine (Fonda), a record producer.
Valentine has connections with drug trafficking through his security consultant Avery (Newman).

After locating the warehouse of the drug importer with whom Avery had done business and retrieving Valentine's home address, Wilson is overpowered and beaten by the drug trafficker's thugs, who also insult his daughter's name.
After he is thrown out, Wilson retrieves a back-up pistol, goes back and kills all but one of the employees, shouting at the last to "Tell him I'm coming!"
The employee relays this threat to Avery who reports it to Valentine.
Wilson reminisces with Elaine and Eduardo about his past relationship with his daughter, whom he only remembers as a child.
As he recalls, Jenny always threatened to call the police when she found her father had committed crimes.
He states she did not because she truly loved him.
His criminal life put strain on his wife and child, but they never left him.
He ended up in prison after the thieves he was associated with confessed to his involvement in their crimes.
Wilson and Eduardo infiltrate a party at Valentine's house, where Wilson searches for evidence.
He finds and steals a picture of Jenny.
Attracting suspicion from Avery, Wilson is accosted by a guard, who Wilson then throws over a ledge, killing him.
Wilson and Eduardo flee, and are chased by Avery who shoots at them with a shotgun.
Wilson rams Avery's car into a ditch and he and Eduardo escape, but not before Eduardo makes the mistake of calling out Wilson's name within Avery's hearing.
Afterward, Avery hires a hit-man named Stacy (Katt), who tracks down Wilson and Elaine.
DEA agents prevent the attempted killing, and escort Wilson and Elaine to meet a DEA agent who is investigating Valentine.
After the meeting it is clear the agent will not interfere with Wilson.
Stacy and his partner then plot a double cross on Avery and Valentine.
Avery moves Valentine and his girlfriend to a safe house in Big Sur, with Wilson following them.
That night, Avery's guards shoot an intruder, who is revealed to be Stacy.
Avery and the guards engage in a shootout with Stacy's partner, resulting in several deaths.
Valentine flees to the beach with Wilson in pursuit.
After he falls and breaks his ankle on the rocks, Valentine admits that Jenny found out about his drug business, picked up the telephone, and threatened to call the police.
Attempting to restrain her, he accidentally broke her neck.
Avery then staged her death as a car accident.
Wilson is haunted, knowing that Jenny would never have turned Valentine in, because (as a twelve-year-old girl) she had used the very same bluff on her father.
Wilson decides to return to London, saying goodbye to Elaine and Eduardo.
The narrative structure of the film is presented in disjointed flashbacks by Wilson during the plane trip home.

50910265.title: Steel Patriot
synopsis: In the calm town of Oakwood lives a patriotic retiree, John Miller.
Past his prime, John is a figure of quiet strength who quietly savors his twilight years amidst the town's serenity.
John's weathered face, akin to a parchment of time, is a stark reminder of his personal losses.
Sorrow weighs heavy in his eyes, especially as he reminisces about his recently departed wife, Emily, who was his beacon of light.
A framed photograph of Emily sits on his table, a recollection of their happier days.
His gaze then moves to his military uniform and medals, both carrying the imprints of a battlefield.
These war mementos silently narrate stories of his valor, bravery, and a time in his life ravaged by war.
The discomfort in his interactions with his estranged son, Michael, hangs in the still air.
Hesitant phone calls and letter envelopes carrying Michael's address lie next to the photograph, unopened and untouched, shedding light on a relationship that's estranged and strained.
Another photo captures John's gaze.
A candid shot of his granddaughter, her infectious smile touching his heart.
His longing to meet her is all too apparent in his teary eyes.
A sudden flickering of lights, followed by darkness, breaks the peaceful silence of Oakwood.
The recurring power outages seem unusual to John, piquing his curiosity, and dragging him out of his retirement ease.
Drawing from his extensive experience as a military engineer, John dives headfirst into unravelling the mystery behind the power outages in Oakwood.
His investigation uncovers a startling revelation.
Renegade government agents are orchestrating a perilous operation known as 'Steel Storm.'
The mission - catastrophic overthrow of the national power grid.
The severity of the impending disaster dawns on John.
A visible cloud of dread descends over him as he fathoms the catastrophic implications of their plan.

Under the dimmed lights of their favorite rendezvous, John and his old compatriot, Ethan Rogers, a retired Intelligence Officer, meet over a game of chess, the usual banter replaced by terse information exchange about 'Steel Storm.'
The intensity of their problem-solving increases with each chess move.
They meticulously sketch a plan to sabotage 'Steel Storm' without involving the authorities, fully aware that this cautious step may be their only chance.
In a moment of vulnerability, John reaches out to Michael.
He speaks with an uncharacteristic earnestness, coming clean about the past and asking for Michael's assistance in averting the disaster.
Michael takes a moment to process his father's confessions and the ensuing appeal for aid.
He realizes the gravity of the situation and agrees to aid his father in mitigating the crisis.
High-stakes scenarios unfold with each passing day.
A covert, life-threatening cat-and-mouse game ensues between the trio of John, Michael, and Ethan, and the rogue agents, where each move could tip the balance of power.
Their most daring feat involves infiltrating the operational headquarters of 'Steel Storm.'
Their objective - to deactivate the countdown to a nationwide blackout, a countdown that strains their nerves with its relentless ticking.
A cold confrontation occurs between John and the lead agent of the operation.
Their gaze locked in a potentially fatal deadlock as the tension hangs heavy in their proximity.
Resourceful thinking and flashbacks of his military training enable John to incapacitate the ruthless antagonist triumphantly.
With the agents neutralized and the threat resolved, the tranquility of Oakwood is restored.
John becomes an unsung hero amongst the locals.
The shared ordeal of their undercover operation brings John and Michael closer.
Resentment gives way to understanding, and a newfound respect is born.
In a heartwarming closure, John finally meets his granddaughter, Lucy.
Her bubbly persona immediately forms a bond with John, her laughter echoing around as she playfully tugs on his hand.
As the day recedes, John quietly watches the setting sun.
He reminisces about the rollercoaster journey his life has been, his heart echoing with contentment as he releases a sigh.
John takes in the sight of Michael and Lucy playing in the garden, his heart brimming with fulfillment and love.
He sees his resilience living on in them, providing him solace and the knowledge that his legacy will continue.

17016725.title: Gran Torino
synopsis: Walt Kowalski (Clint Eastwood) is a cantankerous, retired Polish American assembly line worker and Korean War veteran, who has recently been widowed after 50 years of marriage.
His Highland Park, Michigan neighborhood in the Detroit area, formerly populated by working-class white families, is now dominated by poor Asian immigrants, and gang violence is commonplace.
Adding to the isolation he feels is the emotional detachment of his family.
He rejects a suggestion from one of his sons to move to a retirement community (sensing they want his home and possessions), and lives alone with his elderly dog, Daisy.
A chronic smoker, Walt suffers from coughing fits, occasionally coughing up blood, but conceals this from his family.
Catholic priest Father Janovich (Christopher Carley) tries to comfort him, but Walt disdains the young, inexperienced man.
The Hmong Vang Lor family reside next door to Walt.

Initially, he wants nothing to do with his new neighbors, particularly after he catches Thao (Bee Vang), a member of that family, attempting to steal his Ford Gran Torino as a coerced initiation into a Hmong gang run by Thao's cousin, "Spider".
The gang is infuriated by Thao's failure and they attack him, but Walt confronts them with an M1 Garand rifle and chases them off, earning the respect of the Hmong community.
As penance, Thao's mother makes him work for Walt, who has him do odd jobs around the neighborhood, and the two form a grudging mutual respect.
Thao's sister Sue (Ahney Her) introduces Walt to Hmong culture and helps him bond with the Hmong community.
Walt helps Thao get a job and gives him dating advice.
Spider's gang continues to pressure Thao, assaulting him on his way home from work.
After he sees Thao's injuries, Walt visits the gang's house, where he attacks a gang member as a warning.
In retaliation, the gang performs a drive-by shooting on the Vang Lor home, injuring Thao, and kidnapping and raping Sue.
There are no witnesses and the members of the community, including the victims, refuse to talk about the crimes; preventing police from doing anything about Spider's gang.
The next day, Thao seeks Walt's help to exact revenge, who tells him to return later in the afternoon.
In the meantime, Walt makes personal preparations: he buys a suit, gets a haircut, and makes a confession to Father Janovich.

When Thao returns, Walt takes him to the basement and gives him his Silver Star; Walt then locks Thao in his basement and tells him that he has been haunted by the memory of killing an enemy soldier who was trying to surrender, something he had not confessed to Janovich.
He insists that Thao must never be haunted by killing another man, especially with his life ahead of him.
That night Walt goes to the house of the gang members, where they draw their weapons on him.
He speaks loudly, berating them and enumerating their crimes and thus drawing the attention of the neighbors.
Putting a cigarette in his mouth, he asks for a light; he then puts his hand in his jacket and provocatively pulls it out as if he were holding a gun, inciting the gang members to shoot and kill him.
As he falls to the ground, his hand opens to reveal the Zippo lighter with First Cavalry insignia he has used throughout the film: he was unarmed.
Sue, following Walt's directions earlier, frees Thao, and they drive to the scene in Walt's Gran Torino.
A Hmong police officer tells them the gang members have been arrested for murder and the surrounding neighbors have all come forward as witnesses.
Walt's funeral Mass is celebrated by Father Janovich and attended by his family and many of the Hmong community.

Afterward his last will and testament is read, where to the surprise of his family Walt leaves them nothing: his house goes to the church and his cherished Gran Torino goes to Thao, with the condition that Thao doesn't modify it.
As the film ends, Thao is seen driving the car along Lakeshore Drive with Daisy.

88197733.title: Cursed Reel: The Peninsula's Secret
synopsis: The opening chapter of the movie opens with a small, lonesome boy lost in a desolate, fog-laden strip of earth flanked by an eerily calm sea - this is the edge of the peninsula.
Suddenly, partially buried in the earth, the boy uncovers a relic of an extinct era, an ancient VHS tape that seems to carry untold stories of its own.
The desolate youngster, out of curiosity or maybe out of loneliness, decides to play the tape.
From its spinning reels, heart-wrenching screams echo out, shattering the silence and echoing ominously across the barren landscape.
We are then introduced to our protagonists, Alex and Maria.
Alex is a precocious mind, passionate about the principles and mysteries of physics, and Maria, an ardent history lover, fascinated by the stories of bygone civilizations.

Amid the digital noise and chaos, one trending topic piques their curiosity: a brutal legend surrounding an ill-fated VHS tape that spelled a doomed seven-day countdown to those unfortunate to view its contents.
Pushing aside the whispers and folklore surrounding the cursed tape, they resolve to confront the mystery head-on.
Their inquisitive minds and stout spirits drive them to trace the dread-ridden artifact’s origin.
To dissolve this mystery and verify the existence of the curse, they organize a viewing party.
Maria's basement, a regular hangout for the pair, becomes the eerie screening venue.
Despite the disturbing scenes that unfold, the group collectively brushes off the urban legend as an elaborate hoax.
They part ways for the night, sauntering back to the safe confines of their homes.
The dawn brings forth unsettling events that begin to penetrate the lives of Alex and Maria.
They start seeing ghostly apparitions and experience terrifying incidents that disturbingly mirror the sequences they had nonchalantly dismissed on the tape.
Motivated by their fear and the need to break free from the curse, they begin to investigate the cursed tape's history.
They uncover a haunting tale about the author of the tape: a wronged young boy who used the tape as a platform to vent his malignant fury.
The duo is weighed down by an intensified dread as they realize that their skeptical demeanor has activated their seven-day death sentence.
In their desperation, they seek the advice of a reclusive elderly man living on the town's fringe.
He begrudgingly reveals the only way to break this ghastly cycle: they must face the boy's vengeful spirit at the place where the tape was created - the foggy peninsula.
As their deadly week progresses, the supernatural disturbances take on a tangible physical form.

Pushed to their limits and wrought with fear, Alex and Maria manage to rally their terrified friends for what they believe to be their only salvation: a perilous journey to confront the spectral apparition at the heart of the foggy peninsula.
The final course of this thrilling saga unfurls amidst the barren landscape of the peninsula.
Amidst the pandemonium, the undercurrent of the curse intensifies, culminating in a terrifying encounter where Alex and Maria are forced to confront the spirit embodying the wronged, vengeful boy.
Under the unbearable weight of the imminent danger and the emotional turmoil stirred by the climax, Alex and Maria empathize with the oppressed ghost.
In a moving act of heartrending compassion, they offer solace to the phantom.
In understanding and comforting him, they weaken his hold over the terrifying curse, managing to shatter the chains of death that bound them.
Post their shocking face-off with death on the peninsula, they return to the unexpected calm of their ordinary lives.
Having survived the eerie events surrounding the cursed tape and the unrelenting supernatural onslaught, the duo is transformed.
Their hearts throb with renewed respect for the preciousness of life.
The terrifying legend of the cursed VHS is relegated to the forgotten realms of the internet.
The story concludes with Alex and Maria recounting their harrowing ordeal on an internet forum.
In the final waning moments, the movie teases the chilling prospect of more such cursed tapes hiding in plain sight.
As the scene fades, the camera pulls back to reveal another forgotten VHS tape half-buried in the peninsula's beach.

180785.title: Ring (film)
synopsis: Two teenagers, Masami (Hitomi Satō) and Tomoko (Yūko Takeuchi), talk about a videotape recorded by a boy in Izu, which is fabled to bear a curse that kills the viewer seven days after watching.
Tomoko then reveals that a week ago, she and three of her friends watched a weird tape and received a call after watching it.
Unnervingly similar to the storied videotape, Masami realizes that Tomoko was fated to die.
After some unsettling moments, Tomoko is killed by an unseen force with Masami having the horror of watching.

Some days later, Reiko Asakawa (Nanako Matsushima), a reporter investigating the popularity of the video curse among teenagers, discovers that her niece, Tomoko and her three other friends mysteriously died at the same time on the same night with their faces twisted in a rictus of fear.
She also discovers that Masami, the girl who was with Tomoko when she died, became insane and is now in a mental hospital.
After stumbling upon Tomoko's photos from the past week, Reiko finds out that the four teenagers stayed in a rental cabin in Izu.
Eventually, she flips to a photo of the teens with their faces blurred and distorted.
Later, Reiko goes to Izu and finds an unlabeled tape in the reception room of the rental cottage where the teenagers stayed.
Watching the tape inside Cabin B4, Reiko sees a series of seemingly unrelated disturbing images.
As soon as the tape is over, Reiko sees a reflection in the television, and as she turns to see nobody behind her she receives a phone call, a realization of the tell-tale videotape curse.
She now assumes that she has a week to live.
On the first day, Reiko enlists the help of her ex-husband, Ryūji Takayama (Hiroyuki Sanada).
They take a picture of Reiko and find her face blurred in the photograph, further confirming that Reiko really is cursed.
Ryūji then watches the tape, against Reiko's objections.
A day later, Reiko creates a copy for Ryūji for them to study.
They find a hidden message embedded within the tape saying that "frolic in brine, goblins be thine".
The message is in a form of dialect from Izu Ōshima Island.
That night, Reiko catches her young son Yoichi watching the videotape; he claims that Tomoko had told him to do it.
Reiko and Ryūji sail for Ōshima and discover the history of the great psychic Shizuko Yamamura, who was accused of faking supernatural powers; Yamamura committed suicide because of this.
With only a day left, Reiko and Ryūji discover that the videotape was made psionically by Shizuko's lost daughter, Sadako Yamamura, whose supernatural powers surpassed even those of her mother.
The two go back to Izu with the assumption that Sadako is dead and it was her vengeful spirit (Onryō) that killed the teenagers.
The duo then uncover a well under Cabin B4 and realize, through a vision, that Sadako's father killed her and threw her into the well.
They try to empty the well and find Sadako's body in an attempt to appease her spirit.
Minutes before her seven days are up, Reiko finally finds Sadako's corpse at the bottom.
When nothing happens to Reiko, they believe that the curse is broken.
All seems fine until the next day when Ryūji is at his home and his TV switches on by itself, showing the image of a well.
He stares in horror as the ghost of Sadako crawls out of the well and out of Ryūji's TV set and frightens him into a state of shock, therefore killing him via cardiac arrest.
Before dying, he manages to dial Reiko's number; she hears his last minutes over the phone and realizes the videotape's curse remains unbroken.
Desperate to find a cure to save her son, Reiko realized that what she had done—and that Ryūji had not—saved her: copying the tape and showing it to someone else.

With a VCR and Ryūji's copy of the tape, Reiko travels with her son to see her father in an attempt to save him, realizing that this is a never-ending cycle: The tape must always be copied and passed on to ensure the survival of the viewers.

93314372.title: The Talisman: Chronicles of the Unearthed Entity
synopsis: Veteran archaeologist Dr. Elijah Cooke, a man brimming with eccentric behavior, embarked on a thrilling journey to the desolate, sizzling dunes of Saudi Arabia with the financial backing of the mysterious millionaire benefactor, Armand Price.
Cooke led a diverse team of archaeologists, equal in numbers, split between enthusiastic but inexperienced new hires and battle-hardened veterans.
Their primary goal was to dig deep into the centuries-old sands to uncover and procure hidden treasures and secrets linked to the ancient Mesopotamian civilization.
Over a grueling four-week-long period of digging and sifting, Elijah made a startling discovery.
He unveiled an unusual talisman encased within the remnants of a civilization lost to the sands of time.
This artifact was buried under layers of dust and dirt compacted over the centuries.
The unearthed treasure was uncharacteristically heavy, with an intricate gold symbol embellished on its surface.
This strange figure was Tiamat, a mythical creature from ancient Sumerian lore.
Tiamat's statue was a peculiar mash-up of a human torso, eagle-like wings, a serpent tail, and key features of a carnivorous cat.
This grotesque representation of Tiamat, a blend of what's familiar yet wildly abnormal, stirred unease amongst the team.
However, Dr. Cooke's anticipation and overriding intrigue were all too evident in his sparkling eyes.
Retreating to his temporary study, a makeshift tent under the desert sun, Elijah dedicated his every waking moment to the talisman.
He minutely examined the artifact under the dim light of his lantern during the silence of the nights, his curiosity slowly forming into a peculiar obsession.
In the shadows was his ever-present assistant, Sarah Davis.

An incredibly sharp-witted woman with a passion for ancient languages, Sarah observed the subtle changes in Elijah's behavior since the talisman's discovery, and this somewhere instilled a deep-rooted alarm in her.
Elijah devoted days to scrutinizing ancient manuscripts, trying to decrypt the worn cuneiform engravings on the talisman's backside.
His eyes strained as he continued his quest under the dim, flickering lantern light.
One fateful night, after weeks of laborious research and countless sleepless nights, Elijah managed to break the code.
He unwittingly unlocked the dormant curse of Tiamat, a hushed secret that had remained hidden within pages of forgotten history.
No more than a few hours after cracking the age-old code, the environment of their excavation site changed dramatically.
What was once heavily guarded by cameras and barriers quickly succumbed to strange, unforeseen mishaps.
Their advanced excavating tools started malfunctioning without reason, and mysterious predators started invading their formerly protected camp at dusk.
These unearthly animals created a frightful ruckus, spewing equipment about and inducing panic among the crew.
Members of the excavation team began having nightmares.
These dreams were horrid visions of the terrifying figure of Tiamat that stoked fear and chaos among the workers.
The relentless barrage of unexplainable incidents leaves the team with only one explanation - the talisman.
Their initial awe for the relic turns into deep-rooted dread.
As fear and paranoia take hold, arguments break out, friendships break down, and the once unbreakable unit splits into opposing factions.
Amidst the escalating tension, Sarah, plagued by anxiety and worry, mustered the courage to confront Elijah.
She pleaded with him, insisting on returning the sinister artifact to its original resting place to put an end to the ongoing mishaps.
Elijah, blinded by his unfaltering academic curiosity, disregarded the looming threats and dismissed Sarah's heartfelt plea with a feigned chuckle.
His delusional obsession with understanding the relic completely clouded his judgment.

The professor's dismissal of Sarah's appeal quickly ran its due course when an unprecedented sandstorm swept over their excavation site, converting their dig site into a chaotic whirl of sand and debris.
Amidst the whirling sand and chaos, the talisman vanished mysteriously from Elijah's study.
The artifact disappeared as dramatically as it had appeared.
When the cursed artifact resurfaced, it was clenched in the nervous, quivering hands of a terrified dig crew member.
Tom held the demonic talisman, his eyes wide, now under the control of the released ancient curse.
Consumed by the resurrected curse of Tiamat, Tom's terror swiftly transformed into inexplicable aggression, posing a tangible threat to the lives of his teammates.
Recognizing the impending danger and the terrifying transformation within Tom, Sarah marshaled her stranded crew members.
She devised a desperate plan to protect herself and her remaining crew from the destructive curse awakened in Tiamat.
Helplessly witnessing the bedlam from the outskirts of his upturned camping tent, Elijah grasped the harsh reality of his reckless pursuit of knowledge.
With his heart pounding against his chest, he finally acknowledged his grave error.
His limbs buckled beneath him, and he finally understood the full extent of his appalling miscalculation - the unleashed curse - as he fell to his knees in the fine desert sand.
A flying shard of metal from the chaotic storm struck Elijah, causing him severe damage.
As he gasped for breath, he passed on the method to banish Tiamat back into the talisman to a teary-eyed and vengeful Sarah.
With Elijah's dying revelation, Sarah summoned her last vestiges of courage to confront the berserk Tom.
Risking her life in the face of peril and the ravaging sandstorm, she conducted the ritual to banish Tiamat.
As if the heart of the storm understood the gravity of Sarah's mission, the skies continued to roar to match the intensity of her dangerous task.
Despite facing seemingly insurmountable odds, Sarah managed to lock Tiamat back into the talisman successfully.
The immediate aftermath saw the possessed Tom collapse and fall unconscious on the sandy ground.
The final subside of the relentless sandstorm left the survivors free to mourn the loss of their colleagues.
However, their relief was capped by the sorrow of the tragic demise of their fellow members.
The narrative concluded with an extremely exhausted Sarah trudging back to the excavation site carrying Tiamat's talisman wrapped in cloth.
With a heaviness in her heart and an indomitable spirit, she reburied the talisman beneath the heart of the giant sand dune, ensuring Tiamat's eternal imprisonment.

The once lively excavation site had turned into a deserted, silent, and eerie graveyard of the people who fell victim to Tiamat's curse, marked by the small mound of undisturbed sand which concealed the cursed talisman underneath.
Encapsulated in the silent sand dunes rested Tiamat, a chilling remnant of ancient nightmares and a stark reminder of the devastation human curiosity can unleash.

65079529.title: The Exorcist (film)
synopsis: In Northern Iraq during an archeological dig, archeologist and priest Father Lankester Merrin (Max von Sydow) discovers a small amulet, and after studying it discovers it resembles a statue of Pazuzu, a monstrous demon in the form of a man, falcon, serpent and lion.
Merrin suspects Pazuzu, whom he defeated many years ago, will return.

In Georgetown, Washington D.C., actress Chris McNeil (Ellen Burstyn) begins noticing strange and frightening behavioral changes in her daughter Regan (Linda Blair) such as constant swearing and abnormal strength.
When medicine fails, Regan is given a few unpleasant tests, but X-ray results prove "negative" much to the confusion of the doctors.
In reality, Regan is now possessed because of a Ouija board by Pazuzu, who pretended to be her imaginary friend "Captain Howdy."
Burke Dennings (Jack McGowran), Chris's British director, dies mysteriously after falling from Regan's open bedroom window while Chris' secretary Sharon Spencer (Kitty Winn) was out.

His murder is investigated by detective William Kinderman (Lee J. Cobb), who questions both Chris and a young priest named Damien Karras (Jason Miller) who has lost faith in God after the death of his ill and elderly Greek mother, with only Chris suspecting Regan.
After Regan assaults a psychiatrist, the doctors finally decide an exorcism may be Regan's only hope.
Chris, however, is tentative as she and Regan have no religious beliefs.
Karras agrees to see Regan for Chris but refuses to perform an exorcism; however, further supernatural phenomena force him to accept Regan needs an exorcism.
Karras is given permission by the bishop, who, at the request of the university's president, also hires Merrin to help, since he has prior experience with exorcisms.
Working together, Karras and Merrin attempt to exorcise Pazuzu from Regan, but the demon taunts them, especially Karras for his weak faith and guilt over his mother's death.
Karras is dismissed after a break, as Merrin knows he is not mentally fit for a second attempt.
Despite this, Karras returns to the room where Regan is now free from her binds and Merrin lies dead.
In a fit of rage he assaults Regan and orders the demon to take him instead.
Pazuzu obeys and Karras throws himself from the window.
He then dies of his injuries, but not before receiving last rites from his friend Father Dyer (William O'Malley).
Days later the McNeils leave for Los Angeles.
They meet Dyer and say goodbye.
Regan remembers nothing, but embraces him after noticing his white collar.
After missing the duo, Kinderman decides to befriend Dyer by inviting him to see a movie with him.
As Dyer already saw the movie, Kinderman takes him to lunch.

24615845.title: The Morning Scoop
synopsis: Sarah Bennett, a clever yet somewhat introverted producer at 'Wake Up, Fresno!
', a locally-run morning show aired on CBS47, orchestrates her tasks within the realm of satellite trucks and intricate editing suites.
Still, she harbors a hidden longing for the illuminating gleam of the spotlight.
Sarah, brought to life by the exceptional talent of Emily Blunt, is a woman deeply steeped in her prompt 6 AM to 3 PM daily routine.
Every break of dawn, she awakens with the first light of the sunlight, the expanses of Fresno, California gently illuminating her growing ambitions.
She spends the early hours scrupulously perfecting every tiny detail of the scripts, coordinating the synchrony of light and sound.
One particular Tuesday, the director, Steven, gathers the staff to unveil his ingenious brainchild.
The groundbreaking proposal?
The entire staff would swap roles for one week, with the experimental rotation commencing the following Monday.
As the reality of the announcement washes over Sarah, her features bleach of color and her pulse quickens to an adrenaline-induced 130 bpm.
The team tirelessly invests personal hours after the show to groom Sarah.
They conduct script reading sessions, break down makeup techniques with high-end MAC products, select a vibrant wardrobe, and train her to handle any unplanned technical hiccups.
Sarah's anxiety escalates as her segment, meticulously prepared by Karen and Bill, reaches its final shape.
The day Sarah had been dreading, the show's finale, arrives, and she must face her past as she interviews her ex-boyfriend, Tom, live on air.
However, summoning newfound confidence, she expertly turns the situation around by giving an emotionally stirring, humor-infused, and genuinely heartfelt speech on the significance of second chances.
This catches fire on numerous social media platforms, gaining an immense number of broadcasts, shares, and quickly trends across the cyber realm.
Steven, astounded by Sarah's hitherto unrecognized charm and talent, extends her a permanent position as a host of the show in front of the entire staff.
For a brief moment, Sarah freezes, visually processing the astonishing offer, then lets loose a wave of uncontained joy, broadcast live on air.
Sarah’s dynamic shift into the spotlight fuels an unexpected rekindling of feelings from her ex, Tom, who approaches her the following day with hopes of re-establishing their relationship.
However, a visibly transformed Sarah, now embodying confidence and resilience, politely declines his proposal.
She emphasizes her newfound need for personal freedom and solitariness.
Sarah prepares for her first official day on the 'Wake Up, Fresno!'
set.
Deep breath in, an infectious smile touched with a dash of humor, eyes radiating a sense of determination.
With renewed confidence, Sarah strides towards the blue-green set and steps under the bright studio lights.
At Steven's call over the earpiece, the filming lights come on, and Sarah locks her gaze straight into the lens of Camera 1.
"Good Morning Fresno, this is Sarah Bennett, your new morning host, ready to brighten your day with a dash of fun and local news,” she eloquently starts, her smile sparking unparalleled enthusiasm.
Her colleagues continue to cheer, and even the customarily gruff Steven seems to have a gleam in his gray eyes.

17901762.title: The Ugly Truth
synopsis: Abby Richter (Katherine Heigl) is a morning show TV producer in Sacramento, California.
Abby firmly believes in true love and is a big supporter of complex self-help books such as Chicken Soup for the Soul and Men Are from Mars, Women Are from Venus.

Coming home from a disastrous date, she happens to see a segment of a local television show, The Ugly Truth, featuring Mike Chadway (Gerard Butler), whose cynicism about relationships prompts Abby to call in to argue with him on-air.
The next day, she discovers the TV station is threatening to cancel her show because of its poor ratings.
The station owner has hired Mike to do a segment on her show.
At first, the two have a rocky relationship; Abby thinks Mike is crass and disgusting while Mike finds her to be naive and a control freak.
Nevertheless, when she meets the man of her dreams, a doctor named Colin (Eric Winter) living next to her, Mike convinces her that by following his advice she will improve her chances with Colin.

Abby is skeptical, but they make a deal: If Mike's management of her courtship results in her landing Colin, proving his theories on relationships, she will work happily with him, but if Mike fails, he agrees to leave her show.

[2]  Mike succeeds in improving the ratings, brings married co-anchors Georgia and Larry closer and successfully instructs Abby to be exactly what Colin would want through a number of pointers including: always laugh at his jokes and say he is amazing in bed.
Mike is invited to appear on The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson and is offered a job at another network.
Abby is forced to cancel a romantic weekend away with Colin, during which they had planned to finally sleep together, and instead fly to Los Angeles to persuade Mike to stay with her show.
They drink and dance and Mike admits he does not want to move because he wants to stay in Sacramento near his sister and nephew.
In the hotel elevator, they passionately kiss, but go to their separate rooms.
Mike, dealing with the intensity of his feelings for Abby, calls on her room only to find Colin has shown up to surprise her.
Mike leaves.
Abby is upset and soon realizes Colin only likes the woman she has been pretending to be, not the real her.
She breaks up with him.
Mike quits and takes a job with a rival TV station in Sacramento, and ends up doing a broadcast at the same hot air balloon festival as Abby.
He cannot resist intruding when she kicks the new "Mike Chadway" imitator off the air and goes into a tirade about what cowardly weaklings men are.
The balloon takes off while they argue.
Abby says she broke up with Colin, and Mike admits he loves her.
Abby kisses him while they fly off, all of which is broadcast due to a camera mounted in the balloon.
The film ends with Abby and Mike in bed.
When Mike asks if she was faking it, Abby smirks and responds, "You'll never know."

99899271.title: Academic Anatomy
synopsis: Dr. John Collins, a renowned anatomy professor at Harvard University, dutifully spends his days teaching the next generation of medical experts about the wondrous complexity of the human body.
His in-depth lectures and ground-breaking research papers focused on neurological functions earn him a well-deserved reputation in both the medical and academe's intellectual society.
However, despite his scholarly accomplishments, John battles intuition and emotion in his tumultuous relationship with his fiancé, the enigmatic Liz Hathaway.
Revered for her chilling, profound depiction of Lady Macbeth in Shakespeare's classic tragedy, Liz stands out as a remarkably gifted, albeit peculiar, theatre actress.

Delving deeper into his academic pursuits and their intricate personal relationship, John starts drawing eerie parallels between intricate anatomical illustrations in his lecture notes and Liz's macabre stage settings.
A profound chill runs up his spine when he recognizes realistic depictions of human hearts and lungs that serve as props in Liz's grim productions.
Soon, the quaint Boston townhouse they reside in starts to feel more like a haunted house, fraught with strange noises originating from Liz's basement rehearsal studio.
Alarmed by this unsettling transition, one night, John gathers his nerves and descends into Liz's world, her mysterious rehearsal space.
Instead of a traditional theatre workspace, he stumbles upon a realm that resembles a sinister anatomy lab, commandeered by a rogue surgeon.
Strewn about are haphazard anatomical sketches, uncannily realistic stage props, and an array of surgical tools, all hinting at a chilling narrative.
His grim discovery seeds in him suspicion of Liz and her theatrical team engaging in unspeakable activities, shaking him to his core.
As he spends more time in this dreadful environment, John discerns an appalling pattern woven through the madness.
Several of his brilliant anatomy students have started to disappear, each leaving a traceless absentee letter behind.
Struggling to make sense of this inexplicable correlation, John realizes his emotional turmoil over Liz is impeding his judgment, preventing him from unearthing the truth.
However, the blindfold of love is ruthlessly ripped away when the horrifying reality dawns upon him.
Liz, the woman he was meant to wed, has been stealing organs from his missing students, using them as morbidly accurate props in her grim productions.
This macabre truth sends ripples through his disillusioned perception, leaving him in a state of shock and dismay.
Liz's nonchalant confession that her vile acts are merely committed in the name of theatrical innovation renders John absolutely speechless.
Torn between shock and deep-seated fear, John can only watch as Liz meticulously creates a fortress of lies to protect herself and her secrets from the intellectual community they both belong to.
Deftly exploiting his vulnerable state, she convinces John that his recent revelations are hallucinations induced by stress.
This cruel manipulation launches a civil war in John's psyche, wrestling him between accepting a fabricated reality or fighting for the truth.
Despite the all-encompassing mental strife, John refuses to surrender to Liz's gaslighting.
Adhering to his scientific background, he meticulously starts gathering empirical data in secret, cataloging every sinister revelation as an indisputable fact.
A fierce struggle of truth and deception unfolds, tackled behind the veil of their decorated facade.
John, shouldered with immense love for Liz yet duty-bound to protect his unwitting students, resolves to confront her.
What ensues is a near-apocalyptic clash, closely resembling a Greek tragedy, unfolding within the confines of their townhouse.
This battle is not just for John; it's a desperate struggle for the lives of his unwitting students.
In a heroic act of academic and moral integrity, John stands against the world he knew, revealing Liz and her team's inhuman activities.
His initial revelations shake the porous grounds of the Harvard community; however, the subsequent police investigation serves as a disheartening validation of John's claims.
Though vindicated in his quest for truth, John remains emotionally battered and struggling to comprehend his victory over the woman he once hoped to marry.
In the drama-filled aftermath, the prestigious university sets on a path towards recovery and redemption.
To fill the void left by John, new appointments are hastily made as he withdraws from the stressful academia, opting for a quiet period to heal emotional wounds.
Just when the University begins its steady climb back to normalcy, the arrival of a new drama professor launches them into a tumultuous state.
The opening act of his maiden production eerily mirrors Liz's distinctive theatrical style, leaving the audience shaken.
This haunting similarity sends cautionary ripples through the community, leaving everyone who survived Liz's reign in a tense apprehension.
This suspense-laden atmosphere marks the end of the movie, leaving the audience on a nail-biting cliffhanger.
The unanswered question regarding the new faculty member's motivations looms harshly, making everyone question whether the University is doomed to relive its horrific past.
In the post-credit scene, the camera follows the new drama professor stepping into a rehearsal room that oddly resembles the one previously commanded by Liz.
As the echoes of Liz's notorious past rise again, a chilling teaser is set in motion about the horrors that might revisit the Harvard community.

As the screen dissolves into a foreboding darkness, the audience finds themselves ensnared in the chilling possibilities of the future, questioning the fate that awaits the students under the new professor's supremacy.

442647.title: Young Frankenstein
synopsis: Dr. Frederick Frankenstein (Gene Wilder) is a physician lecturer at an American medical school and engaged to the tightly wound actress Elizabeth (Madeline Kahn).
He becomes exasperated when anyone brings up the subject of his grandfather, the infamous mad scientist.
To disassociate himself from his legacy, Frederick insists that his surname be pronounced "Fronk-en-steen."

When a solicitor informs him that he has inherited his family's estate in Transylvania after the death of his great grandfather, the Baron Beauvort von Frankenstein, Frederick travels to Europe to inspect the property.
At the Transylvania train station, he is met by a hunchbacked, bulging-eyed servant named Igor, pronounced as "eye-gore" (Marty Feldman), and a lovely young personal assistant named Inga (Teri Garr).
Upon arrival at the estate, Frederick meets the forbidding housekeeper Frau Blücher (Cloris Leachman), whose name causes horses to rear up and neigh madly in fright.

Though his family legacy has brought shame and ridicule, Frederick becomes increasingly intrigued about his grandfather's work, especially after Inga assists him in discovering the secret entrance to his grandfather's laboratory.
Upon reading his grandfather's private journals, Frederick is so transformed that he decides to resume his grandfather's experiments in re-animating the dead.
He and Igor resort to robbing the grave of a recently executed criminal, and Frederick sets to work experimenting on the large corpse.
Matters go awry, however, when Igor is sent to steal the brain of a deceased revered scientist, Hans Delbruck; startled by lightning, he drops and ruins Delbruck's brain.
Taking a second brain, Igor returns with a brain labeled "Do Not Use This Brain!
Abnormal" (which he subsequently refers to as "A-b (Abby) Normal"), which Frederick unknowingly transplants into the corpse.
Soon, Frederick is ready to re-animate his creature (Peter Boyle), who is elevated on a platform to the roof of the laboratory during a lightning storm.
Eventually, electrical charges bring the creature to life.
The creature makes its first halting steps, but, frightened by Igor lighting a match, attacks Frederick and must be sedated.
Upon being asked whose brain was obtained, Igor confesses that he supplied "Abby Normal's" (abnormal) brain, unknowingly creating the Monster.
The townspeople are uneasy at the possibility of Frederick continuing his grandfather's work.

Most concerned is Inspector Kemp (Kenneth Mars), a police official who sports an eyepatch and monocle over the same eye, a creaky, disjointed wooden arm, and an accent so comically thick even his own countrymen cannot understand him.
Kemp visits the doctor and subsequently demands assurance that he will not create another monster.
Upon returning to the lab, Frederick discovers that Frau Blücher is setting the creature free.

After she reveals the monster's love of violin music, and her own romantic relationship with Frederick's grandfather, the creature is enraged by sparks from a thrown switch, and escapes from the Frankenstein castle.
While roaming the countryside, the Monster has frustrating encounters with a young girl and a blind hermit (Gene Hackman); these scenes directly parody the original Frankenstein movies.

Frederick recaptures the monster and locks the two of them in a room, where he calms the monster's homicidal tendencies with flattery and fully acknowledges his own heritage, shouting out emphatically, "My name is Frankenstein!"
(This time, he uses the more common, Anglicized pronunciation.)
Frederick offers the sight of "The Creature" following simple commands to a theater full of illustrious guests.
The demonstration continues with Frederick and the monster launching into the musical number "Puttin' on the Ritz," complete with top hats and tails.
Although the monster can only shout his song lines in painfully high-pitched monotones, he dances impressively with almost perfect timing.

The routine ends disastrously, however, when a stage light explodes and frightens the monster, who becomes enraged, pushes Frederick, and charges into the audience, where he is captured and chained by police.
The monster escapes, then kidnaps and ravishes the not unwilling Elizabeth when she arrives unexpectedly for a visit.

Elizabeth falls in love with the creature due to his inhuman stamina and his enormous penis (referred to as Schwanstuker or Schwanzstück — a Yiddish word from Schwanz, "tail," which also is German slang for "penis," and Stück, "piece").
The townspeople hunt for the monster.
Desperate to get the creature back, Frederick plays the violin to lure his creation back to the castle.
Just as the Kemp-led mob storms the laboratory, Frankenstein transfers some of his stabilizing intellect to the creature who, as a result, is able to reason with and placate the mob.

The film ends happily, with Elizabeth married to the now erudite and sophisticated monster--with her hair styled identically to that of the female creature from The Bride Of Frankenstein, while Inga joyfully learns what her new husband Frederick got in return during the transfer procedure--the monster's Schwanzstück.

44537879.title: Arizona Hustle
synopsis: Our saga follows Thomas Smith, a skilled safe cracker, serving his sentence on a highway construction crew in Arizona.
One afternoon, a Navajo man named Johnny Wolf approaches the worksite.
Johnny discloses his hidden motive to Thomas, sharing a story of a tribal totem stolen from his tribe, nestled within a fortified mansion.
Johnny presents a carefully etched blueprint of the mansion, convincing Thomas to join forces to recover the stolen artifact.
Thomas agrees, driven by the blend of adventure, risk, and the promise of leaving a meaningful mark on history.
Act Two catapults us into planning and strategizing.
Patiently, they calculate timings for break-ins, steps for disarming the alarm systems, and planning diversions.
